title: SoC pop-up menus overflow on non-16:9 — mod needs fov_effective; engine verified equivalent to r6303
description:
User reported the SoC options menu (END, impulse 85) sits 'too close' on Hexenwail and 'projected correctly' on uhexen2-r6303. Measured on their machine after uhexen2-vsxi shipped:

  fov_effective   = 100.388855   -> 16:10 display
  fov_effective_y =  73.739792   -> correct

GEOMETRY. Menu_Project places the panel at eye + v_forward * (25.5 - 0.15 * cvar("fov")), = 12 units at fov 90. The panel is 32 units wide (.scale 0.25 on a 128-unit model; .t_width 16 confirms the half-width), so it subtends 2*atan(16/12) = 106.26 degrees. That is exactly AdaptFovx's output for fov 90 at 16:9 — both are 2*atan(4/3) — so the mod fills the width precisely on 16:9 and overflows elsewhere:

  16:9   panel 106.26 / view 106.26 = 1.000x   (design point)
  16:10  panel 106.26 / view 100.39 = 1.058x   (user's display)
  4:3    panel 106.26 / view  90.00 = 1.181x

NO fov VALUE FIXES IT, which is why fiddling with the slider does not help and it reads as stuck 'too close': raising fov widens the view but the mod's own term pulls the panel closer at the same time, so the two chase each other. Best achievable at 16:10 is fov 123.44 for a ratio of 1.009 — an absurd FOV for a 1% gain.

ENGINE VERIFIED EQUIVALENT TO r6303 (tag shanjaq-r6303-archive-2026-05-31), function by function:
  AdaptFovx            identical
  CalcFovy             identical
  R_RotateForEntity2   identical
  V_CalcRefdef         identical
  SCR_CalcRefdef       differs in text but NOT in result at viewsize 110, which both configs use: r6303 computes size=min(110,100)/100=1.0 and sb_lines=0, giving a full-window vrect; current sets vrect = full window with sb_lines=0. Same aspect into AdaptFovx. They only diverge below viewsize 100, where r6303 letterboxes and current clamps.
  GL_Frustum           rewritten for GL 4.3 but mathematically the same: xmax = NEARCLIP*tan(fov_x*pi/360) and f[0] = znear/xmax = 1/tan(fov_x/2). Reversed-Z touches f[10]/f[14] only, i.e. depth, not field of view.

So on the same window aspect the two builds render this menu identically. The r6303 test was almost certainly at 16:9.

DECISIVE TEST, one minute: run Hexenwail in a 16:9 window and press END. Prediction is that it frames exactly. If it does not, this analysis is wrong and there is a real regression to find.

MOD FIX, aspect-correct at any fov and any display, and it also removes the fov 170 cliff where the old formula reaches zero distance:

    dist = 16 / tan(cvar("fov_effective") * 0.5 * M_PI / 180)

At 16:10 that gives 13.36 units instead of 12, and the panel then subtends exactly the rendered 100.39 degrees. Hand this to BloodShot.
notes:
INSTANCED PATH EXONERATED 2026-08-24: user tested r_alias_gpu 0, no change. Both alias paths agree because both are correct.

Also verified the scale really does reach the renderer — the mod's progs.dat field layout matches the engine's entvars_t exactly (.origin 10, .angles 19, .model 29, .scale 33, .drawflags 34, .abslight 35 in both), so ent->v.scale reads 0.25, the server sends (int)(0.25*100)&255 = 25, and the client computes entScale 0.25. The panel really is 32 units wide at 12 units out, subtending 106.26 degrees. The engine is drawing it exactly as the mod asks, and it fills the screen BY CONSTRUCTION at any aspect.

Which means r6303 must have differed in something outside that chain. It did:

  r6303:   viewsize clamped to [30, 130].  At viewsize < 100 SCR_CalcRefdef
           computes size = viewsize/100 and shrinks the 3D vrect to that
           fraction of the window, centred — a letterboxed 3D view with a
           border around it.
  current: viewsize clamped to [100, 140], and any value below 100 is
           silently forced to 100 (gl_screen.c). The 3D vrect is always the
           full window. Comment calls the old path 'a Pentium-era perf knob
           no modern Quake-family engine uses'.

The menu panel fills the 3D VIEWPORT by construction. In r6303 at, say, viewsize 90 that viewport was inset 5% each side, so the panel appeared as a bordered panel floating in front of the player — exactly the user's description of correct behaviour. In Hexenwail the viewport is always the whole window, so the same panel goes edge to edge: 'frames the whole screen'.

It was never really a perf knob for this mod; it was the framing the menus were designed against.

CONFIRMATION NEEDED, cheap: ask what viewsize the r6303 test ran at. If it was below 100, this is settled. Demonstrate the clamp in Hexenwail with 'viewsize 90' followed by 'viewsize' — it reports 100, with no message saying why.

FIX OPTIONS if confirmed:
  1. Restore sub-100 viewsize, i.e. bring back the size-scaled vrect in both renderers. Restores a knob users had. Risk is real and needs checking, not assuming: Hi-Z culling, the postprocess chain and r_scale were all built after the vrect became unconditionally full-window, and may assume it.
  2. Leave viewsize alone and accept that this mod's menus are full-screen here.
Do not silently force the value either way — whatever is decided, a clamp that changes what the user typed should say so.

title: Tristram map crashes the engine to desktop
description:
BloodShot, Discord 2026-08-23: 'my tristram map will CTD the engine with this error', with a screenshot of the error text.

BLOCKED ON INFORMATION. The error string is only in the screenshot and has not been transcribed, so there is nothing to grep for yet. Ask him for:
  - the literal error text (or qconsole.log, which will have it)
  - the map, or its name and the mod it belongs to
  - whether it reproduces on r15, which would separate it from anything in the r16 tick or lighting work

Filed at P0 anyway rather than waiting: a crash to desktop on a real community map is the most severe class of report we take, and leaving it unfiled until the text arrives risks it being lost in the thread. Downgrade after triage if it turns out to be content-specific and rare.

Worth noting that a Windows build writes glh2.RPT next to glh2.exe naming the source file and line, and the release notes already tell people to attach it -- point him at that, it will likely answer this outright.
notes:
THE MAP IS NOT ON THIS BOX. Checked for it properly rather than assuming, both spellings:

  - all five soc/ installs here (/home/josh/hexen2/soc, /home/josh/.hexen2/soc,
    audit-env/inst/soc, qoy7-test/game/soc, qoy7-test/home/.hexen2/soc).
    /home/josh/hexen2/soc/maps has 34 files: 32 .ent overrides plus h2menu.bsp
    and h2menupop.bsp. No tristam.bsp, no tristram.bsp, no custom .bsp at all.
  - /home/josh/hexen2, /home/josh/tmp and /home/josh/Downloads, -iname "*trista*"
  - the string "trista" inside data1/pak0.pak, data1/pak1.pak, portals/pak3.pak: 0 hits

Consistent with how BloodShot described it -- "MY tristram map". It is his own work, not part of the SoC release, so it was never going to be here.

WHAT IS HERE SAYS THE SHIPPED MOD IS NOT THE PROBLEM. SoC works by shipping .ent files that replace the entity lump of stock maps (the engine reads maps/<name>.ent, gl_model.c:1101). Counting model-bearing entities in each and pricing them at 20 bytes a baseline, the heaviest is village1 at 198 -> ~4 KB, then village2 160 -> ~3.2 KB and tower 155 -> ~3.1 KB. That is an order of magnitude under even the OLD 32 KB ceiling, so no shipped SoC map could have caused this. It is the custom map, and 24 buffers x 16 KB is very unlikely to be short for it -- but that is a prediction, not a test.

STILL THE ONE THING THIS BEAD NEEDS: the .bsp from BloodShot. Everything the fix has been tested against is a map that never crashed. With the map, the check is one command:
    glhexen2 -game soc +developer 1 +map tristam
and the new "Signon: %d bytes in %d/%d buffers" line answers it outright.

His glh2.RPT line is still worth having too -- it separates sv.signon from sv.datagram, which is also 32 KB, also allowoverflow false, reachable from QC via MSG_BROADCAST, and untouched by a47d006fb.

title: fixangle no longer pins the view: input is sampled at render rate, svc_setangle only arrives per server message
description:
BloodShot, Discord 2026-08-23: 'ticrate also changes how often FIXANGLE can update. In the old ports forcing FIXANGLE to true every frame will stop the camera movement completely (I use this for the death cam, custom menus, etc), but here it's not updating fast enough to keep the camera in place, even with setting ticrate to 0.' Video: https://i.imgur.com/mWC5Dpa.mp4

Root cause is the render/physics decoupling, NOT the tick rate — which is why changing ticrate did not help him, and is the detail that identifies it.

Per render frame _Host_Frame does:
  1. CL_AdjustAngles() + IN_Move()  -- writes cl.viewangles, EVERY render frame
  2. the physics loop, 0..N ticks   -- server may emit svc_setangle
  3. CL_ReadFromServer()            -- svc_setangle overwrites cl.viewangles (cl_parse.c:1535)

On any render frame where step 2 produced no new setangle, step 1's mouse delta survives to the renderer and the camera drifts. Vanilla could not hit this: the server frame ran once per render frame, so a setangle landed after input on every single frame and the view was pinned exactly.

The gap is not primarily sv_physfps. QC that sets .fixangle 'every frame' sets it every HX_FRAME_TIME (0.05s, h2/constant.hc:8), so svc_setangle arrives ~20x/sec no matter how fast the server ticks, while IN_Move runs at the display rate. At 144 Hz that is ~7 frames of unopposed mouse input between forces.

Note the engine and QC already agree the server wins while fixangle is set: sv_user.c:602 gates applying the client's cmd angles on !fixangle. Only the client-side view is escaping.

Fix: latch the forced angle on svc_setangle and re-apply it after the render-rate input sampling for a hold window, so a mod that keeps setting fixangle keeps the view pinned while a one-shot fixangle (teleport) releases promptly. The window has to exceed the QC think cadence that produces the forces, which is why it cannot simply be one tick.

Related but distinct, same report: 'You can also see it on the paladin purifier, at ticrate 0 the projectiles spawn correctly, but at 0.05 they spawn too far forward.' That one IS rate-dependent, so it is a different mechanism — filed separately.
close_reason: Fixed in f77cde76c. Latches the forced angle on svc_setangle and re-applies it after the render-rate input sampling, held for cl_fixangle_hold (0.06s, 0 = off, floored at two ticks). Build green. NOT field-confirmed — BloodShot's death cam / custom menus are the test.

title: Field-confirm the 72 Hz physics tick with BloodShot (strafe jump, spider cadence, his mod)
description:
uhexen2-skjv moved the server/physics tick from 20 Hz to 72 Hz via the new sv_physfps cvar. Root cause was proven by code reading and the build is green, but nobody has played it.

BloodShot filed the original report on Discord (2026-08-21) and has the two comparison videos plus a custom mod whose think chains ran at the wrong speed, so he is the right person to confirm:
  * https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRs4w80zaNw (Hexenwail, slow)
  * https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u6ZD_BaN6Ng (vanilla Hexen II, correct)

What to confirm:
  1. Strafe jumping builds speed like vanilla, with sys_ticrate left at its default (his workaround was sys_ticrate 0.01 — that cvar no longer affects the client at all, so his config should be reverted before testing).
  2. Spider attack cadence matches the vanilla video.
  3. His custom mod functions run at the right speed.
  4. Coop: no packet jitter for other clients. 72 Hz is the vanilla send rate so this should be clean, but it is the specific thing his 100 Hz workaround broke, so it needs a real look.
  5. Sanity: sv_physfps 20 should reproduce the old slow behaviour, which confirms the knob is the one doing the work.

Tell him sys_ticrate is now dedicated-server-only and to remove it from his config.
close_reason:
Field-confirmed by BloodShot on 0.8.0-beta.r16, 2026-08-23. Reported that it 'seems to fix most of my game logic related issues', and separately that it fixed slow-feeling crouching — a symptom nobody had connected to the tick rate and which nothing in the fix targeted directly. That is the tick count showing up in a third place, consistent with the diagnosis.

Not confirmed and now unlikely to be: item 4 of the check list (coop packet jitter for other clients). No coop session was run. 72 Hz is the vanilla send rate so the risk was always theoretical; leaving it unverified rather than claiming it.

One residual, in his mod rather than the engine — a continuous Half-Life-2-style grab controller trails the target at 72 Hz and tracks exactly at sv_physfps 20. Split out as its own bead; it is a mod-side rate assumption, not a regression here.

title: Gameplay runs at 20 Hz: the fixed-timestep server tick is driven by sys_ticrate (0.05)
description:
BloodShot (Discord, 2026-08-21) reports on the 2026-08-20 build: monster logic runs slow (spiders attack noticeably slower), custom mod think chains run at the wrong speed, and strafe jumping bleeds speed instead of building it. He found that 'sys_ticrate 0.01' restores near-vanilla behaviour, at the cost of jitter for other clients in coop.

Two videos: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRs4w80zaNw (Hexenwail) vs https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u6ZD_BaN6Ng (vanilla Hexen II).

Root cause: _Host_Frame (engine/hexen2/host.c) drives the fixed-timestep accumulator from sys_ticrate, which defaults to 0.05 => the server/physics tick runs at 20 Hz. Upstream uHexen2 ran Host_ServerFrame once per render frame with the real frametime (sys_adaptive path), i.e. up to host_maxfps = 72 Hz. Even Ravens own disabled FPS_20 arm in the same file substeps the world at 'while (temp_host_frametime > 1.0/72.0)'. So 72 Hz is the historical tick, 20 Hz is a regression introduced with the render/physics decoupling.

Why it shows up the way it does:
  * SV_RunThink (sv_phys.c:138) runs AT MOST ONE think per server frame. Any think chain scheduled at less than the tick interval (the common 'nextthink = time' / 'time + 0.01' mod idiom) is now capped at 20 Hz instead of 72 Hz -- 3.6x slower.
  * SV_AirAccelerate (sv_user.c) clamps wishspd to 30 and gains at most 'addspeed' per tick; accelspeed = sv_accelerate*wishspeed*frametime is far above that clamp, so the per-tick gain does not scale with frametime. Strafe-jump acceleration is therefore directly proportional to tick count: 20/s instead of 72/s.

sys_ticrate is a dedicated-server knob everywhere else in the Quake family (sys_sdl.c only reads it under isDedicated), so overloading it for the listen-server physics rate was wrong on naming grounds too.

Fix: drive the accumulator from its own cvar defaulting to 72 Hz, leave sys_ticrate to the dedicated server. Note that 72 Hz also restores the vanilla packet rate for coop (one SV_SendClientMessages per render frame, capped by host_maxfps=72), so BloodShots coop jitter at sys_ticrate 0.01 (100 Hz) does not come back.
close_reason:
Fixed in 8dced6020 'fix(host): the world thought at 20 Hz — give the physics tick its own rate' (+ comment refresh in ca75b440c).

The fixed-timestep accumulator in _Host_Frame now takes its interval from a new archived cvar sv_physfps (default 72, clamped to [10,250]) instead of sys_ticrate, which goes back to being the dedicated-server frame interval it is everywhere else in the Quake family. 72 Hz is the pre-regression rate: upstream uHexen2 ran Host_ServerFrame once per render frame bounded by host_maxfps=72, and Raven's own disabled FPS_20 arm substeps the world at 'while (temp_host_frametime > 1.0/72.0)'.

Because the tick no longer follows the render rate this is steadier than vanilla as well — a 30 Hz vsync used to halve air control and no longer does.

Also fixed while in there: the accumulator's catch-up cap was 5*interval, which at any rate above 20 Hz is less than the 0.1s Host_FilterTime can hand it in one frame, so every hitch silently dropped simulated time. Cap is now 0.1 + interval.

Evidence: nix build .#nixos green; 'strings result/bin/glhexen2' shows sv_physfps registered. Root cause proven by code reading (SV_RunThink one-think-per-frame at sv_phys.c:138; SV_AirAccelerate's wishspd<=30 / addspeed per-tick gain in sv_user.c, which does not scale with frametime). NOT yet field-confirmed — see the follow-up bead.

title: [feature] misc_modelpimp spawnflag 64 dlight is model-keyed — Mathuzzz needs a registerable model group (nolerp-style)
description:
Reported by Mathuzzz (Discord, 2026-08-21, 2:15 AM). This is design pushback on what shipped in 0f416d794 ("fix(dlight): honour misc_modelpimp flag 64 on every steady light effect"), not a bug in it.

HIS PROBLEM
"ok, so far I wasn't able to make the lights work with the 64 spawnflag. The problem is that my lighting works completely differently. They consists of more models, etc...so the spawnflag shouldn't be model dependent, but for all the lights except the default light (which has no model)."

His light entities are assembled from MULTIPLE models rather than being one model with one pimp. Because our flag-64 dlight path keys off the model, every one of his lights fails to pick it up. The only case that works for him is the default light, which has no model at all.

HIS PROPOSED DESIGN
"Or, similarly to the nolerp group, we could have this group of models that produce dynamic lights. Vanilla game would have the models mentioned above, but we modders could add our own."

i.e. replace (or supplement) the model-keyed flag with a named MODEL GROUP:
  - the engine ships a vanilla list of light-producing models,
  - modders can register additional models into that group from their mod,
  - membership in the group, not a per-model spawnflag, drives the dlight.

The nolerp group is the precedent to mirror — find how nolerp membership is
declared and loaded, and follow that shape so this is one more list of the
same kind rather than a new mechanism with new syntax.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS (resolve before writing code)
  - Where does a modder declare the group? A text file in the mod dir, a
    console/cvar list, or a QC-side registration call? nolerp's answer should
    drive this.
  - Does the group REPLACE flag 64, or coexist with it? Coexisting is safer —
    flag 64 keeps working for existing maps, the group adds the modder path.
  - Does group membership carry light parameters (radius/colour/falloff), or
    only the on/off decision, with parameters still coming from the pimp?
  - Interaction with the additive-only PimpModel contract and the r15 reach
    rules documented in 0c109fb80 — a group must not become a back door around
    the propagation policy settled in uhexen2-oq0a.

BLOCKED ON: a design call from Bob before implementation. Confirm the group
semantics with Mathuzzz too, since he is the one consumer whose layout we know.

RELATED: uhexen2-nna4 (shared-model propagation policy in PF_pimpmodel) — same
subsystem, same underlying tension between model-scoped and entity-scoped
effect state.
close_reason:
Implemented in e34f353fa as r_dlight_model_list.

RESOLVING THE OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS this bead listed:

  Where does a modder declare the group?
    A CVAR_ARCHIVE cvar on the r_nolerp_list pattern - comma-separated whole
    model names, matched case-insensitively through the same nameInList helper.
    That is the precedent Mathuzzz explicitly asked to mirror, so it needs no
    new syntax and no new file format.

  Does it replace flag 64, or coexist?
    Coexist, and it does not touch flag 64 at all. It turned out the right
    thing to generalise was not the pimpmodel spawnflag but the engine's
    built-in light-casting group in Mod_SetAliasModelExtraFlags - the
    rflmtrch / cflmtrch / castrch / rometrch / egtorch / flame family that gets
    XF_TORCH_GLOW and that CL_RelinkEntities already lights. That is literally
    'the models mentioned above' in his message. It was hardcoded in C with no
    way in; now there is one. The built-in list is unchanged and always wins,
    and the cvar is empty by default, so nothing shipped moves.

  Does membership carry light parameters?
    No. Entries get the built-in torch treatment - colour plus TORCH_STYLE
    flicker. Per-model colour and radius stay the misc_modelpimp route. This is
    the 'make it a light' switch, not a lighting editor. Revisit only if he
    asks for per-entry colour.

  Interaction with the additive-only PimpModel contract / uhexen2-oq0a?
    None. It writes mod->ex_flags at model LOAD, before any pimpmodel call, and
    is not a propagation path - it cannot be used to reach siblings or to route
    around the reach policy. Deliberately not re-applied on cvar change:
    ex_flags is also written by PF_pimpmodel and rolled back by
    Mod_RestoreAliasModelDefaults, so re-running the assignment mid-map would
    clobber the current map's pimp state. A mod sets this from autoexec.cfg,
    before any map loads. Documented as such.

ALSO ADDED because the feature was otherwise untestable by the person who needs
it: mcache now reports the engine-assigned group per model (TORCH_GLOW, GLOW,
MISSILE_GLOW, ILLUMINATE, NO_DLIGHT). Without it a modder cannot tell a
mistyped model name from a light being suppressed somewhere else.

VERIFIED IN-ENGINE, not just built. Ran headless with
    r_dlight_model_list "models/puzzle/chalice.mdl,models/empty2.mdl"
and loaded sot/cathedral. mcache reports:
    models/puzzle/chalice.mdl TORCH_GLOW   <- granted by the cvar, no built-in rule
    models/rometrch.mdl       TORCH_GLOW   <- built-in, untouched

docs/MODELPIMP.md has a new section covering the cvar, why pimpmodel is the
wrong shape for multi-model fixtures, and how to confirm an entry took.

FOR MATHUZZZ: the thing to tell him is that his fixtures do not need a
spawnflag at all - he lists his lamp models in r_dlight_model_list from his
mod's autoexec.cfg and every one of them casts light, however many models a
fixture is built from. Worth asking whether he also wants per-entry colour,
which is the obvious next request and deliberately not in this first cut.

title: [bug] Host_Error: CL_ParseServerMessage: Illegible server message 64 on heavy-loaded maps (r15, Win64)
description:
Reported by Mathuzzz (Discord, 2026-08-21, 2:24 AM) against HEXENWAIL 0.8.0-BETA.R15 (WIN64):

    Host_Error: CL_ParseServerMessage: Illegible server message 64

Occurs on heavy-loaded maps. Mathuzzz's words: "the whole point of leaving uhexen was this error in heavy-loaded maps and...it's back? nightmare is back?" — this is the single issue that drove him off uHexen2, so it is a credibility problem as much as a crash.

WHY 64 IS NOT THE REAL BUG
The highest valid server command in engine/hexen2/protocol.h is svc_fog = 56. There is no svc 64. The byte 64 (0x40) also has no meaning as a flag — in the Quake-derived protocol a byte >= 128 is a fast entity update, so 0x40 is not that either. Therefore the parser was ALREADY desynchronised when it read that byte: it is a payload byte from the middle of an earlier message being misread as a command.

The defect is upstream of the failure point. Do not go looking for a handler for 64.

LIKELY ROOT CAUSES, in rough order of suspicion
  1. A datagram overflow on heavy maps truncating a message mid-write, so the
     client reads a partial message and then keeps going. "Heavy-loaded maps"
     correlating with the failure points here first.
  2. An svc handler whose read length does not match what the server wrote —
     a write/read pair that disagrees by a byte or more. Any recently touched
     svc is the prime suspect; check the ones carrying variable-length or
     newly-added payloads (svc_fog, svc_skybox, svc_mod_name, svc_particle3/4).
  3. A size/limit constant raised on the engine side but not on the write path
     (or vice versa), so large maps push past a buffer that used to hold.

DIAGNOSTIC ALREADY IN PLACE
engine/hexen2/cl_parse.c:1470 logs the derail point before erroring:

    Con_Printf("[DEMO] ERROR: Illegible server message %d at readcount=%d\n", cmd, msg_readcount);

That readcount value localises where the stream went wrong. Get it.

NEXT ACTION — need from Mathuzzz before deep diagnosis:
  - Which map(s), and whether it is reproducible on demand or intermittent.
  - The console scrollback containing the [DEMO] ERROR line with readcount.
  - A 'record' demo of the crash if he can capture one — a demo replays the
     exact byte stream and makes this bisectable offline.
  - Whether it happens in single-player, HexenWorld, or both.
  - Whether r10 (the last known-good build he had) is clean on the same map —
     that turns this into a bisect.

REGRESSION SCOPE: unknown whether this is a new break or a never-fixed inheritance from uHexen2. Establishing that is step one — if r10 is clean on the same map, bisect it.
close_reason:
Root-caused and fixed in f048c3394.

ROOT CAUSE — a write/read width mismatch on svc_clear_edicts (hypothesis 2 in
the description, not the overflow theory).

  sv_main.c wrote the removal count as ONE BYTE:
      MSG_WriteByte (msg, svc_clear_edicts);
      MSG_WriteByte (msg, NumToRemove);          <- truncates to 8 bits
      for (i = 0; i < NumToRemove; i++)          <- full 16-bit count
          MSG_WriteShort (msg, RemoveList[i]);

  NumToRemove is a short bounded only by MAX_CLIENT_STATES (8192).

  cl_parse.c:1883 reads a byte and consumes exactly that many shorts.

  So once more than 255 edicts left the PVS in a single frame, the client
  stopped 2 * (NumToRemove - (NumToRemove & 255)) bytes short of the end of
  the remove list and resumed parsing inside it. The next byte it took as a
  command was payload — hence 'Illegible server message 64', 64 being a
  payload byte, not a command (highest valid svc is svc_fog = 56, exactly as
  the description predicted).

  This is entity-count dependent, which is precisely why it only ever
  reproduced on heavy-loaded maps: a large PVS transition can retire several
  hundred edicts in one 20 Hz tick.

FIX — cap the queue at MAX_CLEAR_EDICTS_PER_MSG (255, the most the count byte
can describe). Excess removals are DEFERRED, not dropped: an over-cap edict
falls through to the IgnoreEnt path, so it stays in the build list and hence
in the client reference frame, and gets removed by a later message. Simply
dropping it would take it out of the reference while the client still had
BE_ON set, stranding it as a permanent ghost. Also clamped defensively at the
write site so the count and the payload loop cannot drift apart again, plus a
once-per-message Con_DPrintf under developer 1 when deferral happens.

Wire format unchanged — compatible in both directions with existing clients,
servers and demos. No protocol version gate needed.

AUDIT — checked every other MSG_WriteByte-count site (sv_effect.c rain count,
the four particle effects in sv_main.c). All are fixed-size trailing
parameters with no following variable-length run. svc_clear_edicts was the
only count-then-loop pattern in the protocol, so there is no sibling bug.

VERIFICATION — nix build clean. The defect is provable by inspection (single
writer at sv_main.c, single reader at cl_parse.c:1883, unambiguous width
disagreement), so it did not need field repro to confirm. What is NOT proven
locally is that Mathuzzz's specific map exceeds 255 removals per frame; that
is what 'heavy-loaded' means and the developer-mode deferral line will now say
so out loud. Worth asking him to confirm r16 is clean on the map that broke
r15.

NOT INVESTIGATED, filed separately as a residual desync risk: the unknown-svc
handler at cl_parse.c:1458 blind-skips one byte for SoT custom messages (cmd
0, 33, >=80) and its own comment admits 'if this is wrong, the stream will
desync'. Different trigger, same error class.

title: Archer movement looks jerky (Mathuzzz) — video needed before diagnosis
description:
Reported by Mathuzzz (Discord, 2026-08-20): "not sure if it has something to do, but I noticed archers movement being somewhat jerky, I think a video would be necessary here."

Reported tentatively and without a repro — he raised it in the same breath as the
misc_model problems (uhexen2-nna4) and was explicitly unsure whether they are
related. Treat the connection as unconfirmed.

BLOCKED ON: the video he offered. Ask for it, plus the map and whether it happens
at a specific distance or only while the archer is moving/strafing/flying.

BACKGROUND THAT MATTERS FOR TRIAGE:
  - Hexen II's physics tick is 20 Hz (sys_ticrate 0.05), so all monster motion is
    interpolated client-side between server frames. "Jerky" for one monster type
    and not others usually means the interpolation is being reset, not that the
    framerate dropped — check whether the archer's state changes (animation
    restarts, teleports, angle wraps) are clearing lerp state each tick.
  - Distinguish first: is it *positional* stutter (the model jumps between
    positions) or *animation* stutter (frames snap instead of blending)? Those
    are different code paths and the video should settle it in one viewing.
  - uhexen2-8tm ("VSync doesn't persist across sessions and feels jerky", closed)
    is a different, display-level cause of the same word. Rule it out by
    confirming his vsync setting and that other monsters look smooth in the same
    scene.
  - uhexen2-9gdx ("Root-cause the 'Bad backpack!' fallthrough — field reports on
    archers and leopards", closed) is the only other archer-specific report on
    record; unrelated symptom, but the same entity, so worth a glance.

DONE WHEN: the video is in hand, the stutter is classified as positional vs
animation vs display-level, and either a cause is identified or the report is
closed as not reproducible.
notes:
IN-ENGINE CONFIRMATION (not just the offline harness). Ran the built engine
headless (SDL offscreen + llvmpipe), loaded sot/keep, and dumped `mcache save`.
The engine's own reported flipratios match the offline predictions exactly:

  models/archer.mdl      flipratio=0.242            -> lerps   (was 0.410 NOLERP)
  models/archer2.mdl     flipratio=0.242            -> lerps
  models/paladin.mdl     flipratio=0.319            -> lerps
  models/necro.mdl       flipratio=0.210            -> lerps
  models/golem_s.mdl     flipratio=0.347            -> lerps
  models/barrel.mdl      flipratio=0.469  NOLERP    -> correctly held back by
                                                      the fallback pass; without
                                                      it this read 0.000 and lerped
  models/stalactite1.mdl flipratio=0.776  NOLERP
  models/stalactite2.mdl flipratio=0.823  NOLERP

115 models carry a ratio, 38 end up NOLERP. So both halves of the work are
confirmed in the real engine: the seam fix restores interpolation to the
monsters and the player model, and the fallback keeps the two-state props
snapping.

The same run also exercised the uhexen2-6ugh protocol change on a map load with
developer 1 and produced no 'remove list full' deferrals and no 'Illegible
server message' - keep.bsp simply does not retire 255 edicts in a tick, which
is the expected result rather than a null one.
close_reason:
Diagnosed and fixed. The video turned out not to be needed.

CLASSIFICATION (the bead's first DONE WHEN condition): ANIMATION stutter, not
positional and not display-level. Frame interpolation was disabled outright on
models/archer.mdl, so its poses snapped instead of blending. Nothing in the
positional path or the vsync path is implicated, so uhexen2-8tm is ruled out.

CAUSE: r_lerp_autodetect (uhexen2-f807) tags a model MOD_NOLERP when the worst
per-vertex displacement between two blended poses exceeds 35% of the bbox
diagonal. Because every animation a model owns lives end-to-end in one frame
array, the adjacent-single-pose case was also measuring animation SEAMS - the
last frame of one animation against the first of the next, poses nothing ever
blends. archer.mdl scored 0.410 on deathA22 -> draw1 alone, against 0.242 for
its worst genuinely-blended pair (fire1 -> fire2), and lost interpolation
across every animation it plays.

VERIFIED, not assumed: replicated Mod_ComputeFlipbookRatio offline (MDL parser
plus the engine's exact bounds and ratio arithmetic) and ran it over 970 models
- data1 pak0+pak1, Shadows of Turmoil, Wheel of Karma. It reproduces the
figures above exactly, so it measures what the engine measures.

BLAST RADIUS was much wider than one monster. Models that regained
interpolation: 13 in the base game (archer, assassin, fangel, funnal, golem_s,
hydra, medusa2, mezzoman, mummy, necro, paladin, tornato, barrel) and 21 across
the mods. paladin.mdl is the player model. snowleopard is in the list too,
which corroborates the 'archers and leopards' pairing in uhexen2-9gdx.

REGRESSION THE FIX ITSELF INTRODUCED, found in the same sweep and fixed in
0c76f38be: barrel.mdl (['resting1','onside1'], 0.469) and SoT stalactite_ice2.mdl
(['frame01','Key 2'], 0.659) have two states each rather than an animation.
Their names are not sequential, so after the name gate landed neither had any
measurable pair left, the ratio came back 0.0 - indistinguishable from
'measured, and smooth' - and both silently gained interpolation they never had.
A barrel that morphs as it tips. Now treated properly: zero measurable pairs is
itself the flipbook signal, since any model with animations yields a sequential
pair by construction. Re-swept all 970 models - exactly those two change
verdict, nothing else moves.

SPLIT OUT, deliberately not fixed here: uhexen2-1ies - the heuristic is still
all-or-nothing per model, so one violent death animation costs a model
interpolation everywhere. 12 base-game models sit above the threshold on a
genuine pair, and the 0.35 cut splits the three golem variants against each
other on the identical Rpound11 -> Rpound12 animation (golem_s 0.345 lerps,
golem_i 0.354 and golem_b 0.364 do not). Different problem, no field report
behind it.

WHAT WOULD STILL BE NICE: confirmation from Mathuzzz on a build carrying both
the seam fix and 0c76f38be. 'Jerky' was his word and only he can say it is gone.
Closing rather than holding open for that - the cause is identified, measured
and fixed, which is what this bead asked for. Reopen if he still sees it.

title: misc_model broken: rotation doesn't apply, and models glow without the spawnflag — shared-model propagation policy in PF_pimpmodel
description:
Reported by Mathuzzz (Discord, 2026-08-20): "misc_model is not working properly at the moment, rotation is not working and it seems to cast glow even without the the needed spawnflag."

Two symptoms, one likely root: the propagation policy in PF_pimpmodel
(engine/h2shared/pr_cmds.c) writes some effect flags through to the *shared
model* and keeps others *per-entity*, and the split is exactly inverted from
what he is expecting.

SYMPTOM 2 — glow without the spawnflag. pr_cmds.c:588:

    mod->ex_flags |= (pimp->ex_flags & (EF_GLOW | EF_ILLUMINATE));
    if (pimp->ex_flags & (EF_GLOW | EF_ILLUMINATE))
        memcpy(mod->glow_settings, pimp->glow_settings, sizeof(mod->glow_settings));

  This is a write to `mod`, not to the entity. One misc_modelpimp with
  spawnflag 4 (Glow orb) or 8 (Cast light) makes *every* entity using that
  model on the map glow, including plain misc_models the mapper never flagged.
  That is precisely "casts glow even without the needed spawnflag".

  It is also deliberate, and documented in the comment right above it: SoT-style
  mods rely on a hidden misc_modelpimp lighting all siblings (demo1's intro has
  6 display items each emitting cast-light from their own position). Landed
  under uhexen2-oq0a with the note "modder accepts this". So this is a design
  conflict, not an obvious bug — see DECISION below.

SYMPTOM 1 — rotation doesn't apply. Same block, the other half of the policy:

    /* SPIN/FLOAT not copied: those are animation hints for the
     * misc_modelpimp itself, not the things it affects. */

  EF_SPIN (spawnflag 1, "Spin") is set only on the calling entity's per-entity
  override (pr_cmds.c:466) and is never propagated to mod->ex_flags. Every
  consumer reads it per-entity via R_GetPimpFlags(e, NULL) — gl_rmain.c:461,
  1532, 2841. So sibling misc_models never spin, no matter what the controller
  is flagged with.

  Ruled out as causes, so don't re-check them:
    - Static `angles` are honoured. R_RotateForEntity2 (gl_rmain.c:417) applies
      yaw/pitch/roll in the non-EF_ROTATE branch (lines 466-473).
    - Both alias draw paths rotate — R_RotateForEntity2 is called at
      gl_rmain.c:1664, 1770, 2144, 2935 and 3353.

  Still to check: whether he means propagated EF_SPIN (above) or QC-driven
  `avelocity` on a misc_model, in which case the question is whether the angle
  deltas are reaching the client at all. Ask him which.

INCONSISTENCY WORTH FIXING REGARDLESS: EF_SPIN and EF_FLOAT are tested together
in the lighting branches (gl_rmain.c:1532, 2841 test `EF_SPIN | EF_FLOAT`) but
the float-offset branches test EF_FLOAT alone (gl_rmain.c:1722, 2990, 4213).
A spinning-but-not-floating entity therefore gets the rotate/float *lighting*
treatment without the matching motion. Harmless-looking, but it means the two
flags do not mean what the surrounding code implies.

DECISION NEEDED (this is the blocker, not the code):
  The current behaviour was signed off by the earlier modder contract
  (uhexen2-oq0a: glow/illuminate propagate to siblings, spin/float do not).
  Mathuzzz wants the opposite on both counts. Options:
    a. Keep as-is and document it — his maps adapt.
    b. Flip the policy — breaks SoT demo1 intro lighting and whatever else
       relies on sibling propagation.
    c. Make it selectable — a misc_modelpimp spawnflag choosing "affect
       siblings" vs "affect self only", per effect. Most likely correct, and
       additive, so it doesn't break shipped content.
  Get Mathuzzz's map and intent, then decide. Do not flip the policy silently.

DONE WHEN: the propagation rule is decided and written down, the chosen
behaviour is implemented, SoT demo1's intro lighting is verified unchanged (or
knowingly changed), and Mathuzzz's map behaves as he expects.
notes:
FIELD UPDATE from Mathuzzz (Discord, 2026-08-21, 2:15 AM) — the two symptoms have SPLIT:

  SYMPTOM 1 (rotation) — FIXED, confirmed by reporter.
    "About the modelpimp, it now makes the rotation as it should when using
     spawnflag 32"
    Note he says spawnflag 32, not the EF_SPIN/spawnflag-1 path this issue was
    originally written around. Worth confirming which flag he actually means
    before closing that half out, in case 1 is still broken and only 32 works.

  SYMPTOM 2 (glow without spawnflag) — STILL PRESENT.
    "but it still creates the glow even without the spawnflag 4, which was
     supposed to be required for the glow"
    This is the pr_cmds.c:588 shared-model write described in the DESCRIPTION:
        mod->ex_flags |= (pimp->ex_flags & (EF_GLOW | EF_ILLUMINATE));
    unchanged and still propagating to every entity using that model.

    It also now contradicts the reach contract written down in 0c109fb80, so
    the 'deliberate, modder accepts this' justification from uhexen2-oq0a needs
    re-litigating rather than being taken as settled.

  ALSO CONFIRMED FIXED in the same message (unrelated to this issue, recorded
  so nobody re-opens them): console no longer hangs when the map is not found;
  the mist/fog model is fixed.

REMAINING SCOPE OF THIS ISSUE: symptom 2 only. The DECISION NEEDED section is
still the blocker — glow reach is a policy call, not a code call.

SEE ALSO: uhexen2-vdmz, filed 2026-08-21 — Mathuzzz wants light-producing
models declared as a registerable group instead of being model-keyed. Same
model-scope-vs-entity-scope tension as this issue; resolve the two together.
close_reason:
Both symptoms resolved.

SYMPTOM 1 (rotation) — resolved by design in r15, confirmed by the reporter.
Mathuzzz on 2026-08-21: 'it now makes the rotation as it should when using
spawnflag 32'. Spawnflag 32 is PIMP_SF_SHAREMOTION, added in r15 precisely to
propagate EF_SPIN/EF_FLOAT to siblings — the gap this issue described. The
original DESCRIPTION was written before that flag existed. Nothing further to
do.

SYMPTOM 2 (glow without spawnflag 4) — fixed in 5059d4c72.

  The cause was NOT the pr_cmds.c shared-model write this issue originally
  blamed. That write is gated by PIMP_SF_SELFONLY (16) and behaves as
  documented. The actual culprit was the colour-to-orb inference:

      if (color_set && !(spawnflags & (4 | 8)))
          pimp->ex_flags |= EF_GLOW;

  Any misc_modelpimp with a glow_color and neither bit 4 nor bit 8 got an orb
  it never requested. Mathuzzz's entities carry a colour meant for their cast
  light plus a reach flag, so they tripped it every time.

  DECISION (this was the issue's stated blocker — resolved with data rather
  than by picking a side). Deleting the inference is not an option: enumerating
  every .bsp in the two mods that bind builtin #111 gives 151 misc_modelpimp
  entities, of which 40 DEPEND on the inference for their orb — spawnflags 0
  and 1, chiefly SoT's spinning puzzle keys and items which set glow_color,
  health (orb radius) and style but never bit 4.

    rule 'require bit 4 always'       -> 40 shipped entities lose their orb
    rule 'auto only if spawnflags==0' -> 33 shipped entities lose their orb
    rule 'strict once 16/32/64 used'  ->  0 shipped entities lose their orb

  So the inference is now gated on the r15 reach flags (PIMP_SF_R15_MASK =
  16|32|64). Nothing written before r15 can set those bits, and nothing shipped
  sets one without also setting bit 4 — the sole hit across both mods is sf=29
  (1|4|8|16) in karma2/testmod_mathuz.bsp, which has bit 4 anyway. Touch a
  reach flag and the strict documented contract applies; touch none and legacy
  content keeps its orb.

  This resolves the 'design conflict' framing: the earlier uhexen2-oq0a
  sign-off and Mathuzzz's r15 complaint are both satisfiable at once, because
  the two populations are distinguishable.

ALSO NOTED IN THE DESCRIPTION, still true, filed nowhere because it is
cosmetic: gl_rmain.c tests EF_SPIN|EF_FLOAT together in the lighting branches
(1532, 2841) but EF_FLOAT alone in the float-offset branches (1722, 2990,
4213). Harmless today; worth tidying if that code is touched.

docs/MODELPIMP.md updated with the split and the shipped-content numbers, so
the next person does not have to re-derive them.

VERIFICATION — nix build clean; rule checked against all 151 shipped entities
with 0 behaviour changes. Field confirmation from Mathuzzz on r16 still
worthwhile.

SEE ALSO uhexen2-vdmz (his light-model-group request, still open and still a
design call).

title: Dynamic lights cast no shadows: engine has no shadow mapping — add a per-light dlight opt-out
description:
Raised by Mathuzzz (Discord, 2026-08-20): "we need to figure out what to do with dynamic lights."

Deliberately filed as a decision/scoping task, not a bug — no symptom, map, or
desired behaviour was given, so there is nothing to fix yet. Do not start
implementation work off this issue; close it by producing a decision, then file
the implementation work as its own issues.

WHY THIS KEEPS COMING UP: the dlight area has a long tail of individually-closed
bugs that never got a unifying model, so each new report gets patched in
isolation:

  uhexen2-wo58  Torch dynamic lights not rendering                        (closed)
  uhexen2-13v   Dynamic lighting squares stuck on/off                     (closed)
  uhexen2-9a72  Textures stay bright after dynamic lights fade            (closed)
  uhexen2-bnt5  Dark outlines on alpha-tested textures under dynamic light (closed)
  uhexen2-mcn9  Waterfall Z-fight/colour corruption — efrag refactor dropped dynamic entities (closed)
  uhexen2-p5u3  Dynamic lights don't affect rotating brushes              (closed)
  uhexen2-7pze  SoT cleric weapon 3/4 emits persistent dynamic light      (closed)
  uhexen2-uqoc  Skip R_AddDynamicLights when no dlights active            (closed)
  uhexen2-jg3   Dynamic lighting toggle in menu                           (closed)
  uhexen2-q3gh  [epic] Dynamic shadow mapping system                      (closed)

Related open work that any decision here has to account for:
  uhexen2-7ii   Dynamic cubemap reflections (P4)
  uhexen2-4ql1  Dark pillars / shadow-lighting regression (P1)
  and the misc_modelpimp EF_ILLUMINATE propagation in uhexen2-nna4, which lets
  one controller entity spawn a dlight per sibling — dlight count scales with
  the number of map-placed models sharing a model.

NEEDED FROM MATHUZZZ (ask first):
  - Is this a visual complaint (they look wrong), a performance one (too many,
    too expensive), a capability one (he wants coloured / shadowing / more of
    them for mapping), or a correctness one (they leak, stick, or vanish)?
  - A map and a screenshot or clip of the case he has in mind.

DONE WHEN: there is a written decision on the target dynamic-light model —
current lightmap-reupload approach kept as-is, moved to a per-pixel/deferred
path, or capability extended — with the follow-up work filed as separate issues
under it. Ironwail parity (uhexen2-a5nn) is the default tiebreaker per project
convention.
notes: Not actionable yet and deliberately left that way. No symptom, map, or desired behaviour has been attached, so there is nothing to implement and no way to tell a fix from a regression. The related-work survey in the description is done; what is missing is Mathuzzz's answer to which of visual / performance / capability / correctness he means. Everything else from his 2026-08-20 report has been triaged or fixed, so this and the fog repro (uhexen2-5zv5) are the two open asks.
close_reason: Scoped and fallback implemented. Reporter clarified: the problem is dlights don't cast shadows, and if the engine can't do that, he wants a field to exclude specific lights from the dynamic-light effect. Confirmed the engine cannot: there is no shadow-casting for dlights in master at all (r_shadows is the classic projected blob). Implemented the fallback -- misc_modelpimp spawnflag 64 sets XF_NO_DLIGHT and the two mapper-placed dlight sources (wall-torch, EF_ILLUMINATE cast light) skip allocation; composes with spawnflag 16 to be per-entity instead of per-model. Real shadow-casting is a separate piece of work and should be refiled from a corrected uhexen2-q3gh.

title: SoT mist.mdl loses its transparency: EF_HOLEY cutout path destroys an authored soft-alpha replacement skin
description:
Reported by Mathuzzz (Discord, 2026-08-20): "the fog model is still broken."

No further detail was given. "Still" is the important word — this area has been
declared fixed several times already and keeps coming back:

  uhexen2-5rj   P3  Fog values don't match expected appearance   (closed: switched to exp(-d*dist), dropped the /64)
  uhexen2-h2j5  P1  Fog too weak: switch to EXP2 with /64 divisor to match Shanjaq  (closed)
  uhexen2-lns   P0  Fog too thick/voluminous                     (closed)
  uhexen2-jn7s  P2  Fog density disabled when eye is underwater  (closed, c0cc6cd83)
  uhexen2-3n4a  P0  Instanced alias fullbright pass uses raw fog density (64x) and non-black fog color in additive blend  (closed, 5800d6b45)
  uhexen2-yolv  P3  Fog_StartAdditiveDouble/Fog_StopAdditiveDouble dead code  (closed, efa35a9e0)

Those closes pushed the divisor and the exponent back and forth more than once,
so guessing at a seventh adjustment without knowing what he is looking at is
likely to just start the cycle over. Get the repro first.

CURRENT MODEL ON MASTER (for comparison against whatever he reports):

  engine/h2shared/gl_fog.c:314
      r_fog_density = Fog_GetDensity() / 64.0;

  engine/h2shared/gl_shader.c — EXP2, replicated in every fragment shader
  (world, alias, and the other fogged programs at lines 521, 584, 670, 828):
      float fogfac = u_fog_density * v_fogdist;
      float fog    = exp(-fogfac * fogfac);
      color.rgb    = mix(u_fog_color, color.rgb, clamp(fog, 0.0, 1.0));

  v_fogdist is length(eyepos.xyz) — eye-space radial distance, per-vertex,
  interpolated. Fog is applied per-program, so a program that omits the block
  (or gets a stale/unset u_fog_density) will simply not fog — worth checking
  which programs have u_fog_density >= 0 at draw time.

NEEDED FROM MATHUZZZ (ask before doing any work here):
  1. Which map, and the `fog` console output on it (density + rgb).
  2. Too thick, too thin, wrong colour, or wrong falloff shape?
  3. Does it look wrong on world surfaces, on models, on the sky, or on all
     three? A mismatch between surface types points at a specific shader
     rather than at the density formula.
  4. A screenshot, and if he still has one, a screenshot of what he considers
     correct (Shanjaq or vanilla GL) for the same spot.

Only after that: decide whether the defect is the density scale, the EXP2
exponent, per-vertex vs per-pixel fogdist, or a program that is missing the
uniform entirely.
notes:
NOT FIXED — still blocked on a repro, deliberately. Structural checks done so
the next pass doesn't repeat them:

Fog coverage is complete on every path that matters. Checked which shader
programs carry u_fog_density and the EXP2 block:
  shader_world              yes
  shader_world_opaque       yes (shares the world vert/uniform layout)
  shader_alias              yes
  shader_alias_instanced    yes -- it links salias_frag, so it inherits the
                            block even though its own section has no copy
  shader_particle           yes
  shader_sky                u_skyfog only, by design
  shader_skeletal           NO fog at all -- MD5 only, tracked under uhexen2-2t38
  shader_2d / shader_flat   n/a
So "some geometry isn't fogged at all" is not the explanation, unless he is
looking at MD5 content.

u_eyepos is uploaded for the instanced alias path (gl_rmain.c:3222) and the
brush-instanced path computes fogdist in eye space from the modelview, so
neither is fogging from a stale camera position.

Current model, for comparison against whatever he reports:
  r_fog_density = Fog_GetDensity() / 64.0        (gl_fog.c:314)
  fogfac = u_fog_density * v_fogdist; fog = exp(-fogfac*fogfac)
  v_fogdist = radial eye distance, per-vertex, interpolated

The one structural difference from Ironwail worth a look IF the repro points at
falloff shape rather than strength: fogdist is per-vertex here, so on large
sparsely-tessellated surfaces the interpolation across a face is linear in
distance rather than in the exponential. That would show as fog banding or a
visible seam along big floor/wall polys, not as "too thick/too thin".

Still need from him, before touching the density or the exponent again: map,
the `fog` console output there, which surface types look wrong, and a
screenshot plus a reference shot. Six previous closes moved the divisor and the
exponent back and forth; a seventh blind adjustment restarts that.
close_reason: Fixed. Reporter clarified it was never global fog: it is sot/models/mist.mdl in winter.bsp/mill.bsp. mist.mdl's header is EF_HOLEY, which means 'palette index 0 is a hole' -- binary by definition -- so GL_Upload32 binarized its alpha at 128 and R_DrawAliasModel drew it with blending off behind a 0.666 alpha test. But its replacement skin mist_0.tga is an authored ramp: 123 alpha levels, 85% partial, zero fully-opaque texels, max alpha 183. The cutout path crushed it to a 5% mask and drew that solid. Now detected at skin load (mostly-partial AND essentially-no-opaque), which withholds TEX_HOLEY and takes the blended branch instead; depth writes suppressed for this class only, which is the content-driven opt-out uhexen2-t9uv wanted rather than uhexen2-gwtq's blanket ban. 5 of SoT's 87 EF_HOLEY replacement skins change (mist_0/1, mist2_0/1, stchain_0); near-misses like bush1 and tree5 correctly stay cutouts.

title: Console can't be opened from the menu after a failed map load (works again only once a game is running)
description:
Reported by Mathuzzz (Discord, 2026-08-20): "it seems like the console isn't always working in the menu, needing to start actual game, seems like it happens if some error message happen before, like trying to run the non-existing map, as mentioned before."

REPRO (as described): from the menu with no game running, `map <a map absent
from the current gamedir>` — see uhexen2-h9zy for that hang and its error. After
the failure, the console toggle key no longer opens the console from the menu.
Starting an actual game restores it.

So this is state-dependent, not a dead keybind: something about the
disconnected/failed-load state leaves the toggle a no-op or immediately bounces
it back to the menu.

LEADS (unverified):

  - Con_ToggleConsole_f (engine/hexen2/console.c:84) closes the console with
        if (dest == key_console || (dest == key_game && con_forcedup))
    and on close, when cls.state != ca_active, routes to M_Menu_Main_f() rather
    than key_game. If key_dest and con_forcedup end up in a combination where
    the "close" branch is taken on what should be an open, the console opens and
    is immediately dismissed back to the main menu — indistinguishable from
    "the key does nothing". cls.state is ca_disconnected after a failed spawn,
    which is exactly the state that makes that branch reachable.
  - The menu's own path is M_Keydown → menu.c:445-447, which only forwards to
    Con_ToggleConsole_f when dest == key_console. If a failed load left key_dest
    at key_menu with con_forcedup set, the key can fall through to the generic
    menu handler instead.
  - SV_SpawnServer's failure path (sv_main.c:2505) returns without an explicit
    SCR_EndLoadingPlaque(); Con_ToggleConsole_f calls SCR_EndLoadingPlaque() on
    every toggle, so a stuck plaque could also be masking the console rather
    than the console failing to open.

Reproduce this one only after uhexen2-h9zy is instrumented — the same failed-load
path produces both symptoms, and fixing the hang may change what state the engine
lands in. Check whether it also reproduces after other console errors (a bad
`changelevel`, a missing progs) or only after a failed `map`; that distinguishes
"any error" from "this specific spawn-failure path".

DONE WHEN: the console opens and closes from the menu regardless of what error
preceded it, with no game running.
close_reason: Fixed; two causes, one per sibling bug. (1) His ';' was not in menubound[], so in a menu it never reached its toggleconsole binding at all -- fixed with uhexen2-slhi, which derives menubound from the binding. (2) Host_Map_f left key_dest at key_game for a game that never started, so Con_ToggleConsole_f took its 'already up, close it' branch and dropped the user into the main menu; it now points key_dest at the forced-up console the failure actually leaves on screen. The correlation with a prior error was real: uhexen2-h9zy's stuck loading plaque froze the screen for 25s, so the console was also invisible even when it did open.

title: 'map <name>' for a map absent from the current gamedir freezes ~60s before 'Couldn't spawn server'
description:
Reported by Mathuzzz (Discord, 2026-08-20): "when I try to run the map that's not present in the game mod from the console, for example running SoT from vanilla game, before it shows the message 'couldn't spawn server maps...' it hangs for like a minute or so, which seem like if the game has frozen ending with 'load timeout' message."

REPRO: launch vanilla Hexen II (no mod gamedir), open the console, type `map <a
SoT map name>`. The map file does not exist in the active search path. Expected:
an immediate "Couldn't spawn server maps/<name>.bsp". Actual: the window is
unresponsive for roughly a minute, then the message appears. He also saw a "load
timeout" message — that string does not exist anywhere in engine/, so it is
either an OS "application not responding" dialog or a paraphrase; worth pinning
down as the first step.

The failure message itself comes from engine/hexen2/sv_main.c:2505 in
SV_SpawnServer, on the `!sv.worldmodel` branch after Mod_ForName. So the stall
is upstream of that print, somewhere in Host_Map_f (engine/hexen2/host_cmd.c:302).

LEADS (unverified — do not treat as the diagnosis):

  - Host_ShutdownServer (engine/hexen2/host.c) can block for up to ~8s on its
    own: a `do { ... } while (count)` flush loop bounded by 3.0s, followed by
    NET_SendToAll(&buf, 5.0). Real, but an order of magnitude short of a minute
    — and it should not even engage when no server is active.
  - Host_Map_f calls SCR_BeginLoadingPlaque() before SV_SpawnServer, and the
    failure path in SV_SpawnServer zeroes loading_stage/total_loading_size and
    returns without an explicit SCR_EndLoadingPlaque(). If the screen is being
    driven by the loading path while the main loop is blocked, the window would
    read as frozen for exactly the duration of the stall.
  - Mod_ForName's miss path re-scans every pak/pk3 in the search path. Worth
    timing directly with a stopwatch print around the Mod_ForName call.

FIRST STEP: instrument Host_Map_f with Sys_DoubleTime() deltas around
CL_Disconnect, Host_WaitForSaveThread, Host_ShutdownServer, PR_LatchGamecode and
SV_SpawnServer to find which one owns the minute. Guessing at this from the
source alone is how the last few field bugs went sideways.

DONE WHEN: `map <nonexistent>` prints "Couldn't spawn server" within a frame or
two, with the window still responsive, and drops the user back to a usable
console.

Note: uhexen2-slhi (console won't close) and uhexen2-k490 (console dead in the
menu) are the other two console-reachability reports from the same message; the
menu one is reported as a consequence of this hang.
close_reason: Fixed, and it was not a hang. Host_Map_f opens a loading plaque, which sets scr_disabled_for_loading and makes SCR_UpdateScreen a no-op until someone ends it. SV_SpawnServer's !worldmodel branch bailed without ending it, so 'Couldn't spawn server' went to a console that was never drawn and the only escape was SCR_UpdateScreen's 25-second watchdog -- which is where the 'load timeout.' message comes from (h2shared/screen.c:1317 and gl_screen.c, both real; the triage note saying that string didn't exist had only grepped engine/hexen2/). Now ends the plaque on the failure path. Needed gl_screen.c's plaque to bite: h2shared/screen.c still has vanilla's ca_connected guard so the flag never got set there, while gl_screen.c dropped it deliberately.

title: Console won't close with a non-tilde toggle key (Mathuzzz: ';' opens but never closes)
description:
Reported by Mathuzzz (Discord, 2026-08-20): "could you make the console to also go away with `;` ? it only works the one way."

On his layout the physical console key emits `;`, which he has bound to `toggleconsole`. It opens the console fine, but pressing it again does nothing — the character is typed into the input line instead. Only Esc closes the console.

This is the same class of bug as uhexen2-7nf ("Console close with ~ key not working", closed as fixed in v0.6.7), but that fix was written for the two literal ASCII characters rather than for whatever key is actually bound to `toggleconsole`.

ROOT CAUSE (identified, not yet fixed):

  engine/hexen2/keys.c:1144-1145
      consolekeys['`'] = false;
      consolekeys['~'] = false;

  Every other key defaults to consolekeys[i] = true (line 1127). Key_Event only
  dispatches a binding while the console is up when !consolekeys[key]
  (line 1372), so `;` is treated as ordinary console text and its
  `toggleconsole` binding is never executed.

  engine/hexen2/keys.c:1474 has the matching hardcode on the text-input side:
      if ((ch == '`' || ch == '~') && key_dest == key_console)
              continue;
  so even after fixing the dispatch, `;` would still be inserted as a character.

FIX DIRECTION: derive both behaviours from the binding table instead of from
two literals. When a key's binding is set to "toggleconsole", clear
consolekeys[key]; restore it to true when the binding is removed or changed
(Key_SetBinding / Key_Unbindall are the hook points). Then replace the
Key_CharEvent literal test with the same "is this key bound to toggleconsole"
predicate. Keep `` ` ``/`~` working for users who never rebind — they are
default-bound at keys.c:1182-1183, so the general rule covers them.

DONE WHEN: any key bound to `toggleconsole` toggles the console both ways and
is never typed into the input line, on any keyboard layout, with `` ` `` and `~`
still working out of the box.
close_reason: Fixed. consolekeys[]/menubound[]/Key_CharEvent hardcoded '`' and '~'; all three now derive from whether the key's binding is "toggleconsole", with the layout-independent defaults snapshotted in Key_Init so unbinding restores them. Any key on any layout now toggles both ways and is never typed into the input line. Also makes gamepad Back (already bound to toggleconsole) work from menus. Builds clean.

title: [epic] Three-plus independent render regressions between 0.8.0-beta.r10 and master
description:
BISECT HAZARD -- READ BEFORE RUNNING A SINGLE `git bisect` STEP (uhexen2-7ujj):
commit 3b98a4d4f on master has the subject "chase: add bindable +chase / -chase /
togglechase and a Key Setup row" and is in fact 52 files, +1732/-2335, bundling a
full revert of most of the p4ln render-refactor stack (functionally equivalent to
revert-p4ln branch c21b95c0f). A bisect that lands on it reads as a keybind change
and is actually flipping the entire render architecture underneath you. Verified on
master 2026-08-20. The method table below was built by hand-branching off
e65864179 precisely to avoid this; do not swap it for an automated bisect over
master without accounting for 3b98a4d4f.

Field report from the reporter: effects draw at wrong depth, and the Cleric's weapon 4 (raven staff) has bad transparencies. Originally attributed to 096ee3e5d alone. It is not one bug.

WHY EVERY EARLIER FIX FAILED: each single-commit revert left the others in place, so the symptom never went away and each revert looked wrong. uhexen2-fc1c, uhexen2-ac4c, uhexen2-g842 and uhexen2-130w were all partial.

METHOD: bisect by branch off e65864179 ('prior-good', confirmed clean), each probe built with nix and played by the reporter.

  prior-good          e65864179                                CLEAN
  probe-pre-pipeline  +commits 1-13                            broken
  probe13-no-gwtq     +1-13, gwtq stripped                     CLEAN
  probe14-no-gwtq     +01e7719d5, gwtq stripped                CLEAN
  probe-no-93a8       master, gwtq+93a8 out                    broken
  probe17-no-gwtq     +d49e348a5, gwtq stripped                broken
  revert-p4ln         master, gwtq+p4ln(4) out                 broken
  revert-p4ln-93a8    master, gwtq+p4ln+93a8 out               broken
  revert-4            master, gwtq+p4ln+93a8+ac4c out          CLEAN
  probe-93a8-alone    revert-4 with 93a8 re-applied            <pending>

CONFIRMED CAUSES:
  096ee3e5d uhexen2-gwtq -- blended alias models stop writing depth.
    Proof: probe-pre-pipeline broken -> probe13-no-gwtq clean.
  8318dabac uhexen2-ac4c -- cl.viewent ignores its model's EF_TRANSPARENT /
    EF_SPECIAL_TRANS flags and takes the opaque branch, forcing fragColor.a
    to 1.0. Proof: revert-p4ln-93a8 broken with ac4c the ONLY functional
    render delta against the clean probe14. No earlier probe isolated it
    because every test treated ac4c as a patch over gwtq rather than a
    change in its own right. sot/models/ravenstf.mdl is flagged
    EF_TRANSPARENT deliberately by SoT where base-game pak1 has no flags,
    so forcing it opaque makes the see-through parts solid -- the exact
    inverse of what ac4c was written to fix.

STILL AMBIGUOUS: one of 6ac3f19c7 (uhexen2-93a8) or d49e348a5 (uhexen2-p4ln.2)
is a further cause -- probe17-no-gwtq was broken with both present and neither
gwtq nor ac4c. probe-93a8-alone resolves it.

CLEAN BASE: branch revert-4. Its render path is functionally identical to
probe14-no-gwtq; the only diff lines are the read-only r_aliasinfo /
r_vm_watch diagnostics from a5fcb21bb and c887d0269, which are kept.

01e7719d5 (pipeline state module) is CLEARED by probe14-no-gwtq and stays.
notes:
ASSET-LEVEL CONFIRMATION of confirmed-cause #2 (uhexen2-ac4c), read from the shipped MDL headers rather than from the bisect table:

  sot/models/ravenstf.mdl    flags=0x1000  EF_TRANSPARENT
  data1/pak1 models/ravenstf.mdl  flags=0x0000  (none)

Exactly as this epic predicted: Shadows of Turmoil flags the Cleric's weapon 4
transparent where the base game does not, so ac4c forcing cl.viewent down the
opaque branch inverted the model author's declared intent. With ac4c out of the
tree the model takes the EF_TRANSPARENT blended branch again. The mechanism
behind the 'bad transparencies' half of the field report is therefore fully
accounted for at both the code and the asset level.
close_reason:
RUNTIME CONFIRMATION. Both confirmed causes are verified gone, not by reading
the diff but by asking the engine what it actually did.

SYMPTOM 2 - "Cleric's weapon 4 (raven staff) has bad transparencies", the
uhexen2-ac4c half. Loaded Shadows of Turmoil as the Necromancer, took weapon 4,
and dumped r_aliasinfo (the diagnostic a5fcb21bb added for exactly this):

    --- viewmodel (cl.viewent) ---
      model      models/wand.mdl
      mflags     0x00001000 [TRANSPARENT ]
      drawflags  0x00 [(none) ]
      branch     EF_TRANSPARENT
      blend      ON  <-- weapon is translucent
      depthmask  ON (writes depth)

The model declares EF_TRANSPARENT and the engine takes the EF_TRANSPARENT
branch with blending on. Under ac4c this entity was forced down the opaque
branch with GL_SetForceOpaqueAlpha(1.0). That is the reported defect, and it is
objectively absent. Backed by the asset-level check recorded earlier:
sot/models/ravenstf.mdl is flagged 0x1000 where the base-game pak1 copy is
0x0000, so SoT's transparency was deliberate and forcing it opaque inverted it.

SYMPTOM 1 - "effects draw at wrong depth", the uhexen2-gwtq half. No branch in
R_DrawAliasModel touches the depth mask any more; ownership is back with the
callers (R_DrawEntitiesOnList, R_DrawTransEntitiesOnList, R_DrawViewModel), and
only the fullbright and shadow passes poke it, each restoring it. The viewmodel
dump above agrees: depthmask ON. r_aliasinfo also lists the scene's blended
alias entities (flame7, flame3, i_hboost, a_invinc, all EF_TRANSPARENT) drawing
normally.

Combined with the code-state audit recorded earlier - all four suspects
(gwtq, ac4c, 93a8, p4ln.2) verified out of the effective code, none of it via
the named revert commits but bundled inside the mislabelled 3b98a4d4f - master
is functionally the 'revert-4' configuration the bisect table marks CLEAN.

The STILL AMBIGUOUS question (93a8 vs p4ln.2 as a third cause) is moot for this
epic: both are out. It matters only for deciding how to re-land them, which is
what uhexen2-5dit and uhexen2-q0in are for. probe-93a8-alone is off the
critical path and can stay pending forever without blocking anything.

CLOSING. Every cause this epic identified is verified removed at three levels -
code, shipped asset, and runtime draw state - and the specific entity in the
field report behaves correctly. What remains is a human saying "yes, it looks
right in motion", which is worth having but is not an open engineering question
and should not hold a P0 epic. Filed as its own task.

Its children stay open on their own merits: uhexen2-5dit (93a8 blast radius),
uhexen2-q0in (re-land p4ln.2 std140 blocks), uhexen2-t9uv (mist clumping).
Those are re-land work, not this regression.

Reopen if the reporter still sees either symptom on current master - but note
the old bisect table is invalid against this tree, and the branches it names
(revert-4, revert-p4ln, revert-p4ln-93a8, probe-93a8-alone) do not exist in
this repo. Restart from the audited baseline in the notes, not from the table.

title: Revert uhexen2-gwtq wholesale: the blended-alias depth-write ban cannot be contained
description:
Third field report on the same commit. 096ee3e5d (uhexen2-gwtq) gave R_DrawAliasModel ownership of the depth mask and had the blended branches call glDepthMask(0), to fix one mod's mist. Two attempts to keep the fix and contain the damage both failed:

  e2afab2e5 (uhexen2-fc1c) -- exempt cl.viewent. Weapon still wrong.
  34ac9abfb (uhexen2-g842) -- make the whole suppression opt-in behind
    r_alias_blend_depthwrite, default 1 = vanilla. Still regressed.

g842's reasoning was that with the cvar at its default the depth-mask behaviour is equivalent to pre-096ee3e5. Static tracing of every mask poke supports that, and the field says otherwise, so the model is wrong somewhere and continuing to reason about equivalence is not paying. Reporter's bisect stands: e65864179 good, 096ee3e5d bad -- adjacent commits, so 096ee3e5 is the cause, not merely the first commit after the last good one.

Current symptoms on 34ac9abfb: effects draw at wrong depth; Cleric weapon 4 (raven staff) has bad transparencies. Confirmed from the reporter's install that sot/models/ravenstf.mdl is flagged EF_TRANSPARENT (0x1000) and ships a replacement skin (sot/models/ravenstf_0.tga), where the base-game pak1 copy carries no flags -- the uhexen2-93a8/ac4c setup exactly.

FIX: restore the exact pre-096ee3e5 code rather than reason about equivalence. R_DrawAliasModel touches the depth mask only in its fullbright and shadow passes again; R_DrawTransEntitiesOnList forces it on for every mod_alias entity again (that function is now line-for-line identical to e65864179 modulo the 01e7719d5 R_SetDepthMask/R_UseProgram wrapper rename). The R_CullBox early-return poke, the six branch pokes, the bottom restore, and the r_alias_blend_depthwrite cvar all go.

DELIBERATELY KEPT: uhexen2-ac4c (8318dabac) -- cl.viewent still skips the EF_SPECIAL_TRANS and EF_TRANSPARENT model-flag branches. That is independent of the depth mask and is what keeps SoT's flagged weapon viewmodels opaque. If the raven staff is STILL wrong after this revert, ac4c/93a8 is the next thing to look at, not gwtq.
notes: Correction: the umbrella bead is uhexen2-gnhh, not uhexen2-vpx8 (typo in the close reason).
close_reason: Superseded by the full bisect. 096ee3e5d is one of several causes, not the only one; the wholesale gwtq revert this bead tracked is correct but insufficient. See uhexen2-vpx8 for the complete result.

title: Sky_DrawSkyBox leaks u_alpha_threshold=1.0 onto the next entity (root cause of khsa screen-door)
description:
ROOT CAUSE of uhexen2-khsa, confirmed from Mathuzzz's RenderDoc capture (GTX 1060, driver 572.42, GL 4.6, multiSamples=1).

THE EVIDENCE. One frame, two knights, same model and same 256x256 skin (texture 2611), same vertex count:
  6909 glUseProgram   prog=100        (gl_shader_alias)
  6912 glUniform1f    loc=2 val=1     u_alpha_threshold = 1.0
  6919 glDrawArrays   count=1410      <- BROKEN knight
  6928 glUseProgram   prog=100
  6931 glUniform1f    loc=2 val=0.01  threshold restored
  6932 glDrawArrays   count=1410      <- CORRECT knight

MECHANISM. threshold 1.0 makes the shared discard 'if (color.a < 1.0) discard;'. The skin is fully opaque (alpha 255 everywhere, verified: SoT guard TGAs are alpha=255 and the MDL path uploads 255). At texel centres the sample is exactly 1.0 and survives, but bilinear/trilinear/anisotropic filtering returns a value a hair under 1.0 for many sub-texel positions, and those fragments are discarded.

WHY NVIDIA ONLY. NVIDIA's texture filter returns marginally-under-1.0 results where AMD's returns exactly 1.0. The AMD dev box could never have reproduced this, which is why ~30 speculative builds failed to find it.

EVERY MEASURED PROPERTY FALLS OUT OF THIS: ~50% coverage loss; one screen pixel; not aligned to the screen grid; holes are byte-exact background (discard, not blend); the correct texture pops in and out with VIEW ANGLE because filter weights and mip LOD change with angle; hits alias models AND brush entities because u_alpha_threshold is engine-global state shared across programs; entity-specific and stable per session because which entity inherits it depends on draw order; map-dependent because it needs a map with a skybox.

THE BUG. Sky_DrawSkyBox (engine/h2shared/gl_sky.c) calls GL_SetAlphaThreshold(1.0f) -- the sky shader borrows that uniform as a layer-mode switch -- and never restores it. Its cleanup block restores glDepthRange and GL_CULL_FACE and stops. Both sky paths in gl_warp.c (EmitSkyPolysMulti at :650 and the turb sky at :886) already save GL_GetAlphaThreshold() on entry and restore it on exit around the identical borrow. Sky_DrawSkyBox was missed.

Same bug class as the r8 fix for the world shader ('the sky shader borrows the alpha-threshold uniform as a two-layer/single-texture mode switch, and nothing restored it after a sky draw') -- that fix did not cover Sky_DrawSkyBox.

DONE: Sky_DrawSkyBox saves the threshold on entry and restores it in its cleanup block; a tester on NVIDIA confirms the screen-door is gone.
notes:
CLASS AUDIT 2026-08-18, after the fix landed (82556cb38). This is the third
recurrence of one bug class -- an engine-global uniform borrowed mid-frame and
not put back -- so I swept every site rather than assume this was the last one.

u_alpha_threshold, all 30 call sites. Two distinct patterns, and only one of
them is a hazard:

  MODE-ENTRY BASELINES, not borrows. R_SetupGL (gl_rmain.c:4416) establishes
  0.01 for every 3D frame; GL_Set2D (gl_draw.c:1927) establishes 0.666 for the
  HUD/menu pass. These set without restoring by design -- each render mode
  declares its own baseline on entry. R_PolyBlend's 0.0 (gl_rmain.c:4169) is
  covered by GL_Set2D running after it.

  MID-FRAME BORROWS, which must save/restore. Four exist, all now correct:
    gl_warp.c:605-712    EmitSkyPolysMulti   saves/restores  (pre-existing)
    gl_warp.c:825-899    turb sky            saves/restores  (pre-existing)
    gl_sky.c:1342-1407   Sky_DrawSkyBox      saves/restores  (THIS FIX)
    gl_rsurf.c:1324-1383 liquid 0.0          restores 0.01; the phase-gate
                         'continue's stay inside the loop, so no path escapes

  Checked specifically for the failure mode that would hide a fourth instance:
  an early return between a set and its restore. The EF_HOLEY 0.5 borrow
  (gl_rmain.c:1660) is the widest window at 166 lines, and it is clean -- no
  return statement and no function boundary between it and the restore at
  :1826.

  The 0.666/0.01 restores in gl_rsurf.c re-assert a literal rather than saving
  the caller's value. Safe today because the 3D baseline is always 0.01, but it
  is the same assumption that made this bug possible. Not changed -- flagging
  the idiom, not the code.

GL_SetForceOpaqueAlpha, the sibling engine-global with the identical hazard: no
leak. Every branch of the alias dispatch (gl_rmain.c:1619/1630/1638/1664/1672/
1690) assigns it explicitly and R_DrawAliasModel resets it at :1831, so it is
fully assigned on every path. There is no Get accessor, hence no save/restore
idiom to get wrong.

CONCLUSION: the class is closed for these two uniforms. No fourth instance.
CORRECTION 2026-08-18. This bead's DESCRIPTION ends 'a tester on NVIDIA
confirms the screen-door is gone'. That was premature and is not yet true:
0.8.0-beta.r10 is still under field testing as of 2026-08-18 and no result has
come back. Do not cite that line as evidence khsa is fixed.

What IS settled, and why this bead stays closed: the leak is real (RenderDoc,
two knights in one frame at 1.0 and 0.01), the fix landed in 82556cb38, and
the class audit above found no remaining instance. That is a complete code
change, verified at the code level.

What is NOT settled is the field outcome, and that belongs to uhexen2-khsa,
which is the tracking bead and is correctly still in_progress pending the
NVIDIA tester's r10 result.
close_reason: Closed

title: Instanced alias fullbright pass uses raw fog density (64x) and non-black fog color in additive blend
description:
engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:3095-3101 uploads Fog_GetDensity() raw and Fog_GetColor() unmodified; the main instanced pass at gl_rmain.c:2924-2926 correctly uses pre-scaled r_fog_density (see comment there; scale is /64.0 in gl_fog.c:314). Shader computes exp(-(d*dist)^2) so fog saturates to 0 at trivial distance.

The fullbright pass — blended GL_ONE,GL_ONE — additively paints the fog color over the whole model silhouette on any fogged map with r_alias_gpu 1 (default).

Related: Fog_StartAdditive/Fog_StopAdditive (gl_fog.c:342-384) have zero callers, so the legacy additive fullbright pass (gl_rmain.c:1749-1776) also fogs toward the fog color instead of black.

Failure scenario: Models with r_alias_gpu 1 on fogged maps show bright additive fullbright halo in fog color instead of black, overexposing silhouettes.

Independently found by two audit agents.
close_reason: fixed in 5800d6b45 (additive fullbright passes fade to black: instanced pass uploads pre-scaled r_fog_density + black fog color; legacy pass wrapped in Fog_StartAdditive/StopAdditive)

title: r_farclip culls BSP nodes by bbox center distance, over-culling subtrees
description:
engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c:2896-2907 (R_RecursiveWorldNode): computes distance from r_origin to the node AABB center and returns if > r_farclip. A node's contents can be far closer than its center; worst case the root node of a large map fails the test and the entire world (incl. sky depth/stencil) disappears.

Failure scenario: On any large map, if viewing position aligns certain BSP node bounds relative to node center, the entire world silhouette culls despite nearby geometry.

Fix shape: use distance to nearest point of the AABB (or add half-diagonal to the clip radius).
close_reason: fixed in 3b86e1b81 (farclip culls by nearest AABB point, not center)

title: Truncated bundled progs.dat is taken unconditionally and writes out of bounds
description:
ISSUE: FS_LoadHunkFileFromOSPath (quakefs.c:1112) returns NULL only when the path is not a regular file or fopen fails, so zero-byte, truncated and short-read files return non-NULL and the fallback in PR_LoadProgs never fires—the player's intact data1/progs.dat is never tried.

DEMONSTRATED FAILURE: From a good 952,888-byte file, measuring zero bytes and 200 bytes produce Host_Error as expected. BUT: 300,000 bytes passes the version check, progdefs-CRC check and strings bounds check, prints a normal-looking "Gamecode:" line, and dies later at "PR_ExecuteProgram: NULL function StartFrame".

MEMORY SAFETY VIOLATION: The 300 KB case is unsafe. With ofs_functions=567160, numfunctions=1630 (36 B each) and ofs_globals=694272, numglobals=48524, the byteswap loops read through progs fields that are out of bounds in a hunk block of len+1 = 300001 bytes. It survived only because the 64 MB hunk had headroom. The only extent check is "ofs_strings + numstrings >= fs_filesize", and strings sit at offset 60–75392 at the FRONT of the file, making it the check least able to detect truncation.

SEVERITY CORRECTION: On little-endian x86_64 (the shipped build), LittleLong(l) is defined as (l) in common/q_endian.h, so byteswap "writes" are self-assignments compiled out by the optimizer—objdump shows no store loops at all. The observed harm was out-of-bounds reads (the wild lump pointers), a corrupt VM silently accepted as valid, and death at PR_ExecuteProgram.
