The OOB write hazard is real but conditional: it materializes on big-endian, at -O0, or under a compiler that does not elide self-assignment. The fix is correct either way; the urgency rests on the crashes and the silent acceptance of corrupt code, not on a guaranteed write on the current platform.

REACHABILITY: Partial unzip, interrupted download, AV quarantine, disk-full, or packaging slip. Note the asymmetry: before this feature the only truncatable progs was the player's own; now the engine prefers a PACKAGING-CONTROLLED file over a known-good one.

FIX HAS TWO PARTS:
(a) Validate a bundled progs and fall back rather than escalate to Host_Error.
(b) Make the lump extent checks in PR_LoadProgs actually cover everything the byteswap loops read—this is PRE-EXISTING and reachable through a corrupt player progs.dat today, so fixing only (a) would leave a real hole while appearing to close it.

STATUS: Fixed in commit 9f52d0a6a.
close_reason:
BOTH HALVES LANDED. Part (b) — making the extent checks actually cover the lumps — was done fully rather than deferred, and the same helper covers the player's own file, so the pre-existing exposure is closed too.

IMPLEMENTATION: new PR_LumpFits() (pr_edict.c:2220), an overflow-safe "does count × elemsize at ofs fit in filelen", written as a division so neither the multiply nor the addition can overflow on an unvetted header. New PR_CheckProgsExtents() (:2247) byteswaps the header into a local copy — so it can run before PR_LoadProgs commits to an image — and checks statements, globaldefs, fielddefs, functions, globals and strings at the element size the file's own version implies (v6 defs 8 / v7 12; v6 stmts 8 / v7 16, the widths PR_ConvertV6Defs and PR_ConvertV6Stmts read through). Defined outside the !H2W guard so both paths share it.

Bundled path (:2336): Hunk_LowMark before the load; on a failed open OR a failed extent check it prints the file and the reason, Hunk_FreeToLowMark's, sets progs = NULL and falls through to FS_LoadHunkFile. Main path (:2378): same check, Host_Error on failure, placed before the header byteswap — which is itself a write through progs. The old ofs_strings + numstrings >= fs_filesize check was removed, its strict >= semantics preserved inside the helper rather than loosened to the uniform "fits" rule.

MEASURED, before vs after (bwrap, whole filesystem read-only except the test root):

| bundle | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| good (888,368 B) | loads bundle, crc 10626 | unchanged |
| 0 bytes | Host_Error: unsupported version (0…) | Ignoring bundled …: file is 0 bytes, too short for a 60 byte header → falls back |
| 200 bytes | Host_Error: strings go past end of file | Ignoring bundled …: statements go past end of file → falls back |
| 300,000 bytes | normal Gamecode: line, ~590 KB OOB writes, dies at NULL function StartFrame | Ignoring bundled …: statements go past end of file → falls back |
| mode 000 | fell back silently | now names the reason |

Identical on h2ded and the GL client. Provenance stays honest — every fallback reports the file that actually loaded (crc 17499, retail), the good case reports the bundle (crc 10626).

PART (b) PROVEN INDEPENDENTLY, with no bundle present and the player's own data1/progs.dat truncated: at 300,000 bytes, before the fix the engine printed a normal Gamecode: line and then died at NULL function StartFrame — i.e. the out-of-bounds writes had already happened; after, it Host_Error's at the extent check before anything writes. This is the half that was reachable today by a corrupt player file and predates the bundled-gamecode feature entirely.

title: DropBackpack builds a bag then deletes it when the drop is mana/health only (total==0)
description:
Found while investigating uhexen2-hwky ("Bad backpack!"). This is a SEPARATE and more damaging defect on the same code path: it destroys loot silently, with no console message at all.

MECHANISM (gamecode/hc/h2/items.hc, DropBackpack):

"total" counts artifacts and FULL (==20) armor pieces only -- it never counts bluemana, greenmana or spawn_health (those are copied to the item at 1564-1566, after accumulation).

The four single-item conditions at 1586-1589 each require the OTHER instant items to be zero:
  (total==1 && !blue && !green && !health) || (total==0 && blue && !green && !health)
  || (total==0 && !blue && green && !health) || (total==0 && !blue && !green && health)

So a drop holding TWO OR MORE of {bluemana, greenmana, spawn_health} and no artifacts/full armor matches none of them, and falls to the multi-item bag branch at 1716. That branch correctly builds a real backpack -- setmodel models/bag.mdl, setsize, HULL_POINT, BackpackTouch, 120s SUB_Remove -- and then immediately runs:

    if (!total)          // items.hc:1730
    {
        remove(item);
        return;
    }

total is still 0 because mana and health never contributed to it, so the bag it just finished building is deleted. The player gets nothing and there is no dprint, so this is invisible even under "developer 1".

DESTROYED CASES (zero artifacts and zero full armor):
  - bluemana AND greenmana
  - bluemana AND spawn_health
  - greenmana AND spawn_health
  - all three

WHO HITS IT:

1. PLAYERS (allplay.hc:462-463, deathmatch || coop). Any player dying while carrying both mana types and no artifacts / no full armor piece drops nothing. Carrying some of both manas is the normal state, so this is not an edge case.

2. MONSTERS via MonsterDropStuff (items.hc:1247). CLASS_GRUNT rolls the both-mana case at 25% of its drops (items.hc:1264-1268); CLASS_HENCHMAN at 8% (items.hc:1288-1292). monster_archer is CLASS_GRUNT (archer.hc:730), so a quarter of all archer drops in blackmarsh are constructed and deleted. This is consistent with the tester report of Hexen II feeling unnaturally mana-starved.

3. item_spawner (artifact.hc:616) -- a map-placed entity that just calls DropBackpack. A mana-only spawner configuration is deleted at use. Worth checking against the mod item-spawn reports; unrelated to uhexen2-4p8t but the same user-visible symptom.

SCOPE -- affected trees:
  h2      items.hc:1730   AFFECTED
  portals items.hc:1753   AFFECTED
  hw      items.hc:2561   AFFECTED
  siege   items.hc:2530   NOT AFFECTED -- siege forces total=TRUE at items.hc:2381-2382 right after the nothing-to-drop early-out, so its if(!total) is unreachable. Siege already has, in effect, the correct fix.

SHIPPING CAVEAT (same as uhexen2-hwky): this is progs.dat, not the engine. gamecode/ is excluded from the nix build (flake.nix:46) and we ship no progs.dat, so a source fix reaches only players running rebuilt gamecode. Retail Raven progs.dat keeps the bug. See the related packaging question about shipping uHexen2 gamecode (gamecode/README documents fixes through 1.29c; gamecode/patch111/ carries data1 + patchdat).
acceptance_criteria: A player dying in coop/deathmatch with both mana types and no artifacts drops a usable backpack containing that mana. A CLASS_GRUNT monster rolling the both-mana branch of MonsterDropStuff drops a bag rather than nothing. No behavioural change for drops that already worked (single artifact, single mana type, instant health alone, artifact+mana combinations). All four gamecode trees compile clean with hcc.
notes:
[HISTORICAL] The close_reason validation section lists byte counts from commit bb570666a:
- progs.dat 889056 bytes (h2)
- progs2.dat 839396 bytes (h2)
- progs.dat 1148080 bytes (portals)

These sizes became stale after ce8c9d1c4 (fix(gamecode): revert TimeBomb glyph 
to retail behaviour), which changed compiled output. Correct current values:
- h2/progs.dat: 888368 bytes
- h2/progs2.dat: 838712 bytes
- portals/progs.dat: 1147444 bytes

See uhexen2-8qp3 and uhexen2-qj8s for context and corrected figures.
close_reason:
Fixed in commit bb570666a on master.

WHAT CHANGED
Removed the destructive `if (!total) { remove(item); return; }` block from the multi-item bag branch in three trees:
- gamecode/hc/h2/items.hc:1730
- gamecode/hc/portals/items.hc:1753
- gamecode/hc/hw/items.hc:2561

Each deletion was replaced with a six-line comment explaining why the check must not return: bluemana, greenmana and spawn_health are copied to the item after `total` is accumulated, so they never count toward it. A mana/health-only drop reaches the bag branch with total==0 and must survive. The genuine nothing-to-drop case already returned at the early-out above (per precedent ~15 lines above in uhexen2-hwky).

gamecode/hc/siege/items.hc was deliberately left untouched (git diff is empty over gamecode/hc/siege/) — siege forces `total = TRUE` after its early-out, so its copy of the check is already unreachable.

title: Bindless textures: reconsider only with a measured need and a batched multi-draw design
description:
The bindless scaffolding was removed in 8124ed055 (uhexen2-ubsu) rather than completed. This bead exists so the decision is revisitable, not so someone re-adds the same shape.

What was wrong with the removed version, beyond the six defects uhexen2-ubsu catalogued: the ARB entry points were declared through GL_FUNCTION_OPT, which GL_Init_Functions expands to nothing, and nothing else called SDL_GL_GetProcAddress for them. They were permanently NULL, so gl_bindless_able could never be true on any hardware and none of the downstream code had ever run.

If this is picked up again, two things must be true first:

1. A MEASURED need. The removed code saved about two glBindTexture calls per draw and populated exactly one SSBO entry -- no batching at all. That is not worth an extension dependency. The win only exists if DrawTextureChains is restructured so many texture chains submit as one multi-draw with per-draw handles, which is the refactor gl_rsurf.c's own comment admitted was required. Profile first (r_speeds 2) and show that per-draw texture binding is actually a dominant bucket.

2. A way to TEST it. llvmpipe does not implement ARB_bindless_texture, so neither this dev box nor CI can exercise the path -- that is why the removed version sat unvalidated indefinitely. Either a machine with a bindless-capable GPU is in the loop, or the feature does not land enabled.

Also note Ironwail does not use ARB_bindless_texture; if the goal is fewer binds, its texture-array / batching approach is the parity-consistent direction and needs no extension.

Prerequisite reading: the removal commit 8124ed055 and history/ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md.
notes:
GATE 1 ANSWERED 2026-08-20, and the answer is no. Closing.

The bead's rule is its own: "Profile first (r_speeds 2) and show that per-draw texture binding is actually a dominant bucket... If it is small relative to draw count, the bead's own argument says stop." It is small. Detail below, because the evidence is not the r_speeds run the bead imagined and the difference matters.

HOW IT WAS MEASURED. Not with r_speeds -- that needs a GPU and a person, and this box is llvmpipe. Measured from the other end instead, which for this particular question is actually the stronger form: DrawTextureChains (gl_rsurf.c:2090) loops `ti < cl.worldmodel->numtextures` and issues one GL_Bind per chain that has visible surfaces. So the number of distinct textures a map's faces reference is a HARD CEILING on world-pass binds per frame, fixed by the content and knowable offline. tools/bsp_texcount.py (commit 832744e6d) parses the BSP lumps and reports it.

THE NUMBER, across all 59 shipped maps in data1, portals, sot, soc, karma2 and GameOfTomes:
  distinct textures referenced by faces -- max 119 (village2.bsp), mean 58.3
  faces -- max 10080 (keep5.bsp), mean 4879
So the world pass cannot exceed ~119 binds/frame on the heaviest map anyone ships, and averages under 60.

THE OTHER BIND SOURCES, checked rather than assumed:
- Lightmaps: gl_lmatlas defaults to 1 (gl_rmain.c:344), so the atlas path is live and binds ONE atlas texture per frame at TU1 -- via a direct glBindTexture, so it does not even reach c_texbinds. The per-block GL_Bind(lightmap_textures[i]) sites at gl_rsurf.c:1035 and :1199 are the non-atlas fallback.
- Alias models: already batched. GL_Bind(batch->skin_tex) at gl_rmain.c:3286 is once per batch, not once per entity, plus an optional fullbright at :3443. MAX_VISEDICTS is 16384 but the bind count tracks distinct skins, not entities.
- Brush entities: the one real amplifier. The bmodel loop (gl_rsurf.c:2793+) walks surfaces in surface order and flushes on texture CHANGE, so an interleaved bmodel re-binds the same texture repeatedly. That is a sorting defect and its fix is to sort the surfaces, not to adopt an extension -- bindless would paper over it.

CONCLUSION. Generously totalled, a few hundred binds per frame. glBindTexture is order-100ns on a real driver, so order-0.05ms against a 16.7ms frame: well under 1%. Per-draw texture binding is not a dominant bucket in this engine and cannot become one on Hexen II content, because the content itself caps it. An ARB_bindless_texture dependency cannot pay for itself here.

Gate 2 (a bindless-capable GPU in the loop) remains unmet and is now moot.

CORRECTING THIS BEAD'S OWN DESCRIPTION: it ends "Also note Ironwail does not use ARB_bindless_texture". That is FALSE and history/ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md already corrected it on 2026-08-18 -- Ironwail has a live bindless path (gl_bindless_able in gl_vidsdl.c, TEXPREF_BINDLESS, GL_GetTextureSamplerHandleARB in gl_texmgr.c, used on r_world.c's draw path). The closing argument above does NOT rest on that stale claim; it rests on the bind ceiling, which is a fact about our content regardless of what Ironwail does.

SO THE PARITY ROW STAYS ❌ MISSING, not ➖ N/A. This is a real gap we are declining on measured grounds, not an irrelevance. Anyone reversing this should reverse it with a number: c_texbinds is on master now (652dc8452), r_speeds 2 prints it, and one minute on real hardware falsifies the estimate above if it is wrong. If it comes back large, reopen -- and note the first thing to try is still sorting the bmodel surface walk, which needs no extension.
close_reason: Closed

title: Windows MIDI use-after-free from FreeBuffers in StreamBufferSetup error paths
description:
SHIPPED REGRESSION in 0.7.9-beta.r5, r6, r7. Introduced by commit 6c1928cb0 (2026-08-11 14:15), which was fixing uhexen2-5rir.

Before 6c1928cb0, FreeBuffers() in engine/h2shared/midi_win.c had one caller: MIDI_Stop's STATUS_CALLBACKDEAD branch, which safely stops the stream and waits for buffer return before freeing.

6c1928cb0 added four FreeBuffers() calls to StreamBufferSetup error paths. Three can execute AFTER buffers are already handed to the device with no stream stop/wait:
- midiStreamProperty failure (~line 409)
- ConvertToBuffer failure (~line 434)  
- midiOutPrepareHeader failure (~line 446)

When FreeBuffers tries to unprepare a queued buffer:
1. midiOutUnprepareHeader fails with MIDIERR_STILLPLAYING, does NOT unprepare
2. Error reported, execution continues
3. Z_Free's mh.lpData — memory the MIDI device callback owns
4. Sets prepared=FALSE despite failed unprepare; next StreamBufferSetup will re-prepare a buffer device still holds, with fresh lpData

Result: callback thread holds stale pointers into freed zone memory. Z_Malloc/Z_Free are unsynchronised (per commit 392edce10). Corruption surfaces nondeterministically later.

Suspected root cause of BOTH: music-volume crash AND earlier Barbican changelevel crash (uhexen2-13m9). Explains nondeterminism and "retrying works fine" observations.

FIX: drop all four FreeBuffers() calls from StreamBufferSetup; keep the `if (!stream_bufs[i].mh.lpData)` reuse guard. The guard alone fixes uhexen2-5rir (prevents Z_Malloc over live lpData), and the frees are what introduced the UAF. Shutdown still releases via MIDI_Stop's handshake.

Acceptance: no FreeBuffers call while a buffer is queued; uhexen2-5rir stays fixed; nix build .#win64 clean.
close_reason:
FIXED IN COMMIT a2a06e219. That commit's message is "fix(worldcull): don't run the GPU cull path without the lightmap atlas (uhexen2-qt7s)" and says NOTHING about MIDI. The midi_win.c fix was swept into it by accident: a parallel Claude session working uhexen2-qt7s ran a broad `git commit -a` while the MIDI edit was still uncommitted in the shared working tree. Verified: `git show a2a06e219 --stat` lists engine/h2shared/midi_win.c (28 lines changed), and the hunk is exactly the intended fix.

DECISION: NOT splitting the commit or rewriting history. Master had other live sessions committing to it, and a soft-reset is precisely the operation that would clobber their in-flight uncommitted work — the same failure that caused this mix-up. Cost of leaving it is release-note accuracy only, handled separately (see release-note memory).

FIX DESCRIPTION: Removed all four FreeBuffers() calls that commit 6c1928cb0 had added to StreamBufferSetup's error paths in engine/h2shared/midi_win.c. Kept the `if (!stream_bufs[i].mh.lpData)` reuse guard, which is what actually fixes the original leak (uhexen2-5rir) — that leak was Z_Malloc'ing over a live lpData pointer, and reuse makes that impossible. FreeBuffers() is back to exactly one caller: the STATUS_CALLBACKDEAD branch in MIDI_Stop (midi_win.c:287), whose stop-the-stream-and-wait-on-hBufferReturnEvent handshake is the only thing that makes freeing safe. The comment above the reuse guard was rewritten to state that these error paths must NOT free.

VALIDATION: nix build .#win64 PASS (the target that actually compiles midi_win.c — it is Windows-only, in PLATFORM_SOURCES under the Windows branch at engine/CMakeLists.txt:456) and nix build .#default PASS.

NOT RUNTIME TESTED. Not yet confirmed by the reporting tester ("Tome of Power Abuser", Windows 10). This was diagnosed by code reading; the causal link to their two crash reports is a strong hypothesis, not a proven one.

title: MD5/IQM index buffer is identity permutation — OOB GPU vertex reads (gl_mesh.c:444-447)
description: MD5 meshes upload numverts unique verts but GL_MakeAliasGPUMesh fills the IBO with an identity permutation 0..numtris*3-1 (~6x the vertex-buffer size). Every MD5/IQM model renders with destroyed topology AND fetches ~6x past the per-vertex attribute buffers (vbo_verts, texcoord VBO) — garbage/zeroed verts, GL errors/crash on non-robust contexts. Root cause: real connectivity (tris[]) is parsed in md5mesh.c but never persisted to aliashdr_t (see sibling issue). Currently LATENT: the MD5 loader (gl_model.c:350-360) returns before GL_MakeAliasGPUMesh, so it is a half-wired skeletal feature; defect is unconditional once the path is exercised. FIX: persist tris[] into aliashdr_t (add triangledata offset field, copy into hunk) and build the IBO from real indices; assert numverts<=65535 for GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT or widen IBO+draw to GL_UNSIGNED_INT.
close_reason: Fix applied (IBO built from persisted MD5 triangle indices); root cause ssct also fixed; nix build passes. Runtime pending on test box.

title: Waterfall clipping regression in 0.7.8-beta.r11
description:
User observed waterfall clipping regression after upgrading to 0.7.8-beta.r11. Tabled during khsa investigation — pick this up once khsa lands (or sooner if r11 is the actual culprit and the swizzle change needs reverting).

Symptom: not yet characterized (tabled before details captured). User will describe when work resumes.

Bisect range to investigate when picked back up:
- Good (suspect): r6 (093637e1c) — last build before khsa diagnostic chain started
- Bad: r11 fix (ce9280b49) — current head

Candidate commits in range:
- f3f09e732 r7  — diag dump only (additive, unlikely to break rendering)
- b7a14f097 r8  — r_alias_minlight cvar, lighting floor in R_DrawAliasModel (alias only, not water)
- 8ab6bf9bf r9  — gl_solid_format/gl_alpha_format changed from 3/4 → GL_RGB8/GL_RGBA8 (affects every texture upload, including water)
- 7c627f5d4 r10 — dump extension only (additive)
- 01b4ee3e8 r11 — GL_TEXTURE_SWIZZLE_A=GL_ONE on opaque skin upload (affects every !TEX_ALPHA texture, water included)
- ce9280b49     — mingw GL_TEXTURE_SWIZZLE_A shim (header-only, no behavior change)

Most likely culprits in order of suspicion: r11, r9. Both touch texture upload state for all textures, not just alias models. Water textures are usually !TEX_ALPHA so they get the swizzle and sized format changes.

If r11 IS the culprit, the fix is to scope the swizzle by texture purpose (only apply to alias skins, not world/water/sky), not the upload path's TEX_ALPHA flag.

Bisect protocol per project convention: user builds and tests each step themselves; do not spawn nix-builder during bisects.

Phase 1 closed earlier; phases 2 and 3 landed in 5670c942b — .md5anim parser with parent-before-child bone propagation and anim_world*inv_rest composition, PV_IQM draw dispatch through GL_DrawAliasSkeletal, two-pose shader blending, real shadedots-equivalent lighting, skin loading from the mesh shader string, and animated culling bounds. Also fixed three latent md5mesh.c bugs the phase-1 crash-safety review missed (substring section matching, file-order weight binning, zero hdr->scale). Verified against new synthetic models in engine/tests/md5. Real-asset visual verification tracked as uhexen2-2t38.

title: Port Ironwail a65a88e: frame-major alias pose SSBO layout
description: Ironwail commit a65a88e reorganized alias-model GPU pose data from surface-major to frame-major order so the VBO/SSBO is bound once per model instead of once per surface, cutting CPU-side bind calls on multi-surface alias models (Hexen II has many). Also adds a Mod_NextSurface() helper (gl_model.h). Hexenwail still allocates ssbo_pose per-surface (h2shared/gl_mesh.c:667-690) with a separate ssbo_pose_md3. Substantial restructuring: aliashdr_t layout, gl_mesh.c upload, gl_rmain.c draw dispatch, and the alias/skeletal shaders. High effort, high regression risk, no correctness bug driving it — defer until after uhexen2-ayrn (light-trace cache) which also touches the alias hot path.
notes: Checked 2026-08-20 during a P0 sweep: still blocked, correctly. Depends on uhexen2-ayrn (light-trace cache), which is in_progress and touches the same alias hot path — the bead's own description says to defer until after it. Not started; taking it now would mean rebasing a substantial aliashdr_t/gl_mesh/gl_rmain/shader restructure onto a moving target for no correctness gain.
close_reason:
ALREADY SATISFIED — verified against the code 2026-08-20, the premise was false. Forcing past the uhexen2-ayrn gate because there is no work to sequence: the port is a no-op here.

The bead says 'Hexenwail still allocates ssbo_pose per-surface (gl_mesh.c:667-690)'. It does not. Four checks:

1. LAYOUT IS ALREADY FRAME-MAJOR. GL_MakeAliasModelDisplayLists (gl_mesh.c:346-350) writes posedata as 'for (i=0;i<numposes;i++) for (j=0;j<numorder;j++) *verts++ = poseverts[i][vertexorder[j]]' — outer loop pose, inner loop vertex. aliashdr_t's own field comment agrees ('numposes*poseverts trivert_t'). GL_MakeAliasGPUMesh packs that linearly and the shader indexes pose_data[Pose0 + gl_VertexID], Pose0 = pose*poseverts.

2. ONE SSBO PER MODEL. alias_gpu_meshes[] is keyed by aliashdr_t (alias_gpu_owners[i] == hdr); glBufferData sizes it numposes*poseverts for the whole model.

3. BOUND ONCE PER BATCH, WITH A REDUNDANT-BIND FILTER. R_DrawAliasInstanced tracks last_pose_ssbo and rebinds only on change — the exact saving a65a88e was written to get.

4. NO MULTI-SURFACE ALIAS MODELS EXIST. aliashdr_t is single-surface by construction. MD3 would be the multi-surface case, but nothing sets poseverttype = PV_MD3: model.c:384 Sys_Errors on MD3_IDENT, and the PV_MD3 upload/shader paths are unreached scaffolding. The MD5 loader added today reads only the first mesh block by design.

Ironwail needed a65a88e because its rerelease MD5 models are genuinely multi-surface. Hexen II's .mdl never was, so the layout a65a88e moves TO is what this engine started with. Mod_NextSurface has no meaning here — there is no surface chain to walk.

The ayrn hold is separately moot: ayrn landed in 1f6af22cc and is in current history.

title: Port Ironwail 1011ff8/74d8e74: apply TEXPREF_UNCOMPRESSED to alpha-tested and 2D textures
description: Ironwail commits 1011ff8 + 74d8e74 'Disable compression for alpha-tested and 2D textures' (gl_model.c, gl_texmgr.c, gl_draw.c). TEXPREF_UNCOMPRESSED is already defined (h2shared/gl_texmgr.h:38) but never applied. Once GPU texture compression lands, exempt HUD/2D textures (char_texture, char_smalltexture, char_menufonttexture, conback in gl_draw.c) and alpha-tested model/world skins (TEX_HOLEY / TEX_FENCE in gl_model.c) from compression to avoid block-artifact fringing on alpha edges and text. Low effort once the prerequisite lands; ZERO impact until then. BLOCKED on uhexen2-8dks (GPU texture compression).
notes:
Caveat surfaced by the 2026-08-18 parity audit: the premise that this bead is ZERO impact until uhexen2-8dks lands is no longer fully true. Commit 74e8eccde (uhexen2-0vgo.5) gave HD replacement packs compressed DDS/KTX upload — img_dds.c parses DXT1/3/5, ATI1/ATI2, DX10-header BC1-BC5/BC7 and KTX 1.1, and hands the payload to glCompressedTexImage2D as-is. So compressed textures already reach the GPU on this engine; they just arrive from the content author rather than from an engine-side compressor.

That means a pack shipping BC1 conchars, HUD art or fence/holey skins hits exactly the block-artifact fringing on alpha edges and text that Ironwail 1011ff8 and 74d8e74 guard against, and it hits it TODAY, with no engine compression system in sight.

The engine cannot fix that by setting a TEXPREF flag — it does not choose the format, the pack does. The realistic scope for the external-pack half is: warn (or refuse the compressed path and fall through to the RGBA decode) when a DDS/KTX replacement lands on a texture the engine knows is alpha-tested or 2D. The original TEXPREF_UNCOMPRESSED scope still applies to engine-generated textures and still waits on uhexen2-8dks.

Also still true from the 2026-08-13 correction: TEXPREF_UNCOMPRESSED itself no longer exists anywhere — h2shared/gl_texmgr.h was deleted in 8124ed055. Whoever picks this up defines the flag fresh in glquake.h.

Recorded in history/ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md on the 1011ff8 bug-fix row.
HASH CORRECTION 2026-08-19.  The bindless-scaffolding removal is cited here as 8124ed055, which is not in master.  Survivor is bbf4a97a5, same subject and the same seven source files (gl_draw.c, gl_func.h, glquake.h, gl_shader.c, gl_texmgr.h, gl_vidsdl.c, gl_rsurf.c); only the squashed-in beads export makes the patch-id differ.
close_reason: Implemented in 387fc2e40. gl_compress_textures (default 0, archived) selects GL_COMPRESSED_RGBA_BPTC_UNORM in GL_Upload32 and the embedded-mips path, matching Ironwail's cvar name, default and format. Exemptions landed with it: TEX_FENCE/TEX_HOLEY checked centrally in GL_InternalFormat, new TEX_UNCOMPRESSED flag on conchars/tinyfont/menufont/conback/GL_LoadPicTexture/external-HUD. External-pack half: IMG_LoadReplacement gained allow_compressed and declines DDS/KTX containers for alpha-tested textures (fences detected by name, EF_HOLEY passed by the caller), falling through to the decoded image. Not runtime-verified visually — cvar is default-off so the risk is opt-in.

title: SoT SIGABRT: R_BuildLightMap memset overflow on tiled (turb) surfaces
description: ACTUAL cause of the glhexen2 -game sot abort (gdb bt: R_BuildLightMap <- R_LightmapRebuildIfDirty <- R_RecursiveWorldNode <- R_DrawWorld). Turbulent/sky surfaces get placeholder extents=16384 in Mod_SetDrawingFlags (model.c:1072), so smax*tmax = 1025*1025. When a dynamic light marks a water surface near the player, R_LightmapRebuildIfDirty calls R_BuildLightMap which memsets blocklights[]/blocklightscolor[] (sized 128*128) with size*3 uints -> overruns -> _FORTIFY_SOURCE __memset_chk abort. The earlier uhexen2-iihz fix only enlarged the buffer to 128x128, which can't hold a 16384-extent tiled surface. Real fix: skip SURF_DRAWTILED surfaces in R_BuildLightMap and R_LightmapRebuildIfDirty (tiled surfaces never sample a lightmap; matches vanilla). discovered-from uhexen2-coqr.
close_reason: Fixed and committed (0.7.7-beta.r11)

title: Fortify buffer overflow (SIGABRT) at map spawn parsing worldspawn
description: glhexen2 -game sot aborts with glibc '*** buffer overflow detected ***' / SIGABRT at map spawn. Root cause: COM_Parse (h2shared/common.c) writes com_token[1024] with no bounds check in both quoted-string and word loops; a worldspawn key/value >=1024 chars overruns it. Additionally Sky_NewMap (gl_sky.c:823/825) and Fog_NewMap (gl_fog.c:218/220) strcpy into key[128] from com_token (any key 128-1023 chars overflows the stack array), and both have a key[strlen(key)-1] underflow on empty keys. Fix: bound com_token writes in COM_Parse; replace strcpy with q_strlcpy in Sky_NewMap/Fog_NewMap; guard the trailing-space trim against empty key.
close_reason: Fixed and committed (0.7.7-beta.r11)

title: r7 SoT crash: blocklights buffer overflow exposed by R_RecursiveWorldNode hook
description: Fix landed in working tree for 0.7.7-beta.r8. The uhexen2-iihz fix (commit 25649d846) hoisted R_LightmapRebuildIfDirty into R_RecursiveWorldNode so every visible world surface gets rebuilt before R_UpdateLightmaps#1. SoT has surfaces with extents > 256 world units (smax*tmax > 324) that the legacy 18*18 blocklights[]/blocklightscolor[] static arrays could not hold. The moment the new hook exposed them to R_BuildLightMap, glibc fortified memset caught the overflow as a SIGABRT during SoT map load on r7. Fix: size blocklights[] and blocklightscolor[] for BLOCK_WIDTH*BLOCK_HEIGHT (128*128) which matches the lightmap atlas page — AllocBlock won't place a single surface larger than one page so this is a hard ceiling. engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c
close_reason: Fixed in eaae2152b — blocklights[] / blocklightscolor[] resized to BLOCK_WIDTH*BLOCK_HEIGHT to match atlas page

title: Publish canonical pre-2024 (r6303-era) Shanjaq builds: glhexen2 + glhwcl + hwsv for Linux/Windows x64
description:
Discord community request from JakubM via Discord: 'The latest Shanjaq version, I'd like 64-bit Windows and Linux builds of GL Hexen 2, glhwcl and hwsv from JakubM'.

Hexenwail should become the source of truth for the original Shanjaq H2 fork's binary distribution — these builds are otherwise unavailable to the community. 'Pre-2024 (r6303)' anchors this to the upstream sezero/uhexen2 SVN revision range Shanjaq's tip sat at before our modernization rebase.

Context: history was squashed 2026-03-21 into 'sezero base + 1 Shanjaq squash commit + 1 Hexenwail squash commit' on master. The full pre-squash history lives in the local-only branch 'master-pre-squash' (not yet pushed to any remote).

Work breakdown:

Build the six binaries (3 targets x 2 platforms), package as a zip per platform with the three executables + any required runtime DLLs (codec DLLs already bundled in current flake for win64), and publish as a GitHub Release on hexenwail/hexenwail with a descriptive tag (e.g., 'shanjaq-r6303-archive-2026-05').

Source: Discord community request 2026-05-30.
notes:

title: Flame group-pose lerp blacklist + animation smoothness
description:
Followups from Mathuzzz testing uhexen2-jb0q:

1. Some flame models look REALLY ugly with the new group-pose lerp because consecutive poses don't share vertex topology (the flame 'jumps sides' between poses). Need to honor MOD_NOLERP — the r_nolerp_list cvar already exists in gl_rmain.c with a Hexen 2-tuned default list, and Mod_SetExtraFlags already sets MOD_NOLERP on matching models, but:
   - r_nolerp_list is never registered (Cvar_RegisterVariable missing in gl_rmisc.c) — defaults still take effect because Mod_SetExtraFlags reads .string directly
   - MOD_NOLERP is never checked in the renderer — it's a dangling Ironwail port
   Wire it up: skip both group-pose lerp AND server-frame lerp when MOD_NOLERP is set (matches Ironwail intent — flames AND v_weapons).

2. Model animation still doesn't look smooth even with r_lerpmodels 1. Root cause: cl_parse.c hardcodes lerpdur=0.1s, but Hexen 2 server ticks at 20Hz=50ms, so every new frame interrupts the previous lerp halfway. r_animsmoothing (uhexen2-wax3) was supposed to fix this by measuring the actual interval, but:
   - Defaults to 0
   - Has a 'if (lerpdur < 0.1f) lerpdur = 0.1f' floor that defeats sub-100ms intervals (the exact case it was supposed to help)
   Fix: default r_animsmoothing to 1, lower the floor from 0.1 to ~0.025.
close_reason: Pose-driven alias lerp refactor in commit 9acf64752: R_AliasResolveLerp unifies CPU+GPU paths, MOD_NOLERP honored for both group-pose lerp and server-frame lerp, r_nolerp_list registered with Hexen 2 fire-model defaults, single-pose lerp duration dropped to 0.05s to match 20Hz tick. r_animsmoothing/lastframechange removed (obsolete).

title: CRITICAL: IQM/MD5 skeletal animation is non-functional skeleton (mislabeled IQM)
description:
5 commits (2084b6765, 48753b791, d18ca709c, 34a02fff1, fa6185969). Parity tracker claims completion. Reality: would crash on first real .md5mesh load, and even if it didn't, every vertex renders at origin with garbage SSBO.

NAMING: Title says IQM but code parses MD5mesh (ASCII id format). No .iqm parser exists, no iqm.h. iqmvert_t is just internal vertex struct name reused from Ironwail.

CRITICAL bugs in md5mesh.c:
1. md5mesh.c:165 — 96KB stack array (tris) + 128KB (verts) → SIGSEGV on first real load
2. md5mesh.c:190-194 — stores stack-address offset into hunk pointer, use-after-stack memcpy
3. md5mesh.c:176 — hunk allocation missing bone-pose data; boneposedata field never set; gl_mesh.c:629 uploads garbage to SSBO
4. NO .md5anim parser anywhere — no animation, no quaternion→matrix, no parent-before-child propagation. Hardcoded numposes=1 (md5mesh.c:186). Rest pose only.
5. md5mesh.c:97 — bone weights not normalized. >4 influences silently dropped, vertices shrink to origin.
6. md5mesh.c:85 — rest-pose XYZ set to zero. Every vertex collapses to origin. Cross-product of zero vectors → all normals zero.

HIGH bugs:
- gl_shader.c:594-595 mat3x4 std430 layout mismatch (64B GLSL vs 48B CPU)
- gl_mesh.c:642-646 confusing double-increment / dead code
- md5mesh.c:33,65 NULL not checked after strchr → crash on malformed input
- gl_model.c:352 hardcoded 1MB size, relies on null-termination

The skeletal shader is NEVER invoked — grep gl_shader_skeletal returns only declaration + InitProgram call. Zero draw-site references. R_DrawAliasModel has no PV_IQM branch.

d18ca709c commit is mislabeled — 265 of 315 lines are Bloom post-process, unrelated. Only ~41 lines are the skeletal shader.

Fix: Revert parity tracker claims (history/ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md should be 🔶 ~30%, not ✅). Either complete the work properly or remove the half-implementation.
close_reason: Doc revert. Reclassified MD5/IQM 🔶 Partial ~30% in ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md (was ✅), renamed row 'IQM' → 'MD5mesh / IQM', enumerated critical bugs. Scorecard 80/1/1/8. Code work deferred.

title: CRITICAL: Bindless texture support is non-functional skeleton labeled 'complete'
description:
15+ commits (880b52d0d through 31455e83f, 2d5b1ac71). Despite parity tracker claiming completion, the bindless path produces zero working draws.

CRITICAL issues:
1. Shaders compiled with BINDLESS=0 regardless of +bindless flag — gl_vidsdl.c:983 calls GL_Shaders_Init() before line 1000 sets gl_bindless_able. Bindless GLSL branches are unreachable.
2. TEX_BINDLESS flag never passed by any caller — zero call sites in entire codebase. glt->bindless_handle always 0; SSBO upload at gl_rsurf.c:2061-2062 writes zero handles.
3. TexMgr_LoadImage ignores bindless entirely — gl_texmgr.c:120-183 has no references to bindless_handle, TEXPREF_BINDLESS, or any bindless API.
4. Two divergent gltexture_t structs (glquake.h:130 vs gl_texmgr.h:46), only one used by draw path.

HIGH issues:
- Sampler objects created but never bound (dead code)
- No ARB_gpu_shader_int64 capability check — shader compile fails on driver without int64 GLSL extension
- gl_rsurf.c:38-56 own comment admits 'stub status'

Docs claim complete:
- f53b01709: 'Texture handles made resident on load' — false
- history/bindless_test_procedure.md:52: 'implementation complete' — false

Fix: Either complete the implementation (significant work) or revert/disable the feature and revert the parity tracker claims.
close_reason: Doc revert. Reclassified bindless ❌ Missing in ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md (was ✅), updated scorecard (80/1/1/8), added warning to bindless_test_procedure.md. Code work deferred to future feature commit.

title: CRITICAL: Skybox cache use-after-free via texture pointer aliasing
description:
Commit 78933d173 (skybox cache). In gl_sky.c:434-435, Sky_LoadSkyBox calls TexMgr_FreeTexture(skybox_textures[i]) unconditionally when switching skies. After a cache HIT at line 425, skybox_textures[] aliases the cached entry's textures[] (memcpy of pointers). On the next non-cached Sky_LoadSkyBox(otherName), the purge loop frees those pointers — corrupting the cache and producing use-after-free on subsequent rebind.

Fix: Track whether current skybox came from cache (matches Ironwail approach). Skip the purge loop if cached, or make cached entries own a reference that prevents free.
close_reason: Fixed by commit b722e9ae6. Established single ownership rule (cache owns all textures; skybox_textures[] is non-owning view) by removing the offending purge-loop free and adding LRU-bump to Sky_CacheLookup so the active entry is never evicted. Latent today (TexMgr_FreeTexture is a no-op stub at gl_texmgr.c:72-75) — would become a live UAF/double-free the moment the stub is replaced with a real implementation. Adjacent texmgr-pool-exhaustion finding tracked separately as uhexen2-z7dj.

title: CRITICAL: R_AddStaticModels is dead code — static entities won't render
description:
In commit d01b8c03a (efrag simplification), R_AddStaticModels is defined in gl_refrag.c:127 and declared in glquake.h:406, but NEVER called anywhere. The old R_StoreEfrags call site in R_RecursiveWorldNode was removed without adding the replacement caller. Result: static map entities (torches, candles, ambient decorative models) will not render on any map.

Fix: Call R_AddStaticModels(vis) from R_DrawWorld in gl_rsurf.c:3191 or R_RenderScene, passing the current view's PVS (Mod_LeafPVS(r_viewleaf, cl.worldmodel) or cached vis array).

Build succeeds because R_AddStaticModels has external linkage; linker doesn't enforce caller existence.
close_reason:
Audit finding is incorrect. Verified 2026-05-31:
- 'R_AddStaticModels' has ZERO references in the entire engine tree — the function does not exist.
- R_StoreEfrags is alive: declared at glquake.h:406, defined at gl_refrag.c:191, and CALLED at gl_rsurf.c:2835 inside R_RecursiveWorldNode (live, unguarded code).
- The static-entity pipeline works as standard Quake: R_RecursiveWorldNode walks visible leafs, hits each leaf's efrag chain, calls R_StoreEfrags, which pushes entities into cl_visedicts.
- The Haiku 4.5 reviewer apparently invented a function name and speculated about commit d01b8c03a's intent without checking the actual code.
No fix required.

title: Group-frame pose interpolation missing (fire/torch jitter)
description:
Multi-pose MDL frame groups (numposes>1) — fire, torches, candles, runes — are rendered with discrete pose switching instead of interpolation. The lerp path in gl_rmain.c is only entered when the server-driven frame changes (prevframe != frame), but for group frames the server-frame never changes; only the pose index cycles via (int)(cl.time/interval) % numposes. Result: visible pose-to-pose pops on auto-animating models. Mathuzzz reported this as 'broken visuals' on fire models — frame switching is noticeable.

Fix: also interpolate between consecutive poses inside a numposes>1 group using the fractional part of cl.time/interval as lerpfrac. Apply to both:
  - CPU path: R_SetupAliasFrame (gl_rmain.c:841)
  - GPU instanced path: alias instance setup (gl_rmain.c:2128+)

Ironwail and QuakeSpasm-Spiked already do this. Engine HAS interpolation infrastructure (r_lerpmodels, r_animsmoothing) — this is purely a missed code path for group frames.
close_reason: Implemented group-frame pose interpolation in both CPU (R_SetupAliasFrame) and GPU instanced paths. Uses fmod(cl.time, gpn*interval) for precision-safe cycle reduction, then blends between consecutive poses with the fractional time within the current pose interval. Disabled during fullbright pass and LERP_RESETANIM to avoid pose mismatch across passes. Fire/torch/candle/rune jitter should now be smooth.

title: Port Ironwail: Light trace cache for alias models
description: Ironwail commit e2f39505 (Oct 2021) adds caching for light trace calculations on alias models. Modifies gl_rlight.c, r_alias.c, render.h. Specialized optimization for model lighting performance.
notes:
STATIC AUDIT 2026-08-20 — clean. No runtime verification (declined for this box; llvmpipe, and the check is a visual one). This does not close the bead, but it removes the "is the code even right" half of the risk, leaving only the visual confirmation.

First, the thing that bit twice today elsewhere in this repo: CONFIRMED ON MASTER. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 1f6af22cc master` passes and the symbols are live — lightcache_t at render.h:67, entity_t.lightcache at render.h:124, InterpolateLightmap at gl_rlight.c:550, R_LightPointColor(p, cache) at :682. The hash-correction note above is accurate; the implementation did survive the rebase.

WHAT WAS CHECKED, and what each check concluded:

1. Cache-hit correctness for lightstyles. The hit path calls InterpolateLightmap unconditionally when surfidx > 0, and InterpolateLightmap re-reads d_lightstylevalue[] every call. So a torch keeps animating on a standing-still model. The design claim holds in the code.

2. The lightspot divergence, which the note flags as the thing to check if shadows look wrong. Correct as written. Miss path: trace, then VectorCopy(lightspot, cache->spot). Hit path: VectorCopy(cache->spot, lightspot) BEFORE the interpolate. And the restore can never hand back a garbage spot, because it only runs when surfidx > 0, and surfidx > 0 can only be set at the same node-split where VectorCopy(mid, lightspot) just wrote it. A trace that hits nothing leaves surfidx 0 and therefore always re-traces rather than restoring a stale spot.

3. Cache thrash between the two sample points. This was the specific thing I expected to find and did not. gl_rmain.c:4348 passes e->origin, not adjust_origin, which would thrash a shared cache — but it is R_DrawViewModel operating on &cl.viewent, a DIFFERENT entity with its own lightcache, and it is that entity's only cached caller. Every other cached call goes through AliasModelGetLightInfo (gl_rmain.c:1462, called at :1528, :1562, :2837, :2860, :3345), which derives adjust_origin from e->origin and e->model identically each time. So per entity the sample point is stable within a frame and the second call really is a hit.

4. Uninitialised read in the NULL-cache path. R_LightPointColor sets only scratch.surfidx = 0, leaving scratch.pos indeterminate — but `cache->surfidx <= 0` is the FIRST clause of the invalidation test, so || short-circuits before any fabs(cache->pos[...]) is evaluated, and pos is written before the trace. Correct, though it depends on clause order; worth not reordering that condition.

5. Stale cache across a map change. Both claimed guards verified: cl_main.c CL_ClearState does memset(&cl, ...) and memset(cl_entities, ...) at lines 93/99, zeroing surfidx for both cl.viewent and every cl_entities slot, and R_LightPointColor independently rejects surfidx > cl.worldmodel->numsurfaces.

6. The int accumulators in InterpolateLightmap (r00 etc. int, `+= (float)lightmap[0] * scale`) truncate per lightstyle. That is the vanilla Quake idiom, unchanged from the code this was split out of — not introduced here.

7. surfidx == -1 re-traces every frame, as documented, because it fails `<= 0`. Matches Ironwail. Harmless.

ONE PRE-EXISTING BEHAVIOUR worth knowing, NOT introduced by this port: the `if (!cl.worldmodel->lightdata)` early return sets lightcolor to 255 and returns without touching lightspot, so on a map with no lightdata GL_DrawAliasShadow reads whatever lightspot held last. The early return predates the cache.

STILL NOT DONE, unchanged: the in-game look with r_shadows 1 — shadows landing at the right floor height, and a flickering lightstyle still animating on a standing-still model.

RUNTIME VERIFICATION DONE 2026-08-20 — headless on this box, llvmpipe under Xvfb. Both outstanding visual claims confirmed. Engine built from master at 0.8.0-beta.r15 (nix build .#default).

CLAIM 1, shadow floor height on a cache hit: CONFIRMED.
demo1, chase cam, r_shadows 1, player standing still ~20s (so every frame is a hit, not a fresh trace). Toggling r_shadows 1 -> 0 and differencing isolates exactly one ground feature: a shadow polygon whose top edge meets the boot soles, lying on the floor plane. Not floating at the model's origin, not sunk below the floor. Re-confirmed on eidolon at frame 30 of a 30-frame burst. If the cache handed back a stale or garbage spot, this is where it would show, and it does not.

CLAIM 2, lightstyle still animating on a stationary model: CONFIRMED, but only on the fourth attempt, and the three failures are the useful part of this note.

The measurement that finally worked: eidolon, teleported with setpos onto face #24 (styles[] = [2,0,255,255]; style 2 is the 50-frame a..z sweep, ~5s, the largest amplitude available). viewpos confirms the player settled at exactly (1817 32 40), and no input at all was sent during the burst, so every frame is a cache hit. 30 back-to-back frames:

  model tabard (light-cache path)   mean 42.2  sd 4.54  range 34.5% of mean
  world floor  (lightmap path)      mean 45.7  sd 5.63  range 39.8% of mean
  Pearson r, model vs world         +0.9953

Three clean cycles across the burst, matching style 2's period. The two paths are entirely separate code — the world floor goes through the lightmap atlas, the model through R_LightPointColor + InterpolateLightmap — so tracking at r=0.995 is the cache replaying lightstyles on hits, exactly as designed.

Controls, to kill the obvious alternative explanation that some global postprocess was modulating the frame:
  lava portal (fullbright, no lightstyle)   range  2.8%   (its own texture animation)
  HUD status bar (2D, never lit)            range  0.000%  sd 0.000 — pixel-identical across all 30
Nothing global is moving. The modulation is confined to lightstyle-lit surfaces.

WHY IT TOOK FOUR RUNS — worth knowing before anyone re-runs this.
1. First run at demo1's spawn: model brightness varied 0.1%. Correctly read as 'nothing is flickering here'.
2. Second run teleported to what a BSP scan called a style-4 floor. Model varied 17.5% against a 4.75% control, which LOOKED like a pass. It was not: the world reference patch pinned to one exact value for 7 consecutive frames once the player stopped settling, i.e. nothing there was animating either, and the 17.5% was idle animation over a lighting gradient.
3. Root cause of 2: my scan read dface_t.styles[] at byte 12+2 instead of 12. texinfo ends at byte 12, not 14, so it was decoding styles[2], styles[3] and half of lightofs as style numbers. It claimed 905 animated floor faces in demo1. Corrected, demo1 has ZERO — no spot in that map can test this claim at all.
4. Also: sampling at 2s intervals aliases a 10Hz style-4 strobe into noise. Style 2 at ~0.15s intervals is what makes the series readable.

Tooling committed so this is re-runnable rather than re-derivable: tools/bsp_lightstyles.py ('under' = which surface a downtrace hits and its styles; 'scan' = rank maps by best animated floor face), and three scenarios in tools/headless-drive.sh (ayrn_lightcache, ayrn_strobe, ayrn_pulse) with the dead ends documented in their comments.
close_reason: Runtime verification passed 2026-08-20. Shadow lands on the floor plane at the boot soles deep into a cache-hit burst (r_shadows on/off diff, two maps). Lightstyle animation survives cache hits: on eidolon face #24 (style 2), a stationary model's shading tracks the world lightmap at Pearson r=+0.9953 over 30 frames, 34.5% swing, while the HUD stays pixel-identical. Static audit was already clean; this closes the visual half.
