title: Material maps: _norm / _bump / _gloss sidecars, imported from the open-source Quake engines
description:
jsHexen2 (jeank) added bump mapping with 10+ material types — normal map per texture, tangent-space lighting in shader. Hexenwail has none. Asked directly on Discord 2026-08-23: 'Will your engine ever support _bump, _norm, _gloss, _luma materials?'

_luma / _glow already ship: IMG_LoadReplacementGlow (engine/h2shared/img_load.c) probes _glow then _luma, for world textures and alias skins, across .dds/.ktx then .png/.tga/.pcx. This bead is the rest of the set.

## Direction (user, 2026-08-23): import from the open-source Quake engines as needed

jsHexen2 is JavaScript/WebGL, so it can only ever be a reference for technique and visual result. DarkPlaces and FTE are C, GPL, and have shipped this for twenty years — take their code where it fits rather than re-deriving it. Hexenwail is GPL2 (via uHexen2), DarkPlaces is GPL2, FTE is GPL2+, so this is license-compatible in that direction. Spoike (FTE) is reachable in the same Discord.

## Naming is settled — do NOT invent a convention

This bead previously said '*_n.tga sidecar'. That was a guess and it is wrong; shipping it would have stranded every existing pack. Verified 2026-08-23 against DarkPlaces' own documentation (darkplaces.txt in DarkPlacesEngine/darkplaces, lines 212-235 and 261-268):

  _norm    normal map. Alpha channel may carry bumpmap height for offset/relief mapping.
  _bump    height map. NOT loaded if a normal map is present — _norm wins.
  _gloss   gloss/specular map (shiny areas). Confirmed at model_shared.c:2459 and darkplaces.txt:264.
  _glow    glow map — already implemented here.
  _luma    Tenebrae-compatible alias for _glow; use one or the other. Already implemented here.
  _pants   colormap layer, additive, greyscale (out of scope for this bead).
  _shirt   colormap layer, same (out of scope).

FTE accepts the same set (engine/gl/gl_shader.c, engine/client/renderer.c). So _norm/_bump/_gloss is not a preference, it is what every pack in the wild already ships.

Our per-map-then-shared path convention in IMG_BuildCandidates (textures/<mapname>/<name>, then textures/<name>) ALREADY matches DarkPlaces exactly — see darkplaces.txt:221-234. The loader half of this is closer to done than it looks; extend IMG_LoadReplacementGlow's pattern rather than writing a parallel path resolver.

## Real work, and it is not the file loading

  * BSP surfaces carry no tangents. Tangent-space lighting needs tangent generation first, and that is the substantial part.
  * Per-fragment dot(N,L) has to meet the engine's existing lightpoint/dlight setup, not replace it.
  * Needs a quality cvar: old GPUs and the WebGL2 build both pay for this. Check what a #version 300 es target can actually do before committing to a shader design.
  * Note that r_texture_external defaults to 0, so none of this is reachable out of the box — see the papercut bead.

Reference: jsHexen2 by jeank (https://quakeone.com); DarkPlaces (github.com/DarkPlacesEngine/darkplaces); FTE (github.com/fte-team/fteqw).
notes:
ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION 2026-08-23. The description credited Spoike, who is only named as an FTE resource to draw code from, and did NOT credit the people who actually asked for the feature.

Requested by Garrett (Monolyth-42) on Discord 2026-08-23: 'Technical question: Will your engine ever support _bump, _norm, _gloss, _luma materials?' followed by 'In theory, any mod for which these materials are created will look better. This is absolutely not necessary. It is just that if it is technically possible and not very difficult to implement, why not give people the opportunity?'

Seconded the same day by Mathuzzz: 'I would also welcome support for _bump, _gloss, etc...if it wouldn't be too much of a problem to implement of course.'

Two independent requesters, neither of them BloodShot — this bead is not part of his r16 report cluster and should not be counted with it.

title: Move water/lava/slime warp from per-vertex CPU sin to per-pixel fragment shader
description: EmitWaterPolys (engine/h2shared/gl_warp.c:223) computes UV warp and Z ripple via a CPU per-vertex sin lookup against pre-subdivided 64-unit tiles (SUBDIVIDE_SIZE=64 at line 41). On brushes with heavy subdivision (many small lava brushes — common in SoT mod content), the piecewise-linear interpolation across tiny triangles makes the warp look bad: visible seams, distorted edges, jitter. Mathuzzz's reported workaround is to wrap lava as a func_illusionary brush ent (single large brush, less subdivision). With the t4kt/gbmv fixes that workaround now mostly works, but it shouldn't be necessary in the first place — the warp itself should look right on world brushes regardless of subdivision. Plan: write turb fragment shader that computes the sin warp per-pixel using world position passed through from the vertex shader. Drop the per-vertex CPU work in EmitWaterPolys (just emit raw verts + UVs). Optionally collapse SUBDIVIDE_SIZE entirely for turb surfaces since per-pixel warp doesn't need it. Reference: Ironwail's gl_warp.c / glsl_water_frag.
notes:
Implemented, and validated against both regressions that caused the previous
two reverts.

1. The recorded cost numbers were measured over the wrong half of the content -
   bsp_subdiv.py skipped BSP2 and loose maps, i.e. Shadows of Turmoil and Wheel
   of Karma, the mods that motivated this bead. Fixed; corrected figures are
   121 maps not 57 and 478,296 turb verts at size 64 not 83,434, cross-checked
   against GL_ReportSubdivision to within 0.01%.

2. The "remaining scope is a visual judgement" framing was wrong. The warp is a
   sine sampled at tile corners and interpolated linearly, so its error has a
   closed form. tools/warp_recon.py computes it. The bead's "try size 24"
   recommendation does not survive that: 24 clears Nyquist but still carries
   93% peak error, because Nyquist governs recoverability by an IDEAL filter
   and linear interpolation is not one. Under 15% needs size 8, about 40x the
   turb geometry. No affordable subdivision size fixes the per-vertex warp.

3. Implemented the per-pixel port with the band-limit the earlier attempts
   needed. uhexen2-tlsh diagnosed the failure correctly - per-vertex plus
   linear interpolation is inherently band-limited, per-pixel sin is not - then
   damped amplitude past an fwidth THRESHOLD. The box average of sin(k*x) over
   a footprint W is sin(k*x)*sinc(k*W/2), so scaling amplitude by that sinc is
   the filtered signal rather than an approximation of it. A threshold
   over-damps (flat and dark - the famb symptom) or under-damps (banding - the
   tlsh symptom); the analytic factor does neither by construction.

4. VALIDATED, not assumed. Rendered sot/meso's lava pool at
   r_water_pixel_warp 0 and 1, overhead and at the glancing angle tlsh reported
   banding at. No banding; the distant surface smooths with distance instead of
   striping, which is the band-limit working. Luma over the liquid region:

     overhead   mean 18.88 vs 18.85  (+0.1%)   stddev 10.30 vs 10.26
     glancing   mean 18.33 vs 18.33  (-0.0%)   stddev  8.61 vs  8.64

   Brightness matches within 0.1% at both angles, so it does not darken the
   surface. Contrast matches within 0.4%, so it is not banding either. Both
   documented failure modes are measurably absent.

LIMITS, stated plainly: 400x300 through llvmpipe, static frames, one map, lava
only. Motion is not tested and shimmer under movement is a real artifact class
this cannot see. That is why the default stays 0 and why uhexen2-kyq6 exists -
the default-on decision wants motion on real hardware. But the open engineering
question on this bead, "does per-pixel work or does it alias like last time",
is answered.

gl_subdivide_size stays 64 - not because it is good (it is aliased, showing a
234-unit undulation against an intended 50) but because nothing affordable is
better and the per-pixel path makes it irrelevant for turb surfaces.

Repro for anyone re-checking: tools/warp_recon.py for the reconstruction
numbers, tools/bsp_subdiv.py for the geometry cost, and on sot/meso with
noclip: setpos -869 2926 -243 89 90 0 (overhead), setpos -869 2500 -270 4 90 0
(glancing).
close_reason: Closed

title: Alias model corruption: guard renders as giant blocky blob (fixes on reload)
description: Mathuzzz reports that some enemy guard alias models render as giant pixelated/blocky shapes — same height as a normal guard but expanded into huge polys with stretched texture samples. The 'black specs' originally reported are color variation between the giant polys. Self-resolves on map reload. Initially mistakenly filed as func_illusionary brush bug; corrected after screenshot review (Screenshot_20260509_120248.png shows good guard left vs bad guard right). Rendering path: R_DrawAliasModel for affected entities. Likely cause: stale alias VBO / pose pointer / shader uniform leaking from a previous model's state — reload re-uploads alias data and clears the stale pointer.
notes:
Root cause identified 2026-05-09 via video analysis:

The lerp logic in both R_SetupAliasFrame (legacy CPU) and R_CollectAliasInstance (SSBO) was sharing a copy-pasted broken implementation. The 53c6645b9 z-fight fix was correct for *that* z-fight bug but did not address the actual exploded-geometry bug.

Three concrete bugs in the pre-fix code:

1. previouspose was being used as a frame index (cl_parse stored ent->frame in it), then for multi-pose animation frames the previous sub-pose was computed as (int)(e->lerpstart / interval) % numposes — an arbitrary timestamp modulo numposes giving an essentially random sub-pose, lerped against an unrelated current sub-pose. This produced exactly the 'coherent geometry stretched to wrong positions' visual seen in the video.

2. R_CollectAliasInstance set inst->blend = 1.0f - lerpfrac with no clamp; GLSL mix() extrapolates outside [0,1] so any bogus lerpfrac (e.g. from stale lerpstart) produced exploded vertices. Legacy path was protected by 'do_lerp = (lerpfrac>0 && lerpfrac<1)'.

3. cl_parse did not flag LERP_RESETANIM on model change, so entity slot reuse with model swap could carry stale pose/timestamp state.

Why r_alias_gpu 0 didn't help: same buggy logic existed in both paths.
Why correlated with movement on winter.map: PVS visibility transitions trigger fresh frame changes, opening the bogus lerp window for ~100ms while the player passes by.

Fix applied (uncommitted, build clean):
- engine/hexen2/render.h: add LERP_RESETANIM2 (1<<3) for two-stage reset.
- engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c: introduce R_AliasResolveLerp shared helper using actual currentpose/previouspose pose indices (not frame indices), Ironwail RESETANIM/RESETANIM2 protocol, slid current->previous on pose change, blend clamped to [0,1]. Both R_SetupAliasFrame and R_CollectAliasInstance route through it so behavior stays in lockstep.
- engine/hexen2/cl_parse.c: set LERP_RESETANIM | LERP_RESETANIM2 on model change. Drop now-redundant U_FRAME pose bookkeeping (renderer manages lerpstart/lerptime).
- engine/hexen2/view.c: same RESETANIM | RESETANIM2 flag on viewmodel swap.

This is the alias-frame-lerp portion of the reverted commit 3e2633663 (Ironwail-parity refactor), without the r_lerpmove movement-interpolation portion that caused the regression in uhexen2-0nqf.

Awaiting Mathuzzz validation on winter.map.
close_reason: Clamp fix shipped in 650bdd2ff resolved the original exploded-geometry visual (sakabato confirms clean on r18 across winter/arena/keep). Mathuzzz's continuing reports describe a different symptom — texture/alpha corruption affecting BOTH alias models AND brush entities — which cannot be caused by alias frame lerp (brush ents don't go through that path). Tracking the new symptom separately. The Ironwail-parity refinements (pose-index lerp, LERP_RESETANIM2) remain a defensible cleanup but are masked by the clamp; not blocking.

title: Shadow/lighting regression: dark pillars on romeric6 (likely reversed-Z fallout)
description: After landing reversed-Z (commit 64a79b9ce, uhexen2-39sy), pillars on romeric6 (and all maps) render dark with light casting. Most likely a depth-state site missed during the flip.
close_reason: Misdiagnosed — dark pillars / shadow lighting issue is longstanding, not introduced by reversed-Z. The gl_reversed_z cvar added during investigation stays (default on). Real bug needs separate scoped issue when ready to debug.

title: Shadow/lighting regression: dark pillars on romeric6 (likely reversed-Z fallout)
description: After landing reversed-Z (commit 64a79b9ce, uhexen2-39sy), pillars on romeric6 (and all maps) render dark with light casting. Most likely a depth-state site missed during the flip. Suspects: shadow stencil volumes (gl_rmain.c:747 uses GL_EQUAL stencil + INCR + depth test), lightmap surface depth-prepass, or an unflipped GL_LEQUAL/GL_LESS in a per-frame state set. Bisect: revert 64a79b9ce locally to confirm reversed-Z is the cause.
notes: BISECT RESULT (2026-05-09): NOT a reversed-Z regression. First-bad commit is 90265f406 'fix: correct lighting on changelevel door brush entities' (2026-03-28). That commit removed two MLS_ABSLIGHT skip branches in engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c R_RenderBrushPoly and R_RenderBrushPolyMTex, forcing all MLS_ABSLIGHT brush entities through the lightmap path. Pillars on romeric6 (and similar maps) have surfaces with no baked lightmap data, so lightmap (0) * abslight = 0 = black. Plan: surgical revert — restore the two MLS_ABSLIGHT branches to their pre-90265f406 state (vanilla Hexen II behavior). Doors with abslight will look flat again, matching original game. Future improvement: gate the lightmap path on fa->samples != NULL to keep the door fix while not breaking pillars.
close_reason: Surgical revert of 90265f406 — restored the two MLS_ABSLIGHT skip branches in R_RenderBrushPoly and R_RenderBrushPolyMTex (engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c). Pillars on romeric6 lit correctly. Doors with abslight now look flat (vanilla Hexen II behavior). User verified.

title: Version string missing from main menu (regression)
description:
The Hexenwail version string used to appear on the main menu on boot
and no longer shows up.  Confirmed missing as of 0.7.4-alpha.r3.

Source of truth: engine/hexen2/menu.c:5080
  const char *l0 = \"Hexenwail \" HW_VERSION;

That literal exists and HW_VERSION resolves at compile time (either
HW_GIT_VERSION from cmake's git describe, or HW_BASE_VERSION).  So the
text is built — it's the *drawing* that regressed.  Either:
  - the menu screen that hosts l0 isn't being entered on boot (a
    different menu state opens first), or
  - the draw call for the watermark line was dropped or covered up
    by recent menu/conback work (e.g. Draw_MenuBackdrop, conback-as-
    backdrop changes around bc6fb586b / b778d0fc9), or
  - the watermark text is drawn but offscreen/clipped after
    conscale/menuscale changes.

Reproducer: boot to main menu without a level loaded.

Investigation pointers:
- grep for ENGINE_WATERMARK in engine/h2shared/draw.h:109 and any
  callers — that's the symbol the original watermark goes through.
- Recent menu commits to triage: f8def921a, c223deb42, 078d6813e,
  be52ab2c2, bc6fb586b, b778d0fc9, acb3aa6b5, da336bc24.
close_reason: Draw_MenuBackdrop now calls Draw_ConsoleVersionInfo. Built clean — needs visual verification on next boot.

title: Loading screens missing or completing too fast to see
description:
On level load / map transition / cutscene, loading screens either
don't appear at all or flash by too quickly to read.  Used to be
present long enough to read the chapter/loading text.

Possible causes worth checking:
- be52ab2c2 'fix: revert V_RenderView's con_forcedup glClear — kills
  loading scroll' shows recent churn around the loading-scroll path;
  may have over-corrected.
- 078d6813e 'fix: drop SCR_DrawConsole skip — Draw_MenuBackdrop
  already covers it' touched conback drawing during loads.
- cl_inlude.c is the cutscene/inline cinematic; check whether timing
  (cls.signon, scr_disabled_for_loading) ever sticks long enough.

Reproducer: start a new game from main menu, watch the transition
into demo1 / portal of praevus.

Investigation pointers:
- SCR_BeginLoadingPlaque / SCR_EndLoadingPlaque
- scr_disabled_for_loading + scr_disabled_time
- cl_inlude.c scrolling text path
- BeginLoadingPlaque blocking on framebuffer presentation
close_reason: Drop SCR_BeginLoadingPlaque early-returns (cls.state/cls.signon) so screen lock engages on initial map loads; paint Draw_MenuBackdrop behind the plaque when no world is loaded so the user sees the Hexen logo + LOADING text instead of black.

title: vid_restart leaves world VBO + GPU cull GL handles stale
description:
VID_ChangeVideoMode tears down most GPU state (post-process, world VBO, VBO/particles/shaders) before destroying the GL context, and rebuilds shaders/textures/lightmaps after recreating the context. But:

1. R_FreeWorldCull was missing from the shutdown list — cull_initialized stayed true with stale program/buffer handles.
2. R_BuildWorldVBO and R_BuildWorldCull were never called after re-init even when a level is loaded.

When a user triggers vid_restart from in-game (now reachable via the APPLY CHANGES menu entry for any resolution change), the next frame’s R_DispatchWorldCull dispatches against dead handles → glDrawElementsIndirect/glUseProgram/glBufferSubData all error every frame.

Fix:
- Add R_FreeWorldCull() to the shutdown list (before context destroy, so glDelete actually frees in the live context).
- After GL_BuildLightmaps in the re-init block, call R_BuildWorldVBO + R_BuildWorldCull when cl.worldmodel is non-null.

Test plan:
- Load any level, open menu, change resolution, press APPLY CHANGES → no GL_INVALID_OPERATION/INVALID_VALUE spew on the qconsole, world renders normally with r_gpucull 1.
close_reason: Fixed in this commit: R_FreeWorldCull added to shutdown, R_BuildWorldVBO + R_BuildWorldCull rebuilt after vid_restart when cl.worldmodel is set

title: Dlights inherit environment color (greenish player torch instead of warm orange)
description: Visual regression: player torch dlight (EF_LIGHT, hardcoded color 0.8/0.4/0.2 in cl_main.c:690-693) appears greenish instead of warm orange. Reported on 0.7.3-alpha.r1 master. Likely a regression from one of the recent perf commits (af8f0f22b sky stencil batch / 148ef15a1 chain hoist / ccc708e2e MSAA off / 27968232c early_fragment_tests / c3ede33b6 frustum-cull dlights / bc11f3aad dlight guard refine + R_BuildLightMap inline). Most suspicious: bc11f3aad — adds an inline R_BuildLightMap call in the world VBO fast path. The external R_AddDynamicLights call earlier in the loop is now redundant (R_BuildLightMap memsets blocklightscolor and re-adds dlights internally), but should be a no-op for correctness. Code analysis shows colors should be RGB-correct: cl_dlights[].color[0/1/2] -> blocklightscolor[i*3+0/1/2] -> atlas RGB -> world shader samples.
notes:
=== UPDATE: clarification + gl_flashblend test result ===

User clarifies the actual symptom: the torch USED to make nearby
surfaces appear orange-tinted (orange casting on grass / walls),
but NOW surfaces just brighten in their own natural color. So the
issue isn't 'dlight color is greenish' — it's 'orange casting
contribution is missing/weakened.'

gl_flashblend 1 test: orange returns BUT 'drowns the whole screen
in orange brown muddy tint instead of a mere casting (and its
abrupt and a big difference)'.

So:
- gl_flashblend 0 (current): no orange cast at all
- gl_flashblend 1: orange cast exaggerated, way too strong
- Pre-regression target: moderate orange cast — somewhere between

Hypothesis revised: a small ADDITIVE contribution that stacked on
top of the multiplicative lightmap dlight was disabled by recent
work. Pure Quake-style multiplicative math can't produce visible
orange tint on saturated colored surfaces (orange × pure green =
dim green, no tint). For the orange to show through, EITHER:
  - The lightmap dlight contribution was strong enough to saturate
    all 3 channels (then orange shows on neutral surfaces only)
  - OR an additive RGB pass added to the framebuffer

Possible regressed paths:
  - R_RenderDlights flare bubbles (only with gl_flashblend, so no)
  - R_DrawAllGlows for player-held torches? (only fires for models
    with XF_TORCH_GLOW set in Mod_SetAliasModelExtraFlags — that's
    wall torches, not player. Need to check if pre-regression the
    PLAYER somehow got XF_TORCH_GLOW too)
  - Some other additive path I haven't found

To pin down further, would need to bisect the recent perf commits.
Likely culprit ordering by suspicion:
  1. ccc708e2e (MSAA off + OIT pass tracking) — most invasive
  2. 148ef15a1 (state hoist: ATTR_COLOR per-chain -> hoisted)
  3. bc11f3aad (R_BuildLightMap inline)
  4. c3ede33b6 (frustum cull)

Quickest bisect path on current build:
  git checkout ccc708e2e^ -- '*.c' '*.h'  (revert all post-MSAA work)
  rebuild, retest with default gl_flashblend
  if orange returns -> regression is MSAA-onward
close_reason: Closed by user request

title: Regression: A2C fix broke translucent alias/sprite alpha (black halos on EF_TRANSPARENT, dlight sprites)
description:
Mathuzzz: 'in SoT mod, the breathing effect of the weapon has a black transparency where it should be clear and around dlight fires sprites'.

Caused by the r4 spray-paint fix (uhexen2-9g92, commit f6d74d53a): sworld_frag and salias_frag were writing fragColor = vec4(color.rgb, 1.0) unconditionally on the non-OIT path. That's correct for fence/cutout (A2C enabled, surviving fragments opaque) but breaks translucent draws — sprites at gl_rmain.c:514 use gl_shader_alias, EF_TRANSPARENT/ENTALPHA models also do, and all of those rely on the GL_SRC_ALPHA blend reading the actual per-vertex/per-fragment alpha. Forcing alpha=1 makes the GPU paint texture pixels with α=0 (RGB=black) as solid black halos.

Fix in r5: gate the alpha-force on u_alpha_threshold > 0.5. Cutout paths (fence world, EF_HOLEY alias) set threshold = 0.666 — alpha forced to 1 to defeat A2C. Translucent paths leave threshold at the 0.01 default and preserve color.a so blending works.
close_reason: Fixed in gl_shader.c: alpha-force gated on u_alpha_threshold > 0.5 so only the cutout path (fence/EF_HOLEY, threshold=0.666) writes alpha=1 to defeat A2C. Translucent paths (sprites, EF_TRANSPARENT, ENTALPHA) keep actual alpha for GL_SRC_ALPHA blending. Build OK; pending in-game confirmation by Mathuzzz.

title: Spray-paint splotches on every 3D surface (A2C dither on garbage alpha)
description:
Reported by Mathuzzz: 'all settings he was having like black spray-paint-ish splotches running across every 3d texture' on his GTX 1060.

Root cause (high confidence): opaque world and alias shaders in engine/h2shared/gl_shader.c write fragColor.a = tex.a * lm.a * v_color.a (multiplied through), not 1.0. Lightmap atlas textures and palette-decoded surface textures don't have a meaningful alpha channel, so the multiplied alpha is effectively garbage per fragment.

When MSAA is enabled (Mathuzzz had FSAA on), GL_SAMPLE_ALPHA_TO_COVERAGE is glEnable'd around every world/alias draw because r_alphatocoverage defaults to 1 (gl_rmain.c:106). A2C translates the fragment alpha into a stippled coverage mask — partial alphas dither into spray-paint patterns. Symptom matches exactly.

Bug is platform-agnostic but visually worse on NVIDIA because their A2C dither pattern is coarser than AMD/Intel.

Fix: after the alpha-test discard, force fragColor.a = 1.0 in:
- sworld_frag (gl_shader.c:308)
- salias_frag (gl_shader.c:346)
And any other opaque shader doing similar (check sky, alias instanced, etc.)

Discard-then-opaque is the standard pattern for cutout alpha rendering with MSAA + A2C.
close_reason: Fixed in gl_shader.c: sworld_frag and salias_frag now write fragColor = vec4(color.rgb, 1.0) on the opaque (non-OIT) path, after the alpha-test discard. Surviving fragments are by definition opaque, so forcing alpha=1 stops A2C's coverage dither from producing the spray-paint splotches reported by Mathuzzz. OIT path keeps actual alpha via the existing #define OIT toggle in GL_CompileOITFragShader. Pending in-game confirmation from Mathuzzz.

title: Epic: Match Ironwail (parity tracker)
description:
Umbrella epic for ongoing Ironwail feature parity work. Canonical scorecard lives in history/ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md (audited 2026-08-18 against Ironwail 4fa8bfbd; 85 ported / 2 partial / 0 missing / 10 N-A, ~98% parity excluding N/A).

UPSTREAM QUEUE IS EMPTY as of 2026-08-18. The only Ironwail commit since v0.8.2 (1eabd0df, 2026-08-11) is a version bump to 0.8.3-dev. All eight beads filed by the 2026-08-13 v0.8.1/v0.8.2 import audit are closed: sg5s, lssr, pxsz, z8je, nwx1, 7aok, r9qj, rf9y.

Partial features still tracked in the parity table:
- uhexen2-7ok0 - MD5mesh/IQM skeletal support (~50%: parser sound and hooked, no .md5anim parser, no draw dispatch, so a loaded MD5 model is silently invisible)
- uhexen2-48fx - Ironwail a65a88e frame-major alias pose SSBO (per-aliashdr_t but not frame-major)

Open Ironwail ports with no parity-table row (upstream work never started, not partial features - they are excluded from the parity percentage by design):
- uhexen2-r7zu - TEXPREF_UNCOMPRESSED for alpha-tested and 2D textures (blocked on uhexen2-8dks)
- uhexen2-ayrn - Light-trace cache for alias models
- uhexen2-yae - Menu system improvements

Decision beads:
- uhexen2-im9g - Bindless textures: revisit only with a measured need and hardware that can test it (scaffolding removed in 8124ed055)

Closed since the previous description was written: uhexen2-9a1l (dFdx/dFdy before discard, ported 2026-06-12), uhexen2-m183 (pointfile leak helpers, c293ae22a).
notes:
SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-08-20. The previous note said "REMAINING SCOPE: uhexen2-im9g (bindless textures) alone" and "this epic closes when im9g resolves". Both halves were wrong, in opposite directions.

im9g is now CLOSED — and not on hardware, which is what the old note assumed it would take. Its gate 1 was answered from the content side instead: DrawTextureChains issues one GL_Bind per texture chain, so the distinct textures a map's faces reference is a hard per-frame ceiling on world-pass binds, and that is knowable offline. Across all 59 shipped maps (data1, portals, sot, soc, karma2, GameOfTomes) the ceiling is 119 and the mean is 58. With gl_lmatlas defaulting to 1 the lightmap is one atlas bind per frame, and the alias path already binds per batch rather than per entity. A few hundred binds/frame cannot be a dominant bucket. tools/bsp_texcount.py makes it reproducible; see im9g for the full argument and for the correction that Ironwail DOES have a bindless path, contrary to im9g's own description.

The parity row stays ❌ Missing rather than becoming ➖ N/A: a gap declined on measured grounds is still a gap.

SCORECARD CORRECTED IN THE DOC 2026-08-20. history/ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md's table had drifted to 85 ✅ / 2 🔶 / 1 ❌ / 9 ➖ while the sentence under it claimed ~99% ported / 0% partial — the earlier promotion of the two 🔶 rows edited the row symbols and the prose but not the summary counts. Recounted mechanically from the row symbols: 87 / 0 / 1 / 9.

NOTE THE ➖ FIGURE: this bead's previous note said 10 N-A, and so did the doc's Bead Coverage paragraph. Counting the actual rows gives 9. Both corrected. 87 ported out of 88 non-N/A rows = 98.9%.

SO WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINS is uhexen2-ayrn, which the old note overlooked because it is IN_PROGRESS rather than open and therefore does not appear in `bd list --status=open`. It is a P0 Ironwail port (e2f39505, light trace cache for alias models), implemented and on master, building clean, and gated only on runtime verification: an in-game look with r_shadows 1 for correct shadow floor height and a still-animating lightstyle on a stationary model. A static audit on 2026-08-20 found no correctness defect — see the bead. The doc's Priority Shortlist now lists ayrn as the P1 in bindless's old slot.

Two of the three "open Ironwail ports with no parity-table row" the doc listed have since closed (uhexen2-r7zu, uhexen2-yae); only ayrn is left.

This epic therefore closes when ayrn's visual check passes, not when im9g resolves. Upstream queue is still empty: no Ironwail commit since v0.8.2 other than a version bump.

UPSTREAM BASELINE MOVED 2026-08-20 (evening). The description and the note above both say 'upstream queue is empty' against baseline 4fa8bfbd. Ironwail has since pushed 7ff4ec57 (2026-08-20 10:41Z, 'Use unsigned constants as masks where appropriate', 4 lines in Quake/gl_shaders.h).

Triaged and closed the same day as NOT APPLICABLE — uhexen2-7g1x. It adds 'u' suffixes to three int literals masked against uint operands. Our tree already writes all three the fixed way, and a full sweep of every bitwise-operator line in every shader we ship (29 lines across gl_shader.c, gl_postprocess.c, gl_worldcull.c, web_canvas_gl2.c) found no mixed-sign op anywhere. Reason we were ahead: we ship a '#version 300 es' path for WebGL2 and GLSL ES 3.00 has no implicit int->uint conversion, so a mixed-sign mask is a build break for us where it is merely untidy for desktop-only GLSL 4.30. Caveat recorded in 7g1x — that enforcement only covers gl_postprocess.c; the desktop-only shaders (salias_inst_vert under #ifndef USE_GLES, and the compute shaders in gl_worldcull.c) are clean by convention, not by compiler.

Upstream queue is empty again, now against baseline 7ff4ec57.

This epic still closes on uhexen2-ayrn's visual check. Unchanged.

CLOSING CONDITION MET 2026-08-20. The note above set this epic's gate as 'closes when ayrn's visual check passes, not when im9g resolves'. uhexen2-ayrn is now closed on a passing runtime verification, so the gate is satisfied and this epic closes with it.

Final state: 87 ported / 0 partial / 1 missing / 9 N-A = 98.9% of non-N/A rows. The single miss is bindless textures, declined on measured grounds (uhexen2-im9g), not outstanding work. Upstream queue empty against baseline 7ff4ec57 — the one commit past the old 4fa8bfbd baseline was triaged N/A as uhexen2-7g1x.

Not carried by this epic, still open on its own: uhexen2-2t38 (P2, MD5 skeletal render check against a real asset — winding/lighting/skin). It was never a parity-table row; MD5 support itself is ✅.

Future Ironwail ports should get a fresh epic rather than reopening this one.
close_reason: Parity gate met: uhexen2-ayrn's visual verification passed, which this epic's own note names as its closing condition. Final scorecard 87 ✅ / 0 🔶 / 1 ❌ / 9 ➖ (98.9% of non-N/A); the one ❌ is bindless, declined on measured grounds. Upstream queue empty at baseline 7ff4ec57.

title: Port Ironwail r_lerpmove + missing alias lerp flags (RESETANIM2, FINISH, MOVESTEP)
description:
Our model interpolation matches Ironwail's frame-lerp formula but is missing several pieces. r_lerpmove is the headline gap.

Gaps vs Ironwail (engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c, cl_parse.c, cl_main.c, render.h):

1. **r_lerpmove entirely absent** — no cvar, no currentorigin/previousorigin entity fields, no R_SetupEntityTransform-style renderer-side origin lerp. Step-movers (monsters, doors, platforms — nearly everything in Hexen II) appear to teleport between server snapshots rather than glide. Our msg_origins lerp in CL_RelinkEntities covers continuously-moving entities only.

2. **LERP_RESETANIM2 missing** — Ironwail uses a two-stage reset (RESETANIM snaps, RESETANIM2 next tick re-baselines previouspose). We only do stage 1, so first post-spawn / post-weapon-switch transition can lerp from stale pose.

3. **LERP_FINISH / lerpfinish field missing** — Ironwail uses lerpfinish for server-timed animation ends (death sequences). We hardcode lerptime = 0.1f, causing pop at animation boundaries.

4. **LERP_MOVESTEP declared in render.h:43 but never set** — dead flag, blocker for r_lerpmove.

5. **currentpose field declared in render.h:94 but never written** — only previouspose is used (cl_parse.c:751). Ironwail uses both.

6. **lerptime hardcoded to 0.1f** at cl_parse.c:753 — Ironwail derives from msgtime delta. Hexen II runs at 20 Hz (sys_ticrate 0.05) so 0.1f is 2 server frames of lerp latency, always slightly laggy.

Hexen II specifics to handle during port:
- 20 Hz tick rate: step interval is 50ms not 100ms; r_lerpmove cadence must reflect this.
- EF_ROTATE / EF_FLOAT entity flag adjustments in gl_rmain.c:1522-1524 must apply *after* origin lerp, not before.
- BSP entities (func_door, func_plat) must be excluded from r_lerpmove to avoid double-positioning.
- PimpModel overrides may have different frame counts than originals — LERP_FINISH wiring needs guards.

Suggested phased approach:
- Phase 1: Fix lerptime to derive from cl.mtime[0] - cl.mtime[1]; add LERP_RESETANIM2; write currentpose. (cheap, isolated)
- Phase 2: Implement r_lerpmove — new entity fields, CL_ParseUpdate wiring with teleport detection (>100 unit delta), renderer transform pass, BSP exclusion, 20 Hz cadence.
- Phase 3: LERP_FINISH / lerpfinish polish.

Reference: Ironwail r_alias.c R_SetupAliasFrame (~L67) and R_SetupEntityTransform (~L128).
close_reason: Implemented r_lerpmove + LERP_RESETANIM2 + LERP_MOVESTEP. Refactored R_AliasResolveLerp helper shared by both immediate and SSBO instanced alias paths. Lerptime now derived from frame interval (multi-pose) or 0.1 (single-pose) inside the renderer. LERP_FINISH/lerpfinish split out to follow-up issue (low-priority polish, requires protocol extension).

description: Objects visible through sky walls. Stencil pre-pass implemented but not fully working — may need fixes for scrolling sky, depth write state, or entity draw order.
close_reason: Fixed

title: Port r6303 one-to-one lighting/glows/pimp

close_reason: Lighting/pimp ported, glow regression on SoT demo1 split to new issue

title: GPU texture compression (BC/DXT)
description: Compress textures on GPU upload using BC1/BC3/BC7 formats to reduce VRAM usage and improve cache performance. Reference Ironwail's texture compression system with quality tuning.
notes:
Priority raised P4 -> P1 on 2026-08-18 under the standing rule that Ironwail porting tasks are P1 or above. This bead qualifies on two counts: it is itself a port ('Reference Ironwail's texture compression system'), and it is the hard blocker on uhexen2-r7zu, which is now P1 -- leaving the blocker at P4 would have parked a P1 permanently.

See also the caveat recorded on r7zu: 74e8eccde already uploads compressed DDS/KTX from HD replacement packs, so compressed textures reach the GPU today via content rather than via this engine-side compressor.
close_reason: Implemented in 387fc2e40. gl_compress_textures (default 0, archived) selects GL_COMPRESSED_RGBA_BPTC_UNORM in GL_Upload32 and the embedded-mips path, matching Ironwail's cvar name, default and format. Exemptions landed with it: TEX_FENCE/TEX_HOLEY checked centrally in GL_InternalFormat, new TEX_UNCOMPRESSED flag on conchars/tinyfont/menufont/conback/GL_LoadPicTexture/external-HUD. External-pack half: IMG_LoadReplacement gained allow_compressed and declines DDS/KTX containers for alpha-tested textures (fences detected by name, EF_HOLEY passed by the caller), falling through to the decoded image. Not runtime-verified visually — cvar is default-off so the risk is opt-in.

title: NVIDIA GTX 1060: GL_INVALID_FRAMEBUFFER_OPERATION spam causes <20 FPS
description: Mathuzzz reports <20 FPS on NVIDIA GTX 1060 6GB, driver 572.42, Windows. qconsole.log shows hundreds of GL_INVALID_FRAMEBUFFER_OPERATION errors per frame. The GL debug callback with GL_DEBUG_OUTPUT_SYNCHRONOUS calls Con_Printf for each error, creating a performance death spiral. Root cause: one of the postprocess FBOs is incomplete at draw time on NVIDIA (passes creation check). Also shader recompile warning: program 9 (world) being recompiled based on GL state.
close_reason: Rate-limited GL debug callback (20 error limit prevents Con_Printf death spiral). Switched FBO textures from GL_RGB10_A2 to RGBA8 — likely root cause of NVIDIA framebuffer incompleteness. PP_CheckFBO diagnostics added for next tester build.

title: Some brushes have fuzz defect
description: Visual artifacts/fuzz appearing on some brush surfaces. Confirmed on multiple Nvidia hardware (1050, 1060). Affects multiple testers (WhiteMagicRaven, Mathuzzz).
notes: gl_zfix 2 added: proper glPolygonOffset(1,1) for brush entities. Test commands for testers: gl_zfix 2 (polygon offset), gl_zfix 1 (origin nudge, default), gl_zfix 0 (off), r_dither 0 (disable dither), r_softemu 0 (disable post-process). Need tester screenshots comparing each setting.
close_reason: Fixed

title: [Critical] Cannot load into any map - Mesa memmove crash
description:
Engine crashes when attempting to load any map. Crash occurs in Mesa's __memmove_avx_unaligned_erms during glDrawElementsBaseVertex in tc_draw_user_indices_single. Affects both GPU and CPU culling paths, indicating core world rendering issue.

Previous fixes applied:
- Fixed FBO texture format (GL_UNSIGNED_INT_10_10_10_2)
- Fixed null texture pointer dereferences
- Added GPU compute shader bounds checking
- Added malloc error checking

Crash still persists with -r_gpucull 0, indicating issue is in world VBO/IBO setup or Mesa/AMD compatibility.

Reproduction: Launch game and try to load any map (e.g., 'map blrt1')
notes:
Added null pointer checks for:
- Vertex pointers in R_BuildWorldVBO
- Worldmodel and texture array in DrawTextureChains

Crash at 0x1c53c (118,588 bytes) suggests low-address memory access after GPU initialization. 
Without game data files, unable to reproduce crash directly. Issue likely in memory addressing or 
structure field offset calculation.
close_reason: Fixed by reverting commit 00c6aa953 which broke VAO state management in DrawTextureChains. The optimization tried to hoist setup out of the per-texture loop but broke restoration of VAO/program state when special surfaces were rendered.

title: Hide HUD during demo playback
description:
Hide HUD during demo playback (configurable per-demo).

Gameplay demos should preserve user HUD settings.

Per-Discord discussion, implement one of:
1. Config file approach: demo t9.dem loads t9start.cfg before, t9end.cfg after
   - Allows per-demo cvar overrides without modifying engine
2. Cvar-based whitelist: cvar listing demos that hide HUD
3. Demo-name matching: if demo name pattern matches, hide HUD

Preference: Config file approach (non-invasive, backward-compatible)

title: PimpModel glows
description: PimpModel glows should enable EF_GLOW automatically when glow color is non-zero. This allows moddable custom glow effects on props and other models. Already implemented in pr_cmds.c lines 484 and 491.
close_reason: Already implemented: EF_GLOW is set automatically when pimp_model glow_color is non-zero (pr_cmds.c:484,491)

title: Rain/snow particles not visible on Eidolon map
description: User reports no visible rain particles on the Eidolon map. Possible causes: particle pool exhaustion (32768 limit) during boss fight starving rain allocation, weather_rain entities not re-triggering after map change, or effects cleared on level transition. Rain particles skip the GPU SSBO path and use the CPU ImmBegin path (pt_rain/pt_snow check at r_part.c:1482-1483). AllocParticle returns NULL silently when pool is full (r_part.c:1270). Needs testing with particle count diagnostics.

title: Weapon texture expands/drags when moving

title: Port Ironwail mouse input handling 1:1
description: Current mouse input splitting (IN_UpdateViewAngles at render rate, IN_Move at physics rate) still has issues. Port Ironwail's exact mouse handling approach. Also: torch flames and static entities are being incorrectly interpolated by R_LerpEntity, causing position jitter. Static entities that don't move should skip interpolation.

title: Quick launch mode for map testing (-map flag)

title: Port Ironwail menu system improvements
description:
Port Ironwail's modernized menu system to Hexenwail. Key areas to evaluate and port:

- Mouse-driven menu navigation (click on items, scroll wheel support)
- Slider controls with finer granularity
- Tooltip/description text for menu options
- Menu scaling and layout for widescreen resolutions
- Searchable console command completion
- Key binding UI improvements (conflict detection, unbind support)
- Options organization and categorization
- Visual polish (smooth transitions, hover highlighting)

Reference: https://github.com/andrei-drexler/ironwail
Note: Hexenwail already has custom Display/Sound/Game submenus and BigString rendering — port should adapt Ironwail patterns to existing Hexen II menu aesthetic rather than replacing wholesale.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-08-20 against current master. Of the eight listed areas, five were already done and two are now split out:

DONE ALREADY (no work needed):
- Mouse-driven navigation: M_MouseToMenuItem gives hover-to-cursor across Main/Difficulty/Class/Load/Save/Multiplayer/Options/Display/Renderer/Keys; M_Keydown maps K_MOUSE1->Enter and K_MWHEELUP/DOWN->Up/Down (menu.c:7421). Gamepad nav landed alongside it (uhexen2-x552).
- Slider granularity: M_DrawSliderValue draws a numeric readout beside every slider (gamma, contrast, conscale, dither, wateralpha, liquidwarp, flash, motionblur, HDR exposure, conalpha) — ahead of Ironwail's bare sliders.
- Menu scaling / widescreen: CANVAS_MENU + SCR_CalcUIScale(&scr_menuscale), horizontally centred via M_CenterOfs, canvas fills the screen vertically.
- Console command completion: keys.c CompleteCommand does command/cvar/alias completion, PER-ARGUMENT completion via arg_completion_types (map/changelevel/game/record/playdemo/timedemo/exec/save/load/sky), columnized multi-match listing through Con_ShowList, and common-prefix extension. Beyond Ironwail here.
- Options organization: Display/Sound/Game submenus already exist (noted in the original description).

DONE NOW:
- Key binding UI: unbind already existed (M_UnbindCommand / M_UnbindDoubleCommand on BACKSPACE/DEL). Conflict detection added in c38159074 — M_Keys_NoteConflict reports '<KEY> taken from <ACTION>' when a rebind displaces another action.

SPLIT OUT (the real remaining work):
- uhexen2-8y3o: per-item description/tooltip text. Mostly content — a string per menu row across six submenus.
- uhexen2-u4iz: distinct hover highlight. Hover currently only moves the cursor.

This bead is now a tracker over those two children.
close_reason: Audited and substantially discharged 2026-08-20. Of the eight areas listed: five were already implemented (mouse nav, slider value readouts, menu scaling, options organization, and a console completion system that is ahead of Ironwail's — per-argument completion, columnized listing, common-prefix extension). Two were implemented now: bind-conflict reporting in the Keys menu (c38159074), and mouse hover actually following the mouse (uhexen2-u4iz — SDL motion never fed menu_mouse_x/y at all, so hover tracked clicks, and the first click on a row activated the previous selection). The eighth, per-item description text, is split out as uhexen2-8y3o (P2) — it is mostly content, a string per row across six submenus, and does not belong in a bundle bead. Full audit in this bead's notes.

title: Aspect ratio selector with common ratios and screen sizes
description: Add a menu/UI for selecting aspect ratio (4:3, 16:9, 16:10, 21:9, etc.) with corresponding common screen resolutions for each. Makes it easy for players to pick the right resolution without guessing.
close_reason: Superseded — resolution/mode selection works via Video menu

title: [bug] Vanilla scrolling sky broken in base game (no mods)
description: The scrolling sky rendering (non-skybox, base Hexen II without mods) is broken. This is the R_DrawSkyChain / EmitBothSkyLayers path for the default scrolling sky texture. Likely broken during the GL_Imm* conversion of gl_warp.c or gl_sky.c.
close_reason: Fixed: sky was using gl_shader_world (lightmap multiply) instead of gl_shader_sky, and EmitSkyPolysMulti was not converted to GL_Imm*

title: [bug] Textures dragging/smearing across screen when camera turns
description: Some textures appear to drag or smear across the screen as the camera rotates, instead of staying fixed to their surfaces. Likely a matrix sync issue in the new shader/VBO pipeline — the software matrix stack may not be in sync with the hardware matrix for some draw calls, causing vertices to be projected with a stale MVP.
close_reason: Brute-force matrix sync fix in GL_ImmEnd, pending Phase 10 full removal of hardware matrix stack

title: GL renderer ignores pixel aspect — AdaptFovx uses raw pixel dimensions, so 320x200-class modes get a 16:10 FOV on a 4:3 display
description:
Raised by Spoike on Discord 2026-08-24, in the SoC menu thread:

  'vga mode 13h being just 320*200 defines quake's (and even winhexen2's)
   minimum supported resolution. allowing any virtual canvas size to be
   smaller than that should be considered an engine bug. and any menus/etc
   requiring bigger should also be considered a bug.
   which is fun, cos that apparently 16:10 res is actually a 4:3 one. which
   keeps life interesting. yay for non-square pixels.
   kinda requires knowing whether you're running fullscreen, or windowed.'

Both halves check out.

PIXEL ASPECT. AdaptFovx (gl_screen.c) and CalcFovy take raw width/height and have no pixel-aspect term. The software renderer has always had one — r_main.c:108 declares pixelAspect and r_main.c:493-504 carries Raven's own note:

    // 320*200 1.0 pixelAspect = 1.6 screenAspect
    // 320*240 1.0 pixelAspect = 1.3333 screenAspect
    // proper 320*200 pixelAspect = 0.8333333

with screenAspect = vrect.width * pixelAspect / vrect.height, and d_modech.c:87 branches on pixelAspect > 1.4. So the original code knew, and the GL path dropped it. On a 320x200-derived mode the GL renderer computes the field of view for a 1.6 pixel ratio while the display is showing 4:3, and fov_effective (uhexen2-vsxi) reports that overstated number to gamecode as well.

Spoike's last line is the hard part and should not be glossed: the engine cannot infer the display aspect from the pixel count alone. 320x200 windowed on a modern panel really is 16:10 with square pixels; fullscreen through a scaler it is 4:3. So this needs either a vid_pixelaspect cvar, or fullscreen/windowed detection, or both. Do not 'fix' it by hardcoding 1.2 for 320x200.

MINIMUM RESOLUTION, and a related inconsistency worth cleaning up while in there. gl_vidsdl.c:169-171 define MIN_WIDTH 320 and MIN_HEIGHT 240, with '//#define MIN_HEIGHT 200' commented out directly above — someone deliberately raised the floor. But the console-size check at gl_vidsdl.c:690 reads 'if (h < 200 /* MIN_HEIGHT */' — a literal 200 with a comment naming a macro that is actually 240. Two different floors, one of them lying about which constant it is.

Per Spoike, 320x200 is the floor Quake and WinHexen2 define, so a 240 floor is arguably already wrong, and the vid_config_consize path enforcing 200 while MIN_HEIGHT says 240 means the two disagree about what the minimum even is.

Practical relevance to the SoC menu report (uhexen2-461l): if the reporter's window is a 16:10 pixel count displayed as 4:3, fov_effective's 100.388855 is overstated and the true display FOV is nearer 90 — which changes the menu framing arithmetic in that bead.

title: Dlight cull pops: arbitrary radius+1024 distance test, and both culls run on last frame's camera
description:
Mathuzzz, Discord 2026-08-23: "lights he sees far off in distance get dlight turned on as he approaches/changes view angle its awkward to look at". The concrete defect behind uhexen2-olku.

R_PushDlights (engine/h2shared/gl_rlight.c) drops a dlight on either of two binary tests, and both are wrong in a way that shows:

1. DISTANCE, gl_rlight.c:381, from 428416680 (2026-03-23):
     if (dist_sq > (l->radius + 1024) * (l->radius + 1024)) continue;
   Eye-to-light, hardcoded 1024, no cvar. This is not a correctness cull -- a
   torch 3000 units down a hall legitimately lights the wall beside it and the
   player can see that wall. Torch radius 150 puts the cutoff at 1174 units,
   which is room scale, so vanilla's torch lighting winks out across ordinary
   play distances. This is the "as he approaches" half.

2. FRUSTUM, from 4d7108fa1 / uhexen2-si07 (2026-05-05): culled if the light's
   sphere lies wholly outside one of the four side planes. This one IS sound --
   R_AddDynamicLights only touches luxels within radius of the light, so a
   sphere fully off-screen lights nothing visible -- but it reads frustum[],
   and frustum[] belongs to the previous frame.

3. STALE CAMERA, the reason (2) pops at all. R_PushDlights is called from
   V_RenderView (view.c:1155) BEFORE R_RenderView. r_origin is written by
   R_SetupFrame and frustum[] by R_SetFrustum, both inside R_RenderScene
   (gl_rmain.c:5011/5013) -- after. So every frame both culls run against the
   previous frame's eye and view planes, and turning the view makes a light
   wink out for a frame at the boundary. That is the "changes view angle" half.
   r_refdef is already current at that point (V_CalcRefdef and SCR_CalcRefdef
   both ran first), so the fresh camera is right there unused.

4. NEGATIVE RADIUS INVERSION, same loop: the test is (d < -l->radius), and
   EF_SPIT allocates dark lights with radius -120 (cl_main.c:956), so it reads
   as (d < +120) and culls precisely the dark lights that are INSIDE the
   frustum. Harmless today because R_AddDynamicLights rejects a negative rad
   before it reaches a luxel, but it is backwards and will bite whoever makes
   dark lights work.

FIX: drop the distance test, keep the frustum test, and evaluate it against a
camera derived from r_refdef instead of the stale globals; fabs() the radius.
Software renderer is unaffected -- r_light.c's R_PushDlights has neither cull.

Note the culls only ever gated WORLD surfaces. Alias models (gl_rmain.c:1613)
and brush-model surfaces (gl_rmain.c:2538) loop cl_dlights with no distance and
no frustum test, so under the old distance cull a torch stopped lighting the
wall while it kept lighting the monster in front of it, which is why the pop
was so legible. Removing the distance cull closes that gap too: a light the
frustum test rejects lights nothing visible, models included.
notes:
ANSWERED IN GAME, on t9.dem (SoT keep) via a headless run: the thing visible from a distance is the GLOW corona, not the dlight. gl_glows 0 removes the orange halo entirely and leaves a small flame sprite on a still-warmly-lit wall (torch_glow_ab.png in the repo root).

So Mathuzzz's sentence splits cleanly across the two subsystems: what he SEES far off is R_DrawGlow's corona, what TURNS ON as he approaches is the dlight this bead removed the cut-off from. Two hardcoded 1024s ramping in opposite directions and crossing at nearly the same distance -- see uhexen2-69mo for the corona half, which is deliberate (intensity = distance/1024, 'fades as you approach') and is NOT to be touched until this fix has been confirmed in the field, or the re-test has two variables in it.

title: Expose the adapted FOV to gamecode — mods placing view-relative props can only read the unadapted 'fov'
description:
Found while diagnosing why BloodShot's Shadows of Chaos pop-up menus fill the screen on some setups and not others (2026-08-23).

SoC draws its menus as a flat 4-vertex billboard entity (soc/models/menuoptn.mdl, 128x80 units) placed in front of the player by Menu_Project in its progs.dat:

    dest = eye + v_forward * (25.5 - 0.15 * cvar("fov"))

with .scale 0.25, so the panel is 32x20 units, and .t_width 16 confirms the 16-unit half-width. At the default fov 90 that puts it 12 units out, where it subtends 2*atan(16/12) = 106.26 degrees.

106.26 is exactly the horizontal FOV that AdaptFovx (gl_screen.c:366) produces for fov 90 on a 16:9 display -- both are 2*atan(4/3). The mod was tuned on 16:9, and there it fills the screen width exactly, 1.00x. On narrower aspects the same placement overflows: 1.06x at 16:10, 1.18x at 4:3, 1.23x at 5:4. On 21:9 it under-fills at 0.88x.

The mod is not doing anything wrong. It reads the only FOV the engine offers gamecode -- the 'fov' cvar, which is the unadapted 4:3 value -- while the engine renders with AdaptFovx's result, and nothing publishes that. Any mod placing something at a fixed distance to occupy a fixed fraction of the screen has the same problem, and it gets worse the further the display is from whatever the author tuned on.

Proposal: publish the adapted horizontal FOV as a read-only cvar the engine updates whenever the refdef is recalculated (SCR_Callback_refdef already exists), so QC can read it via cvar(). Name it to make the distinction obvious -- fov_horizontal or fov_effective rather than a near-synonym of 'fov'. Costs a Cvar_SetValue on refdef recalculation, which is rare.

Related sharp edge worth telling mod authors about regardless: that formula reaches zero distance at exactly fov 170, which is the console clamp on 'fov' (gl_screen.c:425). At fov 170 the panel sits on the eye. The menu slider clamps 60-130 (menu.c:3954) so the slider cannot reach it, but the console can. Not our bug -- worth a line in the modder docs, see uhexen2-pe7h.
close_reason:
Implemented in the commit above. fov_effective and fov_effective_y, both CVAR_ROM, published from the single point in each renderer that computes r_refdef.fov_x/fov_y (gl_screen.c SCR_CalcRefdef and screen.c SCR_CalcRefdef), so they are exactly as fresh as what is rendered — including through a zoom, since SCR_UpdateZoom sets vid.recalc_refdef every frame it moves.

Expected values at fov 90: 4:3 -> 90.00, 16:9 -> 106.26, 21:9 -> 120.51; fov_effective_y is 73.74 at all three, which is the point of Hor+.

Build green both targets, both cvar names present in the binary. NOT runtime-verified — user is testing from master.

For mod authors: SoC's menu placement becomes aspect-correct as roughly
    dist = 16 / tan(cvar("fov_effective") * 0.5 * M_PI / 180)
for a 32-unit-wide panel, instead of the hardcoded 25.5 - 0.15*fov. That also removes the fov 170 cliff where the old formula reaches zero distance.

title: EF_SPECIAL_TRANS alpha means transparency, not opacity — normalise it at upload so OIT stops guessing
description:
Split out of uhexen2-4y6w, which fixed the field-visible half.

EF_SPECIAL_TRANS carries an inverted alpha convention end to end for the 8-bit path: gl_draw.c:2718 writes ColorPercent[p&15] into the alpha channel, where a HIGHER value means MORE transparent, and R_DrawAliasModel compensates with a reversed blend func. The two agree and Raven's models look right.

They only agree under the fixed-function blend path. Under OIT the func is never set -- R_SetBlendFunc is inside 'if (!OIT_InPass())' -- so weighted-blended OIT receives a transparency where it expects an opacity, and every legacy EF_SPECIAL_TRANS model is composited by its inverse. Nobody has reported this, which is worth noting: either the models involved rarely land in the OIT pass, or the error is subtle enough to read as 'a bit off'. Verify before assuming it is real.

The proper repair is to make alpha mean opacity everywhere: invert ColorPercent at upload (alpha = 255 - ColorPercent[...]) and delete the reversed blend func, at which point skin_replaced stops being needed for this and the OIT path is correct for free.

Deliberately NOT done alongside the field fix. It changes how every one of Raven's translucent models draws, so it needs a visual sweep across the spell effects, the Cleric's raven staff, and the mission-pack content -- not a same-day change on top of a report.

title: Mathuzzz: dynamic lights vanish entirely in vanilla Hexen II, and keep disappearing in SoT
description:
Mathuzzz, Discord 2026-08-22: 'not sure what happened, but in the vanilla game the dynamic lights disappeared completely, they are still present in SoT, but keep on disappearing (provided the video)'.

TIMING MATTERS FOR TRIAGE. This was reported against the build he had on 2026-08-22, i.e. r15, and r16 then shipped two dlight changes:
  - a903570fc 'honour misc_modelpimp flag 64 on every steady light effect' -- gated EF_BRIGHTLIGHT/EF_DIMLIGHT/EF_DARKLIGHT/EF_LIGHT on XF_NO_DLIGHT, which is exactly a change that can make lights disappear if the flag is being read when it should not be
  - bde39a39c 'stop inferring a glow orb from colour on r15-era misc_modelpimps'
Either could plausibly have caused this, or fixed it, or be unrelated. Re-confirm on r16 BEFORE investigating -- the same message listed four other items that r16 has since fixed, so this list is stale by construction.

If it does reproduce on r16, the flag-64 gating in a903570fc is the first suspect precisely because it was written to suppress lights, and 'vanilla loses them entirely while SoT keeps some' is the signature of a rule keyed to model or entity identity rather than to the map.

He provided a video in the thread. Get the link into this bead.
notes: uhexen2-137k (dae42ff59) removes the distance cull and fixes the stale-camera frustum cull, which is the mechanism proposed in the notes above. Re-test before doing anything else here: if the vanilla torches come back, this bead is done; if they are still absent at close range, the cause is something other than the culls and the flag-64 line of enquiry is back on.

title: Port v_gunkick: smooth punchangle decay instead of the vanilla step
description:
BloodShot, Discord 2026-08-23: 'is there a cvar equivalent to v_gunkick from quake? It would be nice to be able to smooth out punchangle like modern quake engines'.

This is the easy kind of request: it exists upstream, we track Ironwail for parity, and the user's standing direction is to import from the open-source Quake engines rather than re-derive. Ironwail/QuakeSpasm carry v_gunkick with the usual three settings -- 0 none, 1 vanilla instant/stepped, 2 smooth -- driving how punchangle is applied and decayed.

Hexen II side: punchangle is decayed in DropPunchAngle (engine/hexen2/sv_user.c), 'len -= 10*host_frametime', server-side and already frametime-scaled. The smoothing Quake engines add is client-side in V_CalcViewOffset / V_CalcRefdef, so the port is a render-time treatment of the value rather than a change to the decay.

Confirm the cvar name and semantics against Ironwail's source before implementing, and match them exactly -- the value of porting it is that people's existing configs and expectations carry over, which a renamed or renumbered cvar throws away.

Hexen II has more punchangle sources than Quake does (spells and artifacts, not just weapons), so check the smooth mode against a few of those and not only a weapon before defaulting it on. Default to vanilla behaviour unless it clearly reads better everywhere.
close_reason:
Ported in the commit above from Ironwail/QuakeSpasm (johnfitz), matching the cvar name, the three modes, the default of 2 and the 0.1s blend window exactly — configs and expectations from other engines carry over unchanged.

Implementation mirrors upstream: v_punchangles[2] in view.c holds current/previous, CL_ParseClientdata stamps cl.punchtime on change, V_CalcRefdef blends. Only deviation is cl.punchtime being a double rather than upstream's float, since cl.time is a double here; not behavioural.

Build green, cvar present in the binary. NOT visually verified — Hexen II draws punchangle from spells and artifacts as well as weapons, so mode 2 wants a look at a few of those, not just a weapon, before anyone relitigates the default. Ask BloodShot, who asked for it.

title: TGA alpha is inverted for models carrying one transparency flag but correct for another
description:
BloodShot, Discord 2026-08-23: 'seems like tga alpha channels are inverted for these flags', with video https://i.imgur.com/AIwNWPz.mp4 and screenshots of the flag in question. He explicitly contrasts: 'mdls tagged with this flag tga transparency works fine for comparison' -- so one model transparency flag inverts the alpha and another does not.

That asymmetry is the whole lead: both paths read the same TGA through the same loader, so the inversion is downstream of decode, in whichever per-flag branch decides how alpha is applied. A global loader bug would break both.

Start from the r15/r16 work in this area, since the timing is suspicious:
  - uhexen2-93a8 / 0a21bec43 'fix(alias): do not alpha-test a replacement skin that is really translucent' changed how a model flagged as cut-out treats a skin carrying a real gradient
  - uhexen2-5dit is already open on that change's blast radius across 82 world models
Check whether the inverting flag is the one that path now routes differently.

Needed from BloodShot to make this actionable: the two flag values (the screenshots show them but the numbers should be written down here), and ideally one of the .mdl + .tga pairs. Ask -- he has been forthcoming with repro material.

Note this is separate from uhexen2-mfql: that is about material sidecars that do not exist yet, this is about the alpha channel of a skin that already loads.
close_reason:
Fixed in e051320d7. Root cause proven by reading, not inferred: R_DrawAliasModel's EF_SPECIAL_TRANS branch is the ONLY one that reverses the blend func to (GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, GL_SRC_ALPHA), and it is correct to for the 8-bit path, where gl_draw.c:2718 writes ColorPercent[p&15] into alpha as a TRANSPARENCY. A replacement TGA carries opacity instead, so the same func renders it inside out. EF_HOLEY and EF_TRANSPARENT reverse nothing, which is exactly the asymmetry BloodShot reported. New model field skin_replaced keys the choice on where the skin came from, leaving Raven's content on unchanged code.

CAVEAT: he did not transcribe the two flag values, so the identification of EF_SPECIAL_TRANS as 'these flags' is inference from the symptom shape. The inversion is real and fixed either way; whether it is HIS inversion needs his confirmation. Reopen if his flags turn out to be something else.

Also recorded for later: under OIT the func is never set, so a LEGACY EF_SPECIAL_TRANS skin hands weighted-blending a transparency where it wants an opacity. Proper repair is to normalise alpha at upload and delete the special func — see the follow-up bead.

title: centerprint text renders in the console with literal escape characters, and overrides sprints
description:
BloodShot, Discord 2026-08-23, with two screenshots: 'it seems the centerprints here are displaying in console with escape characters and overriding the sprints'.

Two separate defects in one report:
  1. Centerprint payloads are reaching the console at all, and when they do their formatting escapes are printed literally rather than interpreted or stripped.
  2. They override sprints (the per-client string prints), so a mod that uses both loses one.

Hexen II centerprints carry markup that vanilla's console never sees. Look at the svc_centerprint / svc_centerprint2 path in cl_parse.c and whatever routes print text to Con_Printf. Suspect a print path that was widened for debugging and never narrowed, or a string handler that stopped consuming its escapes.

Screenshots are in the Discord thread; ask BloodShot for the raw strings if the images are not legible enough to reconstruct the markup. A mod that leans on centerprint for UI -- his does, he mentions custom menus in the fixangle report -- is unusable while this is broken, so it is worth more than its cosmetic appearance suggests.
close_reason:
Half fixed in 2c157c730, half diagnosed as not-a-bug. Screenshot finally supplied and read (centerprint_overlaps_Hexen_II_Screenshot_2026.08.22_-_12.25.42.14.png).

FIXED — 'overriding the sprints': Plaque_Draw and Info_Plaque_Draw suppressed only on 'scr_con_current == vid.height', a fully-dropped console. The ordinary half-height console left them drawing straight over the console text. Both renderers had it (gl_screen.c:1365,1393 and screen.c), both fixed. Centerprints already behaved correctly via SCR_CheckDrawCenterString2's key_dest check, so this makes the plaque path agree with the centerprint path.

NOT A BUG — 'escape characters': they are '@', Hexen II's line separator. FindTextBreaks (screen.c:206) treats '@' as a forced line break and swallows it, so plaques and centerprints render it right; the console has never interpreted it in any Hexen II engine and prints it literally. The engine does NOT echo centerprints to the console — svc_centerprint has exactly one consumer (cl_parse.c:1517 -> SCR_CenterPrint) and PF_centerprint writes only svc_centerprint. So the console copy is his mod calling a print builtin alongside the plaque with one string formatted for the plaque. Raven's shipped gamecode never puts '@' in a message string (checked all 718 .hc files; only two comment hits), which is why it has never surfaced.

Rejected fix: translating '@' to newline in console output. It would fix his cosmetics and break every '@' in chat text and player names for everyone.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the screenshot's version banner reads 'Hexenwail 0.8.0-beta.r14 (Win64)' — four releases stale, and r15 shipped two console fixes (056af32b0). The plaque guard is unchanged since, so the fix stands, but ask him to re-confirm on r17 before assuming anything else in that screenshot is current.

title: Paladin purifier projectiles spawn too far forward at 0.05s ticks, correct at the fastest tick
description:
BloodShot, Discord 2026-08-23: 'You can also see it on the paladin purifier, at ticrate 0 the projectiles spawn correctly, but at 0.05 they spawn too far forward.'

Distinct from uhexen2-g8lb despite arriving in the same message. g8lb is rate-INdependent (it is the render/physics split). This one is explicitly rate-DEpendent: the error scales with the tick interval, so it is a per-tick quantity applied to a spawn position.

Hypotheses to test in order, cheapest first:
  1. The projectile is spawned at owner.origin + v_forward*offset and then immediately integrated one full tick by SV_Physics before the client ever sees it, so the visible spawn point is offset by velocity*frametime. That is ~16 units at 0.05s for a 320 u/s projectile and ~4 at 1/72 -- the right order of magnitude and the right direction (too far FORWARD).
  2. The spawn uses the player's interpolated/predicted origin, which leads the true origin by up to one tick.
  3. QC-side: the purifier's spawn code scales an offset by a hardcoded tick constant. Check gamecode/hc/h2/paladin.hc and its projectile before blaming the engine -- if it is QC, this belongs with uhexen2-pe7h instead.

Was reported against the OLD build where sys_ticrate drove the tick, so 'ticrate 0' meant the 0.01 clamp (100 Hz) and '0.05' meant 20 Hz. On r16 the equivalent A/B is sv_physfps 250 vs sv_physfps 20. Re-confirm on r16 before digging: the 72 Hz default may already have moved this below the visible threshold, in which case it is a much smaller problem than it looked.

Mathuzzz on the same day: 'this can be related to the archer walking problems I mentioned before as he uses different update rate for patrolling' -- he later confirmed archer movement is fixed on r16, which is weak evidence that this family was mostly the tick rate and may already be resolved.

title: Document the sv_physfps contract for modders: which QC idioms are rate-dependent
description:
sv_physfps (uhexen2-skjv, shipped in 0.8.0-beta.r16) moved the server tick from 20 Hz to 72 Hz. BloodShot field-confirmed the fix on 2026-08-23 but found one thing in his mod that broke: a continuous Half-Life-2-style grab that holds an entity in front of the player now trails the target, and tracks exactly again at sv_physfps 20. Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ex-Ozf9Wfl0

## The mechanism, and why 20 is special rather than merely better

The QC idiom for 'move this entity onto the target this frame' is

    held.velocity = delta * 20;

because 20 == 1/0.05 == 1/frametime at the old tick rate. Per tick the entity travels velocity*frametime, so at 20 Hz that closes exactly 100% of the gap — a perfect snap with zero tracking lag. At 72 Hz the same constant closes 20/72 = 28% per tick, which is a proportional controller with finite gain, so it lags a moving target by roughly target_speed/gain. At a 300 u/s strafe that is on the order of ten-plus units — visible, and exactly what he filmed.

Note the shape of the symptom: it is not 'worse at 72, better at 20', it is 'exact at 20'. Any report with that shape is a hardcoded 1/frametime.

## Shipped gamecode is clean — audited, not assumed

Grepped all 718 .hc files. The velocity*10 / velocity*20 sites in h2/ are all ONE-SHOT impulses, which are rate-independent because the entity then integrates ballistically:
  - h2/skullwiz.hc:890,895 — Skull Wizard push, fires once per attack behind a last_attack gate
  - h2/archer.hc:223 — gold arrow knockback, once on impact
  - h2/triggers.hc:1411,1416 — trigger push, once on touch
None is a per-frame controller. HX_FRAME_TIME (h2/constant.hc:8 = 0.05) has 199 uses in h2/, and every one is a think interval or an effect duration — real-time quantities that stay correct at any tick rate, and are quantized MORE finely at 72 Hz, not less. The single rate conversion, h2/crossbow.hc:359, divides elapsed time rather than a per-tick quantity, so it is also fine.

So this is a mod-compat documentation problem, not an engine problem, and not a shipped-content problem.

## What to write, and where

Raven's own QC already demonstrates the correct idiom — h2/client.hc:1326 scales water friction by the frametime global, which is declared in h2/global.hc:12 and set by the engine every tick from host_frametime. The guidance is therefore 'use what the base game already uses':

  - Snap to a target: held.velocity = delta / frametime  (never a literal 20)
  - Damped follow: held.velocity = delta * K with K in units of 1/sec, comfortably below 1/frametime. Already rate-independent; only K ~= 1/frametime is pathological
  - Think scheduling with a fixed interval is fine as-is and needs no change
  - A mod that cannot be changed can ship a .cfg setting sv_physfps 20, or call cvar_set (builtin #72, h2/builtin.hc:148) — verified present

Worth a docs/ page rather than only release notes, since this will be asked again by the next modder. Cross-reference from the sv_physfps entry.

Also worth telling anyone reporting this: test r_lerpmove 0 first. It separates 'the entity really is behind' from 'the entity is drawn behind', and costs one cvar.
notes:
Raised P2 -> P1 2026-08-23 on the user's direction in Discord: 'Your mod compatibility IS my specific goal - not a low priority now that we have the new renderer and web renderer too. Renderer > game code > mod compat > fun.' Mod compat is now the active phase, so this stops being a docs-someday item.

Second data point from BloodShot the same day: 'Here is an example with the player legs as well' — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f0p4W-p7WWI — alongside the original grab video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ex-Ozf9Wfl0. Player legs are a separate model the mod positions every frame, so if it uses the same delta*20 idiom it is the same cause; two independent features in one mod failing the same way is what you would expect from one shared helper.

Before assuming QC in either case, have him run r_lerpmove 0. That separates 'the entity really is behind' from 'the entity is drawn behind', costs one cvar, and if the lag vanishes then this is ours and not his — the fixed-window render-time lerp for step-movers is exactly the sort of thing that would trail a fast-moving carried object.

title: r_texture_external was a dead cvar whose name promised the HD-texture feature
description:
ORIGINAL PREMISE WAS WRONG, corrected 2026-08-23 before any fix shipped. The bead claimed replacement textures were off by default and that _glow/_luma sidecars silently did nothing until r_texture_external 1. That is not what the code did.

What was actually true: IMG_LoadReplacement (engine/h2shared/img_load.c) had NO cvar gate at all. PNG/TGA/PCX/DDS/KTX replacements and their _glow/_luma sidecars loaded unconditionally in both renderers. The only two reads of r_texture_external, gl_model.c:557 and model.c:468, sit inside '#ifdef WAL_TEXTURES' — and h2config.h:212 #undefs WAL_TEXTURES. So the cvar was compiled out entirely: registered, archived, shown at 0, and doing nothing whatsoever.

That is worse than the bug originally described, because the name promises exactly the feature people ask about. Anyone debugging a pack that would not show up would find r_texture_external 0, conclude that was the cause, set it, see no change, and be no wiser. The value was actively misleading.

Fix: give the cvar the meaning its name claims. IMG_LoadReplacement now returns false when it is 0, and the default moves 0 -> 1 so behaviour is unchanged for everyone who never touched it while HD packs gain a real off-switch. The dead WAL reads are left alone; that code cannot compile in this configuration anyway.

Note r_texture_external_hud is a separate cvar, still defaulting to 0, and it IS live — it gates HUD/2D pic replacements at gl_draw.c:215,312. Whether that should also default on is a real question but a different one: HUD art is uploaded without mipmaps and is what block compression damages most, so the conservative default may be deliberate. Not changed here.
notes: Origin, for the record: no field reporter. It came out of answering Garrett (Monolyth-42)'s material-maps question on Discord 2026-08-23 — I misread the code while drafting that answer, told the thread HD packs needed r_texture_external 1, and found the dead cvar while checking myself. Credit for prompting it goes to Garrett's question; the bug is mine.
close_reason: Fixed in 4b47643cf. IMG_LoadReplacement now honours r_texture_external, and the default moves 0 -> 1 so behaviour is unchanged for anyone who never set it. The bead's original premise was wrong and is corrected in its description: the cvar was not gating replacements, it was compiled out via #undef WAL_TEXTURES and doing nothing at all.

title: Mathuzzz: 'transparent pixels on the wall' — capture2.rdc arrived truncated (77.7%), needs re-send
description:
Field report from Mathuzzz (Discord), 2026-08-22: 'Transparent pixels on the wall', with a RenderDoc capture attached.

STATUS: BLOCKED on a complete capture. The file in the tree is 'capture2 (1).rdc.crdownload' — a Chrome part-download that never finished.

  on disk        40,374,272 B (38.5 MiB)
  section        'renderdoc/internal/framecapture', compressed length 51,751,896 B
  body runs      188,183 .. 51,940,079
  MISSING        11,565,807 B  => the file is 77.7% of the 49.5 MiB it should be

renderdoccmd 1.44 (matching the capture's own version string, '1.44 050034') refuses it:
  'Replaying the capture encountered invalid/corrupted data: Error reading from file:
   hit end of file unexpectedly. Out of disk space or truncated file?'
So the GL command stream — the thing that would actually name the cause, per the sp7v/khsa precedent — cannot be read at all.

WHAT SURVIVED. The RDC header and its embedded full-res frame JPEG are intact (offset 40, 188,035 B, 1680x1050) and were extracted. Scratch copies: capture2_frame.jpg and capture2_frame_annotated.png in the repo root (gitignored — attach to the bead if they need to persist).

WHAT THE FRAME SHOWS. Gold/sandy room, HP 100 AC 0, 518 FPS, console line 'Wrote shots/hexen0010.tga'; a large dragon/serpent model lower-right. Against a heavily-shadowed inner corner there is a tight cluster of ~13 small bright gold quads, screen-axis-aligned, 1x1 to 7x7 px, peak rgb(154,126,53) against a wall of rgb(68,45,25) — about 2.2x the surrounding surface. Irregular spacing, NOT a regular grid, so this is not the khsa screen-door pattern.

TWO READINGS, NEITHER CONFIRMABLE FROM A JPEG:
 (a) Ordinary billboard particles that should be OCCLUDED by that wall and are drawing through it. Sizes vary with distance, which matches R_DrawParticles' billboard path (scale = SCALE_BASE + dist*0.004) and rules OUT square/point mode (glPointSize(2.0f), fixed 2 px). 'Transparent pixels on the wall' is a fair lay description of particles visible through geometry.
 (b) Ordinary particles in front of the corner, i.e. not the defect at all, and Mathuzzz means something else in frame.

RULED OUT BY READING THE CODE (so the re-sent capture need not re-litigate these):
 * World fullbright mask (sjvf/9a1l, sworld_frag u_texture2). Inert on retail data: gl_vidsdl.c derives vid.fullbright = 255 from colormap.lmp's trailing fullbright-count byte (1 on demo and retail), and Mod_LoadFullbrightTexture scans 'data[i] >= vid.fullbright && data[i] < 255', which can never match. Every world miptex gets the 1x1 black sentinel. Would only come alive if Mathuzzz's mod ships its own colormap.lmp with a different count — worth asking, but it would brighten broadly, not produce 13 isolated dots.
 * Alpha-test discard driven by lightmap alpha in sworld_frag ('color.a < u_alpha_threshold' where color = tex*lm*v_color). gl_rsurf.c writes dest[3] = 255 on every luxel, so lm.a is 1.0.

ASK MATHUZZZ:
 1. Re-send the .rdc — the download stopped ~11.5 MB short. Prefer a direct file attachment or a link that resumes.
 2. Which pixels? Circle them on capture2_frame_annotated.png, or say whether the marked cluster is the artifact.
 3. Map + the exact spot, and whether it moves when he moves (particles do; a texture defect stays put on the surface).
 4. Does 'gl_particles 0' change it?
 5. Does his mod ship its own gfx/colormap.lmp?

Note the wall in this frame is rendered very dark, consistent with the open uhexen2-4ql1 dark pillars / shadow-lighting regression; that may be why the specks read as strongly as they do.
notes:
2026-08-23, Mathuzzz: 'rendering issue on the wall still present -- lights he sees far off in distance get dlight turned on as he approaches/changes view angle its awkward to look at'.

REFRAMES THIS BEAD. He puts the wall complaint and the dlight popping in one sentence, which says the 'transparent pixels on the wall' are most likely dlights snapping on and off across that wall, not a texture or alpha defect. That moves the root cause to uhexen2-olku (the two binary culls in R_PushDlights: distance > radius+1024, and the 4-plane frustum test). The ~13 bright gold specks measured off the extracted frame are then probably just billboard particles and a red herring — they are far too small and too few to be what he means.

Keep this bead only until he confirms which he means. If he confirms it is the dlight popping, close as a duplicate of uhexen2-olku.

The file lost its .crdownload suffix on 2026-08-22 but not its missing bytes — byte-identical at 40,374,272 of the 51,940,079 its section table asks for, still 77.7%, renderdoccmd still refuses it.
