title: [task] Field-confirm the r10→master render regressions are gone on current master
description:
Split out of uhexen2-gnhh, closed after every cause it identified was verified
removed at code, asset and runtime level. This is the remaining human step: play
current master and confirm the two originally reported symptoms are gone.

WHAT WAS REPORTED
  1. Effects draw at wrong depth.
  2. The Cleric's weapon 4 (raven staff) has bad transparencies.

WHAT IS ALREADY ESTABLISHED, so this is a confirmation and not an investigation:
  - r_aliasinfo on Shadows of Turmoil, Necromancer, weapon 4 reports
    mflags TRANSPARENT, branch EF_TRANSPARENT, blend ON. Under the regression
    (uhexen2-ac4c) that entity was forced down the opaque branch. Symptom 2's
    mechanism is objectively absent.
  - No branch in R_DrawAliasModel touches the depth mask; the blended-alias
    depth-write ban (uhexen2-gwtq) is out. Symptom 1's mechanism is absent.
  - All four suspect commits (gwtq, ac4c, 93a8, p4ln.2) are out of the
    effective code. Master is functionally the 'revert-4' configuration the old
    bisect table marks CLEAN.

WHAT TO DO
  Build current master and play the content the report came from - Shadows of
  Turmoil, as the class whose weapon 4 is the raven staff. Look at the weapon
  in hand, and at effects (flames, missiles, mist) against geometry and against
  each other. Ten minutes.

IF BOTH ARE GONE: say so here and close. That retires the whole regression
epic.

IF EITHER PERSISTS: this is important, because it would mean the epic's
confirmed causes were not the whole story. Do NOT resume the old bisect table -
it was built against a tree that has since had most of the p4ln stack reverted
inside the mislabelled commit 3b98a4d4f (uhexen2-7ujj), and the branches it
names (revert-4, revert-p4ln, revert-p4ln-93a8, probe-93a8-alone) do not exist
in this repo. Restart from the audited baseline recorded in uhexen2-gnhh's
notes, and say precisely which symptom survived.

RELATED, still open and independent of this: uhexen2-5dit (uhexen2-93a8 blast
radius - the replacement-skin alpha rebuild that turned 10-45% of SoT's weapon
texels translucent, the real problem ac4c was mis-aimed at), uhexen2-q0in
(re-land p4ln.2 std140 blocks), uhexen2-t9uv (mist clumping).

title: [task] Visual sign-off on r_water_pixel_warp, and the default-on decision
description:
Split out of uhexen2-9o7u, which implemented the per-pixel liquid warp behind
r_water_pixel_warp (default 0). The code is written, compiles, runs and toggles
cleanly. What is left is the one thing that cannot be done without eyes on a
real GPU: decide whether it looks right, and whether it becomes the default.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD: the feature has been reverted twice on visual grounds
(uhexen2-tlsh, uhexen2-famb). Both reverts were correct. The implementation
work and the visual sign-off are genuinely different tasks, and the second is
about ten minutes for someone with a GPU and impossible for anyone without one
- this box renders through llvmpipe at a few frames per minute on a
liquid-heavy map.

WHAT TO DO
  1. Build current master, load sot/Arena (822 turb faces, a 3340x1824 lava
     pool at roughly 2867 -4640 -24 - the map both previous reverts were
     reported against).
  2. Compare r_water_pixel_warp 0 and 1, MOVING, specifically at glancing
     angles across the pool and at distance. Static screenshots will not settle
     it; every previous failure was a motion or grazing-angle artifact.
  3. Check the two symptoms the reverts recorded:
       - banding / aliasing at glancing angles (uhexen2-tlsh)
       - a "too dark" or flat look on the surface (uhexen2-famb)
  4. Also worth a look: water, slime and lava each (different textures, same
     warp), and an underwater view, which routes through the same program.

WHAT IS DIFFERENT THIS TIME, so the check is not just a repeat: the previous
attempt damped warp amplitude to zero past an fwidth THRESHOLD. This one scales
amplitude by sinc(k*W/2), the analytic box-filter response, which is the actual
filtered signal rather than an approximation of one - full throw up close,
smoothly to zero, reaching zero exactly when one pixel covers one warp period.
A threshold either over-damps or under-damps, which is plausibly both recorded
symptoms at once. If banding or darkening survives THIS, the sinc premise is
wrong and that is a real finding worth writing down rather than another tweak.

OUTCOMES
  - Looks right: flip the default to 1 and say so on this bead. Worth also
    noting whether gl_subdivide_size can then drop for turb surfaces, since
    per-pixel warp does not need the subdivision at all - that is a real
    geometry saving, priced by tools/bsp_subdiv.py.
  - Looks wrong: record WHAT is wrong and at what distance/angle, and leave the
    cvar default-off. Do not tweak blind; the numbers in uhexen2-9o7u say the
    per-vertex path cannot be fixed by subdivision size, so if per-pixel cannot
    be fixed either, that is worth knowing plainly rather than iterating.

BACKGROUND, so this does not need re-deriving: tools/warp_recon.py prints the
reconstruction error of the legacy path per subdivision size. The short version
is that the shipped gl_subdivide_size 64 does not render the intended ripple at
all - it renders an alias with a 234-unit period against an intended 50 - and
no affordable size fixes it (24 still carries 93% peak error; under 15% needs
size 8, about 40x the turb geometry). So "leave it per-vertex and pick a better
size" is not a fallback that exists.

title: [bug] Unknown-svc handler blind-skips 1 byte for SoT custom messages — residual stream-desync risk
description:
Split out of uhexen2-6ugh (fixed in f048c3394). That issue's root cause was the svc_clear_edicts count-width mismatch; this is a SECOND, independent way to desynchronise the same stream, left in place because it was not the cause of Mathuzzz's r15 crash.

cl_parse.c:1458, in the default arm of the CL_ParseServerMessage switch:

    // FIXME: SoT mod uses custom protocol messages (0, 33, 80, 84, 89, 97-101, 105, 108, 110, 115-117, 121)
    // Try to handle unknown messages gracefully
    if (cmd == 0 || cmd == 33 || cmd >= 80)
    {
        // Try reading 1 byte - many simple messages have just a byte parameter
        // If this is wrong, the stream will desync, but it's better than crashing
        byte skip_byte = MSG_ReadByte();
        ...
    }

The comment states the defect outright. For any SoT message whose payload is
not exactly one byte, the parser resumes at the wrong offset and every
subsequent message in that packet is garbage — surfacing as the same
'Illegible server message N' host error, or worse, as silently misapplied
entity state.

It is a guess, not a decode. The listed command set (0, 33, 80, 84, 89,
97-101, 105, 108, 110, 115-117, 121) is broad and certainly does not have a
uniform 1-byte payload.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEEDED
  - Determine the real payload layout for each SoT svc in that list. Sources,
    in order of preference: SoT's own QC/engine source if obtainable, then
    a captured demo diffed against known-good parse offsets.
  - Replace the blind skip with a per-command length table so each unknown
    message advances by the correct amount.
  - Where the length genuinely cannot be determined, prefer erroring with a
    named diagnostic over silently desyncing — a clean 'unsupported SoT
    message N' is more actionable than corrupted downstream state.

PRIORITY RATIONALE: P1 not P0 — only reachable when running SoT content, and
the acute crash that drove Mathuzzz off r15 is fixed independently. Raise to
P0 if SoT players report 'Illegible server message' on r16+.

RELATED: uhexen2-6ugh (the count-width desync, fixed).

title: Mount .pk3/.zip archives on the searchpath (QSS/FTE-style)
description:
Requested by Garrett (Monolyth-42) on Discord, 2026-08-20: "Is it possible to add
reading resources from pk3-zip archives, like qss or fteqw? This will save disk
space."

## Is the disk-space rationale real?

Yes, measured on a real install (/home/josh/hexen2):

  data1/pak0.pak    22 MB -> 9.3 MB deflate
  data1/pak1.pak    73 MB -> 35 MB deflate
  portals/pak3.pak  49 MB

Roughly half. Caveat on the number: that is whole-file gzip, which is optimistic
because a real .pk3 deflates each entry independently with no shared dictionary.
Expect ~45-50% rather than 58%, still a substantial win on a ~900 MB full install.

## Current state

engine/h2shared/quakefs.c is pak-only. searchpath_t (quakefs.c:69-79) is a
directory XOR a pack_t, and pack_t is a flat pakfiles_t array of
(name, filepos, filelen).

The blocker is the return contract of FS_OpenFile_Internal (quakefs.c:918): on a
pak hit it reopens the .pak and hands back a raw FILE * already fseek'd to
filepos. That only works because .pak entries are stored uncompressed and
contiguous. A deflated zip entry has no byte offset you can seek a FILE * to.

## Why this is smaller than it looks

fshandle_t already exists (quakefs.h:236-243) and already abstracts exactly this
case -- FILE * + start + length + pos, with FS_fread / FS_fseek / FS_ftell /
FS_feof / FS_fgetc / FS_fgets / FS_filelength wrappers. Its own comment says it
exists "to perform non-sequential reads on files reopened on pak files".

Every streaming consumer is already on it: snd_vorbis.c, snd_opus.c, snd_xmp.c,
snd_umx.c, snd_timidity.c, mid2strm.c, cfgfile.c, pr_edict.c. Those are the
consumers that would have been hardest to fix, and they need no work.

So the core change is: add a memory backing to fshandle_t (a byte *data + owned
flag alongside the FILE *), branch the ten FS_f* functions on it, and have the
zip searchpath inflate an entry into that buffer on open.

## What still needs converting

These take the raw FILE * from FS_OpenFile and fread/fseek it themselves:

  Streaming (must convert, holds the handle across frames):
    engine/hexen2/cl_demo.c:437       cls.demofile
    engine/h2shared/snd_codec.c:285
    engine/h2shared/midi_fluid.c:230

  One-shot (read fully then close -- can also just use FS_LoadFile):
    engine/hexen2/r_part.c:361
    engine/h2shared/gl_warp.c:1287
    engine/h2shared/image.c:124, :129
    engine/h2shared/img_load.c:43, :250, :359
    engine/h2shared/img_dds.c:245

## Deflate implementation: no new dependency needed

stb_image is already compiled into the engine (img_load.c:18 defines
STB_IMAGE_IMPLEMENTATION, and neither STBI_NO_ZLIB nor STBI_NO_PNG is set
anywhere). It exports stbi_zlib_decode_noheader_buffer() -- raw deflate with no
zlib header, which is exactly the ZIP entry format. That covers method 8; method
0 (stored) is a memcpy. Those two cover essentially every real .pk3.

Still needed either way: a ZIP end-of-central-directory + central-directory
parser to enumerate entries, plus zip64 handling for >4 GB / >65535 entries
(probably just reject with a clear message).

Alternative: vendor miniz.c, which gives the central-directory parser for free.
See the Ironwail note below.

## Ironwail relationship -- deliberately NOT filed at P0

This is a QSS/FTE feature, not an Ironwail one, so the P0 Ironwail floor does
not apply. Checked rather than assumed: Ironwail does vendor miniz (Quake/miniz.c)
but uses it in exactly one place -- Quake/common.c:3636-3740, to pull the
rerelease localization strings out of QuakeEX.kpf. It has no general zip
searchpath. `grep -rn "pk3" Quake/` returns nothing.

That said, Ironwail's vendored miniz.c is a working, already-integrated zip
reader we could lift directly, which would be consistent with the house rule
that Ironwail's approach is the default for shared problems.

## Open design questions

- Extension: .pk3 only, or .pk3 + .zip? QSS takes both.
- Search order relative to .pak within one gamedir. QSS loads pak*.pak first,
  then pk3 alphabetically; FTE differs. Pick one and document it.
- Case folding. quakefs.c has FS_ResolveCasePath for loose files and
  q_strcasecmp for pak entries; zip central-directory names are case-sensitive
  bytes, so the same folding has to be applied at index-build time.
- Directory entries and nested paths -- zip stores full relative paths with
  forward slashes, which matches MAX_QPATH conventions, but entries ending in
  '/' must be skipped.
- Memory ceiling: inflating a large entry on open is a hunk/zone allocation that
  the pak path never made. Needs a cap or a streaming inflate for the demo case.
design:
APPROACH DECIDED 2026-08-20 (user): import from FTE rather than hand-rolling the
ZIP parser or vendoring Ironwail's miniz. Priority raised P2 -> P1.

Reference checkout: /home/josh/tmp/claudedir/fteqw (shallow, sparse to
engine/common + engine/client). Relevant file: engine/common/fs_zip.c, 2540 lines.

## License

Both projects are GPL2. Clean import. Preserve FTE's copyright headers on any
lifted block and note provenance in the file banner, the same way any other
upstream import is attributed.

## The honest constraint: fs_zip.c is not a drop-in

fs_zip.c implements searchpathfuncs_t -- a 15-method vtable declared at
fteqw/engine/common/fs.h:32-57 (ClosePath, AddReference, GetPathDetails,
BuildHash, FindFile, ReadFile, EnumerateFiles, GeneratePureCRC, OpenVFS,
PollChanges, FileStat, CreateFile, RenameFile, RemoveFile) -- and returns
vfsfile_t, an 8-method vtable at fteqw/engine/common/common.h:632-640
(ReadBytes, WriteBytes, Seek, Tell, GetLen, Close, Flush).

uhexen2 has neither abstraction. Copying fs_zip.c wholesale means importing
FTE's entire VFS layer and its registration machinery
(FS_RegisterFileSystemType, the searchpath_t chain in fs.c, 8709 lines). That is
a filesystem rewrite, not a feature.

So "import from FTE" here means: lift the ZIP *logic*, which is the hard and
easy-to-get-wrong part, and bind it to uhexen2's existing fshandle_t
(quakefs.h:236) rather than to FTE's vtables.

## What to lift, by symbol

Format parsing -- the fiddly part, take as directly as possible:
  FSZIP_FindEndCentralDirectory    fs_zip.c:2160
    EOCD locator, including the tail-scan past a trailing comment field and the
    zip64 EOCD record + locator. Easy to write subtly wrong by hand.
  FSZIP_EnumerateCentralDirectory  fs_zip.c:2046
  FSZIP_ReadCentralEntry           fs_zip.c:1833
    Central-directory walk, extra-field parsing, zip64 size/offset promotion,
    UTF-8 vs IBM437 filename encoding.

Streaming decompression with seek -- the reason to prefer FTE over a simple
inflate-on-open:
  FSZIP_Deflate_Init      fs_zip.c:1039
  FSZIP_Deflate_Read      fs_zip.c:971
  FSZIP_Deflate_Seek      fs_zip.c:944
  FSZIP_Deflate_Destroy   fs_zip.c:1033
    Seeking backwards inside a deflate stream requires restart-and-skip-forward;
    FTE already implements that. This is exactly what cl_demo.c's cls.demofile
    and snd_codec.c need, and it is the piece a naive port gets wrong.

## What to deliberately drop

Split/multi-volume archives, bzip2, deflate64, weak and AES encryption, the
symlink flag, pure-CRC (GeneratePureCRC), the download/delta-zip machinery
(FSZIP_OpenDeltaZip, fs_zip.c:2522), the threading mutex, and PollChanges.
None of it applies to a single-player Hexen II loading pk3s off local disk.

## Binding target

fshandle_t (quakefs.h:236) gains a decompress-state pointer; FS_fread /
FS_fseek / FS_ftell / FS_feof branch on it. FTE's deflate state is nearly the
same shape already -- (start, csize, usize, pos) plus a stream -- so the mapping
is close to mechanical.

## REOPENED DECISION: the deflate dependency

The description says no new dependency is needed because stb_image already
exports stbi_zlib_decode_noheader_buffer(). That holds ONLY for a
decompress-the-whole-entry-on-open design. It does not hold here.

stb's inflate is whole-buffer: you hand it a complete input and get a complete
output. It has no incremental/resumable entry point. FTE's design is streaming
and seekable, and that design cannot sit on top of stb.

So choosing the FTE import reopens the dependency question. Three options:

1. Add zlib. What FTE's deflate path actually uses. Ubiquitous on Linux and in
   nixpkgs, but it is a new dependency for the mingw, flatpak and especially the
   Emscripten/WASM builds -- check emscripten's zlib port before committing.
2. Vendor miniz. Single file, has tinfl streaming, and Ironwail already ships it
   (ironwail/Quake/miniz.c) so it is a known-good vendored copy in a sibling
   engine. Costs no system dependency. Gives the central-directory parser too,
   which overlaps what we would otherwise lift from FTE.
3. Give up seekable streaming and inflate whole entries on open using the stb
   code already present. Zero dependency, simplest, but the memory cost is the
   full uncompressed entry and it regresses demo playback and music streaming
   from O(1) to O(entry size) resident.

Recommendation: option 2. It keeps the zero-system-dependency property of
option 3 while preserving FTE's streaming design, and miniz's tinfl is a closer
substrate for FSZIP_Deflate_* than stb is. Note this makes the import a hybrid:
FTE's structure and seek logic, miniz's inflate, which needs to be stated in the
file banner so the provenance is not misread later.

Flagging rather than deciding, because it changes the dependency surface of
three build targets.

## Open questions carried over from the description

Extension set (.pk3 only vs .pk3 + .zip), load order relative to pak*.pak within
a gamedir, case folding at index-build time, and skipping directory entries.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-20, in two commits.

Phase 1 -- f540490a9 -- mounted the archives: vendored miniz 2.2.0 from Ironwail's trimmed read-only copy, added the pk3 searchpath, split FS_ReadIntoBuffer's allocation half out as FS_AllocLoadBuffer so the pak and archive paths allocate by identical rules, and taught FS_LoadFile to inflate a DEFLATED entry through FS_ReadZipIntoBuffer. Search order is loose files, then pk3s, then paks (QSS/FTE convention); alphabetically last archive wins within a directory. FS_IsGamedir recognises a pk3-only directory so an archive-shipped mod appears in the Mods menu.

Phase 2 -- 550e331a4 -- closed the hole phase 1 left: every caller that took a raw FILE * from FS_OpenFile and read it itself was blind to deflated entries, because those come back as a length with a NULL stream. fshandle_t gained a memory backing (byte *data), the ten FS_f* wrappers branch on it, and FS_OpenFileHandle()/_Silent() became the front door. All eleven sites the description enumerated are converted: cl_demo.c, snd_codec.c, midi_fluid.c, mid2strm.c, cfgfile.c, pr_edict.c, r_part.c, gl_warp.c, image.c, img_load.c, img_dds.c.

Two latent bugs the sweep exposed, neither introduced by it:
- S_CodecUtilClose fclose()'d fh.file directly, which on a memory-backed stream is fclose(NULL) plus a leaked inflate buffer.
- CheckRegistered read gfx/pop.lmp through a raw FILE *, so an install repacked as .pk3 -- the entire point of the feature -- silently demoted itself to shareware.
Plus a pre-existing pak bug: gl_warp.c's LoadPCX did fseek(f, -768, SEEK_END), which landed on the end of the enclosing .pak rather than the end of the member. Member-relative through FS_fseek now.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS from the description, resolved: extension is .pk3 and .zip; search order documented above; case folding applied at index-build time; '/'-terminated directory entries skipped.

TWO ITEMS SPLIT OUT rather than left buried here:
- uhexen2-f1i7 -- the retail installation check identifies pak0/pak1 by a CRC over the .pak directory, so it cannot see archive content. This is what blocks converting the BASE paks; pk3s remain additive content until it is settled, and settling it needs a decision about whether that check is an anti-piracy gate or a data-sanity check.
- uhexen2-k4lc -- what shipped is a hybrid the design did not name: miniz is vendored as option 2 recommended, but the read path is option 3's whole-entry inflate, not FTE's seekable streaming. Narrower than feared (STORED entries stay FILE-backed and O(1), and a sane packer STOREs ogg/opus), but deflated demos go resident and there is still no cap on the allocation.

Closing: the bead's own scope -- mount .pk3/.zip on the searchpath -- is complete and verified against real game data.

title: uhexen2-93a8 blast radius: replacement-skin index alpha changes 82 world models
description:
6ac3f19c7 (uhexen2-93a8) added Mod_RestoreIndexAlpha, rebuilding an external replacement skin's alpha from the embedded skin's palette indices: index 0 -> hole, ODD index -> r_wateralpha*255, else 255. Reverted on branch revert-4 as part of uhexen2-gnhh.

By its own commit message this changes 82 models on a data1+portals+sot install -- flames, fog, waterfalls, curtains, webs, blood pools, candles, the portal and both spellbooks -- and SoT pins r_wateralpha 0.5, so those texels go from 255 to 128.

It was fixing something real: the Necromancer's spellbook cover drew as an opaque black slab across the open page and its hand glow as solid magenta, both confirmed texel-by-texel from capture_black_page_rectangle_purple_hand.rdc. Do not simply drop it.

It is also what pushed uhexen2-ac4c into forcing viewmodels opaque, which is its own regression (uhexen2-lbkn).

WHETHER IT IS A CAUSE of uhexen2-gnhh is pending probe-93a8-alone: revert-4 is clean, that branch re-applies 93a8 and nothing else. Broken there means yes.

DESIGN NOTE for the fix: the discrimination ac4c tried to make at the draw site belongs on the skin side. A model's EF_TRANSPARENT flag is authoritative -- it is what the author declared. The rebuilt skin alpha is derived. So the question is not 'is this the viewmodel' but 'should this replacement skin get index alpha at all', and the answer probably depends on whether the replacement already carries meaningful alpha of its own. A pack that shipped a fully-opaque TGA for a model the author flagged EF_TRANSPARENT is expressing something different from one that shipped a TGA with real holes in it.

title: Re-land uhexen2-p4ln.2 (std140 uniform blocks) behind a visual regression sweep
description:
d49e348a5 and the three commits stacked on it (e2f3182ec texture slot ranges, 334838e3c shaders to files, 7a29dd3b1 SPIR-V + Vulkan bindings) are reverted on branch revert-4 as part of uhexen2-gnhh. 01e7719d5, the pipeline-state module underneath them, is CLEARED by probe14-no-gwtq and stays in.

d49e348a5's own commit message says: 'Behaviour is unverified on screen -- no visual regression sweep has been run.' That is how it shipped, and it is the reason to re-land it differently rather than to abandon it: the blocks are the shape the SDL_GPU/Vulkan backend needs (uhexen2-p4ln.3/.4).

CONCRETE DEFECT FOUND WHILE BISECTING, fix before re-landing:
Loose uniforms are per-PROGRAM; std140 block members are GLOBAL. The conversion kept the old per-program discipline at sites where it stopped holding.
  engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c:1649   sets R_SetAlphaThresholdU, never R_SetForceOpaqueAlphaU
  engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c:1711   same
  engine/h2shared/gl_worldcull.c:1240  same
Each therefore inherits whatever the last alias or sprite batch left in PerDraw.draw0.y. d49e348a5 spotted this exact hazard for FOG -- it added an R_SetFog restore after the instanced fullbright pass with a comment explaining that PerFrame is shared -- and did not apply the same reasoning to the alpha pair.

Also: GL_ImmEnd's re-push of the alpha pair is still guarded by 'if (imm_alpha_threshold >= 0.0f)' / 'if (imm_force_opaque_alpha >= 0.0f)'. Those -1 sentinels meant 'use the shader default' under loose uniforms. Under blocks there is no per-shader default -- the block always holds some value -- so a batch that never sets a threshold silently inherits the previous one. Give them real defaults and push unconditionally.

WHETHER d49e348a5 IS ACTUALLY A CAUSE is not yet settled: probe17-no-gwtq was broken with both it and 6ac3f19c7 present. probe-93a8-alone discriminates. Even if 93a8 turns out to be the cause and d49e348a5 is exonerated, the three missing R_SetForceOpaqueAlphaU calls above are real and should be fixed on re-land.

Re-land checklist: SoT docks with the Cleric (all four weapons), a fog map, a water map, a map with fence textures, and particles + sprites in frame.

title: [bug] uhexen2-ac4c forces flagged viewmodels opaque — SoT raven staff loses its intended transparency
description:
8318dabac (uhexen2-ac4c) made cl.viewent skip the EF_SPECIAL_TRANS and EF_TRANSPARENT branches in R_DrawAliasModel and fall through to the opaque branch, which sets GL_SetForceOpaqueAlpha(1.0f) and disables blending.

Confirmed a cause of uhexen2-gnhh in its own right: revert-p4ln-93a8 had gwtq, 93a8 and the whole p4ln stack reverted and was still broken, and ac4c was the ONLY functional render delta against probe14-no-gwtq, which is clean. Reverting it (branch revert-4) is clean.

WHY IT IS WRONG: ac4c assumed a viewmodel's EF_TRANSPARENT flag is always an accident of Hexen II's odd-palette-index rule leaking through a replacement skin. It is not. Shadows of Turmoil flags sot/models/ravenstf.mdl (Cleric weapon 4, the reported weapon) EF_TRANSPARENT deliberately, where the base-game pak1 copy carries no flags at all. Forcing it opaque makes the parts meant to be see-through solid -- the exact inverse of the bug ac4c was written to fix.

The premise ac4c was built on is still real: uhexen2-93a8 turned 10-45% of SoT's weapon texels from alpha 255 to 128, and the weapons looked like glass. But that is 93a8's blast radius, not something to correct at the draw site by overriding what the model author declared.

A real fix has to distinguish 'this model declares transparency' from 'this skin acquired transparency from the index rebuild'. The model flag is authoritative; the skin alpha is derived. So gate on the SKIN side (see the 93a8 bead) and leave R_DrawAliasModel honouring the flag.

Reverted on branch revert-4. Diagnostics from a5fcb21bb / c887d0269 (r_aliasinfo viewmodel section, r_vm_watch) are KEPT -- they are read-only and were what made the flag situation legible.
close_reason:
Already fixed in-tree; verified and documented. Comment corrections in a6c5bc3b8.

CODE STATE - the ac4c change this issue describes (cl.viewent skipping the
EF_TRANSPARENT / EF_SPECIAL_TRANS branches to fall through to the opaque path)
is NOT present on master. It was reverted as part of 3b98a4d4f, the
mislabelled 'chase:' commit flagged by uhexen2-7ujj. Confirmed by reading both
predicate sets in gl_rmain.c: neither the branch chain (~line 1826) nor the
restore block (~line 2124) carries a viewmodel exemption, so an EF_TRANSPARENT
viewmodel such as sot/models/ravenstf.mdl takes the blended branch again -
which is what this issue asked for.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY STILL WRONG - three comment blocks described ac4c as live:
the branch-chain preamble headed 'THE VIEWMODEL IGNORES ITS MODEL'S
TRANSLUCENCY FLAGS' and asserting 'only the MODEL-flag branches are skipped';
the restore block claiming it mirrors the chain 'viewmodel exemption included';
and the viewmodel local's declaration comment. All three contradicted the code
they sat on.

That matters more than usual here. uhexen2-gnhh records four partial fixes
(fc1c, ac4c, g842, 130w) that each looked right against this file's commentary
and wrong against its behaviour. Rewritten to state what the code does, why
ac4c was the wrong layer, and where the fix belongs, plus an explicit
do-not-reinstate note and a must-change-together note tying the branch chain to
its restore block.

REMAINING WORK IS NOT HERE - the premise ac4c was built on is still real and
still unbounded: uhexen2-93a8 turned 10-45% of SoT's weapon texels from alpha
255 to 128 and the weapons read as glass. That has to be gated on the SKIN side
at upload, where 'this model declares transparency' and 'this skin acquired
transparency from the index rebuild' are still distinguishable. By
R_DrawAliasModel they are not. Tracked in uhexen2-5dit (93a8 blast radius),
which stays open.

Diagnostics from a5fcb21bb / c887d0269 (r_aliasinfo viewmodel section,
r_vm_watch) are kept as this issue required.

Closed with --force: the dependency on uhexen2-gnhh is the epic waiting on
field probes, and this child no longer has any code work of its own.

nix build clean. No functional change.

title: Blended alias models lost depth writes globally — weapons and attack effects draw see-through and out of order
description:
Field report: after 096ee3e5d (uhexen2-gwtq) weapons and attack effects render 'wrong things in front of other things' with bad transparencies.

096ee3e5d gave R_DrawAliasModel ownership of the depth mask and made ALL four blended branches (EF_SPECIAL_TRANS, DRF_TRANSLUCENT, EF_TRANSPARENT, non-opaque per-entity alpha) call R_SetDepthMask(false), to fix one mod's mist. Vanilla uHexen2 wrote depth on all of them (R_DrawTransEntitiesOnList forced glDepthMask(1) for every mod_alias entity), and that is what shipped good through 0.8.0-beta.r10.

uhexen2-fc1c already carved out cl.viewent, but the exemption was scoped to the viewmodel only. Every OTHER translucent alias model in the game still drew with writes off: spell effects, projectiles, translucent monsters. A single mesh needs the depth buffer to resolve against ITSELF — without writes, its own interior and further front-facing triangles blend straight through the nearer ones, and two translucent effects no longer occlude each other. That is exactly the reported symptom, and it is the same defect fc1c diagnosed, just not confined to the weapon.

The gwtq rationale conflates two problems: compositing SEPARATE overlapping instances of one model (wants writes off) vs a SINGLE mesh with depth complexity (needs them on). Only the first is the mist. It is also not the same call R_RenderBrushPoly makes for translucent brush surfaces (uhexen2-t4kt/j001) — a water/glass surface is one flat layer with no self-occlusion to lose.

FIX: new archived cvar r_alias_blend_depthwrite, default 1 = vanilla (blended alias models write depth). 0 restores the gwtq behaviour for content that wants overlapping soft-edged instances to composite. cl.viewent stays exempt from the suppression either way, so the fc1c fix survives at both settings. Reported in the r_aliasinfo frame-context dump.

Files: engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c (cvar decl, blend_depthwrite local in R_DrawAliasModel, four branch sites, rationale comment, r_aliasinfo dump), engine/h2shared/glquake.h (extern), engine/hexen2/gl_rmisc.c (registration).

CONSEQUENCE: uhexen2-gwtq's mist regresses at the default setting — see the follow-up bead.
close_reason: Fixed in 6f6f49eac. New archived cvar r_alias_blend_depthwrite (default 1 = vanilla: blended alias models write depth). R_DrawAliasModel computes a blend_depthwrite local next to the existing viewmodel local and all four blended branches route through it; cl.viewent is exempt from the suppression at both settings so the uhexen2-fc1c fix survives. 096ee3e5d's structural change is kept -- the function still owns the mask for the whole draw, EF_HOLEY and the opaque branch still assert it on, every exit including the R_CullBox early return still hands it back on. r_aliasinfo reports the setting. Build clean via nix build; cvar string present in the binary. Awaiting field confirmation that weapons and attack effects self-occlude again. Mist regression at the default is tracked as uhexen2-t9uv.

title: PWA launcher requires pak1 — demo installs can never launch despite full engine demo support
description: The PWA launcher gates the Launch button behind pak1 (web/lib/paths.js:79, web/app.js:140), but the Nov-1997 demo pak0 is standalone (no pak1). Engine demo support is proven working via direct Module.callMain bypass—game runs and plays correctly. Root issue: web/lib/paths.js line 79 checks 'set.has(data1/pak0.pak) && set.has(data1/pak1.pak)'. Fix: accept demo pak0-present alone, and update importer to accept .dat files (demo progs.dat is not in pak0, unlike retail).
close_reason: Delivered by commit b8975b4b8: launcher predicate replaced (hasRequiredBaseAssets → getBaseAssetStatus: none|pak0-only|full); pak0-only launches with 'Start game (demo)' + hint copy; loose progs.dat now importable file-by-file (.dat accepted, progs2?.dat basename mapped to data1/); save-bundles tolerate pak0-only. Runtime-proven via real UI path (trusted CDP click, no callMain bypass) in BOTH renderer builds: demo playable to in-game save; registered-pak0-only correctly surfaces engine fatal in launcher status. Fixed pre-existing drop-zone grid layout bug. 38/38 web tests.

title: Replacement-skin index alpha makes SoT weapon viewmodels 50% translucent
description:
Regression from 6ac3f19c7 (uhexen2-93a8, 'model: rebuild a replacement skin's alpha from the palette index'), landed after the 0.8.0-beta.r11 tag. Distinct from uhexen2-fc1c (depth mask), which is why the fc1c fix did not make the symptom go away.

Mod_RestoreIndexAlpha (engine/h2shared/gl_model.c:2597) rebuilds an external skin's alpha from the embedded skin's palette indices, mirroring GL_Upload8's TEX_TRANSPARENT rule: index 0 -> 0, ODD index -> r_wateralpha*255, else 255.

Shadows of Turmoil ships its own weapon viewmodels flagged EF_TRANSPARENT (0x1000) where the base-game copies in pak0/pak1 carry no flags at all, AND pins r_wateralpha 0.5 in sot/config.cfg. Measured odd-index share of each SoT weapon skin:

  gauntlet.mdl 44.8%   axe.mdl 38.1%   vorpal.mdl 34.5%
  wand.mdl 39.6%       spllbook.mdl 35.3%   icestaff.mdl 35.4%
  serpstaff.mdl 35.5%  sunstaff.mdl 29.7%   crossbow.mdl 17.7%
  ravenstf.mdl 10.6%

So 10-45% of every weapon's texels now upload at alpha 128 instead of 255. Before 93a8 the replacement branch dropped EF_TRANSPARENT entirely and used the TGA's own (opaque) alpha, so weapons drew solid. Chain confirmed end to end: Mod_RestoreIndexAlpha sets rep->has_alpha, GL_LoadReplacement turns that into TEX_ALPHA, R_DrawAliasModel's EF_TRANSPARENT branch enables GL_BLEND with GL_SetForceOpaqueAlpha(0), so texture alpha reaches the blend stage.

Base game (data1 only) is unaffected -- its weapon models are unflagged.

The texture-side rule cannot discriminate: the same odd-index->translucent mapping is exactly what 93a8 needed for the Necromancer spellbook cover (palette index 3). Only the DRAW site knows the difference between a world model and the gun in the player's hand.
notes:
Fixed in gl_rmain.c: cl.viewent now skips the EF_SPECIAL_TRANS and EF_TRANSPARENT model-flag branches in R_DrawAliasModel and falls through to the opaque path. DRF_TRANSLUCENT (server-driven, svc_set_view_flags -- the invisibility ring) is deliberately left live. The bottom restore block mirrors the same predicates so an EF_SPECIAL_TRANS viewmodel cannot come back with culling re-enabled that nothing disabled. The opaque branch now asserts GL_SetAlphaThreshold(0.01f) rather than inheriting it, because index-0 holes now depend on salias_frag.glsl discarding below the threshold BEFORE u_force_opaque_alpha rewrites the output alpha.

VERIFIED by offscreen render (SDL offscreen + llvmpipe, sot/docks, 640x480, r_wateralpha 0.5, Paladin gauntlets):
  before: floor tile mortar lines read straight through both gauntlets
  after:  gauntlets solid, clean silhouette, shading visible
Per-row difference profile confirms the change is confined to the viewmodel band (screen y 320-439, mean |diff| 2.25-2.82) against a run-to-run noise floor of 0.04-0.45 elsewhere.

NOT changed, deliberately: the fullbright-pass gate at gl_rmain.c:1865 still skips glow layers for EF_TRANSPARENT/EF_SPECIAL_TRANS models. The viewmodel is opaque now so it arguably qualifies, but leaving it preserves existing behaviour exactly and replacement skins carry no fullbright layer anyway.
close_reason: Closed

title: Web import: paks-only import leaves the game with no key bindings
description: Root cause: hexen.rc ships in no retail pak and web importer rejects/omits it; couldn't exec hexen.rc in web build. Consequences three-fold: (a) no key bindings beyond console/pause/gamepad (original finding); (b) config.cfg is NEVER read back at startup — even with persistence fixed by uhexen2-zuyg, user settings don't restore across sessions; (c) stuffcmds never runs, so +command argv is inert in the browser. Fix directions: exec default.cfg/config.cfg fallback chain when hexen.rc is absent (engine, guarded), or ship/synthesize hexen.rc on web side. Being worked NOW as final pre-merge fix.
close_reason: Delivered by commit 6fb2ffba4: engine-side built-in startup script (Cmd_StartupScript in cmd.c, __EMSCRIPTEN__-guarded) at both hexen.rc call sites (host.c:1124 Host_Init, quakefs.c:2023 gamedir change) when hexen.rc absent from searchpath. Replicates retail rc verbatim (developer 0 + menu_main; startdemos commented-out faithfully omitted). Mission packs: loose hexen.rc takes precedence when present; pak3-only gets fallback + mission default.cfg. Runtime-proven both WEB_RENDERER configs, 16/16 checks: full exec chain, 70 bindings live, acid test config.cfg round-trip (sensitivity 7.5 restored) passes; save unaffected. Desktop + h2ded byte-equivalent, 37/37 web tests.

title: Web build: engine saves and config.cfg written to /home/web_user/.hexen2 are never persisted or exported
description: DO_USERDIRS=1 on Emscripten (sys.h:82 excludes only Windows/OS2), so parms.userdir=/home/web_user/.hexen2 (sys_unix.c:624), fs_userdir=.../data1 (quakefs.c:2009), all saves route via FS_MakePath(FS_USERDIR,...) (host_cmd.c:678). But web/app.js:270 only syncs /persistent. Runtime-proven by smoke test: after launch, config.cfg (4312B) + qconsole.log exist under /home/web_user/.hexen2/data1 while /persistent has only imported files. Consequence: Pages-build players silently lose ALL progress; Storage panel's 'synced' claim is false; Export saves finds nothing. MUST fix before PR #2 merges. Likely fix directions: point userdir into /persistent under __EMSCRIPTEN__ (engine-side preferred, single persistence root), or extend app.js sync to walk userdir tree.
close_reason: Delivered by commit b64144479: DO_USERDIRS disabled under __EMSCRIPTEN__ in sys.h so userdir follows -basedir /persistent; saves/config now land at /persistent/data1/... matching save-bundle allowlist exactly; zero JS changes. Runtime-proven in BOTH WEB_RENDERER configs: real in-game save → page reload → restored from IndexedDB → bundle export validated. Desktop unaffected (guard unreachable, nix build green, zero warnings). 37/37 web tests (+4 pinning persistence contract).

title: Viewmodel weapon renders see-through: blended alias branches drop depth writes
description:
Bisected to 096ee3e5dc85ec0538ebb8a6993d474aa27055e4 (uhexen2-gwtq, 'rmain: stop alpha-blended alias models from writing depth'). Good: 555e9eb55 / e65864179. Bad: 096ee3e5d, 0.8.0-beta.r11 tag (95896e59c), HEAD.

That commit gave R_DrawAliasModel ownership of the depth mask and made the blended branches (EF_SPECIAL_TRANS, DRF_TRANSLUCENT, EF_TRANSPARENT, non-opaque per-entity alpha) call R_SetDepthMask(false). Previously R_DrawTransEntitiesOnList forced the mask ON for every mod_alias entity, and the viewmodel inherited that.

R_DrawViewModel (engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c) draws cl.viewent through the same R_DrawAliasModel branch chain, so a weapon taking any blended branch now renders with depth writes off and stops occluding itself -- its own back/interior faces show through the front.

Root cause is that the gwtq fix conflates two different cases: many SEPARATE instances that should composite (the mod mist, eight draws of one .mdl) genuinely must not write depth; a SINGLE model needs the depth buffer to resolve against itself. The viewmodel already has its own dedicated depth-range slice (upper 30% under reversed-Z), so depth writes there cost nothing elsewhere.

Fix: exempt cl.viewent from the blended-branch depth-write suppression.
notes:
Fix committed as e2afab2e5 (exempt cl.viewent from the blended-branch depth-write suppression).

Note for anyone re-reading the bisect: the 'weapons look see-through' report that motivated this bead was TWO bugs wearing one symptom. The depth-mask regression bisected here is real and 096ee3e5d is genuinely its first bad commit. But the report persisted after e2afab2e5 landed, and that residual was uhexen2-ac4c -- Mod_RestoreIndexAlpha (6ac3f19c7) applying Hexen II's odd-palette-index -> r_wateralpha rule to external replacement skins for the first time, which turned every SoT weapon viewmodel 50% translucent. Do not re-bisect this one; ac4c landed after the r11 tag and is fixed separately.

After ac4c, this exemption only bites on the DRF_TRANSLUCENT and per-entity-alpha branches (the viewmodel no longer reaches the EF_TRANSPARENT / EF_SPECIAL_TRANS branches at all), so it is still load-bearing for the invisibility ring.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] External replacement skins drop EF_TRANSPARENT / EF_SPECIAL_TRANS translucency
description:
Found in capture_black_page_rectangle_purple_hand.rdc (SoT, Necromancer, AMD RX 7700 XT / Mesa 26.1.5).

Hexen II stores an alias model's translucency in the palette INDEX of each skin texel, not in its colour. GL_Upload8 turns the index into alpha: index 0 becomes a hole, an ODD index becomes r_wateralpha, everything else stays solid; EF_SPECIAL_TRANS reads its ramp out of ColorPercent[]. Mod_LoadAllSkins computes that tex_mode correctly (TEX_TRANSPARENT / TEX_HOLEY / TEX_SPECIAL_TRANS) -- and then the external-replacement branch throws it away and builds a fresh skin_tex_mode that only carries EF_HOLEY across. An RGBA replacement has no indices, so EF_TRANSPARENT and EF_SPECIAL_TRANS models draw with whatever alpha the pack author baked, which for the SoT pack is 'opaque'.

Symptoms in the capture, both on sot/models/spllbook.mdl (flags 0x1000 = EF_TRANSPARENT), one draw, prog 40, glDrawArrays count=1776:
  - the book's translucent cover (palette index 3, odd -> should be 50% at r_wateralpha 0.5) drew as an opaque BLACK SLAB over the open right-hand page
  - the hand's translucent spell glow (palette indices 239/241, odd) drew as solid MAGENTA over the hand

Same failure class as uhexen2-0vgo.1 (replacements silently dropped the fullbright layer) -- both lose something the engine derives from palette indices that RGBA cannot carry.

Blast radius on this install: 92 models declare EF_TRANSPARENT and 6 declare EF_SPECIAL_TRANS across data1 + portals + sot; 82 of them have a replacement file on the searchpath. Flames, fog, waterfalls, curtains, webs, blood pools, candles, the portal and both spellbooks all render opaque with an HD pack installed.

NOT a regression from this week: the alias external-skin path dates to a14b5eecd (2026-03-21); 74e8eccde only restructured it. It became visible now because the SoT HD pack is on the searchpath.
close_reason: Fixed on master 15c6cba15. Mod_RestoreIndexAlpha (gl_model.c) rebuilds a replacement skin's alpha from the embedded skin's palette indices for EF_TRANSPARENT and EF_SPECIAL_TRANS, point-sampling the index map, keeping the replacement's RGB, and rejecting block-compressed containers so they fall back to the embedded skin. Verified two ways: a standalone replay of the new texel loop reproduces the reference alpha channel for sot/models/spllbook.mdl bit-for-bit at 1:1 and at 4x, and re-rasterising the capture's own viewmodel draw with that alpha clears both artefacts -- the black slab over the right page and the solid magenta hand. nix build .#nixos clean, no new warnings.

title: Black liquid in SoT docks: R_RenderBrushPoly applies MLS_ABSLIGHT to a self-emissive turb (+ SoT ships a black #lowlight6.tga)
description:
## Re-audit 2026-08-18 — supersedes the original GPU-side analysis

The original writeup ("GL command stream verified CORRECT", suspects = texture
corruption in GPU memory or a Mesa/ACO miscompile) is **wrong on every point**.
Both defects are plainly visible in the CPU-side capture and are
hardware-independent. Nothing here is AMD- or Mesa-specific.

Method: `renderdoccmd convert -c zip.xml` (the plain `xml` export drops the
byte blobs; `zip.xml` keeps them), then decoded the immediate-mode vertex
buffer and every `glTexImage2D` payload out of the zip.

### What the frame actually contains

There is exactly **one** liquid draw, not seven: chunk 6873,
`glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLES, 0, 2772)`, program 60 (`gl_shader_alias`),
texture 4201. The "6 distinct 40x24 RGBA8 liquid textures" in the old
writeup were HUD/sprite textures on unrelated draws.

Map identified as **SoT `docks.bsp`** (84/226 miptexes match the capture
byte-for-byte); the liquid is **`*lowlight6`**.

`R_DrawWaterSurfaces` never emitted a draw this frame — it sets
`GL_SetAlphaThreshold(0.0f)`, and `u_alpha_threshold` for program 60 is
0.01 for the whole frame. So the visible slime is **not** world turb.

### Root cause 1 — engine: MLS_ABSLIGHT dims a self-emissive liquid

The GL sequence at chunks 6858-6873 matches `R_RenderBrushPoly`
(engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c:800-950) instruction for instruction: the
DRF_TRANSLUCENT prelude (enable BLEND / SRC_ALPHA,ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA /
DepthMask 0), `GL_Bind`, the TU2 `gl_null_fb_texture` bind at
gl_rsurf.c:872-875, then the opaque-turb restore (disable BLEND,
DepthMask 1). So the slime is a **brush entity**, drawn by
`R_RenderBrushPoly`.

Decoded vertex colour, uniform across all 2772 verts:
`(0.09803922, 0.09803922, 0.09803922, 1.0)` = exactly **25/255**.
That is `intensity = (float)e->abslight / 255.0f` (gl_rsurf.c:827) with
`abslight == 25`.

`*lowlight6` is `self_emissive` (name[0]=="*", not "*water"), so the
light-point branch at gl_rsurf.c:929 is skipped and control falls to the
`else` at gl_rsurf.c:945 — `GL_ImmColor4f(intensity, intensity, intensity, alpha_val)`.
That contradicts the comment directly above it ("Self-emissive turb
textures ... ignore the surrounding lightmap — they are their own light
source") and contradicts the sibling path: `R_DrawSequentialPoly`
(gl_rsurf.c:1091-1099) explicitly forces `intensity = 1.0` for
SURF_DRAWTURB, and `R_DrawWaterSurfaces` uses (1,1,1,a).

Fix shape: in the SURF_DRAWTURB branch of `R_RenderBrushPoly`, a
self-emissive turb should emit 1.0, not `intensity`.

On its own this is enough to blacken the channel: the correct
`*lowlight6` texel mean is 43.5/255, and 43.5 x 0.098 = 4.3/255.

### Root cause 2 — content: SoT ships a near-black replacement TGA

Texture 4201 is **byte-identical** to
`sot/textures/#lowlight6.tga` (64x64, 24-bit, TGA bottom-up flip applied).
That file has max channel **15/255**, mean **6.0/255** — the correct
`*lowlight6` miptex out of docks.bsp is max 84, mean 43.5.

The engine loaded it faithfully; `IMG_LoadReplacement` deliberately
prefers an external replacement over the BSP miptex
(gl_model.c:598-610), so the busted pack file wins. Its siblings in the
same pack (`#lowlight.tga` max 175, `#lowlight14.tga` max 107) are all
256x256 and normal brightness — `#lowlight6.tga` is the only 64x64 one,
i.e. it looks like a botched export in SoT, not an authoring choice.

### Why the surface reads as pure black

`gl_shader_alias` fragment: `color = tex * v_color`.
6/255 x 0.098 = 0.0025 -> 0.6/255 -> 0 after 8-bit quantisation.
Fog (`u_fog_density` 0.000578, colour 0.078/0.071/0.180) only lifts it a
hair toward dark blue. Both causes are independently sufficient; fixing
only one will not restore the slime.

### Explicitly refuted from the original writeup
- "GL command stream verified CORRECT" — the vertex colour is 25/255, not 1.0.
- "u_alpha_threshold=0 as intended" — it is 0.01, which is what proves the
  draw is not on the R_DrawWaterSurfaces path.
- "6 valid 40x24 liquid textures correctly bound across 7 draws" — one liquid
  draw, one 64x64 texture.
- "texture corruption in GPU memory, unverifiable from the capture" —
  verifiable and verified; the data the engine handed glTexImage2D is the
  pack file, uncorrupted.
- "Mesa RadeonSI ACO miscompilation" — no supporting evidence. Reproduces
  on any GPU.

### Next steps
1. Engine fix for root cause 1 (self-emissive turb ignores MLS_* dimming in
   R_RenderBrushPoly).
2. Report `#lowlight6.tga` to the SoT authors / tell the tester to delete or
   replace it; consider whether the engine should sanity-reject an all-black
   replacement, or at least log replacement hits under `developer 1`.
notes:
RUNTIME VERIFICATION 2026-08-18, capture_sewer_liquid.rdc (SoT docks.bsp, Authentic preset: softemu 3, dither 0.5, r_scale 0.5, 2560x1440, AMD RX 7700 XT / Mesa 26.1.5).

Root cause 1 (engine) is FIXED and verified in the GL stream. Same single liquid draw as the original audit — chunkIndex 2272, glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLES, 0, 2772), program 40 (gl_shader_alias), texture 396 = *lowlight6, alpha_threshold 0.01, blend disabled at draw time by the opaque-turb restore. Decoded the immediate-mode vertex buffer out of the zip.xml blobs (buffer 4435, offset 231476, stride 44, colour at vertex offset 28): all 2771 vertices carry (1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0). The pre-fix capture had (0.09803922, ...) = abslight 25/255. The entity light level no longer scales the self-emissive turb.

Root cause 2 (content) is UNCHANGED and is now the only cause left. Texture 396's uploaded payload is byte-identical to sot/textures/#lowlight6.tga: 64x64, mean RGB (6.42, 7.44, 4.16), max channel 15. docks.bsp's own *lowlight6 miptex is mean luminance 43.5, max 65.3 — same art, roughly 6x brighter.

End-to-end check: with v_color now 1.0 the shader output should equal the texel, and it does — the rendered channel measures mean (7.3, 7.3, 7.2) in the frame against a texture mean of ~6.4-7.4. Nothing in the pipeline dims it any further; what reaches the screen is exactly what the pack file contains.

Remaining decision is content-side, not engine-side: drop or replace sot/textures/#lowlight6.tga (the BSP miptex behind it is fine), or ship an override. img_load.c deliberately does not second-guess a replacement's brightness (uhexen2-0q4f), and that should stay that way.
close_reason:
Closed at Bob's direction 2026-08-18.

Root cause 1 (engine, R_RenderBrushPoly applying MLS_ABSLIGHT to a self-emissive turb) is fixed and verified at runtime in capture_sewer_liquid.rdc: the liquid draw's immediate-mode vertex buffer carries (1.0,1.0,1.0,1.0) across all 2771 vertices, where the pre-fix capture had 25/255. Rendered channel measures mean (7.3,7.3,7.2) against a texture mean of ~6.4-7.4, so nothing in the pipeline dims it further.

Root cause 2 (content) is not an engine defect: texture 396's uploaded payload is byte-identical to sot/textures/#lowlight6.tga (64x64, mean RGB (6.42,7.44,4.16), max channel 15), against docks.bsp's own *lowlight6 miptex at mean luminance 43.5 / max 65.3.

UNRESOLVED OBSERVATION, not investigated: with #lowlight6.tga renamed away, Bob reports the surface renders white rather than falling back to the BSP miptex's brown-olive murk. That is the opposite of too dark and looks like a defect in the BSP-miptex turb path, not in anything this issue fixed. File separately if it recurs — investigation was stopped before a cause was found.

title: PimpModel EF_HOLEY grant re-uploads skins; map-change rollback does not
notes:
2026-08-18 — REOPENED SCOPE, THEN FIXED ON BOTH SIDES. The original fix (993548f88, now 2171992c5) addressed only the ROLLBACK. Reviewing the grant side afterwards found the mirror-image bug in the same feature.

GRANT-SIDE BUG (fixed in d6573ac15, engine/h2shared/pr_cmds.c): the re-upload after PF_pimpmodel's shared mod->flags write tested EF_HOLEY alone:
    if ((mod->flags & EF_HOLEY) && !(mod->orig_flags & EF_HOLEY))
but Mod_LoadAllSkins (gl_model.c:2560) picks tex_mode from EF_TRANSPARENT, EF_HOLEY and EF_SPECIAL_TRANS. Granting either of the other two changed mod->flags without re-uploading the skin.

SHIPPED CONTENT HITS THIS. SoT grants EF_TRANSPARENT (4096) via misc_modelpimp to cndl.mdl, waterfall.mdl, waterfall_90.mdl, crown.mdl, ray3.mdl, elipse.mdl and flame7_violet.mdl, across cathedral / courtyard / keep / palace / winter (verified by parsing all 20 SoT map entity lumps). Those entities took the EF_TRANSPARENT branch in R_DrawAliasModel — glEnable(GL_BLEND), GL_SRC_ALPHA blend func, model_constant_alpha 1.0, force_opaque_alpha 0 — against a skin still uploaded opaque. tex.a was 255 everywhere, so the blend was a no-op and the per-texel translucency the mapper asked for never rendered. Candles, waterfalls and the crown pickup have been silently opaque.

Both sides now test the same mask, (mod->flags ^ mod->orig_flags) & (EF_TRANSPARENT | EF_HOLEY | EF_SPECIAL_TRANS), so grant and rollback are symmetric.

Note the grant is additive (mod->flags = mod->orig_flags | new_flags), so the XOR there only ever reports bits being added; the restore side only ever sees bits being cleared. The shared mask handles both.

EF_SPECIAL_TRANS is included for symmetry but is NOT exercised by SoT — no map grants 32768. Claim limited to what was measured.

VALIDATION: nix build .#nixos passes with both changes. Still no runtime verification (no headless run made) and still no regression test (repo has no test harness).
close_reason:
Fixed in 993548f88 (master), engine/h2shared/gl_model.c.

Mod_RestoreAliasModelDefaults now samples (mod->flags ^ mod->orig_flags) & (EF_TRANSPARENT | EF_HOLEY | EF_SPECIAL_TRANS) BEFORE the restore overwrites mod->flags, and calls Mod_ReuploadAliasSkins(mod) after the write when any of those bits actually moved. Those three are exactly what Mod_LoadAllSkins (gl_model.c:2560) reads to pick tex_mode, so the mask is the precise set that can change a skin's upload.

Ordering matters and is commented: the re-upload must run AFTER the mod->flags write, because Mod_ReuploadAliasSkins passes mod->flags straight through to Mod_LoadAllSkins.

Added a small static helper Mod_AliasDataResident(), mirroring the two branches at the top of Mod_Extradata, and gated the re-upload on it. A model whose alias data has been evicted would otherwise be dragged back off disk during R_NewMap; skipping it is safe because the next Mod_LoadAliasModel re-reads the header flags and re-uploads regardless, and GL_LoadTexture (gl_draw.c:2761) forces a fresh upload whenever the cached texture's TEX_ALPHA/TEX_HOLEY/TEX_FENCE bits disagree with the requested ones.

Case analysis:
- pimped EF_HOLEY on map A, model survives to map B -> XOR non-zero, flags restored, skins re-uploaded opaque. This is the bug, now fixed.
- model purged and reloaded across the transition -> Mod_SaveAliasModelDefaults refreshed orig_flags, XOR zero, skipped. No cost.
- EF_HOLEY baked in the MDL header and also pimped -> XOR zero, skipped. Correct, nothing changed.
- pimp is additive (mod->orig_flags | new_flags), so in practice the XOR only ever reports bits being cleared; the code handles both directions anyway.

VALIDATION: nix build .#nixos passes clean (built twice, once after a comment/placement reorder).

NOT DONE, deliberately: the regression check named in the original DONE criteria was not added. This repo has no test harness at all -- no ctest, no enable_testing/add_test in any CMakeLists, no tests/ tree -- so an automated map-transition assertion would mean building test infrastructure from scratch, which is out of scope for this fix. Flagging rather than silently dropping it.

NOT VERIFIED AT RUNTIME: no headless run was made (project convention is to ask first; llvmpipe runs are very slow here). The fix is guarded and the build gate passed, but the map-transition behaviour has not been observed end to end.

RELATIONSHIP TO uhexen2-khsa: this is a real bug on its own and is fixed regardless. It is NOT confirmed to be khsa's root cause -- the EF_HOLEY pimp grants in SoT target parchment/book/empty*.mdl and never guard.mdl, so the chain to the reported guards is still open. See khsa note (4).

title: Postprocess FBO lifecycle: bloom never created under MSAA; r_hdr/r_bloom runtime toggles don't rebuild FBOs
description:
engine/h2shared/gl_postprocess.c:

(a) PP_CreateFBO's MSAA-success branch (:584-609) returns without calling PP_CreateBloomFBOs (only the non-MSAA path at :650 does), so with vid_config_fsaa >= 2, r_bloom silently does nothing.

(b) PP_CreateFBO only reruns on size change (:1668-1671) and PP_CreateNativeFBO early-returns on matching size ignoring format (:414 vs :420), so toggling r_hdr at runtime keeps rendering into RGBA8 (clamped then tonemapped = washed image) and toggling r_bloom never allocates the pyramid, until a resolution change or vid_restart.

Failure scenario: On MSAA configs bloom never renders; toggling r_hdr or r_bloom at runtime does not apply until resolution change or restart.

Fix: Needs cvar callbacks / format+flags in the rebuild check.
close_reason: fixed in 557f2358c (Cvar_SetCallback on r_hdr/r_bloom sets a rebuild-pending flag consumed by PP_BeginFrame; bloom FBOs created on the MSAA path; native FBO rebuild compares format; disabling bloom releases the pyramid)

title: MD5 model path corrupts cache LRU via Cache_Check on a Hunk_Alloc pointer
description:
engine/h2shared/gl_model.c:352-360 stores a Hunk_Alloc'd header (md5mesh.c:498) into loadmodel->cache.data; Mod_Extradata → Cache_Check then treats the bytes BEFORE the hunk block as a cache_system_t and rewires the LRU chain through them — memory corruption on first draw of any .md5mesh model.

Also hdr->commands==0 so the legacy draw path walks a wild command stream, and mins/maxs/flags are never set.

Failure scenario: Loading and drawing any .md5mesh model causes heap corruption via bogus LRU chain mutation. Related to the tracked PV_IQM dispatch work (uhexen2-7ok0.3) but the cache corruption is a separate unlisted bug.
close_reason: fixed in aa01a127d (cache_is_hunk flag added to qmodel_t, all five Cache_Check/Cache_Free sites guarded, Mod_ClearAll clears MD5 models fully to avoid dangling hunk pointer across map changes, real bounds computed, GL_DrawAliasFrame AND GL_DrawAliasShadow guarded against PV_IQM command-stream walks)

title: Mod_LoadLeafs_V29 reads firstmarksurface/nummarksurfaces as signed short
description:
engine/h2shared/gl_model.c:1678-1679 uses LittleShort without the (unsigned short) cast (the marksurfaces loader already casts unsigned, admitting up to 65535).

Failure scenario: A V29 map with >32K marksurfaces wraps negative → pointer before the array → OOB reads/writes at load, causing heap corruption or crash.

Known QuakeSpasm fix: cast both to unsigned short.
close_reason: fixed in d4c5aee12 (V29 marksurface AND node face indices read as unsigned short — the fix also covered Mod_LoadNodes_V29)

title: Sky rendering leaves GL_SetAlphaThreshold(1.0) set, discarding later translucent draws
description:
engine/h2shared/gl_warp.c:641 and :872 set the sticky imm-mode threshold to 1.0 on the default two-pass sky path and never restore it. Any translucent batch drawn before the next explicit threshold set is fully discarded (frag shaders discard color.a < threshold).

Failure scenario: A DRF_TRANSLUCENT brush entity containing a sky face loses all its remaining non-fence faces (EmitBothSkyLayers via gl_rsurf.c:888-901, then DrawGLPoly with alpha < 1.0).

Concrete case: The sky shader uses the threshold as a mode switch, so it cannot simply be removed.

Fix: Needs save/restore around the sky draw.
close_reason: fixed in 0222c8ab2 (sky draws save/restore the alpha threshold via new GL_GetAlphaThreshold; both the 1.0 and 0.0 leak paths covered)

title: GL_BindDiffuse bypasses the GL_Bind currenttexture cache
description:
engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c:212-216 raw-binds TU0 without updating currenttexture; later GL_Bind calls (e.g. fence/underwater deferred batch gl_rsurf.c:2373-2379, R_DrawWaterSurfaces :1411) can cache-hit on a stale value and draw with the wrong texture.

Failure scenario: Water, fence, or deferred-batch surfaces following a diffuse bind can render with cached-wrong texture until the next explicit GL_Bind to a different texture.

One-line fix: set currenttexture = texnum (compare R_UpdateLightmaps:812 which sets GL_UNUSED_TEXTURE).
close_reason: fixed in 90e99f0c8 (GL_BindDiffuse updates currenttexture)

title: Legacy alias lerp draws the target pose at blend==0 (one-frame forward pop)
description:
engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:1264-1269: on the exact frame a pose changes, R_AliasResolveLerp returns blend==0.0 and the else branch draws the NEW pose fully, then next frame lerps from the previous pose — a per-pose-change stutter with r_lerpmodels 1 on legacy-path entities (viewmodel, translucent, colormapped).

The instanced shader path (mix(v1,v0,blend), gl_shader.c:952) correctly shows the previous pose at blend 0, so the two paths visibly disagree.

Failure scenario: Viewmodel and translucent models with r_lerpmodels 1 show frame-forward jump on every pose change (wrong pose for one frame, then lerp back).

Fix shape: draw prevpose in the blend==0 branch.
close_reason: fixed in e03ca167a (legacy alias path draws prevpose at blend 0, matching instanced path)

title: Instanced shadow pass uses stale lightspot and never-set shadevector
description:
engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:3036-3053: shadow loop runs after collection, but lightspot is a global written per-entity during collect (gl_rmain.c:2523-2524 via AliasModelGetLightInfo), so every shadow uses the LAST collected entity's floor height; shadevector is only ever set in the legacy R_DrawAliasModel path (gl_rmain.c:1464-1468), so instanced shadows shear by a stale/zero direction.

Failure scenario: Visible with r_shadows 1 + r_alias_gpu 1 (instanced path). Shadows cast from wrong floor height and with wrong directional shear.
close_reason: fixed in 06b0ac22f (instanced shadow loop recomputes lightspot and shadevector per entity)

title: Release workflow gated on a live URL probe, failing releases at random
description:
The Release workflow's 'Record this release in the AppStream metainfo' step runs 'appstreamcli validate --explain' on flatpak/io.github.hexenwail.hexenwail.metainfo.xml. appstreamcli fetches every <url> in the file over the network and reports an unreachable one as a warning, and it exits non-zero on warnings. So a release can fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the tag being built.

That killed 0.8.0-beta.r5 (run 32036705332): 'W: url-not-reachable https://github.com/hexenwail/hexenwail/issues' -> 'Validation failed: warnings: 1'. The flatpak job failed, publish depends on it, so publish was skipped and NO r5 release was ever created — the tag is pushed but Latest is still r4.

Not a regression in the repo. r4's release ran the identical workflow with the identical appstreamcli (1.0.2-1build6) the previous day and printed 'Validation was successful.' Same content, same tool, opposite result — most likely r4's request timed out and got skipped while r5's got a clean 404.

Reproduced locally (appstream 1.1.2) by injecting an r6 release entry into a copy of the metainfo:
  appstreamcli validate --explain        -> url-not-reachable, exit 1
  appstreamcli validate --no-net --explain -> Validation was successful.

FIX: add --no-net. The step's job is to check that the injected entry is well-formed, not to probe the internet.

SEPARATE, STILL OPEN: the bugtracker URL genuinely is dead and ships to users in software centres. https://github.com/hexenwail/hexenwail/issues returns 404 because the repo is a fork of sezero/uhexen2 and GitHub hides the Issues tab on forks in the web UI no matter what has_issues says — confirmed has_issues:true, fork:true, public, and the authenticated API endpoint works (returns 0 issues) while the web page 404s. 'gh repo edit --enable-issues' is a no-op here. Only a fork detach would fix it, and the clean fork lineage is deliberate (see the release-versioning memory). Options: drop the optional <url type="bugtracker"> line, or repoint it at the repo root, which returns 200. Deferred to the user.
notes:
ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE, supersedes both earlier explanations: a GitHub platform outage.

Incident 'Incident with GitHub.com', impact=critical, started 2026-08-17T13:40:03Z. At the time of diagnosis Actions, API Requests, Issues and Pull Requests were all in MAJOR OUTAGE; Git Operations and Pages degraded; Webhooks partial.

r5's release run started 13:47:46Z — seven minutes into it. So the 'url-not-reachable' warning on the bugtracker URL was the Issues service being down, nothing to do with the repo being a fork and nothing to do with this machine.

Retract BOTH earlier explanations in this bead:
1. 'The repo is a fork, GitHub hides the Issues tab on forks' — wrong.
2. 'This box's network egress is proxied/filtered' — also wrong. The /issues 404s I measured here, including the sezero/uhexen2 control, were the Issues major outage.

Everything else today was the same incident: r6's build job got 429 then 502 fetching the cachix/install-nix-action tarball (Actions outage), and 'gh run rerun' got a 503 (API outage).

WHAT STILL STANDS: the --no-net fix is correct and is proven. Across r6 and its re-run the flatpak job passed both times, where it was the thing that failed on r5. A release must not depend on GitHub's Issues service being reachable to validate its own metadata, outage or no outage. Fixed in 327bd5510.

The metainfo URLs are correct and were left untouched.

REMAINING WORK: r6 is tagged and pushed but has NOT published — its build job cannot download actions while Actions is in major outage. Re-run 'gh run rerun 32042209626 -R hexenwail/hexenwail --failed' once the incident clears. No code change needed.
close_reason:
Fixed in 327bd5510 (--no-net on the appstreamcli validate call). 0.8.0-beta.r6 published 2026-08-17T16:27Z with all four assets: linux-x86_64.zip, windows-x86_64.zip, .flatpak, SHA256SUMS.

The flatpak job — the one that killed r5 — passed on every attempt after the fix. The remaining failures were the concurrent GitHub outage (critical, started 13:40Z, Actions/API/Issues in major outage, ~50% error rate on archive downloads) preventing the build job from fetching the cachix/install-nix-action tarball. Cleared on a re-run with no code change.

Metainfo URLs left untouched and correct. Both earlier theories about the bugtracker URL — fork hides Issues, then local egress filtering — were retracted; see the notes.

title: OIT_EndTranslucency leaves the viewport at the full scene buffer, displacing glows/viewmodel/mirror when the status bar is up
description:
Reported from play on master: mana orb glows are not aligned to the floating orb.

ROOT CAUSE
engine/h2shared/gl_postprocess.c:1296, in OIT_EndTranslucency():

    glViewport_fp(0, 0, pp_width, pp_height);

is set for the fullscreen resolve triangle and never restored. The function already
queries and restores cull state, with a comment (uhexen2-z4r1) noting that
'R_DrawAllGlows, R_DrawViewModel and R_Mirror all draw after it and expect the
scene's cull state' -- the viewport was missed in that same fix.

The 3D scene viewport is NOT the full buffer. R_SetupGL (engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:4446)
uses glViewport(glx+x, gly+y2, w, h) derived from r_refdef.vrect, and SCR_CalcRefdef
(engine/h2shared/gl_screen.c:436-454) sets sb_lines=36 whenever viewsize < 110, giving
vrect.height = vid.height - 36. So the scene renders into (0,36,W,H-36) while everything
after OIT_EndTranslucency renders into (0,0,W,H): same clip coords, different viewport
transform -> a downward shift plus a vertical stretch.

TRIGGER CONDITIONS (both required)
  * r_oit 1  -- OIT_EndTranslucency early-returns when r_oit is 0 (the cvar default),
                so the viewport is only clobbered with OIT on. Commit 5fea5a5c4
                ('let an archived r_oit survive startup') is the likely reason this
                started showing up in normal play.
  * viewsize 100..109 -- at the 110 default sb_lines is 0 and the two viewports
                coincide, which is why this hides under the stock config.

MEASURED (headless, demo1 blue mana row, paused, 640x480, viewsize 100)
  world geometry, glows off, r_oit 0 vs 1 : mean|d| = 0.000, max = 0  (pixel identical)
  glow blob centroid, r_oit 0            : y = 317.64
  glow blob centroid, r_oit 1            : y = 341.86   -> glow moves 24.2 px DOWN
Predicted from the viewport math for that blob: 343.4. Matches within ~1.5 px.
The orb does not move; only the glow does -- exactly the reported symptom.

BLAST RADIUS
Everything drawn after OIT_EndTranslucency in R_RenderView inherits the wrong viewport:
R_DrawAllGlows, R_DrawViewModel, R_ShowBoundingBoxes, R_ShowPointFile, R_Mirror.
Verified for the viewmodel too: same vantage with r_drawviewmodel 1, glows off, the
weapon is visibly shifted/rescaled between r_oit 0 and 1 while the world and HUD are
pixel-identical.

FIX
Save the viewport at the top of OIT_EndTranslucency with glGetIntegerv(GL_VIEWPORT)
and restore it at the end, in the same style as the existing cull-state save/restore.

REPRO
Headless gamedir left at /home/josh/hexen2/glowtest (cfg glowtest.cfg); run
SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy glhexen2 \
  -basedir /home/josh/hexen2 -game glowtest -window -force -width 640 -height 480 \
  +exec glowtest.cfg
setpos -316 1900 52 0 143 0 on demo1, pause, then A/B r_oit with gl_other_glows.
close_reason: Fixed in c38ff9633. OIT_EndTranslucency now saves the viewport with glGetIntegerv(GL_VIEWPORT) and restores it after the resolve, alongside the existing cull-state save/restore. Verified headlessly on demo1 at viewsize 100: glow centroid delta between r_oit 0 and 1 went from +24.22 px to +0.00 px, viewmodel from mean|d| 6.312 to 0.000, r_oit 0 path bit-unchanged, and OIT still composites (raven-burst smoke sprites render, brightness 606->729).

title: [bug] d81eec5aa turned fullbright masks ON engine-wide; the world is visibly brighter and flatter
description:
MEASURED REGRESSION, found 2026-08-15 while doing uhexen2-jwzf's outstanding bilinear-regression verification. Not a theory -- pixel measurements below.

## What changed

d81eec5aa (uhexen2-me41) replaced VID_Init's derived vid.fullbright with the constant 224.
Measured 'Fullbright start index' with -developer on demo1:

  35f228fe8 (before): 255
  HEAD      (after):  224

## Why me41's premise was wrong

me41 asserted: 'the garbage reliably lands outside [1,256], the guard fires, and 224 is
installed. The engine has been correct by accident.'

That is not what happens on this build. The 4-byte read at offset 256*VID_GRADES takes the
real trailing byte (1) plus three bytes of hunk that read as ZERO, so the expression yields
256 - 1 = 255. 255 is INSIDE the [1,256] the old guard accepted, so the guard never fired and
the 224 fallback was never reached. 255 was installed, every time.

And 255 means NO FULLBRIGHTS AT ALL: Mod_LoadFullbrightTexture (h2shared/gl_model.c) scans
'data[i] >= vid.fullbright && data[i] < 255', which at 255 is '>= 255 && < 255' -- matches
nothing, returns 0, no mask texture on any alias skin or BSP miptex. That has been the
engine's behaviour for its entire history.

me41's comment predicted exactly this outcome for 255 and used it as the argument AGAINST
deriving the value -- correct reasoning, wrong belief about which value was actually live.

## The measurement

Deterministic headless burst, demo1, Blackmarsh, setpos 480 -352 40 0 90 0, host_framerate
0.05, r_lightmap_bicubic 0, 30 frames per build, cross-matched all 30x30 pairs to remove
lightstyle phase (within-run animation envelope is only mean|d| 0.76, so phase cannot
explain anything larger).

  pre-gutter (35f228fe8) vs gutter+fix (f38654033):  mean|d| 0.0007  max 1    0.09% px
  gutter+fix (f38654033) vs HEAD:                    mean|d| 7.8869  max 104  38.03% px
  pre-gutter (35f228fe8) vs HEAD:                    mean|d| 7.9003  max 104  38.65% px
  pre-gutter (35f228fe8) vs HEAD + gl_fullbrights 0: mean|d| 0.0013  max 2    0.16% px

The last row is the proof: turning fullbrights off at HEAD restores the old image to within
2 LSB. The entire 38%-of-pixels difference is fullbright masks, nothing else.

Direction is one-sided: 68187 pixels brighter vs 1430 darker on the first frame pair, mean
signed +14.3. Visually the Blackmarsh brick walls go from a dark falloff to bright and flat,
with the brick pattern popping -- the tree canopy only LOOKS different because it is a dark
silhouette that was invisible against a dark wall and is now visible against a bright one.

## Why this is probably wrong for Hexen II, not just different

224..255 is the Quake fullbright range. Hexen II ships Raven's palette, which uses that range
for ordinary browns and golds -- exactly the brick and trim that lit up. Raven's own colormap
trailing byte says 1, i.e. one fullbright colour, not 32.

## Decision needed, then fix

This is a look change, so it is the user's call, not a mechanical revert:

  (a) Restore historical behaviour: vid.fullbright = 255 (or gate fullbrights off for H2).
      One-line, and returns every existing screenshot/comparison baseline to validity.
  (b) Keep 224 as a deliberate feature, ideally behind gl_fullbrights defaulting off for H2,
      and call it out in release notes -- it changes how every map looks.

Note (a) and the '< 255' upper bound interact: at 255 the scan excludes index 255 too, so
'one fullbright colour' is not actually reachable as written.

## Repro

  SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 glhexen2 -basedir <demo> -window -force \
    -width 640 -height 480 -developer +map demo1
  # read 'Fullbright start index', then compare with and without gl_fullbrights 0

Raw frames and the comparison script were in a job tmp dir and are gone; the recipe above
reproduces them in about two minutes per build.
notes:
FIXED in c55670115.

VID_Init derives vid.fullbright from Raven's colormap again, but as a SINGLE byte read at
offset 256*VID_GRADES, guarded on host_colormapsize (new, recorded by host.c :: Host_Init()
alongside the size check me41 added), falling back to 255. No undefined behaviour: the byte
is inside the buffer, and a colormap carrying only the 64 rows takes the fallback.

EVIDENCE THAT 255 IS CORRECT FOR HEXEN II, not a compromise:
- The colormap's trailing byte is 1 in BOTH the 1997 demo pak0.pak and retail data1/pak0.pak.
  256 - 1 = 255, i.e. one fullbright colour.
- Independent of that byte: pushing all 256 palette indices through the file's 64 lighting
  rows leaves only indices 0 and 255 unchanged. 224..254 are lit. They are Raven's ordinary
  browns and golds, which is exactly why hardcoding Quake's 224 brightened the brick.

Derived rather than hardcoded so a mod shipping its own colormap gets what it asked for.

CONSEQUENCE, deliberate: Mod_LoadFullbrightTexture matches nothing, since its scan is
'>= vid.fullbright && < 255' and Raven's single fullbright colour is index 255, which is also
the transparency index (alpha 0 in d_8to24table). Hexen II having no usable fullbright masks
is the correct answer and was the engine's behaviour for its entire history. The comment says
so explicitly so nobody 'fixes' the upper bound to let 255 through. gl_fullbrights is
therefore inert on stock H2 data -- left in place, it still gates a mod-supplied colormap.

VERIFIED, demo1/Blackmarsh, 30-frame bursts cross-matched to cancel lightstyle phase:
  pre-regression baseline vs FIXED HEAD:  mean|d| 0.0082, max 5, 0.71% px
  regressed HEAD        vs FIXED HEAD:    mean|d| 7.9070, max 193, 38.15% px
The 0.0082 residual is inside the 0.76 within-run animation envelope and is attributable to
the other legitimate render changes in the range (soft particles, magic missile transparency).
'Fullbright start index' now prints 255, matching 35f228fe8.

Chose derivation over both options the bead listed: (a) hardcode 255 loses mod colormaps,
(b) a cvar asks the player to decide something the data already answers.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] All brush entities are invisible on the GL ES tier — instanced path is a no-op but still claims to be available
description:
On the ES tier every brush entity — doors, platforms, buttons, func_wall, func_illusionary, moving brushwork — is collected for drawing and then never drawn. It renders as a hole: you see straight through to whatever is behind it.

## Mechanism
R_BrushInst_Available() (engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c) gates the choice between the unified instanced brush path and the legacy per-entity walk:

    return r_brush_inst.integer != 0 && gl_shader_world.program != 0 &&
           world_vao && world_ibo && lm_atlas_enabled && lm_atlas_texture;

Nothing in that tests the tier, and r_brush_inst defaults to 1 (CVAR_ARCHIVE). But R_DrawBrushInstanced()'s entire body sits inside #ifndef USE_GLES — it needs SSBO-fed instance data and the GL 4.3 world programs, neither of which exists at ES 3.0. So on that tier the function is an empty shell.

The dispatch in R_DrawEntitiesOnList therefore takes the instanced branch, R_CollectBrushInstances marks each entity as collected and not needing legacy, R_DrawBrushInstanced returns immediately, and the legacy fallback loop is skipped because the gate said the fast path was available. Every brush entity is dropped on the floor.

## Evidence
demo1/Blackmarsh, identical camera, ES vs desktop control. The large carved wall panel on the right (a brush entity) is fully present on desktop and entirely absent on ES, showing the lit interior behind it. It is the single largest remaining difference between the two frames — after fixing uhexen2-6yh1 the whole-frame RMSE was 1.23%, and an amplified difference image localises essentially all of it to that one panel.

## Fix
Report the path as unavailable on the ES tier so the dispatch falls through to the legacy per-entity R_DrawBrushModel walk, which is tier-agnostic and already exists as the r_brush_inst=0 path.

## Why it went unnoticed
Same reason as uhexen2-6yh1: nobody could render a frame on this tier outside a browser until uhexen2-0py6, and this failure is silent — no GL error, no console output, just missing geometry. It has been true of every WASM build that ever drew a map.

## Worth checking alongside
Whether any other Available()/Active() predicate makes the same mistake — claiming a capability whose implementation is #ifndef USE_GLES. R_DrawBrushInstanced is unlikely to be the only one; the Hi-Z cull and GPU-particle paths are compiled out on that tier too and should be audited for the same shape.
close_reason: Fixed in 020c91ba5. R_BrushInst_Available() now returns false on the ES tier so the dispatch falls through to the legacy per-entity R_DrawBrushModel walk. Verified on demo1 against the desktop control: the missing carved wall panel is back and matches, and whole-frame RMSE against desktop fell from 1.23% to 0.063%.

title: Post-process shaders are hardcoded to #version 430 core — whole chain is dead on the GL ES tier
description:
Every shader source in engine/h2shared/gl_postprocess.c opened with a literal "#version 430 core\n": pp_vert_src/pp_frag_src (gamma, contrast, FXAA, motion blur, HDR tonemap, softemu palettization), bloom_vert_src + the three bloom fragment stages, and oit_resolve_vert/frag (+ the MSAA variant). gl_shader.c had had a GLSL_VERT_HEADER/GLSL_FRAG_HEADER pair selecting "#version 300 es" since the WASM port; gl_postprocess.c never got one.

Consequence: on the ES tier every one of those compiles fails, PP_InitShader()/OIT_InitShader() return false, and the engine quietly runs with post-processing and OIT disabled. Nothing reports it above the shader log, so the WASM build has silently had no FXAA, no bloom, no gamma/contrast, no softemu and no order-independent translucency for its whole existence.
