Found by building the tier on the desktop for the first time (uhexen2-0py6, -DUSE_GLES=ON against Mesa 26.1.5/llvmpipe), where it is not quiet: Mesa segfaults inside cross_validate_globals() while formatting the link error for the rejected program, so GL_PostProcess_Init() takes the process down at startup.

Beyond the version line, the ES-3.00 violations were:
- no default float precision (the fragment language declares none), and int defaults to mediump, which is too narrow for bayer16's 32-bit shifts — needs both 'precision highp float;' and 'precision highp int;'
- layout(binding=N) on samplers is ES 3.10 / GL 4.2. Redundant here anyway: every one of these units is already set explicitly with glUniform1i (gl_postprocess.c:1117-1118, :803, :1601/:1614/:1634), so the qualifier was dropped on both tiers rather than forked.
- bitfieldReverse() in bayer16 is GLSL 4.00 / ES 3.10 — needs a polyfill on ES.
- oit_resolve_frag_msaa uses sampler2DMS + gl_SampleID (ES 3.10). It could never be selected on ES (glTexImage2DMultisample_fp is a no-op there so oit_samples stays 1), and is now not compiled there at all.
notes:
FIXED in 6f4bccaa7. gl_postprocess.c now has PP_VERT_HEADER/PP_FRAG_HEADER mirroring gl_shader.c, plus an ES precision block (highp float/int/sampler3D), a bitfieldReverse polyfill for bayer16, layout(binding=) dropped from samplers on both tiers (they were already set with glUniform1i), and oit_resolve_frag_msaa not compiled on ES.

VERIFIED on a -DUSE_GLES=ON build against Mesa 26.1.5/llvmpipe under SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen, loading demo1: 'PostProcess: gamma/contrast shader ready' and all three OIT variants report OK, where before the whole chain failed and Mesa segfaulted in cross_validate_globals. Desktop build unaffected (header macro still expands to #version 430 core; the dropped bindings were redundant).

NOT verified in a browser -- no browser here. The WASM build compiles and links (1.7 MB wasm via shell-wasm.nix), but whether WebGL2 accepts these shaders is one browser run away and worth doing before claiming bloom/FXAA/OIT work on the web target.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] VM statement operands index pr_globals with no bounds check — attacker-controlled OOB read AND write
description:
engine/h2shared/pr_exec.c:145-147 defines OPA/OPB/OPC as &pr_globals[st->a] (and .b/.c) with st->a a raw int32 read straight from the progs image. Nothing validates it against progs->numglobals — not at load, not in the dispatch loop. The unsigned short casts that would at least have bounded it to 64K are #if 0'd out at :139-141, disabled deliberately when the engine moved to processing everything internally as v7.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE HEADER-FIELD BEADS (sgw7 / la6r / uglw / 6z5o / w70p, all now closed): those were out-of-bounds READS or writes bounded by a lump size. This is an arbitrary, attacker-chosen index into a float array, and OPC is a WRITE target — 'c->_float = a->_float + b->_float' and friends. A full int32 index reaches +/-8 GB from pr_globals. That is a write primitive, not an information leak.

REACHABLE WITH A PLAYER-SUPPLIED FILE. csprogs.dat arrives with downloaded mod or server content. CL_LoadCSProgs() requires only that the image pass PR_CheckProgsExtents() and export CSQC_DrawHud; from then on csqc_active is true and the bytecode runs every frame via the HUD entry point. The loader hardening just landed in bc9fbb288 vets the *container* (lump extents, string pool terminator, entityfields, numglobals reach) — it deliberately says nothing about the *bytecode*, which is the gap this bead names.

FIX SHAPE: validate operands once at load rather than per-dispatch, so the hot loop keeps its speed. For each statement, check a/b/c against numglobals for the opcodes that use them as global offsets (the operand roles differ per opcode — jumps and OP_IF/OP_IFNOT use them as statement deltas, not global offsets, so a blanket check will produce false rejections). Cross-check against how Ironwail and FTE bound theirs; per the project's Ironwail-parity default, prefer their approach. An alternative worth costing is restoring a mask/clamp in the OPx macros, which is cheap but changes v7 semantics for legitimate large-global images.

Discovered 2026-08-13 while closing uhexen2-uglw. Related: uhexen2-la6r, uhexen2-sgw7, uhexen2-ql7h (untrusted-input tracking). Blocked-by nothing; independent of the closed beads.
close_reason: Fixed in ff66e0567: PR_ValidateBytecode() validates statement operands (per-opcode role table), function first_statement/parm_start/locals/numparms, jump targets, and lump-terminating statement at load; OP_CALL function index and OP_FETCH_GBL reach bounded at dispatch. Verified: 77 real progs images accepted, forged variants refused, 6 game dirs load and play.

title: gamecode/README.txt tells Windows players to overwrite Raven's progs.dat for no benefit
description:
The README's Windows section instructs Windows players to copy gamecode\data1\progs.dat over the game's own file. That instruction is now both POINTLESS and DESTRUCTIVE:

POINTLESS: the Windows release zip is flat, so gamecode/ already sits beside glh2.exe and IS the bundle the engine loads. Wine testing under uhexen2-qoy7 confirmed it is already active with no copying at all.

DESTRUCTIVE: retail progs.dat ships LOOSE with no packed copy to restore from, so the overwrite is irreversible. That exact finding is what shaped uhexen2-8qp3's staged layout in the first place — the release deliberately stages rather than overlays precisely so no instruction ever tells a player to do this.

So the README currently tells Windows users to take an irreversible action that gains them nothing.

BUILD_INFO.txt already has the accurate framing — it presents the staged tree as being for a hand install INTO ANOTHER ENGINE, not into the one shipping beside it. The README's Windows block just lacks that caveat.

Note that Unix is fine: uhexen2-qoy7 retargeted it at the userdir, which both works and is reversible with rm.

RELATED WORK: This is the same class of doc drift as uhexen2-wnkk (the still-stale release-notes text at .github/workflows/release.yml:191-199, which carries the same superseded "It is not installed for you / copy it yourself" wording). Both would sensibly be fixed together.
notes: RAISED FROM P2: This is shipping text in gamecode/README.txt that tells Windows players to overwrite a retail progs.dat file for zero benefit. The file ships loose with no packed copy to restore from, making this instruction irreversible. A release must not ship carrying this instruction.
close_reason: gamecode/README.txt rewritten in 17f8c258c. Removed the harmful Windows instruction to copy progs.dat into the game folder (irreversible, pointless after bundle integration). Replaced with: (1) document that bundled gamecode already sits beside glh2.exe and is automatically loaded (lookup layer 1 satisfied); (2) explain that copying into game folder has no effect because of override ordering (user > bundle > install per uhexen2-qoy7). The copy instruction now lives only under "USING THESE WITH A DIFFERENT ENGINE", where it is a genuine escape hatch for legacy engines that don't read beside their own executable. Three unprompted implementer corrections also adopted: added GAME_REGISTERED gate to PR_BundledProgsPath docs; fixed pre-existing wrong comment about -vanillaprogs fallback; softened "ten maps" to "some" pending progs2.dat map count verification (uhexen2-2z1z filed as follow-up).

title: Site: generated Hexen II entity reference with tutorial cross-index
description:
Build a structured, generated entity reference — the highest-leverage single feature on the site.

Two prior efforts define the target:

1. hexenworld.com's `/h2entities/` was ~150 hand-written HTML pages (`alphents.htm`, `ang_trig.htm`, `artifact.htm`, `ballista.htm`, ...). Comprehensive, and completely dead.
2. Inky's Tips & Tricks page carries a **"Search by entity" cross-reference**: `breakable_brush` → the four articles that use it; `func_door_rotating` → three articles; `func_illusionary` → five. That reverse index is the part that makes documentation actually usable while you are in the editor at 2am.

Do it as **data, not pages**: one YAML file per entity, generating both the reference pages and the cross-reference.

Per entity: name, category (brush / point / trigger / monster / item / light / misc), what it does, every key with type/default/meaning, spawnflags with bit values, which game it exists in (Hexen II, Portal of Praevus, HexenWorld, mod-specific), related entities, worked example `.map` snippet, and **which tutorials and which shipped Raven maps use it**.

The Raven-map usage data is mechanically derivable — decompile or parse the shipped `.map`/BSP entity lumps and count occurrences. Inky's MapSearch tool exists precisely for this and should be evaluated as the extraction path.

Generated views: alphabetical index, by category, and the entity → tutorial reverse index.

Definition of done: schema settled, the full vanilla Hexen II entity set entered, cross-reference generating automatically from tutorial front-matter, and every entity page linking to at least one real usage example.

title: Site: mapping & modding documentation hub
description:
Build the mapping & modding documentation hub — the section that decides whether the community gains new mappers or keeps losing them.

Inky states the problem directly on his site: "I've been struggling to grasp every piece of knowledge about everything (lmp files, coding, texturing, models, etc.) and it's extremely time consuming and often frustrating... it's better to spend time on making awesome maps than trying to solve mundane problems when the solution is known by others."

Structure, following Inky's categorisation:

- **Getting set up** — TrenchBroom + ericw-tools + a Hexen II game config, first compile, first run. The single most important page on the site.
- **Mapping tips & tricks, no coding required** — e.g. rotating doors, ladders and CLIP brushes, monster-blocking, `func_train_mp` tricks, fixing leaks, intermission screens, Quake-style secrets, model skin swaps, objective signposting, outdoor/water setups.
- **Tips & tricks involving HexenC** — chained events, reward drops, armor handling, client effects on models ("Pimp my model").
- **Mapping Academy** — tutorials on native Hexen II features that are simply undocumented: hubs and puzzle pieces, class-specific behaviour, the mission-pack differences.
- **HexenC / progs.dat** — toolchain, compiling, the source layout, what differs from QuakeC.
- **Assets** — models (`.mdl`), skins, textures/WADs, `.lmp` files, sounds, MIDI.
- **The old references, rehosted** — hexenworld.com's `/h2entities/` (~150 pages), `/hexdev/`, `/citadel/`, `/workshop/`, `/mappersshrine2/`, `/nikz/hexenc/`, `/stables/edit.htm`.

Every article carries a **date and a "verified against engine X version Y" line**. Undated tutorials are how the previous generation of documentation became untrustworthy.

**Inky's tutorials are not ours to copy.** Default to linking to his site with a summary; ask permission before mirroring. See the preservation issue for the general policy.

Definition of done: the "getting set up" path is complete and independently walked end-to-end by someone who has never mapped for Hexen II, and the article template with date/verified-against metadata is in use.

title: Site: maps & mods database (data-driven release pages)
description:
Build the maps & mods database — the thing Hexen II has never had and Quake has in Quaddicted.

This is the highest-value original content on the site. Hexen II releases are currently scattered across a dead WordPress, Discord scrollback, ModDB, and archive.org, with no canonical index.

Model: **one YAML/JSON data file per release**, generating a detail page and feeding the index. Fields:

- title, author(s), release date, type (single map / episode / mission pack / total conversion / DM / HexenWorld), version
- required engine and minimum engine version; whether vanilla-compatible
- requires Portal of Praevus? single-player / co-op / deathmatch support
- playable classes, if the release restricts them
- description, screenshots, the author's readme (verbatim, quoted)
- download links (via the files issue), size, SHA-256
- source links: ModDB / archive.org / GitHub / the original release thread
- tags: hub-based, puzzle-heavy, horror, Egyptian, etc.

Index views: newest-first, by author, by type, by engine requirement, by tag.

Seed set: the releases hexenworld.org announced (Privateer's Hold by IronFox, The Tomb of Osiris by Garyou, Tales of the Arabian Deadly Nights by WhirledTsar, Inky's Wheel Of Karma: A Tulku Odyssey and the Karmaverse), plus everything recoverable from the `h2_hexenworld_dot_org_mods` archive.org item and the mods that had hosted sites on hexenworld.com (Siege, DungeonBreak, HexArena, RavenHurst, Rival Kingdoms, HWCTF, Ghost, The Down, The Glyphs).

Definition of done: schema documented, at least 20 releases entered, all index views working, and adding a release is a single new data file plus screenshots.

title: Site: theme, templates, and typography (readable, no-JS, mobile)
description:
Build the theme: templates, CSS, typography, and the base page furniture.

Requirements:

- **Readable first.** These are long technical documents. Body text is the product; the Hexen II atmosphere is trim. Do not repeat the 1999 mistake of dark-red text on a stone-texture tile.
- Dark default, light option, respecting `prefers-color-scheme`.
- **Mobile and small-window layouts must work.** The old sites were 800×600 frame-sets; a large share of readers will now arrive on a phone.
- **No JavaScript required** to read any content page. JS may progressively enhance (search, image lightbox) but never gate content.
- No web fonts loaded from third-party hosts; self-host or use system stacks. No trackers, no analytics beacons, no ad network — the GameSpy banner farm is exactly what killed the reading experience on the original.
- Templates needed: home/news index, news post, doc/article page with a table of contents, database index page with filters, database detail page (map/mod), download list, plain page.
- Article pages need first-class support for **screenshots, inline code blocks (HexenC and `.map` entity snippets), and callout/warning boxes** — Inky's tutorials lean on all three.
- Accessibility: real heading hierarchy, alt text, sufficient contrast, visible focus rings.

Definition of done: every template renders with representative content, the site passes an accessibility audit at a basic level, and it is legible at 360px wide and at 2560px.

title: Site: information architecture, URL scheme, and old-link redirect map
description:
Design the top-level information architecture and the permanent URL scheme.

Proposed top level, derived from what the archived hexenworld.com actually shipped and what modern visitors need:

- `/` — news feed + "start here" entry point
- `/play/` — getting the game, engines per OS, mission pack, installing mods, multiplayer
- `/files/` — downloads: engines, mods, map packs, tools
- `/maps/` — the maps & mods database
- `/modding/` — mapping and HexenC documentation hub
- `/reference/` — entity reference, cvars, console commands, file formats
- `/community/` — Discord, GitHub, active projects, people
- `/archive/` — preserved history: interviews, articles, `.plan` updates, old-site rescues
- `/about/`, `/contribute/`

URL rules (these matter more than the layout — they are what keeps the site linkable in 20 years):

- Lowercase, hyphenated, **no file extensions and no dates in paths** for evergreen content. News posts may be dated.
- URLs are permanent. Renames require a redirect entry, never a silent 404.
- Build a **redirect / "old link" map** for the paths people still link to: `hexenworld.com/h2entities/*`, `/walk/*`, `/siege/*`, `/hexdev/*`, `/citadel/*`, `/workshop/*`, `/mappersshrine2/*`, and the `hexenworld.org` WordPress permalinks. Where we have no equivalent page, point at the Wayback capture rather than dropping the link.
- Every page reachable within three clicks of `/`.

Definition of done: a sitemap document (page tree + URL for each), the navigation model, and the old-link redirect table, all committed to the repo.

title: Site: choose static site generator, hosting, and domain
description:
Pick and record the stack before any content is written, because IA, theme and content format all depend on it.

Decide and document:

- **Static site generator.** Requirements: Markdown content, data files (YAML/JSON) that can drive generated pages (needed for the entity reference and the maps/mods database), taxonomy/tag support, RSS output, and a build that still runs in five years. Candidates: Hugo (single binary, no dependency rot — strongest fit for the durability goal), Eleventy, Zola, or hand-written HTML in Inky's style.
- **Hosting.** GitHub Pages / Codeberg Pages / Netlify, plus a plan for large binaries (see the downloads issue — mod archives can be hundreds of MB and do not belong in the site repo).
- **Domain.** A name that is not `hexenworld.*` unless the old owner hands it over; check availability and note the registrar. Long registration matters more than the name.
- **Repo layout** and whether content lives in the same repo as the theme.
- **Licensing**: site code license, prose/content license, and the fact that third-party mods/maps keep their own terms.

Definition of done: an ADR-style decision recorded on this issue with the chosen generator, host, domain and repo layout, plus a one-paragraph "why not the alternatives".

title: Bundled gamecode overrides a player-installed progs.dat in the userdir
description:
ISSUE: FS_AddGameDirectory assigns the same path_id to a gamedir's basedir and userdir entries, so path_id == 1U is true for both and PR_BundledProgsPath cannot distinguish them. docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md:650-653 (failure mode 7) explicitly assumed the predicate could "consult it and stand down when the player's own file is there"—it cannot.

DEMONSTRATED: With a foreign progs (crc 28154) placed in each location, bundle still wins with crc 10626:
  userdir progs           -> bundle          (crc 10626)
  userdir progs -vanillaprogs -> userdir progs (crc 28154)
  install data1 progs     -> bundle          (crc 10626)

OWNER'S DECISION: The ordering should be: userdir > bundle > install directory.

REASONING:
- The install's data1/PROGS.DAT is Raven's file, and superseding it IS the feature. Every retail install has one, so if a loose file there beat the bundle the bundle would never load at all.
- ~/.hexen2/data1/progs.dat is never created by anything but a deliberate act—retail does not put it there and no installer does. Overriding it silently is the engine second-guessing the only signal of intent available. This also matches the vendor-default < bundled-default < user-override ordering that the rest of the design already assumes.

IMPLEMENTATION: Probe <userdir>/<gamedir>/<progname> (e.g. with Sys_FileType) before substituting, and stand down if present. Windows has no userdir (sys.h :: DO_USERDIRS forced to 0) so the behaviour there is unchanged, and the bundle already sits beside the exe.

COUPLED DOCS CHANGE (also decided): gamecode/README.txt currently directs manual installs into the game's data1/, which per this finding now has no effect. Point it at the USERDIR instead. That makes the manual path work again, stops telling players to overwrite retail files that have no packed copy to restore from, and makes uninstalling "rm" on files they own. Windows keeps the install-dir instruction.

This supersedes the separate M1 finding (a player following release N's README then running release N+1 would otherwise get N+1's bundle by default and N's gamecode under -vanillaprogs, never Raven's).

Note: -vanillaprogs then means precisely "do not use the bundled gamecode", and the startup provenance line names the exact file that loaded, so no bug report is ambiguous.

BLOCKED ON: H1 bead (uhexen2-sgw7)—both touch the same predicate and would collide.
close_reason:
ORDERING NOW: user directory > bundle > install directory. Implemented as a third stand-down condition in PR_BundledProgsPath, deliberately leaving untouched the two conditions an adversarial audit had cleared across 40+ configurations. The new condition can only make the predicate decline more often, never substitute where it previously declined — confirmed empirically by the unchanged mod, portals and bundle-absent rows.

The decision's reasoning: the install's data1/PROGS.DAT is Raven's file and superseding it IS the feature — every retail tree has one, so ranking it above the bundle would make the bundle dead code. But nothing creates ~/.hexen2/data1/progs.dat except a deliberate act: not retail, not any installer. That file is the only statement of intent the engine gets, so it wins.

VALIDATION — the four-row table, both h2ded and the GL client (bundle 10626, retail install 17499, foreign 20799):
- userdir foreign progs → userdir file loads (20799), bundle declined
- same + -vanillaprogs → userdir file (20799), unchanged
- install-dir foreign progs → bundle still loads (10626). Not a tautology: the install's PROGS.DAT was replaced with the same foreign bytes used in row 1, and the bundle still won.
- no player file → bundle (10626), unchanged

Mod rows unchanged, both binaries: sot 28154, soc 58269, karma2 22850, GameOfTomes 41534 each loading their own progs; -portals loading the bundled portals file (44043).

Four extra rows added by the implementer, because condition 3 was otherwise under-covered: a userdir portals/progs.dat with -portals is honoured; a userdir uppercase PROGS.DAT is honoured (case-fold path); a userdir data1 file with -game sot does not leak into the mod; and with the bundle absent, legacy behaviour is unchanged.

COMPOSITION WITH 9f52d0a6a (truncated-bundle extent validation, landed after this work was written): with a userdir file present and the bundle truncated, the engine stands down before the bundle is ever opened — 1 Gamecode: line, 0 Ignoring lines, so the truncation never matters. With no userdir file and the bundle truncated, the extent check still rejects it and falls back — 1 of each. No double-reporting, and FS_LastFileSource() names only the file that actually loaded.

WINDOWS TESTED FOR REAL, not just compiled: the win64 binary was run under wine. userdir is: equals basedir is:, and with a foreign progs in the install data1/ the bundle still won (10626) — proving the new probe is genuinely inert on the DO_USERDIRS 0 path rather than standing the feature down on every retail Windows tree. -vanillaprogs reached the install file; -portals took the bundled one.

Builds PASS on .#default, .#h2ded, .#win64, .#h2ded-win64. /home/josh/hexen2 verified byte-identical across 6739 files before, during and after.

BUILD_INFO.txt needed no change; it had already been retargeted in the same work.

Landed in b93860c0b.

title: Update BUILD_INFO.txt and release notes once bundled-gamecode lookup ships
description: BUILD_INFO.txt currently states the gamecode 'is NOT installed for you', which is true today because nothing reads share/hexenwail/, but becomes WRONG FOR LINUX the moment uhexen2-uwtq lands. The same applies to release-notes text in .github/workflows/release.yml (lines 186-207). Deliberately left untouched by the packaging pass — documenting behaviour that does not yet exist would be worse than the gap. Must be updated in step with piece 3, not before.
notes: RAISED FROM P2: This is shipping text in .github/workflows/release.yml (~lines 186-199) that tells Linux players to copy gamecode files for no benefit. The release now ships bundled gamecode in the right place, and per uhexen2-qoy7's design, files placed in the install directory are overridden by the bundle anyway. A release must not ship carrying these obsolete instructions.
close_reason: BUILD_INFO.txt and .github/workflows/release.yml rewritten in 17f8c258c. Updated to reflect actual bundle state: removed stale phrasing "It is not installed for you" and "copy it yourself", both now false after uhexen2-r32l shipped bundled progs files. Documented actual behaviour: bundled gamecode in <platform>/share/hexenwail/{data1,portals} is automatically loaded by engine via PR_BundledProgsPath (uhexen2-uwtq, landed 9f52d0a6a), no manual copy required. Windows answer improved over brief: documented replacing files inside gamecode\ beside glh2.exe works (layer 1 lookup), those are our files not Raven's, and re-extracting zip restores them. Six passages in docs/GAMECODE.md and docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md corrected where they contradicted the rewrite. Released builds now carry accurate docs for both platforms.

title: Run full verification matrix from BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md
description:
Execute all verification rows from docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md: P1-P10 (precedence), B1-B8 (base behaviour), S1-S4 (savegame), D1-D3 (demo), K1-K5 (known-file) under both h2ded and the GL client.

title: Verify console mouse-selection clamps past end-of-line (Ironwail c03a5bdc1)
description:
CORRECTED RECORD (2026-08-13):

Ironwail c03a5bdc1's actual subject is "Fix up console selection to avoid crash on copy (#415)". It is a CRASH fix caused by length arithmetic, NOT a garbage/stale-character read as previously described.

**Mechanism (Ironwail Quake/console.c:817-825):** eol.col = Con_StrLen(cursor.line) TRIMS trailing spaces; if cursor.col lands past that trimmed length, eol.col - cursor.col goes negative and is passed as a size_t count to Vec_Append, underflowing into a huge memcpy and crashing.

**Why Hexenwail is immune:**

1. Con_ScreenToOffset (engine/hexen2/console.c:817-819) clamps column only to [0, con_linewidth-1] with no knowledge of the line's real text length. Clicking column 60 on a 12-char line yields col == 60. (Original audit was correct on this point.)

2. Console text buffer past end-of-text always contains SPACES (0x20), never garbage. Exhaustive write inventory for con->text:
   - Con_Clear_f (console.c:117-122) space-fills all CON_TEXTSIZE cells, unconditionally reached from Con_Init
   - Con_Linefeed (console.c:265-276) re-fills each newly advanced line with spaces across full con_linewidth
   - Con_Print (console.c:360) writes real characters
   - Con_CheckResize reflow (console.c:220) copies from already-space-filled snapshot
   - con->current incremented only at console.c:272 inside Con_Linefeed, immediately followed by space fill
   - Only decrement at console.c:335 (\r rewind) always followed by Con_Linefeed at :339
   - No line can hold text without being space-filled first

3. Hexenwail's copy loop (console.c:1055) is bounded: for (col = line_start; col <= line_end && buf_pos < (int)sizeof(buf) - 2; col++) — if line_start > line_end, body never executes. No length subtraction to underflow.

4. Hexenwail never trims trailing spaces anywhere in the selection path. Only trim in console.c is at :588-591, in notify-center DRAW code, unrelated to selection.

5. Reads provably in bounds: max index is (con_totallines-1)*con_linewidth + con_linewidth-1 <= CON_TEXTSIZE-1.

**Practical impact of clicking past end-of-line in Hexenwail:** Harmless trailing whitespace in pasted text. No crash, no garbage, no out-of-bounds read. Independent implementation (commit e091812e7) sidestepped entire bug class by never trimming and using bounded loop instead of pointer+length arithmetic.

**RESULT:** Not applicable — Hexenwail immune due to design difference.
notes: Working by dispatched dev agent in worktree as of 2026-08-13. VERIFY task: agent will confirm defect is real before changing anything; no-change result is acceptable outcome (like uhexen2-pxsz). Specific question: does Con_ScreenToOffset (engine/hexen2/console.c:856) clamp click past end-of-line to line's real text length or only to con_linewidth? Does console line buffer past end-of-text hold spaces (harmless) or garbage (bug)?
close_reason: Not applicable: Hexenwail implementation is immune to Ironwail c03a5bdc1 crash hazard due to bounded loop and space-filled buffers; see corrected issue description.

title: Clamp frametime for options-menu live preview (Ironwail 15ab44f36)
description:
Ironwail clamps host_rawframetime to 1/30s before driving the options-menu preview fade so a frame hitch (e.g. toggling a heavy option) doesn't cause a visible jump in the preview animation.

Hexenwail has its own live-preview system (see engine/hexen2/menu.c:7038, "Restore default character alpha in case live preview reduced it") but no equivalent clamp was found. Needs a direct compare against Hexenwail's preview update function before porting — the implementations may differ structurally.

Ironwail commit 15ab44f36 (v0.8.2).

Effort: small once the equivalent function is located.
notes: NOT APPLICABLE / WON'T FIX. No code changed; nothing committed. Ironwail 15ab44f36 patches M_Options_UpdatePreview() (ironwail Quake/menu.c:4690) which ACCUMULATES raw deltas into persistent struct. Hexenwail's Options live-preview was REMOVED in commit 6fc28ba65 (uhexen2-mxx5.8) which deleted M_LivePreviewAlpha, M_FlagLiveEdit, menu_live_edit_time, ui_live_preview cvar, UI_PREVIEW_* constants. Greps for host_rawframetime, UpdatePreview, PREVIEW_FADE, live_preview, M_LivePreview return zero hits across engine/. When it existed it was hitch-immune: M_LivePreviewAlpha computed fade as pure function of absolute timestamp (realtime - menu_live_edit_time), never accumulated delta — nothing to clamp. Surviving preview (waterwarp in gl_postprocess.c:1821) is timestamp-based: pp_waterwarp_preview_end = cl.time + duration, using absolute deadline comparisons. Only host_frametime accumulators in menu.c are ScrollTitle() and credits scroll, not Options preview — and host_frametime is already globally clamped to 0.1s at host.c:739-740. FORWARD-LOOKING: If Options live-preview re-implemented, add 1/30s clamp WITH it — do not lose this concern.

title: Turn off gamepad LED on shutdown (Ironwail b6bbafcf3)
description:
IN_ShutdownGamepad() in engine/h2shared/in_sdl.c calls SDL_CloseGamepad directly without clearing the controller LED first, so some controllers keep the last LED color lit after the process exits.

Hexenwail already has richer LED control than Ironwail (IN_ApplyGamepadLED, joy_led cvar) — just needs a set-LED-to-black call before SDL_CloseGamepad.

Ironwail commit b6bbafcf3 (v0.8.1).

Effort: one call.
notes: FIXED in c88650738. in_sdl.c:358-363 calls SDL_SetGamepadLED(gp_active, 0, 0, 0) before SDL_CloseGamepad(gp_active). CAVEATS: (1) No LED capability guard added — IN_ApplyGamepadLED has none (only guards on gp_active). SDL_SetGamepadLED returns false harmlessly on pads without LED. SDL3 property-based detection would be inconsistent with existing code. (2) RUNTIME-UNVERIFIED: compile-only. No physical gamepad on build box. Needs Windows tester (Mathuzzz) or box with pad to confirm. (3) Covers clean-shutdown path via IN_ShutdownGamepad only (in_sdl.c:917). Crash/SIGKILL leaves LED lit — inherent, matches Ironwail scope. title: BSP entity lump missing NUL terminator (Ironwail 39ba13eda)
description:
Some BSPs ship an entity lump with no trailing NUL. Hexenwail's entity loading does `Hunk_AllocName(l->filelen, "entities")` + `memcpy` of exactly filelen bytes with no +1 and no explicit NUL write — it relies on incidental zero padding from Hunk_AllocName's 16-byte rounding (engine/h2shared/zone.c:396-424 does `size = sizeof(hunk_t) + ((size+15)&~15)` then memset 0). When filelen lands on a 16-byte boundary there is no padding and the entity string is unterminated, so the parser walks off the end.

Affects engine/h2shared/gl_model.c:978 and engine/h2shared/sv_model.c:333.

Fix matches Ironwail commit 39ba13eda line-for-line in root cause: allocate filelen+1, memcpy filelen, then write buf[filelen] = '\0'.

Effort: trivial.
notes: FIXED in df9845ca7. Both Mod_LoadEntities (gl_model.c:978-981, sv_model.c:333-336) now allocate l->filelen+1 and write entities[l->filelen]='\0'. FINDINGS: (1) External .ent file path uses FS_LoadHunkFile->FS_LoadFile, already allocates len+1 with terminator (quakefs.c:1054,1083) — no fix needed. Defect confined to embedded lump path. (2) entity_file_size left at l->filelen (NOT +1) — it's used as progress-bar denominator (pr_edict.c:1776), +1 there would silently break progress math. Verified: nix build + nix build .#h2ded both pass on master.

title: Bundle compiled progs.dat in the release zip
description:
The owner has decided releases should ship our compiled gamecode, so uhexen2-9r3n's fix and uhexen2-hwky's BadBackpackDump instrumentation actually reach players instead of being inert. packages.gamecode (commit 8272423e1) already produces the artifacts — data1/progs.dat (889056 B), data1/progs2.dat (839396 B), portals/progs.dat (1148080 B), hw/hwprogs.dat (953380 B), siege/hwprogs.dat (796276 B), bit-reproducible. What is missing is wiring them into packages.release and the release workflow.

========== SCOPE: SHIP DATA1 + PORTALS ONLY ==========

**Ship in release zip:**
- data1/progs.dat (889056 B)
- data1/progs2.dat (839396 B)
- portals/progs.dat (1148080 B)

**Do not ship (deferred):**
- hw/hwprogs.dat (953380 B)
- siege/hwprogs.dat (796276 B)

**Reasoning for portals inclusion:**
docs/GAMECODE.md's precedence trace shows that the gamedir search order is prepend-only; portals/progs.dat shadows data1/progs.dat for players with the mission pack active (those passing -game, -portals, -missionpack, or running a mission pack mod). Shipping only data1/progs.dat would silently leave Portals players running retail bytecode even though we have a compiled version. The uhexen2-8zia audit confirmed this: portals/progs.dat has 2043 functions vs retail's 2041, with 160 opcode differences. A bare launch with no arguments does reach data1/progs.dat, so both trees must be included.

**Reasoning for hw/siege deferral:**
No retail HexenWorld bytecode exists on the dev box (find /home/josh/hexen2 -iname hwprogs.dat returns nothing), so the uhexen2-8zia audit cannot classify hw/siege divergences. Shipping them would mean releasing gamecode of exactly the class of unknown that uhexen2-qj8s turned out to be — an undocumented fork divergence nobody decided on. Deferred until reference bytecode exists and uhexen2-onfa (the HW audit task) completes. Related work: uhexen2-o4tn flags undecided fork gamecode present in hw and siege trees.

Three things this must get right, all established by work done today:

1. **Which trees to ship.** DECIDED: data1 + portals. hw/siege deferred until audit complete.

2. **uhexen2-qj8s is a hard blocker.** Our gamecode/hc/h2/invntory.hc disagrees with every shipped progs.dat about the Crusader's Glyph of the Ancients (TimeBombThink, orbits, 5s fuse — versus TimeBombBoom, detonates in place at +0.75s). Bundling without resolving it ships a silent gameplay change to a core artifact. Audit classified this as an unreverted accident; the owner is reverting Use_TimeBomb/TimeBombTouch in h2 and portals only (hw/siege intentionally untouched, consistent with this scope deferral).

3. **It changes what 'vanilla' means for every future bug report.** zmb3 flagged this explicitly and it cuts both ways — a tester reporting odd behaviour may now be running our gamecode, not Raven's. Worth a line in the release notes and possibly a console line at startup identifying which progs is loaded.

Unblocks the practical value of uhexen2-9r3n and uhexen2-9gdx.
notes:
AUDIT ESTABLISHES TWO HARD CONSTRAINTS FOR BUNDLING 2026-08-13

Gamedir search order (quakefs.c:420-434, 1537-1747):
- data1/ added first
- mod gamedir added last

This means portals/progs.dat shadows data1/progs.dat for Portals players (those passing -game, -portals, -missionpack, or running a mission pack mod that adds portals to the search path).

1. TRIGGER WAS DEAD — The original keyed off `push` to branch `mathuzzz_mdl_fixes`, which no longer exists. Replaced with `workflow_dispatch` (optional `ref` input) plus `push: tester/**`. The `ref` input is load-bearing: `workflow_dispatch` can only run a workflow file on the selected ref, and the commits most worth handing to a tester (khsa probe builds on `rescue/khsa-*`) predate this file. Dispatching from master with `ref` set is the only way to build them.

3. REAL BUG FIXED — The original copied `result/release/linux-x86_64/bin/glhexen2` ALONE. Confirmed with patchelf that the binary carries `rpath: $ORIGIN/../lib` and `interpreter: /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`, while the required 36 shared objects live in `linux-x86_64/lib/`. A single-file copy meant **every Linux tester build from that workflow was unrunnable.** Now copies the whole tree (bin/ + lib/ + licenses + BUILD_INFO), matching release.yml. Also closed a script-injection hole: dispatch `ref` reaches the packaging step via `env:` rather than being pasted into unquoted heredoc.

DELIBERATE OMISSION: gamecode is NOT bundled into tester builds. .#release ships no progs.dat today, so bundling would make tester builds differ from releases in gamecode content — worst confusion for khsa/zroc where reports are about rendering. Follow-up filed (new task).

Packaging executed by hand against real .#release tree. `nix build .#release` and `nix run .#nixos -- -help` both succeed.

NOT VALIDATED: GitHub Actions itself (cannot be run locally). The workflow has never executed — only its nix commands and packaging shell. Linux bundle proven to link correctly but not to run (this box lacks /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2). First real use should be sanity-checked on a normal distro.

0ce621e42 bindless nonresident-before-delete -- DISCARDED. uhexen2-ubsu removed the bindless scaffolding entirely (8124ed055); there is no 'bindless' or 'BINDLESS' identifier left in engine/. The commit made glMakeTextureHandleNonResidentARB run before texture deletion, and both the call site and the entry point are gone. uhexen2-im9g holds the preconditions if bindless is ever revisited, and this hygiene point should be re-derived from that design rather than cherry-picked onto it.

4e10fe2cc r19 drop r_gl_dither -- LANDED via uhexen2-ymie as fcef8f5d2. No r_gl_dither identifier remains in engine/.

c18e0ec0e r18 dither callback -- DISCARDED as moot. It mitigated the r17 callback firing glEnable(GL_DITHER) at init; the r19 revert removed the cvar, the callback and the registration outright, so there is no longer anything for the mitigation to attach to. Per r19's own message all three GL_DITHER variants regressed alpha-test cutouts, so re-landing the r18 half would reintroduce the runtime flip that was the point of removing it.

87719ff2e ci-mdl.yml -- LANDED via uhexen2-n3lb as 9997d68af, adapted rather than restored verbatim: the original keyed off 'push: branches: [mathuzzz_mdl_fixes]', a branch that no longer exists, so it was retriggered on workflow_dispatch (with a ref input) plus 'push tester/**'. The file is present at .github/workflows/ci-mdl.yml.

Acceptance met on both halves: preserved (pushed) and consciously dispositioned (one re-landed, two landed elsewhere, two discarded with reason).

title: r_gl_dither still live on master: restore the lost r19 revert
description:
LIVE REGRESSION: r_gl_dither is still live on master in its r17 form (gl_rmain.c:119-126; gl_rmisc.c:236-252 and 374-377). Default '1' plus the '/* apply initial state */' callback at gl_rmisc.c:377 fires glEnable(GL_DITHER) at startup — exactly what r19 removed.

The lost r19 revert (4e10fe2cc) should be re-applied by restoring the r19 hunks from gl_rmain.c and gl_rmisc.c (deliberately NOT the quakedef.h version hunk, which would move the version backwards from 0.7.9-beta.r11 to 0.7.8-beta.r19).

CONSTRAINT: This is independent of the screen-door bug in uhexen2-khsa — it is its own rendering regression.

ACCEPTANCE: r_gl_dither code removed from gl_rmain.c and gl_rmisc.c; master builds cleanly.
close_reason:
Fixed on master in fcef8f5d2 — "revert(khsa): drop r_gl_dither cvar; restore lost r19 revert".

The r19 revert (4e10fe2cc) was lost along with the deleted mathuzzz_mdl_fixes branch, so its removal never reached master and the cvar kept shipping in its r17 form — cvar_t r_gl_dither = {"r_gl_dither", "1", CVAR_ARCHIVE} at gl_rmain.c:119-126, R_GLDitherChanged_f at gl_rmisc.c:236-252, and registration plus an /* apply initial state */ call at gl_rmisc.c:374-377 that fired glEnable(GL_DITHER) at startup. All three regions matched the original description exactly; all three are now removed.

Per r19's own commit message, this is the variant that regressed alpha-test cutouts: "Three rounds of GL_DITHER experimentation all regressed alpha-test cutouts on bobberb's card — r16 (unconditional glDisable), r17 (cvar fired glEnable at init), r18 (cvar skipped init glEnable but still allowed runtime flip). Even the spec-no-op call by itself was enough to perturb downstream alpha-test on this driver." The r18 mitigation was missing too, so master had been sitting at the worst of the three since 0.7.8-beta.r29.

Validation: nix-builder PASS on default Linux and win64 with zero new warnings; headless runtime confirms the cvar now prints Unknown command.

title: Ship a rebuilt progs.dat so gamecode fixes actually reach players
description:
Every gamecode fix we land is currently inert for real users. gamecode/ is excluded from the nix build (flake.nix:46) and we ship no progs.dat, so players run Raven's retail data1/progs.dat from 1997. Two P0/P3 bugs are already in this state:

- uhexen2-9r3n (P0): DropBackpack deletes mana-only drops. Fix is a 5-line deletion in gamecode; reaches nobody.
- uhexen2-hwky: the non-destructive "Bad backpack!" fallthrough and BadBackpackDump instrumentation. The instrumentation is the only way to root-cause the remaining field reports, and testers cannot run it.

Raised directly by the field. Tome of Power Abuser pulled r11 expecting the backpack fix and asked "there is still a bug AND progs.dat isn't in the zip?". Spoike's advice on Discord 2026-08-13: "if you've got pop then use that instead... or the data1 .dat from uhexen2. even if it doesn't resolve the actual problem, it'll help avoid other weirdness", plus "frankly, Raven's original data1/progs.dat was buggy as heck, and data1/progs2.dat was just an extra annoying weirdness".

We are well positioned for this: gamecode/ in this repo IS the uHexen2 (Hammer of Thyrion) gamecode, with a changelog of Raven bug fixes through 1.29c (gamecode/README), and gamecode/patch111/ already carries a data1/ tree plus patchdat. gamecode/COMPILE documents the hcc invocation, and hcc builds from .#utils. All four trees (h2, portals, hw, siege) were verified to compile clean during uhexen2-hwky.

Open questions to settle before committing to this:
- Which trees do we ship? h2 needs both progs.dat and progs2.dat.
- Savegame and demo compatibility across a progs change, and behaviour when a user mixes our progs.dat with a mod that ships its own.
- Mission pack and mod interaction: portals has its own progs.dat, and SoT / Wheel of Karma ship theirs. We must not override a mod's progs.
- Distribution: bundled in the zip vs an optional download. Bundling changes what "vanilla" means for every bug report we receive, which cuts both ways.
- Licensing / redistribution of Raven-derived gamecode -- check what uHexen2 itself does, since they already distribute it.
design:
Smallest useful first step is a build-and-verify pipeline, not a distribution decision: add an optional nix output that runs hcc over gamecode/hc/h2 and emits progs.dat + progs2.dat, so gamecode changes are at least COMPILED in CI and cannot silently rot. Distribution can stay off by default while that lands.

Then decide bundling separately, with the mod-override question answered first: confirm the engine's gamedir search order means a mod-supplied progs.dat always wins over one we place in data1/.
acceptance_criteria: gamecode/hc/h2 builds to progs.dat + progs2.dat as part of a nix output, and a documented path exists by which a player can obtain and install it. The mod-override behaviour is confirmed, not assumed.
notes:
DECIDED 2026-08-13:\n\n1. cachix: continue serving compiled progs.dat from CI. Rationale: repo already ships .hc sources in every clone, so compiling adds no new exposure; upstream uHexen2 distributed compiled progs for 20 years while shipping Raven pak content only as xdelta patches, drawing the line in the same place assets/demo/README.md does.\n\n2. bundling: progs.dat will be bundled in release zips. Reverses zmb3's original default of 'distribution stays off'. Every player installing a release will run our compiled gamecode, enabling fixes like uhexen2-9r3n and instrumentation like BadBackpackDump to actually reach users.\n\nSTILL UNDECIDED: savegame and demo compatibility across progs change; behaviour when user mixes our data1 progs with a mod that ships its own (precedence already established: mod wins). docs/GAMECODE.md 'Not yet decided' section requires updating (dev work, not bd).
[HISTORICAL] The close_reason validation section lists byte counts from commit 8272423e1:
- 889056 (data1/progs.dat)
- 839396 (data1/progs2.dat)
- 1148080 (portals/progs.dat)
- 953380 (hw/hwprogs.dat)
- 796276 (siege/hwprogs.dat)

These sizes for data1 and portals became stale after ce8c9d1c4 (fix(gamecode): 
revert TimeBomb glyph to retail behaviour). Correct current values:
- data1/progs.dat: 888368 bytes
- data1/progs2.dat: 838712 bytes
- portals/progs.dat: 1147444 bytes
- hw/hwprogs.dat: 953380 (unchanged)
- siege/hwprogs.dat: 796276 (unchanged)

See uhexen2-8qp3 and uhexen2-qj8s for context and corrected figures.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in commit 8272423e1 ("build(nix): compile the gamecode in CI so .hc fixes stop rotting"):

WHAT: new packages.gamecode (flake.nix:316) running hcc over all four HexenC trees (h2, portals, hw, siege), producing progs.dat and progs2.dat. Includes new gamecodeSrc filter (flake.nix:99) scoped to gamecode/hc/ only. CI "Build gamecode" step added (.github/workflows/ci.yml:90). New docs/GAMECODE.md documents build, install, precedence, and licensing.

VALIDATION: nix build .#gamecode PASS. All five outputs bit-reproducible and matching reference byte counts (889056 / 839396 / 1148080 / 953380 / 796276). Engine input hash unchanged — .drv paths identical to pristine bb570666a for all six targets (nixos, h2ded, win64, h2ded-win64, utils, utils-win64); .#nixos and .#h2ded were pure store hits with nothing rebuilt.

DESIGN: gamecodeSrc separate from filteredSrc (not extending it). Rationale: sharing a source would rebuild every downstream target (engine, h2ded, both mingw builds, WASM, toolchain) and invalidate all user cache on any .hc edit — files that cannot affect a byte of any binary. Verified both by .drv paths and by empirical cache hits.

MOD PRECEDENCE (the critical confirmed fact): a mod's progs.dat beats one in data1/ unconditionally. Search path is prepend-only (quakefs.c:420-421, 434-435), lookup returns first hit and stops (quakefs.c:865, 887, 910). data1/ added first (quakefs.c:1537-1538), mod gamedir last (quakefs.c:1727-1747 → 565). progs loaded by relative name (pr_edict.c:1919, 2084-2085). No .pak vs loose-file dependence — all mod entries sit above all data1 entries. Related: loose files beat .paks within a directory (quakefs.c:424-428), which is why any data1/ drop-in works at all.

LICENSING: upstream hcode is Raven's own public source release (README-hcode_archive.txt; siegesrc.txt is Mike Gummelt's hand-off). uHexen2 shipped compiled progs in gamedata-all-*.tgz and binary packages ~20 years, while shipping Raven pak content in the same tarball only as xdelta patches. Upstream draws the line where assets/demo/README.md does, progs on the redistributable side. No COPYING accompanies gamecode upstream or here. demodata got lib.licenses.unfree + hydraPlatforms=[] because compiling adds exposure; gamecode sources already ship in every clone, so compiling adds none. Kept licenses.gpl2Plus. Full reasoning in docs/GAMECODE.md.

FLAGGED FOR REVIEW (not a blocker): compiled progs.dat bytes now served from our binary cache. Documented reasoning above; cachix exclusion is the remedy if anyone disagrees. Record this explicitly so it stays reviewable.

LEFT UNDECIDED for a later pass (these were zmb3's own open questions):
- Release-zip bundling vs optional download
- Savegame and demo compatibility across a progs change
- Behaviour when user mixes our data1/ progs with a mod that ships its own
- Install helper/script
- .#gamecode referenced by other outputs

ACCEPTANCE MET: gamecode/hc/h2 builds to progs.dat + progs2.dat as part of nix output; documented path exists (docs/GAMECODE.md § Installation); mod-override behaviour confirmed analytically (search path, lookup, gamedir order) not assumed.

title: Audit client_t/svs for other pointers into hunk or sv.* that dangle across changelevel
description:
Generalises the uhexen2-rutp root cause (fixed in d46d000c5).

The pattern: Host_ClearMemory does Hunk_FreeToLowMark(host_hunklevel) then memset(&sv, 0, sizeof(sv)) on every map load, so everything sv points at is freed and every sv.* pointer is nulled and reallocated at a new address. But svs.clients is allocated once in Host_Init, below host_hunklevel, and survives — memset only happens in Host_ClearClients. So ANY pointer cached in client_t (or elsewhere in svs) that aims into the hunk or into a per-map sv allocation is dangling for the rest of the session after the first changelevel.

client->ex_inventory was one instance and produced a nondeterministic P1 crash that went unexplained for months. This bead is to find the others before they do the same.

Fields to check in client_t: edict (points into sv.edicts, which is hunk memory reallocated per map), and every other pointer member. Also anything in server_static_t. And the mirror question on the client side: cl is memset by Host_ClearMemory too, so anything outside cl caching a pointer into cl.* or into per-map hunk allocations has the same shape.

Method that worked for rutp: read Host_ClearMemory, list what it frees/zeroes, then grep for pointer fields in the surviving structures and check every assignment site to see whether it re-runs per map. Confirm suspects by reproducing headlessly — 'map demo1' then 'changelevel demo2' under gdb on the demo data is enough, no mod or Windows box needed.

ACCEPTANCE: every pointer field in client_t and server_static_t is either shown to be re-assigned on each map load, shown not to point at freed memory, or fixed.
notes: The changelevel/signon observation is filed as uhexen2-y3i5.
close_reason:
Audit done. Result: client_t and server_static_t are clean apart from the ex_inventory bug already fixed in d46d000c5. No new dangling pointers found, and that is a useful answer — it means uhexen2-rutp was the single instance of this class, not the first of many.

client_t has exactly three pointer fields:
  netconnection  — owned by the net layer, not hunk memory. Safe.
  edict          — points into sv.edicts, which IS per-map hunk memory, but SV_SpawnServer re-points it for every client at sv_main.c:2481 ('svs.clients[i].edict = ent'). Safe.
  ex_inventory   — was the bug. Fixed.
Its message/datagram sizebufs point at msgbuf/datagram_buf, which are inline arrays inside client_t itself, so they move with the struct and are never freed independently.

server_static_t.clients is allocated once in Host_Init below host_hunklevel — it is the thing that survives Hunk_FreeToLowMark by design, which is what made the ex_inventory mismatch possible in the first place.

Client-side mirror (cl is memset by Host_ClearMemory too): cl.ex_items and cl.scores live inside cl, so the memset nulls them and they are reallocated per map; cl.ex_inventory is an inline array, not a pointer. Nothing outside cl caches a pointer into it.

Renderer globals that aim into per-map model memory: r_viewleaf is explicitly NULLed by R_NewMap; r_oldviewleaf is never dereferenced anywhere — only compared and assigned — and R_SetupFrame overwrites it from r_viewleaf before any use, so a stale value cannot be read. player_models[] is reassigned on every map in CL_ParseServerInfo and points into the static mod_known[] array rather than the hunk.

Startup allocations (particles, notexture, con_main, inverse_pal) all happen before host_hunklevel is taken at host.c:1102 — R_Init runs at 1075 — so Hunk_FreeToLowMark never reaches them.

The dangerous shape specifically searched for was 'file-scope static pointer + alloc-once guard + allocated above host_hunklevel', since that never re-allocates after the first Host_ClearMemory. Four alloc-once guards exist. Three are on sv./cl. members, where the memset nulls the guard variable so it correctly re-fires each map. The fourth is inverse_pal, which is startup-only and is read nowhere outside its own construction.

Empirical backstop: demo1 -> demo2 -> demo1 -> demo2 -> demo1, five server spawns, completes clean with no crash and no protocol error. The same script segfaults on the pre-fix baseline.

One note recorded as uhexen2-<changelevel-signon>: issuing 'changelevel' from a script before signon completes produces a client-side 'svc_updatename > MAX_CLIENTS' Host_Error. That is a test-harness artifact rather than a field bug — a player cannot type into the console mid-signon — but it cost time to distinguish from a real desync, so it is written down.

title: Items missing from maps vs FTEQW port — possible entity spawn regression
description:
## Report

Participants:
- **Garrett (Monolyth-42)** — external tester / bug reporter. Plays Hexen II across engines and is comparing Hexenwail against the FTEQW port. Source of this report; posted screenshots (not available as text).
- **Spoike** — FTEQW / FTE engine developer (NOT a Hexenwail maintainer). Offered diagnostic hypotheses from engine-dev perspective; hypotheses are informed guesses, not confirmed findings.
- **sakabato** — Hexenwail maintainer. Requested repro details; noted this is the SECOND missing-item report.

## Symptoms

Garrett reports items which "should be there but aren't" are missing in Hexenwail, while the FTEQW port DOES spawn these items. A green key was cited as one comparison case. Screenshots from Discord showed the item present in FTEQW but missing in Hexenwail.

**KEY BLOCKER: Exact item names, map/level, engine version, OS and GPU are all UNKNOWN.** The maintainer asked for these details and had not received an answer at transcript time.

## Diagnostic Hypotheses (from Spoike)

Record these as leads to investigate IN THIS ORDER:

1. **Entities falling out of the world** — Enable `developer 1` and check for messages about items dropping out of the level.

2. **Spawnflags class/gamemode filtering** — Hexen II filters entity spawns by player class and by coop/deathmatch spawnflags (bitmask). An off-by-one or misinterpretation in spawnflag parsing would silently delete items while the rest of the map remains playable.
   - **Strong signal:** The "green key" detail is suggestive here. Keys are class/progression-gated items in Hexen II; a spawnflag class-filter bug is a plausible fit for selective missing items.

## Analysis: Screenshot Provenance (2026-08-12)

**FINDING 1: Screenshot is NOT from Hexenwail (high confidence, two independent proofs)**

The window title bar reads "Hexen II MP: docks". Hexenwail cannot produce that string:
- `engine/h2shared/gl_vidsdl.c:578` is the ONLY `SDL_SetWindowTitle` call site in the engine; it passes compile-time constant `WM_TITLEBAR_TEXT`.
- `WM_TITLEBAR_TEXT` (defined `gl_vidsdl.c:143-152`) is only `"HexenWorld"` (H2W builds) or `"Hexen II"` (all others). The `"Hexen II+"` mission-pack variant (lines 146-148) is COMMENTED OUT, so even H2MP builds fall through to plain `"Hexen II"`.
- Hexenwail's title is static and never appends the current map name. The screenshot title has both an `MP` tag and `: docks`.

The console spam reads `PF_FCLOSE: FILE OUT OF RANGE` (4 lines). Hexenwail cannot produce that either:
- "out of range" (case-insensitive) appears nowhere in Hexenwail except unrelated sites: `sv_model.c:884,912` (clipping hull), `hashindex.c:86`, `stb_image.h:2514`.
- Hexenwail has NO QuakeC file builtins (`PF_fopen`, `PF_fclose`, `PF_fgets`, `PF_fputs`) and no FRIK_FILE extension anywhere. Grep returns empty.
- `PF_FCLOSE` is not a builtin Hexenwail implements; that message cannot originate from us.

CONCLUSION: This is Garrett's CONTROL screenshot — evidence that the item exists in the OTHER engine (FTEQW port). It is NOT evidence of a Hexenwail defect. **We now have ZERO screenshots of the bug reproducing in Hexenwail.** This is the single most critical gap.

**FINDING 2: PF_FCLOSE spam is the other engine's bug, not Hexenwail's**

Worth recording to prevent chasing dead leads. The reported floats (3.74147E-43, 4.30199E-43, 4.33001E-43, 4.82047E-43) decode to small integer bit patterns (267, 307, 309, 344). This is the classic signature of raw integer file handles stored in float-typed QuakeC variables without conversion: host's fopen returned an int handle, progs passed the bit pattern to fclose, and fclose validated it as a float and rejected it out-of-range. This is a host/progs ABI mismatch in the OTHER engine's FRIK_FILE implementation. NOT related to our missing-items report and must NOT be filed against Hexenwail.

**FINDING 3: Map name confirmed; campaign still unknown**

The map is **`docks`** (from window title). This answers one outstanding repro question. Caveat: the `MP` tag indicates a mission-pack-capable build, but grepping `gamecode/` for "docks" returns nothing (map names live in .bsp changelevel triggers, not in HexenC). So campaign still needs confirmation from Garrett.

## Status

**BLOCKED ON REPORTER INFO.** Cannot investigate further without the following from Garrett:

### Blocker Checklist

- [ ] **URGENT: Screenshot or video of the item MISSING in Hexenwail itself** — the greenkey.jpg shown is from the OTHER engine. We have zero visual evidence the bug reproduces in Hexenwail at all.
- [ ] **URGENT: Confirm which campaign `docks` is from** — the map name is now known to be "docks", but we need the campaign (vanilla Hexen II, Hexen II: Portal of Praevus, or Hexen II: Wrath of Chromatic Dragon) to load the correct .bsp.
- [x] **Map name / level** — ANSWERED: `docks`
- [ ] Item name(s) that are missing
- [ ] Hexenwail version tested (latest release: 0.7.9-beta.r9)
- [ ] OS and GPU used
- [ ] Game mode: single-player vs coop vs deathmatch, and which player class
- [ ] Whether `developer 1` prints anything about the entity at spawn time

This is the second such report; if a previous related issue exists, link/merge into it.
notes:
EXTERNALLY CONFIRMED 2026-08-13. Garrett (Monolyth-42) reported back on Discord: "Yes, it's all right now", with screenshots, running a master build on Storm OS (Arch), GOG data, AMD RX 590. Wheel of Karma level 1 and Storm over Thyrion both spawn their items. That satisfies the "still worth a tester pass" caveat in the close reason -- Linux rather than Windows, but from the original reporter with the original data set.

Note the workaround this issue narrowed (v.mins/v.maxs -> absmin/absmax) has since been REMOVED outright in uhexen2-cm1a, after it turned out never to have been load-bearing. The item-spawn fix now stands on the progs sizing itself in PlaceItem, not on anything the engine supplies.
close_reason:
Root-caused and fixed in c86f09b14.

The regression is 8ca3be8bb (2026-05-13), Hexenwail's own workaround for uncollectable puzzle pieces. It wrote a -8 -8 -28 / 8 8 8 box into v.mins/v.maxs in SV_LinkEdict for any 'puzzle*' entity that linked with zero size. v.mins/v.maxs is the physics box, so PlaceItem's droptofloor() then traced that fattened box downward; any piece placed within 28 units of a floor brush or flush against a door started solid, a start-solid trace returns fraction == 1, droptofloor() returns 0, and the progs delete the item printing 'fell out of level'. FTEQW carries no such workaround, which is exactly why the item is present there and missing here.

Reproduced locally, no reporter input needed. 'docks' turned out to be a Storm over Thyrion map (sot/maps/docks.bsp), not vanilla or Portals — that answers the outstanding campaign question. Its entity lump holds one puzzle_piece with netname 'Green Key' / puzzle_id 'greenkey' at 1102.4 -1015.2 571, i.e. literally the green key Garrett cited. Loading docks headless (SDL offscreen + llvmpipe) on the pre-fix build destroyed it at load; the map ends up with one puzzle_piece (Yellow Key) instead of two.

Fix: widen only absmin/absmax, which feed SV_TouchLinks, the areanode links and the SV_ClipToLinks broad phase. Every trace and the narrow phase still use v.mins/v.maxs, so the intended pickup box is unchanged and collision is back to vanilla. Worth noting the original ogsd diagnosis was wrong about the progs: StartItem sets the real -8 -8 -28 box itself after droptofloor, in both data1 and SoT progs, so pieces end up correctly sized either way — only the ordering was wrong. The workaround is now effectively vestigial but harmless.

Also added a developer-gated failure reason to PF_droptofloor (start-solid vs no-floor-within-256, plus the blocking entity's classname). The progs' 'fell out of level' line names neither, and that print is what identified this in one run.

Verified: docks spawns both puzzle pieces, Green Key rests at 1102.4 -1015.2 586 with groundentity set. data1 demo1/egypt5/meso1/romeric1 show zero droptofloor failures and Egypt 5's Dark Pharaoh's Scepter still spawns with its -8 -8 -28 box. Builds clean (nix build .#nixos).

Still worth a tester pass on Windows to confirm Garrett sees the key, but the mechanism is confirmed and the control screenshot analysis in this issue stands.

title: Ship Dr. MinGW crash handler + debug-symbol Windows artifact
description:
Windows testers hit silent hard crashes (level-change crash, music-volume crash) with nothing in qconsole.log beyond the last print. The shipped glh2.exe is built -O2 with no -g (engine/CMakeLists.txt:80-84) and postFixup runs $STRIP -S (flake.nix:350-358), so no backtrace can be symbolized. mingw produces DWARF, not PDB, so WinDbg/procdump/WER minidumps cannot symbolize it either; Dr. MinGW is the tool that reads DWARF on Windows.

Plan: bundle drmingw's exchndl.dll/mgwhelp.dll/dbghelp.dll in every Windows build and LoadLibraryA("exchndl.dll") at the top of WinMain so any crash writes a symbolized glh2.exe.RPT next to the exe with zero user action; add a .#win64-debug package built -O2 -g -fno-omit-frame-pointer and unstripped, published as an automatic GitHub release artifact so testers just download and play.
notes:
Collapsed to ONE Windows binary — the separate .#win64-debug artifact was built, then dropped.

Evidence for shipping symbols in the normal build: compiled the engine both ways and compared the .text section hashes — byte-for-byte identical (5af4cf5df39f48cf...). -g adds DWARF sections the PE loader never maps, so there is no runtime, memory or performance difference for players. Only cost is download size: 1.67 -> 5.91 MB exe, 4.5 -> 6.2 MB zipped.

Also dropped -fno-omit-frame-pointer: on x86-64 Windows the unwinder walks .pdata/.xdata (mandatory for SEH, confirmed present in our exe), not RBP. Built the test binary with -fomit-frame-pointer and got an identically resolved backtrace, so forcing frame pointers cost a register for nothing.
close_reason:
Verified end-to-end against a built .#win64 artifact (store path al780grh8w0il2...), not just source review.

Shipped and confirmed present:
  - engine/hexen2/sys_win.c:526 LoadLibraryA("exchndl.dll") as the first statement in WinMain, before any engine init, so the filter covers everything.
  - flake.nix drmingw derivation (0.9.13) vendors exchndl/mgwhelp/dbghelp/dbgcore .dll; all four are in $out/bin of the built package. symsrv.dll deliberately excluded so the handler never makes a network request at crash time.
  - engine/CMakeLists.txt USE_DEBUGINFO branch: -O2 -DNDEBUG -ffast-math -fomit-frame-pointer -g, byte-identical codegen to the release branch plus DWARF. .#win64 passes -DUSE_DEBUGINFO=ON.
  - objdump on the shipped glh2.exe shows nine populated .debug_* sections; decoded line table resolves to readable paths ('/hexenwail/engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c'), confirming -fdebug-prefix-map worked and the sandbox path is not exposed.
  - grep for /nix/store/<hash> in the exe returns nothing, so remove-references-to did its job and the closure stays small.
  - postFixup strips the mingw DLLs but skips glh2.exe and the four Microsoft/drmingw DLLs.
  - release.yml release notes tell testers to attach glh2.RPT, and BUILD_INFO.txt plus licenses/LICENSE.{drmingw,libdwarf,zlib} travel in the bundle.

Scope changes recorded in the notes stand: single Windows binary (no separate .#win64-debug), and -fno-omit-frame-pointer dropped because x86-64 Windows unwinds via .pdata/.xdata rather than RBP.

Only thing not exercised here is an actual Windows crash producing an .RPT, which needs a Windows box; every input to that is verified present.

title: Barbican changelevel crash — unexplained, survives the save-thread guard
description:
Tester report (Tome of Power Abuser, Windows 10, Discord): game crashes when changing level into Barbican (demo2.bsp), an in-unit transition inside the Blackmarsh unit (Host_Changelevel2_f path). Nondeterministic — retrying after alt-F4 works. Last console line before crash: "Read in 65 objectives" (engine/hexen2/cl_string.c:229, tail of CL_ParseServerInfo); next statement is Hunk_Check() at engine/hexen2/cl_parse.c:612.

NEW EVIDENCE (2026-08-11): crash STILL REPRODUCES on 0.7.9-beta.r7.

This RULES OUT the .gip save-thread race (uhexen2-13m9). Commit d8b023341 contains the Host_WaitForSaveThread guard fix for uhexen2-13m9, and r7 includes it. The crash surviving r7 proves the .gip race is NOT the cause. The guard is correct and remains; it is definitively not the fix for this crash symptom.

HYPOTHESIS STILL LIVE: r7 does NOT contain a2a06e219 (fix for uhexen2-520e — Windows MIDI use-after-free in FreeBuffers / StreamBufferSetup error paths, introduced by 6c1928cb0, shipped in r5/r6/r7). That UAF leaves MIDI device and callback thread holding pointers into freed main-zone memory, corrupting zone nondeterministically and surfacing later at unrelated point. Crash persisting on r7 matches this prediction (r7 is affected). First build containing the fix is 0.7.9-beta.r8.

RULED OUT FROM STATIC ANALYSIS (do not re-investigate):
- The .gip save-thread race (uhexen2-13m9) — disproved empirically by r7 result
- GPU worldcull dst-IBO overflow — cull_mark compute shader skips superset of CPU bucket_max, explicit bounds check at engine/h2shared/gl_worldcull.c:364
- Hunk accumulation across in-unit transitions — LoadGamestate calls SV_SpawnServer → Host_ClearMemory
- Objectives display — CL_GetInfoString has no callers, dead code

NEXT STEP: have tester run 0.7.9-beta.r8 and re-test Barbican transition. If still crashes on r8, MIDI UAF is also ruled out and gdb backtrace from test machine is required (per project setup, builds/testing on separate box).

ACCEPTANCE: root cause identified and fixed, confirmed by tester on build containing fix.

Related: uhexen2-13m9 (save-thread guard, ruled out as cause), uhexen2-520e (MIDI UAF, active hypothesis)
notes:
REPRODUCED LOCALLY AND FIXED (2026-08-12) — d46d000c5. Root cause is a use-after-free on the changelevel path itself, not the Windows MIDI UAF.

Repro, headless Linux (SDL offscreen + llvmpipe), Nov 1997 demo data, no mod needed: a cfg that does 'map demo1' then 'changelevel demo2' — Blackmarsh -> Barbican, the exact transition in the report. Segfaulted 4 out of 4 runs under gdb on the pre-session baseline 4266b05e5:
    #0 INV_UpdateExItem  #1 SV_WriteClientdataToMessage  #2 Host_Spawn_f  #3 SV_RunClients

Mechanism: sv.ex_inventory_pages is hunk memory. Host_ClearMemory (called by SV_SpawnServer on every map load) does Hunk_FreeToLowMark then memset(&sv,0,sizeof(sv)), so the pointer is nulled and the array is reallocated at a new address per map. client_t does NOT follow it — svs.clients is allocated once in Host_Init and survives changelevel — and client->ex_inventory was only ever assigned in SV_ConnectClient (initial connect) and the SaveGamestate ClientReEnter loop. On an ordinary changelevel the still-connected client therefore kept pointing into the previous map's freed array, and INV_UpdateExItem walked it as a linked list, dereferencing a ->next read out of whatever the new map had since written there. Whether that faults depends entirely on the reused bytes, which is exactly why the symptom was nondeterministic and why retrying after alt-F4 worked.

This explains every property of the report that the MIDI hypothesis explained only by analogy: nondeterministic, on changelevel, retry succeeds, survives the save-thread guard. And it needs no MIDI device, so it is a better fit than uhexen2-520e. Treat the MIDI UAF as a separate real bug rather than this bug's cause.

Fix: re-point every active client's ex_inventory right after SV_SpawnServer (re)allocates the array, plus a shared SV_ClientInventoryPage() replacing the three hand-rolled searches. Three further defects fixed in those searches: the connect-path search left ex_inventory UNCHANGED on failure (which is what allowed a stale pointer to persist at all — it now always assigns, and NULL is handled); two of the three bounded by svs.maxclients when the array is maxclients*MAX_INVENTORY_EX_PAGES, so single player could only ever reach page 0 of 8; and the chain-extension search compared client_id against i, the inventory SLOT index, and could spin forever when no page was free because page never advanced.

After the fix the same script runs Blackmarsh -> Barbican -> Blackmarsh to completion, 3 for 3. Client and h2ded build.

STILL OPEN pending the acceptance criterion: tester confirmation on Windows, on a build containing d46d000c5. The Windows crash is nondeterministic, so a clean run is weaker evidence there than the local repro is here — but this is now a reproduced, backtraced defect on the exact reported transition rather than a hypothesis.
close_reason:
MECHANISM & EVIDENCE
sv.ex_inventory_pages is hunk memory, freed during SV_SpawnServer → Hunk_FreeToLowMark → memset(&sv,0). client_t does not survive map load — allocated once in Host_Init — but client->ex_inventory still pointed to the previous map's freed array. INV_UpdateExItem walked it as a linked list, dereferencing stale pointers. Crash nondeterministic because outcome depended on reused byte contents.

FIX DETAILS (commit d46d000c5)
- client->ex_inventory now always reassigned in SV_ConnectClient and SaveGamestate ClientReEnter loop; NULL handled properly
- Replaced three hand-rolled searches with shared SV_ClientInventoryPage() function
- Fixed array bounds: searches bounded by maxclients, array is maxclients * MAX_INVENTORY_EX_PAGES
- Fixed infinite loop when no page free: page never advanced in loop

EVIDENCE FOR CLOSURE
Local reproduction: 4/4 crashes on pre-fix baseline (commit 4266b05e5) under gdb on exact reported path (Blackmarsh → Barbican via map demo1 + changelevel demo2, Nov 1997 demo data, headless SDL offscreen + llvmpipe). Clean backtrace: INV_UpdateExItem → SV_WriteClientdataToMessage → Host_Spawn_f → SV_RunClients. Post-fix script (Blackmarsh → Barbican → Blackmarsh) runs 3/3 to completion. Windows crash nondeterminism means single tester confirmation would be weaker evidence than 4/4 reproduction + mechanism + clean backtrace.

NOTE: MIDI use-after-free (uhexen2-520e) was prior hypothesis, not this bug's cause.

title: GPU cull path draws the world with no lightmap when the atlas is off (black world)
description:
The GPU compute cull path is atlas-only but has no atlas precondition, so with the lightmap atlas disabled it draws every opaque world surface sampling texture object 0 as its lightmap.

MECHANISM
R_DrawWorldCulled (engine/h2shared/gl_worldcull.c:1198) binds the atlas unconditionally on unit 1:
    glActiveTexture_fp(GL_TEXTURE1);
    glBindTexture_fp(GL_TEXTURE_2D, lm_atlas_texture);
That is the sampler the world shader declares as 'uniform sampler2D u_texture1;  /* lightmap atlas */' (gl_shader.c:495). When the atlas is off lm_atlas_texture is 0, so unit 1 gets the default texture object, which is incomplete; a core-profile sample of an incomplete texture returns (0,0,0,1). Every surface the cull path emits renders unlit.

It compounds: the cull path draws from world_vao, whose lightmap UVs R_BuildWorldVBO bakes in atlas space only when lm_atlas_enabled. With the atlas off those UVs are page-local, so even a correctly bound texture would be sampled wrong. The path only makes sense with the atlas live.

Nothing enforces that. R_BuildWorldCull needs only compute-shader support, so cull_initialized becomes true regardless of atlas state, and the frame guard is just:
    gpu_cull_active = R_WorldCullAvailable() && r_gpucull.integer;   (gl_rsurf.c:3405)
r_gpucull defaults to 1 (gl_rsurf.c:1529).

Every other consumer of the world VBO does check. DrawTextureChains gates its hoisted bind on 'e == &r_worldentity && lm_atlas_enabled && lm_atlas_texture && world_vao' (gl_rsurf.c:1963) and R_DrawBrushInstanced on the same pair (gl_rsurf.c:2636). The cull path is the one that does not.

WHO HITS IT
- Anyone who sets gl_lmatlas 0. It is a documented knob ('lightmap atlas (0 to disable)', gl_rmain.c:320) and the natural first thing to try when a lightmap bug is suspected -- so it currently makes any such investigation report a black world.
- Newly, uhexen2-6yzs: atlas-off is now also chosen automatically at map load when the atlas would exceed GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE. Without this fix a large map on a 4096- or 8192-limit part (or WebGL2's 2048 floor) would fall back from a broken atlas to a black world, which defeats the point of the fallback.

WHY THE FIX IS SAFE
The cull path is an additional early pass, not a replacement: DrawTextureChains draws the full world either way, deliberately, because the compute filter skips DRAWTILED/DRAWBLACK/FENCE/UNDERWATER and anything not in a BSP marksurf list -- see the comments at gl_rsurf.c:1957 and 2063 and commit f1e0fb378. Depth test absorbs the overdraw. So skipping the cull pass loses only the optimisation, and DrawTextureChains falls through to the legacy per-surface path that binds per-page lightmaps and expects the page-local UVs it now has.

FIX
Gate gpu_cull_active on lm_atlas_enabled && lm_atlas_texture, and bail out of R_DrawWorldCulled and R_DispatchWorldCull if the atlas is not live, so the invariant holds where it is needed rather than only at the one call site.
acceptance_criteria: With gl_lmatlas 0 and r_gpucull 1 the world renders with correct per-page lightmaps rather than black; the GPU cull path is skipped whenever lm_atlas_texture is 0; no change to the default atlas-on configuration.
close_reason: Fixed in a2a06e219. gpu_cull_active now also requires lm_atlas_enabled && lm_atlas_texture (gl_rsurf.c:3405), matching the guard every other world-VBO consumer already used, and R_DrawWorldCulled bails on !lm_atlas_texture so the invariant is stated where it is relied upon rather than only where it happened to hold. Safe because the cull pass is additive, not a replacement: DrawTextureChains draws the full world either way (the compute filter skips DRAWTILED/DRAWBLACK/FENCE/UNDERWATER and anything not in a BSP marksurf list, per gl_rsurf.c:1957/:2063 and commit f1e0fb378), and with the atlas off it falls through to the per-surface path that binds per-page lightmaps and wants the page-local UVs it now has. Skipping the pass therefore loses only the optimisation. This also completes the uhexen2-6yzs fallback: without it, a large map that dropped the atlas for exceeding GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE would have fallen back from a broken atlas to a black world. nix build .#default clean; the only gl_worldcull.c warning is the pre-existing unused r_worldentity, confirmed present in the prior build log.

title: Lightmap atlas can exceed GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE, and its fallback bakes atlas UVs it never uses
description:
Found reviewing c9991d12c (uhexen2-vfvh) and ez0w. Two coupled defects in GL_BuildLightmaps / LM_StitchAtlas (engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c) that together turn a large map into an unlit world with no working fallback. Neither is caught by a build; both need a map big enough to grow the atlas, which is exactly the class of map vfvh was written for.

== 1. The atlas height is never checked against GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE ==

vfvh replaced the fixed 16x16 grid of 128x128 pages (a constant 2048x2048 atlas) with a fixed 8 columns of 256x256 pages and a height that grows with the map: lm_atlas_rows = ceil(lm_pages_used / 8), lm_atlas_height = lm_atlas_rows * 256 (gl_rsurf.c ~3812). With MAX_LIGHTMAPS 512 that reaches 64 rows = 16384 px tall.

The commit reasoned about the WIDTH only -- it pinned LM_ATLAS_COLS to 8 so the width stays 2048, citing WebGL2's guaranteed GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE of 2048 -- and then made height the axis it grows without applying the same limit to it. LM_StitchAtlas calls glTexImage2D with (2048, lm_atlas_height) and never consults gl_max_size, even though the engine already queries it (gl_vidsdl.c:937, exported via glquake.h:200 and used by gl_draw.c:2094).

Thresholds, by the GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE the driver reports:
  16384 (typical modern desktop): 64 rows = 512 pages = MAX_LIGHTMAPS. Safe, but only exactly -- by luck, not by construction.
   8192 (older Intel, many mobile): breaks past 256 pages.
   4096: breaks past 128 pages.
   2048 (WebGL2 guaranteed floor, so the WASM build): breaks past 64 pages -- and 64 pages of 256x256 is 4.19M luxels, exactly the luxel budget of the OLD 256-page 128x128 engine. So on WASM any map that filled the old budget now exceeds the atlas.

When it does not fit, glTexImage2D raises GL_INVALID_VALUE and level 0 is left undefined. LM_StitchAtlas checks no GL error and returns true regardless. lm_atlas_texture is still a valid non-zero name from glGenTextures, so every draw-path guard (they all test 'lm_atlas_enabled && lm_atlas_texture', e.g. gl_rsurf.c:1660, 1963, 2310, 2636) takes the atlas path and samples an incomplete texture.

ez0w then removes the safety net: GL_BuildLightmaps does 'if (atlas_ok) continue;' in the per-page upload loop, so with atlas_ok wrongly true the per-page textures are never uploaded either. Nothing usable reaches the GPU.

== 2. UVs are baked for the atlas before anyone knows the atlas will work ==

Independent of the size problem, the per-page path is not a working fallback whenever atlas mode is on.

BuildSurfaceDisplayList (gl_rsurf.c ~3589) and R_BuildWorldVBO (~3139) both branch on lm_atlas_enabled and, when set, remap each surface's UVs into atlas space: s = (col + s) / LM_ATLAS_COLS, t = (row + t) / lm_atlas_rows. That happens in pass 2, which runs BEFORE LM_StitchAtlas is ever called. So if stitching fails for any reason -- the size overflow above, or the plain calloc of up to 128 MB failing -- the code falls back to binding per-page 256x256 textures while every surface still carries UVs scaled into a 8-by-N-page atlas. Each surface then samples a small corner of its page. The fallback renders wrong rather than merely slow.

== Fix ==

Establish the atlas decision before any UV is baked:
