  a. After pass 1 sizes lm_atlas_height, and before pass 2, reject the atlas if LM_ATLAS_WIDTH or lm_atlas_height exceeds gl_max_size; clear lm_atlas_enabled and say so on the console.
  b. Move LM_StitchAtlas ahead of pass 2 -- it only needs lightmaps[], which pass 1 fills via R_BuildLightMap, so it does not depend on pass 2 at all -- and have it clear lm_atlas_enabled and zero lm_atlas_texture on any failure. Pass 2 then bakes against a decision that is already final and true.
  c. Check glGetError after the atlas glTexImage2D so a driver-side rejection (VRAM, an unexpected internalformat) is treated as failure rather than silently believed.
  d. R_RebuildAllLightmaps calls LM_StitchAtlas too, with UVs already baked; a failure there must leave the previous atlas alone rather than switching modes underneath baked UVs.

Worth also reconsidering the 8-column shape: a squarer atlas (e.g. columns chosen so width and height grow together) would push the limit out a long way instead of spending the whole budget on one axis.
acceptance_criteria: lm_atlas_height is validated against gl_max_size before UVs are baked; when the atlas is unavailable for any reason, lm_atlas_enabled is false before pass 2 so surfaces get page-local UVs and the per-page upload runs; the atlas glTexImage2D is error-checked; a map needing more pages than the atlas can hold loads and renders correctly with per-page lightmaps instead of an unlit world.
close_reason: Fixed in 13f88d5ce. (a) GL_BuildLightmaps now rejects the atlas when LM_ATLAS_WIDTH or lm_atlas_height exceeds gl_max_size, before pass 2 bakes any UV, and says so on the console. (b) LM_StitchAtlas moved ahead of pass 2 — it reads only lightmaps[], which pass 1 fills, so the move is free — and a failure now clears lm_atlas_enabled and deletes lm_atlas_texture while that still changes what pass 2 produces, so the per-page path gets page-local UVs and a real per-page upload. (c) the atlas glTexImage2D is error-checked via a new glGetError_fp (added to all three gl_func.h variants: GL_DLSYM list, Emscripten block, desktop-direct block). (d) LM_StitchAtlas reports and returns false but no longer touches the texture itself — GL_BuildLightmaps tears it down, while R_RebuildAllLightmaps deliberately ignores the result and keeps its stale-but-correctly-shaped atlas, since UVs are baked by then and it cannot re-bake; GL leaves texture contents intact on a failed glTexImage2D so that atlas still matches the UVs. nix build .#default clean, no new warnings, new console string verified in the binary. The size path is deterministic; the driver-rejection path is not reproducible on this box.

title: Demo bundle has no redistribution grant: SUBLICENSE.doc is Activision's retail EULA
description:
Found while doing uhexen2-menr.2 (extracting the demo license docs). The uhexen2-menr epic plans to ship Raven's Hexen II demo data1/ inside Hexenwail release artifacts (demo-linux, demo-windows, demo-wasm zips, attached to GitHub releases). The license file that upstream ships with that data does not permit it.

WHAT THE FILE ACTUALLY IS
hexen2demo_nov1997-linux-i586.tgz contains SUBLICENSE.doc (OLE2 Word 97, 30208 bytes). Converted with antiword and committed as assets/demo/HEXEN2_DEMO_LICENSE.txt. It is Activision's RETAIL sublicense agreement, not a shareware or demo license:

- The strings 'shareware', 'demo', 'redistribute', 'freely' and 'non-commercial' do not appear anywhere in the document (verified by grep over the full 176-line conversion).
- It speaks throughout of 'the original consumer purchaser', 90-day warranty replacement of defective CD-ROM media (with postal addresses in the US, UK and Australia), and requires you to 'run this Program from the included CD-ROM'.
- Under 'YOU SHALL NOT' it explicitly forbids: 'Sell, rent, lease, license, distribute or otherwise transfer this Program, or any copies of this Program, without the express prior written consent of Activision.'
- It also forbids copying the Program to a hard drive and making copies of the Program or any part thereof.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Deliverables 2-5 of uhexen2-menr all consist of redistributing this content: flake outputs demo-linux / demo-windows / demo-wasm, release.yml attaching the zips to GitHub releases, GitHub Pages auto-deploy of demo-wasm, and release notes advertising a 'Demo (no data needed)' download. Every one of those is 'distribute or otherwise transfer copies of this Program'. Publishing to GitHub releases and Pages is public distribution, and it is hard to undo once mirrored.

The engine side is fine and is not in question: Hexenwail is GPLv2+, and so are the Hammer of Thyrion binaries inside the tarball. This is purely about the Raven game content in data1/pak0.pak.

WHAT IS NOT YET ESTABLISHED
The Nov 1997 demo did circulate freely for ~25 years, and uHexen2 has hosted it on SourceForge for most of that time without apparent objection. So a permission probably exists somewhere - it is just not this file. Most likely upstream copied the retail EULA into the demo package by mistake. Do not assume the practice is the permission.

ACTION
1. Find the actual demo distribution terms if they exist. Candidates: the original 1997 hexen2demo self-extracting distribution and its own readme/license, id Software's shareware distribution terms of the era, the Hexen2Demo-Nov.1997 SourceForge directory README (fetched: 4 lines, engine build notes only, no license text), or a statement from the uHexen2 maintainers about why they consider hosting it permissible.
2. If no grant is found, the epic ships engine-only and the demo data becomes a documented user-fetched download (a first-run 'point me at your data1' flow), not a bundled artifact.
3. Either way, record the conclusion in assets/demo/README.md, which currently states the question is open and points here.

This is P1 not because it is urgent (the epic is P4 and unstarted) but because it is a blocking precondition: any work on menr.3-menr.8 is wasted or worse if the answer is no. It should be settled before that work starts, not after.
acceptance_criteria: A documented yes/no on whether Hexenwail may redistribute the Nov 1997 Hexen II demo data1/, with the supporting license text or statement cited; assets/demo/README.md updated with the conclusion; uhexen2-menr deliverables 2-5 either unblocked or rescoped to engine-only.
notes:
=== 2026-08-11: searched for a redistribution grant; none found ===

ACTION step 1 done. Every avenue checked came back empty:

1. The demo's own data carries no license. data1/pak0.pak unpacked and all 797 entries enumerated: game assets plus strings.txt, puzzles.txt, maplist.txt and menu .lmp graphics. No license, readme, order form or legal file of any kind.

2. Neither do the surrounding docs. Everything under docs/ in the tarball is Hammer of Thyrion engine documentation -- including COPYING, which is the ENGINE's GPL, not the data's terms. SUBLICENSE.doc remains the only document in the package that speaks to the game content.

3. Upstream's release notes say nothing about terms. Fetched the README from both the Hexen2Demo-Nov.1997 and Hexen2Demo-Aug.1997 SourceForge directories: four lines each, describing which engine build was used and the h2config.h settings. No license text.

4. A second port reached the same conclusion independently. The Hexen 2 Dreamcast port (github.com/Shockblast/hexen2-dreamcast) states verbatim: 'Hexen II Demo version Data files have another Licence. In my view, Hexen II Demo version can't re-distribute without Activison's permission.' Stated as an opinion, not a legal determination -- but it is a separate party reading the same materials and landing in the same place.

5. The Hexen line was not shareware. By the mid-90s the shareware model had fallen out of favour; Hexen shipped a small demo rather than a shareware episode and was explicitly not a shareware product. So the freely-redistributable grant that came with e.g. Quake shareware is not something that exists to be found here.

FALSE LEAD, recorded so nobody re-walks it: archive.org item HexenII_1020 is titled 'Hexen II Demo' and its h2demo.zip does contain a license.txt and README.TXT -- but the archive is mislabeled. Contents are HEROES2.AGG, HEROES2.HLP, H2DEMOW.EXE, CAMPAIGN.HS: it is the Heroes of Might and Magic II demo. Not relevant.

COUNTERWEIGHT: uHexen2 has hosted these packages on SourceForge for roughly two decades with no visible objection. That is practice, not permission, and not a permission this project inherits.

CONCLUSION: no redistribution grant can be established. The answer to the acceptance criterion's yes/no is NO on the evidence available.

REMAINING DECISION (why this stays open): two paths, and the choice is the maintainer's, not a research question.
  (a) Rescope uhexen2-menr to engine-only. The demo becomes a documented user-fetched download -- README instructions plus, ideally, a first-run 'point me at your data1' flow. menr.3-.8 get rewritten rather than unblocked.
  (b) Ask Activision. SUBLICENSE.doc names the contact for exactly this ('Activision may offer a separate Site License Agreement...; see the contact information below'), though the 1997 addresses are long stale and Activision is now Microsoft-owned. Slow, uncertain, but it is the only route to a real yes.

Findings written up in assets/demo/README.md so the conclusion is visible to anyone who opens the directory, not only to whoever reads this issue.
close_reason:
Decision made and recorded: Hexenwail ships engine-only. No Raven demo data in any artifact we publish.

ACTION step 1 (find a grant) was already done and came back empty — recorded in the notes above. This closes steps 2 and 3.

Step 2 — the epic's scope follows the pre-agreed fallback in this issue's own ACTION list: no grant found, so the demo becomes a user-fetched download rather than a bundled artifact. That route already exists and did not need building: uhexen2-49ep (9cec08fd5) shipped scripts/get_demo.sh, scripts/get_demo.cmd/.ps1 and 'nix run .#get-demo', each verifying the tarball against the sha256 before unpacking, and the engine's no-data error names the script so the path is discoverable from the failure. Verified no flake output and no release.yml step references demo data today, so nothing had to be removed — the tree was already compliant, it just was not written down.

The line the decision draws: pointing a user at uHexen2's URL is not distribution; serving them the bytes is. We do the former.

Step 3 — assets/demo/README.md rewritten. The 'unresolved, decision not made' tail is replaced with a Decision section (engine-only, the three fetch routes, why the tarball in that directory is a local working copy and not a build input), a Consequences list naming which menr deliverables drop, and a 'what would reopen this' section: a written grant from Activision/Microsoft, or a period document not yet found. Explicitly not reopened by the demo's 25 years of free circulation — that is evidence about practice, not about rights.

.gitignore's comment on the tarball updated too; it still said the terms were unresolved.

Closing the epic's sub-issues that this gated (menr.3-.8) as won't-ship. Reopening the bundling path needs a real grant, at which point they can be reopened unchanged.

title: Host_Changelevel2_f missing Host_WaitForSaveThread guard
description:
Commit d153b99c1 ("feat(async): add async main-thread task queue and background save thread") added Host_WaitForSaveThread() guards at, per its own commit message, "changelevel, map load, loadgame, shutdown" state-change points. It missed one: Host_Changelevel2_f, the in-unit level transition.

Current state of the four level-change/save entry points in engine/hexen2/host_cmd.c:
- Host_Map_f            -> Host_WaitForSaveThread() at host_cmd.c:264   (guarded)
- Host_Changelevel_f    -> Host_WaitForSaveThread() at host_cmd.c:337   (guarded)
- Host_Loadgame_f       -> Host_WaitForSaveThread() at host_cmd.c:708   (guarded)
- Host_Changelevel2_f   -> NO GUARD; goes straight to SaveGamestate(false) at host_cmd.c:384

Why it matters: Host_Changelevel2_f calls SaveGamestate(false), which writes <userdir>/*.gip on the main thread. The background save worker (SaveThread_f in engine/hexen2/host_async.c:210) concurrently runs Host_CopyFiles(sd.userdir, "*.gip", sd.savedest), reading those same files. Host_Changelevel2_f then calls LoadGamestate() which reads them back. Unsynchronised read/write on the same .gip set — can corrupt the destination save slot and/or read a partially written file.

Reported symptom that surfaced this: tester "Tome of Power Abuser" reports a crash on level change into the Barbican (demo2.bsp), an in-unit transition inside the Blackmarsh unit, i.e. exactly the changelevel2 path. Crash is nondeterministic — retrying after alt-F4 works fine, which fits a race that only fires when a background save is in flight. Last console line before the crash was "Read in 65 objectives" (engine/hexen2/cl_string.c:229), i.e. the tail of CL_ParseServerInfo.

IMPORTANT caveat to record in the issue (do not overstate): this is NOT confirmed as the cause of that crash. The timing does not fully line up — CL_ParseServerInfo runs after LoadGamestate on this path, so a corrupt-.gip race would be expected to bite earlier. The guard is a genuine defect on the crashing code path and is correct to fix regardless, but the crash root cause is still open pending a gdb backtrace from the test machine. Discriminating test requested from tester: does it reproduce on a run with NO prior in-game save? If yes, the save-thread race is ruled out.

Design/fix: insert Host_WaitForSaveThread(); in Host_Changelevel2_f after SV_SaveSpawnparms() and before the SaveGamestate(false) call, matching the placement in Host_Changelevel_f.

Acceptance: Host_Changelevel2_f waits for the save thread before touching .gip files; nix build .#default clean.

---

## STATUS UPDATE (2026-08-11)

**Fix committed, but issue held OPEN pending confirmation from tester "Tome of Power Abuser".**

**Fix landed:** commit d8b023341 on master, "fix(save): wait for the save thread before an in-unit changelevel (uhexen2-13m9)". One line — Host_WaitForSaveThread(); inserted at engine/hexen2/host_cmd.c:381, after SV_SaveSpawnparms() and before SaveGamestate(false), mirroring the placement in Host_Changelevel_f. nix build .#default clean, no new warnings. NOT yet pushed to remote.

**Why still open:** The committed guard closes a genuine unsynchronised read/write race on the .gip file set, but it is NOT confirmed to be the cause of the crash that surfaced it. The timing does not fully line up — CL_ParseServerInfo (where the console log ends, at "Read in 65 objectives", engine/hexen2/cl_string.c:229) runs AFTER LoadGamestate on the changelevel2 path, so a corrupt-.gip race would be expected to bite earlier. The crash root cause remains open.

Additionally the guard is a no-op unless a background save is actually in flight, so it cannot be runtime-verified without deliberately triggering an in-unit transition while a save is still copying.

**Outstanding — needed from tester "Tome of Power Abuser" before this can be closed:**
1. Does the crash reproduce on a run with NO prior in-game save? If yes, the save-thread race is ruled out as the cause and the real root cause is still unfound.
2. A gdb backtrace from the test machine. Per project setup, builds and runtime testing happen on a separate box — no display or core dumps on the dev machine — so a backtrace from the test box is what actually settles this.

---

## DEMOTION & ROOT CAUSE REASSESSMENT (2026-08-11, post-investigation)

**uhexen2-520e (Windows MIDI use-after-free from FreeBuffers in StreamBufferSetup error paths) is now the STRONGER CANDIDATE for the Barbican changelevel crash, and would also explain the same tester's music-volume crash.**

**Why it fits better:** The MIDI use-after-free corrupts the main zone nondeterministically and surfaces later at an unrelated moment, which matches the observed symptom exactly: "crash on changelevel, retry after alt-F4 works fine". The UAF also RESOLVES the timing objection previously recorded on this issue — that CL_ParseServerInfo runs after LoadGamestate, so a .gip race should have bitten earlier. Zone corruption is not constrained by that call order; it will bite whenever memory allocation or access patterns collide with the corrupted region.

uhexen2-520e was introduced in commit 6c1928cb0 (2026-08-11 14:15) and shipped in 0.7.9-beta.r5, r6, and r7. It is a use-after-free: FreeBuffers() was added to three StreamBufferSetup error paths without the stream-stop and buffer-return handshake that exists in MIDI_Stop, allowing the device callback thread to hold stale pointers into freed zone memory. This is a better fit for nondeterministic crashes than a file-I/O race.

**The Host_WaitForSaveThread guard (commit d8b023341) remains CORRECT and STAYS.** It closes a genuine unsynchronised read/write race on the .gip file set. It should simply no longer be presented as the likely fix for the Barbican changelevel crash — that crash is now attributed to the MIDI use-after-free. The guard is still valuable for preventing silent corruption of saved games.

**Still open pending the items already recorded:** reproduction with no prior in-game save, and a gdb backtrace from the test machine.
notes:
TESTER CONFIRMATION (2026-08-11): "Tome of Power Abuser" has re-tested on 0.7.9-beta.r7, which contains this issue's fix (commit d8b023341 — Host_WaitForSaveThread guard added to Host_Changelevel2_f). THE BARBICAN CHANGELEVEL CRASH STILL REPRODUCES.

This definitively rules out the .gip save-thread race described on this issue as the cause of the crash symptom.

OUTCOME FOR THIS ISSUE:
- The code defect described here (Host_Changelevel2_f missing the Host_WaitForSaveThread guard) IS REAL and IS FIXED by commit d8b023341
- The guard is validated by a clean nix build .#default
- All stated acceptance criteria for THIS ISSUE are MET
- The guard REMAINS CORRECT — it closes a genuine unsynchronised read/write race on the .gip file set and prevents silent save corruption

- The crash symptom has been split out to its own issue (uhexen2-rutp) for independent investigation
- uhexen2-520e (Windows MIDI use-after-free) is now the stronger candidate for the crash root cause

STATUS: This issue is READY TO CLOSE on its own merits. The code defect is fixed, acceptance criteria met, and the crash root cause has been reassigned to uhexen2-rutp. Being held open only pending explicit decision from user.
close_reason:
Acceptance met and the open question has moved elsewhere. The guard landed in d8b023341 and is present in the tree at engine/hexen2/host_cmd.c:381, after SV_SaveSpawnparms() and before SaveGamestate(false), matching Host_Changelevel_f — all four level-change/save entry points now wait for the save thread. That closes a genuine unsynchronised read/write race on the .gip file set, which is the whole of this issue's scope.

This was held open pending tester confirmation of the Barbican crash, but uhexen2-rutp now records that the crash STILL reproduces on 0.7.9-beta.r7, which contains d8b023341 — so the .gip race is definitively ruled out as that crash's cause, and the crash investigation lives in uhexen2-rutp (current prime suspect: the MIDI use-after-free uhexen2-520e, first fixed in r8). Nothing further is owed here: the guard is a no-op unless a background save is in flight, so there is no runtime check to run beyond it compiling and being on the right code path.

title: Dead CODECTYPE_MID fallback: wire the MIDI streamer tier (vendor libtimidity 0.2.8 SF2)
description:
bgmusic.c runs MIDI as two tiers: MIDIDRIVER_MID (driver, bgmusic.c:73) then CODECTYPE_MID (streamer codec fallback, bgmusic.c:74). Tier 2 is dead wiring. CODECTYPE_MID is defined at snd_codec.h:90, the handler sits in wanted_handlers[], and bgmusic.c:357-363 deliberately falls through to it when no MIDI driver registered -- but S_CodecInit() (snd_codec.c:65-82) registers wav, flac, mp3, vorbis, opus, umx and xmp, and NO mid codec. The fallthrough can never be satisfied. The two implementations that used to fill the slot (snd_timidity.c, snd_wildmidi.c) were removed in a14b5eecd (SDL3/GL4.3 modernization) and the plumbing was left behind, so the code currently lies about having a fallback.

Consequence today: any build where tier 1 is absent has silently no MIDI and no fallback. Two such configurations exist. (a) WASM -- engine/CMakeLists.txt:432-434 hard-sets midi_nul.c plus -D_NO_MIDIDRV, so there is zero MIDI in the browser. (b) Linux where pkg-config does not find fluidsynth -- CMakeLists.txt:498-501 drops to midi_nul.c and every MIDI track logs "Couldnt handle music file <name>".

Why now: upstream sezero merged libtimidity 0.2.8 (merged here as 6fd6a0906, content no-op). 0.2.8 adds SF2/SBK parsing (sndfont.c, readsbk.c, sbk.h, sflayer.h, ~1800 lines) plus mid_set_soundfont(). Before 0.2.8 libtimidity needed GUS patch sets plus timidity.cfg -- a different data format from SF2 -- which is why dropping it cost nothing. It can now consume the exact TimGM6mb.sf2 already shipped in the Flatpak (/app/share/soundfonts/default.sf2) and next to the portable binary (bin/soundfont.sf2). One soundfont, two synths.

Fix: either wire a real codec to the slot (preferred, plan below) or delete the CODECTYPE_MID handler so the fallthrough stops lying.
design:
FluidSynth STAYS tier 1 everywhere it is available. libtimidity is tier 2 only. Rationale: fluidsynth is the better synth (reverb/chorus, more complete SF2 handling) but carries a heavy runtime closure -- verified glib 2.88, dbus, libjack2, libpulseaudio, libsndfile -- which is why it cannot go to WASM. libtimidity SF2 path includes only stdio/string/stdlib/math plus its own headers (verified against sezero/master), so it is pure C with no external deps and compiles to WASM cleanly. This is a fallback, not a replacement: on Windows (midi_win.c native midiStream) and on Linux-with-fluidsynth, tier 1 must continue to win and timidity must never be reached.

Port feasibility already verified against this tree: FS_fread and fshandle_t exist (quakefs.h), S_CodecUtilOpen and snd_stream_t exist (snd_codec.h, snd_codeci.h), filenames.h exists at common/filenames.h (upstream snd_timidity.c includes it unqualified -- include-path detail only). Upstream vendored libtimidity is exactly 0.2.8, satisfying the LIBTIMIDITY_VERSION >= 0x000208L gate that guards mid_set_soundfont.

Known wrinkle: upstream soundfont discovery is env-var only (TIMIDITY_SOUNDFONT). Our good search lives in find_soundfont() inside midi_fluid.c, which is compiled ONLY when FLUIDSYNTH_FOUND -- exactly the configurations where the codec is needed are the ones where that TU is absent. It must be factored out before the codec can use it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Linux build configured WITHOUT fluidsynth plays midi/*.mid through the timidity codec (no "Couldnt handle music file" errors).
2. WASM build plays MIDI music in the browser.
3. Windows unchanged: midi_win.c still wins tier 1; timidity never initialized.
4. Linux WITH fluidsynth unchanged: BGM reports FluidSynth as the MIDI driver, timidity never reached.
5. Same TimGM6mb.sf2 already shipped serves both synths -- no second soundfont added to any package.
6. No dead branch remains: bgmusic.c:357-363 fallthrough reaches a registered codec.
notes:
PLAN
1. Re-vendor libs/timidity from the merged upstream: git checkout sezero/master -- libs/timidity (46 files, ~5k lines). These were deleted in a14b5eecd; the merge 6fd6a0906 kept them deleted, so they must be restored explicitly.
2. Restore engine/h2shared/snd_timidity.c and snd_timidity.h from sezero/master. Fix the filenames.h include to point at common/.
3. Factor find_soundfont() out of midi_fluid.c into a platform-neutral TU (engine/h2shared/soundfont.c/.h) preserving the current search order: snd_soundfont cvar, <exe dir>/soundfont.sf2|sf3 via /proc/self/exe, <basedir>/soundfont.sf2|sf3, <basedir>/data1/, compile-time SOUNDFONT_PATH, then system paths. midi_fluid.c then calls into it instead of owning it.
4. In S_TIMIDITY_CodecInitialize, keep TIMIDITY_SOUNDFONT env as the highest-priority override, then fall back to the shared find_soundfont() and mid_set_soundfont() rather than requiring the env var.
5. Register timidity_codec in S_CodecInit (snd_codec.c) under USE_CODEC_TIMIDITY.
6. CMake: add a USE_CODEC_TIMIDITY option plus the libs/timidity sources. Enable it in the EMSCRIPTEN branch and as the fallback arm when FLUIDSYNTH_FOUND is false. IMPORTANT: check that -D_NO_MIDIDRV only disables tier 1 and does not also compile out the tier 2 streamer path -- if it gates both, the define needs splitting.
7. WASM: get the 6 MB TimGM6mb.sf2 into the emscripten virtual FS (--preload-file) or fetch it at startup. Note the download-size tradeoff; consider a smaller GM font for the web target if 6 MB is too heavy.
8. Do NOT restore snd_wildmidi.c -- WildMidi is an external dependency and adds nothing over the vendored libtimidity for this purpose.

Audit that produced this issue also confirmed a stale belief: a soundfont IS shipped on every current distribution path (uhexen2-ji75, closed 2026-06-16). This issue is not about bundling a soundfont; it is about the missing fallback synth.
close_reason:
SHIPPED (commits 59343680d, 7fdbfd8a8):

libs/timidity/* re-vendored from sezero/master (46 files, 0.2.8 confirmed). engine/h2shared/snd_timidity.c/.h restored with SF2 search preceding timidity.cfg. New shared TU engine/h2shared/soundfont.c/.h with find_soundfont() moved verbatim from midi_fluid.c (which lost 130 lines, now calls shared API). timidity_codec registered in snd_codec.c:38,86. Corrected log line in bgmusic.c:283. USE_CODEC_TIMIDITY plus sources and gating in engine/CMakeLists.txt.

VERIFIED (1, 4, 5, 6):
1. Linux without FluidSynth: libTiMidity v0.2.8 initialized, "BGM: stream codecs: ... umx mid", no errors. Negative control (music NOSUCHTRACK) proves tier is reached. Disk capture of music ORB: peak 28779 / RMS 1929-5803 vs. 0.0 for silence control. Real synthesized PCM.
4. Linux with FluidSynth: "BGM: MIDI driver: FluidSynth", mid absent from codec list. nm finds zero timidity symbols, not in binary.
5. Same TimGM6mb.sf2 serves both synths; no new packaging files touched.
6. mid registered, dead fallthrough branch at bgmusic.c:357-363 now lands on it.

NOT VERIFIED (transparently):
2. WASM in browser: compiles/links (1.70 MB .wasm), but SF2 not yet in emscripten virtual FS; audibility requires browser. Split out as follow-up (uhexen2-wz8x or similar).
3. Windows unchanged: argued from build log only (midi_win.c/mid2strm.c, no timidity objects); win64 cross-compile passes but runtime untested.

ORIGINAL PLAN CORRECTIONS:
- snd_timidity.c filenames.h did NOT need fixing; common/ already on include path via ${UHEXEN2_SHARED}.
- -D_NO_MIDIDRV does NOT gate tier 2; it only selects inside bgmnull.c under _NO_SOUND, never blocking the streamer path.

ADDITION BEYOND PLAN:
USE_FLUIDSYNTH CMake option (default ON). Without it fallback unreachable on machines with FluidSynth, making criterion 1 untestable and leaving path permanently unexercised in CI.

FOLLOW-UP FIX (already made in 7fdbfd8a8):
flake.nix filteredSrc allowlist had no libs entry since 924588ba0 (uhexen2-jivr strict allowlist). Added. Default Linux/win64 unaffected (drop to FluidSynth, never compile timidity); packages.wasm would have failed without it.

LATENT WART (not fixed):
If SF2 is corrupt, mid_song_load fails and user sees "<file> is not a valid MIDI file" (misleading, MIDI is fine). mid_set_soundfont() only records path, no early validation point.

title: [bug] AllocBlock: full — lightmap atlas exhausted, fatal on large maps (SoT tibet)
description:
Loading the SoT map 'tibet' in Hexenwail dies with FATAL ERROR: AllocBlock: full. Reproduced independently by two testers (Mathuzzz and Garrett/Monolyth-42) on Discord 2026-06-27. The map is unplayable — hard Sys_Error exit, not a degrade.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed in tree):
AllocBlock (engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c:3374) scans lightmap pages 0..MAX_LIGHTMAPS-1 for a free rectangle and calls Sys_Error when every page is full. MAX_LIGHTMAPS is 256 (engine/h2shared/glquake.h:32) and pages are BLOCK_WIDTH x BLOCK_HEIGHT = 128x128 (gl_rsurf.c:107-108), so the hard ceiling is 256*128*128 = 4.19M luxels for the whole map. tibet is a very large map and exceeds it.

WHY A ONE-LINE CONSTANT BUMP WILL NOT WORK:
Everything downstream is statically sized against MAX_LIGHTMAPS:
  - lightmaps[4*MAX_LIGHTMAPS*BLOCK_WIDTH*BLOCK_HEIGHT] — 16 MB static array (gl_rsurf.c:147)
  - allocated[MAX_LIGHTMAPS][BLOCK_WIDTH] (gl_rsurf.c:143)
  - lightmap_polys / lightmap_modified / lightmap_rectmin / lightmap_rectmax (gl_rsurf.c:113-118)
  - lightmap_textures[MAX_LIGHTMAPS] (glquake.h:167)
and the GPU-side atlas is a fixed 16x16 page grid = 2048x2048 (LM_ATLAS_COLS/LM_ATLAS_ROWS, gl_rsurf.c:150-153), whose page->UV math is also consumed by gl_worldcull.c via lm_atlas_texture. Raising the count requires growing the atlas geometry and heap-allocating the CPU-side arrays together.

TWO FIX PATHS:
(a) Fast unblock — go to a 32x32 grid / 4096x4096 atlas (1024 pages, 4x capacity) and heap-allocate the lightmaps backing store sized to the page count actually used by the loaded map instead of a 16 MB static worst case. Small diff, keeps the existing atlas UV math.
(b) Ironwail parity (project default) — GL_TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY of 128x128 layers grown dynamically as QuakeSpasm/Ironwail do (realloc on demand, MAX_SANITY_LIGHTMAPS as a runaway guard). Removes the fixed grid entirely and deletes the atlas row/col coordinate math in gl_worldcull.c.

Recommend (b) per the Ironwail-parity convention, but (a) is acceptable as an interim if it ships sooner — this is blocking a tester.

ALSO IN SCOPE: whatever the ceiling ends up being, the failure should print the map name, the page count reached and the configured maximum before exiting, so the next report is diagnosable instead of a bare 'full'. A console line reporting lightmap page usage after each map load would let us see how close other maps run.
design: Ironwail/QuakeSpasm allocate lightmaps dynamically rather than from a fixed pool; this tree still carries the original static 256-page Quake layout, which is the actual limit being hit. The GL 4.3 pipeline already requires texture arrays elsewhere, so a 2D array of lightmap layers is not new infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria: map tibet (SoT) loads and renders in Hexenwail with correct lighting and no Sys_Error; console reports lightmap page usage after map load; no regression in lightmap appearance or update cost on stock Hexen II maps.
notes:
Mathuzzz's claim that 'uHexen manage to run it' refers to a custom prebuilt engine downloaded from the now-dead hexenworld site whose source was never published — NOT this tree, and not upstream uHexen2 (which carries the same 256-page limit). Do not treat this as a regression or try to bisect it.

Spoike's mapper-side workarounds, useful to relay to Mathuzzz if the engine fix proves insufficient: invisible submodel surfaces (including trigger brushes) still consume lightmap space even though they are never drawn — swapping the trigger texture for 'skip' removes them from the engine's view entirely; texture scaling on large surfaces cuts luxel count; qbsp chopping that yields a grid rather than overlapping diagonals wastes less rectangle area; splitting the map is the reliable last resort. Mathuzzz notes tibet uses few invisible-surface brushes and that its triggers use a dedicated trigger texture, so the 'skip' trick may buy less than usual here.

=== 2026-08-11: fix implemented in c9991d12c, awaiting tester verification ===

Investigating turned up a SECOND failure mode wearing the same error message, which the original writeup above missed. Mod_CalcSurfaceExtents (gl_model.c:1214) accepts surfaces up to MAX_SURFACE_LIGHTMAP = 255 luxels, but lightmap pages were 128x128 — so a surface between 129 and 255 luxels across passed load and then failed in AllocBlock, which could not place it in ANY page no matter how many existed. That mismatch dates from when MAX_SURFACE_LIGHTMAP was raised for SoT while pages stayed at 128. Given tibet is a huge map with large open surfaces, this is at least as likely the cause as page exhaustion. Neither fix path sketched above would have caught it.

Landed:
  - BLOCK_WIDTH/HEIGHT 128 -> 256, so a page is at least as large as the biggest surface the loader admits (+768 KB in blocklights/blocklightscolor)
  - MAX_LIGHTMAPS 256 -> 512; with 256x256 pages that is 33.5M luxels vs the old 4.19M, an 8x budget
  - lightmaps[] converted from a 16 MB static array to a geometrically grown heap buffer — at the new limits a static worst case would be 128 MB of BSS on every map, which the WASM build could not carry
  - R_UpdateLightmaps and R_RebuildAllLightmaps bounded by pages-in-use; their !lightmap_textures[i] break never fired (all texture names are generated up front) so both walked every slot — harmless against a static array, an overread against a grown one
  - atlas height sized to the pages in use rather than a fixed 16x16 grid; width held at 2048 because WebGL2 only guarantees GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE 2048. GL_BuildLightmaps split into pack-then-bake passes because UVs normalise against the atlas height. Shaders sample via textureSize() so they needed no change.
  - AllocBlock's shelf scan used < where it needed <=, rejecting a surface exactly one page wide even on an empty page
  - the two failure modes now raise distinct errors naming the offending model, and the page count prints on every map load

Went with a dynamically-sized 2D atlas rather than the GL_TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY in fix path (b): the array conversion buys the same capacity but touches every atlas UV consumer, and this is a P1 with a blocked tester. The array remains the cleaner long-term shape if the atlas grows again.

Builds clean (nix build .#nixos). NOT verified against tibet — that needs a tester with the map. If it still fails, the new console line ('Lightmaps: N/512 pages') and the split error messages will identify which limit was hit, which the old bare 'full' never could.

Follow-up filed: uhexen2-ez0w (per-page lightmap textures are still uploaded in atlas mode, now 256 KB each).
close_reason:
Verified locally on the actual map. SoT tibet.bsp is present on the dev box (/home/josh/hexen2/sot/maps/tibet.bsp), so the fix in c9991d12c no longer needs a tester.

Headless load (SDL offscreen + llvmpipe, -game sot +map tibet):
  Precache: 1013/2047 models, 346/511 sounds
  Lightmaps: 91/512 pages (256x256), atlas 2048x3072
  World VBO: 320402 verts, 175384 tris in static buffer
  Sky stencil VBO: 985476 verts, 493786 tris
  CL_SignonReply: 4  (fully in-game, no Sys_Error)

No 'AllocBlock: full', no fatal exit. 91 pages of 512 at the new 256x256 page size = 5.96M luxels, which is 42 percent above the old engine's entire 4.19M ceiling — consistent with the map having been unloadable before and with plenty of headroom now (18 percent of the new budget used).

Note this does not by itself prove which of the two failure modes tibet was hitting, since the fix addressed both. The instrumentation the fix added is doing its job: the page-usage line is what makes the above readable at all.

Renderer correctness beyond 'it loads and lights' is not covered here — this was a headless llvmpipe load, not a visual pass. Follow-up uhexen2-ez0w (per-page uploads in atlas mode) already landed separately.

title: Background save worker uses zone allocator, va() and the global find handle
description:
The background save worker (SaveThread_f, engine/hexen2/host_async.c:141) calls Host_RemoveGIPFiles and Host_CopyFiles, which reach three pieces of non-thread-safe global engine state:

1. Zone allocator. FS_CopyFile (engine/h2shared/quakefs.c:604) does Z_Strdup/Z_Free on the main zone to build a mutable path for FS_CreatePath. Z_Malloc/Z_Free have no locking, so a save running concurrently with any main-thread zone allocation can corrupt the heap. On Unix, Sys_FindFirstFile (engine/hexen2/sys_unix.c:198) also Z_Strdup's its path and pattern.

2. va(). Sys_FindNextFile on Unix (sys_unix.c:215) formats its stat path with va(), a shared rotating static buffer used all over the main thread. Concurrent use hands one of the two threads a clobbered string.

3. Global find handle. Sys_FindFirstFile/NextFile/Close keep a single static handle plus a single static result buffer (findhandle/finddata in sys_win.c:176, finddir/finddata/findpath/findpattern in sys_unix.c:185). Sys_FindFirstFile calls Sys_Error('Sys_FindFirst without FindClose') if the handle is already open, so a main-thread enumeration starting while the worker is mid-walk is a hard fatal error; worse orderings silently cross-thread the results. The returned filename also points into a shared static buffer on Windows (Sys_WideToUTF8).

Main-thread enumeration paths that can collide: Host_RemoveGIPFiles from menu.c:1092, cl_main.c:170, host.c:989, host_cmd.c:709/793, and the map-list scan at quakefs.c:1280.
acceptance_criteria: SaveThread_f reaches no zone allocation, no va(), and no shared find state. Two threads can enumerate directories concurrently without a Sys_Error or crossed results. All five call sites and four platform implementations updated; Unix and Windows builds clean.
close_reason: Fixed in 392edce10: global find state replaced with caller-owned fsfind_t (malloc'd platform half, per-context name buffer, no va()); zone allocation removed from FS_CopyFile and FS_WriteFileFromHandle. All 5 call sites and 4 platform impls updated. nix build .#default and .#win64 clean.

title: Con_Printf called from background save worker thread
description:
Host_CopyFiles (engine/hexen2/host.c:163) calls Con_Printf directly to report a copy failure, and Host_Error (host.c:156) on a path-buffer overflow. Both run on the background save worker thread when reached via SaveThread_f -> Host_CopyFiles (host_async.c:161).

Con_Printf is not thread-safe: it touches the console buffer, notify lines and the log file with no locking, racing the main thread's own output. Host_Error is worse — it longjmps to host_abort, which is the MAIN thread's setjmp target. A longjmp from the worker thread is undefined behaviour and will corrupt or crash the process.

SaveThread_f already demonstrates the intended pattern: it routes its own failure through Host_InvokeOnMainThread(SaveError_CB) precisely to avoid printing off-thread. Host_CopyFiles bypasses that guard, so the 'Error copying ...' line users saw in the uhexen2 save bug was in fact emitted from the wrong thread.

Note Host_CopyFiles is called from BOTH threads (host_cmd.c:796 on the main thread during load, host_async.c:161 on the worker), so it cannot simply assume one context.
design: Add a thread-aware print helper in host_async.c: record the main thread's SDL id at AsyncQueue_Init, expose Host_OnMainThread(), and add Host_PrintAsync(fmt, ...) that Con_Printf's directly when on the main thread and otherwise queues a malloc'd copy of the formatted message through Host_InvokeOnMainThread for AsyncQueue_Drain (host.c:851) to print and free. Replace Host_CopyFiles' Con_Printf with Host_PrintAsync, and replace its Host_Error with Host_PrintAsync + return -1 — the caller at host_cmd.c:797 already escalates a non-zero return to Host_Error on the main thread.
acceptance_criteria: No Con_Printf, Host_Error or other longjmp-capable call remains reachable from SaveThread_f. Copy failures still surface to the console with the same text. Main-thread callers of Host_CopyFiles print synchronously as before.
close_reason: Fixed in 392edce10: Host_CopyFiles now reports via new Host_PrintAsync (inline on main thread, deferred to AsyncQueue_Drain otherwise) and returns the error instead of longjmping via Host_Error. Deferral uses non-blocking Host_TryInvokeOnMainThread to avoid a deadlock against Host_WaitForSaveThread.

title: MP3 tag length integer-overflow UB on malformed input
close_reason:
Fixed in 6c1928cb0. The issue had no description, so recording the actual defect: snd_mp3tag.c assembled 32-bit tag fields as (data[n] << 24) | ... — an unsigned char promotes to int, so any byte >= 0x80 shifted left 24 overflows a 32-bit signed int. That is UB rather than the wraparound the code assumed, at is_apetag/get_ape_len (version, size, flags) and get_musicmatch_len (imgext_ofs, version_ofs, image size). All now assembled in unsigned arithmetic.

Removing the wrap cost two implicit range checks that depended on it — the MusicMatch offsets were validated with <= 0, which caught high-bit-set values only because they had gone negative — so those ranges are now bounded explicitly, and get_ape_len refuses a size that cannot survive conversion to long.

The reachable damage: both APE callers tested only len >= fh.length, never len < 0, and a negative length is SUBTRACTED from fh.length, growing it and running the reader past the end of the file. Those guards were missing and are added.

Builds clean (nix build .#nixos).

title: Windows MIDI buffer leak per failed open (StreamBufferSetup)
close_reason:
Fixed in 6c1928cb0. The issue had no description, so recording the actual defect: StreamBufferSetup (midi_win.c) unconditionally Z_Malloc'd NUM_STREAM_BUFFERS x OUT_BUFFER_SIZE into stream_bufs[i].mh.lpData at the top of every call, overwriting whatever the previous attempt left there, and every error path below returns without releasing the buffers it allocated. So each failed open abandoned the prior set — for a mod with a bad or missing MIDI track that is once per level load, against Z_MAINZONE.

Fix: reuse a buffer that is still held rather than overwriting the pointer, and call FreeBuffers() on the setup error paths (ConverterInit, midiStreamProperty, initial ConvertToBuffer, midiOutPrepareHeader).

Noted but deliberately NOT changed: a midiStreamOut failure inside the buffer loop does MidiErrorMessageBox then 'break', so StreamBufferSetup returns 0 (success) with fewer buffers queued than intended. That is a separate correctness question from the leak and was left alone rather than folded into a leak fix.

Windows target builds clean (nix build .#win64; midi_win.c confirmed compiled, no warnings).

title: Portable Linux release zip ships without bundled libs
notes: 2026-08-13: A second instance of this bug class was discovered in ci-mdl.yml (commit 9997d68af). The workflow copied result/release/linux-x86_64/bin/glhexen2 alone without its required 36 shared objects from lib/, making Linux artifacts unrunnable — same error pattern as the original issue. Worth noting because it suggests the "copy the binary" shortcut is an easy mistake to repeat anywhere build artifacts are assembled by hand. A grep for other places that copy glhexen2 without lib/ would be cheap insurance.
close_reason:
Fixed in ce13ad3e8. Issue had no description; recording the defect: flake.nix's release rule copied only ${linux-fhs}/bin into release/linux-x86_64/. The linux-fhs package patchelfs the binary to rpath $ORIGIN/../lib and bundles 36 shared objects into $out/lib, none of which was copied — so the portable zip contained a binary whose rpath pointed at a directory that did not exist. It would only start on a machine that already had those libraries system-wide, i.e. it failed on precisely the distros the portable build is for.

Fix: also 'cp -rL ${linux-fhs}/lib' into the portable directory.

Verified against real builds rather than by inspection: before, nix build .#release produced release/linux-x86_64 containing bin only; after, it contains bin and lib with 36 objects, and bin/../lib resolves. Also checked every DT_NEEDED entry of the shipped binary — libSDL3, libasound, libvorbisfile, libvorbis, libogg, libxmp, libopusfile, libfluidsynth all resolve from the bundle, while glibc (libc/libm/libmvec/libdl/ld-linux) and libGLX/libOpenGL correctly come from the host, which is what a portable build wants: bundling GL would break driver matching.

title: FluidSynth MIDI uses its own audio driver — silent in Flatpak sandbox; route through engine SDL mixer
description: On Linux, midi_fluid.c (FMIDI_Init, engine/h2shared/midi_fluid.c:220-241) opens FluidSynth's OWN audio driver via new_fluid_audio_driver() with a pipewire->pulseaudio->alsa cascade. This is a separate audio thread, independent of the engine's SDL audio that plays SFX and streamed OGG. In the Flatpak sandbox (manifest exposes --socket=pulseaudio; FluidSynth is built from source v2.4.6 with NO explicit -Denable audio-driver flags, so drivers are auto-detected against the freedesktop SDK), the cascade can fail to find a working driver -> "FluidSynth: couldn't create audio driver" -> total MIDI silence even though SFX/OGG work. Vanilla Hexen II music is MIDI-only, so this presents as "no music at all." Durable fix: stop using FluidSynth's audio driver; render to PCM (fluid_synth_write_s16) and feed it through the engine's existing SDL mixer raw-samples sink (same path OGG uses, which works in the sandbox). Also makes MIDI honor bgmvolume and pause/resume. Keep the Windows midiStream path (midi_win.c) unchanged. Acceptance: MIDI on Linux/Flatpak plays through the engine's SDL audio with no separate FluidSynth audio driver; bgmvolume applies; Windows path untouched.
close_reason: FluidSynth MIDI renders through engine SDL mixer (commit dded98db3), not separate driver. engine/h2shared/midi_fluid.c:404-406 renders with fluid_synth_write_s16 into S_RawSamples at fs_rate with bgmvolume applied. rg new_fluid_audio_driver returns zero hits. Windows midi_win.c unchanged.

title: R_DrawBrushModel fast path drops geometry past MAX_BMODEL_BATCH (gl_rsurf.c:2649-2720)
description: surf->visframe is stamped r_framecount before the batch-full guard; when a same-texture run reaches MAX_BMODEL_BATCH(4096), surfaces 4097+ are not appended AND carry visframe==r_framecount so the legacy fallback (draws visframe==-1) skips them too → drawn by neither path. Requires a brush-model entity with 4097+ consecutive same-texture visible non-special faces (very rare). NOTE: merely moving the visframe stamp is insufficient (stale visframe). FIX: on overflow, flush the accumulated group, reset batch_count, then append.

title: R_BuildWorldCull leaks gpu_surfs on partial allocation failure (gl_worldcull.c:530-537)

If gpu_surfs succeeds but cull_bucket_map fails, the error block calls R_FreeWorldCull (which only frees cull_bucket_map) and returns, leaking the still-valid gpu_surfs. OOM-only, once per map load. title: Filter-mode walk loops touch stale deleted texnums (gl_draw.c:448-461)

FIX: add 'if(!glt->identifier[0]) continue;' at the top of each of the three walk loops; optionally zero glt->texnum at the stale-marking site.

title: VBO cache desync: raw glBindBuffer(0) → glBufferSubData targets buffer 0 (gl_vbo.c:541)
description: On GL 4.3 WITHOUT ARB_buffer_storage (engine's stated minimum), GL_Upload's fallback uses GL_BindBufferCached then glBufferSubData. The cleanup at gl_vbo.c:541/592 issues a RAW glBindBuffer(GL_ARRAY_BUFFER,0): GL state→0 but current_array_buffer stays stale==frame->host_buffer. The 2nd+ GL_ImmEnd in a frame reuses the same host_buffer → cache hit skips the bind while state is 0 → glBufferSubData hits buffer 0 (GL_INVALID_OPERATION), data not written, subsequent glBindVertexBuffer reads stale bytes → corrupted geometry. title: Mod_ReloadTextures never re-uploads gl_fb_texturenum (gl_model.c:694-712)
description: On video mode change, D_ClearOpenGLTextures wipes the texture cache and the GL context is destroyed/recreated, invalidating all handles. Mod_ReloadTextures re-uploads gl_texturenum but never re-runs Mod_LoadFullbrightTexture, so tx->gl_fb_texturenum keeps a dangling handle. Because glGenTextures restarts ID allocation low, the stale fb ID is reissued to a different new texture → the fullbright additive pass (gl_worldcull.c:1270) samples the WRONG live texture, no GL error. Also non-eligible (*turb, {fence) textures never reset fb to 0. Common trigger (resolution/fullscreen change with map loaded), persistent corruption. FIX: regenerate gl_fb_texturenum in Mod_ReloadTextures via Mod_LoadFullbrightTexture for eligible textures, set 0 for the rest.

title: Auto-detect flipbook alias models for MOD_NOLERP (replace r_nolerp_list maintenance)
description:
Animation smoothing (model lerp) morphs flipbook-style alias models — flames, torches, waterfalls (SoT waterfallt.mdl), explosions — because their adjacent poses are unrelated geometry sheets, not deformations of one mesh. Today these are suppressed by name via r_nolerp_list (engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:176), which is a maintenance treadmill: every mod ships new models under new names that morph until manually appended.

Replace name matching with a geometry heuristic at load time. The data is available right after pose load (poseverts[] trivertx_t, pheader->numverts, pheader->scale; engine/h2shared/gl_model.c:3149). For each adjacent pose pair compute max per-vertex displacement in world units, normalize by the model's bbox diagonal, and set MOD_NOLERP when the jump exceeds a threshold (~0.35). Gate behind a new cvar r_lerp_autodetect (default on). Keep r_nolerp_list as an explicit override (union), so curated entries always win.

Restrict the test to cases lerp actually blends: looping multi-pose groups and adjacent single-pose frames. Final threshold tuning requires a real run on the test box (false-positive risk: a genuinely fast/large deform frame could lose smoothing).

Stopgap already applied (uncommitted): waterfallt.mdl appended to r_nolerp_list default.
notes:
2026-06-16 r29 implementation:

WHY: m0rk fix (extend r_nolerp_list with waterfall.mdl + waterfall_90.mdl) still left the SoT waterfall flashing.  Either the user's flashing model isn't in mcache as a 'waterfall'-named entry, or a load path clobbers MOD_NOLERP.  Rather than chase per-mod variants forever, implement f807's heuristic now — auto-flag any alias model whose pose pairs jump too far to be a deformation.

IMPL SHAPE:
- Mod_ComputeFlipbookRatio (engine/h2shared/gl_model.c): walks each frame's pose pairs, computes max-per-vertex world-units displacement / model bbox diagonal, stores worst ratio on mod->flipbook_max_ratio.  Tested pairs:
  - intra-multi-pose-group adjacent pairs INCLUDING wrap (the group cycles via cl.time/interval)
  - adjacent single-pose-frame pairs (sequential frame transitions are the typical lerp targets)
  Skips frames with no real next-pose to lerp to.
- Called at end of BOTH Mod_LoadAliasModel and Mod_LoadAliasModelNew (after GL_MakeAliasModelDisplayLists, before Hunk_FreeToLowMark — poseverts[] is hunk-allocated).
- Mod_SetExtraFlags (now) unions MOD_NOLERP from EITHER nameInList(r_nolerp_list, ...) OR (r_lerp_autodetect && flipbook_max_ratio > r_lerp_autodetect_threshold).  Static list wins precedence; threshold tunable at runtime without rebuild (no re-read of pose data — ratio is sticky).
- Cvars: r_lerp_autodetect (default 1, archived), r_lerp_autodetect_threshold (default 0.35, not archived).  Both hooked to R_Model_ExtraFlags_List_f so toggling at runtime re-applies on every cached model.
- mcache extended: prints 'flipratio=%.3f NOLERP' for alias models, so threshold tuning is empirical.

THRESHOLD CHOICE:
- 0.35 default, conservative.
- Flipbook frames have ratios ~0.7-1.0 (entire geometry swap).
- Smooth deforming anims (walk/idle) sit ~0.05-0.15.
- Cross-anim boundaries in single-pose frame sequences (e.g. death_end -> idle_first) are the false-positive risk; a single huge jump in an otherwise smooth model would still flag MOD_NOLERP.  If observed in testing, two fallbacks: (a) raise the threshold via the cvar, (b) follow up by switching MAX-of-ratios to AVG-of-ratios in Mod_ComputeFlipbookRatio.

WAITING ON: tester run.  Plan:
  1. r29 + this patch, load SoT, r_lerpmodels 1, walk to broken waterfall.  Should be stable.
  2. mcache save in the same scene — check waterfall variants show flipratio > 0.35 NOLERP, and check no combat models are flagged.
  3. If false positives observed, tune r_lerp_autodetect_threshold up (0.45+).
  4. If true positives missed, tune threshold down (0.25-) or report which model.

LONGER TERM: when stable, the static r_nolerp_list (engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:213) becomes effectively documentation/override-only; could trim curated entries once the heuristic has been validated across H2/PoP/SoT/HW maps.
