title: Replace immediate mode GL with vertex buffers
description:
Major renderer rewrite: migrate from GL 1.x immediate mode to GL 4.3 core profile.

## Why
Required for: retro palettization/dithering, compute shader culling, bindless textures, proper MSAA via FBO, order-independent transparency, and all modern rendering features from Ironwail.

## Architecture (based on Ironwail analysis)

### Phase 1: VBO/VAO Foundation
- Replace all glBegin/glEnd with vertex buffer objects
- World geometry (BSP surfaces) → static VBOs built at map load
- Alias models → dynamic VBOs updated per-frame
- Particles → instanced point sprites or quad VBOs
- Sky → VBO quads
- 2D HUD/menu → orthographic VBO quad batch

### Phase 2: Shader Pipeline
- World shader: lightmap × diffuse, fog, dithering (GLSL 430)
- Alias model shader: per-vertex lighting, colormap
- Particle shader: point sprites or instanced quads
- Sky shader: scrolling layers or cubemap
- Postprocess shader: gamma, contrast, palettization, dithering
- Water shader: warp, alpha, lit water

### Phase 3: Modern GL Features
- GL 4.3 core context (remove compatibility profile)
- Uniform Buffer Objects for frame data (view/proj matrix, fog, time)
- Compute shader frustum culling (Ironwail approach)
- 3D palette LUT texture for retro palettization
- SSBO for light data
- Indirect multi-draw for world geometry
- Optional: bindless textures, persistent buffer mapping

### Phase 4: Advanced Effects
- Order-Independent Transparency (weighted blended OIT)
- MSAA via multisampled FBOs
- Retro softemu modes (fine dither, coarse dither, banded)
- Lightmapped liquid surfaces

## Reference
- Ironwail source at /home/josh/tmp/claudedir/ironwail/Quake/
- Key files: gl_shaders.h (all GLSL), gl_shaders.c (program management), gl_rmain.c (render pipeline), r_world.c (BSP rendering), r_alias.c (model rendering)
- Ironwail requires GL 4.3 minimum

## Effort Estimate
Very large — weeks of focused work. Should be done on a dedicated branch.
close_reason: GL 4.3 VBO/shader migration complete — zero immediate mode, zero hardware matrix stack

title: Torch corona brightens with distance (intensity = distance/1024) — the other half of the 137k step
description:
Verified in game on t9.dem (SoT, the keep) with a headless run: what you SEE of a torch from a distance is the corona R_DrawGlow draws, not the dynamic light. Toggling gl_glows 0 removes the orange halo entirely and leaves a small dim flame sprite on a wall that is still warmly lit. Side-by-side kept as torch_glow_ab.png / torch_glow_ab_full.png in the repo root (gitignored scratch).

That matters because the corona has its own hardcoded 1024, and it ramps the OPPOSITE way to the dlight cull that uhexen2-137k just removed. gl_rmain.c, in R_DrawGlow:

    // Diminish torch flare inversely with distance.
    intensity = (1024.0f - distance) / 1024.0f;
    // Invert (fades as you approach).
    intensity = (1.0f - intensity);
    clamp to [0,1]

which reduces to intensity = distance / 1024, clamped. So the corona is INVISIBLE at the torch, and at FULL brightness from 1024 units out. The comment says the fade-as-you-approach is deliberate, and it is the classic Shanjaq corona behaviour, so this is not obviously a bug on its own.

Paired with the old dlight cut-off at radius + 1024 (150 + 1024 = 1174 for a torch) it produced the thing Mathuzzz complained about, though:

  beyond ~1174 units : corona at full brightness, dlight OFF
                       -> a bright halo floating over unlit geometry
  inside  ~1174 units : dlight ON, corona fading toward nothing as you close
                       -> lit geometry, no halo

Neither distance showed both at once, and the handover was a hard step, which is exactly "lights he sees far off in distance get dlight turned on as he approaches ... its awkward to look at". Two subsystems, two 1024s, pulling in opposite directions and crossing at nearly the same distance.

uhexen2-137k fixed one half: the geometry is now lit at any distance, so the corona no longer floats over darkness. Open question for this bead is whether the other half wants changing too:

  1. Is intensity = distance/1024 still right now that the dlight is present at
     range? The corona was arguably compensating for the missing dlight -- it
     was the only cue that a distant torch existed. With the dlight back, a
     full-brightness halo at range may now read as too much.
  2. The 1024 is hardcoded in both places and was never one shared constant.
     If the ramp stays, it wants a name, and probably a cvar.
  3. Ask Mathuzzz to re-check with the 137k build BEFORE changing anything
     here -- removing the dlight step may be all he wanted, and changing the
     corona ramp on top of it would be two variables at once.

Do not touch this until 137k has been confirmed in the field.
notes: Blocked in practice on the 137k field confirmation, not on any code.

[bug] r_lerp_autodetect is all-or-nothing per model — one violent animation costs a model interpolation everywhere
description:
Split out of uhexen2-aqm0. That bead fixed the heuristic measuring animation
SEAMS (pairs the QC never blends). This is the separate problem that one
genuinely-blended bad pair still costs a model interpolation across every
animation it plays.

r_lerp_autodetect flags MOD_NOLERP when the worst per-vertex displacement over
any measured pose pair exceeds r_lerp_autodetect_threshold (0.35) of the bbox
diagonal. The verdict is per MODEL, so a single violent frame transition -
almost always in a death or heavy-attack animation - disables blending for the
model's idle, walk and run too, which is where smoothness is actually noticed.

Measured over data1 pak0 + pak1 (offline replication of
Mod_ComputeFlipbookRatio; same harness that confirmed uhexen2-aqm0). Still
NOLERP after the seam fix, with the pair responsible:

  models/ballista.mdl        0.425  Blista4  -> Blista5
  models/skullwiz.mdl        0.417  skdeth6  -> skdeth7     (death)
  models/mumshot.mdl         0.389  1fire8   -> 1fire9
  models/axblade.mdl         0.366  AXE5     -> AXE6
  models/boss/warrider.mdl   0.366  RaxeD9   -> RaxeD10
  models/golem_b.mdl         0.364  Rpound11 -> Rpound12
  models/spider.mdl          0.361  sdeath8  -> sdeath9     (death)
  models/golem_i.mdl         0.354  Rpound11 -> Rpound12
  models/flaming.mdl         0.353  flarow4  -> flarow5
  models/stlghtng.mdl        0.350  STRIKE5  -> STRIKE6
  models/flame1.mdl          0.460  (multi-pose group; also in r_nolerp_list)

THE TELL that the threshold is doing something arbitrary rather than
principled: the three golem variants share the identical Rpound11 -> Rpound12
animation and land on opposite sides of the cut.

  golem_s  0.345  ->  lerps
  golem_i  0.354  ->  does not
  golem_b  0.364  ->  does not

Same monster, same animation, different smoothness, decided by 0.02 of bbox
diagonal. No player-visible reason for the split.

DIRECTIONS WORTH WEIGHING (not a decision):
  1. Per-frame-run verdicts instead of per-model. Store the flag against the
     animation run that violates, and consult it with the entity's current
     frame. Most faithful - a violent death stops blending, the walk cycle
     keeps it - and the most work, since MOD_NOLERP is read per model at the
     draw site (gl_rmain.c:1379).
  2. Clamp rather than disable: blend normally but cap per-vertex travel, so a
     bad pair degrades toward a snap instead of switching the model off.
  3. Leave the mechanism and re-tune the threshold, accepting it stays a
     blunt instrument. Cheapest, and the golem split says the current value is
     not obviously right, but any single value has the same failure mode.

Worth noting the curated r_nolerp_list already wins outright and covers the
flame/torch cases the heuristic exists to generalise, so the autodetect's real
job is unmaintained mod content - which argues for erring toward blending and
handling the exceptions by name.

NOT URGENT: nothing here is a field report. It surfaced while verifying
uhexen2-aqm0 and is recorded so the data does not have to be re-derived. The
offline harness that produced these numbers is straightforward to rebuild -
parse the MDL, replicate the bounds inflation and the ratio loop.

title: Software/WASM renderer ignores EF_SPIN and EF_FLOAT from misc_modelpimp
description:
engine/hexen2/r_alias.c honours only the raw MDL header bit `currententity->model->flags & EF_ROTATE` at all three of its motion/lighting sites — R_AliasSetUpTransform's yaw (r_alias.c:439), the float offset in the same function (r_alias.c:507), and the item-style pulsing light in R_AliasDrawModel (r_alias.c:952). It never calls R_GetPimpFlags, so neither the per-entity override nor the shared model->ex_flags is consulted.

The GL renderer honours both flags at five sites: gl_rmain.c:461 (spin yaw), 1532 and 2880 (SPIN|FLOAT lighting), 1723 and 3030 (FLOAT bob offset).

Consequence: a misc_modelpimp with spawnflag 1 (Spin) or 2 (Float) does nothing in the software renderer, including the WEB_RENDERER=software web build. The spawnflag 32 (Share motion) added under uhexen2-nna4 in 0.8.0-beta.r15 is likewise inert there. EF_GLOW orbs are also GL-only. EF_ILLUMINATE does work in both, because the dlight is allocated in cl_main.c, which both renderers share.

Found while verifying uhexen2-nna4; not the cause of Mathuzzz's report (he is on the Windows GL build).

FIX SKETCH: r_alias.c has no entity_t* in scope other than currententity, and R_GetPimpFlags is already provided for the software build by r_soft_web.c:144 with the same model->ex_flags OR semantics as GL. Replace the three raw tests with the GL predicate — EF_ROTATE from the header OR EF_SPIN/EF_FLOAT from R_GetPimpFlags, keeping GL's split (SPIN|FLOAT for the lighting site, FLOAT alone for the bob offset, SPIN for the yaw).

DONE WHEN: a misc_modelpimp with spawnflag 1 spins its target in the software build, spawnflag 2 bobs it, and a shipped SoT map renders motion identically under both renderers.

title: No-dynamic-light control is keyed to the model, which does not scale past a few custom light models
description:
Raised by Mathuzzz: 'regarding the lights, it shouldn't be model dependent as I use like 2 dozens of additional models for light sources. bloodshot probably use different ones in his mod, etc...'

This is a fair criticism of the design, not a misunderstanding.

HOW IT IS MODEL-KEYED TODAY, in two separate places:
1. PF_pimpmodel (engine/h2shared/pr_cmds.c) propagates XF_NO_DLIGHT into mod->ex_flags, so spawnflag 64 without 16 applies to every entity on the map sharing that model. One misc_modelpimp per model.
2. XF_TORCH_GLOW — the thing that makes stock torches cast their dlight at all — is assigned by a HARDCODED MODEL NAME LIST in Mod_SetAliasModelExtraFlags (engine/h2shared/gl_model.c): rflmtrch, cflmtrch, castrch, rometrch, egtorch, flame, eflmtrch. A custom light model is not in that list and never will be, so a mapper's own light props cannot participate in the torch path either way.

THERE IS A PER-ENTITY ESCAPE, but it is not obvious and it is not documented anywhere: spawnflags 16|64 = 80. Because 16 (SELFONLY) skips the propagation block, XF_NO_DLIGHT lands only on that entity's pimp_overrides[] slot and never on mod->ex_flags, so it affects that one entity regardless of model. Whether a mapper can actually place that per light source depends on the mod's QC, since misc_modelpimp lives mod-side (SoT) and this repo has no pimpmodel .hc — how it chooses its ref_ent is not ours to assume.

WHY THAT IS STILL NOT AN ANSWER for the reported use case: with ~two dozen distinct light models the mapper needs either 24 misc_modelpimp controllers (one per model, flag 64) or one per light entity (flag 80). Both are bookkeeping the engine should not be imposing. And a second mod with a different model set repeats the whole exercise.

WHAT IS MISSING is a control that is neither model-keyed nor per-entity-hand-placed. Options worth weighing before building anything:
- A cvar in the gl_torch_dlight family covering the misc_modelpimp cast-light and the EF_*LIGHT dlights. Player-side, blunt, but zero mapper work. Note r_dynamic 0 already exists and is far too blunt — it kills dlights on world surfaces wholesale, weapon flashes included.
- A QC-settable per-entity field, so a mod can flag its own light props at spawn without a misc_modelpimp each.
- Letting a mapper extend the XF_TORCH_GLOW name list from a map or mod config, which fixes the second half of the problem (custom models cannot be torches) rather than the first.

Ask Mathuzzz which shape actually helps before implementing: the answer differs a lot depending on whether the goal is 'my mod's props never spill light through walls' (cvar or QC field) or 'this specific sconce is too bright' (what flag 80 already does).

title: headless-drive.sh: display selection races, so concurrent runs share an X display and screenshot each other
description:
Found while trying to build a runtime regression test for uhexen2-vyfi. Cost several hours of misleading results, so worth fixing before the harness is trusted again.

TWO DEFECTS, both in tools/headless-drive.sh.

1. Display selection is not atomic. The free-display scan is

     for n in $(seq 99 120); do [ -e "/tmp/.X11-unix/X$n" ] || { DISP=":$n"; break; }; done

   Two runs started close together both see X99 missing and both pick :99, because the socket is not created until Xvfb actually starts. The second engine then renders into the same X display as the first, 'xdotool search --name "." | tail -1' can select either window, and 'import -window root' captures whichever is on top.

   Observed: three glhexen2 processes alive on :99 at once. A 15-frame burst came back with standard deviation exactly 0.000 across all frames — it was photographing a stale idle window from a previous run, not the run under test. That reads as a clean pass.

2. Cleanup is unreliable, which is what lets 1 happen. The EXIT trap kills $GPID/$XPID, but runs killed by the outer 'timeout', or by a pkill that matches the wrapper shell rather than the script, leave the engine and Xvfb behind. Stale processes then collide with the next run.

SUGGESTED FIX for 1: create the lock before starting Xvfb rather than testing for it — e.g. 'mkdir /tmp/.hdrive-lock-$n' as the claim (mkdir is atomic), or use 'Xvfb -displayfd' and read back the display Xvfb actually chose, which is the purpose-built mechanism. For 2: trap on INT/TERM as well as EXIT, and have the script write its engine/Xvfb PIDs into the outdir so a later run can reap strays.

ALSO WORTH ADDING once 1 is fixed: a self-check that the window being captured belongs to this run's engine, so a display collision fails loudly instead of returning a confident wrong answer. That is the property the whole harness depends on and currently does not verify.

title: misc_modelpimp spawnflag 64 (No dynamic light) only gates 2 of 6 dlight sources
description:
Reported indirectly by Mathuzzz, who found spawnflag 16 did not stop walltorch dynamic lights. 16 is Self-only, so that part is user error (64 is the no-dlight flag) — but checking it turned up a real limitation in 64.

The r15 release notes describe flag 64 as 'cast no dynamic light at all, leaving the baked lighting to carry it'. XF_NO_DLIGHT does not deliver that. In CL_RelinkEntities (engine/hexen2/cl_main.c) an entity can allocate a dlight from six places, and XF_NO_DLIGHT is only tested at two of them:

  GATED:
    ~cl_main.c:823  XF_TORCH_GLOW torch dlight   (also gated by gl_torch_dlight)
    ~cl_main.c:842  EF_ILLUMINATE modelpimp cast light

  NOT GATED:
    ~cl_main.c:770  EF_BRIGHTLIGHT
    ~cl_main.c:786  EF_DIMLIGHT
    ~cl_main.c:798  EF_DARKLIGHT
    ~cl_main.c:806  EF_LIGHT      (fixed radius 200)

So a mapper who sets 64 on a model whose entities carry any EF_*LIGHT effect still gets a dynamic light, with no indication why.

Stock light_torch_small_walltorch is NOT affected: gamecode/hc/portals/light.hc sets .weaponmodel to models/flame.mdl and never touches .effects, and models/flame is one of the names Mod_SetAliasModelExtraFlags (engine/h2shared/gl_model.c:3297) tags XF_TORCH_GLOW by filename. So for stock torches flag 64 does work. The gap bites mod content that sets EF_LIGHT/EF_DIMLIGHT on a prop.

Fix is to test XF_NO_DLIGHT alongside the other four, via R_GetPimpFlags, the same way the torch branch does. Note that costs an R_GetPimpFlags call earlier in the loop for every entity, so hoist the single lookup above the whole dlight block rather than calling it six times.
notes:
FIX WRITTEN 2026-08-20, engine/hexen2/cl_main.c (CL_RelinkEntities).

Shape of the change:
- Hoisted one R_GetPimpFlags(ent, &pimp_gs) call above the whole dlight run, plus a derived 'nodlight' boolean. Declarations went in the function's opening block rather than mid-block: the surrounding code is C89-style throughout (every other local here is declared at the top, and the two existing pimp lookups were wrapped in braces specifically to stay legal), and this engine still targets compilers that care.
- Added '&& !nodlight' to the four steady effects that lacked it: EF_BRIGHTLIGHT, EF_DIMLIGHT, EF_DARKLIGHT, EF_LIGHT.
- Repointed the two already-gated branches (torch glow, EF_ILLUMINATE) at the hoisted values instead of re-fetching. Net R_GetPimpFlags calls per entity go 2 -> 1, so this is cheaper than before despite covering three times as many branches.

ONE DELIBERATE EXCLUSION: EF_MUZZLEFLASH is left ungated, and the reasoning is in the code comment so it is not silently re-litigated. The flag exists so a mapper can stop a prop's standing light bleeding through a wall; a muzzle flash is a 0.1s event belonging to the act of firing rather than to the model's own lighting, it already has its own switch in gl_missile_glows, and gating it would change weapon feel for any model that happens to be pimped. That makes the count 5 of 6 rather than 6 of 6 — deliberately. Reopen if a mapper actually wants it.

BUILDS, all clean:
  nix build .#default   OK  (0.8.0-beta.r15)
  nix build .#h2ded     OK
  WASM software renderer via shell-wasm.nix + scripts/wasm-build.sh software: OK, '[100%] Built target hexenwail', 0 errors. This is the path that matters for the change, since r_soft_web.c is where the non-GL R_GetPimpFlags lives.
  nix build .#wasm fails, but on DNS ('Temporary failure in name resolution') while compiling gl_rmain.c, a file this change does not touch. scripts/wasm-build.sh documents that target as expected-to-fail in the sandbox: emscripten fetches its SDL3 port over the network at configure time and the nix sandbox has none.

Runtime regression guard added as scenario vyfi_torch_regression in tools/headless-drive.sh: stands beside a light_torch_castle in demo1 (models/castrch.mdl, XF_TORCH_GLOW by name) and toggles gl_torch_dlight on/off/on. The on/off pair must differ and the two 'on' shots must match — the second 'on' specifically catches a stale hoisted flag value, which is the failure mode the refactor could plausibly introduce.

RUNTIME TEST: NOT DONE. Verified by build (3 targets) and code inspection only.

Two blockers, both filed:
- uhexen2-fwal: headless-drive.sh races on X display selection. Concurrent runs shared :99 and screenshotted each other; one 15-frame burst came back with sd exactly 0.000 because it was photographing a stale idle window from an earlier run. That reads as a clean pass. No measurement taken through this harness can be trusted until that is fixed.
- uhexen2-d697: nothing in stock content reaches the newly-gated path anyway. Stock walltorches light via XF_TORCH_GLOW (assigned by model NAME in Mod_SetAliasModelExtraFlags) and never set EF_LIGHT; light_torch_small_walltorch touches only .weaponmodel and .abslight. Testing the four newly-gated effects needs a purpose-built entity.

A scenario (vyfi_torch_regression) was written and then REMOVED rather than committed. It never produced a valid measurement — first aimed at a wall with no torch in frame, then at a wall receiving no torch dlight, and its numbers came from a stale window regardless. Committing it would have left behind a test that passes vacuously, which is the exact failure the ayrn verification spent three runs on.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED WITHOUT IT:
1. Builds clean on .#default, .#h2ded, and the WASM software renderer via shell-wasm.nix.
2. The four added gates are literal '&& !nodlight' additions to existing conditions — nothing else in those branches changed.
3. Hoisting the lookup is safe, and this was checked rather than assumed: between the hoist point and its two consumers the only writes are 'dl = CL_AllocDlight(i)' and dl->* field stores. Nothing touches ent->model or pimp_overrides[], and R_GetPimpFlags is a pure read of both, so the hoisted value cannot go stale within one loop iteration.

That is adequate for a change of this size, but it is not a runtime test, and the bead should not be read as if it were.
close_reason: Fixed in d68cdb9ea. EF_BRIGHTLIGHT/DIMLIGHT/DARKLIGHT/LIGHT now test XF_NO_DLIGHT via a single hoisted R_GetPimpFlags lookup shared with the two branches that already had it (net 1 lookup per entity, down from 2). EF_MUZZLEFLASH deliberately excluded, rationale in the code. Builds clean on .#default, .#h2ded and WASM software. No runtime test — see uhexen2-d697 and uhexen2-fwal.

title: Real shadow-casting for dynamic lights (uhexen2-q3gh was closed without it landing)
description:
Split out of uhexen2-kd3g. Mathuzzz asked for dynamic lights that cast
shadows; uhexen2-kd3g delivered only the fallback he offered (a per-light
opt-out from the dlight set, misc_modelpimp spawnflag 64 / XF_NO_DLIGHT).
This is the real thing.

STARTING POINT, AND WHAT IS NOT TRUE:

uhexen2-q3gh is closed with the reason "All subtasks complete: FBO, shadow
pass, per-pixel shader sampling with PCF, preset integration, alias model
shadow casting". Do not build on that assumption. In master:

  - engine/h2shared/gl_shadow.c / .h do not exist.
  - The only shadow cvar in the engine is r_shadows, the classic projected
    blob (gl_rmain.c:143, default 0).
  - Commit 226a06f4c "render: add shadow mapping system, make dynamic lights
    always-on" added gl_shadow.c (411 lines), gl_shadow.h and menu/cvar
    plumbing -- but it is an ancestor of no branch and never reached master,
    and its own message says "Stub geometry pass for now", so it allocated
    the FBO and picked the lights and then drew nothing into it.

So the honest state is: infrastructure sketch exists in a dangling commit,
no shadow has ever been rendered.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE FEATURE REQUEST: Hexen II dlights don't test
occlusion, so a torch near a wall spills onto whatever is on the other side.
That is the concrete complaint behind "they don't cast shadows" -- it isn't
that a missing shadow looks bare, it's that the light goes where it
shouldn't. Any fix has to address occlusion, not just add a shadow.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (from 226a06f4c, worth reusing):
  - depth-only FBO, one cube or one 2D map per light
  - select top N nearest/brightest dlights per frame rather than all of them
  - resolution scaled by preset: 64-128px for the retro tiers, 512-1024 for
    modern/ultra, GL_NEAREST for retro and PCF above it
  - the geometry pass 226a06f4c left as a stub is the actual work

Check Ironwail first per project convention (uhexen2-a5nn) -- if it has
nothing here, this is a Hexenwail-only feature and the bar for complexity
should be set accordingly.

DONE WHEN: a torch behind a wall no longer lights the room on the other
side, at a frame cost the retro presets can absorb.

title: DEFLATED .pk3 entries inflate whole on open — demos and music lose O(1) streaming
description:
What shipped for pk3 support deviates from what uhexen2-pzha's DESIGN section recommended, deliberately and with a working result, but the deviation has a cost that should be tracked rather than forgotten.

pzha's design compared three options for the deflate substrate and recommended option 2: lift FTE's seekable streaming deflate (FSZIP_Deflate_Init / _Read / _Seek / _Destroy, fteqw/engine/common/fs_zip.c:944-1039) onto miniz's tinfl, explicitly because "this is exactly what cl_demo.c's cls.demofile and snd_codec.c need, and it is the piece a naive port gets wrong." It named option 3 -- inflate the whole entry on open -- as the one that "regresses demo playback and music streaming from O(1) to O(entry size) resident."

What landed is a hybrid nobody wrote down: miniz IS vendored (option 2's dependency answer), but the read path is option 3's shape. FS_OpenFileHandle_Internal (quakefs.c) mallocs the full uncompressed length and calls FS_ZipReadEntry once; fshandle_t serves the bytes from that buffer afterwards, and FS_fclose frees it. There is no incremental inflate and no seek-by-restart-and-skip.

The gap is narrower than pzha feared, which is why this is P2 and not higher:
- STORED entries never take the memory path at all. They are contiguous in the archive, so they stay FILE-backed and stream O(1) exactly like a pak member.
- Already-compressed media -- ogg, opus, mp3 -- is what a sanely built .pk3 STOREs rather than deflates, so the music case that worried the design mostly does not arise in practice.

What is genuinely affected: a .dem shipped deflated (demos compress well, so a packer will deflate them) is now resident in full for the length of playback instead of streaming, and any large deflated entry pays a full-size malloc at open. There is no cap on that allocation.

Two things to decide, not necessarily together:
1. A ceiling. pzha's own open-questions list ends with "Memory ceiling: inflating a large entry on open is a hunk/zone allocation that the pak path never made. Needs a cap or a streaming inflate for the demo case." Neither exists yet. A cap with a clear refusal message is much cheaper than streaming and closes the pathological case.
2. Whether streaming is worth it at all. It is only worth building if someone actually ships deflated demos or deflated music. Measure before porting FSZIP_Deflate_*; the fear may be theoretical.

Prerequisite reading: uhexen2-pzha's DESIGN section, commit f540490a9 (mounting) and 550e331a4 (the fshandle_t memory backing).

title: Retail installation check cannot see content that arrived through a .pk3
description:
Known gap called out in the pzha commit message (f540490a9) and now that pk3 mounting is complete, the thing standing between "pk3s are additive content" and "you can ship your whole install as pk3s", which is what Garrett (Monolyth-42) actually asked for.

check_known_paks (engine/h2shared/quakefs.c:272) identifies pak0.pak / pak1.pak by a CRC computed over the .pak directory structure, plus the file count, and compares against the pakdata / old_pakdata / demo_pakdata / oem0_pakdata tables. FS_LoadPackFile feeds it at quakefs.c:413. A .pk3 has an entirely different directory format, so no archive can ever produce a matching CRC, and gameflags never picks up the registered/retail bits.

Consequence: convert data1/pak0.pak and pak1.pak to .pk3 -- exactly the ~50% disk saving the feature exists for -- and the engine mounts every file correctly but still reports the install as unregistered.

Partially mitigated already: CheckRegistered's gfx/pop.lmp read went through a raw FILE * and therefore failed outright on a deflated entry; it now reads through FS_OpenFileHandle (commit 550e331a4), so the pop.lmp half of the identification works from an archive. The CRC-over-pak-directory half does not and is what this bead is about.

Design question to settle first, because it decides everything else: is the check an anti-piracy gate or a "you have the right data files" sanity check? If the latter, identifying content by the presence and size of known member files inside whichever container they arrived in is straightforward and container-agnostic. If the former, any archive-aware scheme is trivially forgeable and the honest answer may be to keep requiring a real pak0.pak/pak1.pak for identification while letting pk3s supply everything else -- i.e. document the current behaviour rather than change it.

Do NOT weaken the check without deciding that question explicitly.

title: Menu: per-item description/tooltip text
description: Last substantial gap from uhexen2-yae's Ironwail menu list. Hexenwail menus have no description text: an item's name is all the player gets, and names like 'Render Scale', 'Dither', 'Overbright Models' or 'Alpha To Coverage' do not explain themselves. Ironwail shows a one-line description for the highlighted item. Scope is mostly content, not code: a description string per row across Options/Display/Renderer/Graphics/Sound/Game submenus, plus a draw slot and the plumbing to key it off the active menu's cursor. Note the menu canvas is only guaranteed 200 logical units tall (gl_draw.c CANVAS_MENU), so the description slot has to fit inside the existing layout rather than being appended below it.

title: MD5: verify skeletal render with a real asset (winding, lighting, skin)
description: uhexen2-7ok0 phases 2 and 3 landed in 5670c942b and are verified against the synthetic models in engine/tests/md5 (parser math, inverse-bind composition, hierarchy propagation, bounds). What synthetic models cannot settle: (1) triangle winding — MD5 index order is passed through unchanged, and if id's winding is opposite Hexen II's front-face convention every MD5 model renders inside-out; (2) whether the in-shader 1.0+dot(normal,shadevector) lighting matches the shadedots table closely enough side by side; (3) skin resolution from the mesh's shader string against a real material path. Needs an actual .md5mesh/.md5anim pair with art. Ironwail's Quake-rerelease MD5 models are the obvious source.

title: Commit 3b98a4d4f is mislabelled: chase-cam message hides a 2300-line revert of the p4ln render stack
description:
On master, commit 3b98a4d4f (chase: add bindable +chase / -chase / togglechase and a Key Setup row) actually bundles a full revert of most of the p4ln render-refactor stack — 52 files, −2335 lines; functionally equivalent to revert-p4ln branch c21b95c0f.

Anyone bisecting the uhexen2-gnhh regression umbrella will be misled: a bisect landing on 3b98a4d4f looks like a keybind change but flips the entire render architecture.

SUGGESTED REMEDIES:
1. Note this prominently in uhexen2-gnhh so bisectors know to expect the mislabelling.
2. If master gets force-pushed again (it has been twice already as of 2026-08-20), split and relabel the commit.

Discovered 2026-08-20 during PR #2 merge dry-run (uhexen2-waw8).
notes:
REMEDY 1 APPLIED 2026-08-20. The mislabelling is now the first thing anyone reads on uhexen2-gnhh: its description opens with a BISECT HAZARD block naming 3b98a4d4f, its real shape (52 files, +1732/-2335), what it is equivalent to (revert-p4ln c21b95c0f), and the instruction not to replace gnhh's hand-branched probe table with an automated bisect over master without accounting for it.

Re-verified against master before writing the warning rather than trusting the original report: `git show --stat 3b98a4d4f` is 52 files / +1732 / -2335 under the subject "chase: add bindable +chase / -chase / togglechase and a Key Setup row", and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 3b98a4d4f master` confirms it is on master. The claim holds exactly as filed.

REMEDY 2 (split and relabel the commit) deliberately NOT done. It is conditional in the bead's own wording -- "if master gets force-pushed again" -- and rewriting master history right now would invalidate the probe branches uhexen2-gnhh's bisect table is built from (prior-good, probe-pre-pipeline, probe13-no-gwtq, probe14-no-gwtq, probe17-no-gwtq, probe-no-93a8, revert-p4ln, revert-4), which is the opposite of helping the investigation it blocks. It should be done on the next intentional force-push, not before.

Closing: the bisect hazard this bead exists to prevent is now documented where a bisector will hit it. If master is rewritten later, reopen for remedy 2.

description: -game portals is deliberate no-op in engine (FS_Gamedir ignores it); Mission Pack launches via separate -portals/-missionpack/-h2mp flag. description: chase_active is only reachable from Options -> Game (menu.c:3951) or the console. There is no bindable command, so a player cannot put 3rd person on a key. Mirror the existing zoom precedent (+zoom/-zoom/togglezoom, gl_screen.c:591-593) with +chase/-chase/togglechase in chase.c, and add a 'togglechase' row to the Key Setup bindnames table in menu.c so it is discoverable without console use.

title: Launcher 'Play the demo' button via optional same-origin demo bundle
description:
User-requested (2026-08-20): the demo should be reachable from a button, not a manual zip hunt. Constraints discovered from scripts/get_demo.sh: the project deliberately does NOT mirror the demo (Raven data, no redistribution grant — assets/demo/README.md), and the canonical SourceForge URL is unfetchable from a browser anyway (no CORS; browser user-agents get an interstitial/403). Design: launcher probes same-origin ./demo/hexen2demo.zip (data1/ layout: pak0.pak + loose progs.dat) at load; if present, show a "Play the demo" button that fetches it, feeds the existing ZIP import pipeline, verifies the known demo pak0 hash (md5 8e598d82bf53436ed7a0e133aa4b9f09 per quakefs.c:133 — compute/pin sha256 too), then the existing pak0-only flow (b8975b4b8) presents "Start game (demo)". No bundle → no button; the public Pages deploy ships WITHOUT the bundle (keeps the no-mirroring stance); self-hosted deploys opt in by dropping the zip beside the site. Consider docs/PWA.md section for self-hosters, and the sw.js precache list must NOT include demo/ (optional asset). Builds on uhexen2-cae5 (closed — pak0-only launchable).

INVESTIGATION FINDINGS (2026-08-20):

Direct-fetch feasibility was investigated and ruled out for now:
  (a) downloads.sourceforge.net sends no CORS headers AND serves browser user-agents an interstitial/403 (server policy, no client workaround)
  (b) archive.org has NO genuine copy — item HexenII_1020 titled "Hexen II Demo" is actually the Heroes of Might & Magic II demo (verified by parsing its zip central directory: HEROES2.AGG, H2DEMOW.EXE); other items are engine-only builds or the full retail game
  (c) Wayback Machine never captured the demo tarball, only SourceForge's redirect HTML

Design consequence: make the button's fetch URL CONFIGURABLE — probe same-origin ./demo/ first (the bundle design already specified), with an optional remote URL knob so that if a CORS-open third-party host (e.g. a future archive.org upload — NOT to be done under the project's name; assets/demo/README.md declines redistribution) appears, it's a config change not a code change. A self-hosted reverse-proxy relay (server fetches from SourceForge with a tool UA, stores nothing) is a documented option for self-hosters, impossible on GitHub Pages.
notes: ARCHIVE.ORG DISCOVERY (2026-08-20): A genuine copy now exists on archive.org: item hexen2demo_nov1997-linux-x86_64, file hexen2demo_nov1997-linux-x86_64.tgz (13,244,368 bytes, tgz sha256 e26e0f2de6f8fba9577d6ffcf9e3548c291325443b626f46fd83f57709ce45be); contains the complete demo data1/ (pak0.pak verified md5 8e598d82bf53436ed7a0e133aa4b9f09 = the genuine demo per quakefs.c:133, plus loose progs.dat, hexen.rc, default.cfg, autoexec.cfg) and unused x86_64 engine binaries. CORS verified working via https://archive.org/cors/hexen2demo_nov1997-linux-x86_64/hexen2demo_nov1997-linux-x86_64.tgz (echoes Origin, allows GET+Range). Implementation starting now with this as the remote source.

Fetch: same-origin ./demo/hexen2demo.zip else https://archive.org/cors/hexen2demo_nov1997-linux-x86_64/...tgz. DecompressionStream gunzip + minimal tar parser (no external libs); all 7 data1/ files individually size+sha256 pinned and WebCrypto-verified before install; files through mapImportedPath/storeImportedFiles; SW not caching. Runtime-proven 3x (local CORS, real archive.org, software artifact) 18/18 checks each; 52/52 web tests; docs/PWA.md section added. Deployed to /tank/josh/public/webexen (both configs, 0.8.0-beta.r12-3-g8f8177223).

title: Mod mist clumping returns at r_alias_blend_depthwrite 1 — needs a fix that is not a global depth-write ban
description:
uhexen2-gwtq was closed by 096ee3e5d, which banned depth writes for every blended alias branch. uhexen2-g842 reverted that to opt-in (r_alias_blend_depthwrite, default 1 = vanilla) because it broke self-occlusion for weapons and attack effects. The mist therefore clumps again at the default setting; 'r_alias_blend_depthwrite 0' is the workaround.

What the mist actually needs: the model is 34 tris drawn 8x/frame with a binary-alpha (0/255) skin. Mip/bilinear filtering turns those hard edges into a soft alpha ramp, and those partially-transparent edge fragments pass the 0.01 alpha threshold, blend, AND write depth — so one instance's soft edge hard-rejects the next. That is a soft-edge problem, not a general translucency problem.

Candidate fixes that do not cost self-occlusion elsewhere:
- r_oit 1 (already implemented, defaults 0) makes the whole question moot inside the OIT pass; check whether the reporter's clumping survives r_oit 1.
- r_softparticles / soft-depth fade (GL_SoftDepth_Capture already exists, uhexen2-mf9u) for the ground-intersection hard line noted in gwtq.
- Raise the alpha threshold for this class so filtered edge fragments are discarded rather than blended-and-depth-written.
- Per-model or per-mod opt-out driven by content rather than a global switch.

Do NOT re-fix by banning depth writes for all blended alias draws — that is uhexen2-g842.
notes:
PREMISE CORRECTED (uhexen2-5zv5). This bead assumed the mist skin is 'binary-alpha (0/255)' and that mip/bilinear filtering was manufacturing the soft edge. It isn't: sot/models/mist_0.tga is authored soft -- 123 distinct alpha values, 85% of texels partially transparent, and not one fully opaque texel (max alpha 183). The filtering theory is dead.

What was actually happening: mist.mdl is flagged EF_HOLEY, so the engine treated it as a cutout twice over -- GL_Upload32 binarized its alpha at 128, then R_DrawAliasModel alpha-tested it at 0.666 with blending off. It never got to be translucent at all.

Fixed under uhexen2-5zv5, which also takes the depth-write half: soft-alpha holey models no longer write depth, which is the 'per-model opt-out driven by content rather than a global switch' this bead listed as the wanted fix. Weapons and attack effects are untouched because they have solid skins.

This bead should be re-checked against a build with 5zv5 in before any further work -- the clumping it describes may simply be gone. If it isn't, r_oit 1 is still the next thing to try.

title: Launcher page layout let content stretch the game canvas off-screen
description: Root cause (commit 721c218b2): page-LAYOUT bug inherited from fork — body had min-height:100vh but no definite height, so .shell grid's 1fr row resolved to launcher column's ~2400px content height, #canvas (height:100%) grew to ~817x2352, and VID_DestRect correctly letterboxed 4:3 frame ~900px below fold. Fix: body height:100dvh (min-height:100vh fallback kept) + grid-template-rows: minmax(0,1fr) so #control-panel scrolls internally; new tripwire test web/test/shell-layout.test.js. Runtime-proven 1280x720 (was black → rendered HUD), 1920x1080, 1400x2600, webgl2 re-verified; 39/39 web tests; zero C changes.

title: Renderer toggle menu: software / opengl-sdl / vulkan-sdl / (metal-sdl) / (d3d12-sdl), gated per platform
description:
GOAL: Implement runtime renderer backend selection in the Rendering submenu, showing only backends available on the current platform.

RENDERER OPTIONS (and current state):
- software: 8bpp classic rasterizer, restored in 0.8.0-beta.r12 (commit 8e5f562f6). Currently web-only via WEB_RENDERER=software build flag, presented via WebGL2 palette-LUT blit (web_canvas_gl2.c). Desktop presenter using the same palette-LUT model would unlock selection everywhere.
- opengl-sdl: Current GL 4.3 core pipeline (only desktop renderer today).
- vulkan-sdl: Builds on render refactor in flight (commits 01e7719d5..7a29dd3b1): draw-state routed through one pipeline module, uniforms in std140 blocks, texture slot-range binding, shaders moved to files with SPIR-V compilation and explicit Vulkan bindings — clear Vulkan prep.
- metal-sdl, d3d12-sdl: Parenthesized as aspirational (macOS/Windows). Evaluate SDL3 GPU API as unifying route before committing to per-API renderers.

DESIGN DECISIONS TO RECORD:
- Per-platform gating: menu shows only compiled + runtime-supported backends (web: software/webgl2; WEB_RENDERER split may become runtime-selectable or stay build-time with menu hidden).
- Renderer switch may require vid_restart or full engine restart — decide and make menu truthful about cost.
- Persist choice in archived cvar (e.g. r_renderer) round-tripping through config.cfg on all platforms, including web (persistence works since b64144479).

RELATED WORK:
- Epic uhexen2-vcif (web/PWA re-upstream; closed children include software renderer work).
- Master render refactor (find existing bead if one exists and link).

title: Write docs/web/ARCHITECTURE.md and SOFTWARE_RENDERER.md for our two-config web build

description:
From fork commit 9e53fb2: implement predictable iOS PWA startup/exit/upgrade lifecycle handling.

iOS Safari PWAs have unique lifecycle constraints (suspend on backgrounding, forced relaunches on upgrade, no persistent foreground). This work ensures Hexen II handles:
- Graceful suspend on app background (pause state)
- Correct reload on app relaunch
- Safe upgrade/install transitions (no state corruption)
- Audio/input state recovery

Improves iOS PWA UX and prevents crashes or lost game state on common iOS scenarios.

Depends on uhexen2-qukx (PWA foundation must exist first).

title: Mine alextnewman/hexenwail fork: PWA plumbing, web capabilities, and software renderer restoration
description:
## Why

The fork at https://github.com/alextnewman/hexenwail (branched from our master circa 2026-06-23, last shared commit dded98d) has pivoted to an Emscripten-only web/PWA build of Hexen II. It contains web-port capabilities and a restored classic software renderer (8bpp) that the user wants ported back into Hexenwail for live archival — keeping the original rasterizer alive and runnable alongside GL 4.3, not just in git history.

## Mining targets (from fork commit history, newest first)

- **08166a8** (Aug 18): Place the HUD and menu 2D canvases instead of ignoring them
- **0b1906a** (Aug 18): WEB_RENDERER=software|webgl2 build-time selector (software default). Restores uHexen2's 8bpp software rasterizer verbatim with WebGL2 palette-LUT blit display. New files: draw_soft_web.c, vid_soft_web.c, soft_web.h; guard macros WEBSOFT/WEBQUAKE; CI builds both renderer configs to prevent rot.
- **9e53fb2** (Aug 8): Predictable iOS PWA startup/exit/upgrade lifecycle handling
- **ded4da2** (Aug 7): Portable PWA save bundles (export/import saves out of browser storage)
- **4116151** (Aug 7): Emscripten SDL3 build fix + PR-level PWA/WASM CI
- **25b134c** (Aug 7): PWA shell, offline service worker, ZIP game-data import, save-game persistence, GitHub Pages CI

## Constraints

- Fork is Emscripten-ONLY (CMake hard-fails on other toolchains, desktop builds deleted). Every piece must adapt to coexist with desktop nix builds and GL 4.3 pipeline.
- Software renderer must come back as a build/runtime option alongside GL 4.3 (never replacing), per Ironwail-parity direction. Their WebGL2 palette-LUT blit is the display model.
- Our existing WASM/WebGL2 build (shell-wasm.nix, working since 2026-03-26) is the base the PWA plumbing wraps.

## Epic: Child beads

This is an umbrella issue tracking the following work items:

1. uhexen2-a598 — Restore 8bpp software renderer as a co-existing renderer option
2. uhexen2-qukx — PWA shell with offline service worker + GitHub Pages deploy CI
3. uhexen2-zmct — ZIP game-data import for web build (depends on uhexen2-qukx)
4. uhexen2-sf6b — Save-game persistence + portable save bundles for web build (depends on uhexen2-qukx)
5. uhexen2-9qk5 — iOS PWA lifecycle handling (depends on uhexen2-qukx)
6. uhexen2-yi47 — Emscripten SDL3 build fix + PR-level WASM CI
7. uhexen2-fr2v — Place HUD and menu 2D canvases in web build

Definition of done for epic: All child beads closed. Software renderer and PWA plumbing coexist with desktop GL 4.3 build. CI tests both.

title: Hashes written into beads at close time are systematically stale — the beads-squash rebase rewrites them
description:
Found while closing uhexen2-rp1z, whose notes recorded the fix as 92e6ee3bb -- a hash not in master.  The survivor is 40d7bb04f.  uhexen2-nkj1 needed the identical correction on 2026-08-19.  Two hand corrections for the same cause is a pattern, so this is the pattern's bead.

## It is not bad luck, it is the workflow

The house style is: commit the code, then commit the beads update that documents it, then later squash the beads commit back into the code commit.  Squashing B into A replaces A with a NEW commit and a new hash.  The bead's close reason was written between those steps, so it names A's pre-squash hash -- which the squash then destroys.

Any hash written into a bead before its beads commit is squashed is therefore GUARANTEED stale, not occasionally stale.  That matches what the sweep found: the failures cluster exactly on commits that had a beads commit folded into them.

DEMONSTRATED LIVE THIS SESSION, which is the strongest evidence available.  The lint fix for uhexen2-5zei was committed as 7e43e8ea0, that hash was written into two beads, and by the next audit run it had become 73a9c74c5.  Minutes.  The tool caught its own author.

Note there is no hook doing this -- .git/hooks has nothing that rebases.  It is done by hand or by a concurrent session (one committed 'warp: put speed and throw knobs on the liquid surface warp' into this working tree mid-session), which is why it cannot be fixed by editing a hook.

## The sweep

tools/bd_hash_audit.py, added as 382f6f7af, over all 917 records:

    311  reachable from HEAD -- fine
     48  REWRITTEN: object exists, master has the same subject under a new hash
      9  DANGLING: on no ref, no surviving subject.  These were beads-ONLY
         commits squashed into a code commit -- no single hash replaces them
     26  ARCHIVED: not in master but on another ref, e.g. archive/26.03-alpha.7i.
         Legitimate; uhexen2-ntb9 cites one on purpose.  Reported separately so
         a sweep does not 'correct' a deliberate reference

Seven of the bad ones were cited by OPEN beads, i.e. by work someone would act on.  All seven are now annotated with their survivor or with why none exists.

## Options

1. GATE IT.  Run tools/bd_hash_audit.py at session close, next to the existing push checklist.  It exits 1 only when an OPEN bead cites an unacknowledged bad hash, so it stays quiet in the normal case.  Cheapest, and catches the error in the session that made it, while the author still remembers which commit was meant.

2. STOP RECORDING RAW HASHES.  Cite the subject line plus the bead id, both of which survive a rebase, and let the reader run git log --grep.  Removes the failure mode rather than detecting it.  Costs the convenience of a copy-pasteable hash.

3. SQUASH FIRST, CLOSE SECOND.  Fold the beads commit before writing the close reason, so the hash recorded is the final one.  Correct but relies on discipline at exactly the moment attention is lowest, which is how this got to 57.

Recommendation: 1 and 2 together -- 2 for new prose, 1 as the backstop.  3 is what should already have been happening and demonstrably is not.

## Note for whoever takes this

The 48 rewritten hashes cited only by CLOSED beads were left alone deliberately: the mapping is mechanical (tools/bd_hash_audit.py --all prints old -> new for every one) but rewriting closed history in bulk is churn with no reader.  Fix them if a closed bead is ever reopened.

title: Water surface warp is too fast/strong: add gl_waterwarp_speed and gl_waterwarp_amount
description:
Bob asked for the liquid surface warp to be slowed down and made less aggressive. Vanilla Hexen II hardcodes it: EmitWaterPolys (gl_warp.c) scrolls the texcoord turb at realtime with the full turbsin throw, the Z ripple beside it uses gl_waterripple at realtime, and DrawGLWaterPoly / DrawGLWaterPolyMTexLM (gl_rsurf.c) wobble underwater walls by 8 units at realtime. On a large liquid surface at a modern framerate that reads as seasick.

Two archived cvars, both defaulting to 0.5 (half vanilla rate, half vanilla throw), clamped 0..4 in one shared place (R_WaterWarpSpeed / R_WaterWarpAmount in gl_warp.c) so all three warp sites agree:
- gl_waterwarp_speed  — time multiplier
- gl_waterwarp_amount — displacement multiplier, also scales gl_waterripple

Set both to 1 for the vanilla warp. Distinct from r_waterwarp, which is the fullscreen distortion while submerged.

Clamped at 4 because past roughly vanilla speed the texcoords step more than one turbsin entry per frame and the warp aliases into noise rather than looking faster.

Open question for Bob: the Faithful and Authentic presets aim at vanilla accuracy and currently inherit the new softer defaults. Should they pin both to 1?
notes:
Menu slider added in 127f6f269: Rendering submenu, new 'Liquid Warp' row directly under 'Water Warp', driving gl_waterwarp_amount. Drawn as a percentage of the vanilla throw (50% = shipped default, 100% = stock Hexen II, 0 = 'Off'), stepping 0.1, capped at 200% in the UI while the console still reaches the engine clamp of 4.

Named 'Liquid Warp' rather than folding into the 'Water Warp' row above it, because that row toggles r_waterwarp (the fullscreen distortion while submerged) and sharing a label would imply the two are one effect.

gl_waterwarp_speed deliberately left console-only — strength is the knob people reach for, and a second slider would grow an already long submenu for a rarer want.

Still open: (1) are 0.5/0.5 the right shipped defaults, needs Bob's eye on a real liquid surface; (2) should the Faithful and Authentic presets pin both to 1 for vanilla accuracy?

title: [bug] Distant foliage sparkles: gl_texturemode GL_NEAREST disables mipmapped minification entirely
description:
Symptom: crowns of distant obj_pine_tree models in SoT mill.bsp carry isolated bright neutral-grey specks (~(70,70,70) against a warm local mean of ~19). Reported as 'white tipped trees', capture_white_tipped_trees.rdc.

Cause: gl_texmodes[0] (gl_draw.c:436) is { GL_NEAREST, GL_NEAREST } — the minification filter has no mipmap component, so the uploaded mip chain is never sampled. Every screen pixel point-samples one texel of a heavily minified skin, and the skin's brightest texels (pine_1.tga highlights up to (175,151,139), neutral greys to (139,139,139)) alias into sparkles concentrated on the dense minified crowns. r_scale 4 (scene FBO 640x360 upscaled 4x) multiplies each speck into a 4x4 block, and the r_softemu 1 palette pass quantizes them to neutral grey.

Measured on models/pine_1.tga at 8x minification: point sampling leaves 2.55% of visible pixels with all channels >=100, vs 0.37% box-filtered — a ~7x speckle density difference.

Ironwail's equivalent 'classic' preset is GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR, not plain GL_NEAREST: same crunchy magnification, mipmapped minification. Options: (a) point the menu's nearest/classic preset at gl_texmodes[2], (b) drop plain GL_NEAREST from the selectable list, (c) leave it and document. Confirm first by setting gl_texturemode GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR in the same spot and re-checking the crowns.

Related: uhexen2-nkj1 (flood fix, separate latent hazard on the same assets).
close_reason:
Fixed in 80c8293ce. gl_texturemode GL_NEAREST now resolves to GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR in Draw_TextureMode_f with a one-line notice; magnification is GL_NEAREST in both, so only minification changes and the pixelated look is preserved. Redirect rather than reject keeps old configs loading, and the resolved name is written back to the cvar so a config carrying GL_NEAREST heals on the next write (the reporter's ~/.hexen2/sot/config.cfg is one).

Checked while fixing: the menu path was already correct — the Rendering submenu's Classic/Smooth toggle sets GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR (gl_vidsdl.c:2593), and no display preset selects gl_texmodes[0]. Only a hand-set cvar could reach it.

Left deliberately alone: presets Crunchy/Retro/Authentic/Faithful set GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST (menu.c:2302/2323/2344/2365), which does mipmap — one level, no cross-level blend — so they do not sparkle. Moving them to GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR is an art-direction call, not a bug fix, and would also collapse the Faithful/Clean distinction that M_Display_DetectPreset keys on (gl_filter_idx <= 1 vs == 2, menu.c:2255-2258). File separately if wanted.

title: GL_Upload32 alpha bleed reached only 1 texel: donors are alpha==255, flooded texels keep alpha 0
description:
Follow-up defect in the uhexen2-pcd1 bleed. GL_Upload32 ran 'for (pass = 0; pass < 4; pass++)' over the RGBA buffer, but the donor test inside accepted only neighbours with alpha==255, and a texel the flood fills keeps alpha 0 forever. So a filled texel never became a donor and passes 2-4 recomputed the identical one-texel ring — effective reach was 1 texel, exactly the 'one pass only bleeds 1 pixel out' failure pcd1's own description warned about.

Why it matters: the Hexen II palette's transparent index 255 is (252,252,252) — white — so unreached transparent texels carry white RGB, and any filtering that samples across a cutout boundary (mip levels >= 1, anisotropic taps) mixes that white into surviving alpha-tested pixels. Measured on SoT models/pine_1.tga: 39286 near-white transparent texels survived the old flood (42.5% of all transparent texels); 5640 of them sit 2-8 texels from visible art, i.e. inside the band mip levels 1-3 sample. A scan of sot/models and sot/textures found 39 assets with white in that band (worst: stltng2_0.tga 83739 texels, {CurtWind1512.tga 8698, {moss1U.tga 8332, deadtree_0.tga 7666, pine_2.tga 5791).

Found while evaluating capture_white_tipped_trees.rdc (SoT mill.bsp, AMD RX 7700 XT / Mesa 26.1.5).
notes: Correction to the close reason: your rebase rewrote the fix commit, it is now 36a0f50ac (was be50834b0), already on hexenwail/master. The follow-up for the sparkle itself is uhexen2-kl6w (closed, 80c8293ce) — the 'nkj2 if filed' placeholder in the close reason was never used.
close_reason: Fixed in be50834b0. Replaced the 4-pass loop in GL_Upload32 with a two-pass city-block distance transform (forward scan propagates the nearest donor down/right, backward scan up/left): exact 4-neighbour L1 nearest opaque texel, O(w*h), one uint16 per texel of transient hunk space. Fractional-alpha texels are visible so they neither donate nor receive; they act as walls and the flood routes around them. Verified against SoT models/pine_1.tga: near-white transparent texels after the flood went 39286 -> 0. nix build clean; texbuf_bleed present in result/bin/glhexen2. Note: does not by itself change the sparkling pine crowns in capture_white_tipped_trees.rdc — under gl_texturemode GL_NEAREST no mip level is sampled, so that symptom is point-sample aliasing (see uhexen2-nkj2 if filed).

title: Move shaders out of C string literals into files with an offline SPIR-V build step
description:
Shader sources are currently inline C string literals in engine/h2shared/gl_shader.c and gl_postprocess.c, duplicated across two dialects (#version 430 core x7 and #version 300 es x4). Move them to real .vert/.frag/.comp files with shared .inc includes, and add a build rule that compiles them to SPIR-V offline.

This is a HARD BLOCKER for the SDL_GPU backend, not just hygiene: SDL_GPU accepts SPIR-V, DXBC, DXIL, MSL and metallib -- it does NOT accept GLSL. Whatever the backend consumes has to be produced at build time.

Current inline shader entry points in gl_shader.c: s2d_vert, sflat_vert, sworld_vert, salias_vert, sskeletal_vert, spart_vert, spart_gpu_vert, salias_inst_vert, ssky_vert (plus matching fragment sources), and gl_postprocess.c carries its own PP_CompileShader/PP_InitShader/OIT_InitShader set.

Standalone value even without the backend: kills the 430-core / 300-es source duplication that currently spans 12 files and ~77 USE_GLES divergence sites, and makes shader errors point at a real file and line instead of a C string offset.
design:
Layout follows vkQuake's Shaders/ directory, which is GPL-2.0 like uHexen2 and therefore directly liftable as a pattern (and in places as code): per-stage source files plus shared .inc includes (their world_common.inc / alias_common.inc / globals.inc), compiled with glslangValidator, embedded as C byte arrays via their bintoc.c. Their wboit.inc / mboit.inc / wboit_resolve.frag / mboit_resolve.frag are worth reading against our existing OIT path.

Build integration: add the compile step to CMakeLists.txt with glslangValidator from nixpkgs so the nix build stays self-contained. Keep the GL path consuming GLSL text (GL 4.3 can also consume SPIR-V, but there is no reason to force that) and have the SDL_GPU path consume the generated SPIR-V, so both backends share one source of truth.

Depends on the UBO and texture-binding work: SDL_GPU is strict about resource/register layout -- SDL_gpu.h calls this out explicitly as the most common cause of a non-working shader, and directs you to SDL_CreateGPUShader / SDL_CreateGPUComputePipeline for the expected layout. Authoring the shaders with explicit set/binding qualifiers only makes sense once the uniform blocks and descriptor slots are settled, otherwise the layout gets rewritten twice.

For D3D12 and Metal targets, SPIR-V is translated offline with SDL_shadercross. Not required for a Vulkan-only first cut; sequence it after the backend works.

Done when: no shader source remains as a C string literal, the 430/300-es duplication is expressed as shared includes plus a version header, the nix build compiles shaders to SPIR-V as part of the normal build, and both the desktop GL and Emscripten GLES builds still run.

title: Route texture binding through a descriptor-set-shaped call
description:
Replace the individual glActiveTexture + glBindTexture pairs with a batched bind that matches how SDL_GPU (and Vulkan) hand textures to a draw. Pure GL refactor, ships independently.

Measured surface:
  92  glActiveTexture
  73  glBindTexture
 158  glTexParameterf   (sampler state -- becomes immutable sampler objects)
   9  glTexParameteri

SDL_GPU binds textures and samplers as arrays per shader stage (SDL_BindGPUVertexSamplers / SDL_BindGPUFragmentSamplers) with sampler state living in a separate immutable SDL_GPUSampler object, not as per-texture mutable parameters. The 158 glTexParameterf calls are the GL idiom that has no direct equivalent and needs to become a small set of pre-created sampler objects.
design:
Two parts:

1. R_BindTextures(stage, first_slot, count, const rtexture_t **) replacing the activetexture+bindtexture pairs. Slots are already effectively fixed by convention (unit 0 diffuse, unit 1 lightmap / soft-depth, unit 2 fullbright mask -- see u_texture0..2 and gl_null_fb_texture in gl_shader.h), so the slot model is already descriptor-shaped in spirit.

2. Hoist sampler state out of the textures. Enumerate the distinct filter/wrap/anisotropy combinations actually in use across gl_texmgr.c and gl_draw.c and pre-create one sampler object per combination, rather than calling glTexParameterf at bind time. This is where most of the 158 calls go.

Note the existing 1x1 sentinel textures (gl_null_fb_texture, gl_solid_white_texture) -- these exist specifically so shaders can sample unconditionally instead of branching. That pattern is MORE important under SDL_GPU, which is strict about a shader's declared resource count matching what is bound. Keep them.

Blocks the shader/SPIR-V work: SDL_GPU has strict descriptor set numbering conventions that the shader source must be authored against, so the binding model must be settled first.

Done when: no glActiveTexture/glBindTexture pair outside the binding module, sampler state is object-based rather than per-bind, nix build clean, no visual regression.
notes:
HALF LANDED on branch bead/p4ln-1-rpipeline, commit subject 'render: bind textures as a slot range instead of moving a cursor'.

DONE -- the binding half
engine/h2shared/gl_texbind.{c,h}.  Every glActiveTexture+glBindTexture pair (69
activates, 67 binds, nine files) is now R_BindTextures / R_BindTextureSlot /
R_BindTextureTarget, which take the slot as an argument.  The module shadows
every (unit, target) pair.  glDeleteTextures goes through R_DeleteTextures,
which resets the shadow -- not optional, since GL recycles names and a stale
shadow would fold away the bind that makes a newly created texture current.

INVARIANT worth knowing before touching it: every entry point leaves texture
unit 0 active, because 158 glTexParameter calls operate on whatever is bound to
the active unit.  The old code did this by hand with a defensive
glActiveTexture(GL_TEXTURE0) before most binds plus vestigial ones from the
fixed-function era; those are gone, along with GL_EnableMultitexture /
GL_DisableMultitexture.

TWO LATENT BUGS FIXED ON THE WAY.  The old currenttexture global tracked unit 0
but GL_Bind was called from blocks that had made unit 1 active, so it could (a)
bind the lightmap to the wrong unit while recording it under the other, and (b)
worse, cache-HIT and skip the bind entirely when unit 0 already held that
texture, leaving unit 1 with whatever it had.  Both lightmap sites and both sky
paths were exposed.  They are explicit R_BindTextureSlot(1, ...) calls now.

NOT DONE -- the sampler half, which is the larger one
Sampler state is still per-texture mutable glTexParameter: 158 calls, most of
them gl_draw.c setting CLAMP_TO_EDGE before a 2D draw and REPEAT after, plus the
gl_texturemode callback walking every texture to re-apply filters.

WHY IT WAS NOT STARTED RATHER THAN HALF-DONE: a GL sampler object fully
overrides the texture object's own parameters for whichever unit it is bound to.
That makes it all-or-nothing per unit -- you cannot bind samplers for some
textures and inherit for others on the same unit -- so doing it properly means
moving gl_texmgr.c from 'the texture remembers its filter' to 'the sampler is
chosen at bind time', which means a sampler descriptor per gltexture_t and a
bind path that carries it.  Sketch that survives contact with the seam that now
exists:
  - add a sampler index to gltexture_t, derived from TEXPREF_* + gl_filter_idx
    + anisotropy;
  - pre-create the distinct combinations as GL sampler objects at init;
  - R_BindTextures binds texture and sampler together, passing 0 for the
    textures with no gltextures[] entry (FBO attachments, lightmap atlas, the
    1x1 sentinels) so they keep using their own parameters;
  - the per-draw CLAMP/REPEAT churn in gl_draw.c becomes an explicit
    bind-with-clamp variant rather than two glTexParameter calls around a draw;
  - the gl_texturemode callback then re-derives indices instead of touching GL
    at all, which is a win on its own.
Note the 1x1 sentinels (gl_null_fb_texture, gl_solid_white_texture) must stay --
SDL_GPU is strict about a shader's declared resource count matching what is
bound, so unconditional sampling matters more there, not less.

NO VISUAL REGRESSION SWEEP HAS BEEN RUN.

is superseded.

  - R_BindProgramBlocks's GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_DATA_SIZE check does NOT fire, so

  - GL debug output is enabled and emits nothing for a whole session.

NOT COVERED: OIT translucency was only shown to compile and link, not to

which is the path R_PipelineResetState / R_Uniforms_Init / R_TexBind_Init exist
to survive.  Both are cheap to add to the same harness.

THE SAMPLER HALF IS DONE.  Branch bead/p4ln-2-ppblocks, commit subject 'render:
move texture filter and wrap into sampler objects'.  The 'NOT DONE -- the
sampler half, which is the larger one' section above is superseded; the sketch

WHAT LANDED, against that sketch:
  - a sampler class per texture, derived from TEX_NEAREST / TEX_LINEAR /

    GL_SetTextureFilter because it has to agree with its four branches;
  - the distinct combinations pre-created at init: five classes x two wraps,
    in gl_texbind.c;
  - R_BindTextureSlot binds texture and sampler together, with RS_INHERIT

  - the gl_draw.c CLAMP/REPEAT churn is now R_BindTextureSlotClamped;
  - the gl_texturemode / anisotropy / lodbias callbacks re-derive instead of

157 glTexParameter calls -> 119, and the ones that went were the per-frame ones.

THE LOOKUP QUESTION the sketch left open, answered: the whole engine binds by GL
NAME (GL_Bind is a macro for R_BindTextureSlot), not by gltexture_t*, so a
sampler index living in gltexture_t would not have been reachable at bind time.
It is a texnum-indexed side table in gl_texbind.c instead, filled in by the

THE ASYMMETRY THAT WAS A LATENT BUG: there were thirteen CLAMP sites and only

cannot arise -- but that also means this change is not a pure no-op for any draw
that was relying on a leftover clamp.  None was found; it is why the pixel
comparison below was worth doing rather than reasoning about.

PORTABILITY: GL_TEXTURE_LOD_BIAS was defined locally in gl_draw.c, so the
desktop build was happy and mingw was not.  Moved to glheader.h.  This is the
second time in this bead's history that building only the default package hid a
tier break -- build .#win64 and .#wasm.

VERIFICATION, and the method matters because a console-log diff cannot see a
filtering regression:
  - The LOADING SCREEN is drawn entirely through the 2D pic path this change
    touches and is completely static, which makes it the cleanest test
    available: pixel-identical to the base build, zero differing pixels over
    the full frame.
  - In-game on demo1, screenshotting across gl_texturemode, anisotropy and
    lodbias changes so the reconfigure path runs and not just startup: all

    69 against 73 -- the two runs paused at different game times.

  1. `wait` in a config is consumed during level load.  30 waits after `map`
     leaves you screenshotting the loading plaque, and every frame compares
     equal because it is the same static screen.  400 waits gets you in-game.
     ALWAYS include a check that the thing under test actually moves the image
     -- the first run of this comparison could not have failed.

     if you want a static target.
