title: Replace loose glUniform* calls with std140 uniform blocks
description:
Collapse the per-draw uniform soup into a small number of std140 blocks (per-frame and per-draw). Pure GL refactor -- ships independently, and cuts real per-draw call overhead today.

Measured surface:
  92  glGetUniformLocation
  65  glUniform1f
  37  glUniform1i
  28  glUniform2f
  25  glUniform3f
  24  glUniformMatrix4fv
  ~8 each glUniform4f / glUniform3fv / glUniform4fv / glUniform2i

The glprogram_t struct in engine/h2shared/gl_shader.h is currently ~20 loose GLint location handles (u_mvp, u_texture0..2, u_color, u_fog_density, u_fog_color, u_alpha_threshold, u_modelview, u_time, u_skyfog, u_eyepos, u_wind, u_caustics, u_overbright, u_lightmap_bicubic, u_lightdebug, u_force_opaque_alpha, u_alias_caustics, u_alias_model, u_soft_depth, u_soft_params), plus gl_alias_inst_prog_t and gl_particle_gpu_prog_t variants.

Blocked by nothing; blocks the shader/SPIR-V work, because SDL_GPU freezes the uniform layout and its shaders must be authored against the final block layout.
design:
Split into two blocks:
  - per-frame: view/projection matrices, fog density + color, eye position, time, overbright, caustics params, lightdebug -- uploaded once per frame.
  - per-draw: model matrix, color, alpha threshold, force_opaque_alpha, soft-particle params -- the small values that change per batch.

glBindBufferBase is already in use for the SSBO paths, so the UBO plumbing is not new ground.

SDL_GPU constraint to design against now: its uniform push model (SDL_PushGPUVertexUniformData / SDL_PushGPUFragmentUniformData / SDL_PushGPUComputeUniformData) is for SMALL data. SDL_gpu.h states directly: 'Don't use uniform buffers for large amounts of data (more than a matrix or so). Use a storage buffer instead.' So keep the per-draw block genuinely small and push anything bulk through storage buffers -- which the engine already does for poses, instances and particles.

Watch the existing hazard documented in gl_shader.h: gl_shader_alias is shared by alias models, sprites, warp polys and unlit brush polys, which is why u_alias_caustics is deliberately NOT named u_caustics -- GL_ImmEnd pushes it as per-batch state and a shared name would clobber the per-frame world u_caustics that R_SetupFrame uploads. Preserve that separation when partitioning into blocks; per-batch values belong in the per-draw block, not the per-frame one.

Done when: glprogram_t no longer carries per-draw GLint locations, uniform uploads are block writes, nix build clean, no visual regression.
notes:
LANDED on branch bead/p4ln-1-rpipeline, commit subject 'render: move per-draw uniforms into two shared std140 blocks' (cite subjects, not hashes -- uhexen2-zq7w).

DONE
engine/h2shared/gl_uniforms.{c,h}.  Two blocks, PerFrame and PerDraw, shared by
every draw program.  glprogram_t is down from twenty loose GLint locations to
four sampler bindings; gl_alias_inst_prog_t and gl_particle_gpu_prog_t lost
theirs entirely.  The per-shader uniform cache in gl_vbo.c is gone -- it existed
only because loose uniforms are per-program state.

THE SAFETY ARGUMENT, because this is the change that goes silently wrong.
Every block member is vec4, mat4 or ivec4.  std140 padding is the failure mode
here (a float followed by a vec3 does not land where a naive C struct puts it,
and it compiles clean), and a layout with no under-aligned members has no
padding to get wrong.  Two COMPILE_TIME_ASSERTs pin the mirror sizes;
R_BindProgramBlocks queries GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_DATA_SIZE once and prints a warning
on disagreement.  Do not add a float or a vec3 member.

Draws go through R_DrawArrays / R_DrawElements / R_DrawElementsInstanced /
R_DrawElementsIndirect / R_MultiDrawElementsIndirect (gl_pipeline.c), which
flush the dirty blocks first.  26 sites.  A missed flush would draw a batch with
the previous batch's matrices, so it is deliberately impossible to forget.

TWO BEHAVIOUR CHANGES, both forced by the blocks being shared:
 1. The overbright multiplier is the r_fullbright-gated expression everywhere
    now.  Three sites used the ungated form; with one shared value they cannot
    disagree, and the gated one is what uhexen2-isq7 established.
 2. The instanced alias fullbright pass restores the fog colour after forcing it
    black.  Black fog is needed there (the pass blends ONE,ONE) but it used to
    be scoped to that program's own uniform and now is not.

NOT DONE
gl_postprocess.c (49 glUniform calls) and gl_worldcull.c (24) still use loose
uniforms on their own programs.  Deliberate: they are pass-level and per-dispatch
rather than per-draw, and glprogram_t -- what this bead's done-when names -- does
not cover them.  BUT SEE uhexen2-p4ln.5: Vulkan forbids default-block uniforms
outright, so those two files need their own blocks before either can produce
usable SPIR-V.  That is now the concrete next step, not a nicety.

NO VISUAL REGRESSION SWEEP HAS BEEN RUN.  Desktop and win64 builds clean; the
WASM build compiles every object under -DUSE_GLES=1 and fails only at link for
the sandbox-networking reason in uhexen2-1z31.  All shaders were compiled in
both dialects with glslangValidator before this landed.

VISUAL REGRESSION SWEEP: RUN, AND CLEAN.  The earlier note saying it had not been
is superseded.

Method: tools/headless-drive.sh (Xvfb + xdotool + bwrap, llvmpipe) driving the
oldmission_paladin scenario, plus direct +map loads, against TWO engines -- the
branch tip and a build of 4dba6c593, the commit before any of this work -- with
the same basedir and scenario.  Screenshots compared with ImageMagick.

Maps: demo1 (through the menus, with god/notarget/impulse 9, item spawn and
pickup, expanded status bar, chase cam), romeric6, meso2, egypt5, and egypt4 --
the last chosen because it has the most liquid surfaces of any stock map (274
turb faces), so the lava columns are in frame.

Result: every difference between the two engines is a time-varying element and
nothing else.  Sky (scrolls on cl.time), flame and lava animation frames, the
player model's idle pose, animated pickups, and the HUD health counter.  All
world geometry, lightmaps, textures, fullbright layers, the viewmodel, the
status bar and the inventory grid are PIXEL-IDENTICAL.  RMSE 0.9%-2.8%, all of
it accounted for by those regions.

Startup log evidence, on top of the pixels:
  - all sixteen draw programs link, including world_oit / alias_oit /
    particle_oit and alias_instanced;
  - R_BindProgramBlocks's GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_DATA_SIZE check does NOT fire, so
    Mesa's std140 layout matches the C mirror in gl_uniforms.h exactly;
  - GL debug output is enabled and emits nothing for a whole session.

NOT COVERED: OIT translucency was only shown to compile and link, not to
composite -- no translucent geometry was put in frame.  Nor was a vid_restart,
which is the path R_PipelineResetState / R_Uniforms_Init / R_TexBind_Init exist
to survive.  Both are cheap to add to the same harness.

EXTENDED INTO gl_postprocess.c AND gl_worldcull.c, on branch bead/p4ln-2-ppblocks,
commit subject 'render: move the post-process and compute uniforms into std140
blocks'.

This was sequenced here rather than under p4ln.4 because p4ln.4's own notes
identified it as the real blocker: those thirteen sources declared their
uniforms in the default block, and Vulkan forbids non-opaque uniforms there
outright, so extracting them to files first would have produced files that
still could not become SPIR-V.

Five new blocks: PPParams and PPPalette (composite), BloomParams (shared by
the three bloom programs), CullParams (shared by the clear and mark compute
passes), HizParams (shared by the two Hi-Z passes).

THE BINDING REGISTRY IS THE PART TO KNOW ABOUT.  A uniform buffer binding
point is GLOBAL state, not per-program, so the RU_BINDING_* list in
gl_uniforms.h is now the single place numbers are allocated -- 0..6 today.
Two blocks drawing the same number is a silent bug: the second
glBindBufferBase wins and the first block reads the wrong buffer with no
error anywhere.  Add to the list, do not invent a number locally.

R_BindProgramBlock (gl_uniforms.c) is the new general form of what
R_BindProgramBlocks did for the two draw blocks: bind one named block and
query GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_DATA_SIZE back to check the C mirror.

MILESTONE: the only glUniform* call left anywhere in the engine is
glUniform1i binding a sampler to a texture unit.  Grep-checkable:

    grep -rn 'glUniform[A-Za-z0-9]*_fp *(' engine/hexen2/*.c engine/h2shared/*.c

returns only glUniform1i sampler binds, glUniformBlockBinding, and the
SDL_GL_GetProcAddress loaders in gl_vidsdl.c.  Those loaders are now dead
weight for every entry point except glUniform1i -- glUniform1f is still named
in the capability gate at gl_vidsdl.c:841, which is why they were left alone
rather than removed in the same commit.

TWO BEHAVIOUR NOTES for whoever reads the diff and wonders:

1. pp_params is a persistent static, deliberately.  Loose uniforms were
   per-PROGRAM state, so a field one draw path set and another never touched
   kept its value -- PP_BlitWith3DEffects inherits the bloom strength from
   the last GL_PostProcess_EndFrame and never set it itself.  A zeroed local
   would have quietly changed what that path renders.

2. The softemu palette stopped being rebuilt and re-uploaded on every
   composite.  It is the game palette, so it is compared against a cached
   copy and uploaded only on change: 1 KB of memcmp instead of 4 KB of bus
   traffic per frame.

VERIFICATION: tools/glsl_check_inline.py is new, because none of this is
covered by a build -- a build does not compile GLSL, and glsl_check.py only
knows about engine/shaders/*.glsl.  It hands the real .c files to the real C
preprocessor, extracts the string literals, and compiles all thirteen through
both GL dialects plus the six vertex/fragment links.  32 compiles, 0 failures.
Delete it when p4ln.4 finishes the extraction.

Built default, win64 and wasm.  wasm still stops at link on uhexen2-1z31 but
compiles every object first, which is the ES-tier coverage that matters --
that is the lesson from p4ln.1's first commit and it was followed here.

NO RUNTIME SWEEP HAS BEEN RUN.  The layouts are proven against glslang and
against the C mirrors, not against a driver or a frame.  The engine's own
GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_DATA_SIZE check in R_BindProgramBlock would report a
mismatch on the console at startup, so booting once is a cheap first test.

RUNTIME VERIFICATION: RUN, AND CLEAN.  The 'NO RUNTIME SWEEP HAS BEEN RUN' note
above is superseded.

This was on the REAL GPU, not llvmpipe -- SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen still gets
the AMD driver here, which is worth knowing for future headless work because it
is both faster and a far better test than the software rasteriser:

    GL_RENDERER: AMD Radeon Graphics (radeonsi, renoir, ACO, DRM 3.64, 6.18.43)
    GL_VERSION:  4.6 (Compatibility Profile) Mesa 26.1.5

Method: two engines, this branch and a build of 8318dabac (the branch parent),
same basedir, same command line, demo1, with every path the change touches
forced on:

    +gl_hiz_cull 1 +gl_hiz_stats 20 +r_bloom 1 +r_oit 1 +r_softemu 1
    +gl_fxaa 1 +r_hdr 1 +map demo1

WHAT IT PROVES.  gl_hiz_stats reads the cull compute shader's own counters
back, so it is a direct functional test of the CullParams block rather than a
proxy.  Both engines print, every frame, byte for byte:

    hiz_stats: total=5041 pvs=4453 flags=18 frust=141 hiz=0 accepted=324 dedup=105

  - total=5041 is exactly the marksurf count reported at map load, so
    u_num_marksurfs (u_culli0.y) lands where the shader reads it;
  - frust=141 is non-zero, which is the one that matters most: the frustum is
    a vec4[4] and an array stride or base-offset error in std140 is precisely
    the bug that compiles clean and renders wrong.  Wrong planes reject either
    nothing or everything, not 141;
  - dedup=105 exercises u_framecount (u_culli0.x);
  - the buckets sum: 4453 + 18 + 141 + 105 + 324 = 5041.

hiz=0 is NOT a regression -- the base build reports the same 0 from a standing
start on demo1.

Normalising both console logs (timestamps, absolute paths and the IMG: texture
replacement spam removed) and diffing them gives NO differences across all 923
shared lines.  The only divergence is that the branch run got through more
frames in its 45 seconds, so it repeated the identical stats line more times.

Startup evidence on top of that, both engines identical:
  - all thirteen draw programs link, including world_oit / alias_oit /
    particle_oit and alias_instanced;
  - 'PostProcess: gamma/contrast shader ready' and 'OIT: resolve shader OK',
    so the composite, the three bloom programs and both OIT resolves all
    compiled and linked against the new blocks;
  - R_BindProgramBlock's GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_DATA_SIZE check does NOT fire for
    PPParams, PPPalette, BloomParams, CullParams or HizParams, so Mesa's
    std140 layout agrees with every C mirror;
  - GL debug output is enabled and emits nothing for the whole session.

NOT COVERED, still: no screenshot comparison, so this shows the uniforms
arrive and the culling decisions are unchanged, not that every pixel of the
composite is unchanged.  Softemu, bloom, FXAA and HDR were switched on and
drew without a GL error, which is weaker than a pixel diff.  And no
vid_restart, which is the path PP_InitUniformBlocks / PP_ShutdownUniformBlocks
exist to survive.

TWO TRAPS FOR THE NEXT HEADLESS RUN HERE, both of which cost time today:
  1. The userdir is ~/.hexen2 regardless of $HOME, so qconsole.log lands there
     and the engine REWRITES ~/.hexen2/data1/config.cfg on quit.  Back that up
     before a scripted run with cvars in it, or you will silently change the
     developer's own settings.
  2. '+exec ./foo.cfg' cannot work -- the config has to be inside a gamedir
     the filesystem layer knows about.  Prefer '+cvar value' on the command
     line, which needs no file at all.

title: Collapse scattered GL state into explicit pipeline objects (rpipeline_t)
description:
Replace the scattered set-state-then-draw calls with an immutable pipeline-state struct created up front and bound through a single entry point. This is the single largest de-risking step for a second backend, and it is a pure GL refactor -- no SDL_GPU code required, ships and is testable on its own.

Measured state surface to fold in (engine/h2shared/*.c + engine/hexen2/*.c, all via *_fp):
  80  glEnable / glDisable
  46  glDepthMask
  29  glBlendFunc
   9  glPolygonOffset
   8  glDepthFunc
   8  glDepthRange
   7  glBlendFunci
   6  glCullFace
   4  glStencilFunc / 4 glStencilOp
   3  glColorMask
  70  glUseProgram

Distinct blend funcs actually used (only 4):
  22x (SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA)
   5x (ONE, ONE)
   1x (ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, SRC_ALPHA)
   1x (DST_COLOR, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA)

Distinct enable/disable targets actually used (only 6 real ones):
  BLEND (47 dis / 33 en), DEPTH_TEST (8/7), CULL_FACE (7/4),
  SAMPLE_ALPHA_TO_COVERAGE (6/5), POLYGON_OFFSET_FILL (5/5), STENCIL_TEST (3/3)
  (plus MULTISAMPLE_ARB and the two DEBUG_OUTPUT toggles, which are init-time, not per-draw)

So the pipeline permutation count is roughly 30-60, not hundreds. That is small enough to enumerate statically rather than hash-and-cache.
design:
Introduce rpipeline_t bundling: program handle, blend enable + src/dst factors (per color target, so the OIT MRT case with its 7 glBlendFunci sites is expressible), depth test enable, depth write mask, depth compare func, cull mode, polygon offset enable + factor/units, color write mask, stencil state, alpha-to-coverage enable.

Then a single R_BindPipeline(const rpipeline_t *) replaces the glEnable/glDepthMask/glBlendFunc/glUseProgram clusters at each draw site. The GL implementation keeps a shadow of currently-bound state and skips redundant calls -- that alone is a measurable GL win given 80 enable/disable and 46 depth-mask calls per frame's worth of draw sites.

Order the work by call density: gl_postprocess.c (434 GL calls) and gl_rsurf.c (249) / gl_rmain.c (224) first.

Care needed around gl_postprocess.c: it owns the FBO/pass graph (scene FBO, bloom FBOs, OIT accum/revealage via OIT_BeginTranslucency/OIT_EndTranslucency, soft-depth capture via GL_SoftDepth_Capture, native FBO) and mixes per-pass state with per-draw state. Keep that separation explicit -- pass-level state becomes render-pass/target config later, draw-level state becomes the pipeline.

Done when: no glEnable/glDisable/glDepthMask/glBlendFunc/glBlendFunci/glDepthFunc/glCullFace/glColorMask/glPolygonOffset/glStencil* call remains outside the pipeline module and one-time init in gl_vidsdl.c; nix build clean; no visual regression on a map sweep covering OIT translucency, sky, liquids and alias models.
notes:
LANDED (bead/p4ln-1-rpipeline, commit subject 'render: route every draw-state change through one pipeline module' -- cite the subject, not a hash, see uhexen2-zq7w).

WHAT IS DONE
engine/h2shared/gl_pipeline.{c,h}.  311 raw state calls across 14 files now go
through R_Set* / R_UseProgram, which shadow the current state and drop any call
that would not change it.  The invariant is grep-checkable:

    grep -rnE 'gl(Enable|Disable|DepthMask|BlendFunc|BlendFunci|DepthFunc|DepthRange|CullFace|PolygonOffset|StencilFunc|StencilOp|ColorMask|UseProgram)_fp *\(' engine/hexen2/*.c engine/h2shared/*.c | grep -v gl_pipeline.c

should return exactly 8 lines: 3 init-time toggles in gl_vidsdl.c for state the
module does not track (GL_MULTISAMPLE_ARB, GL_DEBUG_OUTPUT*), and 5 lines of
#if 0 fixed-function zfix leftovers that do not compile.

THE ONE TRAP, for whoever touches this next.  A redundancy filter is not
transparent.  GL_ImmEnd (gl_vbo.c) deliberately re-issues the WBOIT glBlendFunci
pair before every draw inside the OIT pass, because enabling GL_BLEND resets
per-draw-buffer blend funcs to the global pair on some drivers and the revealage
buffer dies silently.  That is exactly the call shape a filter eats.  R_SetBlend
models the quirk instead: when it actually issues glEnable(GL_BLEND) it marks the
indexed funcs unknown.  Any future 'optimisation' that removes that marking
reintroduces the vanishing-translucency bug with no compile error.

Shadow staleness has two sources and both are handled: R_PipelineResetState
(GL_Init, so vid_restart is covered) forces GL to a known state and seeds from
it; R_PipelineForgetProgram covers GL reusing program names after a delete.

WHAT IS NOT DONE
1. rpipeline_t + R_BindPipeline exist but no draw site uses them.  Converting one
   means choosing an explicit depth-write value, and the depth mask is the single
   piece of state the scattered clusters leave implicit -- e.g.
   PP_BlitWith3DEffects disables the depth test and never touches the mask, so a
   bundle that specifies depth_write changes what the NEXT pass inherits.  That
   needs a look at a real frame, not a mechanical rewrite.  This is the remaining
   work on this bead.
2. NO VISUAL REGRESSION SWEEP HAS BEEN RUN.  nix build is clean and the rewrite
   is mechanical, but the done-when calls for a map sweep over OIT translucency,
   sky, liquids and alias models and that has not happened.  Do not close on the
   build alone.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FINISHING: it de-risks uhexen2-p4ln.5 (SDL_GPU backend) and
unblocks uhexen2-p4ln.3 (descriptor-shaped texture binding), both of which need
the state to be knowable in one place.

ADDENDUM, from the session that went on to land .2-.4.

THE FIRST COMMIT BROKE THE WASM BUILD AND THE CLAIM 'nix build clean' WAS TOO
NARROW.  R_SetPolygonOffsetLine named GL_POLYGON_OFFSET_LINE unconditionally;
the token does not exist on the ES tier, so every emscripten build failed to
compile gl_pipeline.c.  Only the default (desktop) package had been built.
Fixed in the commit 'render: move per-draw uniforms into two shared std140
blocks' -- the function is a no-op under USE_GLES, which is right, since its
only callers are #if 0 fixed-function leftovers.

LESSON FOR THE NEXT RENDERER CHANGE HERE: build .#win64 and .#wasm too, not just
the default.  The wasm build stops at link with a name-resolution failure
(uhexen2-1z31, no network in the sandbox) but it compiles every object first,
which is the ES-tier coverage that matters.

R_BindPipeline is still not bound at any draw site; see the note above for why.
Every draw does now go through the R_Draw* wrappers added in .2, so the
recording seam a second backend needs exists even though the state bundle is
not yet applied as a bundle.

VISUAL REGRESSION SWEEP: RUN, AND CLEAN.  The earlier note saying it had not been
is superseded.

Method: tools/headless-drive.sh (Xvfb + xdotool + bwrap, llvmpipe) driving the
oldmission_paladin scenario, plus direct +map loads, against TWO engines -- the
branch tip and a build of 4dba6c593, the commit before any of this work -- with
the same basedir and scenario.  Screenshots compared with ImageMagick.

Maps: demo1 (through the menus, with god/notarget/impulse 9, item spawn and
pickup, expanded status bar, chase cam), romeric6, meso2, egypt5, and egypt4 --
the last chosen because it has the most liquid surfaces of any stock map (274
turb faces), so the lava columns are in frame.

Result: every difference between the two engines is a time-varying element and
nothing else.  Sky (scrolls on cl.time), flame and lava animation frames, the
player model's idle pose, animated pickups, and the HUD health counter.  All
world geometry, lightmaps, textures, fullbright layers, the viewmodel, the
status bar and the inventory grid are PIXEL-IDENTICAL.  RMSE 0.9%-2.8%, all of
it accounted for by those regions.

Startup log evidence, on top of the pixels:
  - all sixteen draw programs link, including world_oit / alias_oit /
    particle_oit and alias_instanced;
  - R_BindProgramBlocks's GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_DATA_SIZE check does NOT fire, so
    Mesa's std140 layout matches the C mirror in gl_uniforms.h exactly;
  - GL debug output is enabled and emits nothing for a whole session.

NOT COVERED: OIT translucency was only shown to compile and link, not to
composite -- no translucent geometry was put in frame.  Nor was a vid_restart,
which is the path R_PipelineResetState / R_Uniforms_Init / R_TexBind_Init exist
to survive.  Both are cheap to add to the same harness.

'WHAT IS NOT DONE' ITEM 1 IS PART-DONE.  Branch bead/p4ln-2-ppblocks, commit
subject 'render: bind the first five draw sites through rpipeline_t'.  Five
sites now bind bundles; the note above saying no draw site uses R_BindPipeline
is superseded.

THE LOOK AT A REAL FRAME THAT THE NOTE ASKED FOR HAS BEEN TAKEN, and the method
is worth reusing rather than re-inventing.  Every R_Draw* was temporarily
instrumented to dump the whole state shadow plus __builtin_return_address(0),
behind an r_pipedump cvar.  One capture of demo1 with bloom, OIT, softemu, FXAA
and HDR forced on gave 4000 draws in 18 distinct (call site, state)
combinations.  Return addresses resolve against `nm` output once you subtract
the PIE slide -- dump the address of a known function in the same line and
subtract its link-time address, otherwise every caller symbolises as _fini.

WHAT THE FRAME SAID, which is the thing that was unknowable from the source:
  - depth mask is TRUE at every site but two (a flat-shaded additive
    GL_ImmEnd batch, and the OIT resolve).  The implicit value the clusters
    leave behind is almost always 'on';
  - depth compare is GEQUAL everywhere -- reversed-Z is live -- so depth_func
    must stay RP_KEEP_ENUM in every bundle and cannot be baked;
  - culling where enabled is FRONT, not BACK.

CONVERTED: R_DrawWorldCulled (1151 draws, and it previously set NO draw state
at all -- program only, everything else inherited from R_DrawWorld),
OIT_EndTranslucency, and the three bloom passes (two bundles, opaque and
additive).

THE BLOOM BUNDLES CARRY depth_write=true DELIBERATELY.  Nothing there writes
depth -- GL drops depth writes when the test is off -- but true is what those
draws measurably ran with, and R_BindPipeline sets the mask unconditionally.
Putting false there would leave the mask off behind the pass, which is exactly
the 'changes what the NEXT pass inherits' failure this bead's original note
warned about.  Do not 'correct' it.

VERIFICATION METHOD WORTH COPYING FOR THE NEXT CONVERSION: leave the
instrumentation in across the change and capture twice.  The full 4000-draw
SEQUENCE of states was identical before and after, not just the multiset --
which makes the conversion behaviour-preserving by measurement instead of by
argument.  The instrumentation is then reverted and not committed.

WHAT IS LEFT, and it is a different shape of problem: everything that draws
through GL_ImmEnd.  That is not one pipeline.  Its state is chosen by whichever
caller opened the batch, and the capture shows it drawing under six distinct
states (2D at prog 3, alias at 15, flat additive at 6 with the depth mask off,
sky at 24 both blended and not, and an alias batch with depth range 0.7..1).
Converting it means pushing the bundle up into its callers, which is a bigger
change than the five done here and wants its own pass.

Also still true: rpipeline_t has no stencil, polygon-offset or colour-mask
field, so the sky-stencil pass (colour mask 0000) cannot be expressed as a
bundle alone.  That is arguably right -- those read as pass state rather than
per-draw state -- but it is a decision the SDL_GPU work should confirm rather
than inherit silently.

title: Entities behind sky-windowed openings are z-rejected again (uhexen2-4h32 regressed by the ixdb fix)
description:
Reinstates uhexen2-4h32, which 95896e59c intentionally reverted.

## What broke, and why on purpose

4h32: the sky depth+stencil pre-pass in DrawTextureChains writes sky-surface depth,
so any entity drawn later at greater depth than a sky brush fails the depth test.
An enemy 'outside' a window/portal that maps to a sky brush is invisible -- you see
skybox where the monster should be. 4h32 fixed it by drawing the skybox with
glDepthMask(1) in the have_stencil branch of Sky_DrawSky: Sky_DrawSkyBox pins
glDepthRange(0,0), so writing depth stamps far-plane depth over the sky-wall depth
and later passes z-test against far.

ixdb: that same stamp is what un-hid geometry a modder had deliberately parked
behind a sky brush -- a standard visibility/perf trick. 95896e59c set the mask back
to 0, matching Ironwail/QuakeSpasm (sky SURFACES write depth, the skybox does not).
That is the right default -- it costs one map's window effect instead of sky
occlusion on every map -- but it does put 4h32's symptom back.

## The conflict

Both cannot hold with a single depth value at a sky pixel:
- 4h32 wants far-plane depth there, so entities beyond the sky wall still draw.
- ixdb wants sky-wall depth there, so geometry beyond it stays occluded.

## Directions worth trying

- Discriminate rather than flatten: an entity in a leaf that is actually visible
  through the opening should draw; geometry a mapper hid in a sealed void should
  not. The stencil buffer already marks genuine sky pixels, so the information to
  separate the two cases may be reachable without flattening depth for everyone.
- A cvar, if no principled discriminator falls out. Defaulting to the
  Ironwail/QuakeSpasm behaviour that 95896e59c restored.

## Before coding

Get a repro map for each side. 4h32 closed without one recorded, which is part of
why its fix traded away the general case; ixdb has capture_skybug.rdc. Both
behaviours need to be demonstrable before a fix can claim to satisfy them.

Read uhexen2-4h32 and uhexen2-ixdb together -- the comment in the have_stencil
branch of gl_sky.c names both so the mask does not get flipped back blind.

title: [bug] Translucent alias models write depth — overlapping mist instances punch hard-edged holes in each other
description:
RenderDoc capture capture_mist.rdc. Field report: mist renders 'clumpy' — hard-edged chunks instead of a soft overlapping cloud.

WHAT THE MIST ACTUALLY IS: not a sprite. It is an alias model (.mdl), 34 triangles, drawn 8 times per frame via the legacy immediate path — glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLES, count=102) on the alias program. Skin is a 256x128 grey cloud with BINARY alpha (only 0 and 255, 94.9% transparent) because sprite/model skins load with TEX_ALPHA|TEX_HOLEY index-255 keying. Texture extracted from the capture and visually confirmed to match the on-screen blob silhouette.

ROOT CAUSE: translucent alias models write depth.
- gl_rmain.c R_DrawTransEntitiesOnList: 'case mod_alias' unconditionally does glDepthMask(1) before R_DrawAliasModel. Only 'case mod_sprite' drops to glDepthMask(0).
- gl_rmain.c R_DrawAliasModel: all four translucent branches (EF_SPECIAL_TRANS ~1612, DRF_TRANSLUCENT ~1621, EF_TRANSPARENT ~1632, e->alpha ~1667) call glEnable(GL_BLEND) but NEVER touch glDepthMask. The only glDepthMask(0) in the function is the fullbright additive pass (~1775) and the shadow pass (~3063), both of which restore to 1.

Capture confirms: every mist draw runs blend=ON, GL_SRC_ALPHA/GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, u_force_opaque_alpha=0, and dmask=TRUE (glDepthMask(true) at chunk 8880 / 8977, mist draws at 8946, 8987, 9019, 9033, 9090, 9104, 9118, 9132).

CONSEQUENCE: each blended mist instance writes depth, so a later instance is depth-rejected wherever an earlier one already covered — the overlap region is replaced wholesale instead of compositing. That is the hard-edged 'clumpy' patchwork (visible as straight cut lines between blobs in the frame). r_alphasort=1 sorts by entity origin, which does not fix interpenetrating instances.

Contrast: R_RenderBrushPoly already does glDepthMask(0) for DRF_TRANSLUCENT brush surfaces (uhexen2-t4kt/j001). The alias path never got the same treatment.

SUGGESTED FIX: set glDepthMask(0) in R_DrawAliasModel's translucent branches (restore after), and/or stop forcing glDepthMask(1) for alias entities in R_DrawTransEntitiesOnList when the entity is blended. Note the depthMaskWrite shadow variable in that loop must stay in sync with whatever R_DrawAliasModel leaves behind.

SECONDARY (not the main cause, worth noting): r_softparticles defaults to 0, so no soft-particle fade runs — where a mist model intersects the ground/gravestone the intersection is a hard line. Enabling it would further soften the effect but does not address the mutual occlusion.
close_reason: Fixed in 096ee3e5d. R_DrawAliasModel (engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c) now owns the depth mask for the whole draw instead of inheriting it: the four blended branches (EF_SPECIAL_TRANS, DRF_TRANSLUCENT, EF_TRANSPARENT, non-opaque per-entity alpha) turn depth writes off, EF_HOLEY and the opaque branch assert them on (EF_HOLEY is an alpha-TEST cutout whose survivors are opaque, and it reaches the function via the translucent list, which no longer pre-enables the mask), and every exit path -- the R_CullBox early return included -- hands the mask back on. R_DrawTransEntitiesOnList stopped forcing glDepthMask(1) for mod_alias and now updates its depthMaskWrite shadow from that return guarantee rather than from a pre-call assumption that was already stale, since the callee flips the mask internally for its fullbright and shadow passes. Mirrors the discipline R_RenderBrushPoly already follows for translucent brush surfaces (uhexen2-t4kt, uhexen2-j001). Sorting could not substitute: r_alphasort orders back-to-front by squared distance to entity ORIGIN, which says nothing about interpenetrating instances of the same 34-tri mist .mdl drawn eight times. All pokes stay gated on !OIT_InPass(), where OIT_BeginTranslucency owns blend and depth state. Build clean; awaiting field confirmation from the reporter that the mist composites smoothly. The secondary note in this bead -- r_softparticles defaults to 0, so mist/ground intersections stay hard-edged -- was not addressed and was never the mutual-occlusion cause; refile if it still reads wrong in the field.

title: [bug] Skybox depth-write (4h32) un-hides geometry mappers deliberately placed behind sky brushes
description:
RenderDoc capture capture_skybug.rdc. Modder reports geometry he intentionally hid behind sky brushes (for performance) is now visible.

ROOT CAUSE — regression from uhexen2-4h32.
gl_sky.c Sky_DrawSky() have_stencil branch sets glDepthFunc(GL_ALWAYS) + glDepthMask(1) before Sky_DrawSkyBox(), and Sky_DrawSkyBox() pins glDepthRange(0,0) (reversed-Z far plane). The skybox therefore OVERWRITES the sky-wall depth that the sky depth+stencil pre-pass (gl_rsurf.c DrawTextureChains) laid down, replacing it with far-plane depth at every sky pixel.

Capture evidence (chunk indices, skybug.xml):
  11496  prog91  colormask=0000 stencil ALWAYS ref=1   -> sky depth+stencil pre-pass (40 draws)
  11559  prog97  stencil ALWAYS ref=0                  -> world chain, resets stencil (1671 draws)
  13685-13842 prog109/91 stencil EQUAL ref=1 dfunc=GL_ALWAYS dmask=true -> skybox, clobbers depth
  13888  prog97  STENCIL TEST OFF, dfunc=GL_GEQUAL     -> 139 more world/brush-ent draws
  14175+ prog100 alias entities

Everything after the skybox (brush ents at 13888, alias entities at 14175+) z-tests against far-plane depth instead of the sky wall, so it always passes and paints over the sky.

The 4h32 close note claims the fix 'preserves world occlusion' — that is only true for the world chain phase, which runs BEFORE the skybox. Entities and brush entities run after and lost their occluder. 4h32 also explicitly recorded that the alternative (dropping the pre-pass depth-write) 'exposed hidden geometry behind sky brushes' — the shipped fix has the same side effect, just for the later passes.

CONFLICT TO RESOLVE: 4h32 wanted entities visible THROUGH sky-windowed openings; mappers rely on sky brushes OCCLUDING anything behind them (vanilla/QuakeSpasm behavior = sky surfaces write depth, skybox does not). Both cannot hold with a single depth value.

Suggested direction: restore glDepthMask(0) for the skybox draw (the non-stencil else-branch already does this) so the sky-wall depth survives, and solve 4h32's window case differently — e.g. only entities whose leaf is actually visible/inside the map, or a cvar.
close_reason: Fixed in 95896e59c. The have_stencil branch of Sky_DrawSky (engine/h2shared/gl_sky.c) now draws the skybox with glDepthMask(0) instead of 1, matching Ironwail/QuakeSpasm: sky SURFACES write depth via the DrawTextureChains pre-pass, the skybox itself does not. Sky_DrawSkyBox pins glDepthRange(0,0), so the old mask=1 stamped far-plane depth over the sky-wall depth at every sky pixel and every later pass (brush ents at capture chunk 13888, alias at 14175+) z-tested against far and painted over the sky. Stencil GL_EQUAL ref 1 is kept -- that is what confines the fill to genuine sky pixels -- and GL_ALWAYS is kept because with writes off the draw is a pure stencil-limited colour fill that must not fail against the wall depth the pre-pass just wrote. The non-stencil fallback branch already did the right thing and is untouched. This intentionally reverts uhexen2-4h32; its case (entities visible through sky-windowed openings) is refiled as uhexen2-7pyq, and the branch comment names both beads so nobody flips the mask back without reading them. Build clean; not yet confirmed against capture_skybug.rdc's map in the field.

title: Log when an external replacement texture wins over the BSP miptex
description:
## Why

Nothing in the engine says which texture a surface actually got.  IMG_LoadReplacement
deliberately prefers an external file over the BSP miptex (gl_model.c:598-610) and
returns silently, so a broken or unexpected pack file is invisible from inside the
game -- the surface just looks wrong and every hypothesis points at the renderer.

uhexen2-nqwl cost a full RenderDoc capture teardown for exactly this.  The visible
symptom was black slime in SoT docks; the eventual finding was that
sot/textures/#lowlight6.tga is a near-black export (peak 15/255 against the miptex.s
84) that the engine was loading faithfully.  Getting there meant converting the
capture with `renderdoccmd convert -c zip.xml`, decoding every glTexImage2D payload,
structurally matching the uploaded texels back to a BSP miptex index array, and then
searching the local game install for a byte-identical file.  A single Con_DPrintf at
the moment the replacement won would have printed the path in seconds.

## What

In IMG_LoadReplacement (engine/h2shared/img_load.c:595), Con_DPrintf the resolved
path and the dimensions on a hit -- and ideally the fact that it displaced a miptex,
since that is the surprising half.  Same for IMG_LoadReplacementGlow.

Gate it on developer / Con_DPrintf so a normal session stays quiet.  A field tester
can then be asked for a `developer 1` log instead of a capture.

## Deliberately NOT in scope

Rejecting or "fixing" a replacement that looks wrong (all-black, suspiciously small,
mismatched aspect).  That is a heuristic that would silently override legitimate
authoring choices -- dark liquids and low-res replacements are both legal.  The point
here is visibility, not policy.

Discovered while re-auditing uhexen2-nqwl.
notes:
## Runtime-verified 2026-08-18 (build 0.8.0-beta.r11, headless llvmpipe)

The close reason said "not runtime-verified (no replacement pack on this box)".
That was wrong on the premise -- the packs are in the basedir /home/josh/hexen2,
not the userdir ~/.hexen2 -- and it is now verified. Every branch of the new
logging was exercised.

FIXTURE: a throwaway -game imgtest dir holding hand-authored replacements aimed
at demo1.bsp miptex names, sizes chosen NOT to match the BSP so the reported
dimensions prove themselves. Removed afterwards; nothing left on disk.

RESULTS, from ~/.hexen2/qconsole.log with -devlog:

  shared pool + miptex displacement
    IMG: "rtex413" replaced by textures/rtex413.png (32x32)
    IMG: BSP miptex "rtex413" (128x128) displaced
  per-map dir WINS over shared pool, and the log says which won
    IMG: "rtex148" replaced by textures/demo1/rtex148.png (16x16)
    (a 64x64 textures/rtex148.png was planted as the loser; correctly not named)
  glow sidecar, via IMG_LoadReplacementGlow -> IMG_LoadReplacement
    IMG: "rtex413_glow" replaced by textures/rtex413_glow.png (32x32)
  compressed container, incl. the ", compressed" suffix and the q_strlcpy
  that sits INSIDE the IMG_CompressedFits success branch
    IMG: "rtex020" replaced by textures/rtex020.dds (16x16, compressed)
    (hand-authored 16x16 DXT1; llvmpipe reports S3TC yes)
  liquid name mangling, '*' -> '#' via IMG_SafeName -- the nqwl shape
    IMG: "*lowlight" replaced by textures/#lowlight.png (8x8)
    IMG: BSP miptex "*lowlight" (64x64) displaced
  2D/HUD path, IMG_LoadExternalTexture, fires at renderer init before any map
    IMG: "particle" replaced by textures/particle.png (16x16)
  MDL skins, alias path -- correctly NO "BSP miptex" line, they are not miptexes
    IMG: "models/paladin_0" replaced by models/paladin_0.tga (1584x924)

QUIET BY DEFAULT, verified as a negative: with +developer 0 the terminal got
0 IMG: lines while the -devlog file got 354. (An earlier run appeared to print
to the terminal only because this box's own ~/.hexen2/data1/config.cfg carries
developer "1"; the cvar default is "0".)

FIELD RECIPE: -devlog alone is enough. CON_Printf routes _PRINT_DEVEL to the
log whenever con_debuglog has LOG_DEVEL, without the tester touching the
developer cvar. Ask for the flag, get ~/.hexen2/qconsole.log back, grep '^IMG:'.

PAYOFF DEMONSTRATED against the bug that motivated this bead -- see uhexen2-nqwl
for the full re-measurement. Running -game sot +map docks on r11 prints
`IMG: "*lowlight6" replaced by textures/#lowlight6.tga (64x64)` beside its
256x256 siblings, making the outlier visible by eye. That is the entire
RenderDoc teardown, replaced by one grep.
close_reason: Fixed in 291d9ae3d. IMG_LogReplacement (engine/h2shared/img_load.c) Con_DPrintfs the resolved file and its dimensions whenever an external image wins, covering both the decoded (.png/.tga/.pcx) and compressed (.dds/.ktx) paths plus the glow sidecar, since IMG_LoadReplacementGlow routes through IMG_LoadReplacement. IMG_TryDecoded/IMG_TryCompressed grew a pathout param because the caller's base path does not say which extension resolved; IMG_TryCompressed writes it only on success so a size-rejected container is not reported as the winner. The BSP miptex caller (gl_model.c:607) adds the half only it knows -- 'BSP miptex "NAME" (WxH) displaced' -- so a replacement out of step with the map's own texture is legible. IMG_LoadExternalTexture (2D/HUD/particle) logs too. The three developer>=2 'Loaded external texture' prints in IMG_TryDecoded were dropped as superseded. No rejection heuristic, per the explicit out-of-scope note. nix build .#nixos clean; not runtime-verified (no replacement pack on this box).

title: khsa: EF_HOLEY alpha threshold 0.5 revisit — the theory that justified it is dead
description:
Direct sibling of uhexen2-izii, unfiled until now. Same shape: a khsa
speculative change whose justifying theory has since been disproven, still
live in the tree, applying a global visual change for a dead reason.

WHAT IS IN THE TREE. gl_rmain.c:1660 sets GL_SetAlphaThreshold(0.5f) on the
EF_HOLEY alias branch. Landed as bba219b22, 'fix(alias): lower EF_HOLEY
alpha-test threshold 0.666 -> 0.5 (uhexen2-khsa)', and note that commit was
itself a RE-APPLY of an earlier reverted fix -- this value has already
flip-flopped once.

WHY THE JUSTIFICATION IS DEAD. The commit message and the 20-line comment
above the call both argue from the khsa symptom: 'bilinear/mip filtering of
the TEX_HOLEY alpha mask produces fractional alpha clustered around 0.5 at
cutout boundaries; a 0.666 threshold puts the pass/fail boundary right in the
noisy zone, so sub-pixel and mip-LOD shifts move texels across it under viewer
motion -- the screen-door / bus-ad shimmer Mathuzzz reported.'

uhexen2-sp7v settled what that shimmer actually was: Sky_DrawSkyBox leaked
u_alpha_threshold=1.0 onto the next entity, and Mathuzzz's RenderDoc capture
showed two identical knights in one frame, one at threshold 1.0 shot through
with holes and one at 0.01 perfect. Every property the 0.666-noise theory was
invented to explain -- motion dependence, view-angle dependence, ~50% coverage
loss, one-pixel dither -- falls out of the leak instead. The commit's premise
was the artifact; the artifact had a different cause.

THE CONCRETE COST, which is not just tidiness. The engine is now internally
inconsistent about the same operation: alias EF_HOLEY cutouts test at 0.5
while brush SURF_DRAWFENCE cutouts test at 0.666 in gl_rsurf.c:975 and
gl_rsurf.c:1128. A grate modelled as a brush and a grate modelled as an alias
model get different cutout coverage in the same scene. 0.666 is also the
engine's own legacy value and what the rest of the tree uses.

NOT AN OPEN-AND-SHUT REVERT, which is why this is a decision bead and not a
patch. 0.5 has an independent argument the dead theory does not touch: with
A2C a no-op (MSAA is hard-disabled on the main FBO, gl_postprocess.c:436) the
discard is binary, and 0.5 is a defensible centre for a binarized alpha mask.
The question is whether anyone can still justify it on its own merits now that
the bug it was written for is gone.

OPTIONS, mirroring izii:
  1. Revert to 0.666, restoring consistency with the brush fence path and the
     engine's legacy value. Recommended unless (2) can be evidenced.
  2. Keep 0.5 and rewrite the comment to argue from cutout quality alone --
     and then consider moving the brush fence sites to 0.5 as well, because
     the inconsistency is a defect under either value.

Either way the comment at gl_rmain.c:1640-1660 must go: it is 20 lines
asserting a mechanism that is now known to be the wrong one, sitting directly
above the code, and it will mislead the next reader.

Found while auditing the u_alpha_threshold class for uhexen2-sp7v.
notes: HASH CORRECTION 2026-08-19.  The close reason cites the fix as 9393eaec5.  That hash no longer exists: a rebase squashed the follow-up beads commit into it, and the survivor is 63c890804, same subject ('alias: restore the 0.666 cutout threshold on EF_HOLEY') and the same single file.  Nothing about the change itself differs.
close_reason:
Option 1, reverted to 0.666 in 9393eaec5.  The alias EF_HOLEY branch (gl_rmain.c) now discards at the same threshold as the two brush SURF_DRAWFENCE sites (gl_rsurf.c:994, gl_rsurf.c:1147) and the 2D path (gl_draw.c:1952), so a grate loses the same texels whether it is modelled as a brush or as an alias model.  The 20-line dead comment is gone, replaced by one that records the decision.

Option 2 was not evidenced, and its stated basis does not survive checking.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE FOR OPTION 2 IS STALE.  It reads 'with A2C a no-op (MSAA is hard-disabled on the main FBO, gl_postprocess.c:436) the discard is binary, and 0.5 is a defensible centre for a binarized alpha mask.'  MSAA is not hard-disabled: vid_config_fsaa defaults to 4 (gl_vidsdl.c:315) and PP_CreateFBO sets pp_samples = samples on a multisampled main FBO (gl_postprocess.c:626); the OIT path was since reworked to allocate accum/revealage as GL_TEXTURE_2D_MULTISAMPLE and resolve per-sample.  A2C is inert today only because r_alphatocoverage defaults to 0 -- an opt-in cvar, not a structural absence.

AND THAT CORRECTION POINTS THE OTHER WAY, which is worth being explicit about rather than banking it as support for the revert.  Under A2C the shader discard is a floor on the coverage ramp, so a LOWER threshold leaves a wider ramp -- an argument for 0.5, not against it.  What kills it as a case for the split is that the two brush fence sites carry the identical 'if (r_alphatocoverage.integer) glEnable(GL_SAMPLE_ALPHA_TO_COVERAGE)' pattern at 0.666.  Whatever value is right for the ramp is right for all three.  The replacement comment says exactly that, so the next person to tune this moves all three or none.

CHECKED FOR A HIDDEN CLIFF AT 0.5, because a threshold sitting on a shader predicate would have made this riskier than a value change.  There is a 'u_alpha_threshold > 0.5' branch in gl_shader.c:1025, but it is in ssky_frag, where the uniform is overloaded as a sky mode selector (1.0 single-texture vs 0.0 two-layer).  salias_frag discards unconditionally (gl_shader.c:650) -- r20 having deliberately removed r15's threshold gate there.  No coupling; 0.5 vs 0.666 on the alias path changes nothing but coverage.

Verified: nix build .# clean, no new warnings.  Not visually verified -- no rendered frame was taken.  The visible change is one third of a step of cutout coverage on EF_HOLEY models (CASTLE_TR.MDL is the known one), in the direction of what brush grates already do.

title: Leftover TEMP DEBUG console spam from uhexen2-zo7x still on master
description:
engine/h2shared/gl_draw.c:2643-2655, inside GL_Upload8, still carries the diagnostic block added while chasing uhexen2-zo7x (magic missile black square). It scans the whole converted texture and Con_Printf's a 'ZO7X ...' line for every texture whose identifier contains 'ball' or 'star'. zo7x was closed 2026-08-15 (fixed in 0d020a9ca) but the probe was never torn out.

The block is marked '/* TEMP DEBUG uhexen2-zo7x */' in the source, so intent is unambiguous.

Two costs: console spam on every map load for any matching texture (the 'star' substring is broad — it matches sky/decorative textures across the base game and mods), and a full width*height alpha scan per matching upload.

Found while doing screenshot forensics for uhexen2-khsa; unrelated to that bug.

DONE: the TEMP DEBUG block is removed from GL_Upload8, engine builds clean, and no 'ZO7X' string remains in the tree.
close_reason: Removed in b53214b88 (master). The TEMP DEBUG block is gone from GL_Upload8 (engine/h2shared/gl_draw.c); 'grep -rn ZO7X engine/' is now empty and nix build .#nixos passes. MASK_a/SHIFT_a remain in use by the TEX_TRANSPARENT branch above, so nothing was orphaned. Swept the tree for siblings while in there: the only other hit is link_ops.h:31 'FIXME: remove this mess!', which is upstream Quake and not ours.

title: WASM port: productionize the working WebGL2 build
description:
The engine builds and runs under Emscripten/WebGL2 via shell-wasm.nix (proven 2026-03-26), but it's a dev-shell artifact, not a shippable port. This is the main productionization track for epic uhexen2-a7l4.

- Promote to a proper nix flake output (e.g., `nix build .#wasm`) so it's reproducible like linux-fhs/win64

**Hosted Deployment:**

## Related Work
