## Dependency Note
Blocks uhexen2-vigl (Android port), which depends on WASM productionization to harden the GLES path.

title: SSBO binding-0 range cache desynced by raw glBindBufferBase unbinds
description:
GL_BindBufferRange caches the index-0 SSBO binding (gl_buffer.c:114-130), but teardown in the instanced alias path uses raw glBindBufferBase_fp(GL_SHADER_STORAGE_BUFFER, 0, 0) (engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:3025 and :3153), which the cache never sees.

Symptom: If subsequent frames have zero alias instances and the next instanced frame lands on the same ring slot with identical offsets/size, GL_BindBufferRange cache-hits and skips the real bind — one frame of garbage/collapsed alias models, self-healing.

Fix options: Route the unbinds through the cached wrapper or add an invalidation helper the teardown calls.
close_reason: fixed in 6bfc00a17 (new cached GL_BindBufferBase wrapper; all 20 raw glBindBufferBase_fp sites engine-wide converted — the audit's cache-desync hazard in gl_worldcull.c:1133 covered too; GLES stub still performs the bind)

title: IQM VAO feeds integer bone indices through the float attribute pipeline
description: engine/h2shared/gl_mesh.c:620 sets up a_indices with glVertexAttribPointer, but the skeletal shader declares `in uvec4 a_indices` — an integer attribute must use glVertexAttribIPointer or the bone indices are garbage. Latent (nothing draws with this program until IQM dispatch lands); found while fixing uhexen2-bynk. Should be fixed with, or as a dependency of, uhexen2-7ok0.3.
close_reason: fixed in 4928f988f (IQM bone indices fed via glVertexAttribIPointer, matching the shader's uvec4; weights verified already correct as normalized float)

title: [bug] Flatpak ships with no FluidSynth MIDI driver — silently falls back to null + Timidity
description:
The Flatpak build does not detect FluidSynth, so it compiles midi_nul.c instead of midi_fluid.c and MIDI runs through the libTiMidity fallback codec. Confirmed from the build log:

  -- Checking for module 'fluidsynth'
  -- FluidSynth MIDI: not found, disabled
  -- MIDI fallback codec (libTiMidity): ON
  [113/116] Building C object CMakeFiles/glhexen2.dir/h2shared/midi_nul.c.o

PRE-EXISTING, not caused by dropping the ogg/vorbis/opus modules in 5636acd8a. The last successful flatpak build before that change (CI run 32106015292) also compiled midi_nul.c.o and no midi_fluid.c.o.

Why it matters: the manifest goes to considerable trouble for FluidSynth and all of it is currently inert — it builds fluidsynth v2.4.6, disables every one of its audio backends specifically because the driver stack failed inside the sandbox (uhexen2-tdss, uhexen2-hfd6), bundles a 6 MB TimGM6mb soundfont to /app/share/soundfonts/default.sf2, and passes -DSOUNDFONT_PATH to the engine. The engine then never links it. Flatpak users get Timidity, not FluidSynth, and nobody would know.

NOT the cause — ruled out:
- pkg-config works in that build (found 2.5.1) and successfully resolved opusfile and libxmp, which we also build into /app. So /app/lib/pkgconfig IS on PKG_CONFIG_PATH and readable.
- USE_FLUIDSYNTH defaults ON (engine/CMakeLists.txt:33) and nothing in the manifest turns it off.
- Detection is engine/CMakeLists.txt:556-576: find_package(PkgConfig) then pkg_check_modules(FLUIDSYNTH fluidsynth), and the else arm quietly appends midi_nul.c and defines _NO_MIDIDRV.

NEXT STEP: find where fluidsynth's .pc lands. The module builds cmake-ninja with -DLIB_SUFFIX= ; if FluidSynth 2.4.6 honours CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR instead, the .pc may be at /app/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/pkgconfig rather than /app/lib/pkgconfig. The install output was not in the log because flatpak-builder restored that stage from cache — re-run with the cache cleared, or add 'ls -la /app/lib/pkgconfig' to a post-install, to see it.

Related: the guard added in 5636acd8a would have caught this on any build; it is currently narrowed to the three codecs that do work so master is not blocked on this bug. Restore libfluidsynth.so.3 to that list when this is fixed.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 92e6ee3bb -- but NOT verified here, see below.

The bead's NEXT STEP guessed right in substance and wrong in mechanism. It
supposed FluidSynth 2.4.6 might honour CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR 'instead of'
LIB_SUFFIX. It is stronger than that: LIB_SUFFIX does not exist in FluidSynth
2.4.6 at all. Checked against the actual v2.4.6 tree (rev a7792513b) -- the
only occurrence of the string in the entire repository is a stale line in
their own .azure/cmake-android.yml. So '-DLIB_SUFFIX=' in the manifest was a
pure no-op and had never controlled anything.

THE CHAIN, each link verified against source rather than inferred:

  1. cmake_admin/DefaultDirs.cmake is a bare include(GNUInstallDirs) with no
     libdir override.
  2. CMakeLists.txt:882 installs fluidsynth.pc to
     ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}/pkgconfig.
  3. GNUInstallDirs defaults CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR to lib64 on 64-bit Linux.
     Read the module: the Debian-multiarch branch needs /etc/debian_version
     AND a prefix matching ^/usr/?$, neither of which holds in the freedesktop
     runtime at prefix /app; and in CMake 4.x the distro exceptions are gone
     altogether, leaving only a conda check. __GNUInstallDirs_default_in_usr
     rewrites nothing unless the prefix is literally '/'.
  4. => /app/lib64/pkgconfig/fluidsynth.pc, which is not on flatpak's
     PKG_CONFIG_PATH. pkg_check_modules misses it, engine/CMakeLists.txt:556
     takes its silent else arm, midi_nul.c is compiled, _NO_MIDIDRV defined.

This also settles the bead's 'NOT the cause' item about pkg-config working:
opusfile and libxmp resolved because both are autotools and install to
/app/lib. The path was fine; fluidsynth simply was not in it.

FIX: -DCMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR=lib replaces the dead -DLIB_SUFFIX=, and
libfluidsynth.so.3 goes back into the post-install SONAME guard as the bead
asked.

NOT VERIFIED HERE, and this matters. flatpak-builder is not installed on this
box, so I could not build the manifest. Everything above is source-level
evidence, not an observed green build. The restored guard is deliberately the
safety net for that: if the diagnosis is wrong the next CI run fails loudly on
'glhexen2 did not link libfluidsynth.so.3' instead of silently shipping
Timidity again. Someone should confirm the CI run before this is called done.

SIDE OBSERVATION, not fixed, probably harmless. This module builds FluidSynth
with -Denable-libsndfile=off, so the Flatpak's FluidSynth cannot decode SF3.
midi_fluid.c passes allow_compressed=true to SF_FindSoundFont (added in
c7cf3f493 for uhexen2-d4e7) on the premise that FluidSynth reads SF3 via
libsndfile, which is false for this build specifically. Consequence is benign:
FluidSynth fails an SF3 load cleanly and prints, rather than playing noise the
way libTiMidity would, and the bundled default.sf2 plus SOUNDFONT_PATH sit
ahead of every .sf3 probe path anyway. Worth a comment if anyone touches that
call site.
close_reason:
CONFIRMED GREEN IN CI.  The fix landed as 40d7bb04f and the bead's own acceptance -- 'someone should confirm the CI run before this is called done' -- is now met from the flatpak job log of CI run 32191409317 (commit 95896e59c, the first master push containing the fix).

WHAT THE LOG SHOWS, against the exact lines the bead quoted as evidence of the bug:

    -- Checking for module 'fluidsynth'
    --   Found fluidsynth, version 2.4.6
    -- FluidSynth MIDI: enabled (soundfont: /app/share/soundfonts/default.sf2)
    -- Installing: /app/lib/libfluidsynth.so.3
    Building C object CMakeFiles/glhexen2.dir/h2shared/midi_fluid.c.o

Every one is the inverse of what the bead recorded: pkg_check_modules resolves instead of missing, the .pc lands under /app/lib instead of /app/lib64, and midi_fluid.c compiles where midi_nul.c.o used to.  No midi_nul.c.o appears in the run at all.  So the diagnosis in the notes -- FluidSynth 2.4.6 has no LIB_SUFFIX, GNUInstallDirs defaults CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR to lib64 under prefix /app -- is confirmed at runtime, not just from source.

NOT A CACHE ARTEFACT, which was the specific worry that made the original diagnosis hard (the bead notes the install output was missing from the earlier log because flatpak-builder restored that stage from cache).  This run shows fluidsynth's own ninja steps [50/52] and [51/52] linking libfluidsynth.so.3.3.6 and creating the symlink, and the engine module compiling, so both modules built fresh.

THE SONAME GUARD PASSED, and it is the assertion that matters.  The restored loop over libvorbisfile.so.3 / libopusfile.so.0 / libxmp.so.4 / libfluidsynth.so.3 prints only on failure and exits 1; the job is green, so all four matched in /app/bin/glhexen2.  That is the safety net the notes set up working as designed, and it now guards against a third silent regression.

BOOKKEEPING CORRECTION.  The notes above record the fix as 92e6ee3bb.  That hash no longer exists in master -- an interactive rebase squashed the beads commits into their code commits, and the surviving commit is 40d7bb04f, 'flatpak: pin fluidsynth's libdir so the engine can actually find it' (pushed, ancestor of hexenwail/master).  Same class of error uhexen2-nkj1 needed corrected on 2026-08-19; worth watching for whenever a hash is written down here before a rebase.

CARRIED FORWARD, not closed with this bead: the SF3 side observation (the module builds FluidSynth -Denable-libsndfile=off, so allow_compressed=true in midi_fluid.c's SF_FindSoundFont call is inert for the Flatpak specifically).  Benign per the analysis -- clean failure, and bundled default.sf2 precedes every .sf3 probe path -- and left as a note for whoever touches that call site.

title: Skeletal shader attrib locations don't match IQM VAO (latent, blocks uhexen2-7ok0.3)
description:
gl_shader.c:1241 links gl_shader_skeletal with only locations 0-3 bound (gl_shader.c:100-103) while the IQM VAO (gl_mesh.c:607-620) hardcodes position=0, normal=1, texcoord=2, weights=3, indices=4 — texcoord reads normal bytes.

Failure scenario: IQM skeletal models render with corrupted vertex data / misaligned coordinates.

Status: Latent bug — must be fixed as part of the IQM dispatch work. Consider adding as a note/dependency on uhexen2-7ok0.3 instead of a new issue if that's cleaner.
close_reason: fixed in f26c55e6e (skeletal shader uses explicit layout(location) qualifiers matching the IQM VAO; GLSL validated with glslangValidator)

title: Multi-sky-texture maps lose extra sky chains on the fast path
description:
engine/hexen2/gl_rmisc.c:557-566 keeps only the last sky* texture as skytexturenum; other sky chains land in the atlas fast path which skips SURF_DRAWSKY (gl_rsurf.c:2075) then nulls the chain (:2244) — those sky faces never draw (HOM).

Failure scenario: Mod maps with two sky textures render one sky texture correctly but the second sky texture's surfaces are missing (holes in geometry where sky should appear).
close_reason: fixed in 0bb67f114 (sky dispatch keys on the chain's SURF_DRAWSKY flag instead of skytexturenum; stencil pre-pass generalized to all sky chains)

title: Brush-model special-surface visframe=-1 markers never cleared
description:
engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c:2673 marks special surfaces visframe=-1 for the legacy pass (:2822-2831); a surface marked in frame N and backface-culled in frame N+1 still has the marker and gets drawn whenever any other special surface queued — backface culling of sky/turb/fence faces on brush models unreliable across frames.

Failure scenario: Sky, turb, and fence surfaces on brush entities (e.g., door frames with sky windows) flicker between visible/culled as camera rotates or other entities move, instead of staying consistently backface-culled.
close_reason: fixed in e109ff783 (visframe -1 sentinel replaced by a negative per-pass id stamp; stale marks can never match)

title: Fast-path texture chains silently drop surfaces past fixed caps
description:
engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c:2085 stops collecting past MAX_BATCH_SURFS (4096) without flushing (the R_DrawBrushModel sibling at :2750-2779 flushes correctly); same pattern for world_deferred[4096] (:2080) and sky_runs[8192] (:1832-1839, sky past the cap gets no depth/stencil so skybox bleeds through walls).

Failure scenario: Visible hole risk mainly with r_gpucull 0 / WASM on very dense maps. Surfaces beyond the batch cap silently fail to render.
close_reason: fixed in 52b053737 (world fast-path batch, deferred fence/underwater batch, and sky stencil runs all flush-and-continue when full instead of dropping surfaces)

title: gl_lightmapfmt GL_LUMINANCE broken in core GL 4.3 pipeline
description:
GL_LUMINANCE isn't a core 4.3 format (upload fails, gl_rsurf.c:361-364 + :3999 silently → black world); even if uploaded, R_BuildLightMap stores INVERTED luminance (dest[j]=255-t, gl_rsurf.c:582 — legacy GL_BLEND texenv relic) while shaders multiply; and R_LightPointColor walks 3 bytes/luxel over 1-byte data (gl_rlight.c:607-624) reading past sample blocks.

Failure scenario: Setting gl_lightmapfmt to GL_LUMINANCE results in black world or incorrect lighting calculations with out-of-bounds memory reads.

Fix: Either fix for core GL or reject the cvar value.
close_reason: fixed in b95f8bfed (GL_LUMINANCE lightmap format retired with console warning, pinned to RGBA; dead luminance branches and blocklights accumulator removed from gl_rsurf.c)

title: Legacy vs instanced alias path divergences: colorshade tint and GL_LUMINANCE lighting
description:
Two legacy/instanced divergences:

(a) engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:926-933: legacy RGBA branch drops the RTint/GTint/BTint[colorshade] multiply that the instanced collect applies (:2711-2718) — same entity renders tinted or untinted depending on which path it takes.

(b) In GL_LUMINANCE lightmap mode the instanced collect (:2728-2737) multiplies two already-/200-scaled factors → quadratically dark vs legacy (:936-940).

Failure scenario: On maps with colorshade or with gl_lightmapfmt GL_LUMINANCE set, entities rendered via different paths (legacy viewmodel vs instanced main model, or depending on r_alias_gpu toggle) have visibly different lighting/tint.

Edge configs but user-visible inconsistency.
close_reason: fixed in 695336a00 (legacy RGBA alias branch applies the colorshade tint, matching the instanced path; the GL_LUMINANCE half is moot after uhexen2-q3j7)

title: [bug] External replacement textures silently drop the fullbright/glow layer
description:
Replacing a world texture or model skin with an external PNG/TGA/PCX kills its fullbright (glow) pass. Torches, runes, monster eyes and lava detail go dark the moment a HD pack is installed — which makes this the first thing any pack author will hit.

Cause: the fullbright mask is only built on the *fallback* (embedded-data) branch.

  engine/h2shared/gl_model.c:539-575  (world textures)
    external branch sets gl_texturenum and never touches gl_fb_texturenum;
    Mod_LoadFullbrightTexture("<name>_glow", ...) is called only in the else branch.

  engine/h2shared/gl_model.c:2570-2588  (alias skins, single-skin path)
    external branch explicitly sets gl_fb_texturenum[i][0..3] = 0.

  engine/h2shared/gl_model.c:2631-2650  (alias skins, group-skin path)
    external branch explicitly sets gl_fb_texturenum[i][j&3] = 0.

The mask is derived from palette indices >= vid.fullbright (224), which an RGBA replacement no longer has — so it cannot be recovered from the image itself. It has to come from a sidecar file.

Fix: on the external path, try a companion image and upload it as the fb texture:
  world:  textures/<texname>_glow.{png,tga,pcx}
  skins:  models/<model>_<n>_glow.{png,tga,pcx}
Accept _luma as an alias (FTE/jsHexen2 packs use that name). If no sidecar exists, leave gl_fb_texturenum at 0 — current behaviour, no regression for packs that do not ship glow maps.

Done when: a replacement texture plus its _glow sidecar renders with the additive fullbright pass, a replacement without a sidecar behaves as it does today, and the embedded (no-replacement) path is untouched.
close_reason: Fixed on master 74e8eccde. All three call sites (gl_model.c world textures, and both alias-skin paths) now resolve a <name>_glow / <name>_luma sidecar via IMG_LoadReplacementGlow when the base texture was replaced, instead of leaving gl_fb_texturenum at 0. No sidecar means no glow layer, which is the previous behaviour, so nothing regresses for packs that do not ship one.

title: CI audit follow-ups: silent-pass smoke test, live-network lint, token scope
description:
Applying findings 1, 2, 4, 5, 7 and 10 from the CI audit (artifact: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/21c6234c-df04-4df0-96b3-e34c7253b64a).

1. ci.yml:29 — appstreamcli validate had no --no-net, the same defect that failed release r5 and blocked two r6 attempts. release.yml was fixed in 327bd5510; this is its twin.
2. ci.yml:65, ci-mdl.yml:69 — the smoke test could not fail. No 'set -o pipefail', so the pipeline reported head's status, and '|| true' swallowed what survived. Verified: 'false | head -20' exits 0 even without the '|| true'. It is the only step that runs the engine rather than compiling it.
4. ci.yml, ci-mdl.yml — no permissions block, so both inherited the repo default. security-scan.yml:24 already does this correctly with contents: read.
5. release.yml:9 — contents: write declared workflow-wide, so the flatpak and build jobs held a write-capable token they never use. Only publish writes.
7. ci.yml:65, ci-mdl.yml:69 — plain 'timeout 10' on an engine documented to ignore SIGTERM during shutdown; needs -k. With no job timeout (finding 6, not in scope here) a wedged process is a six-hour run.
10. ci.yml:18 — apt-get install with no apt-get update, while the flatpak job in the same file does update at line 115.

Checked before making the smoke test strict: sys_unix.c:578 handles -help by calling PrintHelp then exit(0), before any SDL or video init, and a local run confirms exit 0. So enforcing the status will not turn CI red.

NOT in scope, still open from the audit: 3 (no test suite), 6 (no job timeouts), 8 (tag builds run no lint), 9 (no concurrency groups), 11 (security-scan cache comment contradicts its key).
notes:
APPLIED in 3f156181c. All six build/parse clean: every workflow passes yq, and every multi-line run: block passes bash -n.

Evidence for the two substantive ones:

Finding 2/7 (smoke test) — verified in the form GitHub actually uses, bash -e on a script file:
  healthy binary  -> exit 0
  crashing binary -> exit 139  (under the old form: 0)
IMPORTANT GOTCHA for anyone re-testing this: 'set -e' is silently suppressed in some interactive/wrapper shells. A bare '( set -e; false; echo REACHED )' printed REACHED in this sandbox, which made an early test wrongly report the fix as ineffective. Test it with 'bash -e <file>' or 'bash -c', not an interactive subshell.

Finding 1 (--no-net) — 'appstreamcli validate --no-net --explain' on the real metainfo returns 'Validation was successful.'

Finding 5 — confirmed post-edit via yq: all four workflows now read contents: read at top level, and release.yml's publish job alone carries contents: write.

Also checked before making the smoke test strict: sys_unix.c:578 handles -help with PrintHelp() then exit(0) before any SDL or video init, so asserting the exit status cannot turn CI red on a healthy build. Confirmed by running the real step verbatim out of the YAML.

STILL OPEN from the audit, deliberately out of scope here:
  3  — no test suite exists (no add_test, no enable_testing, no tests/)
  6  — no timeout-minutes on any job; six-hour default
  8  — tag builds run no lint (it lives only in ci.yml, which has tags-ignore)
  9  — no concurrency groups
  11 — security-scan.yml:48 comment says the NVD cache is keyed by week; the key is github.run_id

3 and 8 are design calls. 6, 9 and 11 are one-liners whenever wanted.
close_reason:
All applied. 3f156181c covered findings 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 10; 45ba4f3d3 covered 6, 9, 11. Nine of the audit's eleven findings are now fixed.

45ba4f3d3 specifics:
- timeout-minutes on all nine jobs across all four workflows, sized from measured runtime (warm-cache maxima: build 2m, flatpak 1m, lint <1m, vulnix 6m, publish <1m) at roughly 10-15x, so a cold cache still fits. Verified via yq that no job is left without one.
- concurrency groups on ci.yml, ci-mdl.yml and security-scan.yml. ci-mdl.yml is keyed on 'inputs.ref || github.ref' rather than github.ref, because under workflow_dispatch github.ref is always the workflow's own branch — the naive key would make two dispatches for two different commits cancel each other, killing a tester build someone is waiting on.
- release.yml deliberately gets NO concurrency, and now carries a comment saying why: cancelling mid-flight can leave a tag with assets uploaded and no body.
- security-scan.yml cache comment corrected rather than the key changed. Rolling (run_id) is the right behaviour: NVD publishes continuously, so a genuinely weekly key would serve a stale feed for up to seven days.

Verified after the edits: all four workflows parse under yq, every job has a timeout, and every multi-line run: block passes bash -n.

Remaining audit findings 3 (no test suite) and 8 (tag builds run no lint) are design calls and are tracked separately.

title: Remove noindex once the site's content is real
description:
## Why

The site is live at https://hexenwail.github.io/blog/ and publicly crawlable, but it still ships placeholder content: lorem ipsum body prose, dummy SHA-256 values, download URLs that say EXAMPLE, and a placeholder Discord invite.

Being the top search result for "hexen 2 downloads" while the checksums are fake would be worse than not being found at all — especially for a site whose entire argument is that the previous two Hexen II hubs became untrustworthy before they died. So every page currently carries `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">`.

That is a temporary state. It has to be undone deliberately, or the site launches invisible.

## Blocked on

Do not flip this until the placeholders are gone:

- real body prose replacing the lorem ipsum
- real SHA-256 values in `data/files.yaml`
- real download URLs (no `EXAMPLE`)
- real Discord invite in `hugo.toml`

## How

Delete one line from `hugo.toml`:

```toml
[params]
  noindex = true
```

That is the whole switch. Then run the `publish` workflow.

Verify afterwards — expect 18 of 116 HTML files still tagged, and only those:

```sh
grep -rl "content=\"noindex" public --include="*.html" | wc -l
```

## Do NOT use robots.txt for this

`layouts/robots.txt` is deliberately permissive and says so at length. Two reasons it must stay that way:

1. While the site is served from a subdirectory (`/blog/`), robots.txt is ignored entirely — crawlers only honour it at a domain root. `hexenwail.github.io/robots.txt` is a 404 belonging to a different repo.
2. Even once hexenworld.org serves the site from a root, `Disallow` is the wrong tool. A crawler must fetch a page to see a noindex tag, so blocking hides the tag rather than the page, and a blocked-but-linked URL can still be listed as a bare link with no description. Blocking causes more indexing, not less.

## Note on the alias stubs

`layouts/alias.html` sets noindex unconditionally and should stay that way after this issue is closed. Those 18 pages are the legacy old-link redirects; an alias is a redirect, not a page, and what belongs in an index is the target it points at.

title: Warn at load time when "Classic" gamecode loads Hexenwail's own progs
description:
When sv_gamecode is 0 ("Classic") but PR_ClassifyGamecode() identifies the loaded gamecode as Hexenwail's own build, the player's intent (use retail Raven gamecode) and the actual outcome (running Hexenwail code) disagree.

This happens when a loose progs.dat from a previous Hexenwail install (CRC 24008, recorded in docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md:915) shadows the retail PROGS.DAT in pak0.pak—filesystem priority in quakefs.c:489-497 causes the loose file to load first.

**Current state:** The provenance information exists in the startup log (engine/h2shared/pr_edict.c:3183-3195) but is buried among hundreds of lines, so the player never sees it at the moment it matters.

**Fix:** Emit an explicit Con_Printf() warning when this mismatch is detected, naming the loose file's path so the player can identify and remove it.

**Cross-references:**
- uhexen2-8r3e: Added the status row to surface this exact issue
- uhexen2-8qp3: Documents the pre-bundle install method that creates stale loose files

**Reported by:** Josh (2026-08-16, running 0.8.0-beta.r4)
close_reason: Fixed in b85802d45: Con_Printf warning added in PR_LoadProgs when player's selected gamecode source is the install's own file but loaded image identifies as Hexenwail's, suppressed against repeats via lastreport guard

title: Undated "hexenwail" gamecode ident is unreadable next to dated versions
description:
The PR_ClassifyGamecode() function in engine/h2shared/pr_edict.c returns a bare "hexenwail" string in two cases:
1. The GAMECODE_SENTINEL marker function is present but lacks or has an unparseable "_YYYYMMDD" suffix (lines 876-881)
2. The marker function is absent and the legacy BadBackpackDump fallback fires (lines 886-889)

In the 8px menu font, the bare "hexenwail" string is visually indistinguishable from "hexenwail-2026-08-15", causing players to flip the Classic/Updated toggle and see no change in the status line—making them think the toggle is broken.

**Fix:** Render the undated form as "hexenwail (undated)" so the two states cannot be confused visually. The status row is drawn at x=16 on a 320-unit canvas with a 17-character label prefix (engine/hexen2/menu.c:4079-4084, 4085-4092), leaving sufficient room for the longer string.

**Reported by:** Josh (2026-08-16, running 0.8.0-beta.r4)
**Related:** uhexen2-8r3e (status row addition that surfaces this issue)
close_reason: Fixed in b85802d45: PR_ClassifyGamecode() now returns 'hexenwail (undated)' instead of bare 'hexenwail' in both places that produced the undated form

title: [bug] SoT rain/snow reported missing in the field (Garrett)
description:
Garrett reports Storm over Thyrion's rain/snow weather effects are missing on 0.8.0-beta.r3. Triage checklist sent to him: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/5a704911-f106-4bb7-9a10-cf481a7c92f5

## Verified intact (headless, no rendering)

Built .#h2ded and loaded winter / tibet / demo1, dumping the savegame SV_SaveEffects table:
- winter: 15 CE_SNOW effects, correct boxes, flags=1 (SFL_FLUFFY), dir=(-0.8,0,-250), counts 4-50
- tibet: 18 CE_SNOW (2 of the 20 weather_snow ents are trigger-gated via snow_use)
- demo1: 1 CE_RAIN, box x1688..2912 y-528..912 top z760, color 414, count 300, wait 0.1

Also confirmed identical to sezero/master: cl_effect.c CE_RAIN/CE_SNOW parse, CL_UpdateEffects, R_RainEffect, R_SnowEffect, R_UpdateParticles, particle.h, d_8to24TranslucentTable construction. SoT progs disassembly (tools/qcdis.py) shows weather_snow/weather_rain starteffect arg order matches SV_ParseEffect. SoT uses builtins 1-106 + #111 pimpmodel; our 107-113 extensions do not collide.

## Leading non-bug explanation

CL_UpdateEffects gates CE_SNOW on `distance < 1024` measured from the camera to the CENTRE of the snow brush, ignoring brush size. This is stock Raven code, byte-identical in HoT and in Shanjaq's fork (the engine SoT targets). SoT's volumes are map-scale (up to ~2200x2400), so most of each volume's own footprint sits outside its own cutoff.

Measured: at EVERY info_player_start in winter and tibet, zero volumes pass the gate.
- winter from keep (-3120,664): nearest centre 1375
- winter from palace (14,1144): nearest centre 1078
- tibet from arena (3879,1919): nearest centre 1751

So 'no snow on arrival' is correct stock behaviour. Possible fix if we want SoT to look right: scale the cutoff by the volume's own half-extent instead of a flat 1024.

## Open suspects if Garrett's Test 1 (rain on demo1) fails

Rain has no proximity gate and demo1's spawn is inside the rain footprint, so no rain there means a real render-path fault. Candidates: particle_oit shader link failure on his driver (r_oit defaults 0 and no preset sets it, so only if he enabled it), gl_particles 0, snow_active 0.

Needs from Garrett: which map, qconsole.log, GPU/driver, and which build last worked.
notes:
## Spawn-solid trap measured and closed 2026-08-18 (0cda668cd)

The trap is real but it is NOT the sky case predicted above. Scanned every
weather_rain on this box -- 5 maps, 21 volumes -- sampling each volume's top
plane against the worldmodel:

- castle4 (data1/pak1.pak, RETAIL) embeds rain brushes in the architecture.
  10 of its 17 volumes have 50-98% of their spawn plane inside SOLID, worst
  at 97.9%.
- eidolon (also retail) has one volume at 19%.
- sot/demo1, portals/thomas, soc/h2menu: 100% empty, clean.
- CONTENTS_SKY does not occur anywhere. The predicted sky trap is not the
  one that exists.

Consequence: r_raincollide defaulting to 1 had been silently deleting half
the rain in a shipping map. Across castle4, 50.5% of drops died on the frame
they spawned.

Fixed by giving rain the retry loop snow already had, choosing the spot
before committing a particle to it. castle4 goes 50.5% -> 97.4% of drops
surviving; the 97.9%-solid volume goes 2.1% -> 56.4%. demo1 is unaffected
(already 100% empty, so it returns on the first try). With r_raincollide off
the path is unchanged down to the RNG sequence.

Also guards the `rand() % e_size` division stock never did.

## Remaining on this bead

- Rain still dies in WATER/SLIME/LAVA leaves as well as SOLID, since the
  test is `!= CONTENTS_EMPTY`. Over water that is arguably right (the drop
  should stop at the surface) and the gamecode has a separate splatter
  effect, but it is untested and unmeasured -- none of the five maps put a
  rain volume over liquid.
- Nothing here has been seen on screen. Every number is measured off the
  BSPs and the source. The r_rainintensity/r_snowintensity default of 2
  still wants eyes on it.
## 2026-08-18 — the "Leading non-bug explanation" above is no longer live

That section reads as an open suggestion ("Possible fix if we want SoT to look
right: scale the cutoff by the volume's own half-extent"). It shipped:
uhexen2-ykqw, commit 6ec79963c. CL_UpdateEffects (engine/hexen2/cl_effect.c:1060)
now measures the snow gate to the nearest point on the volume's XY footprint --
zero while you stand inside it -- keeping the 1024 budget and the
height-agnostic behaviour. Measured before/after at the very spawns this bead
cites: winter keep 0 -> 3 volumes, winter palace 0 -> 5, tibet arena 0 -> 1.

So "no snow on arrival in winter/tibet" should no longer reproduce, and the
most likely explanation for Garrett's report is closed. What remains is what
the Remaining section already lists, and all of it needs eyes or a field build
rather than more source reading.

Next action is Garrett's, not the tree's: on a build carrying 6ec79963c and
0cda668cd, does winter/tibet show snow and demo1 show rain?

title: Settle whether Garrett's 'bright lines' are surface seams or diagonal shadow stepping
description:
Split out of uhexen2-5nle, whose other half (large-map lightmap page ceiling) is
answered and closed. This half never was about the gutter -- it is about whether
uhexen2-jwzf was ever Garrett's bug at all.

## The question

Garrett reported "bright lines cutting through squares of area". Two completely
different causes look similar in a screenshot:

- lines along SURFACE BOUNDARIES -> inter-surface lightmap bleed. That was
  uhexen2-jwzf, fixed by c10eb1e40 + f38654033 (LM_GUTTER 2, replicated edge
  luxels, pages 256 -> 260).
- lines along DIAGONAL SHADOW EDGES -> lightmap-resolution stepping. Inherent to
  the format, not a defect, and what bicubic filtering is meant to REDUCE rather
  than remove -- Spoike's own framing.

jwzf was filed off Spoike's Discord remark plus a reading of the code. Nobody has
looked at the actual images. If they show the second kind, jwzf never was his bug
and his report is still open, so telling him it is fixed would be wrong.

## Why this cannot be answered here

His screenshots predate the gutter, so rendering the current build proves nothing
about them -- a surface seam that is gone now was still there when he shot it.
The discriminator is geometric and has to be read off HIS images: do the lines
run along brush-face boundaries, or along the lit/unlit diagonal?

## What to ask him for, all three

1. The original screenshots, or new ones plus his build version.
2. The console output alongside them. uhexen2-2mwz now prints an explicit line
   when a .lit is stale, and his all-yellow report is consistent with exactly
   that. Do not diagnose the colour without it.
3. Whether he is on a build after uhexen2-6rqa (fullbright masks enabled
   engine-wide), which brightens things for an unrelated reason and will
   otherwise be read as a regression.

DONE = the lines in his images classified as seam or stepping, and jwzf either
confirmed as his fix or reopened as a separate report.

BLOCKED ON: Garrett supplying the images. Data acquisition, not engineering.

title: Decide: build fluidsynth with -Denable-libsndfile=0 to drop 5 parser CVEs from the closure
description:
Successor to uhexen2-ql7h, which established that waiting for a libsndfile bump
is an indefinite hold (1.2.2 released 2023-08-13 is still the latest upstream
release as of 2026-08-15, and nixpkgs master carries the same version).

## The option

libsndfile is not in glhexen2's DT_NEEDED -- verified with readelf -d on the
built binary. It enters the runtime closure only through libfluidsynth.so.3.

FluidSynth links libsndfile for two features:
  1. SF3 soundfonts (Vorbis-compressed sample data)
  2. the file renderer (writing rendered audio to .wav)

Hexenwail uses neither. flake.nix:661 bundles TimGM6mb.sf2 and flake.nix:226
sets -DSOUNDFONT_PATH to FluidR3_GM2-2.sf2; both are uncompressed SF2, and
playback uses the realtime audio driver. So an overlay building fluidsynth with
-Denable-libsndfile=0 removes CVE-2025-52194, CVE-2026-37555, CVE-2024-50613,
CVE-2024-50612 and CVE-2025-56226 from the closure rather than tracking them.

nixpkgs fluidsynth 2.5.6 already sets cmakeFlags (-Denable-framework=off,
-Denable-libinstpatch=0), so this is a one-line override, not a fork.

## Why it is a decision and not just a patch

Two real costs:

1. BINARY CACHE. Overriding fluidsynth means building it from source. Every
   build (and every hexenwail.cachix.org consumer) loses the cache hit for
   fluidsynth and its build closure. Measure this before committing to it.

2. CAPABILITY LOSS. find_soundfont() in engine/hexen2/midi_fluid.c probes
   .sf2 AND .sf3, and snd_soundfont is a user-settable cvar. A player pointing
   it at an .sf3 today gets working music; after this change FluidSynth would
   refuse to load it. SF3 is meaningfully smaller for the same GM coverage,
   which matters for the WASM target (see uhexen2-g3j9, which is explicitly
   shopping for a smaller GM font for web).

That second point is the sharp one: uhexen2-g3j9 may WANT SF3 precisely because
it is small. Settle g3j9's soundfont choice before closing this, or the two
decisions fight.

## Alternatives if the tradeoff is refused

- Carry upstream master's parser fixes as nixpkgs patches (upstream master is
  active -- most recent commit 2026-07-21 -- but unreleased).
- Accept and document: the attack requires the player to point snd_soundfont at
  a hostile file, or to install a mod that ships one. Same trust level as
  installing the mod at all.

DONE = a decision recorded with the cache-hit cost measured, and either the
overlay landed or this bead closed with the rationale for accepting the CVEs.
notes:
MEASURED AND REJECTED 2026-08-15. The premise is false: this change removes
ZERO CVEs from the closure. Do not implement it as written.

## What was measured

Built the exact override the bead proposes (fluidsynth 2.5.6 with libsndfile
dropped from buildInputs and -Denable-libsndfile=0):

    /nix/store/1n8g19bnyi37aqgv7ls72wy0zd5bb5kn-fluidsynth-2.5.6
    build cost: 29.3 s wall clock, one time per machine

It works -- readelf -d on the resulting libfluidsynth.so.3 shows no libsndfile
in DT_NEEDED. And libsndfile is STILL in its runtime closure, because nixpkgs
fluidsynth also links libpulseaudio on Linux and libpulseaudio needs libsndfile.

## The finding that kills it

`nix why-depends --all ./result <libsndfile>` on the current build. libsndfile
reaches the engine closure by SEVEN paths, only one of which is the one this
bead targets:

    hexenwail -> fluidsynth -> libsndfile                      <- the bead's target
    hexenwail -> fluidsynth -> libpulseaudio -> libsndfile
    hexenwail -> sdl3 -> pipewire -> libsndfile                <- unavoidable
    hexenwail -> sdl3 -> pipewire -> lilv -> libsndfile
    hexenwail -> sdl3 -> pipewire -> spandsp -> libsndfile
    hexenwail -> sdl3 -> pipewire -> roc-toolkit -> libsndfile
    hexenwail -> sdl3 -> pipewire -> roc-toolkit -> sox -> libsndfile

SDL3 -> pipewire -> libsndfile is direct and the engine cannot drop SDL3. So
vulnix will keep reporting all five advisories no matter what fluidsynth is
built with, and this bead's acceptance criterion ("libsndfile no longer reports
active advisories") is unreachable by any action inside this project.

## Where the parent bead went wrong

uhexen2-ql7h concluded from `readelf -d glhexen2` that "libsndfile arrives ONLY
transitively through libfluidsynth.so.3". readelf sees DT_NEEDED, which is the
engine's own direct links; it does not see the transitive closure, and pipewire
is dlopened by SDL3 rather than linked. The observation was right and the
inference from it was wrong.

## The tradeoffs the bead asked to weigh, now measured, and moot

1. BINARY CACHE: 29.3 s to build fluidsynth from source, once per machine.
   Cheaper than feared -- but bought nothing.
2. CAPABILITY LOSS: real. FluidSynth without libsndfile refuses SF3 outright.

## What survives: a reachability argument, not a closure argument

Dropping libsndfile from fluidsynth would still close the specific attack path
ql7h described -- a crafted .sf3 reaching a parser through snd_soundfont. That
is worth something even though libsndfile stays in the closure via pipewire,
because the engine never hands pipewire's copy a soundfont. But if that is the
goal, the cheap lever is in our own code, not in an overlay: stop offering .sf3
to a synth at all (SF_FindSoundFont, engine/h2shared/soundfont.c:88-120, probes
soundfont.sf3 in four places). Zero build cost, no cache miss, no overlay to
maintain -- and it fixes a separate real defect on the libTiMidity tier, filed
alongside this.

## Unrelated finding, recorded so it is not re-derived

The engine never creates a fluid_audio_driver_t. midi_fluid.c:311 renders with
fluid_synth_write_s16() and feeds the result to SDL. So fluidsynth's ALSA,
PulseAudio and JACK backends are all dead weight in this build. Disabling them
(-Denable-pulseaudio=0 -Denable-jack=0 -Denable-alsa=0) is a legitimate closure
trim on its own merits -- but it does not remove libsndfile either, for the same
pipewire reason, so it is a size question and not a security one.
close_reason: Premise falsified by measurement. libsndfile reaches the closure via SDL3 -> pipewire (plus 5 other paths), not only via fluidsynth, so -Denable-libsndfile=0 removes zero CVEs and the acceptance criterion is unreachable. Built and measured the exact override (29.3s, links clean, still pulls libsndfile through libpulseaudio). Force-closed past the uhexen2-g3j9 gate because that gate is now moot: g3j9 cannot want SF3 (libTiMidity has no Vorbis decoder), so the two decisions no longer fight. Evidence in notes.

title: Report whose gamecode is loaded: Raven vs Hexenwail vs third-party
description:
The 'Gamecode:' startup line named the file's path, progdefs version and whole-file CRC, but not WHOSE code it is. The path cannot answer that: our progs.dat hand-copied into the install's data1/ (the pre-bundle install method from uhexen2-8qp3) loads from a path indistinguishable from Raven's, and reads as 'Classic' in the Game Options menu while running our fixes. Whole-file CRC cannot answer it either for our side, because every gamecode/hc edit moves it -- docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md stamps its own CRC table 'dated, and expected to move'.

Adds PR_ClassifyGamecode() in engine/h2shared/pr_edict.c: the three retail whole-file CRCs (17499/20799/33075, fixed since 1997) identify Raven and carry the release number from progs->crc; a marker function HexenwailGamecode, defined in a new gamecode/hc/<tree>/ident.hc, identifies ours; anything else is third-party. A BadBackpackDump probe covers our builds that predate the marker.

A function rather than a string global because hcc.c::WriteData() strips global names under -on (used for portals, hw, siege) unless the global carries DEF_SAVEGLOBAL, which hcc only sets for uninitialized globals. Function names always survive (the strip test is type < ev_field, and ev_function sorts above). The marker is not an entity field, so gamecode/fieldsets stays byte-identical, and PR_WriteProgdefs CRCs only globals up to end_sys_globals plus the field table, so the progdefs CRC is untouched.

Surfaced twice: appended to the existing Gamecode: line (extended in place, since that line is what the release notes ask bug reporters to paste), and as a read-only 'Running:' row under the Gamecode toggle in Game Options. The row is absent until a map has loaded, which is also the honest answer on a client attached to a remote server.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] VID_SetMode zeroes vid_config_fsaa on every mode set, so MSAA and the MSAA OIT resolve are unreachable
description:
Found 2026-08-15 while trying to exercise the MSAA OIT resolve for uhexen2-hhs1.

## Root cause

VID_SetMode (h2shared/gl_vidsdl.c) does two things that combine badly:

1. It sets the file-static "multisample" to 0 unconditionally, with a deliberate comment
   citing uhexen2-zroc: window MSAA is intentionally not requested, because a multisampled
   default framebuffer mis-rendered translucent surfaces (the "glass" screen-door).

2. A few dozen lines later it does Cvar_SetValueQuick(&vid_config_fsaa, multisample),
   writing that same 0 back into the cvar.

Step 2 is the bug. Step 1 is a decision about the WINDOW; step 2 destroys the setting that
everything else reads. vid_config_fsaa can therefore never hold a non-zero value past a mode
set, no matter where it came from.

The comment on step 1 also asserts "The main scene FBO already force-disables MSAA
(gl_postprocess.c PP_CreateFBO)". That is not what PP_CreateFBO does. It reads the cvar:

    int samples = (vid_config_fsaa.integer > 1) ? vid_config_fsaa.integer : 0;

So the FBO does not force anything off -- it asks the cvar, and the cvar has just been
zeroed. The comment describes an intent the code does not implement.

## Consequences

- The multisampled scene FBO branch in PP_CreateFBO is unreachable.
- oit_samples (h2shared/gl_postprocess.c) therefore never exceeds 0, so
  oit_resolve_prog_msaa is compiled on every startup and never selected. Dead code shipping
  in every build, and the reason uhexen2-hhs1 could not verify the MSAA OIT path.
- The cvar's own default is "4", so the shipped default is a value that can never take
  effect.
- The video menu has a multisample row (VID_MULTISAMPLE) that lets the player pick a value
  which is silently discarded on the next mode set.
- Any run also REWRITES the player's config.cfg with vid_config_fsaa "0" on quit, so the
  setting is not merely ignored, it is erased.

## Evidence

Same config.cfg, two early-read cvars, one run:

    vid_config_consize "512"  ->  runtime reports 512   (CFG_ReadCvars works, right file)
    vid_config_fsaa    "4"    ->  runtime reports 0

So this is not CFG_ReadCvars and not a file-priority problem -- both values come out of the
same file in the same pass. And "multisample buffer with %i samples" never prints, confirming
multisample is already 0 by the time VID_SetMode reaches that branch.

## Fixing it is a decision, not a patch

Simply not clobbering the cvar would make the MSAA scene-FBO path live for everyone, since
the default is 4 -- and that path, plus the MSAA OIT resolve behind it, has never been
exercised. Do not do that blind.

Options:
  (a) Keep window MSAA off (zroc stands) but stop writing the window's achieved sample count
      into vid_config_fsaa; give the window its own variable. Then decide separately whether
      the FBO path should honour the cvar, and test it before letting it default on.
  (b) If FBO MSAA is not wanted either, make PP_CreateFBO actually force samples to 0, fix
      the comment to match, and remove or disable the menu row so the player is not offered
      a setting that does nothing.
Either way the stale comment should go, and whichever is chosen should be reflected in the
menu.
close_reason: Fixed in cf4abbb28. Split the overloaded 'multisample' static into three: window request (still pinned 0), vid_config_fsaa (player setting, no longer stomped by VID_SetMode), vid_menu_fsaa (menu-pending, written to cvar on Apply). Removed the Cvar_SetValueQuick(&vid_config_fsaa, multisample) at the end of VID_SetMode that was the actual bug. Also: -fsaa N now sets the cvar; menu availability gated on GL_MAX_SAMPLES>1; legacy menu's open-coded 0/2/4/8 ladder replaced with VID_MenuAdjustMultisample so both menus respect GL_MAX_SAMPLES; PP_CreateFBO clamps samples to GL_MAX_SAMPLES. Verified headless on llvmpipe (GL_MAX_SAMPLES 8) with -fsaa 4: cvar reads back 4, config.cfg archives 4 (was being erased to 0 every run), and demo1 hits 'PostProcess: 640x480 FBO with 4x MSAA' + 'OIT: 640x480 FBO ready' with no GL errors. The MSAA OIT resolve path is now reachable — unblocks verification for uhexen2-hhs1.

title: r_oit is force-reset to 0 at registration; revisit now that OIT actually composites
description:
GL_PostProcess_Init (h2shared/gl_postprocess.c, right after Cvar_RegisterVariable(&r_oit)) does:

    if (r_oit.integer)
        Cvar_Set("r_oit", "0");

so an archived r_oit 1 is discarded at every startup. That was added because OIT rendered
nothing -- which was uhexen2-z4r1, fixed in 8dcbc6284: the resolve's fullscreen triangle was
being front-face culled, so correctly-filled accum/revealage buffers were composited nowhere.

The workaround is now papering over a fixed bug. It also makes the feature untestable in the
normal way: a player can still set r_oit 1 at runtime (the reset only runs at registration),
but it never survives a restart, so nobody accumulates real playtime on it.

## Before removing it

The z4r1 verification was one scene -- demo1, sprites, llvmpipe, 640x480. Removing the reset
makes r_oit a persistable setting, so it wants broader evidence first:

1. Translucent WATER through OIT. R_DrawWaterSurfaces(WATER_PHASE_TRANSLUCENT) runs inside
   the pass and was equally broken; nobody has looked at it since the fix. Watch for the
   opaque/translucent phase gate (gl_rsurf.c) doing the right thing now that the translucent
   half is actually visible.
2. PARTICLES through OIT (r_part.c draws inside the pass).
3. The MSAA path. oit_resolve_prog_msaa is a separate program selected when oit_samples > 1;
   the fix is in the shared C code so it should apply, but it has never been exercised.
4. Real hardware. uhexen2-a0hp's Iris Xe report was written off as a driver quirk and turns
   out to have been this bug, so Mathuzzz's Windows box is worth a pass.
5. Sorting quality. WBOIT is an approximation -- the z4r1 measurement showed OIT frames a few
   percent brighter than the sorted path. Decide whether that is acceptable as a default or
   whether r_oit stays opt-in.

## Then

If it holds up, delete the force-reset and decide the default. r_oit stays 0 by default
either way unless 5 says otherwise -- this bead is about letting the setting persist, not
about turning OIT on for everyone.
notes:
DONE in 5fea5a5c4. Force-reset removed; r_oit still DEFAULTS to 0, it just persists now.

1. TRANSLUCENT WATER -- verified. keep.bsp, r_wateralpha 0.5, 12 shots cross-matched to
   cancel animation phase. Camera placed deliberately: parsed the BSP2 leaf lump for
   CONTENTS_WATER volumes, took the largest (centre 2836,2870, z -164..7) and used
   'noclip; setpos 2836 2470 200 40 90 0' so the frame is mostly water rather than whatever
   the spawn happens to face -- the first attempt spawned in a stone room and measured
   nothing, which is worth knowing before repeating this.
     r_oit 0 vs 1: mean|d| 0.4874, max 116, 22.0% of pixels
     within-run animation envelope: 1.4955
   Below the envelope, roughly balanced brighter/darker (31139 vs 33288 px, mean signed
   -0.65). WBOIT approximating the blend, not a defect.

2. PARTICLES/SPRITES -- verified as part of z4r1: r_oit 1 now tracks r_oit 0 frame for frame
   (peak mean luma x10 563 vs 556) where before the fix it was flat at 283.

3. MSAA PATH -- STILL UNEXERCISED, and unreachable for a reason worth stating precisely,
   because my first diagnosis of it was wrong. It is NOT a config-reading problem: proved by
   setting two early-read cvars in the same config.cfg in one run -- vid_config_consize "512"
   came out as 512 while vid_config_fsaa "4" came out as 0.
   The actual cause: VID_SetMode (gl_vidsdl.c) sets its multisample local to 0 unconditionally
   (window MSAA deliberately unwanted, per uhexen2-zroc) and then does
   Cvar_SetValueQuick(&vid_config_fsaa, multisample), writing that 0 into the cvar PP_CreateFBO
   reads for its FBO sample count. So the MSAA FBO branch is unreachable, oit_samples stays 0,
   and oit_resolve_prog_msaa can never be selected. Filed as uhexen2-eh1c -- much broader than
   OIT, and it also erases the player's setting in config.cfg on quit.
   Mitigating for THIS bead: the z4r1 fix sits in OIT_EndTranslucency's shared C code, ahead of
   the MSAA/non-MSAA program choice, so it covers both resolve programs by construction.

4. REAL HARDWARE -- not done, needs Mathuzzz. Worth a pass now that the setting persists,
   which is precisely what makes such a pass possible.

5. SORTING QUALITY -- measured rather than argued: OIT reads a few percent different from the
   sorted path (sprite frames slightly brighter, water roughly balanced). Acceptable for an
   opt-in setting, which is why the default stays 0.

VERIFIED: with r_oit "1" archived in config.cfg, startup now reports r_oit is 1. Before this
commit it would have been silently reset to 0.
close_reason: Closed

title: Verify the lightmap gutter on a large map, and check Garrett's screenshots against it
description:
Carried over from uhexen2-jwzf, which closed on its fix (c10eb1e40 + f38654033) once the bilinear regression frame was measured clean (mean|d| 0.0007, max 1 LSB). Two of that bead's three verification items were never done.

## 1. Large-map page-ceiling test

The gutter makes padding cost superlinear on small rects, and most Quake/Hexen II surfaces
are tiny (4x4 -> 8x8). demo1 measured 4 -> 10 pages, a 2.5x multiplier, and MAX_LIGHTMAPS was
raised 512 -> 1536 on 3x headroom chosen from that SINGLE sample.

That multiplier depends entirely on the surface-size distribution of the map. SoT tibet is the
map that motivated the previous ceiling raise and is the real test of both the multiplier and
whether 1536 is enough. Retail data + mods are at /home/josh/hexen2.

Load it and read the 'Lightmaps: N/1536 pages' line. If N is anywhere near 1536 on a real map,
the headroom is not headroom. AllocBlock Sys_Errors when it runs out, so this fails hard, not
gracefully.

## 2. Garrett's screenshots

Still unexamined. jwzf was filed off Spoike's Discord remark and a reading of the code, not off
the actual images. The open question is whether Garrett's 'bright lines cutting through squares
of area' follow SURFACE BOUNDARIES (this bug, now fixed) or run along DIAGONAL SHADOW EDGES
(lightmap-resolution stepping, which is inherent and which cubic filtering is meant to REDUCE,
per Spoike's own framing).

If it is the latter, jwzf never was his bug and the report is still open. Worth settling before
telling him it is fixed.

Note his all-yellow report may also be a stale .lit -- uhexen2-2mwz now prints a console line
that says so outright, so ask him for the console output too. And uhexen2-6rqa (fullbright masks
turned on engine-wide) landed after his screenshots, so anything he sends from a newer build is
brighter for an unrelated reason.
notes:
ITEM 1 (large-map page ceiling) ANSWERED 2026-08-15 -- the ceiling is fine, with room to spare.

Loaded the four largest SoT maps on the post-gutter build and read the Lightmaps line:

  courtyard   189/1536 pages (260x260), atlas 2080x6240
  tibet       182/1536 pages (260x260), atlas 2080x5980
  cathedral   148/1536 pages (260x260), atlas 2080x4940
  Arena       145/1536 pages (260x260), atlas 2080x4940

Worst case is 189, i.e. 12% of the ceiling and roughly 8x headroom. tibet -- the map that
motivated the previous ceiling raise and the one this bead specifically called out -- is not
even the worst of the set.

So the 1536 chosen off demo1's single 4 -> 10 sample holds up on real content, and AllocBlock
is nowhere near Sys_Error-ing. No action needed on MAX_LIGHTMAPS.

Worth noting the atlas is now 2080x6240 on courtyard, an 8-column layout 24 rows deep. That
is a legal NPOT 2D texture and GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE covers the outer border, but it is a much
taller texture than anything the pre-gutter build produced (demo1 was 2048x256). Nothing
observed wrong with it -- recorded because it is the number that grew most, not because it

title: Mod_LoadLighting accepts a size-mismatched .lit file without validation
description:
## Problem

`Mod_LoadLighting` in `engine/h2shared/gl_model.c` loads LordHavoc-format `.lit` colored-lightmap sidecars (`maps/<name>.lit`, QLIT magic + version 1). The function validates the magic and version (gl_model.c:810-822) but then loads the entire file without checking that it contains the correct number of luxels for this BSP.

## Impact

`.lit` files for Hexen II are community-authored and frequently built against a different compile of the map than the one the player has. Any recompile shifts every luxel, so a stale `.lit` is not merely "slightly off" — every surface reads another map's lightmap data at an arbitrary offset. Symptoms include uniform bizarre tints across the level and potential reads past the end of the hunk allocation when the `.lit` is shorter than expected.

Alias models are hit hardest because `AliasModelGetLightInfo` (engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:1285) calls `R_LightPointColor`, which samples the same lightmap under the entity origin and applies the RGB nearly straight onto the model skin instead of multiplying it against a wall texture — a corrupt or misaligned `.lit` turns whole player models a flat solid color.

## Solution

Port the QuakeSpasm/Ironwail check: before accepting the data, require `8 + l->filelen*3 == com_filesize`. On mismatch:
1. Call `Hunk_FreeToLowMark(mark)`
2. Issue a console message naming both expected and actual byte counts (e.g., "Outdated .lit file (%s should be %u bytes, not %u)")
3. Fall through to the existing `_load_internal` label to expand the BSP's white lighting to greyscale

Note: both the default blend path (gl_model.c:825-829) and the `gl_coloredlight == 2` path (gl_model.c:836-881) need this guard, since the latter both reads and writes into the `.lit` buffer.

## Discovery Context

Surfaced 2026-08-15 while addressing a Discord screenshot from tester Garrett (Monolyth-42), who reported an all-yellow color scheme in-game. A stale-`.lit` mismatch is a plausible cause alongside deliberate warm-tinted lighting packs. This fix will provide users a diagnostic console message to identify the problem.
notes:
FIXED in 768e647b5.

Mod_LoadLighting (h2shared/gl_model.c) now requires 8 + l->filelen*3 == the .lit's
file size after the magic and version checks; on mismatch it frees to the mark,
prints 'Outdated .lit file (<name> should be N bytes, not M)' and falls through to
_load_internal for the greyscale expansion. Guards both the gl_coloredlight 1 path
and the ==2 blend path, since the check sits above both.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION from the QuakeSpasm/Ironwail check: skipped when l->filelen is
0. This engine has an explicit 'No white light data. Using colored only' path that a
strict check would kill, and with no lighting lump there is no expected size to
compare against anyway.

fs_filesize is copied into a local right after FS_LoadHunkFile rather than read at
the point of use -- it describes only the last FS call.

VERIFIED headless on demo1 (lighting lump 198601 bytes -> 595811 expected):
- 108-byte QLIT rejected: 'Outdated .lit file (maps/demo1.lit should be 595811 bytes,
  not 108)', map still loads on internal lighting.
- correctly sized QLIT still accepted: 'maps/demo1.lit loaded' / 'Loaded colored
  light (32-bit)'.
- no .lit present: unchanged.

Does not confirm Garrett's all-yellow screenshot was a stale .lit -- it gives him a
console line that will say so if it was.
close_reason: Closed

title: Magic missile draws a black square: base-game ball.mdl is missing EF_HOLEY
description:
The Necromancer's magic missile (models/ball.mdl) renders as an opaque black quad with the glowing ball in the middle.

Root cause is a data bug Raven shipped: ball.mdl in data1/pak0.pak declares flags 0x00090000 = EF_FACE_VIEW | EF_MAGICMISSILE and no transparency mode at all. It is an 8-vertex / 4-triangle billboard whose skin is a radial glow painted on palette index 0, built identically to star.mdl, glowball.mdl and handfx.mdl -- all three of which are EF_HOLEY (0x4000). Without a transparency bit Mod_LoadAllSkins picks an opaque tex_mode and R_DrawAliasModel takes the opaque branch, so index 0 stays black.

Raven fixed it themselves in the mission pack: portals/pak3.pak ships ball.mdl as RAPO v50 with flags 0x00084000 = EF_HOLEY | EF_MAGICMISSILE. That copy wins whenever portals/ is on the searchpath, which is why the black box only appears for base-game-only installs (repro needs -noportals).

Fix: Mod_FixupMissingModelFlags in engine/h2shared/gl_model.c adds EF_HOLEY to models/ball.mdl at load time, before Mod_LoadAllSkins reads mod->flags, and only when the loaded copy declares no transparency mode -- so mod-supplied ball.mdl files (e.g. Shadows of Turmoil's, already EF_HOLEY) are untouched.
close_reason:
Fixed in 0d020a9ca (on master). Mod_FixupMissingModelFlags in engine/h2shared/gl_model.c:2979 adds EF_HOLEY to models/ball.mdl when the loaded header declares no transparency mode at all (EF_TRANSPARENT | EF_HOLEY | EF_SPECIAL_TRANS all clear), so a mod shipping its own already-fixed or deliberately different ball.mdl -- Shadows of Turmoil's, for one -- is untouched.

Verified the call ordering the fix depends on: it runs at gl_model.c:3326 in Mod_LoadAliasModelNew and :3524 in Mod_LoadAliasModel, both ahead of their Mod_LoadAllSkins calls at :3383 and :3575. That matters because Mod_LoadAllSkins reads mod->flags to pick the skin's tex_mode; patching after it would leave the opaque texture already uploaded.

title: Console tab completion for command arguments (map, changelevel, game, record, playdemo, timedemo)
description:
## Why This Issue Exists

User requested tab completion of argument values in the console for commands like `map`, `changelevel`, `game`, etc. Currently, only command/cvar/alias names complete; argument completion is blocked.

## Design: (Command, Argument Index) Keyed Completion Table

The original design completed only the first argument of specific commands. The scope has expanded to handle multi-argument commands where different positional arguments require different completers:

- **`map` arg1** → ListMaps (map names)
- **`changelevel` arg1** → ListMaps (map names)
- **`game` arg1** → ListGames (mod directory names)
- **`record` arg1** → ListDemos, **arg2** → ListMaps (demoname, optional map override)
- **`playdemo` arg1** → ListDemos (demo filenames)
- **`timedemo` arg1** → ListDemos (demo filenames; registered at `engine/hexen2/cl_main.c:1186-1187`)

The table in keys.c now uses (command, argument_index) as the lookup key, not just command.

## Implementation Components

### 1. ListMaps (Existing pattern, reusable)
- Extract existing enumeration from `FS_Maplist_f` / `processMapname` (`engine/h2shared/quakefs.c:1376-1485`)
- Signature: `int ListMaps(const char *prefix, const char **buf, int pos)` (matches `ListCommands`/`ListCvars`/`ListAlias` at `engine/h2shared/cmd.c:843`)
- Scans pak searchpaths and loose `maps/*.bsp` entries
- Dedupes and strips `.bsp` suffix
- Callers have explicit control over lifetime via `FS_FreeMaplist()`

### 2. ListGames (New)
- Extract mod-directory scan from menu code into quakefs.c
- Current menu code at `engine/hexen2/menu.c:4830` (`M_IsModDir`) and `engine/hexen2/menu.c:4858` (`M_ScanMods`)
- Test: `progs.dat` or any `pak0-9.pak` present in candidate directory
- **Deliberate design difference**: Completer must offer all mod directories that `Host_Game_f` (`engine/h2shared/quakefs.c:1543`) accepts. The menu excludes `data1`, `portals`, and `hw` for UI reasons, but the completer must not — it reflects what the command accepts.

### 3. ListDemos (New)
- Demo enumeration does not exist in current codebase
- Mirrors ListMaps pattern but with `.dem` suffix
- Demos stored at gamedir *root* (not subdirectory like `maps/`)
- Searchpath walk must include root-level entries
- **Open question for verification**: `CL_Record_f` writes demos via `FS_MakePath_BUF(FS_USERDIR, ...)` (`engine/hexen2/cl_demo.c:306-311`). User-directory demos must be reachable by searchpath walk; needs verification that they appear in enumeration.

## Known Hazards

Both write paths in `CompleteCommand()` hardcode `workline + 1`, which clobbers the command word when completing an argument. Must fix or work around.

## Definition of Done

- ListMaps(), FS_FreeMaplist() implemented in quakefs.c
- ListGames() implemented in quakefs.c (extracted from menu.c)
- ListDemos() implemented in quakefs.c with root-level .dem search
- (command, argument_index) table wired in keys.c for all 6 commands
- Completion respects prefix filtering and dedupes
- Tested interactively: tab after each command and argument position completes correctly
- Demo directory enumeration verified to include user-directory entries
close_reason:
Landed in commit afcc75e68 ("complete map, mod and demo names when you tab in the console") on master.

## What Landed

**engine/h2shared/quakefs.c** — Shared name-listing layer (FS_ScanFiles, addListName, addFileName, fillMatches, FS_FreeNameList) backing new ListMaps, ListDemos, ListGames, plus FS_IsGamedir. FS_Maplist_f rewritten to call into it; the maplist console command's output was verified byte-identical to a pre-change baseline build on real game data.

**engine/h2shared/quakefs.h** — Declarations under #if !defined(SERVERONLY), with the ownership contract documented (one shared list; pointers valid until the next List*() or FS_FreeNameList()).

**engine/hexen2/keys.c** — arg_completion_types table keyed on (command, argument slot) and a reworked CompleteCommand.

**engine/hexen2/menu.c** — M_IsModDir replaced by shared FS_IsGamedir; Mods menu rendering unchanged.

## Bug Found and Fixed During Review

Completion was writing at hardcoded workline + 1, which is user-controlled. Neither write-back path was bounded against MAXCMDLINE (256). The longest-common-prefix path's strncpy reached key_linepos 314 — 59 bytes past the end of the row, corrupting the neighbouring key_lines entry — reproduced as SIGSEGV and AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow. Both paths now clamped with the clamp applied before the copy; a no-room case does nothing rather than truncating typed input.

## Verification

nix build clean on both .#nixos and .#h2ded; all compiler warnings confirmed pre-existing by diffing against change hunts; logic harness covering all 7 table rows, refused slots, mid-line edits, repeated TAB, consecutive spaces, boundary sweep of 755 near-full lines, passing plain and under ASAN at edit_line 0 and 31.

## Residual, Not Done

A literal TAB keypress was never driven (needs interactive SDL key events). The completion logic is harness-verified and listers are verified against real game data in a live engine, but the keypress-to-CompleteCommand wiring (pre-existing code) was not exercised end to end. Also unwired but now one table row each: exec (.cfg), save/load, sky. Recorded as follow-up P4 issue.

title: [bug] r_lightmap_bicubic samples outside each surface's lightmap rect — no gutter, no clamp
description:
Spoike's remark on Discord — that cubic lightmap filtering "requires more samples, apparently samples outside of the per-surface lightmap data" — applies to this engine verbatim. Confirmed by reading the code; not yet confirmed against Garrett's screenshots, which have not been examined.

## The arithmetic
LM_SurfaceLightmapUV (engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c) emits, page-local:

    uv = (light_s*16 + local + 8) / (BLOCK_WIDTH*16)

so in texel space that is light_s + local/16 + 0.5. The '+ 8' is a half-luxel inset and it is sized for exactly one thing: hardware bilinear, whose footprint is +/-0.5 texel. It keeps bilinear inside the surface's own rect and has no margin beyond that.

GLSL_BICUBIC_LM_FN (engine/h2shared/gl_shader.c) then computes tc = uv*ts - 0.5 = light_s + local/16, and its four Sigg/Hadwiger taps sit at floor(tc)+0.5+h0 and floor(tc)+0.5+h1 with h0 in [-1,0] and h1 in [1,2] texels. Each is itself a bilinear fetch, so the real footprint is the 4x4 B-spline support: texels floor(tc)-1 through floor(tc)+2.

  - at the near edge (local = 0): reads light_s - 1, one luxel BEFORE the rect
  - at the far edge (local = 16*(smax-1)): reads light_s + smax + 1, two luxels PAST it

## Why that is not harmless here
AllocBlock (gl_rsurf.c) packs surfaces edge-to-edge with no gutter — it records allocated[texnum][*x+i] = best + h and reserves no border. So the luxels bicubic reaches into belong to a DIFFERENT, unrelated surface, or to never-written page space. BicubicLightmap does no clamping of its taps to the surface rect; there is nothing anywhere that bounds them.

With the atlas on (gl_lmatlas 1, the default) there is a second and worse boundary: LM_SurfaceLightmapUV remaps into an 8-column atlas, so a surface at a page edge has bicubic reaching into an adjacent PAGE — a wholly unrelated set of surfaces. GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE on the atlas texture only protects the outer border of the whole atlas, not any internal page or rect boundary.

Expected appearance: bright or dark seams along surface boundaries, on a grid, which is consistent with a report of "bright lines cutting through squares of area" — though see the caveat below about which artifact that report actually is.

## Distinct from uhexen2-ebpk
ebpk is the Clean preset, which sets r_lightmap_bicubic 0, and its reporter said bicubic made things look slightly BETTER. So ebpk is a bilinear-domain or non-lightmap artifact. Same family (atlas rects with no padding), different trigger. Fixing this one should not be expected to fix that one.

## Fix options, in rough order of correctness
1. Gutter in AllocBlock: reserve a 2-luxel border per surface and fill it by edge-extension when the lightmap is built/updated. The standard fix, and the only one that makes the sample legal rather than merely bounded. Costs atlas space, worst for many small surfaces, and touches the allocator that uhexen2-vfvh and uhexen2-iihz already had to be careful with.
2. Clamp the taps in the shader: pass each surface's rect as a vertex attribute (the world VBO already exists) and clamp the four fetches into it. No atlas cost; adds a vec4 per vertex and makes the filter slightly wrong at edges rather than very wrong.
3. Fade bicubic toward bilinear within 2 luxels of a rect edge. Cheap, hides it, does not fix it.

Currently mitigated only by the default: r_lightmap_bicubic is 0, and only the Modern and Ultra display presets turn it on. Anyone on those presets has this.

## Before implementing
Get the actual screenshots and check whether the reported lines follow surface boundaries (this bug) or run along diagonal shadow edges (lightmap resolution stepping, which is inherent and not a bug). Spoike's own framing was that cubic filtering REDUCES diagonal stepping — so if that is what Garrett has, this bead is a caveat on the mitigation rather than the cause of his report.
notes:
FIXED in c10eb1e40 with the gutter approach, stride bug fixed in f38654033.

AllocBlock reserves the surface rect grown by LM_GUTTER (2) on all four sides and returns the
inner origin, so callers still deal in unpadded coordinates. LM_FillGutter edge-extends the
block into the padding on every rebuild (not just load -- a stale gutter beside fresh luxels
is its own seam). LM_ExpandDirtyRect grows by the same amount, at the one place rather than
the six call sites.

LIMITS RAISED (user approved): BLOCK_WIDTH/HEIGHT 256 -> 260 (MAX_SURFACE_LIGHTMAP 255, so
padded worst case 259; no power-of-two requirement anywhere). MAX_LIGHTMAPS 512 -> 1536
(padding is superlinear on small rects; demo1 measured 4 -> 10 pages, 3x headroom chosen).
COST +1.09 MB static bookkeeping.

=== VERIFICATION ITEM 1 NOW CLOSED (2026-08-15) ===

The open question was the bilinear regression frame: r_lightmap_bicubic 0 against the
pre-gutter baseline, expected pixel-identical BY REASONING rather than measurement. Measured
now, and the reasoning holds.

Method: deterministic headless burst on demo1/Blackmarsh, setpos 480 -352 40 0 90 0,
host_framerate 0.05, r_lightmap_bicubic 0, gl_lmatlas 1, 30 frames per build, all 30x30 pairs
cross-matched so lightstyle phase cannot masquerade as a difference. Within-run animation
envelope measured at mean|d| 0.76, i.e. the noise floor is known and small.

  35f228fe8 (pre-gutter) vs f38654033 (gutter + stride fix):
      best mean|d| = 0.0007, max|d| = 1, 0.09% of pixels differ

One LSB on a tenth of a percent of pixels. Bilinear's +/-0.5 texel footprint never enters the
padding, as claimed. Page count went 4/512 (256x256, atlas 2048x256) -> 10/1536 (260x260,
atlas 2080x520) and the visible result did not move.

That comparison ALSO caught an unrelated regression in a later commit -- HEAD differs from
pre-gutter by mean|d| 7.90 across 38% of pixels, all of it fullbright masks, none of it the
gutter. Filed as uhexen2-6rqa.

=== STILL OPEN, MOVED TO A FOLLOW-UP BEAD ===

Items 2 (large-map page-ceiling test) and 3 (Garrett's screenshots) are untouched and are now
tracked separately so this bead can close on the fix itself.
close_reason: Closed

title: In-game Classic/Updated gamecode selector
description:
Requested: an in-game option to choose between the original gamecode and this fork's fixed gamecode, rather than the command-line-only -vanillaprogs switch that exists today.

## What exists already
PR_BundledProgsPath (engine/h2shared/pr_edict.c) loads our progs.dat from beside the executable in place of the install's, for data1 and portals, when the install is GAME_REGISTERED and the player has not put their own copy in the userdir. -vanillaprogs turns that off. Its comment argued against ever making it a cvar on two grounds:
  1. PR_LoadProgs runs on every map spawn, so a live cvar would let the gamecode change between levels of a single campaign.
  2. CVAR_ARCHIVE would write an engine-packaging decision into the player's config tree.

Ground 1 is real and is handled by latching (below). Ground 2 no longer applies once this is a deliberate player choice with a menu entry rather than something the packager decided for them.

## Design
- cvar sv_gamecode, CVAR_ARCHIVE, default 1 (Updated = current behaviour, so nothing changes for anyone who does not touch it).
- Latched: PR_LatchGamecode() copies the cvar into a static, and is called ONLY when a new game starts. changelevel, restart and savegame loads must not re-latch — a campaign has to finish on the gamecode it started with, and a savegame's progdefs CRC is validated against whatever is loaded, so swapping mid-run would leave the player unable to load their own saves.
- -vanillaprogs still outranks the cvar, so a packager or a bug report can take engine gamecode out of the picture entirely.
- Menu entry under Options > Game, labelled Classic / Updated, hidden when no bundle is present (PR_GamecodeAvailable) because there would be nothing to switch to.

## Scope note
This selects between the install's gamecode and ours, for BOTH data1 and portals. It is deliberately not wired to jsHexen2-progs: that repo contains only portals/, so it cannot back a Classic/Updated choice for the base game, which is what most players run. The mechanism has room for a third value if a vendored variant is added later.
close_reason: Implemented in ebd68cc11. sv_gamecode cvar (CVAR_ARCHIVE, default 1=Updated), latched at new-game only via PR_LatchGamecode from Host_Map_f so campaigns and savegames keep the gamecode they started with. Menu row under Options > Game, hidden when no bundle is available. -vanillaprogs still outranks it. Verified end to end: sv_gamecode 1 loads the bundled progs (crc 24008), sv_gamecode 0 loads the install's (crc 17499).

title: ES tier reports no GL errors at all — the debug callback is GL 4.3 only
description:
GL_Init installs an error reporter only on the desktop tier (engine/h2shared/gl_vidsdl.c):

    #ifndef USE_GLES
      glDebugMessageCallback_fp = SDL_GL_GetProcAddress("glDebugMessageCallback");
      if (glDebugMessageCallback_fp) { glEnable(GL_DEBUG_OUTPUT); ... }
    #endif

KHR_debug is GL 4.3 / GLES 3.2, and the engine only asks SDL for an ES 3.0 context, so the ES tier gets nothing — no callback, and no glGetError polling either. Every GL error it makes is discarded silently.

This is not hypothetical. uhexen2-6yh1 was 55 failed texture uploads on every single map load, blacking out the status bar, conback, the sky and the liquid warps, and it produced not one line of console output. It was found by eyeballing a screenshot against a desktop control, and root-caused only after hand-instrumenting glTexImage2D with a temporary glGetError probe. A polled check would have printed it on the first run, years ago, in the browser.

## Suggested shape
A GL_CheckErrors()-style poll, called once per frame (and ideally after init and after each map load), that drains glGetError and prints the code plus a caller tag. Cheap: one glGetError per frame is negligible, and glthread already forces a sync for it only when there is an error queued.

Gating: match the existing desktop behaviour rather than inventing a new cvar — the desktop callback is unconditional once the entry point is found, so an unconditional per-frame poll on the ES tier is the parallel choice. If per-frame is judged too eager, gate on developer, but note that the default-off case is exactly the case that hid uhexen2-6yh1.

Worth also probing for KHR_debug at runtime: Mesa's desktop ES context reports itself as OpenGL ES 3.2 and does expose the extension, so on that configuration the real callback can be used and the poll is only the fallback. WebGL2 has no equivalent, so the poll is what actually covers the browser.

## Measurement to reproduce the scale of it
With a temporary drain-then-check probe around GL_Upload32's glTexImage2D on demo1 (pre-fix build), 55 uploads failed outright and a further ~710 errors were observed already queued at the top of subsequent uploads — largely the mipmap-level uploads of the same broken textures. Post-fix that should fall to near zero, which is also a decent acceptance test for this bead: instrument, load demo1, expect a clean error queue.
close_reason: Implemented in 602b5098f. GL_PollErrors drains and reports the GL error queue at the end of GL_Init and once per frame in GL_EndRendering, with a 32-report budget reset per GL_Init. Tested both directions: fires GL_INVALID_OPERATION with the RGB8 bug reintroduced, silent once fixed. Desktop, GLES and WASM builds all green.

title: [bug] Status bar background renders as solid black on the GL ES tier
description:
On a -DUSE_GLES=ON build (uhexen2-0py6), in-game on demo1/Blackmarsh, the status bar area is a solid black rectangle. The numeric readouts and the small item boxes draw on top of it correctly; the ornate bar artwork behind them is missing. Desktop GL 4.3 from the same commit, same map, same camera, same config renders the bar correctly.

The quad IS being drawn -- the bar occludes the 3D view exactly where it should, it is just black -- so this is a texture sampling as black, not geometry that failed to emit.

## What has been ruled out
- NOT caused by post-processing. Re-ran with v_gamma 1, v_contrast 1, r_scale 1, r_softemu 0, gl_fxaa 0, r_waterwarp 0, r_motionblur 0, r_hdr 0, r_oit 0, r_bloom 0, so PP_NeedsPostProcess() is false and pp_active never gets set. Frame is pixel-identical to the PP-on one, bar still black.
- NOT a regression from the ES-tier fixes in uhexen2-7wdv/-g63k/-dfay/-vp8t/-3cke. Before those the tier could not reach a rendered frame at all on the desktop, so there is no 'before' where this worked. It is pre-existing, and it applies equally to the WASM build, where nobody would have noticed because the ES tier was never rendering a correct frame anyway.
- NOT a general Draw_CachePic failure. The Hexen II title screen and loading plaque -- also .lmp pics through Draw_CachePic -- render perfectly on the ES tier, full detail and correct colours.
- No GL errors reported in the console log for the whole run.

## The lead
The two missing pics are gfx/topbar1.lmp and gfx/topbar2.lmp (sbar.c:301-302). They are the only sbar elements drawn through Sbar_DrawPic -> Draw_PicCropped (gl_draw.c); the elements that DO render use other draw paths.

Draw_PicCropped is distinctive in two ways worth checking first:
1. it emits through GL_ImmBegin/GL_ImmEnd(GL_QUADS, &gl_shader_2d) -- the immediate-mode emulator, whose quad-to-triangle conversion and vertex-attrib setup both have USE_GLES branches (gl_vbo.c:79, :101, :171, :354, :545, the ES side using legacy glVertexAttribPointer rather than glVertexAttribFormat/glBindVertexBuffer)
2. it flips GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_S/T to GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE around the draw and sets them back to GL_REPEAT immediately after -- which, if GL_ImmEnd defers rather than draws synchronously, would apply the restore before the draw

Draw_SubPicCropped just below it has the same shape and is presumably affected identically.

notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED.

Not Draw_PicCropped and not the immediate-mode emulator — the lead in the original description was wrong. It is the texture upload.

engine/h2shared/glquake.h defined gl_solid_format as 0x8051 (GL_RGB8) for textures without TEX_ALPHA, and GL_Upload32 (gl_draw.c) always passes format=GL_RGBA, type=GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE for the pixel data. Desktop GL permits any format with a sized internal format and just drops the alpha. GL ES 3.0 does not: it validates the (internalformat, format, type) triple against a fixed table in which sized GL_RGB8 admits only format GL_RGB. So the call fails with GL_INVALID_OPERATION and the texture object is left with no image — it samples black.

MEASURED, on demo1 with a temporary glGetError probe around the glTexImage2D call (drained first, so no stale errors are miscounted): 55 uploads failed, 100% of them internal=0x8051, 100% of them error 0x0502 (GL_INVALID_OPERATION), and ZERO failures among the 0x8058 (GL_RGBA8) uploads.
