Affected: conback, both status bar halves, upsky, the liquid warps (*lowlight, *rtex078, *rtex346) and a number of model skins. The world looked fine only because most world textures carry TEX_ALPHA and so took the RGBA8 path.

FIX: gl_solid_format is GL_RGBA8 on the ES tier. One byte per texel more, no other cost — the source data is already RGBA and the alpha it now keeps is the 255 the loader wrote. Desktop keeps GL_RGB8 unchanged, so the uhexen2-khsa reasoning in the surrounding comment still holds there.

VERIFIED: same map, same camera, ES vs desktop. Status bar now pixel-matches. Whole-frame RMSE against the desktop control fell from 4.05% to 1.23% (residual is precision/dither, not missing content).

WHY IT SURVIVED: the ES tier has no GL error reporting at all — glDebugMessageCallback is GL 4.3 and its setup is behind !USE_GLES — so 55 failed uploads per map load produced not one line of output. Filed separately.
close_reason: Root-caused to gl_solid_format = GL_RGB8, which GL ES 3.0 rejects when paired with GL_RGBA pixel data. Fixed in 0ac21b596; ES status bar now pixel-matches desktop and whole-frame RMSE fell from 4.05% to 1.23%.

title: Verify the ES-tier render fixes in an actual browser (WebGL2)
description:
uhexen2-0py6 made the GL ES 3.0 tier reachable on the desktop and that immediately turned up five latent bugs, four of which had been silently degrading the WASM build: no post-processing at all (uhexen2-7wdv), no order-independent translucency (uhexen2-g63k), a failed skeletal shader compile on every startup (uhexen2-dfay), 1 MB of dead SSBO + 1 MB of dead BSS (uhexen2-vp8t), and broken screenshots (uhexen2-3cke).

All five are fixed and verified against Mesa 26.1.5 on a desktop GLES 3.2 context (radeonsi), which is the closest proxy available here. None of them has been run in a browser, because there is no browser in this environment.

What needs checking, in one session with the WASM build loaded in Chrome and Firefox:
1. The shader log. Every program that reports OK on desktop GLES should report OK on WebGL2. The risk is real but narrow — WebGL2 is stricter than desktop ES about a few things (no implicit conversions, stricter loop/indexing rules, and it validates against the GLSL ES 3.00 spec rather than whatever the desktop driver tolerates).
2. That post-processing visibly does something: gamma/contrast, FXAA, bloom, softemu palettization. Previously all silently off.
3. That translucent surfaces composite through the OIT path rather than falling back.
4. bayer16's bitfieldReverse polyfill specifically, since it is new hand-written GLSL and the only place the ES and desktop shader bodies differ rather than just their headers. softemu 1 with dither on is the way to exercise it.
5. A screenshot, to confirm the RGBA readback works there too.

Build: nix develop -f shell-wasm.nix, then emcmake cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DUSE_CODEC_VORBIS=OFF -DUSE_ALSA=OFF -DUSE_SDL3_STATIC=ON, emmake make. Produces a 1.7 MB hexenwail.wasm; confirmed building as of this bead.

Alternatively, a desktop -DUSE_GLES=ON build is now the cheap way to catch the same class of bug without a browser at all (documented in docs/COMPILE).

title: Screenshot and screenhash read pixels as GL_RGB, which GL ES 3.0 does not guarantee — ES screenshots are a green smear
description:
SCR_ScreenShot_f and SCR_ScreenHash_f (engine/h2shared/gl_screen.c) both call

    glReadPixels(glx, gly, glwidth, glheight, GL_RGB, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, ...)

GL ES 3.0 guarantees exactly ONE accepted format/type pair for glReadPixels on a normalized fixed-point target -- GL_RGBA/GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE -- plus a second, implementation-chosen pair that has to be queried via GL_IMPLEMENTATION_COLOR_READ_FORMAT / _TYPE. GL_RGB is a desktop-GL spelling and is not required to work.

Observed on a -DUSE_GLES=ON build against Mesa 26.1.5/llvmpipe (uhexen2-0py6): the TGA came out as a fine vertical green/black interference pattern -- the signature of a 3-byte destination walked with 4-byte source stride -- rather than the frame. Same defect would apply to WebGL2, where screenshots were simply never exercised.

Fixed by reading GL_RGBA on BOTH tiers and packing down at the CPU, rather than forking: desktop GL accepts RGBA equally, the extra byte per pixel exists only in a scratch buffer during the call, and one path means the ES tier cannot silently diverge again. For SCR_ScreenShot_f the pack also folds in the RGB->BGR swap the TGA needs, replacing the separate in-place swap loop. For SCR_ScreenHash_f the alpha byte is skipped and the RGB bytes are hashed in the original order, so hashes recorded by the uhexen2-8pzr Hi-Z regression sweep remain comparable.
close_reason: Closed

title: OIT fragment variants cannot compile on the GL ES tier — preamble spliced ahead of the precision qualifier
description:
GL_CompileOITFragShader (engine/h2shared/gl_shader.c) builds the OIT variant of a fragment shader by splitting the source at the first newline — assumed to be the end of the #version line — and splicing its MRT preamble in there.

On the ES tier GLSL_FRAG_HEADER is "#version 300 es\nprecision mediump float;\n", so the first newline lands BEFORE the precision declaration. The preamble, which declares 'vec4 fragColor', two 'out vec4' targets and several floats, therefore ends up ahead of it. GLSL ES requires a default precision to be declared before the first use of the type, so all three OIT programs (world, alias, particle) failed with:

  0:3(1): error: No precision specified in this scope for type `vec4'

i.e. no order-independent translucency at all on the ES tier. Desktop is unaffected — its header has no precision line, so the split point was always correct there.

Fix: after skipping the #version line, keep skipping while the next line begins with "precision ". No-op on desktop.

Surfaced by uhexen2-0py6 (-DUSE_GLES=ON desktop build). Related: uhexen2-7wdv, the same class of bug in gl_postprocess.c.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] r_fullbright does not affect world surfaces and r_lightmap is a dead cvar — the two standard lighting-debug switches both no-op
description:
Both of the Quake-family cvars that a renderer investigation reaches for first are non-functional in the GL 4.3 pipeline, silently.

r_fullbright (engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:120) is read in exactly two places, and neither is the world: gl_rmain.c:1660 and gl_rmain.c:2945, both gating the ALIAS-model additive fullbright re-draw pass. The world fragment shaders -- sworld_frag and sworld_frag_opaque in engine/h2shared/gl_shader.c -- have no fullbright input at all. So 'r_fullbright 1' leaves every brush surface exactly as lit as before.

r_lightmap (gl_rmain.c:121) is registered at gl_rmisc.c:263 and then never read anywhere. grep for 'r_lightmap\.' across the tree returns nothing (r_lightmap_bicubic is a different cvar and does work).

MEASURED, not just grepped: SoT Arena, paused so the world is frozen, 1280x960 offscreen, screenshot before and after 'r_fullbright 1'. Mean absolute luminance difference over the floor region is 0.000 -- byte-identical to the control pair taken with no cvar change at all.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE COSMETICS: uhexen2-ebpk's entire investigation plan is 'run r_fullbright 1 on the same spot; line disappears -> lightmap atlas, line persists -> lightmap theory dead'. That test cannot discriminate anything, because the cvar does not reach the domain it is supposed to isolate. Any future 'is this lighting or texture' question hits the same wall, and the answer will look like evidence.

FIX SHAPE: both are one uniform. The world programs already carry per-frame uniforms pushed to all three variants (u_overbright, u_lightmap_bicubic, gl_rmain.c:4232-4270) -- add a vec2 u_lightdebug on the same plumbing. x replaces the lightmap sample with white (r_fullbright), y replaces the diffuse sample with white and suppresses the fullbright-mask add (r_lightmap). r_fullbright must also force the overbright multiplier to 1.0 or the result is a 2x blowout.

ACCEPTANCE: 'r_fullbright 1' visibly flattens world lighting and 'r_lightmap 1' shows the lightmap alone, both measurable as a large mean-luminance delta on the frozen-Arena harness; the multiplayer cheat clamp at R_SetupFrame still applies to r_fullbright.
close_reason: Fixed in 3d7775941. Added a vec2 u_lightdebug to both world fragment shaders (sworld_frag and sworld_frag_opaque, the latter also covering the OIT variant), pushed per-frame to all three world program variants on the same plumbing u_overbright and u_lightmap_bicubic already use. x whites out the lightmap sample (r_fullbright), y whites out the diffuse sample and suppresses the fullbright mask (r_lightmap). Applied to the samples rather than the final colour so overbright, caustics, fog and the alpha test keep seeing a well-formed value, and rgb-only on the diffuse so r_lightmap cannot turn a fence into a solid sheet. r_fullbright also forces the overbright multiplier back to 1.0, since doubling an already-white lightmap blows out the texture detail the mode exists to show. Verified on the frozen-Arena harness at 1280x960 offscreen: mean frame luminance 21.76 normal / 78.40 under r_fullbright 1 / 122.83 under r_lightmap 1 / 21.78 on return, against run-to-run control noise of 0.06. Visually correct too -- fullbright shows flat-lit full texture detail with no blowout, r_lightmap shows the bare lightmap. The multiplayer cheat clamp on r_fullbright at R_SetupFrame is untouched.

title: game data1 does not roll back the mission-pack searchpath: base-game maps then run portals gamecode
description:
Returning to Hexen II from a mod through the Mods menu (or `game data1`) leaves the `portals` searchpath entry that was added as the mod's base. Since portals sits ABOVE data1, `progs.dat` keeps resolving inside portals/, and the uhexen2-8qp3 substitution — which gates on gamedir identity, now 'data1' — does not fire for it. The player silently runs mission-pack gamecode on base-game maps.

OBSERVED (GL client, offscreen, -basedir at a retail tree, engine at bb3e9480e + the uhexen2-5mhd fix):

    glhexen2 -basedir <tree> -game sot +map Arena ... +game data1
      Added packfile <tree>/data1/pak0.pak
      Added packfile <tree>/data1/pak1.pak
      Added packfile <tree>/portals/pak3.pak        <- added at startup as the mod's base
      SV_SpawnServer: Arena
      Gamecode: progs.dat from <tree>/sot/progs.dat        (H2MP/v1.12, crc 28154)
      game changed to "data1"
      SV_SpawnServer: demo1                                 <- a DATA1 map
      Gamecode: progs.dat from <tree>/portals/progs.dat    (H2MP/v1.12, crc 20799)

Expected on that last line is the data1 bundle, crc 10626 — which is exactly what a bare launch gives (docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md verification row P1). pak3 is added once at startup and never removed by the switch.

TWO SEPARATE WRONGS, and they should be fixed in that order:
1. The searchpath is wrong. data1 is the base game; portals is not part of it. Whatever added portals for the mod has to be undone when the mod is.
2. Only because of (1) does the gamecode come out wrong. Do NOT patch this in PR_LoadProgs by widening the substitution gate — that would paper over a searchpath the rest of the engine is also reading (maps, models, sounds, .cfg all resolve through the same list, so the player is getting mission-pack content on base-game maps too, not just gamecode).

THIS IS F3, AND IT WAS A DOCUMENTED PREREQUISITE. docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md's Prerequisites section lists 'Fix fs_gamedir_nopath in the mission-pack rollback (F3) — independently correct, and it removes one fail-closed corner from this feature's state space' as item 3. It was never done. F3's own section is 'fs_gamedir_nopath is reliable, with one pre-existing exception' — this is that exception, now with a reproduction.

FOUND BY: uhexen2-ctv7's B3 row (runtime gamedir switching, the F4 row no command-line test covers). B3 also turned up uhexen2-5mhd, which had to be fixed before the switch would run at all.

HARNESS NOTE for whoever picks this up: Host_Game_f calls Cbuf_Clear(), so a '+game X +map Y' command line silently loses the map. Drive the post-switch spawn from the new gamedir's autoexec.cfg — the switch ends with 'exec hexen.rc', which reaches it.

ACCEPTANCE: after -game <portals-based mod> then 'game data1', a data1 map spawns on the data1 gamecode (bundled crc 10626 on a stock build), FS_Path shows no portals entry, and 'game portals' still works afterwards.
close_reason: Fixed in ffce89f7c. FS_Init now records fs_base_nomp_searchpaths (the mark at the end of step 1, data1 only) and Host_Game_f unwinds to that instead of fs_base_searchpaths, which a -game launch had folded portals into. Portals is re-added only when the destination wants it. The three open-coded unwind loops were centralised into FS_UnwindSearchpaths, which also clears fs_portals_path_id when those entries go away (PR_LoadProgs's gate matches on it) and fixes a use-after-free in FS_Init's rollback narration. H2W collapses the two marks, since hw sits above portals and no single pointer can keep hw while dropping the mission pack. Verified headless on the retail tree at /home/josh/hexen2 -- all three acceptance criteria: -game sot then 'game data1' shows data1 alone in FS_Path and spawns demo1 on the bundled data1 progs.dat crc 10626; 'game portals' afterwards loads bundled portals crc 44043; 'game sot 1' rebuilds a path byte-identical to the launch one with no duplicate portals entry. docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md updated: F3 rewritten as two fixed exceptions, failure mode 4 and prerequisite 3 marked satisfied, B3 gets the verification table.

title: Host_Game_f probes host_parms->basedir, so runtime mod switching fails under -basedir
description:
engine/h2shared/quakefs.c :: Host_Game_f() validates the target mod directory with

    q_snprintf (path, sizeof(path), "%s/%s", host_parms->basedir, dir);
    if (Sys_FileType(path) != FS_ENT_DIRECTORY) { Con_Printf("Game directory \"%s\" not found\n", dir); return; }

and does the same again twenty lines below for the optional portals base. Every other path in that file uses the file-module's own `fs_basedir`.

Those two are not the same variable. FS_Init sets `fs_basedir = com_argv[i+1]` when -basedir is given, and `host_parms->basedir` is NEVER updated -- the only thing under the -basedir branch that writes through host_parms is `host_parms->userdir`, and only when !DO_USERDIRS. sys_unix.c and sys_win.c both set parms.basedir = cwd once at startup and nothing reassigns it. So with -basedir in play, Host_Game_f probes <cwd>/<mod> while the whole rest of the filesystem lives under <basedir>/.

SYMPTOM: every mod reports 'Game directory "<name>" not found' and the switch is refused. The Mods menu is the same code path -- menu.c:5126 issues `game "<dir>" <portals>` through Cbuf_AddText -- so the menu lists mods that FS_ enumerated from fs_basedir and then refuses to load any of them. Cross-platform: the write host_parms->basedir would need never happens on Windows either.

OBSERVED, not deduced. Found running uhexen2-ctv7's B3 row (runtime gamedir switching, the uhexen2-8qp3 F4 row that no command-line test covers) against a GL client launched with -basedir pointing at a game tree outside the install:

    Game directory "sot" not found
    Already running: data1
    Game directory "portals" not found

and the follow-up `map Arena` then failed with 'can't find maps/Arena.bsp' because the searchpath never changed.

FIX: use fs_basedir in both q_snprintf calls. It is a static in the same translation unit, so no plumbing.

WHY P2 rather than P3: this is the only way to change mods without relaunching, it is wired to a menu the user can see, and the failure is a flat refusal with a message that blames the mod. Anyone launching through a shortcut, launcher or wrapper that passes -basedir -- which is the normal shape for a non-portable install -- has a Mods menu that cannot work.

ACCEPTANCE: with -basedir set, `game sot` switches, a map from that mod spawns, `game data1` returns, and `game portals 0` reaches the mission pack. Both binaries where the command exists (it is #if !defined(SERVERONLY), so GL client only).
close_reason: Fixed in 7e0f77126. Both q_snprintf calls in Host_Game_f now use fs_basedir instead of host_parms->basedir. Verified on the GL client with -basedir pointing at a retail tree outside the install: before, 'Game directory "sot" not found' / 'Game directory "portals" not found' and the follow-up map failed with 'can't find maps/Arena.bsp'; after, 'game changed to "sot"' with Gamecode: <tree>/sot/progs.dat (crc 28154) on an Arena spawn, and 'game changed to "portals"' with Gamecode: <exedir>/../share/hexenwail/portals/progs.dat (crc 44043) on keep1. Found by uhexen2-ctv7's B3 row. Two things the next person needs and neither is obvious: 'game' is GL-client-only (#if !defined(SERVERONLY)), and Host_Game_f calls Cbuf_Clear(), so '+game X +map Y' on one command line silently loses the map — drive the post-switch spawn from the new gamedir's autoexec.cfg, which the switch reaches via its closing 'exec hexen.rc'. NOT fixed here and filed separately: the leg back from a portals-based mod. 'game data1' does not drop the portals searchpath entry, so a data1 map then spawns on portals/progs.dat instead of the data1 bundle — uhexen2-5vb6, which is F3 / prerequisite 3 of docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md.

title: Flake install path ships no bundled gamecode — nix run users get retail progs
description:
The bundled-gamecode feature (uhexen2-xsmc) reaches release-zip users but not flake users.

.#nixos's installPhase (flake.nix, the nixos = pkgs.stdenv.mkDerivation block) does 'mkdir -p $out/share/hexenwail' and then installs only bin/glhexen2 into it. Verified against a built output: /nix/store/...-hexenwail-0.8.0-beta.r1/ contains exactly bin/glhexen2 and an EMPTY share/hexenwail/ directory. Since .#nixos is packages.default and what apps.default runs, anyone doing 'nix run github:bobberb/hexenwail', 'nix profile install' or importing the flake into a NixOS config gets the engine with none of our progs.dat -- so they silently run Raven's 1997 gamecode and none of the .hc fixes (dropped backpacks, notarget, tripwire damage, and the rest recorded in gamecode/README).

Found while closing uhexen2-2tia, which removed the linux-x86_64-nixos/ tree from .#release on the grounds that NixOS users are served by the flake instead. That reasoning is sound for the binary but exposes this: the flake path is now the ONLY path for NixOS users, and it is the one path with no gamecode.

CONSTRAINT that makes this non-trivial: uhexen2-r32l's rule -- do NOT reference ${gamecode} from the engine derivation. Coupling the engine's .drv hash to the gamecode source would make every .hc edit rebuild the whole engine, which is exactly the property gamecodeSrc exists to protect. So the fix cannot be 'copy the progs into .#nixos's installPhase'.

FIX SHAPE: a separate output that composes the two without either depending on the other -- the same trick .#linux-fhs already uses (it consumes nixosPkg and reassembles). Either a new .#nixos-bundled (symlinkJoin or runCommand over .#nixos + .#gamecode) that becomes packages.default and apps.default, or a makeWrapper that points the existing binary at ${gamecode}/share/hexenwail. Check which one keeps the engine .drv hash stable under a .hc edit -- verify with 'nix eval .#nixos.drvPath' before and after touching a .hc file, the same check r32l used.

Also decide whether h2ded needs the same treatment: it loads progs too, and .#h2ded has the same bare installPhase.

Reference: docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md row K2.
close_reason:
Fixed in 6a0656aaf. Added packages.nixos-bundled (and h2ded-bundled), now packages.default and apps.default.

MEASURED before/after on the same retail basedir:
  .#nixos          -> 'Gamecode: /home/josh/hexen2/data1/PROGS.DAT (H2/v1.11, file crc 17499)'  = Raven's
  .#nixos-bundled  -> 'Gamecode: <store>/bin/../share/hexenwail/data1/progs.dat (H2/v1.11, file crc 10626)' = ours

APPROACH: separate runCommand composing .#nixos + .#gamecode, the same pattern .#linux-fhs already uses on .#nixos, chosen over makeWrapper because it needs no wrapper script and matches the release tree's layout exactly (bin/glhexen2 with the progs at ../share/hexenwail = PR_FindBundleDir layer 2).

r32l CONSTRAINT VERIFIED, not just respected by construction: appended a line to gamecode/hc/h2/items.hc and re-evaluated. .#gamecode.drvPath moved (6nr96xrc -> phir81n1) while .#nixos.drvPath and .#h2ded.drvPath were byte-identical. Restored the file afterwards.

TWO TRAPS FOUND while doing it, both now documented in flake.nix and docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md:

1. The binary must be COPIED, not symlinked. PR_FindBundleDir resolves the bundle from Sys_GetExeDir(), which reads /proc/self/exe, and Linux resolves that through a symlink to the real target -- so the obvious symlinkJoin would have sent the lookup back to the gamecode-less .#nixos output and silently found nothing. This would have looked like it worked in review.

2. .#nixos's empty 'mkdir -p $out/share/hexenwail' was not just useless, it was actively harmful: PR_FindBundleDir's layer 2 matches on the DIRECTORY existing, so it returned that empty dir as the bundle dir and shadowed layer 3's BUNDLED_GAMECODE_DIR for any distribution packager who set one. The mkdir is now gone entirely, and a new verification row K2a in BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md guards against it coming back.

h2ded QUESTION, which this bead left open: ANSWERED YES, added .#h2ded-bundled. h2ded calls PR_LoadProgs exactly as the client does, and it is the engine the project uses for headless gamecode investigation (cf uhexen2-cwld) -- a run that silently used Raven's progs would invalidate its own results. Verified it prints the store path for its Gamecode: line.

REGRESSION CHECKS: -vanillaprogs on the bundled build still falls back to the player's PROGS.DAT; .#release builds and its tree is unchanged (gamecode/ staging and linux-x86_64/share/hexenwail both intact); nix flake show lists all outputs; bare .#nixos and .#h2ded remain engine-only for anyone composing their own.

title: h2ded floods the log with 'Console input too long!' when stdin is at EOF
description:
engine/hexen2/sys_unix.c:380 Sys_ConsoleInput() loops on select(stdin) and calls read(0, &c, 1) without checking the return value (the -Wunused-result warning at :395 is the same line). At EOF -- stdin redirected from /dev/null, from a file that has been consumed, or from a closed pipe -- select() reports the descriptor readable forever and read() returns 0 without writing to c, so the loop appends whatever c last held until the 256-byte buffer fills, prints 'Console input too long!', and starts over. The result is one message per frame: a 30-second h2ded run wrote 8 KB of it, and it drowns out every other line in the log.

This matters now that h2ded can actually run mod content (uhexen2-ti8y, fixed a7a9c1573): the dedicated server is the cheap way to run headless map/monster/physics investigations, and every such run is either driven with stdin closed or piped from a script, which is exactly the case that spins. Working around it needs 'tail -f /dev/null | h2ded', which is not obvious.

FIX SHAPE: treat read() <= 0 as end-of-input -- stop polling stdin for the rest of the run rather than returning to select(), since a descriptor at EOF stays readable. Worth checking sys_win.c for the same shape, and whether Sys_PrintTerm's message should say 'stdin closed' once instead. Discovered 2026-08-13 while verifying uhexen2-ti8y.
close_reason: Fixed in 8fe86e802. Sys_ConsoleInput() in both engine/hexen2/server/sys_unix.c and engine/hexen2/sys_unix.c now checks read()'s return: <=0 is treated as end of input, printed once as 'stdin at EOF, console input disabled', after which stdin is no longer polled for the rest of the run. EINTR/EAGAIN end the frame's poll instead of counting as EOF. The select() call is now tested with > 0 so an error return no longer enters the loop. Checked sys_win.c (both client and server): they use GetNumberOfConsoleInputEvents/ReadConsoleInput, which report zero events when idle, so they do not have this shape -- no change needed there. Verified at runtime against retail data in /home/josh/hexen2 with stdin at /dev/null: pre-fix binary wrote 490 'Console input too long!' lines / 12918 bytes in a 25s run; post-fix binary writes one EOF line / 706 bytes total. Also silences the -Wunused-result warning that was on the same line.

title: Faint scanline on tile floors during forward motion — SoT Arena, Clean preset
description:
## Report Summary
Bob Bobber (Intel Iris Xe / Mesa, laptop) observed a very subtle horizontal line visible on tile floors during forward motion in SoT Arena with the Clean display preset. "A scanline I can just barely make out" — only noticeable in motion on large flat regularly-patterned surfaces.

## Critical Clarification (Investigation Direction)
**IMPORTANT:** Initially reported as "very mild almost microstutter" (frame-pacing framing), then clarified by reporter to be a *visual line*, not a timing problem. The first characterization sent investigation down a wrong path. This distinction matters: timing issues vs. rendering artifact are wholly different root-cause trees.

## Evidence & Hypothesis Testing

### Current Evidence
- `r_lightmap_bicubic 1` "maybe makes it look a little better" — **suggestive but not confirming**. Bicubic softens lightmap sampling generally, so it would improve almost any lightmap-domain artifact *and* leave a texture-mip or tearing artifact looking identical. Does not discriminate.

### Next Action (Decisive Test)
**Run `r_fullbright 1` on the same spot:**
- **Line disappears** → problem is in the lightmap atlas (edge bleed between surfaces)
- **Line persists** → lightmap theory is dead; suspect texture filtering or screen-space tearing

### Secondary Discriminators (if needed)
- `gl_texture_anisotropy 16` — detect mip-band artifacts
- `vid_vsync 1` — rule out tearing
- Screen-space vs world-space fixation — whether line moves with camera or sticks to geometry

## Prime Suspect: Lightmap Atlas Repacking
**Commit:** `c9991d12c` (2026-08-11, uhexen2-vfvh)
- Raised lightmap pages from 128×128 to 256×256
- Raised page ceiling from 256 to 512
- Reason: prevent SoT tibet from exhausting AllocBlock
- Side effect: **repacks every surface in the lightmap atlas**

### Mechanism
`AllocBlock` (engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c) places surfaces edge-to-edge with **no padding between them**. Lightmap sampling is bilinear, so a fragment at the edge of one surface's lightmap rect can bleed into an adjacent surface's data. This is stock Quake behaviour, not new — but *which surfaces neighbour each other in the atlas* changed, so a bleed previously invisible can surface somewhere noticeable without introducing a new defect.

**Why Arena + Clean preset:** Arena is a large map (same class that motivated the page-size change). Clean preset disables masking filters that would hide this:
- Clean: `gl_texture_anisotropy 1` (disabled), `r_lightmap_bicubic 0`
- Modern: anisotropy maxed, bicubic on (both would soften the line)

### Test: Does Modern Preset Show It?
**Ask reporter:** try Modern preset on same spot. If Modern is clean, problem is *masking*, not a Clean-specific defect. This reduces the search space significantly.

## Related Work
Commits in the same ~month window that could intersect:
- `13f88d5ce` — "settle the atlas decision before baking UVs against it"
- `6059af819` — re-bake surface UVs on video restart
- `216d20eeb` — 25 GL 4.3 correctness fixes (includes stale-buffer glBufferSubData mis-target)
- `f52826282` — bicubic lightmap filter (`r_lightmap_bicubic`, uhexen2-b2f0)

## Reproduction Constraints
- Devbox runs llvmpipe (software GL); subtle Intel Iris Xe filtering artifact may not reproduce
- Screenshot from reporter's laptop with line visible is more useful than local attempts
- SoT installed at `/home/josh/hexen2/sot`; Arena can be driven headless for world-space artifact capture
- Screen-space artifacts unlikely to capture headless; world-space ones possible

## Status
First field report against 0.8.0-beta.r1 (released 2026-08-13).
Actionable as soon as `r_fullbright 1` result arrives — not blocked by anything.
notes:
PRIME SUSPECT ELIMINATED 2026-08-15 -- it was fixed the same day this was filed,
so the entire "Next Action" section was written against a build that no longer
exists. Re-test before spending anything else here.

WHAT THE BEAD SAYS THE MECHANISM IS:
  "AllocBlock (engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c) places surfaces edge-to-edge with no
   padding between them. Lightmap sampling is bilinear, so a fragment at the
   edge of one surface's lightmap rect can bleed into an adjacent surface's
   data."

THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE. uhexen2-jwzf landed a gutter:
  c10eb1e40  2026-08-14  "give every lightmap rect a gutter so bicubic stops
                          reading its neighbour"
  f38654033  2026-08-15  "fix the gutter fill walking rows by a mangled stride"

gl_rsurf.c:86 now defines LM_GUTTER 2; AllocBlock allocates w+4 x h+4 for every
surface and the surrounding border is filled with replicated edge luxels
(gl_rsurf.c:379). BLOCK_* went 256 -> 260 to keep the padded worst case fitting.
A fragment sampling at a rect edge now reads that surface's OWN replicated
luxels, not its neighbour's. This bead was filed 2026-08-14; c10eb1e40 is dated
the same day.

VERIFIED LIVE ON THE REPORTED MAP, not just in the source. Loading SoT Arena on
the current build:

    Lightmaps: 145/1536 pages (260x260), atlas 2080x4940

260x260 is the gutter-enabled page size (256 + 2*LM_GUTTER), so the padding is
in effect on exactly the map the report names.

WHAT TO DO NEXT, in order:
1. Re-observe on a current build, same spot, same Clean preset. If the line is
   gone, close this as fixed by c10eb1e40 and note that jwzf covered it.
2. Only if it persists, run the bead's own discriminator (r_fullbright 1). It
   is still the right test -- but now a POSITIVE result means something other
   than inter-surface bleed, because bleed is what the gutter removed.

WHY THIS BOX CANNOT SETTLE IT. Do not ask the headless harness for this one.
The report is Intel Iris Xe / Mesa, and everything here renders on llvmpipe.
A "very subtle" line on a regularly-patterned surface, visible only in motion,
is exactly the class of artifact -- mip selection, filter precision, raster
sample positions -- where a software rasteriser is not a stand-in for a real
driver. tools/headless-drive.sh can now drive real key events and screenshot a
moving camera (see uhexen2-q6ap), so the run is mechanically possible; it just
would not be evidence either way. This needs the reporter's own hardware.

title: [bug] PR_ExecuteProgram's statement walk has no upper bound against numstatements
description:
engine/h2shared/pr_exec.c:181-186: PR_ExecuteProgram() sets st = &pr_statements[EnterFunction(f)] and then does a bare st++ at the top of an unbounded while(1). Nothing compares st against pr_statements + progs->numstatements. A function whose body is not terminated by a DONE/RETURN opcode inside the lump — trivially arranged in a forged image, and also possible in a truncated one — walks the interpreter straight off the end of the statements lump and executes whatever follows it in the hunk as bytecode.

EnterFunction() returns f->first_statement - 1 (:887) and f->first_statement is likewise unvalidated on the positive side; the only check is the negative-value builtin branch at :545-547. So the entry point can also start outside the lump.

Same root as uhexen2-1p3o (progs bytecode is executed without being validated) but a distinct fix: 1p3o is about operand values, this is about the instruction pointer's range. Both are reachable through a player-supplied csprogs.dat, since CL_LoadCSProgs() runs the image every frame once CSQC_DrawHud is exported.

FIX SHAPE: bound first_statement to [0, numstatements) at load, and either add a cheap st bounds check in the dispatch loop or guarantee termination at load by verifying each function's reachable range ends in DONE/RETURN. The load-time option keeps the interpreter hot loop untouched, which matters given r_speeds work.

Discovered 2026-08-13 while closing uhexen2-uglw. Related: uhexen2-1p3o, uhexen2-la6r, uhexen2-sgw7.
close_reason: Fixed in ff66e0567: PR_ValidateBytecode() validates statement operands (per-opcode role table), function first_statement/parm_start/locals/numparms, jump targets, and lump-terminating statement at load; OP_CALL function index and OP_FETCH_GBL reach bounded at dispatch. Verified: 77 real progs images accepted, forged variants refused, 6 game dirs load and play.

title: dfunction_t.s_name is unvalidated in entry-point scan — OOB read into strcmp
description: engine/hexen2/cl_csqc.c:222 does csqc_state.strings + fn->s_name when scanning for entry points, with s_name unvalidated — an out-of-bounds read fed directly into strcmp. PR_LoadProgs has the identical pattern at a different path. Affects both client (player-supplied csprogs.dat) and server path. Each offset within the strings lump must be validated against stringssize before use in string operations. Similar helper fix to PR_CheckProgsExtents (see uhexen2-la6r) could serve both code paths. Relates to uhexen2-sgw7 and uhexen2-w70p (other header-field validation residuals).
close_reason:
IMPLEMENTATION (bc9fbb288), two halves — a range check alone was not sufficient.

1. PR_CheckProgsExtents() (engine/h2shared/pr_edict.c) now rejects an image whose string pool does not end in a NUL. This is the load-bearing half: it makes ANY in-range offset safe for strcmp(), because a scan starting anywhere inside the pool must meet a terminator at or before the pool's last byte. It covers the server path for free, where every string already goes through the bounded PR_GetString().
2. CL_LoadCSProgs() (engine/hexen2/cl_csqc.c:228) range-checks fn->s_name against csqc_state.stringssize before forming the pointer, and skips the function otherwise.

SERVER-PATH CORRECTION: the bead said 'PR_LoadProgs has the identical pattern at a different path'. It does not — ED_FindFunction()/ED_FindFunctioni()/ED_FindGlobal() all go through PR_GetString(), which already range-checks and Host_Errors. The server's actual residual gap was the missing pool terminator, now closed by (1).

SEVERITY EVIDENCE (headless, llvmpipe, real client binary):
- Forged csprogs.dat, all four s_name = 0x7F000000: PRE-FIX SIGSEGV, exit 139. POST-FIX 'CSQC: csprogs.dat has no CSQC_DrawHud, ignoring', map keeps loading.
- s_name = numstrings+9999 and s_name = -424242: PRE-FIX did NOT crash — the OOB read landed inside the 64 MB hunk and returned garbage that matched no entry point. Worth recording: the defect is an out-of-bounds READ whose observable effect depends on what the offset lands on, not a reliable crash. Same shape as the severity correction in uhexen2-la6r's close note.
- Non-NUL-terminated pool: PRE-FIX loaded normally (strcmp happened to find a NUL just past the pool). POST-FIX 'CSQC: ignoring csprogs.dat: string pool is not null-terminated'.
- Control (good hcc-built v7 csprogs.dat, 1108 B): still 'CSQC: loaded csprogs.dat (4 functions)' before and after.

VALIDATION: builds clean on .#default, .#h2ded, .#win64, .#h2ded-win64, no new diagnostics. All six real progs.dat/progs2.dat images on this box (v6, H2 and Portals) confirmed already NUL-terminated, so the new invariant rejects no legitimate file.

title: gamecode/README.txt tells Windows players to overwrite Raven's progs.dat for no benefit
description:
The README's Windows section instructs Windows players to copy gamecode\data1\progs.dat over the game's own file. That instruction is now both POINTLESS and DESTRUCTIVE:

POINTLESS: the Windows release zip is flat, so gamecode/ already sits beside glh2.exe and IS the bundle the engine loads. Wine testing under uhexen2-qoy7 confirmed it is already active with no copying at all.

DESTRUCTIVE: retail progs.dat ships LOOSE with no packed copy to restore from, so the overwrite is irreversible. That exact finding is what shaped uhexen2-8qp3's staged layout in the first place — the release deliberately stages rather than overlays precisely so no instruction ever tells a player to do this.

So the README currently tells Windows users to take an irreversible action that gains them nothing.

BUILD_INFO.txt already has the accurate framing — it presents the staged tree as being for a hand install INTO ANOTHER ENGINE, not into the one shipping beside it. The README's Windows block just lacks that caveat.

Note that Unix is fine: uhexen2-qoy7 retargeted it at the userdir, which both works and is reversible with rm.

RELATED WORK: This is the same class of doc drift as uhexen2-wnkk (the still-stale release-notes text at .github/workflows/release.yml:191-199, which carries the same superseded \"It is not installed for you / copy it yourself\" wording). Both would sensibly be fixed together.
close_reason: Duplicate of uhexen2-bb6a. Both have identical titles and descriptions regarding Windows players overwriting progs.dat. Keeping bb6a as the survivor.

title: csprogs.dat is loaded with no extent checks at all — same class as sgw7, on a player-supplied file
description:
engine/hexen2/cl_csqc.c:116-200 loads csprogs.dat with no extent check whatsoever — not even the strings check that PR_LoadProgs had before 9f52d0a6a. It is the identical class of defect just fixed in uhexen2-sgw7, and in one respect worse: csprogs.dat is player-supplied, typically arriving with a downloaded mod or server content, whereas progs.dat at least normally comes from the game install.

The fix already exists in shape: PR_CheckProgsExtents() (pr_edict.c:2247) does exactly this job and is version-aware. It is currently static; reusing it here means exporting it. Deliberately left alone by 9f52d0a6a as out of that fix's scope.

Threat model difference: for progs.dat the realistic case is corruption (partial unzip, interrupted download); for csprogs.dat, content arriving from elsewhere makes a malicious file a coherent scenario. Relate to uhexen2-sgw7 and to uhexen2-ql7h (the other untrusted-input tracking bead).

Related: uhexen2-sgw7 (now fixed)
close_reason:
IMPLEMENTATION: PR_CheckProgsExtents() de-static'd in engine/h2shared/pr_edict.c with doc comment; declaration added to engine/h2shared/progs.h; check placed in engine/hexen2/cl_csqc.c before header byteswap and before lump pointer computation; entityfields guard covers negative values and multiply overflow.

THE PATH IS REACHABLE: CL_LoadCSProgs() called from CL_SignonReply() case 4 (cl_main.c:258) on every level load; currently returns early because FS_FileExists("csprogs.dat") fails; drop a csprogs.dat into data1/ and it runs.

RUNTIME EVIDENCE: 17 malformed images declined with named reason, exit 0, map load unaffected. Good hcc-built v7 csprogs.dat (1108 B, v7 confirmed via tools/qcdis.py) still loads: "CSQC: loaded csprogs.dat (4 functions)".

Pre-fix testing: 8-byte file → SIGSEGV; forged ofs_globals → SIGSEGV after "loaded"; truncated/forged/negative-entityfields → silently accepted as valid.

SEVERITY CORRECTION: Urgency rests on crashes and silent acceptance, not OOB writes. On little-endian x86_64 (shipped build), byteswap stores are compiled out (LittleLong is self-assign). OOB reads and corrupt VM acceptance are what bite. Write hazard remains real on big-endian, -O0, or different compiler.

VALIDATION: Builds PASS on .#default, .#h2ded, .#win64, .#h2ded-win64; no unused/missing-prototype diagnostics. v6 rejection and version check at cl_csqc.c:145 deliberately unchanged.

Fixed in commit c1b139f83.

title: Site: launch checklist and ongoing link-rot maintenance
description:
Launch checklist and the ongoing maintenance loop.

Pre-launch:

- Domain registered for **multiple years** with auto-renew and a documented owner; DNS access held by at least two people.
- HTTPS with auto-renewal. (Note: Inky's site is HTTP-only, which is why some fetchers cannot reach it — do not repeat that.)
- `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`, canonical URLs, per-page meta description, OpenGraph/Twitter cards for link previews in Discord.
- Redirect table from the IA issue deployed and spot-checked.
- CI: build, HTML validation, internal + external link check, feed validation.
- Full pass on mobile, and on a text-only browser to confirm the no-JS baseline.
- Performance budget: content pages under ~200KB excluding images; images sized and lazy-loaded.
- No analytics, or self-hosted and privacy-respecting only.

Launch:

- Announce on the Hexen II Discord, Quaddicted / func_msgboard, ModDB, r/quake and r/heretic_hexen, and to the mappers whose work is in the database — with a note asking them to correct their own entries.
- Reach out to Inky, and to whoever holds hexenworld.org, offering to host or redirect what they want preserved.

Ongoing:

- Submit the site to the Wayback Machine and set up a periodic capture.
- Quarterly link-rot sweep with the `verified:` dates refreshed.
- A documented backup: repo mirror on a second forge, plus the built site pushed to an Internet Archive item.

Definition of done: site live on the real domain, CI green, announced, first Wayback capture confirmed, backup verified by an actual restore test.

title: Site: contribution workflow, content templates, and bus-factor plan
description:
Make the site contributable, so it outlives whoever builds it.

Every dead site in this epic's history had one maintainer and one hosting account. That is the actual failure mode — not technology.

Deliver:

- **`/contribute/`** — how to submit a map to the database, a news item, a tutorial, or a correction. Written for a mapper, not a developer: the git path *and* a "just open an issue / message us on Discord and we'll do the git part" path.
- **Content templates** in the repo: a new map/mod data file, a new tutorial, a new news post, each with required front-matter and an example.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** — local build in one command, how to preview, the review expectation.
- **Style guide** — voice, heading conventions, screenshot dimensions and format, how to credit authors, how to date and mark "verified against engine X".
- **Licensing** — the content license for contributions, and the rule that third-party works keep their own terms.
- **Bus-factor plan** — at least two people with repo *and* domain/DNS access, documented; the repo mirrored to a second forge; a periodic push of the built site to an Internet Archive item so the site itself is preserved on the same terms it preserves everything else.

Definition of done: someone outside the core team lands a content PR using only the documented process, and the bus-factor plan is executed, not merely written.

title: Site: /archive/ — preserve interviews, .plan updates, and community history
description:
Build the `/archive/` section — deliberate preservation of Hexen II history, done with permission and attribution.

Material worth rescuing, all currently one hosting lapse from gone:

- **Interviews.** Inky's exclusive interviews with **Brian Raffel** (Raven co-founder), **Kevin Schilder** (Hexen II composer) and **Degorram**. hexenworld.com's own `/features/` interviews (`chaosint.html`, `bpelletier.html`, the E3 Heretic II coverage).
- **Raven `.plan` updates** — Kenn Hoekstra, Jake Simpson, Eric Biessman, Rick Johnson, Marcus Whitlock, Michael Raymond-Judy. Wayback has captures; these are primary development-history sources.
- **Articles and features** from `/features/`, `/articles.shtml`, the MailBag.
- **Design documents and author's insights** — Inky's Wheel Of Karma pages, the "Karmaverse" extended-universe proposal, his Quake project insights (Church Of The Unholy, An Excursion to Carcosa, Persistence of Memory).
- **Lore and fiction** — `/mythos/`, `/talesofparthoris/`, `/serpentstale/`.
- **A history of the community itself** — Raven's official site → GameSpy/PlanetHeretic absorption → hexenworld.org → its March 2025 disappearance. Nobody has written this down and it is being forgotten in real time.

**Policy, and this is not optional:**

- Prefer **linking** over mirroring. A Wayback link plus a summary is the default.
- Mirror only with the author's permission, or where the author is unreachable *and* the work would otherwise be lost — and then with prominent attribution, the original URL, the capture date, and a takedown contact.
- **Contact Inky first** (via his site) before reproducing any of his material. His site is live and maintained; the right relationship is linking and cross-promotion, not absorption.
- Never present rescued content as the site's own work.
- Raven Software / id / Activision material is theirs. Historical documents are quoted and credited; game assets are not redistributed.

Definition of done: policy page published, permission requests sent and logged for every intended mirror, and the "history of the community" page written.

title: Site: community directory (Discord, projects, people, servers)
description:
Build the community directory — the static replacement for a forum, a webring and a hosted-sites program.

hexenworld.com's community value was concentrated in three now-impossible features: a message board with 100k+ posts, a WebRing, and ~50 hosted sites. We are not rebuilding any of them. We are rebuilding what they were *for*: finding the other people who still care about this game.

Deliver:

- **Where the community actually is** — Discord invites, Quaddicted/func_msgboard-style forums, subreddits, Matrix/IRC if any, with a "last verified" date on each.
- **Active projects** — engine forks (Hexenwail, uHexen2, FTE), tools, mods in progress, with repo links and a last-commit-checked date.
- **People** — mappers, modders, coders, composers, with links to their own sites. This is the WebRing idea done as a plain outbound-link page. Inky's own site is the model of what belongs here: an independent site we point *to*, not absorb.
- **Servers** — a static list, hand-maintained, honest about staleness. Optionally a JS-only live query as progressive enhancement, but the page must be useful with JS off.

Every outbound link carries a `verified: YYYY-MM-DD` field, and a CI link check flags rot. The failure mode of every previous community directory was a page of dead links presented as if current.

Definition of done: all four pages populated and verified, dates rendered on the page, link check in CI.

title: Site: /play/ — get the game, pick an engine, configure, classes, troubleshooting
description:
Write the `/play/` section — everything a person needs between "I heard Hexen II is good" and "I am playing it well in 2026".

hexenworld.com covered this with QuickFAQ, Official FAQ, Tech Help, Configuration, Classes, Walkthroughs, Servers and a "Buy Hexen II" page. All of it needs rewriting for modern hardware; none of it needs reinventing.

Pages:

- **Get the game** — current storefronts, what each package includes, and whether *Portal of Praevus* is bundled. Note the CD/abandonware situation honestly without hosting the data.
- **Pick an engine** — comparison table (Hexenwail, uHexen2 / Hammer of Thyrion, FTE, and the browser ports), what each is for, current state. Per-OS install: Windows, Linux, macOS, and where the retail files go.
- **First-run configuration** — resolution, FOV, mouse, sound/MIDI and soundfonts, gamma. The single most common modern stumbling block is audio.
- **The four classes** — Paladin, Crusader, Necromancer, Assassin (plus Demoness in Portal of Praevus): stats, weapons, playstyle. hexenworld.com had a Classes page; this is evergreen content that still gets searched for.
- **Installing mods and map packs** — directory layout, `-game`, why a mod that "does nothing" is usually in the wrong folder.
- **Multiplayer** — HexenWorld vs. netquake, how to host, how to join, current known servers.
- **Troubleshooting** — the modern equivalent of the old `glide2x.dll` FAQ entry.
- **Walkthroughs** — port or link the `/walk/` content (andoria, canyon, cloud, ...), with cheats and secrets as separate pages.

Definition of done: a reader on a fresh Windows *and* a fresh Linux machine can each get to the first level using only these pages.

title: Site: downloads archive with mirrors and checksums
description:
Build the downloads section — the file archive, rebuilt so it cannot rot the way every previous one did.

hexenworld.com had "Essential Files" plus a File Archive and pointed at "the Hexen II Stables" as the definitive one. hexenworld.org had a Downloads section and Test Builds. Every one of those is now a dead link. The archive.org item `h2_hexenworld_dot_org_mods` is currently the best surviving snapshot of the hexenworld.org mod collection and should be treated as a primary source.

Deliver:

- Categories: **engines** (Hexenwail, uHexen2 / Hammer of Thyrion, FTE, Heretic II-adjacent), **mods**, **map packs**, **tools** (TrenchBroom, ericw-tools, QuArK, MapSearch, qME, Quake Model Viewer, Bsp2mph2), **utilities/patches**.
- Each entry: name, version, author, date, size, **SHA-256**, short description, license/terms, and *at least two* links — our mirror plus an upstream or archive.org fallback.
- **Do not put large binaries in the site repo.** Decide the mirror target in the stack issue (release assets, an S3-compatible bucket, or an Internet Archive item we control) and record it here.
- A link checker in CI that fails the build on a dead download link.
- Explicitly **do not host the retail game data** (`pak0.pak` etc.). Link to the storefronts instead, as the old site did.

Definition of done: the engines and tools categories are fully populated with working, checksummed links; the link checker runs in CI.

title: Site: news section with RSS and Atom feeds
description:
Ship the news section — the beating-heart page that told people the community was alive.

hexenworld.com ran "Current News" plus a "News Archive"; hexenworld.org's WordPress front page was almost entirely release announcements (Privateer's Hold, The Tomb of Osiris, Tales of the Arabian Deadly Nights, the Karmaverse launch, Inky's tips & tricks). That is the format worth keeping — **when a new map or engine build drops, there is one page that says so.**

Deliver:

- Markdown posts with front-matter: title, date, author, tags, optional hero image.
- Paginated index, per-tag archives, and a full **news archive** page (chronological, all posts, one list).
- **RSS *and* Atom feeds**, both full-content. This is how the fediverse/feedreader-era community actually follows a site, and it is the piece WordPress gave hexenworld.org that a naive static site forgets.
- A post template that can cross-link into a `/maps/` database entry so a release announcement and the permanent map page stay in sync rather than duplicating.
- `JSON Feed` optional.

Definition of done: three real posts published, both feeds validate against the W3C feed validator, and the archive page lists everything.

title: Hexen II community hub — static site
description:
## Why

The Hexen II community has no durable home. The two hubs it has relied on are gone or going:

- **hexenworld.com** — Raven Software's *official* Hexen II site (1997–2002), later absorbed into GameSpy/PlanetHeretic. Dead for two decades; survives only in the Wayback Machine. Archived captures show it was a genuine community hub: current news + news archive, Raven `.plan` updates, MailBag, articles & interviews, class guides, official FAQ, QuickPoll, featured screenshot, a 100k+ post MessageBoard, IRC, a WebRing, a file archive, a servers list, tech help & config guides, walkthroughs (`/walk`), skins, a 150-page Hexen II entity reference (`/h2entities`), and ~50 *hosted sites* — mods (Siege, DungeonBreak, HexArena, RavenHurst, Rival Kingdoms, HWCTF, Ghost, The Down, The Glyphs, Cronos Bots), mapping sites (Mapper's Shrine, The Citadel, The Workshop), strategy (Strategon), and lore/fiction (Tales of Parthoris, Serpent's Tale, Mythos).
- **hexenworld.org** — the modern (2020s) WordPress successor: Development, GitHub, Test Builds, Bug Tracker, Discord, Servers, Hexen II / Heretic II Webtools, Changelog, Downloads, plus news posts announcing new map releases (Privateer's Hold, The Tomb of Osiris, Tales of the Arabian Deadly Nights, Join the Karmaverse). **It went offline around March 2025.** Its mod archive survives on archive.org as `h2_hexenworld_dot_org_mods`.

What still works is the *static* end of the ecosystem: **Inky's Hexen II Mapping Corner** (http://earthday.free.fr/Inkys-Hexen-II-Mapping-Corner/) is hand-written HTML on free hosting, and it is the single best modern Hexen II knowledge resource — 16 dated mapping tips & tricks articles categorised into HexenC-coding / no-coding / "Mapping Academy" / new-features, a cross-reference index mapping **entity name → which articles use it**, an annotated toolbox (TrenchBroom, ericw-tools, QuArK, Bsp2mph2, qME, Quake Model Viewer, Notepad++), the MapSearch `.map` query tool with readme/changelog/zip, project pages for Wheel Of Karma incl. the "Karmaverse" extended-universe proposal, and exclusive interviews with Brian Raffel (Raven co-founder), Kevin Schilder (Hexen II composer) and Degorram.

**The lesson is the architecture.** The dynamic sites (ASP, PHP, WordPress, forum software) all rotted. The static hand-written one is still up after 20+ years. A new community hub should be a **static site in git** so it survives its maintainers.

## What this epic delivers

A static, git-backed, zero-database community site for Hexen II — playing it, modding it, mapping it, and preserving its history. It takes hexenworld.com's *breadth* (news, files, community directory, reference docs, preservation) and Inky's *durability and depth* (hand-authored technical content, cross-referenced, no server-side anything).

## Scope

In scope: site generator + hosting choice, information architecture, theme, news/RSS, downloads mirror, maps & mods database, mapping/modding documentation hub, structured entity reference, getting-started guides, community directory, an archival/preservation section, contribution workflow, client-side search, launch.

Out of scope for v1: forums, user accounts, comments, live server-status polling, file uploads. All of those are the failure modes we are deliberately avoiding — link to Discord/GitHub instead.

## Constraints

- **Static output only.** No database, no server-side execution. Must be servable from a plain file host or the Wayback Machine and still work.
- **Content in git**, plain Markdown/YAML, so anyone can fork it and relaunch it if the maintainer disappears.
- Must degrade gracefully with **JavaScript off** for all content pages.
- **Attribution and permission** are hard requirements for any rescued content — see the preservation child issue.

## Definition of done

Every child issue closed, the site is live on a real domain, and a mapper new to Hexen II can go from "I own the game" to "my first map compiles and runs" using only pages on this site.

title: CI does not build the dedicated server — sv_model.c compiles in no default target
description:
The default `nix build` target does not compile engine/h2shared/sv_model.c. It is gated behind BUILD_DEDICATED in engine/CMakeLists.txt:704-723 and is only built by `nix build .#h2ded` (and `.#h2ded-win64`).

Consequence: any change to sv_model.c — or to any other file exclusive to the dedicated-server target — goes completely uncompiled by the normal build and by CI. A syntax error or type error there would land on master undetected and only surface when someone builds the dedicated server. This is a silent-breakage class of bug, not a one-off.

sv_model.c is not dead code: it is a near-duplicate of gl_model.c carrying the server-side model/BSP loading path, so engine fixes frequently need applying to both copies (uhexen2-sg5s is exactly such a fix — it had to touch gl_model.c AND sv_model.c).

Proposed fix: add the dedicated-server target (`.#h2ded`, and ideally `.#h2ded-win64`) to the CI build matrix in .github/workflows/ci.yml so it is compiled on every PR/push, matching how the client targets are covered.

Note: This was discovered on 2026-08-13 during the uhexen2-sg5s fix, and sg5s's own change to sv_model.c WAS verified by manually building .#h2ded — so sg5s is not at risk, but future changes are.
close_reason: Premise is false: .github/workflows/ci.yml already runs `nix build .#h2ded` (a 'Build dedicated server' step, line 68) and `nix build .#h2ded-win64` (line 79), both added 2026-08-11 in 81d25f3d6a/ba2f3fe77 (uhexen2-hx78, uhexen2-befz) — two days before this bead was filed. sv_model.c is compiled by CI on every PR/push via that step; the SERVER_SOURCES list in engine/CMakeLists.txt (BUILD_DEDICATED block) includes it directly. CONTRIBUTING.md's 'seven build targets' list already names .#h2ded and .#h2ded-win64 among them and is accurate. The filer verified the fix locally (nix build .#h2ded) but did not check whether CI already covered it before concluding it didn't.

title: Implement gamecode substitution with two-condition AND gate
description:
Implement PR_FindBundleDir() three-layer lookup, PR_BundledProgsPath() two-condition AND gating predicate, by-path loader that sets fs_filesize and clears file_from_pak, -vanillaprogs flag with help_strings[] tables and USAGE.md updates, and #if !defined(H2W) gate.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS:
- Gate on BOTH path_id (is this the base game's file?) AND fs_gamedir_nopath (is the base game the current gamedir?)
- Path_id alone would let a gamecode-less mod fall through to portals
- fs_gamedir_nopath alone inherits a pre-existing rollback bug
- Together they fail closed: never override a mod's progs.dat
- Scope is gamedir identity, not fall-through: pure map packs deliberately keep retail gamecode

This gets a fresh-context adversarial audit before merge (precedence-change risk, cf uhexen2-4p8t).
close_reason:
Implementation complete and shipped across three commits. The adversarial audit proved the two-condition AND is necessary, not merely argued, and found zero breaches across 40+ configurations.

**ec556398f** — Substitution. PR_FindBundleDir() with three-layer lookup (exedir/gamecode/, exedir/../share/hexenwail/, compile-time BUNDLED_GAMECODE_DIR). PR_BundledProgsPath() two-condition AND gate (path_id for base-game identity + fs_gamedir_nopath for gamedir match). By-path loader setting fs_filesize and clearing file_from_pak. -vanillaprogs flag in help_strings[] and USAGE.md. H2W guard to gate out non-standard builds.

**9f52d0a6a** — Audit finding H1 (extent validation). Overflow-safe PR_LumpFits() and PR_CheckProgsExtents(), bounds-checking every lump the byteswap loops write on both bundled and player progs. Discovered and fixed a 300,000-byte truncated file that passed version, progdefs-CRC and string bounds checks, printed a normal Gamecode: line, and wrote ~590 KB out of bounds before dying at PR_ExecuteProgram. Player-file half was pre-existing and reachable before this feature.

**b93860c0b** — Audit finding H2 (userdir precedence). Third stand-down condition establishing ordering: user directory > bundle > install directory. Verified under wine on DO_USERDIRS 0 to confirm the new probe is genuinely inert on Windows rather than regressing the feature there.

THE ADVERSARIAL AUDIT: Fresh context attacked across 40+ configurations and could not breach the hard constraint — the bundle never loaded under a mod. Proved the two-condition AND is load-bearing rather than merely argued via instrumented four-stage runtime chain through Host_Game_f: mod's searchpath entry held exactly the recorded portals id, condition 1 alone would have substituted our gamecode, condition 2 alone would have allowed the pre-existing bug. Both findings (sgw7, qoy7) closed.

INCIDENTAL TESTING COVERAGE (to avoid redo in ctv7):
- Precedence: P1, P2, P4–P7 tested (P3, P9, P10 remain)
- Base behaviour: B4 (uppercase PROGS.DAT case-fold), B5 (userdir override), B6 (absent bundle)
- Truncated-bundle rejection and fallback in both userdir-present and userdir-absent cases
- Real Windows under wine confirmation of inert DO_USERDIRS 0 path
- Both h2ded and GL client

Unblocks uhexen2-ctv7.

title: Package bundled gamecode into Linux distributions
description:
Add share/hexenwail/{data1,portals} under each of linux-x86_64/ and linux-x86_64-nixos/ to ship bundled progs files. Windows requires no change (flat zip already satisfies layer 1). Leave root-level gamecode/ staging tree untouched.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: Do NOT reference ${gamecode} from the engine derivation. That would couple the engine's .drv hash to the gamecode source, destroying the property that gamecodeSrc exists to protect and causing every .hc edit to rebuild the entire engine.
close_reason:
SHIPPED: flake.nix release derivation now installs progs files into $out/release/{linux-x86_64,linux-x86_64-nixos}/share/hexenwail/{data1,portals} — data1/progs.dat (888,368), data1/progs2.dat (838,712), portals/progs.dat (1,147,444) in each. Satisfies bundle-location lookup layer 2 since binary sits at <platform>/bin/glhexen2.

.github/workflows/release.yml needed NO change — zip -r already recurses into share/. Verified by extracting Package step verbatim against real .#release trees.

WINDOWS CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: zip root listing has glh2.exe and gamecode/ as siblings (layer 1 satisfied). Windows tree diffs identical; both zips differ only in BUILD_INFO.txt's CRC (build date stamp). All other entry CRCs match; byte size exactly equal.

ENGINE .drv HASH UNCHANGED: nj0f7g9bfzj2y54h0i62rkm4qgjs5p7h-hexenwail-0.7.9-beta.r14.drv. Identical across baseline, dirty post-edit, clean post-commit. Verified nix-store -q --requisites shows zero gamecode paths in closure. flake.nix excluded from filteredSrc by construction.

LAYOUT PROVEN BY DIFF: baseline .#release from clean worktree diffed against post-merge. Only difference: two new share/ directories plus BUILD_INFO.txt build-date line. Root-level gamecode/ byte-identical. Zero hwprogs.dat, hw/, siege/ anywhere in tree or zips.

ZIP SIZE DELTA: +1,096,248 bytes (+1.05 MB) on linux-x86_64; +0 on Windows. Progs bytecode compresses well (2.87 MB to 1.05 MB) — download cost about a third of design estimate.

SCOPE HONESTY: engine code that reads this layout does not exist yet (piece 3: uhexen2-uwtq), so end-to-end discovery not claimed. Path contract proven — <platform>/bin/../share/hexenwail/data1/progs.dat resolves via realpath inside release output on both Linux platforms.

title: Extract Sys_GetExeDir() helper into shared code
description:
Promote soundfont.c's static, Linux-only, client-only /proc/self/exe resolver into a shared, reusable function compiled into both the client and h2ded. Add Windows GetModuleFileName arm. Delete the private copy from soundfont.c.

No behaviour change intended. This is foundational for the bundle discovery mechanism.

CONSTRAINT: Must NOT add the gamecode feature caller — this is the helper only, not the substitution.
close_reason:
Sys_GetExeDir() shipped in TU engine/h2shared/sys_exedir.c, providing const char *Sys_GetExeDir(void) with a contract comment in engine/h2shared/sys.h. Added to COMMON_SOURCES in engine/CMakeLists.txt:361, reaching h2ded via SERVER_SOURCES inheritance. Soundfont.c's private exe_dir() deleted and routed to the shared function; dead <unistd.h> guard removed.

Platform support: Linux via /proc/self/exe, Windows via GetModuleFileName (ANSI, matching Sys_GetBasedir convention), other platforms return NULL per contract. Resolved once and cached for thread safety.

Validation: nix-builder PASS on .#default, .#h2ded, .#win64, .#h2ded-win64 with zero new warnings. nm confirms T Sys_GetExeDir in both glhexen2 and h2ded. Soundfont regression tested A/B against pre-change tree ec497e245 under headless bwrap with cwd=/ and basedir isolation—both old and new load <exedir>/soundfont.sf2 when present, fall through to SOUNDFONT_PATH when absent. Music playback end-to-end verified. Retail data at /home/josh/hexen2 verified md5-identical.

Three implementation decisions documented: signature matches soundfont.c consumption (static buffer, not caller-supplied); caching is safer than predecessor (no concurrent buffer tear); Windows ANSI (GetModuleFileNameA) matches basedir consistency, not a new UTF-8 hole.

Unblocks uhexen2-uwtq (bundled-gamecode caller).

title: Adopt Ironwail release-notes voice/template for GitHub tag notes
description:
Hexenwail should present its GitHub release notes in Ironwail's style for consistency with upstream parity tracking and to provide a terse, scannable, credit-dense presentation rather than a raw changelog dump. ## Ironwail Release-Notes Template Apply the following guidelines to all future Hexenwail tag bodies: 1. **Download section** — shields.io badges (style=for-the-badge) linking release assets directly: - Windows badge: color=blue, logo=windows - Linux badge: color=8A9A5B - One badge per platform 2. **Platform caveat note** — plain text line noting glibc version, build flags (e.g., DO_USERDIRS=0), or other platform-specific requirements 3. **Changes section header** — "### Changes from []():" (always link the previous release) 4. **Flat bullet list** — one per user-visible change, ordered: big features → small cvars → default changes/removals. No per-category subheadings. 5. **Voice** — past-tense verb-first, one line each: - "Added...", "Fixed...", "Changed... to...", "Improved...", "Reduced...", "Removed...", "Made..." - No marketing adjectives, no "we" 6. **Cvar notation** — backticks with default value inline: - E.g., "Added `scr_infoscale` cvar (default: 2.0), controlling debug-text canvas scale" 7. **Inline credits** — "by @user" or "(thanks to @user)". Link external mods, tools, examples referenced. 8. **Grouping** — related items as sub-bullets (+ / -) under one parent instead of repeating a prefix 9. **Long content** — use `
...` blocks for setup instructions 10. **Caveats** — emoji callouts: - "❗ **Note**:" for general notes - "⚠️" for warnings 11. **Closing** — "**Full Changelog**: " 12. **Superseded releases** — retroactively prepend "### :warning: Note: this release is outdated, please download the [latest one](.../releases/latest) instead." ## Download Badges (Critical Correction) Badges are LIVE DOWNLOAD COUNTERS, not static buttons. Each badge image hits shields.io's per-asset download-count endpoint, rendering the live download count for that exact asset at that exact tag. This doubles as social proof: [WINDOWS 64-BIT | 3.4k]. Using a static button loses this entire point. Markup: raw `` anchor wrapping markdown image, one per line with NO blank lines between them. Blank lines stack vertically instead of rendering as a horizontal row. Ready-to-use block for Hexenwail (replace `` with actual release tag): ``` ![Download Windows build](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/hexenwail/hexenwail//hexenwail--windows-x86_64.zip?color=blue&label=Windows%20x86_64&logo=windows&style=for-the-badge) ![Download Linux build](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/hexenwail/hexenwail//hexenwail--linux-x86_64.zip?color=8A9A5B&label=Linux%20x86_64&style=for-the-badge) ![Download Flatpak](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/hexenwail/hexenwail//hexenwail-.flatpak?color=4A90D9&label=Flatpak&logo=flatpak&style=for-the-badge) ``` Colors: `blue` + `logo=windows` for Windows (Ironwail standard), `8A9A5B` (muted olive) NO logo for Linux (Ironwail standard), `4A90D9` + `logo=flatpak` for Flatpak (Hexenwail-specific; Ironwail has no flatpak). Always `style=for-the-badge`. README badge: single static badge placed above the top-level heading, pointing to /releases/latest, using the version endpoint relabeled as "Download": ``` [![Download](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/hexenwail/hexenwail?display_name=release&style=for-the-badge&label=Download)](https://github.com/hexenwail/hexenwail/releases/latest) ``` Renders as [DOWNLOAD | 0.7.9-beta.r13]. ## Additional Style Rules - **NEVER list raw commits or SHAs** in release bodies. Current Hexenwail notes (e.g., 0.7.9-beta.r11) have a "### Commits" section listing commit subjects with short hashes — this is the single biggest deviation from Ironwail style. Each commit must be translated into a user-facing past-tense line, or dropped if not user-visible. - **Release-body headings** are `###` only, never `#` or `##` — keeps the body compact. Current notes use `##`. - **`
`** — note the `open` attribute; expanded by default, not collapsed. - **Emoji in headings** — use `:warning:` shortcode; inline use literal ⚠️/❗. ## Preserve What We Do Better Than Ironwail Hexenwail's existing release notes contain valuable content Ironwail lacks; RETAIN when restyling: - **Crash-reporting instructions** — glh2.RPT + qconsole.log attachment guidance for bug reports - **SHA256SUMS verification instructions** — checksums and how to verify downloads - **Per-platform install/run instructions** — Windows, Linux, Flatpak-specific steps - **Requirements line** — "**Requirements:** OpenGL 4.3 capable GPU (2012+)" - **Warnings in release TITLES** — Hexenwail warns at the title level (e.g., broken-audio r5–r10 releases); Ironwail only banners the body. Keep this improvement — it's a visible signal at the releases list. ## Implementation - Versioning scheme (X.Y.Z-.rN) remains unchanged — this is presentation only - Scope: apply to all future releases; optionally retrofit the most recent Hexenwail release notes - Wire the template into the existing release process/changelog-writer workflow so it's applied automatically at tag time ## Reference Study Ironwail v0.8.2 and v0.8.1 release bodies as worked examples.
close_reason:
Landed in 5e1971348. Acceptance was 'wire the template into the existing release process/changelog-writer workflow so it's applied automatically at tag time' -- the voice itself had already been applied by hand to 0.8.0-beta.r1, but only that one file had it and the template existed nowhere but this bead. Now written down and wired into all three places that produce a release body.

1. docs/RELEASE_NOTES_STYLE.md -- the template, transcribed from this bead: structure, voice, badge colors (blue+windows and 8A9A5B are Ironwail standards, 4A90D9+flatpak is Hexenwail-only), the never-list-raw-commits-or-SHAs rule with the omitted-count sentence that replaces it, ###-only headings, the superseded-release banner, and the 'keep what we do better than Ironwail' list (crash reporting, SHA256SUMS, per-platform install, Requirements line, warnings in release TITLES). Points at docs/release-notes/0.8.0-beta.r1.md as the worked example and at docs/RETIRED_TAGS.md for tag-level bookkeeping.

2. .claude/agents/changelog-writer.md -- was still emitting the OLD shape: '## Hexenwail vX.Y.Z' with '### New Features' / '### Bug Fixes' category subheadings. That is exactly the grouping the template replaces with a flat list, and the '##' violates the ###-only rule. Rewritten to read the style doc first every time, gather from commit BODIES rather than subject lines (the user-facing consequence in this repo is almost always in the body), pick the comparison tag honestly when a run of hotfix tags sits inside one development window, and write output to docs/release-notes/<TAG>.md -- which is where release.yml already looks, closing the loop.

3. .github/workflows/release.yml -- two deviations found that the bead did not know about. Its boilerplate headings were '##' ('## Downloads', '## What's changed since'), and its no-curated-notes fallback emits a '### Commits' raw commit dump, i.e. CI itself would produce the exact anti-pattern this bead names as the single biggest drift. Headings dropped to ###. The fallback is kept deliberately -- an un-curated tag still needs a body and a commit list beats an empty one -- but it now carries the download badges a curated file would have supplied, links the previous tag in its heading, and states in the body itself that the commit list is standing in for hand-written notes. The comment above it points at the style doc and says outright that the fallback is a placeholder, not the format.

4. README.md -- gained the static Download badge above the top-level heading (version endpoint relabeled 'Download', pointing at /releases/latest), which the bead specified and the README did not have.

Already satisfied, so not touched: the workflow boilerplate already preserves every 'keep what we do better' item -- per-platform install steps, the Compiled gamecode section, crash reporting via glh2.RPT + qconsole.log, SHA256SUMS verification, and the Requirements line. 0.8.0-beta.r1.md already had correct badges, 'Changes since [prev](link)', flat past-tense bullets, no commit list and the closing Full Changelog. Retrofitting older release bodies was optional in the bead and is not done; RETIRED_TAGS.md covers the tag-level side.

Verified by extracting the workflow's 'Generate changelog' step with yq and running it both ways against the real repo. Curated path (0.8.0-beta.r1): zero level-2 headings in the assembled body, Full Changelog correctly held back to last. Fallback path (0.9.9-test.r1, no curated file): three badges, '### Initial release', the emoji note, the commit list, and all boilerplate sections at ###. bash -n clean; YAML parses under yq.

title: scr_infoscale cvar for debug-text canvas scale (Ironwail cc03300c7)
description:
Separate scale/canvas for debug text so it doesn't inherit HUD scale.

Hexenwail has no r_showfields but does have an elaborate r_showbboxes family whose text likely reuses a fixed corner canvas. Debug-only convenience, cheap.

Effort: small-medium.
close_reason: Implemented in 95e343654: scr_infoscale cvar + CANVAS_INFO carrying showfps/showclock/showspeed, sized by SCR_InfoCanvasSize(); parity tracker row added. Verified at 640x480 (1x vs clamped 2x screenshots).

title: Mod-specific bindlist.lst entries in Key Setup menu (Ironwail 096c3d952)
description:
Lets a mod ship a bindlist.lst that adds mod-specific rows to the Key Setup menu, merged with engine-defined binds.

No bindlist/.lst parsing exists in Hexenwail's menu.c or keys.c. Good fit alongside the existing moddable-UI work for HexenC modders.

Effort: medium — small file-format parser plus menu integration, no rendering-pipeline risk.
notes: Working by dispatched dev agent in worktree as of 2026-08-13. DESIGN CONSTRAINT: engine/hexen2/menu.c:4286 declares static const char *bindnames[][2] and line 4336 defines NUMCOMMANDS as compile-time sizeof. NUMCOMMANDS used for scrolling, cursor clamping, scrollbar (menu.c:4470,4474,4478,4479,4568). Supporting mod-supplied binds requires converting from compile-time static table to runtime-populated list with runtime count (not append-to-array). Merge semantics: Ironwail 096c3d952 MERGES mod binds with engine binds (appended after), unlike QSS which replaces.
close_reason:
Landed on master as commit d4b01fd39. Implements mod-supplied bindlist.lst rows in the Key Setup menu.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- engine/hexen2/menu.c: NUMCOMMANDS renamed to NUM_ENGINE_BINDS (seed count only); new M_BuildBindList() at ~:4368; runtime list keys_bindlist[] + keys_numcommands replaces the compile-time count throughout (scroll arrows, scrollbar thumb, row loop, cursor wrap, bind/unbind paths, type-to-search).
- engine/hexen2/menu.h:70-73 — M_BuildBindList prototype. engine/h2shared/quakefs.c:1518 — rebuild in Host_Game_f after BGM_Stop.
- NO DYNAMIC ALLOCATION BY DESIGN: keys_bindlist is a static array of const char*; engine rows point at existing bindnames literals, mod rows point into a static modbinds[64] pool. Leak across repeated gamedir switches is structurally impossible. Follows local precedent — menu.c uses no Z_Malloc anywhere.
- File loads via FS_LoadTempFile (temp hunk), so it resolves out of gamedir AND PAKs, is NUL-terminated by FS_LoadFile, and self-reclaims. Tokens copied into static pool before temp hunk can be touched.
- Three rebuild points: M_Init (list never all-NULL), every M_Menu_Keys_f, and Host_Game_f (covers key bound to `game foo` pressed while Key Setup menu is on screen).
- Caps: 64 mod rows, command truncated to 48 chars, label to 32. The 48 is derived — M_Keybind's cmd[80] buffer holds `bind2 "KEY" "command"`, leaving ~50 chars.
- Malformed-input cases verified: missing file, empty, whitespace-only, comment-only, odd token count (dangling command dropped), empty quoted command or label (pair skipped, slot reused), unterminated quote, bare unquoted tokens, binary junk, 8KB strings, 500-pair file (capped at 64). Parse pointer strictly advances on every non-NULL COM_Parse, so skip path cannot spin.
- M_BuildBindList clamps keys_cursor and keys_top at end of every rebuild, making a SHRINKING list safe. Break guard added to draw loop because it previously ran a hard 14 iterations on the safety of a 46-entry compile-time constant.
- Parse loop extracted and validated with -fsanitize=address,undefined; all 15 test cases clean.
- BUILD VERIFIED: `nix build` and `nix build .#h2ded` both pass on master. h2ded check matters because this touches engine/h2shared/quakefs.c and dedicated target is NOT in CI (see uhexen2-thoy).
- RUNTIME-UNVERIFIED: mod rows rendering and binding in live Key Setup menu, scrollbar thumb proportions with longer list, and `game` command rebuilding while menu is on screen. Data-layer logic is sanitizer-covered; only on-screen behavior is untested.

UPSTREAM: Ironwail 096c3d952 semantics (deliberately unlike QSS which replaces).

title: Animated-arrow pointfile visualization (Ironwail 26902e0e2)
description:
Map-leak .pts display switched from per-point particles to batched debug-geometry arrows with a Z-test toggle.

Hexenwail's R_ReadPointFile_f (engine/hexen2/r_part.c:246-290) still allocates a pt_static particle per point. Hexenwail has no R_AddDebugGeometry batching layer to reuse (R_ShowBoundingBoxes at engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:4705+ draws directly), so this means building that small batching layer or adapting arrows to the existing box-drawing style.

Mapper/dev tool, not player-facing.

Effort: medium.
notes: Working by dispatched dev agent in worktree as of 2026-08-13. TEMPLATE: Hexenwail has no R_AddDebugGeometry batching layer (unlike Ironwail), so implement following R_ShowBoundingBoxes template (engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:4705, called from :5149). HARD CONSTRAINT: GL 4.3 core, zero immediate mode, zero hardware matrix stack — agent ran gl-audit to confirm no legacy GL introduced.
close_reason:
Landed on master as commit 3993cff2c. Map leak pointfiles now draw as direction arrows instead of one particle per point.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- engine/hexen2/r_part.c: r_pointfile[]/r_numpointfile storage + R_ClearPointFile (~:249), PointFile_Collinear (~:264), R_ReadPointFile_f rewritten (~:284) with particle allocation path deleted; leak_color un-static'd at :115.
- engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c: r_pointfile_depthtest cvar (:263), R_EmitPointFileArrow + R_ShowPointFile (:4928-5023), call site at :5250 immediately after R_ShowBoundingBoxes.
- engine/hexen2/gl_rmisc.c: cvar registration at :300 beside r_showbboxes block; R_ClearPointFile() in R_NewMap at :534 beside R_ClearParticles().
- engine/h2shared/glquake.h:321,479-484 — externs, MAX_POINTFILE_POINTS, prototypes.

APPROACH (b), direct drawing in R_ShowBoundingBoxes style. R_ShowBoundingBoxes already submits debug geometry through GL_ImmBegin/GL_ImmColor4f/GL_ImmVertex3f/GL_ImmEnd(GL_LINES, &gl_shader_flat) VBO-streaming layer.
