Despite "Imm" name this is NOT legacy immediate mode, it is functionally the batcher Ironwail's R_AddDebugGeometry provides. Rejected building a second abstraction and migrating bbox code onto it as pure risk for a debug tool.

One real difference from Ironwail: GL_Imm silently DROPS vertices past GL_IMM_MAX_VERTS (8192) instead of auto-flushing, so R_ShowPointFile flushes explicitly before any segment that would not fit whole.

CVAR: r_pointfile_depthtest, default "1", CVAR_NONE. 0 draws leak path through walls. Not menu-exposed, matching r_showbboxes family.

CAP: MAX_POINTFILE_POINTS 16384 stored points (192 KB static array). File reading streams via fscanf so no growth there. Straight runs collapsed on load, this bounds DIRECTION CHANGES, not raw file lines — realistic leak path is tens-to-hundreds. On overflow keeps counting raw points so reported total stays honest, then prints "pointfile truncated at %i stored points, leak path is incomplete".

Console output preserved: "couldn't open %s", "Reading %s...", "%i points read" (now "%i points read (%i significant)", Ironwail's wording). Obsolete "Not enough free particles" message is gone.

TWO ADDITIONS BEYOND BRIEF, both justified: (1) collinear-run collapse on load — without it every arrow is a sub-unit stub and feature is pointless; (2) leak_color un-static'd and reused as arrow color via d_8to24table, because dropping particles would otherwise have silently orphaned a registered CVAR_ARCHIVE cvar.

gl-audit: PASS, 0 violations across immediate mode, matrix stack, fixed-function, client arrays, GLSL legacy.
BUILD VERIFIED: `nix build` and `nix build .#h2ded` both pass on master.
RUNTIME-UNVERIFIED (needs real leaking map): arrow head orientation (view-facing cross product), whether POINTFILE_ARROW_SIZE of 8 world units reads well at Hexen II scale, 1 Hz head-slide animation, whether depth-tested-by-default is the right default, and whether palette index 251 (leak_color default) is legible — chosen for particles, not lines.

UPSTREAM: Ironwail 26902e0e2.

title: Ship gamecode beside engine binary — drop-in engine brings its own progs
description:
uhexen2-8qp3 ships gamecode as an opt-in copy, so in practice most players will never install it and uhexen2-9r3n (DropBackpack destroying ~25% of archer drops) still reaches almost nobody.

The owner's model is "you drop in the engine executable and it works", combined with a stated preference for a conservative approach. Those point at the same design: ship the progs beside the binary and have the engine prefer it, so nothing on the player's disk is ever overwritten. That is both the best-reach option and the most conservative one on disk — the manual-copy alternative is only "safe" because it does nothing by default.

HARD CONSTRAINT: our gamecode must NEVER override a mod's progs.dat. /home/josh/hexen2 alone has sot, soc, karma2, and GameOfTomes, each with its own progs.dat. Breaking every mod would be far worse than the bug being fixed. Established precedence is mod > portals > data1 (see docs/GAMECODE.md).

STATUS: a design pass is running now — 2–3 candidate approaches with concrete precedence placement, a recommendation, failure modes, and a verification plan. Implementation is deliberately gated behind that design, because search-path ordering is exactly the class of change that has caused silent P0 regressions here before (see uhexen2-4p8t). The design may legitimately conclude the manual-copy status quo is correct.

Other requirements the design must satisfy:
- progs2.dat must come along (it is never requested by name — maplist.txt maps individual maps to a progs file, re-read on every map spawn, so delivering one without the other produces a silent mismatch)
- the player must be able to turn it off
- Windows has no user directory (sys.h :: DO_USERDIRS is 0) while Unix ~/.hexen2 already outranks the install
- the Portals case needs its own decision since -game auto-adds portals
notes:
STATUS UPDATE 2026-08-13 18:03

IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE — three of four pieces shipped and unblocked:
- uhexen2-hgi3 (Sys_GetExeDir helper) — closed
- uhexen2-r32l (Package into Linux) — closed
- uhexen2-uwtq (Gamecode substitution engine) — closed, audited across 40+ configs

REMAINING: uhexen2-ctv7 (Full verification matrix)

uhexen2-ctv7 NOW UNBLOCKED. Incidental testing already covered P1, P2, P4–P7; B4, B5, B6; truncated-bundle fallback; Windows DO_USERDIRS 0; both binaries. Remaining scope for full matrix: P3, P9, P10, full P8 sweep; B1–B3, B7, B8; all S1–S4 savegame rows; D1–D3 demo rows; K1–K5 known-file rows.
close_reason:
Feature complete; all four implementation children plus the verification matrix are closed.

- uhexen2-hgi3 Sys_GetExeDir helper — closed
- uhexen2-uwtq gamecode substitution with the two-condition AND gate — closed, audited across 40+ configs
- uhexen2-r32l Linux packaging — closed
- uhexen2-ctv7 full verification matrix — closed 2026-08-14, results in docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md (a49783352)

Confirmed against a fresh nix build .#default: the bundle ships at result/share/hexenwail/{data1/progs.dat, data1/progs2.dat, portals/progs.dat}, so progs2.dat comes along as the description required (maplist.txt maps individual maps to a progs file and re-reads it on every spawn, so shipping one without the other is a silent mismatch).

The HARD CONSTRAINT held: the matrix ran against a full retail install with sot, soc, karma2 and GameOfTomes, with game data deliberately outside the install tree so basedir and <exedir> share no ancestor on any row. Mod progs.dat is never overridden.

B3 -- runtime gamedir switching, the only row that exercises it -- turned up two real bugs, both since fixed and closed: uhexen2-5mhd (Host_Game_f probed host_parms->basedir, which -basedir never moves, so the Mods menu could list mods and then refuse all of them; 7e0f77126) and uhexen2-5vb6 ('game data1' left the portals searchpath entry so base-game maps ran mission-pack gamecode; ffce89f7c, which also centralised the three open-coded unwind loops into FS_UnwindSearchpaths and fixed a use-after-free in FS_Init's rollback narration).

Nothing open remains in scope. uhexen2-40e (SoT missing sounds) sits downstream under 8qp3 and is unrelated to shipping gamecode beside the engine.

title: Bundle gamecode into tester builds once 8qp3 lands
description:
ci-mdl.yml (commit 9997d68af) deliberately does not ship progs.dat, because .#release does not either — a tester build differing from the release in gamecode content produces confusing bug reports about rendering.

uhexen2-8qp3 is changing that: releases will bundle data1/progs.dat, data1/progs2.dat and portals/progs.dat (hw/siege excluded until audited, see uhexen2-nr9l). When 8qp3 lands, ci-mdl.yml must follow so tester builds and releases stay in step — same three files, same layout in the archive.

This is a coupled task: only unblock after 8qp3 is landed and its bundle locations are known.
close_reason:
Done in bb3e9480e. ci-mdl.yml now copies staging/gamecode into both packages, same placement as release.yml.

The two halves were not equally broken. Linux was already correct by accident — the engine loads linux-x86_64/share/hexenwail/ and the package copies that whole tree with 'cp -r staging/linux-x86_64/.'; only release.yml's root-level spare copy was missing, which is cosmetic but is what BUILD_INFO.txt and gamecode/README.txt describe. Windows had nothing at all: there is no share/hexenwail layer in the flat Windows layout, gamecode/ beside glh2.exe IS the copy PR_FindBundleDir() loads, and win-pkg copied bin/* and get_demo.* and stopped. So Windows testers — which is who this workflow exists for — were running their own install's retail progs.dat against an engine the release runs our gamecode on.

Verified by replaying the edited packaging step against a real 'nix build .#release' tree, then executing the resulting layout. The Windows shape (engine binary with gamecode/ beside it, no share/hexenwail anywhere) was reproduced with h2ded — same PR_FindBundleDir() lookup, on a platform this box can run: it reported <exedir>/gamecode/data1/progs.dat (crc 10626) and <exedir>/gamecode/portals/progs.dat (crc 44043); deleting gamecode/ fell back to the player's data1/PROGS.DAT (crc 17499). actionlint clean.

TESTING.txt also now tells the tester the build carries its own gamecode and asks for the Gamecode: line plus a -vanillaprogs comparison for game-logic reports.

NOT covered here: running the actual .exe on Windows. That is uhexen2-ctv7's K3 row and needs the Windows test machine.

title: Audit all divergences between gamecode/hc sources and shipped progs.dat
description:
uhexen2-qj8s was found by accident — someone disassembled a progs.dat for an unrelated question (uhexen2-9uzt) and noticed the Crusader glyph differed. Nobody has ever systematically checked whether our HexenC sources match the bytecode players actually run. With bundling now decided, that gap has to close before release.

An audit is in flight using a progs.dat disassembler written for uhexen2-9uzt (being checked into the repo). Scope: compare nix build .#gamecode output against retail data1/PROGS.DAT, data1/progs2.dat and portals/progs.dat, classify each semantic divergence as deliberate-uHexen2-fix / deliberate-fork-change / unreverted-accident / Raven-changed-post-source-release, and distinguish those from cosmetic compiler-level differences (h2 deliberately omits -oi/-on for old-savegame compatibility while other trees use both, so instruction-level noise is expected).

This audit determines whether uhexen2-qj8s's 'our .hc wins' rule can be applied safely to progs bundling, and unblocks the practical value of the bundling task.
notes:
AUDIT COMPLETE 2026-08-13 / RESULTS RECORDED BELOW

========== METHOD AND COVERAGE ==========

Compared nix build .#gamecode output against retail using three tiers of analysis:

TIER 1 — Function Symbol Table (complete)
- Function names present/absent
- numparms and locals counts per function
- Immune to compiler flags (-oi, -on affecting instruction encoding and immediates only)
- Provides ground truth: if 1517 of 1530 h2 functions match exactly on locals, compiler noise is NOT smearing the comparison

TIER 2 — Opcode Sequence per Function Body (complete, comparison baseline)
- Analyzed bytecode span [first_statement, next_function_start) for every function present in both builds
- Accounts for dead-code elimination and real source-level changes
- Immune to -oi/-on global renumbering (immediates still encode the same operation)
- Differences here = real changes to compiled control flow or data flow
- 127 h2 functions opcode-differ; 128 portals functions opcode-differ; 160 portals functions opcode-differ

TIER 3 — Immediate-Constant Multiset (weak, hint-only)
- Temporaries have no definition in hcc output, so many immediates unresolvable
- Under -on (portals), all immediates collapse to LCL+ offsets, making Tier 3 completely unavailable for portals
- Used only as a noise floor / causality hint, not relied upon for decisions

========== COVERAGE TABLE ==========

| Data Tree | Our Functions | Retail Functions | Shared | opcode + immediate-multiset + field-operand match | Opcode-Differing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| data1/progs.dat | 1631 | 1634 | 1628 | **1401** | **127** |
| data1/progs2.dat | 1475 | 1477 | 1471 | **1243** | **128** |
| portals/progs.dat | 2043 | 2041 | 2037 | **1769** | **160** |

NOT COMPARED:
- hw/hwprogs.dat (ours vs retail) — no retail HexenWorld progs exists locally
- siege/hwprogs.dat (ours vs retail) — no retail siege progs exists locally
- These trees remain unaudited and flagged for bundling decision

========== COMPILER NOISE vs REAL DIVERGENCE ==========

Ground truth: h2 deliberately omits -oi/-on (preserve old-savegame format), portals/hw/siege use both.

Flag verification:
- h2 globals: named I+* in both builds (neither used -on) ✓
- portals globals: named LCL+* in both builds (both used -on) ✓
- No dead-code elimination in hcc (-os, -oi, -on affect only string heap, immediates, name table: hcc.c:1097-1099)

Proof noise is not smearing: 1517 of 1530 h2 shared functions match exactly on locals count. If hcc drift were present, locals would diverge randomly. They don't. The ~127 opcode differences are real source divergences.

========== ATTRIBUTION: FIVE FORK-ERA COMMITS TOUCH .hc FILES ==========

All other files under gamecode/hc are upstream uHexen2 (Ozkan Sezer, 2004-2022):

1. fcf9638ba — dead code removal (fablade.hc frame_BLADE comment, ravenai.hc FindDir/find_path/monster_checkpos)
2. fd1ac9ee6 — unused constants (IT_SHOTGUN, UPDATE_*, attck_cnt)
3. ab24f9519 — create_swarm dead code
4. 1ebcc230c — CheckJump parm reduction
5. 7ff652502 — eidolon_enemy added

========== CATEGORIZATION OF DIVERGENCES ==========

CATEGORY (a) — Upstream uHexen2 fixes matching gamecode/README through 1.29c
- Vast majority of the ~127 h2 differences
- Samples verified: fablade frame_BLADE, ravenai dead funcs, unused constants — all documented upstream

CATEGORY (b) — Deliberate documented fork changes
- FindMonsterTarget FL_NOTARGET fix (e9731510a message)
- Portals UseBlast/BecomeImp/Use_Tripwire dmg=50
- Portals artifact_touch sound fix (crusader/Lghtn2.mdl → lghtn2.wav)
- DropBackpack/BadBackpackDump (fe1f2bdc1, bb570666a + bd IDs in messages)
- All named in commit messages

CATEGORY (c) — Three explicit findings (see Jobs 2 and 3)
- Use_TimeBomb unreverted accident (d39212a12, see qj8s update)
- gamecode/README never updated in fork era
- DropBackpack debug spam undecided fork gamecode

CATEGORY (d) — Raven shipped different bytecode than source
- Portals entity fields: sheep_call/scoped/wake_sheep/sheep_run_use, monster_death_use(float) all in Raven source, absent in shipped progs
- Result: our portals has 392 entity fields vs retail 390; offsets shift by 194
- HARMLESS: CRC is over progdefs.h structure (ours 26905 = retail 26905), not the .dat file itself
- SoT runs 514 fields on same CRC without issue

========== QCDIS.PY LIMITATIONS ==========

qcdis.py struct layouts verified against common/pr_comp.h:186-268. Caveats:

- gname/fname use setdefault(): aliases at one offset collapse to whichever def came first
  Result: one false hit (meteor_select weaponframe vs wfs same offset) caught and manually confirmed
  ACTION: any field/global alias diffs need manual re-confirmation
  
- CALL target resolution via gint(a) on static initial value: correct for direct calls, garbage for indirect (self.think pointers)
  ACTION: call targets were not relied upon in any decision

- Tier 3 (immediates) unreliable: no temporaries in hcc output, under -on all become LCL+ so unavailable for portals
  ACTION: only Tiers 1-2 supported decisions; Tier 3 used as hint only

RESIDUAL RISK: a pure constant retune (damage number, timing) inside an unchanged function would show identical opcodes and be missed. Tiers 1-2 are sound.

========== RE-VERIFICATION 2026-08-13 ==========

VERDICT: the original audit's conclusions stand as written. Tiers 1 and 2 reproduce exactly—not merely the counts, but the sets of function names are identical between decoders for opcode-differing, ours-only, retail-only, parm/builtin changes and locals changes. The 1517 of 1530 matching-locals claim reproduces exactly. All four category assignments are unaffected, because they rested on tiers 1-2.

BUILD PINNING PROVEN: the re-run's nix build .#gamecode resolved to store path /nix/store/kv3gvfn57z5f6asvxh0pl179ph01zfvb-hexenwail-gamecode-0.7.9-beta.r11, byte-identical to the original audit's—so the concurrent Use_TimeBomb revert did not contaminate the comparison.

CORRECTION 1 — the "byte-identical bodies" column in this bead's notes was wrong and must be fixed. The recorded figures 1378 / 1206 / 1770 matched neither the buggy tool's output nor the fixed tool's. The original audit's own saved artifacts said 1363 (body_h2.txt:4) and 1768 (body_portals.txt:4)—the bead's numbers were mis-transcribed, off by +15 / +13 / +2 from what the tool actually printed. Corrected in the table above to the fixed tool's figures: 1401 / 1243 / 1769. Tier 1 (symbol table) and Tier 2 (opcodes) were unaffected by the tool bug.

CORRECTION 2 — renamed that column from "Byte-Identical Bodies" to "opcode + immediate-multiset + field-operand match" so nobody reads it as a byte-level comparison. The counter required opcode match and tier-3 immediate-multiset match and field-operand match. Tier 3 was declared unreliable and load-bearing on nothing, so this column's movement while tiers 1-2 held constant is inert.

NO NEW DIVERGENCE WAS MASKED—the fixed-only set is empty in all three pairs; every change is a removed false positive. Const-differing hits dropped 40→2, 52→2 and 2→1. The residual tier-3 hits are Killed + meteor_select (h2 / progs2) and quake_shake_next (portals); meteor_select remains the known field-alias false positive the audit already flagged.
close_reason:
COMPLETE for `gamecode/hc/h2` and `gamecode/hc/portals`. Compared `nix build .#gamecode` output against retail `data1/PROGS.DAT`, `data1/progs2.dat` and `portals/progs.dat` across three tiers (function symbol table; per-function opcode stream; immediate-constant multiset). Every semantic divergence was classified as (a) upstream uHexen2 fix, (b) deliberate fork change, (c) unreverted accident, or (d) Raven's released source differing from Raven's own shipped bytecode. The great majority is (a), matching `gamecode/README` through 1.29c. Attribution was done by reading commit diffs, not grep — only five commits in the entire fork era touch any `.hc` file.

RE-VERIFIED after the tooling was found buggy. The original run used a disassembler that read v6 statement operands as signed when the engine addresses globals through an unsigned cast; it was fixed when landed as `tools/qcdis.py` (`e6dd815f1`). The audit was re-run with the corrected tool: tiers 1 and 2 reproduced exactly — not merely the counts but the *sets* of function names, function-for-function — so all four category assignments stand unchanged. The fixed-only divergence set was empty in all three pairs, confirming the bug corrupted output rather than concealing divergences. Only the operand-derived tier-3 column moved, and nothing rested on it.

ACTIONED: the one category (c) finding of consequence, `uhexen2-qj8s` (`Use_TimeBomb`), was reverted to retail in `ce8c9d1c4`. Two lesser findings were filed rather than fixed: `uhexen2-0lrr` (`gamecode/README` never updated in the fork era) and `uhexen2-o4tn` (undecided `DropBackpack` debug spam).

NOT COVERED — `gamecode/hc/hw` and `gamecode/hc/siege` are unaudited. No retail HexenWorld bytecode exists on the dev box to compare against, so there is no baseline. That gap is tracked in `uhexen2-nr9l` and is the reason `uhexen2-8qp3` ships `data1` + `portals` only.

Method limitation worth carrying forward: tier 3 is unreliable, and under `-on` (used by portals) it is unavailable entirely. A pure constant retune — a damage number, a timing — inside an otherwise unchanged function would show identical opcodes and would be missed. Tiers 1 and 2 are sound; that residual risk is real and bounded.

title: Repo Use_TimeBomb diverges from every shipped progs.dat
description:
gamecode/hc/h2/invntory.hc does not match any shipped progs.dat. Confirmed via bytecode disassembly of retail data1, Portals, and SoT.

**Divergence:**
- Repo: Crusader Glyph spawns at self.origin + v_forward*64 + '0 0 48', uses TimeBombThink() (orbits player, 5-second fuse)
- All shipped progs.dat: spawn at self.origin + self.proj_ofs, use TimeBombBoom (0.75s detonation, then explode)

Different spawn position, fuse length, and think function entirely.

**Why this matters:**
uhexen2-zmb3 (packages.gamecode) compiled these very sources into progs.dat/progs2.dat. If bundled with vanilla data1/progs.dat, the Crusader Glyph of the Ancients would silently diverge from retail behaviour for every player. zmb3 deferred bundling and noted "bundling changes what 'vanilla' means" — this is a concrete instance of exactly that risk.

**Resolution needed:**
Determine which behaviour is correct:
1. Is the repo .hc an uHexen2 improvement over Raven's shipped bytecode?
2. An unreverted experiment?
3. A divergence introduced at some point in this fork's history?

Check gamecode/README (documents Raven fixes through 1.29c) and upstream uHexen2 sources. Document the resolution (whichever way) in docs/GAMECODE.md.

Related to uhexen2-zmb3 (packages.gamecode).
notes:
AUDIT CLASSIFICATION 2026-08-13: CATEGORY (c) — UNREVERTED ACCIDENT

The Use_TimeBomb change is confirmed to diverge from all three shipped builds and was NOT a designed feature. Evidence:

========== PROVENANCE: ACCIDENTAL CHANGE IN UNRELATED COMMIT ==========

Commit d39212a12 message focuses entirely on underscore-prefixed centerprint plaques. It never mentions the Glyph, the Crusader artifact, or TimeBomb at all. The change landed as part of a larger refactor with no recorded intention. This is the classic fingerprint of an unreverted experiment or an accidental mutation that survived a merge.

========== EVIDENCE #1: ALL THREE SHIPPED BUILDS AGREE — OURS MATCHES NONE ==========

Retail data1/progs.dat:
  - Use_TimeBomb spawns at self.origin + self.proj_ofs
  - Calls TimeBombBoom (detonation think, 0.75s)
  - entity is newmis (the projectile)

Retail portals/progs.dat:
  - Use_TimeBomb spawns at self.origin + self.proj_ofs
  - Calls TimeBombBoom (0.75s detonation)

SoT/progs.dat (retail's own hc-to-bytecode):
  - Use_TimeBomb spawns at self.origin + self.proj_ofs
  - Calls TimeBombBoom (0.75s)

Our repo:
  - Use_TimeBomb spawns at self.origin + v_forward*64 + '0 0 48'
  - Calls TimeBombThink (orbits, 5s fuse)
  - Stores orbit center in self.o_angle (captured once at spawn)

We match NONE of them. This is not a faithful uHexen2 backport.

========== EVIDENCE #2: NOT A FAITHFUL BACKPORT OF HEXENWORLD ==========

Raven's HexenWorld TimeBombThink (gamecode/hc/hw/invntory.hc):
  - Orbits the OWNER (self.enemy) at radius 90
  - 10-second fuse
  - Still spawns at self.origin + self.proj_ofs (preserved in hw/invntory.hc, untouched since initial import)
  - Uses TimeBombBoom for detonation

Our repo's TimeBombThink (gamecode/hc/h2/invntory.hc):
  - Orbits a FIXED POINT (self.origin + v_forward*64 + '0 0 48') captured into o_angle at spawn
  - 5-second fuse
  - Radius 48 (not 90)
  - This is a different design entirely, not a port of HexenWorld

========== EVIDENCE #3: CANNOT HAVE FIXED THE REPORTED BUG ==========

d39212a12's motivation was uhexen2-9uzt: "SoT: Glyph of Ancients projectiles drop at feet instead of being thrown"

Critical fact: SoT ships its own progs.dat (siege/hwprogs.dat), which shadows both data1 and portals unconditionally via gamedir search order (mod gamedir is added last, wins on lookup).

SoT's progs.dat is RETAIL HEXENWORLD BYTECODE — it is bit-identical to what Raven shipped. Our Use_TimeBomb change has zero effect on SoT players. The change cannot have fixed that bug.

uhexen2-9uzt's resolution confirmed the bug was NOT a bug: "Stock Hexen II class design. Cleric and Mage Glyphs spawn at player feet by design (0.75s detonation)... Warrior and Rogue variants throw correctly."

This establishes that the _reported_ issue was user confusion about vanilla class balance, not a defect in our code. No actual bug to fix. The Use_TimeBomb change was not remedying anything.

========== SUPPORTING NO-OPS CHECKED ==========

Two things that might obscure the accident if they were real changes:

1. newmis.enemy=world removal: NOT a problem. spawn() zeroes all fields, world is entity 0, so DarkExplosion's ignore=self.enemy hits world either way.
2. T_Damage removal from TimeBombTouch: NOT a problem. Retail's version damaged self.enemy (world), so it was inert anyway.

These are cosmetic and do not explain why TimeBombBoom was replaced with an entirely new TimeBombThink function with different orbit/fuse/spawn logic.

========== RE-CONFIRMATIONS 2026-08-13 ==========

qj8s re-confirmed exactly with the fixed qcdis.py tool (v6 unsigned-operand fix, e6dd815f1):

Our repo (all five trees): TimeBombExplode + TimeBombThink + TimeBombTouch and no TimeBombBoom
Retail data1: TimeBombBoom + TimeBombTouch and no TimeBombThink and no TimeBombExplode
Retail progs2: TimeBombBoom + TimeBombTouch and no TimeBombThink and no TimeBombExplode
Retail portals: TimeBombBoom + TimeBombTouch and no TimeBombThink and no TimeBombExplode
SoT/hwprogs.dat: TimeBombBoom + TimeBombTouch and no TimeBombThink and no TimeBombExplode

Category (d) entity field divergence also re-confirmed analytically: ours 392 entity fields vs retail 390; fields present only in ours are exactly scoped and sheep_call (retail-only: none); 194 shared fields shift offset; wake_sheep and sheep_run_use present in ours and SoT but absent from retail portals; monster_death_use is 1-parm in ours and SoT, 0-parm in retail portals. CRC read from both file headers is 26905 on both sides, and SoT carries 514 entity fields on that same 26905—independent evidence that field count does not enter the CRC and the divergence is harmless.

========== DECISION REQUIRED ==========

This divergence is the exception to the "our .hc wins" governance rule — that rule presumes deliberation, and this one is confirmed accidental.

Owner's pending decision:
- REVERT: h2 + portals Use_TimeBomb/TimeBombTouch to TimeBombBoom (matches all shipped builds, was never designed)
- KEEP + DOCUMENT: if kept, requires:
  (a) gamecode/README entry recording the design intent
  (b) bd issue explaining why the change differs from every shipped build and Raven's HexenWorld code
  (c) this must be decided before bundling (8qp3)

Audit finding remains unchanged: the divergence is real, category (c), and requires owner decision.
close_reason:
DECISION: the owner chose to revert, against the project's general "our .hc wins" rule, because the audit confirmed this divergence was category (c) — an unreverted accident, not a deliberate improvement. It landed in d39212a12, a commit whose message is entirely about centerprint plaques; it is not a faithful backport of Raven's HexenWorld design; and it could not have fixed the SoT report that motivated it, since SoT ships its own shadowing progs.dat.

WHAT CHANGED: gamecode/hc/h2/invntory.hc:316-361 and gamecode/hc/portals/invntory.hc:319-364 — TimeBombExplode renamed back to TimeBombBoom, TimeBombThink deleted, TimeBombTouch and Use_TimeBomb restored to retail. Both function groups are now byte-identical to Raven's imported source (7282897f9) apart from Raven's stray newmis.owner=self;; double semicolon (a no-op).

IMPORTANT — portals was diverged by TWO commits, not one. e9731510a first renamed TimeBombBoom → TimeBombExplode and made it a thrown MOVETYPE_BOUNCE bomb; d39212a12 then replaced that with the orbit. A plain git revert would have restored the thrown-bomb divergence, not retail.

IMPORTANT — restore is behavioural in portals, not just cosmetic. Retail portals has no enemy = world; its touch does self.dmg /= 2; T_Damage(other, self, self.owner, self.dmg) — real damage (37 or 50) to the actual toucher. So Portals players will see the Crusader glyph able to damage them. This is retail behaviour but a larger change than timing and should be called out in release notes.

VALIDATION: nix build .#gamecode — all four trees compile clean, zero warnings. Symbol sets now agree with retail: TimeBombBoom + TimeBombTouch for all h2/portals variants. Pseudo bodies are identical retail-vs-ours after masking absolute statement numbers.

Fixed by ce8c9d1c4 (fix(gamecode): revert TimeBomb glyph to retail behaviour).

title: khsa: MIN_FILTER demotion revisit for r29 fence/holey textures
description:
Deferred from heg1 (r30 cleanup of khsa scaffolding). The r29 MIN_FILTER demotion (gl_draw.c:2247-2266) demotes GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR → GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_NEAREST for TEX_HOLEY/TEX_FENCE textures.

CONTEXT:
The demotion served a hypothesis (mipmap alpha-test shimmer) that was disproven 2026-06-22. The mitigation is partial only — GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_NEAREST still interpolates alpha within each mip level, and anisotropic filtering still multi-taps — so it applies a global mip-pop quality regression to every FENCE/HOLEY texture (world brushes, not just alias) for a dead theory.

The principled half (mip alpha re-binarization at gl_draw.c:2216-2226) stays regardless and is correct.

OPTIONS:
1. Revert the demotion (remove lines 2247-2266 entirely) unless there is independent visual justification on Ironwail parity or known regression grounds
2. Keep and document: if retained, document the design rationale (visual quality trade-off vs. mip pop, parity with another engine, etc.)

ACCEPTANCE:
- r29 demotion either reverted or documented with visual justification
- No dead/unjustified code in the filtering path
close_reason:
Reverted, per option 1. Removed in 8c88a5f29 (gl_draw.c) -- TEX_HOLEY/TEX_FENCE textures now take gl_texturemode like every other mipmapped texture.

Three reasons, the third of which was not in the bead:

1. The theory is dead. r29 targeted cross-LOD interpolation of the pre-binarized mip alpha as the source of the screen-door. The 2026-06-22 repro detail in uhexen2-khsa retired that whole family (always the same entity; which entity breaks shifts between builds; re-running the same map fixes it; a different map in between breaks it again) -- a stale resource across a map transition, not a coverage effect. r29 was never confirmed by the reporter to fix anything.

2. It could not have worked as described, which is the bead's own point and it holds on inspection. GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_NEAREST only stops interpolating BETWEEN mips; sampling within the chosen mip is still bilinear, so every cutout edge still yields the full 0..255 fractional alpha range, and anisotropic filtering still multi-taps. It removed one of two sources of an effect that remained.

3. NEW FINDING -- the demotion was never even stable at runtime. Draw_TouchAllFilterModes (gl_draw.c:443) walks every texture on any gl_texturemode change, including from the Display options menu, and writes gl_texmodes[gl_filter_idx].minimize unconditionally with no FENCE/HOLEY special case. The demotion therefore applied at upload time and was silently undone the first time the player touched the filter setting, leaving upload and re-touch disagreeing for the rest of the session. Half the sessions that shipped with r29 were not running it. That is independent evidence it was not load-bearing, and it means the revert also removes a real inconsistency between the two filter-setting paths rather than merely reverting a quality trade-off.

Cost removed: mip-LOD popping on every FENCE/HOLEY texture -- world brush grates and fences, not just the alias models the report was about.

Kept, as the bead required: the mip alpha re-binarization loop (gl_draw.c, the 'Re-binarize alpha in mipmaps for alpha-tested textures' block) and the GL_RGBA8 internal-format force for TEX_FENCE/TEX_HOLEY. Both are the principled half and are untouched.

A comment now sits where the demotion was, recording why it is gone, so it is not re-added without a repro that a MIN_FILTER change actually moves. Acceptance 'no dead/unjustified code in the filtering path' met.

Not claimed: the r29 comment asserted the demotion 'matches Ironwail'. No Ironwail source was available here to check that either way, so it formed no part of this decision -- the three reasons above stand on their own.

Verified: nix build clean, no new warnings. Headless on SoT cathedral cycling gl_texturemode GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR -> GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST -> GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR under developer 1 -- no GL errors, no invalid enum, clean shutdown.

title: WASM: deliver a soundfont into the emscripten virtual FS
description:
59343680d wired the libTiMidity codec into BGM tier 2 and it builds and links for WASM, but nothing puts an SF2 where SF_FindSoundFont() can see it, so browser MIDI is still silent. exe_dir() compiles out under emscripten and host_parms->basedir maps to the virtual FS, so the reachable hook is <basedir>/soundfont.sf2 or data1/soundfont.sf2.

Two options with a real tradeoff:
- --preload-file: simple, but adds ~6 MB to first load, likely unacceptable for web target.
- Startup fetch into FS before S_CodecInit: keeps initial download small, but needs init-order work, since codec initializes eagerly and failed init drops handler permanently.

A smaller GM font than TimGM6mb is probably the right call for web; this is the one place uhexen2-unvi's criterion 5 ("one soundfont serves both synths, no second soundfont in any package") may need deliberate exception.

Verification requires a browser. Note that flake.nix filteredSrc blocker is resolved in 7fdbfd8a8, so not blocked on it.
notes:
INVESTIGATED 2026-08-15. The bead's open format question is settled, and a
latent defect was found in the process. Delivery mechanism is still open.

2026-08-18: uhexen2-d4e7 is fixed (c7cf3f493) -- SF_FindSoundFont no longer
hands libTiMidity an SF3, so a soundfont delivered into the emscripten FS by
this bead can be an .sf2 without the SF3 hazard sitting behind it. The fix is
unit-tested but has never been heard: when this bead puts a font in the
virtual FS, drop an .sf3 in alongside it once and confirm the engine steps
over it rather than playing noise. That is the cheapest runtime check of
d4e7 available anywhere in the tree.

title: khsa scaffolding teardown and r29 filter-demotion revisit
description:
The r4-r29 arc on uhexen2-khsa involved ~15 probe cvars that are now ruled out. Clean up the codebase by removing the dead scaffolding.

IMMEDIATE TEARDOWN (remove entirely):
- r_alias_fullbright (r21) — RULED OUT, v_color RGB wasn't the issue
- r_alias_nofog (r22) — RULED OUT, fog math wasn't the issue
- r_alias_r6_mode (r22) — worked because it bypassed ALL downstream logic; ACTIVELY HAZARDOUS — this CVAR_ARCHIVE early-returns before all discard logic, so setting it breaks every cutout in the game
- r_alias_stochastic_alpha (r28) — works because hash discard sidesteps the threshold but not the root cause
- Inert desktop precision lines at gl_shader.c:289 and :300 (highp declarations)

KEEP (these are real features, not probes):
- r_aliasinfo — permanent diagnostic, not a probe
- r_alias_minlight — real Ironwail-parity feature, not a probe
- u_force_opaque_alpha — load-bearing for cutout rendering

CONSTRAINT: Must NOT touch gl_shader.c:275-276 — the GLSL ES 3.00 path for WASM/WebGL2 where 'mediump' is deliberate and necessary.

SEPARATELY REVISIT r29 MIN_FILTER demotion (gl_draw.c:2247-2266): The GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR -> GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_NEAREST demotion for TEX_HOLEY/TEX_FENCE serves a hypothesis disproven 2026-06-22 and applies globally to world brush fences. Per the fix-triage: it is a partial mitigation only (still interpolates alpha within-mip; anisotropic filtering still multi-taps), and the principled half (mip alpha re-binarization at gl_draw.c:2216-2226) stays regardless. Recommend revert unless justified on visual grounds. If kept, document the rationale.

COSMETIC FIND: The comment paragraph 'For cutout alpha-test (threshold > 0.5…)' is pasted twice in sworld_frag around gl_shader.c:500-511 — deduplicate.

STATUS: A dev agent is doing the immediate teardown half now; mark in_progress. Leave the r29 revisit as the remaining scope.

ACCEPTANCE: Probe cvars removed; r_alias_r6_mode no longer exists to break cutouts; gl_shader.c cleanup complete; r29 demotion either reverted or documented with visual justification; no duplicate comments in sworld_frag.
close_reason:
IMMEDIATE TEARDOWN COMPLETE (75a3a855b) — "refactor(khsa): remove ruled-out fragment-pipeline scaffolding"

Removed four ruled-out probe cvars (r_alias_fullbright, r_alias_nofog, r_alias_r6_mode, r_alias_stochastic_alpha), inert desktop precision lines (gl_shader.c:289, :300), and associated plumbing: GL_SetAlias* setters, imm_alias_* state in gl_vbo.c, prototypes in gl_vbo.h, struct fields in two structs in gl_shader.h, and a GL_SetAliasStochasticAlpha(0.0f) leak-guard in the sprite path. No dead state left behind.

Kept as intended: r_aliasinfo (permanent diagnostic), r_alias_minlight (real Ironwail-parity feature), u_force_opaque_alpha (load-bearing semantic fix).

GL_SHADER_ES path (gl_shader.c:275-276) was deliberately not touched — mediump is necessary for WASM/WebGL2.

Validation: nix-builder PASS (default Linux + win64, zero new warnings — existing warnings are pre-existing). shader-validator PASS: 29 shaders, 16 desktop + 13 ES 3.0, 0 errors. Headless runtime: all removed cvars print Unknown command; all 13 shader programs compiled and linked live on llvmpipe. WASM: emcc compilation clean on gl_shader.c, gl_vbo.c, gl_rmain.c, gl_rmisc.c.

SCOPE NOTE — r29 MIN_FILTER demotion REVISIT DEFERRED: The bead had two halves and only the teardown half is finished. The r29 MIN_FILTER filter-demotion revisit (demote GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR → GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_NEAREST for TEX_HOLEY/TEX_FENCE at gl_draw.c:2247-2266) was NOT done and must be handled separately. Filed as uhexen2-izii to track the decision: revert unless justified on visual/parity grounds, or document the rationale if kept.

title: SoT: Glyph of Ancients projectiles drop at feet instead of being thrown
description:
Glyph of the Ancients projectiles are not being launched from the character — they drop at the player's feet and explode immediately instead of being thrown as projectiles. This makes them unusable since you can't escape before detonation.

Originally reported bundled with missing-asset issues in uhexen2-40e, but this is a distinct defect: likely projectile spawn velocity/origin defect in engine or gamecode, not a missing asset.

This machine can run the engine headless against /home/josh/hexen2/sot, so this half may be investigable locally (unlike the missing-audio half). Investigate spawn mechanics for this projectile (probably SoT gamecode in *.qc, possibly engine projectile handling).
close_reason: NOT A BUG: Stock Hexen II class design. Cleric and Mage Glyphs (two of four) spawn at player feet by design (0.75s detonation and proximity mine respectively); Warrior and Rogue variants throw correctly. SoT modified only damage, not behavior. This is mod balance, not engine defect. If reporter was testing Warrior/Rogue and still saw drop, that is a separate report.

title: flake: tighten filteredSrc to an allowlist of real build inputs
description:
filteredSrc was a denylist (.beads/.github/history/docs/flatpak/gamecode/*.md/release.sh/.gitignore). Everything else landed in the source copy, including flake.nix itself — so every edit to the build recipe changed the source hash and rebuilt every package from scratch, defeating the cachix hit rate.

Replaced with an allowlist of what the CMake builds actually read: CMakeLists.txt, engine, utils, hw_utils, common, scripts (utils/CMakeLists.txt reads mk_header.c), oslibs (reached as ${UHEXEN2_TOP}/oslibs from engine/CMakeLists.txt:18 for prebuilt Windows SDL3/codecs, and copied by the win64 installPhase — no literal path in any CMakeLists, so easy to drop by mistake).

Dropped: flake.nix, flake.lock, shell-wasm.nix, assets, patches, tools, h2patch, LICENSE, Makefile. The release package reaches scripts/oslibs/COPYING via ${self} (unfiltered), so it is unaffected.

Also corrects a wrong assumption worth recording: gitignored paths (result, capture.rdc, the demo tarball) never reached filteredSrc in the first place — Nix's dirty-git-tree copy already drops them. The filter only ever sees tracked files.
close_reason: Landed in 924588ba0. Verified: appending to flake.nix no longer moves the source path, and all eight nix outputs (nixos, h2ded, win64, h2ded-win64, utils, utils-win64, linux-fhs, release) build, with SDL3.dll from oslibs and the get_demo helpers from $self still in the release bundle.

title: flake: add packages.demodata (user-fetched Nov 1997 demo data1)
description:
Declarative counterpart to 'nix run .#get-demo'. A fetchurl-based derivation, pinned to the SRI hash already recorded in assets/demo/README.md, that unpacks only hexen2demo_nov1997/data1 into $out/share/hexenwail/data1 so it can be used with 'glhexen2 -basedir'.

Constraint from uhexen2-3vmk: the demo's only license is Activision's retail EULA and no redistribution grant exists, so Hexenwail must never SERVE these bytes. That makes this output legal-to-add but dangerous-to-cache: it must never be referenced by packages.release, never appear in a CI workflow, and never reach hexenwail.cachix.org. Marked lib.licenses.unfree (NOT unfreeRedistributable — that label would assert a grant that does not exist) with a scoped allowUnfreePredicate so a user opting in locally still gets a working 'nix build .#demodata'.
close_reason: Added in 75da0dc72. Builds and runs: engine loads pak0.pak (797 files) via -basedir and prints 'Playing the demo version.' Marked lib.licenses.unfree per uhexen2-3vmk (retail EULA, no grant found) rather than unfreeRedistributable; hydraPlatforms=[] plus a never-cache/never-release comment guard the constraint. CI is unaffected — ci.yml and release.yml build named packages individually, so nothing sweeps demodata into hexenwail.cachix.org.

title: Runtime-verify the MIDI callback deferral on Windows (uhexen2-99v0 follow-up)
description:
Follow-up to uhexen2-99v0 / uhexen2-q646, fixed in commit c9ecbc982. engine/h2shared/midi_win.c is Windows-only (PLATFORM_SOURCES, WIN32 branch of engine/CMakeLists.txt), so nothing in that change has been exercised at runtime — it is compile-verified on nix build .#win64 only, and this dev machine has no Windows and no GL.

The change moved work off the midiStream callback thread, so the failure modes to watch for are timing ones, not compile ones.

WHAT TO CHECK on Windows with a real MIDI device (needs a mod or install whose music is .mid and that actually selects the midi_win driver — check the console for 'midiStream for Windows initialized'):
1. Music plays at all, and a track that reaches its natural end tears down cleanly. Teardown now happens on the main thread in MIDI_Update (polled midi_stop_pending flag) rather than inside MidiProc. Watch for a hang, a stuck last note, or silence where the next track should start.
2. Change the music volume slider while a MIDI track is playing. The per-channel rescale now goes through Host_TryInvokeOnMainThread, so it lands up to a frame late; it must still take effect and must not stutter the music.
3. A MIDI file that itself contains main-volume controller events (MIDICTL_MSB_MAIN_VOLUME) — those drive the MOM_POSITIONCB path that was rewritten. Volume balance across channels should sound as before.
4. Switch tracks repeatedly and quickly (changelevel back and forth, or play/stop from the console). MIDI_Stop clears midi_stop_pending on entry specifically so a stale request cannot kill the *next* track; a track that dies immediately after starting would be that bug.
5. A missing or corrupt .mid: the refill error paths now end the track via MidiProc_EndOfData instead of calling ConverterCleanup on the callback thread. Should log 'MidiProc() conversion pass failed!' and stop cleanly rather than crash.
6. Quit while music is playing. AsyncQueue_Destroy moved after the subsystem shutdowns in Host_Shutdown so the callback thread cannot outlive the queue; a hang or crash on exit would point back here.

The pre-existing deadlock this fixed was rare (it needed the callback to reenter the multimedia layer at the wrong moment), so absence of a hang does not by itself prove much — the point of the checks above is that nothing regressed.
notes: 2026-08-13 TRIAGE: marked blocked. Windows-only code path (engine/h2shared/midi_win.c).

title: Give users a one-command way to fetch the Hexen II demo data legitimately
description:
Follow-up to uhexen2-3vmk, which established that Hexenwail cannot bundle Raven's demo data into a release artifact: the only license shipped with it is Activision's retail EULA, which forbids distributing copies without written consent, and no shareware grant exists to be found.

That kills the bundling in uhexen2-menr, but not the goal behind it. A new user should not have to already own a 1997 game to try the engine. What we can do is help them fetch the demo THEMSELVES from where it has been publicly hosted for two decades - uHexen2's SourceForge - rather than mirroring it ourselves. The user performs the download from the existing host; Hexenwail redistributes nothing.

Today a user with no game data gets Sys_Error 'Unable to find a proper Hexen II installation' (quakefs.c:1585) and nothing else - no statement of what data is wanted, where it should go, or how to obtain any. That is the actual wall, and it is a bad first impression regardless of the demo question.

Note the engine ALREADY recognises the demo data: demo_pakdata at quakefs.c:119 identifies the Nov 1997 pak0.pak by file count 797, CRC 22780 and size 27750257 (verified against the local copy), and FS_Init prints 'Playing the demo version.' So nothing in the engine needs to change to make demo data work. Only acquisition and guidance are missing.

DELIVERABLES
1. scripts/get_demo.sh - POSIX sh. Downloads the tarball from the verified SourceForge URL, checks it against the pinned sha256 (2df15cde0128b7a036e71995e068ca853f13be8e2b591caac140025d66643fc0), extracts ONLY data1/ - not the bundled 1997 i586 binaries, which are useless here - and installs it to a destination the user names. Must refuse to clobber existing data. Works with curl or wget, sha256sum or shasum.
2. scripts/get_demo.ps1 - PowerShell equivalent for Windows, where the testers are. Invoke-WebRequest, Get-FileHash, and the bsdtar that ships in Windows 10 1803+.
3. A flake app so 'nix run .#get-demo' works with the fetch tools already provided.
4. Rewrite the no-data Sys_Error to name the basedir it searched, say that owners of Hexen II can copy their existing data1 there, and point at the scripts for those who do not.

DELIBERATELY NOT DOING: an in-engine downloader. The engine has no HTTP stack and adding libcurl to acquire a file once, at first run, is not a trade worth making.

The scripts must be explicit that the user is downloading from the uHexen2 project under whatever terms apply to that data, and that Hexenwail neither hosts nor licenses it.
acceptance_criteria: A user with no game data can run one command, get the demo installed, and launch straight into it; the command verifies the download against the pinned hash and refuses to overwrite existing data; the no-data error names the searched path and points at the command; nothing in a Hexenwail release artifact contains Raven game content.
close_reason:
Done in 9cec08fd5. scripts/get_demo.sh (POSIX sh; curl or wget, sha256sum or shasum), scripts/get_demo.ps1 (Windows), and 'nix run .#get-demo'. Each verifies the pinned SHA-256 before installing, extracts only data1/ (the package also ships 1997 i586 binaries of the old engine), unpacks to a scratch dir and moves into place so an interrupt cannot leave a half-populated data1, and refuses to touch existing game data. The no-data Sys_Error at quakefs.c:1585 now names the searched basedir, tells owners to copy their existing data1, and points at the platform-appropriate fetch command. No engine change was needed for the data itself — demo_pakdata at quakefs.c:119 already identified the Nov 1997 pak0.pak by file count/CRC/size.

TWO THINGS TESTING CAUGHT, both recorded in-code so they do not get undone:
1. Invoke-WebRequest downloaded SourceForge's 143 KB HTML interstitial instead of the tarball. SourceForge chooses between file and page by User-Agent: curl and wget get the file, browser-shaped agents get the page or a 403 from downloads.sourceforge.net. Both scripts now use the direct host; the PowerShell one sets a tool User-Agent. The checksum was the only thing catching it, and only after a 13 MB download.
2. The flake could not read scripts/get_demo.sh until it was git-tracked — the same constraint already noted against menr.3's sketched path literal.

VERIFIED END TO END: sh via curl, sh via wget, PowerShell (under pwsh with tar substituted for tar.exe), and nix run all install a pak0.pak of exactly 27750257 bytes, matching demo_pakdata. Engine then reports 'Added packfile ./data1/pak0.pak (797 files)' and 'Playing the demo version.' (headless run stops after that on the dummy driver lacking OpenGL, well past the data check). Overwrite, missing-destination and checksum-mismatch guards each confirmed to refuse and install nothing. PowerShell script parse-checked and its three guard paths exercised under pwsh 7.6.2.

title: MidiProc calls Windows multimedia functions from inside the MIDI callback
description:
Pre-existing (upstream Hammer of Thyrion), NOT the r5 regression. MidiProc in engine/h2shared/midi_win.c is the midiStream CALLBACK_FUNCTION handler invoked by Windows on its own callback thread. MSDN explicitly forbids calling multimedia (midiOut*/midiStream*) functions from within a MIDI callback — it can deadlock.

Current violations:
- midi_win.c:574 — MIDI_SetChannelVolume calls midiOutShortMsg
- midi_win.c:499 — MIDI_Stop((void **)NULL) calls midiStreamStop and midiOutReset

Additionally, the main thread issues midiOutShortMsg on the same hStream concurrently (MIDI_SetAllChannelVolumes, 16 calls per volume change) with no synchronisation against the callback thread.

This deadlock/corruption risk compounds the use-after-free in uhexen2-520e.

FIX DIRECTION: marshal this work off the callback thread. The engine already has Host_InvokeOnMainThread / AsyncQueue_Drain in engine/hexen2/host_async.c for exactly this pattern.
close_reason: Fixed in c9ecbc982: MIDI_Stop teardown deferred to MIDI_Update on the main thread via a polled flag; per-channel volume rescale deferred via Host_TryInvokeOnMainThread with channel+volume packed into the param (volume_cache is now main-thread-only); Con_Printf in the callback replaced with Host_PrintAsync; hw_vol_capable dead branch removed; MIDI_Play no longer passes (void**)&hStream as a handle slot. Also fixed two latent bugs uncovered en route (refill error paths freeing track data then continuing, and end-of-data hanging when all buffers were already returned) and moved AsyncQueue_Destroy after the subsystem shutdowns so the MIDI callback thread cannot outlive the queue. nix build .#win64 and nix build clean.

title: config.cfg only written on clean shutdown, so crashes discard all settings
description:
Tester reported Misc/HUD menu settings (glow intensity, HUD scale, etc.) not persisting after session. Root cause is NOT the menu — all cvars are correctly CVAR_ARCHIVE: scr_sbarscale, scr_menuscale, scr_crosshairscale, scr_centerprintbg, scr_conalpha, scr_conbrightness, con_maxcols, sbtrans, gl_overbright_models, gl_coloredlight, gl_torch_dlight, gl_glow_intensity, scr_showspeed, showclock.

Host_WriteConfiguration("config.cfg") has only THREE call sites:
- Host_Shutdown in engine/hexen2/host.c:1120
- Gamedir change in engine/h2shared/quakefs.c:1419
- Explicit saveConfig command

Nothing writes config on cvar change or on leaving the menu. Any crash or alt-F4 silently discards all settings changed that session.

FIX DIRECTION: flush config on menu close, or on archive-cvar change with debouncing, so settings survive an unclean exit.

Acceptance: a setting changed in the menu survives a hard kill of the process (SIGKILL or crash).
close_reason: Fixed in d5db241f8. Cvar_SetQuick marks the config stale whenever a CVAR_ARCHIVE cvar's value actually changes (below its no-change early return, so redundant sets don't count), Key_SetBinding marks it too since Host_WriteConfiguration emits bindings, and _Host_Frame flushes at most every 2s (CONFIG_FLUSH_DELAY). Flag lives in cvar.c so h2ded — which uses hexen2/server/host.c and has no Host_WriteConfiguration — is untouched. Host_WriteConfiguration also switched to write-temp-then-Sys_rename: rewriting the live file every 2s during a session that may crash would otherwise open a truncation window, i.e. exactly the loss this issue is about. It now also reports ferror and FS_MakePath truncation instead of silently ignoring both. nix build, .#win64 and .#h2ded all clean. Runtime acceptance (kill -9 then confirm the setting survived) tracked in uhexen2-ekdm — no GL on this dev box, so the engine can't reach a frame loop here.

title: Toggling gl_lmatlas then vid_restart leaves surface UVs baked for the other mode
description:
Adjacent to uhexen2-6yzs, same root shape but a different trigger, and not fixed by it.

TRIGGER (fully user-reachable, no big map needed)
With a map loaded: set gl_lmatlas to the opposite of what it was, then vid_restart. vid_restart is a console command (gl_vidsdl.c:1673) and VID_Restart_f is also called from the video menu when a mode change is applied (gl_vidsdl.c:2234, 2392), so changing resolution after touching the cvar is enough.

WHAT HAPPENS
GL_BuildLightmaps re-reads the cvar unconditionally on every call: lm_atlas_enabled = (Cvar_VariableValue("gl_lmatlas") != 0) at gl_rsurf.c:3803. But on a video restart (draw_reinit true) it deliberately skips pass 2, so BuildSurfaceDisplayList never runs and surf->polys keeps the lightmap UVs it was given at map load - page-local if the atlas was off then, atlas-space if it was on.

The skip is not gratuitous: BuildSurfaceDisplayList allocates a fresh glpoly_t from the hunk and prepends it to fa->polys (gl_rsurf.c:3543-3546), so simply re-running pass 2 would leak a second full set of polygons into the hunk and chain them onto the first. That is why it was written to skip.

So after the toggle the two disagree. Concretely:
- atlas on at load, gl_lmatlas 0 + vid_restart: polys hold atlas-space UVs (s scaled by 1/8, t by 1/rows) and the draw paths now bind a single 256x256 page. Every surface samples a small corner of its own lightmap.
- atlas off at load, gl_lmatlas 1 + vid_restart: R_BuildWorldVBO does re-run on restart (gl_vidsdl.c:1405) and re-bakes its own UVs in the new mode, so world surfaces via the VBO path are right, while anything drawn from surf->polys still carries page-local UVs against the atlas. A split-personality frame.

It stays wrong until the next map load, and nothing on screen says why.

The 6yzs fix does not cover this. That one settles the atlas decision before pass 2 bakes; here pass 2 does not run at all. 6yzs also adds one more way to reach the same state - if the restarted context reported a smaller GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE, the new size check would clear lm_atlas_enabled under already-baked UVs - though in practice the same GPU reports the same limit.

FIX
Re-bake the UVs in place instead of skipping. The lightmap UV for a vertex is a pure function of the vertex world position and the surface's texinfo/light_s/light_t/lightmaptexturenum, and BuildSurfaceDisplayList already stores that world position in poly->verts[i][0..2] (VectorCopy(vec, poly->verts[i])). So the s,t at verts[i][5],[6] can be recomputed from data already in the poly, with no edge walk and no allocation.

Suggested shape:
- factor the UV math out of BuildSurfaceDisplayList into a helper taking (surface, vec) and returning s,t, so the two paths cannot drift;
- add a rebake that walks fa->polys and rewrites verts[i][5],[6] through that helper;
- in pass 2, call BuildSurfaceDisplayList when !draw_reinit and the rebake when draw_reinit, with the same SURF_DRAWTURB / SURF_DRAWSKY skips, instead of wrapping the whole pass in if (!draw_reinit).

Pass 1 already re-runs on restart and is deterministic - allocated[] is memset and last_lightmap_allocated reset, and the iteration order is identical - so light_s/light_t/lightmaptexturenum come back with the same values the rebake needs.
acceptance_criteria: Toggling gl_lmatlas with a map loaded and then running vid_restart renders lightmaps correctly in the newly selected mode, in both directions, without a map reload; no extra hunk allocation on restart.
close_reason: Fixed in 6059af819. Pass 2 no longer skips on draw_reinit; it re-bakes the existing polys' UVs in place instead. The UV math is factored into LM_SurfaceLightmapUV (a pure function of vertex world position + texinfo + light_s/light_t + lightmaptexturenum) and shared by BuildSurfaceDisplayList and the new LM_RebakeSurfaceLightmapUVs, so the two paths cannot drift. The re-bake reads the world position already stored at verts[i][0..2] and rewrites verts[i][5..6] — no edge walk, no hunk allocation, so the reason the pass was skipped (BuildSurfaceDisplayList allocating and prepending a duplicate glpoly_t) no longer applies. Same turb/sky skips as before. This also closes the one new way uhexen2-6yzs could reach the same state, a restarted context reporting a smaller GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE than the UVs were baked under. nix build .#default clean, no new warnings. Not runtime-verified — needs a display; the visible check is: load a map, toggle gl_lmatlas, vid_restart, confirm lightmaps stay correct in both directions.

title: Engine ships no default.cfg, so gamecode/res config fixes never reach players
description:
Discovered while closing uhexen2-wfp6 (zoom binds moved from the fov-stepping alias to togglezoom).

flake.nix:46 excludes the whole 'gamecode' directory from the nix build source filter, and there is no install rule anywhere for gamecode/res/*/default.cfg. So those files are source-of-truth for someone rebuilding a game data pak, and nothing more -- no Hexenwail release artifact contains them.

What players actually run: host.c:1061 execs hexen.rc, which execs default.cfg, and menu.c:2146 re-execs it on 'reset to defaults' ('unbindall; exec default.cfg; +mlook'). With no loose default.cfg in the game directory, the search resolves to Raven's copy inside retail pak0.pak. That copy still contains the old zoom_in/zoom_out fov-stepping aliases and every other pre-Hexenwail default.

Consequences:
1. The uhexen2-wfp6 fix is invisible to retail users. F11 still runs the frame-rate-dependent alias that clobbers the fov cvar, and 'reset to defaults' in the menu restores it.
2. The same is true of any future default-bind or default-cvar change made in gamecode/res. That is a silent trap: the change looks landed and reviewed, and has no effect in the field.
3. Mods that ship their own default.cfg are unaffected either way; this is specifically about the base game dirs.

Options, roughly in increasing order of intrusiveness:
- Ship the repo's default.cfg as a loose file in the release layout (data1/default.cfg etc). Cheapest, but a loose file overrides the pak for every user including those who want vanilla, and it has to be kept in sync per game dir (h2, portals, hw, siege).
- Ship a Hexenwail-specific config execed AFTER default.cfg (e.g. hexenwail.cfg from hexen.rc) that only overrides what we actually changed. Less clobbering, but needs an engine-side exec and a decision about what happens on 'reset to defaults'.
- Apply the defaults in engine code as bind defaults, so no data file is involved at all. Most robust against pak0 contents, biggest change.

Worth deciding before any further gamecode/res config edits, since each one silently accumulates this gap.

Acceptance: a decision on which mechanism to use, and F11 demonstrably zooming via togglezoom on a fresh install with retail pak0.pak and no user config.
close_reason: Fixed in bf38073ea. Chose the engine-side mechanism (option 3 of the three the issue weighed): Cmd_Exec_f injects a minimal engine-defaults string immediately after any default.cfg body. Cbuf_InsertText prepends, so inserting defaults first and the file second gives default.cfg -> engine defaults -> config.cfg; engine beats the stale retail pak defaults, user config still beats the engine. Covers all three default.cfg paths (hexen.rc at startup, 'reset to defaults' in the options menu, gamedir change) with no change to any of them. Contents: zoom_in/zoom_out redefined as togglezoom rather than unaliased, so every key any config bound to them keeps working (F11/MOUSE2 in h2/portals, F11/' in hw, PGUP/PGDN in siege) including a stale user config.cfg. Escape hatch: cfg_enginedefaults 0 (command line, not archived — it must be readable before autoexec.cfg). nix build .#default clean; verified the defaults string and cvar are present in the built binary.

title: CI: flatpak job never hit its build cache (per-SHA cache-key)
description: The flatpak jobs in .github/workflows/ci.yml and release.yml passed cache-key: flatpak-builder-${{ github.sha }} to flatpak/flatpak-github-actions/flatpak-builder@v6. The action expands that to the cache key 'flatpak-builder-<sha>-x86_64', but its ONLY restore fallback is the prefix 'flatpak-builder-<arch>' (index.js: restoreCache(CACHE_PATH, cacheKey, ['flatpak-builder-' + arch])). That prefix can never match a key with the SHA in the middle, so every run logged 'No cache was found', rebuilt all seven modules from scratch, then uploaded a 69 MiB cache nobody would ever read. gh cache list showed 10 orphaned per-SHA caches totalling 722 MB.
design: Drop the cache-key input entirely. The action default is flatpak-builder-<arch>-<sha256(manifest contents)[:20]>, which is stable across commits and IS matched by the prefix fallback. Unchanged manifest => exact hit (which also skips saveCache, since it only saves when cacheKey !== cacheHitKey). Changed manifest => warm restore via prefix, rebuild only from the edited module onward. Tag builds now share the cache CI warmed on master. Also added --no-related to the runtime/SDK preinstall to skip .Locale/.GL.default/.codecs-extra (~16s).
acceptance_criteria: Next CI run's flatpak job logs a cache hit rather than 'No cache was found', and the flatpak job wall time drops from ~237s to roughly 120-140s.
notes: Measured on CI run 31537142710 (flatpak job 237s vs nix job 41s): apt 56s, flatpak install Platform+Sdk 45s, dependency modules 87s (fluidsynth 12 / libogg 5 / libvorbis 11 / libopus 31 / opusfile 7 / libxmp 20 / soundfont 0.3), engine module 24s, export+bundle+cache upload ~17s. Expected after the fix: ~87s of module rebuild plus the cache upload disappear on any commit that does not touch the manifest.
close_reason: Verified in CI run 31539822298 (master, 77727a41e). Flatpak job logged 'Cache hit for: flatpak-builder-x86_64-7851525ab232fe2fc6db' and 'Restored cache with key: ...', then skipped all seven dependency modules ('Cache hit for fluidsynth/libogg/libvorbis/libopus/opusfile/libxmp/timgm6mb-soundfont, skipping build'); only the engine module rebuilt. Wall time 21:51:35 -> 21:53:07 = 92s, against the ~237s baseline and the 120-140s the acceptance predicted. Fix landed in 292abfc81 (drop the per-SHA cache-key so the action's manifest-hash default is used, plus --no-related on the runtime/SDK preinstall). Both acceptance criteria met.

title: Regression: conchars.lmp renders wrong/offset characters after the qpic-header sniff landed
description:
Reported 2026-08-11 (project owner). Bisected to commit 42838fdc5 ("fix(draw): detect qpic-headered conchars.lmp; stop dying on a short one", uhexen2-52gf): console and menu text now display the wrong characters—the character set appears offset or misaligned.

## What Changed (engine/h2shared/gl_draw.c, Draw_Init)

1. Added a qpic-header sniff: if the lump is ≥8+32768 bytes AND the first two little-endian ints read as width=256 and height=128, skip 8 bytes before copying pixels.
2. Replaced the fatal Sys_Error on a short lump with Con_Printf warning + transparent padding, so malformed charsets no longer abort startup.
3. Changed to copy pixels into a static 32768-byte buffer instead of using the FS temp-file buffer directly.

## Ground Truth

Vanilla data is exactly 32768 bytes (raw, no header). Byte sequence verified from demo pak0.pak: `00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 a0 ca ca ca c9 ca ca cb`. Upstream requires exactly 256×128. Therefore the sniff cannot fire on vanilla data (needs ≥32776), and for vanilla the new code is byte-for-byte equivalent to the old. The regression must involve a non-vanilla charset.

## Two Candidate Mechanisms (Not Yet Distinguished)

**Mechanism (a):** The sniff false-fires on a headerless charset ≥32776 bytes whose first 8 bytes coincidentally read as `00 01 00 00 80 00 00 00` (256 and 128), causing an 8-byte shift of the entire atlas and garbled glyphs. Requires a non-blank glyph 0, which is uncommon but possible.

**Mechanism (b):** The charset is SHORT (< 32768 bytes). Before this commit, that triggered a fatal "bad size" Sys_Error at startup. Now it warns and pads with transparent—so the engine boots but draws a partial/corrupted charset. A bisect on "wrong characters" would land on exactly this commit even though the data problem predates it.

## Diagnostic (Run with developer 1)

Report which console line appears; this distinguishes both mechanisms in one run:
- `"conchars.lmp: qpic header found, skipping 8 bytes"` → mechanism (a)
- `"WARNING: gfx/menu/conchars.lmp is short (N of 32768 bytes)"` → mechanism (b)
- `"conchars.lmp: larger file (N bytes), using first 32768"` → neither; sniff did not fire, file is oversize raw, look elsewhere
- none of the above → file is exactly 32768, commit is not the cause

Also provide: which game/mod directory is active, and the exact byte size of that mod's gfx/menu/conchars.lmp.

## Likely Fixes (Once Mechanism Is Known)

**For (a):** Tighten the sniff—require file size to be exactly 8+256×128, and/or require glyph 0 to be blank, or add a cvar/console override to disable the header sniff.

**For (b):** Keep the non-fatal behavior but make the warning unmissable and display the actual file size.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Reporter's charset renders correctly (right characters, no offset).
- Vanilla 32768-byte charsets remain unaffected.
- Genuinely qpic-headered charsets (if they exist in the wild) still render correctly.
- Short charsets still boot rather than aborting.
close_reason: Fixed in 21a632581. Mechanism (a) confirmed by measurement: charsets karma2, SoT (hexen2-sot/ros), portals ship 32776-byte raw conchars.lmp opening 00 01 00 00 80 00 00 00. Match vanilla 79.4% at offset 0 vs 60.8% at offset 8; byte range 8..15 equals vanilla. Vanilla is exactly 32768 raw bytes (eight zero header, gfx/menu/conchars.lmp from demo pak0.pak). Fix: sniff now requires header AND eight zero bytes (glyph 0 blank post-header in all stock-derived charsets). Ambiguous cases treated as raw. All four cases classify correctly; three real mods + vanilla as raw, synthetic headered as headered. NOT screen-verified (no display).

title: [bug] FluidSynth never registers without a startup soundfont, so a later snd_soundfont can't revive MIDI
description:
Follow-up to uhexen2-bsqq, which made snd_soundfont hot-swappable in a live synth. One case that fix deliberately does not cover: when NO soundfont is found at startup, FMIDI_Init returns false, so the FluidSynth MIDI driver never registers with BGM_RegisterMidiDRV. BGM_Init (bgmusic.c:253) then decides handler availability once, from whether any midi driver registered, and reports 'BGM: MIDI driver: none'.

That combination is the common Linux case: a user with no system soundfont sets snd_soundfont in config.cfg to a file they downloaded. The cvar callback added in uhexen2-bsqq cannot help, because fs_synth is NULL and the driver is not in the handler list at all — so MIDI stays dead however valid the path is. Per the project memory on Linux MIDI, there is no MID streamer codec, so MIDIDRIVER_MID is the only route for midi/<name>.mid; losing it loses all MIDI music.

Sketch: split the soundfont load out of FMIDI_Init into a helper called from init, from the cvar callback, and lazily from the play path. Register the driver even with no font loaded, and fail individual tracks with a clear message instead of failing registration. Behaviourally that is no worse when there is genuinely no soundfont anywhere — today those tracks already fail, just with the vaguer 'Couldn't handle music file'.

Not folded into the uhexen2-bsqq commit because it changes startup driver registration and the 'BGM: MIDI driver:' diagnostics, which were added deliberately for troubleshooting, and none of it can be runtime-verified on this machine.
acceptance_criteria: With no soundfont present anywhere at startup, setting snd_soundfont to a valid file (in config.cfg or at the console) results in MIDI music playing without restarting the engine; with no soundfont ever available, midi tracks fail with a FluidSynth-specific message and nothing crashes.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 27c8e27f5. engine/h2shared/midi_fluid.c splits font load: FMIDI_LoadSoundFont (:179), FMIDI_EnsureSoundFont (:202). FMIDI_Init creates synth and returns true with no font, enabling BGM_RegisterMidiDRV. FMIDI_SoundFontChanged works synth-exists/no-font case. FMIDI_Open (:335) retries font search, fails track gracefully if still no font. Desktop nix build passes.

title: Flatpak: disable unused FluidSynth audio drivers
close_reason:
Fixed in ce13ad3e8. Issue had no description; recording it: the Flatpak manifest built FluidSynth with only libsndfile/dbus/systemd disabled, leaving every audio driver backend enabled. Since uhexen2-tdss the engine renders MIDI itself via fluid_synth_write_s16 and feeds the engine's own SDL mixer — confirmed there is no new_fluid_audio_driver call anywhere in midi_fluid.c — so all of those backends are dead code in this build, linking extra libraries into the sandbox for a driver that is never created. It is the same driver stack whose failure inside the sandbox caused uhexen2-tdss in the first place.

Disabled: jack, pulseaudio, alsa, oss, pipewire, portaudio, sdl2 and sdl3. sdl3 matters specifically because org.freedesktop.Platform 25.08 bundles SDL3, so that backend would otherwise be detected and built.

Verified what could be verified without a flatpak-builder run here: all eight option names were checked against FluidSynth v2.4.6's actual CMakeLists.txt (fetched from the tag this manifest pins) rather than assumed, and the manifest was re-parsed afterwards to confirm it is still valid YAML with the expected config-opts list.

NOT built — no flatpak-builder on this machine. The change is declarative and the risk is bounded: if a backend name were wrong CMake would ignore it and the build would behave as before.

title: Native CMake build fails (not degrades) when a codec dev-lib is missing
close_reason:
Fixed in 93d7f5448. Issue had no description; recording the defect: the USE_CODEC_VORBIS/XMP/OPUS options default ON, and engine/CMakeLists.txt used the option value directly to append the codec source and add_definitions(-DUSE_CODEC_x), while only the target_link_libraries step was guarded by the pkg-config *_FOUND result. So with a dev package absent the codec source was still compiled and its -D still set, and the build failed outright rather than degrading.

Fix: after codec discovery, auto-disable each codec whose pkg-config module was not found. Guarded on PKG_CONFIG_FOUND — if pkg-config is unavailable nothing can be concluded and the user's choice is left alone — and Vorbis is exempt on WIN32, where the oslibs prebuilt fallback supplies it without pkg-config. MP3/FLAC/UMX are untouched: dr_mp3/dr_flac are header-only and UMX is built in, so they have no external dev files to miss.

VERIFIED both directions by hiding libxmp from pkg-config in the nix dev shell (dropping its entry from PKG_CONFIG_PATH_FOR_TARGET):
  - before the fix: cmake configured happily reporting 'Tracker (libxmp): ON', then the build failed, ld returned 1, make exit 2
  - after the fix: 'libxmp not found - disabling USE_CODEC_XMP', 'Tracker (libxmp): OFF', configure exit 0, full build and link exit 0
A normal build with everything present is unchanged: Vorbis/libxmp/Opus all still report ON (nix build .#nixos).

title: snd_soundfont user override is dead at startup
close_reason:
Fixed in 3dae52880. The issue had no description, so recording the defect and the cause: snd_soundfont is CVAR_ARCHIVE, but find_soundfont() ran exactly once, from FMIDI_Init, which S_Init calls at host.c:1032 — while 'exec hexen.rc' is only queued at host.c:1066. The config that assigns archived cvars therefore always ran AFTER the soundfont had been chosen, so snd_soundfont.string was read as empty every time and the user override did nothing, on that run or any subsequent one. Setting it at the console did nothing either, since there was no callback and the value was never re-read.

Fix: Cvar_SetCallback(&snd_soundfont, FMIDI_SoundFontChanged), which hot-swaps the soundfont into the live synth. It loads the new font before unloading the old one, so a bad path leaves the current font playing rather than leaving the synth with none.

Scope limit, filed as uhexen2-h2lm rather than left implied: if NO soundfont is found at startup, FMIDI_Init returns false and the driver never registers, so fs_synth is NULL and the callback cannot revive it. That is the common no-system-soundfont Linux case and needs deferred driver registration, which changes startup diagnostics and cannot be runtime-verified here.

Builds clean (nix build .#nixos, FluidSynth 2.5.3 enabled, midi_fluid.c confirmed compiled).

title: BGM_Stop does not flush raw ring for MIDI (stale-PCM tail after stop)
close_reason:
Fixed in dc154621f. Issue had no description; recording the defect: BGM_Stop reset s_rawend inside the 'if (bgmstream)' branch only. Since uhexen2-tdss routed FluidSynth through the engine SDL mixer, the MIDI driver feeds that same raw ring via S_RawSamples in FMIDI_Advance — but it takes the midi_handle branch, not the bgmstream one, so the flush never ran for MIDI. Whatever PCM was already queued ahead of paintedtime kept playing after the stop: the stale-PCM tail in the title. The reset is now unconditional at the end of BGM_Stop, covering both sources.

Builds clean (nix build .#nixos).

title: FluidSynth/CD music ignores bgmloop; non-looping tracks loop forever
close_reason:
Fixed in dc154621f. Issue had no description; recording the defect. Two independent causes behind the one symptom:

1. FluidSynth: midi_fluid.c called fluid_player_set_loop(fs_player, -1) — literally commented 'loop forever' — regardless of bgmloop, so any non-looping track repeated until something else stopped it. It now follows bgmloop at play time, and FMIDI_Advance re-pushes the value whenever it changes, so 'music_loop off' takes effect on the song already playing rather than only the next one. The stale FMIDI_Advance comment that justified the old behaviour ('Loop is forever (-1), so PLAYING is the only state we render') was corrected too.

2. CD: BGM_PlayCDtrack(track, looping) assigned bgmloop only inside its remap branch. The CD file-fallback path at the bottom then opened its stream with S_CodecOpenStreamType(tmp, type, bgmloop) using whatever value the PREVIOUS track had left in the global — so a non-looping track that fell back to a file would loop forever if something looping had played before it. bgmloop is now adopted from the caller once, up front, on every path out of the function.

NOT changed: the cd_*.c drivers keep their own playLooping static, set from the CDAudio_Play argument, which they honour correctly. A later 'music_loop' still will not re-toggle an already-playing CD track — that needs a new API across cd_linux/cd_bsd/cd_win/cd_null and is out of proportion to this bug. Real CD audio is also largely vestigial now.

Builds clean (nix build .#nixos).

title: Latent audio deadlock: unbalanced SDL audio lock on early return
close_reason:
Fixed in 3dae52880. The issue had no description, so recording the defect: S_ClearBuffer (snd_dma.c) and S_Update_ both ran 'qsnd_driver->LockBuffer(); if (!shm->buffer) return;' — returning while still holding the lock. LockBuffer/Submit are a documented pair (snd_sys.h:97-98) and for the SDL driver they are a literal SDL_LockAudioStream / SDL_UnlockAudioStream, so taking that branch leaves the stream locked forever and wedges the audio callback thread.

Latent, as the title said: shm->buffer is currently cleared only in the shutdown paths, which NULL shm as well, so the branch is effectively unreachable today. It is not dead code though — the check exists because a driver may invalidate the buffer under us, and the day one does this becomes a live hang.

Both sites now call Submit() before returning. Checked that this is safe for the ALSA driver as well: S_ALSA_LockBuffer is a no-op and S_ALSA_Submit only touches shm->channels and pcm, never shm->buffer, so calling it on this path cannot fault.

Builds clean (nix build .#nixos).

title: Bicubic lightmap filtering shader (experimental cvar)
description:
WhiteMagicRaven (Discord, 2026-06-17) suggested adding a bicubic filtering path for textures — especially lightmaps — for noticeably smoother results. Cites Sin Reloaded demo as reference for how good it can look.

uHexen2 lightmaps are 16-luxel grid; bilinear exposes the lattice on big flat walls, which is exactly where bicubic shines. Cost is reasonable: classic 4-tap weighted-bilinear (Sigg/Hadwiger) gives a true bicubic for ~4 texture fetches per lightmap sample instead of 1.

Proposed implementation:
- Add BicubicLightmap() helper to world.frag.glsl (and alias/skeletal frags where relevant)
- New cvar r_lightmap_bicubic (archive, default 0) — gate via shader #define permutation so the bilinear path stays branchless
- Most visible at low render scales / low lightmap resolution; subtle at native

Reference engines: Quake2RTX, Ironwail forks, Sin Reloaded — bicubic lightmap sampling is well-trodden territory.
close_reason: Implemented: r_lightmap_bicubic cvar + B-spline 4-tap shader helper in world frags, menu hook (Smooth Lmaps), preset integration (off for Crunchy/Retro/Faithful/Clean, on for Modern/Ultra)

title: Antialiasing 32x causes black screen
description: Reporter: Caco. Setting antialiasing to 32x results in a black screen (no render). 32x MSAA exceeds what most GPUs/drivers support (gl_max_samples), and the window/FBO likely ends up GL_FRAMEBUFFER_INCOMPLETE or the SDL window creation degrades to an unusable state. The menu's VID_MenuAdjustMultisample clamps to gl_max_samples, so 32x was likely reached via console (vid_config_fsaa 32) or a stale config. Need to clamp/validate requested MSAA to gl_max_samples on context creation and fall back gracefully (currently only falls back if window creation fails outright). Related: window MSAA is largely vestigial since the scene FBO force-disables MSAA.
close_reason: Fixed in r26 (c-merge of fix/zroc-fxaa-aa): window MSAA dropped entirely (scene FBO already force-disables MSAA), so 32x can no longer be requested; Antialiasing menu now drives FXAA. Does not address the separate glass bug zroc.
