Mouse hover currently just relocates the selection cursor via M_MouseToMenuItem, so there is no visual difference between 'the keyboard cursor is here' and 'the mouse is over this'. Ironwail highlights the hovered row. M_Print already supports inline charset-bank switches (\\1-\\4) and M_PrintWhite exists, so a highlight needs no new draw primitive — the work is threading a hovered-index alongside the cursor index through each menu's draw function, which currently only tracks the cursor.
close_reason: Implemented 2026-08-20. The bead's premise turned out to understate the problem: SDL_EVENT_MOUSE_MOTION never updated menu_mouse_x/y at all — only the button handler did — so hover did not merely lack a distinct highlight, it did not follow the mouse. Two symptoms fixed: (1) moving the pointer over a row did nothing; (2) the FIRST click on a row activated the previous selection, because input runs before M_Draw so K_MOUSE1 reached M_Keydown as Enter while the cursor was still elsewhere. Motion now feeds menu_mouse_x/y and sets menu_mouse_moved when in a menu. menu_mouse_moved was declared in in_sdl.c and externed in menu.c but read by nothing; it is now the gate inside M_MouseToMenuItem, which returns -1 unless the pointer moved or was clicked this frame — without that, a stationary mouse resting over a row re-pins the cursor every frame and the arrow keys appear dead. Flag consumed at the end of M_Draw, not at the event, since input precedes the draw. Code is in the tree (inside commit 92dd774a3, which a concurrent writer created — every menu.c/in_sdl.c hunk there is this change); clean extraction at ~/hexenwail-p0-sweep/.

title: Master's committed 0.8.0-beta.r12 release notes file is corrupt (sections duplicated)
description: docs/release-notes/0.8.0-beta.r12.md as committed on master (cfe2f92d0 lineage, now aa13afab0's tree) appends verbatim copy of Downloads/gamecode/crash-reporting sections. Discovered resolving add/add conflict during merge commit c476d5ae5 — branch kept published (correct) version, so self-resolves when PR #2 merges. File it in case master releases r13 before that or pattern repeats in r13 notes (check those too). Master-side hygiene, not part of epic uhexen2-vcif.

title: Import mod as .zip (and unwrap single-folder archives)
description: Mods distributed as zips; today importZipFile routes through mapImportedPath (data1-oriented) so mod zips must be hand-extracted and folder-imported. Add mod-zip import path reusing gamedir logic from a926e0053's web/lib/mods.js. Include wrapper-folder UX trap: folder wrapping real mod (Download/mymod/...) makes 'download' the gamedir — auto-unwrap single-child roots.

title: sw.js offline shell precaches almost no lib/ modules — offline boot broken
description: CORE_ASSET_URLS precaches only lib/phone-controls.js; paths.js, zip.js, save-bundle.js, webgl-diagnostics.js, demo-fetch.js, mods.js absent (list keeps growing), so 'offline-capable' shell cannot boot offline. Pre-existing; deliberately not half-fixed during cf1k (a926e0053). Fix: precache full lib/ set; add test asserting app.js imports ⊆ precache list.

title: Launch-time assertion: game canvas box must be inside the visual viewport
description: The webgl-diagnostics black-frame self-test validates presenter offscreen and passed throughout the o6js bug (721c218b2) — it cannot detect 'canvas is fine but off-screen'. A cheap launch-time check (canvas bounding box vs visualViewport) surfaced in runtime log would catch this class of layout bugs in seconds, preventing silent failures.

title: Coarse-pointer layout can still push the game canvas off-screen (iPad-class, phone-mode off)
description: web/index.html's @media (pointer: coarse) ... 820px branch still uses grid-template-rows: auto minmax(18rem,1fr) — the same failure shape 721c218b2 fixed for default layout, on the fork's actual target device class (iPad-class with phone-mode off). Not a regression (unchanged by fix), needs the same definite-height treatment (100dvh + minmax(0,1fr)).

title: Browser fatal error gives desktop-only advice (get_demo.sh / nix run)
description: When the fatal 'Unable to find a proper Hexen II installation' is triggered in the browser (quakefs.c:2129-2139), the error message directs users to run './get_demo.sh' or 'nix run .#get-demo -- /persistent'—desktop-only advice. The code has a PLATFORM_WINDOWS branch but no __EMSCRIPTEN__ fallback. Reproduced by importing registered pak0 without pak1 (GAME_REGISTERED0 set but never promoted at line 2068, falls to else at 2110, fatals). Fix: add __EMSCRIPTEN__ branch in quakefs.c:2129+ pointing users to the PWA launcher's import flow instead.

title: Web canvas not window-bounded outside phone mode
description: web/index.html:37 — 1280x720 browser window yields a 832x2371 drawable. Layout/CSS issue in the launcher page preventing proper canvas sizing.

title: GL_TEXTURE_LOD_BIAS is INVALID_ENUM on WebGL2 — gl_lodbias no-op with GL error spam
description: Probe-confirmed 0x8501→INVALID_ENUM on WebGL2 (anisotropy fine). Called unconditionally at gl_draw.c:577, 2403, 2552. WebGL2 build runtime log shows recurring 'GL error GL_INVALID_ENUM (0x0500) detected at end of frame' — consistent with unconditional GL_TEXTURE_LOD_BIAS calls this bead covers. Confirm attribution when fixing. Pre-existing, newly visible via runtime log from smoke test. Fix: capability-gate it using gl_renderer_caps (available since PR #6 port).

title: Step-8 loose ends: uninspected fork hunks + artifact validation gaps
description: Four items flagged during software renderer port (step 8, commit 8e5f562f6), deferred out of scope: (a) Two fork hunks from 0b1906add never inspected — web/app.js (6 lines) and web/test/phone-controls.test.js (2 lines); launcher side rebuilt from first principles; review those hunks for intentional behavior we might have missed. (b) scripts/wasm-validate-artifact.sh originally required lib/phone-controls.js and lib/webgl-diagnostics.js; now (8f8177223) also requires lib/demo-fetch.js and (a926e0053) lib/mods.js; validate item still incomplete (app.js imports ⊆ precache list test missing per f2zb). (c) CI now runs two full Emscripten builds per PR — watch against 45-min timeout on first cold run. (d) Desktop GLES tier (-DUSE_GLES=ON) has no flake attribute so can't be CI-gated — independent pre-existing gap, document as known limitation. (e) gl_draw.c:91-94 keeps a third private copy of sbar canvas dimensions (SBAR_CANVAS_W/TOP_H/BUMP_H/BOT_H = 320/46/23/98) not covered by new draw.h↔sbar.c assert; add two-line static assert or point it at draw.h constants. (f) scr_sbarscale/scr_menuscale work on webgl2 but inert on software (SCR_CalcUIScale returns 1.0) — placement agrees at scale 1 but configs legitimately differ when user scales; document or unify eventually. (g) qconsole.log lands in MEMFS cwd (LOG_Init runs before FS_Init applies -basedir) — non-durable, deliberately kept (keeps growing log out of 10s IDB sync), not retrievable for bug reports; revisit if testers need logs. (h) Unhandled promise rejection 'Pointer is already locked.' from tryCaptureInput clobbers the status line during software run; pre-existing trap on pointer-lock re-entry. (i) dist-soft/ is untracked and not gitignored (/dist/ is) — one-line .gitignore addition when convenient.

title: Web renderer follow-ups from PR #6 port review
description: Four follow-up items flagged during PR #6 (capability-aware WebGL renderer) port review, deferred out of scope of the initial port. (a) ES fragment shader header uses 'precision mediump float' while upstream fork moved to highp — evaluate visual impact on mobile GPUs; mobile devices may render differently. (b) glUniform3fv_fp is now a dead entry-point load — remove unused function or identify if it should be used. (c) Shader-extractor script parses C string literals with regexes — brittle; breaks loudly if 'static const char x[] = ...' shape changes; consider sturdier extraction (AST-based or manual). (d) SwiftShader leniency means headless WebGL2 CI gate only catches structural regressions, not driver-strictness issues — documented limitation; revisit if real-device reports show divergence between CI and shipping platforms.

title: Phone-mode touch controls: polish + hardware QA
description: Flagged during port review (commit c9f98d0ce) — three items for refinement before shipping to testers. (a) Dead code: PHONE_CONTROL_KEYCODES.run (K_SHIFT) is mapped in BUTTON_ACTIONS but no element has data-phone-action="run"; either add a Run button or drop the mapping. (b) UX: touch-only auto-gate is one-way per session — one trusted keydown/wheel/mouse event hides controls until reload; detaching a Bluetooth keyboard mid-session leaves controls hidden (documented as expected but will read as a bug); workaround is Always Show setting. Consider two-way gate or session-persistence flag. (c) QA: stick feel, look sensitivity, and auto-gate behavior untested on real touch hardware (iPad with trackpad especially); currently only Node DOM stubs cover it. Needs pass on test machine and real devices before testers see it.

title: Save-bundle 'merge' mode won't import new save slots — clarify UX or change semantics
description: As ported from fork (commit 61107b747, test-asserted), merge mode only overwrites bundle paths that already exist on the device. A save slot present in the bundle but absent locally is silently skipped. This means moving a save to a fresh device requires Replace mode, not Merge. Faithful to fork but a user-confusion trap. Decision needed: either the UI copy must spell out merge behavior clearly (only overwrites existing slots) or merge should become a union operation (imports new slots, overwrites existing). Must clarify before shipping to testers.

title: [bug] Mod_LoadAllSkins flood-fills the first skin for every member of a skin group
description:
Spotted while fixing uhexen2-93a8, not fixed there because it is a separate defect with its own blast radius.

engine/h2shared/gl_model.c: Mod_LoadAllSkins sets

    skin = (byte *)(pskintype + 1);

once at function entry and never updates it. The single-skin branch is fine — pskintype still points at that skin when Mod_FloodFillSkin(skin, ...) runs. The ALIAS_SKIN_GROUP branch is not: it walks pskintype forward per group member, but still passes the entry-time 'skin' pointer to Mod_FloodFillSkin on every iteration. So member 0's buffer is flood-filled groupskins times and members 1..n-1 are never flood-filled at all.

Consequence: for an animating skin group, the index-255 alpha-fringe cleanup only ever lands on the first frame's skin. Members 1..n keep raw index-255 texels, so their cutout edges fringe toward the palette's transparent colour under filtering and mip generation — the same class of edge artefact uhexen2-nkj1 chased on the flood in GL_Upload32.

Fix is one line (pass the per-member pointer, matching what GL_LoadTexture two lines below already uses), but it needs a look at which shipped models actually use ALIAS_SKIN_GROUP before it is called verified. Predates Hexenwail; inherited from Hammer of Thyrion.

title: Dedupe web launcher markup between web/index.html and engine/web/shell.html
description: The ported PWA code duplicates substantial HTML/CSS markup between web/index.html (GitHub Pages launcher) and engine/web/shell.html (becomes dist/engine-shell-debug.html). Both define the same outer structure, CSS, event handlers, and initialization logic. Problem: any later launcher-UI edit must be made twice or they drift. Solution: consolidate into a single source of truth. Flagged during port (commits 7dced098c + da77d735f) but left out of initial scope. Definition of done: single source of truth for launcher markup/CSS; both entry points load from it; no duplication.

title: CI test suite: the audit's proposed map-load rung collides with uhexen2-3vmk
description:
Split out of uhexen2-5zei, whose FINDING 8 (lint on tag builds) is fixed in 7e43e8ea0.  This is FINDING 3, which is not a wiring job -- the implementation the audit proposed is barred by a licensing decision already on the books, so it needs a call from the user before any code.

## What 5zei proposed

'Cheapest rung that would have caught a real bug: launch, load a map from the
bundled demo data, quit, assert exit 0 and no Host_Error in qconsole.log.
That alone catches shader link failures, missing assets and startup crashes.'

## Why it cannot be wired as written

The demo data is packages.demodata in flake.nix, and the comment above it
(uhexen2-3vmk, uhexen2-118f) is explicit: 'this output must never be
referenced by release, never appear in a workflow (ci.yml/release.yml build
named packages one by one -- keep it that way, and never add a
build-everything sweep), and never be pushed to the binary cache.'

That is not a stale note.  3vmk found the only licence covering this data is
Activision's retail EULA, which forbids transferring copies, and drew the
line at 'pointing a user at uHexen2 URL is not distribution, serving them
the bytes is.'

AND THE MECHANISM IS LIVE, which is the part worth knowing before anyone
argues the runner is just a user evaluating a fetchurl.  ci.yml build uses
cachix/cachix-action@v17 with an authToken and no pushFilter, so it installs
a post-build hook that pushes EVERY path built in that job to the public
hexenwail.cachix.org.  Building .#demodata in that job would not merely
fetch the data on a runner and discard it -- it would publish Raven bytes to
our binary cache, which is exactly the side of the line 3vmk ruled out.
hydraPlatforms = [] and the unfree licence do not stop cachix.

## And the data-free version of the rung cannot catch what the rung is for

Checked the init order rather than assuming.  host.c loads gfx.wad (1060),
gfx/palette.lmp and gfx/colormap.lmp (1067, 1071, both Sys_Error on miss)
BEFORE VID_Init (1084) and Draw_Init (1085).  So with no data1 the engine
cannot reach GL init at all, and shader link failures -- the headline item
in FINDING 3 justification -- are structurally unreachable without game
data.  A dataless run tests argument parsing and little else.

Note the existing ci.yml Smoke test step (uhexen2-bvei) already covers the
launch/exit-0 sub-rung via -help, which sys_unix.c:578 handles before any
SDL or video init.  It is real, and it is the ceiling of what dataless
buys.

## The three ways forward, for the user to pick

1. AUTHOR OUR OWN MINIMAL data1.  Our palette.lmp and colormap.lmp
   (colormap is derivable from the palette), a small gfx.wad, one .map
   compiled by our own qbsp -- CI already builds .#utils -- and progs.dat
   from .#gamecode, which CI already builds too.  Every byte ours,
   redistributable, cacheable, and it makes the rung permanent rather than
   conditional on somebody licence.  Biggest job of the three and the only
   one that ends the question.

2. RELAX 3vmk FOR CI SPECIFICALLY, with a pushFilter on cachix-action
   excluding hexen2-demodata so the bytes stay on the runner.  Cheapest
   path to a working rung, but it reopens a settled licensing decision and
   the guard would be one YAML line away from silent removal.  Not
   recommended without the user explicitly reversing 3vmk.

3. ACCEPT THE GAP AND WRITE IT DOWN.  Keep the map-load test in the manual
   headless harness (tools/headless-drive.sh), which is where it lives
   today, and record in the CI docs that compiling is deliberately the only
   property CI verifies, because the content needed to verify more cannot
   be redistributed.

Recommendation: (1) if the test suite is wanted at all, (3) otherwise.  (2)
only on an explicit reversal.

Blocked on a user decision, not on engineering.
notes:
Split from uhexen2-5zei, closed 2026-08-19.  5zei's other half (lint on tag builds) shipped in 7e43e8ea0.
HASH CORRECTION 2026-08-19.  The 5zei lint fix is cited above as 7e43e8ea0; that hash was rewritten within minutes of being written down and the survivor is 73a9c74c5, same subject and same three workflow files.  Caught by tools/bd_hash_audit.py (382f6f7af) on its first run -- a fair demonstration of why that tool exists, and why a hash written into a bead in this repo should be treated as perishable.

title: Implement the SDL_GPU backend behind the RHI seam
description:
With pipeline objects, uniform blocks, descriptor-shaped texture binding and offline SPIR-V in place, add the actual SDL_GPU backend as a second implementation behind the same seam. Selected at startup by cvar, falling back to GL.

Scope:
  - Device + swapchain creation (SDL_CreateGPUDevice, SDL_ClaimWindowForGPUDevice). gl_vidsdl.c currently creates an SDL_WINDOW_OPENGL window at gl_vidsdl.c:571/591 and an SDL_GL_CreateContext at :649 -- that becomes a branch.
  - Command buffer + render/copy/compute pass recording.
  - Render passes for the FBO graph gl_postprocess.c already defines: scene FBO, bloom FBOs, OIT accum/revealage, soft-depth capture, native FBO.
  - Pipeline creation from the rpipeline_t descriptions.
  - Buffer upload via transfer buffers, replacing the glBufferStorage / glMapBufferRange persistent-mapped streaming used by GL_Imm.

What SDL_GPU gives us for free, and is the reason this is tractable at all: automatic synchronization and barriers, and no manual GPU memory suballocation. A hand-rolled Vulkan backend would need both -- vkQuake carries gl_heap.c precisely for the latter.

Verified against the vendored oslibs/windows/SDL3/include/SDL3/SDL_gpu.h (SDL 3.2.12) -- everything the current renderer relies on has a mapping:
  glBlendFunci (7 sites, OIT MRT)      -> per-color-target SDL_GPUColorTargetBlendState; independentBlend is a REQUIRED device feature
  glDispatchCompute (7)                -> SDL_BeginGPUComputePass + SDL_DispatchGPUCompute / SDL_DispatchGPUComputeIndirect
  glMultiDrawElementsIndirect (1) / glDrawElementsIndirect (2) -> SDL_DrawGPUIndexedPrimitivesIndirect
  SSBOs / glBindBufferBase (4)         -> SDL_BindGPUVertexStorageBuffers / SDL_BindGPUFragmentStorageBuffers
  MSAA                                 -> SDL_GPU_SAMPLECOUNT_1..8
  glClipControl(ZERO_TO_ONE) (3)       -> native 0..1 depth convention, no equivalent call needed
  glFenceSync (4)                      -> SDL_GPUFence
Baseline is Vulkan 1.0 plus VK_KHR_swapchain, VK_KHR_maintenance1, independentBlend, imageCubeArray, depthClamp, shaderClipDistance, drawIndirectFirstInstance.
design:
Additive only. SDL_GPU has no OpenGL driver (drivers are vulkan / direct3d12 / metal / private), so:
  - The GL 4.3 path stays permanently for older hardware.
  - The Emscripten/WASM build stays GLES/WebGL2 -- SDL 3.2.12 ships no WebGPU backend. Guard the whole backend behind an ifdef so the WASM build never sees it.

Suggested order: Vulkan-only first cut on Linux (fewest moving parts, and the box can build and run headless via SDL offscreen + llvmpipe). Then D3D12 on Windows, which needs SDL_shadercross to translate SPIR-V to DXIL. D3D12 is arguably the higher-value target of the two, since the vendor-specific render bugs that reach us are Windows ones. Metal last.

Verify the Linux/nix SDL3 is >= 3.2 before starting -- the vendored Windows copy is 3.2.12 but the nix-provided one is separate.

RenderDoc works against both backends, so the existing capture-first debugging workflow carries over unchanged.

Done when: cvar-selected SDL_GPU backend renders a map correctly on Vulkan with OIT, sky, liquids, alias models and postprocess intact; GL remains the default; WASM build unaffected.
notes:
NOT STARTED.  Scoping notes from the session that landed .1-.4, so whoever picks this up does not re-derive them.

SDL3 VERSION QUESTION IS ANSWERED.  The bead said 'verify the Linux/nix SDL3 is
>= 3.2 before starting'.  nixpkgs sdl3 is 3.4.10 and ships SDL3/SDL_gpu.h, and
its descriptor-set documentation is identical to the vendored Windows 3.2.12.
Not a blocker.

WHAT IS READY FOR YOU
 - gl_pipeline.c: R_BindPipeline + rpipeline_t exist as the state bundle, and
   every draw goes through R_DrawArrays / R_DrawElements / R_DrawElementsInstanced
   / R_DrawElementsIndirect / R_MultiDrawElementsIndirect.  That is the recording
   seam -- SDL_GPU records draws into a command buffer rather than issuing them,
   and no call site names glDraw* any more.
 - gl_uniforms.c: two std140 blocks, so uniform data is already block-shaped.
   Both are a few hundred bytes, which suits SDL_PushGPUVertexUniformData's
   'small data only' rule; nothing bulk goes through them.
 - gl_texbind.c: R_BindTextures takes a slot range, which is the shape of
   SDL_BindGPUFragmentSamplers.
 - engine/shaders/*.glsl compile to valid SPIR-V with SDL_GPU's set numbering
   (uhexen2-p4ln.4).  Build them with the shaders_spirv target, or run
   tools/glsl_check.py, which also covers both GL dialects and the linked pairs.

WHAT IS NOT, IN THE ORDER IT BITES
 1. gl_postprocess.c and gl_worldcull.c still use DEFAULT-BLOCK UNIFORMS, which
    Vulkan forbids outright.  Neither the post-process chain nor the compute
    culling can produce usable SPIR-V until those become blocks.  This is the
    first thing to fix, and it is an extension of uhexen2-p4ln.2 rather than
    anything new.
 2. Compute shaders use a different set convention from graphics: 0 read-only,
    1 read-write, 2 uniforms.  uniforms.inc only knows the graphics one.
 3. Sampler state is still per-texture glTexParameter, not sampler objects --
    the open half of uhexen2-p4ln.3.  SDL_GPU has no equivalent of mutable
    per-texture sampler state at all, so this one is load-bearing here, unlike
    for the GL path where it is merely tidier.
 4. rpipeline_t exists but NO DRAW SITE BINDS ONE yet.  The state is correct and
    centralised, but it is still applied as individual setters; the bundles that
    a pipeline object would be created from have not been enumerated.  The
    measured permutation count is 30-60 (see the parent bead).

DO NOT expect this to be verifiable by building.  The done-when is 'renders a
map correctly', and every part of that needs a running engine and eyes on the
screen.

READY TO START, as of the p4ln.2/p4ln.4 work on branch bead/p4ln-2-ppblocks.
The four prerequisite refactors have landed far enough that nothing in this
bead is blocked on them any more:

  - EVERY shader in the engine (29: 16 draw, 9 post-process, 4 compute) is a
    file under engine/shaders/ and compiles to SPIR-V.  `make shaders_spirv`
    produces all 29; tools/glsl_check.py checks them.
  - Descriptor annotations are complete and follow SDL_gpu.h: graphics per
    stage (vertex sets 0/1, fragment 2/3) via descriptors.inc, compute per
    access class (0 read-only, 1 read-write, 2 uniforms) via compute.inc.  The
    compute layout was verified by reading it back out of the SPIR-V with
    spirv-cross, not assumed.
  - Every non-opaque uniform is in a std140 block with a C mirror; the only
    glUniform* call left in the engine is glUniform1i binding a sampler.
  - Draw-state changes all go through gl_pipeline.c, and every draw goes
    through the R_Draw* wrappers, so the recording seam exists.

THE ONE PIECE OF p4ln.1 STILL OUTSTANDING: rpipeline_t and R_BindPipeline exist
but no draw site binds a bundle.  Read p4ln.1's notes before assuming that is
trivial -- the depth mask is the one piece of state the scattered clusters
leave implicit, so converting a site means choosing a value that changes what
the NEXT pass inherits.

FIRST CONCRETE STEP when this starts: the .spv rule is deliberately not part of
ALL (a build rule whose output nobody consumes has no business failing the
default build).  It should join ALL in the same commit that first reads the
output.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING: the palette block in the composite shader is 4 KB.
SDL_gpu.h says uniform buffers are for small data and directs anything bulk to
a storage buffer, so PPPalette is the one block that should not be pushed as a
uniform on the SDL_GPU path -- it is already in its own block, kept separate
from PPParams precisely so it can change independently.

title: Second render backend via SDL_GPU (Vulkan / D3D12 / Metal)
description:
Umbrella for adding a second, non-OpenGL render backend using SDL3's SDL_GPU API, which targets Vulkan, D3D12 and Metal behind one interface.

Rationale: SDL3 is already the windowing layer, so this adds no new dependency. SDL_GPU removes the three hardest parts of a hand-rolled Vulkan backend -- GPU memory suballocation, descriptor pool management, and barrier/synchronization (SDL_GPU syncs automatically). D3D12 on Windows comes free, which is arguably worth more than Vulkan given that our Windows-specific render bugs are the ones that reach us via testers.

This is ADDITIVE. SDL_GPU has no OpenGL driver (drivers are vulkan/direct3d12/metal/private), so the GL 4.3 path stays permanently for older hardware, and the Emscripten build stays GLES/WebGL2 -- SDL 3.2.12 has no WebGPU backend.

Feasibility verified against the vendored header oslibs/windows/SDL3/include/SDL3/SDL_gpu.h (SDL 3.2.12):
  - independentBlend is a REQUIRED Vulkan device feature => per-attachment blend is guaranteed, so our 7 glBlendFunci sites (OIT accum/revealage MRT) map directly.
  - Compute shaders + SDL_DispatchGPUComputeIndirect => gl_worldcull.c compute culling survives.
  - SDL_DrawGPUIndexedPrimitivesIndirect => our glMultiDrawElementsIndirect path survives.
  - Storage buffers bind to both vertex and fragment stages => SSBO GPU particles and instanced alias survive.
  - All 4 blend funcs we actually use are in the blend factor enum, DST_COLOR included.
  - MSAA to 8x.
  - Baseline is Vulkan 1.0 + 6 commodity extensions (vs vkQuake's SDK 1.2.162 Linux / 1.4.321 Windows).

Known ceiling: no bindless/descriptor indexing, no mesh shaders, and the SDL_gpu.h FAQ states ray tracing is explicitly not a near-future item. So vkQuake's RT dynamic shadows are not reachable on this path.

Current GL surface (measured): 1667 call sites, 121 distinct entry points, all via the *_fp pointers in engine/h2shared/gl_func.h. 86% of calls live in 7 files: gl_postprocess.c 434, gl_rsurf.c 249, gl_rmain.c 224, gl_worldcull.c 175, gl_shader.c 126, gl_vidsdl.c 122, gl_draw.c 100.
design:
The GL 4.3 migration already did the conceptual work: no fixed function, no matrix stack, no glBegin, and the engine already uses compute dispatch, SSBOs, MDI, glBufferStorage persistent mapping, fences, glClipControl and timer queries. The DATA FLOW is already Vulkan-shaped.

What is NOT Vulkan-shaped is STATE. Scattered across the draw paths: 80 glEnable/glDisable, 46 glDepthMask, 29 glBlendFunc, 9 glPolygonOffset, 70 glUseProgram. GL's set-state-then-draw model has no SDL_GPU/Vulkan equivalent -- those combinations must be frozen into immutable pipeline objects at creation time.

The good news is the real state space is tiny:
  22x glBlendFunc(SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA)
   5x glBlendFunc(ONE, ONE)
   1x glBlendFunc(ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, SRC_ALPHA)
   1x glBlendFunc(DST_COLOR, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA)
plus 6 toggles in real use (BLEND, DEPTH_TEST, CULL_FACE, SAMPLE_ALPHA_TO_COVERAGE, POLYGON_OFFSET_FILL, STENCIL_TEST). That is on the order of 30-60 pipelines, not hundreds.

Sequencing: the four child refactors are all PURE GL changes that ship and are testable with zero SDL_GPU code, and each is a GL win on its own (fewer state and uniform calls per draw). Only the final child introduces a new backend. This keeps the port de-risked and bisectable.

vkQuake (GPL-2.0, same licence as uHexen2) is a reference, but a narrower one on this path than on a hand-rolled Vulkan path: SDL_GPU replaces exactly the device/heap/descriptor plumbing that vkQuake's gl_heap.c and gl_vidsdl.c provide. What remains liftable is its Shaders/ directory -- SPIR-V-ready GLSL with a .inc shared-include pattern, plus bintoc.c for the byte-array embedding -- and its WBOIT/MBOIT resolve shaders for comparison against our existing OIT path. Do NOT copy its renderer architecture: it is QuakeSpasm-era where we have already followed Ironwail.

title: Alias-model caustics/model-matrix resting-state reset skipped when entity has no caustics
description:
## Location
engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c, ~line 1836, inside R_DrawAliasModel per-entity cleanup.

## Issue
Reset of shared gl_shader_alias caustics state is gated behind `if (caustics > 0.0f)`:
- GL_SetAliasCaustics(0,0)
- GL_SetAliasModelMatrix(identity)

Only executes when THIS entity has caustics > 0. If an entity draws WITHOUT caustics, the reset is skipped, leaving stale caustics/model-matrix values from a PREVIOUS entity live in imm_alias_caustics and imm_alias_model shared state.

## Root Cause
gl_shader_alias is also used by water/warp-polys, sprites, and unlit brush-polys (per comments engine/h2shared/gl_shader.h:41-49 and gl_rmain.c:1832-1835). Those downstream call sites never touch this state, so leaving it hot after an alias-model draw leaks the overlay onto them.

## Impact
Latent state-leak: if an entity with caustics>0 draws, then a later entity draws WITHOUT caustics (skipping reset), then water/sprites/unlit-brush-polys draw next, the stale non-zero caustics/model-matrix values cause a visible caustics overlay to bleed onto water, sprites, or unlit surfaces — if frame ordering lines up.

## Fix
Reset GL_SetAliasCaustics(0,0) and GL_SetAliasModelMatrix(identity) unconditionally at end of R_DrawAliasModel, not gated on this entity's own caustics value.

## Discovery Note
Found while investigating water_bug.rdc (black-water capture, filed separately). Did NOT cause that specific bug (caustics uniform was confirmed correctly zeroed in that frame), but is a real latent state-leak.
close_reason: Addressed in 7347d4063, but the reported defect is not real -- correcting the record. The bead claims a live leak: reset gated on caustics > 0.0f, so a no-caustics entity leaves a previous entity's caustics/model-matrix hot for the sprite / warp-poly / unlit-brush-poly draws that share gl_shader_alias. It cannot happen. The SET (gl_rmain.c:1604) is gated on the same expression at the same nesting level as the RESET (was gl_rmain.c:1896), 'caustics' is assigned once from R_CausticsIntensity() at gl_rmain.c:1342 and never reassigned, and there is no return or goto between the two. An entity therefore does both or neither, and one that does neither had nothing to reset. GL_SetAliasCaustics / GL_SetAliasModelMatrix have no other callers in the tree (they only write CPU-side shadows in gl_vbo.c; GL_ImmEnd dirty-compares before uploading). What the bead did surface is that the safety rests on an undocumented invariant -- no early return may sit between set and reset -- and uhexen2-gwtq (096ee3e5d) added an early return to this very function. So the gate on the reset was dropped and the reasoning written into the comment: unconditional costs two stores that GL_ImmEnd then elides, and removes the invariant a future return would have to respect. No behaviour change. nix build .#nixos clean.

title: Android port (SDL3 + GLES3)
description:
Port Hexenwail to Android using SDL3 (which has Android support) and GLES3 renderer. Hardening the WASM port's GLES path is the natural precursor, so complete the WASM productionization work (uhexen2-91t4) before prioritizing this port.

## Scope
- SDL3 + NDK toolchain integration (ideally via nix)
- GLES3 renderer validation (shares ifdef paths with WASM/WebGL2 build)
- APK packaging with game-data import flow (users supply pak files; demo-data fetch as first-run option)
- Touch and gamepad input support
- UI scaling for phone/tablet screens
- CI/build integration for Android target

## Depends on
- uhexen2-91t4 (WASM productionization; GLES path hardening must happen there first)

## Definition of done
APK builds reproducibly via `nix build .#android`; GLES ifdef paths are CI-verified; game-data import flow works; touch input is functional; UI scales for phone screens.

title: Matrix stack overflow/underflow is silent and desyncs push/pop pairing
description:
engine/h2shared/gl_matrix.c:92-124: GL_PushMatrix at max depth (MAT_STACK_DEPTH-1) silently does nothing while the matching GL_PopMatrix still decrements — one saturated push destroys the caller's parent matrix.

Current state: Deepest nesting today is ~3 so it can't fire, but there's no Sys_Error/warning to catch the day it does.

Fixes:
1. Sys_Error (or at minimum a loud warning) on overflow and underflow.
2. Also fold in: gl_matrix.h:33's comment says "modelview * projection" but GL_GetMVP computes projection * modelview (code is right, comment misleads).
close_reason: fixed in c38babe07 (Sys_Error on matrix stack overflow/underflow; GL_GetMVP header comment corrected)

title: gl_waterripple warps with sin(x)*sin(z), degenerate on flat liquid
description:
engine/h2shared/gl_warp.c:253 (EmitWaterPolys): nz += ripple * sin(v[0]*0.05+realtime) * sin(v[2]*0.05+realtime).

On a horizontal liquid plane v[2] is constant, so the ripple collapses to time-pulsed 1-D stripes that periodically flatten.

The classic formula (compare DrawGLWaterPoly, engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c:664-665) uses the two in-plane axes — the second factor should key on v[1].

Fix: Use v[1] instead of v[2] in the second sin() argument.
close_reason: fixed in cc671f490 (water ripple second factor keyed on v[1], matching the classic in-plane formula)

title: GL_ImmEnd overbright upload ignores the r_fullbright gate
description:
engine/h2shared/gl_vbo.c:520-528 uploads ob = gl_overbright ? 2.0 : 1.0, but R_SetupFrame (engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:4333) deliberately gates it: (gl_overbright && !r_fullbright) ? 2.0 : 1.0 (comment there explains surfaces blow out white otherwise).

Symptom: With r_fullbright 1 + gl_overbright 1, the first imm-path world batch after a program switch re-uploads 2.0 — double-bright surfaces.

Fix: Apply the same gate in GL_ImmEnd.
close_reason: fixed in 4cd7f8fa9 (GL_ImmEnd applies the same gl_overbright && !r_fullbright gate as R_SetupFrame)

title: Remove dead GL_LUMINANCE remnants now that the format is retired
description: After b95f8bfed pins gl_lightmap_format to RGBA: the 1-byte lightdata load branch at engine/h2shared/gl_model.c:802 is unreachable, and gl_rmain.c has always-true `gl_lightmap_format == GL_RGBA` tests scattered through the alias paths (e.g. ~1285-1291, ~2728-2737 — the instanced non-RGBA collect branch). Pure cleanup, no behavior change expected.
close_reason: fixed in 7d6e6a5c1 (dead GL_LUMINANCE branches removed from Mod_LoadLighting, Mod_LoadFaces_BSP2/_V29, and five gl_rmain.c sites; the Sys_Error format guard in gl_rsurf.c deliberately kept as the invariant check)

title: Fog_StartAdditiveDouble/Fog_StopAdditiveDouble have zero callers — dead code or missing underwater-fog integration
description:
Found during rendering audit follow-up (2026-08-18): Fog_StartAdditiveDouble (gl_fog.c:352) and Fog_StopAdditiveDouble (gl_fog.c:374) have zero callers. The non-Double variants (Fog_StartAdditive/Fog_StopAdditive) gained callers in commit 5800d6b45, but the Double variants remain uncalled.

Additionally, Fog_StopAdditiveDouble has a declaration-after-statement violation at gl_fog.c:374 (currently compiles under gnu17 but worth fixing if the function is kept).

Decision needed: Determine whether these functions are intended for underwater additive fog integration (and wire them), or delete as dead code.
close_reason: closed in efa35a9e0 (deleted — the pair came from the bulk a14b5eecd import, no prototypes, no callers, no in-flight feature found)

title: [epic] Realtime lighting path (prerequisite for normal-mapped materials)
description:
Deferred out of uhexen2-0vgo by the decision recorded in uhexen2-0vgo.3.

Normal and gloss maps need a light direction to dot the perturbed normal against. Hexen II bakes lighting into the lightmap as intensity per luxel with no direction and no deluxemaps, so there is nothing for a _norm map to work with. FTE makes bumpmapping work by not using the lightmap at all on bumped surfaces and running realtime lights instead.

Scope, if this is ever taken on:
  - extract lights from the BSP entity lump (light, light_fluoro, torches, and the Hexen II specific spawn flags)
  - a light manager with culling and a per-frame active set
  - per-light shadow maps
  - a forward-plus or deferred pass to fold many lights into the existing GL 4.3 world/alias shaders
  - per-vertex tangents for world surfaces and alias models (neither has them today)
  - a compatibility story: this changes how every existing map looks, so it needs to be a toggle with the baked path intact, not a replacement

This is a months-scale project and a look-and-feel decision, not just a rendering one. Do not start it as a side effect of a texture-pack request. Filed so the deferral is recorded rather than forgotten.

Once this exists, reopen uhexen2-0vgo.4 for the _norm/_gloss half of the sidecar convention -- the resolution code already generalises to any suffix.

title: CI has no test suite, and tag builds run no lint
description:
The two CI audit findings that are design calls rather than fixes. Audit: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/21c6234c-df04-4df0-96b3-e34c7253b64a

FINDING 3 — no test suite exists. No add_test, no enable_testing, no tests/ directory. CI builds seven targets (Linux, dedicated, Windows, Windows dedicated, tools, Windows tools, gamecode) and that is the entirety of what is verified. Compiling is the only property under test.

Worth weighing against what this project already does by hand: the engine runs headless under SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen with software GL, loads maps, and writes screenshots — several bugs this month were caught that way. That harness exists and is wired to nothing.

Cheapest rung that would have caught a real bug: launch, load a map from the bundled demo data, quit, assert exit 0 and no Host_Error in qconsole.log. That alone catches shader link failures, missing assets and startup crashes. Note uhexen2-2rxl (square particle mode drawing nothing) would NOT have been caught by that — it needs pixel comparison, which is a further rung.

FINDING 8 — tag builds run no lint. Shellcheck, the structural metainfo validation and the bare-EMSCRIPTEN guard live only in ci.yml's lint job, and ci.yml carries 'tags-ignore: **'. release.yml has none of them. So the lint gate depends entirely on the tagged commit having previously travelled through master — true in practice today, but nothing enforces it, and a tag is the one build that reaches users.

Options: extract lint into a reusable workflow and 'needs:' it from both, or accept the gap deliberately and write down why.
notes: HASH CORRECTION 2026-08-19.  The close reason cites the lint extraction as 7e43e8ea0, rewritten by a rebase in the same session it was written.  Survivor is 73a9c74c5, same subject and the same three files (.github/workflows/lint.yml, ci.yml, release.yml).  uhexen2-eqqn carries the same correction.
close_reason:
FINDING 8 fixed in 7e43e8ea0.  FINDING 3 split out to uhexen2-eqqn, because it turned out not to be a design call this session could make.

FINDING 8 -- TAG BUILDS RUN NO LINT.  Took the first option the bead offered: extracted ci.yml's lint job verbatim into a reusable .github/workflows/lint.yml ('on: workflow_call') and called it from ci.yml and release.yml both.  In release.yml, flatpak and build now 'needs: [lint]', so a red gate costs seconds rather than a full flatpak-builder run, and publish's existing 'needs: [flatpak, build]' makes it transitively impossible for a lint failure to reach a published release.  lint.yml declares 'permissions: contents: read' itself instead of relying on the caller's grant -- a called workflow's token is already capped by the caller, but stating it means a caller that grants more does not hand it to these steps by accident.

Verified with actionlint: clean on ci.yml, release.yml and lint.yml, including the local reusable-workflow reference.  The two SC2016 info notes it reports in security-scan.yml predate this and were left alone.

FINDING 3 -- NO TEST SUITE.  Not implemented, and deliberately not.  The bead's own cheapest rung is 'load a map from the bundled demo data', and that collides head-on with uhexen2-3vmk: the comment over packages.demodata in flake.nix says the output must 'never appear in a workflow ... and never be pushed to the binary cache', because the only licence covering that data is Activision's retail EULA.

The collision is mechanical, not philosophical.  ci.yml's build job runs cachix/cachix-action@v17 with an authToken and NO pushFilter, so it installs a post-build hook that pushes every path built in that job to the public hexenwail.cachix.org.  Building .#demodata there would publish Raven's bytes to our cache, which is precisely the side of the line 3vmk ruled out.  hydraPlatforms = [] and the unfree licence do not stop cachix.

Nor does the dataless variant rescue it.  host.c loads gfx.wad (1060) and gfx/palette.lmp / gfx/colormap.lmp (1067, 1071, both Sys_Error on miss) BEFORE VID_Init (1084) and Draw_Init (1085), so without data1 the engine never reaches GL init and shader link failures -- the headline justification in FINDING 3 -- are structurally unreachable.  The existing '-help' smoke test (uhexen2-bvei) is already the ceiling of what a dataless run buys, since sys_unix.c:578 handles -help before any SDL or video init.

uhexen2-eqqn carries the three ways forward (author our own minimal data1; relax 3vmk with a cachix pushFilter; or accept and document the gap) with a recommendation.  It is blocked on a licensing call that is the user's, not this session's.

title: Compressed texture format support (DDS/KTX + BC) for HD pack VRAM and load time
description:
Nothing in engine/h2shared/ handles DDS, KTX or any block-compressed format — grep for dds/ktx/glCompressedTex returns no hits. Every external replacement is decoded to full 32-bit RGBA by stb_image and uploaded uncompressed.

That is fine for a handful of textures and bad for a real HD pack. A 2048x2048 RGBA texture is 16 MB before mipmaps, ~21 MB with. An episode's worth of those exhausts VRAM on modest cards and makes map load times painful, since every PNG is also being decompressed on the CPU at load.

Two separable pieces:
  1. Accept pre-compressed DDS/KTX containers and hand the blocks straight to glCompressedTexImage2D. Best case — no CPU decode, small on disk, small in VRAM, mips already present.
  2. Optionally compress at upload time for PNG/TGA inputs, so existing packs benefit without being repackaged.

Related: uhexen2-r7zu (port Ironwail 1011ff8/74d8e74, TEXPREF_UNCOMPRESSED for alpha-tested and 2D textures) covers the flag plumbing for opting *out* of compression where it hurts quality — conchars, HUD, alpha-tested fences. Land that first or alongside; the two touch the same texmgr paths.

Done when: a DDS/KTX replacement loads and renders, VRAM use for a large pack is measurably lower than the RGBA path, and 2D/alpha-tested textures are excluded from compression.
close_reason: Implemented on master 74e8eccde. New engine/h2shared/img_dds.c parses DDS (DXT1/3/5, ATI1/ATI2, DX10-header BC1-BC5/BC7) and KTX 1.1; GL_UploadCompressed in gl_draw.c uploads the block payload per level via glCompressedTexImage2D, honouring gl_picmip and gl_max_size by starting further down the file's mip chain and setting GL_TEXTURE_MAX_LEVEL from what was uploaded. Cube maps, volumes, arrays, uncompressed payloads and containers with no level small enough to upload are rejected so the caller falls through to the decoded image. Format availability is probed in GL_Init (gl_have_s3tc/rgtc/bptc). 2D and particle assets stay on the decoded-only path, which is the exclusion uhexen2-r7zu is about. Runtime compression of PNG/TGA input was not done -- packs ship DDS or they do not.

title: Sidecar material map convention (_norm / _gloss / _luma) and texmgr plumbing
description:
There is no material system: no way for a pack to declare that a surface is specular, or to attach a normal map to it. FTE uses Quake3-style .shader/.mat scripts; jsHexen2 leans on filename suffix conventions. Suffixes are the cheaper and more idiomatic fit here — they need no parser, no new file format, and no per-surface state machine.

Convention to adopt (matches what existing FTE/jsHexen2 packs already ship):
  <name>.<ext>        albedo        (already works)
  <name>_luma.<ext>   fullbright    (uhexen2-0vgo.1 — alias of _glow)
  <name>_norm.<ext>   tangent-space normal map
  <name>_gloss.<ext>  specular/gloss

Work: extend IMG_LoadExternalTexture (or add a sibling that takes a suffix) to resolve companions; add texture slots alongside gl_texturenum / gl_fb_texturenum in texture_t and aliashdr_t; bind the extra samplers in the world and alias shaders (engine/h2shared/gl_shader.c, sworld_frag / salias_frag — shaders are inline C strings there); guard everything so a pack that ships only albedo takes the current code path with no extra binds.

Scope depends on uhexen2-0vgo.3. If that decision lands on option C, this issue reduces to _luma only and the _norm/_gloss slots are not worth adding. Do not start the normal-map half before that is settled.

Tangent basis: alias models and world surfaces both need per-vertex tangents to use a tangent-space normal map. Neither currently has them. Budget for generating tangents at load time — this is a real chunk of the work and is easy to underestimate.

Done when: the chosen subset of suffixes loads, renders, and costs nothing measurable for packs that do not ship the sidecars.
notes:
Landed as the _luma/_glow half only, per the decision in uhexen2-0vgo.3 (option C). The _norm and _gloss slots, the extra sampler binds and the per-vertex tangent generation were deliberately NOT implemented -- there is no lighting to consume them until uhexen2-abwd exists.

What shipped: IMG_LoadReplacementGlow in engine/h2shared/img_load.c resolves <name>_glow then <name>_luma through the same search path as the albedo, so FTE and jsHexen2 packs work unmodified. It is a thin wrapper over IMG_LoadReplacement with a suffixed name, so adding _norm/_gloss later is a few lines on this side; the work is all on the rendering side.
close_reason: Landed on master 74e8eccde as the _luma/_glow half only, which is the full scope under decision uhexen2-0vgo.3 (option C). _norm/_gloss slots, sampler binds and tangent generation deliberately not implemented -- nothing would light them until uhexen2-abwd exists. Reopen for that half if it ever does.

title: [decision] Choose the lighting path for normal-mapped materials
description:
This is the decision that gates whether FTE-style materials are worth building at all. Resolve it before writing any normal-map rendering code.

The problem: Hexen II lighting is baked lightmaps. The BSP stores light *intensity* per luxel and no direction. A normal map needs a light vector to dot the perturbed normal against, and there is none. There are no deluxemaps in the format. FTE sidesteps this entirely by not using the lightmap for bumped surfaces — it runs realtime lights (rtlights + shadowmaps) instead.

Options:

A. Realtime lighting path (rtlight-equivalent). Correct, matches FTE, enables shadows and coloured light as a side effect. Large: light extraction from the BSP entity lump, a light manager, per-light shadow maps, a forward-plus or deferred pass, and a whole new performance profile. Months, not weeks, and it changes how every map looks — a compatibility question as much as a rendering one.

B. Fixed key-direction specular. Pick a per-map (or per-surface-normal-hemisphere) key light direction, keep the baked lightmap for diffuse, use the normal map only to modulate a specular highlight. Roughly a week. Looks good on floors, metal and water; looks wrong wherever the real light is not where the key direction says it is. Cheap and reversible.

C. Ship luma/glow sidecars only (see uhexen2-0vgo.1) and no normal mapping. Zero lighting risk, delivers most of the visible 'HD pack' win, honest about what it is.

Recommendation: C now, B behind a default-off cvar if there is appetite, A only as its own tracked project with buy-in — not as an implied part of 'HD texture support'.

Done when: the option is chosen and recorded here, and uhexen2-0vgo.4's scope is narrowed or widened to match.
design:
DECIDED: option C -- glow/luma sidecars only, no normal mapping for now.

Rationale. Options B and A both spend real effort to produce lighting that is either wrong (B) or a different game (A):

- A (realtime lighting / rtlight equivalent) is the only correct answer and is months of work: BSP entity-lump light extraction, a light manager, per-light shadow maps, a forward-plus or deferred pass, and an entirely new performance profile. It also changes how every existing map looks, which makes it a compatibility decision as much as a rendering one. That deserves its own project with explicit buy-in, not to be smuggled in under 'HD texture support'.

- B (fixed key-direction specular) is about a week and looks good on floors, metal and water. But it is wrong wherever the real light is not where the key direction says it is, and Hexen II maps are lit from every direction. Shipping a lighting model that is visibly wrong half the time to support a feature nobody has content for yet is a bad trade.

- C delivers the part of the request that actually has content behind it. Existing FTE and jsHexen2 packs ship _luma/_glow maps; almost none ship _norm/_gloss for Hexen II, because no Hexen II engine consumed them.

Consequence for uhexen2-0vgo.4: scope reduced to the _luma/_glow half. The _norm and _gloss texture slots, the extra sampler binds, and the per-vertex tangent generation are NOT implemented -- adding them now would be dead weight with no lighting to consume them.

This is a reversible call. If A is ever taken on, reopen .4 for the _norm/_gloss half; the sidecar resolution in img_load.c already generalises to any suffix (IMG_LoadReplacementGlow is a thin wrapper over IMG_LoadReplacement with a suffixed name).
close_reason: Decided: option C (sidecar glow only, no normal mapping). Full rationale in the design field. The deferred realtime-lighting work is filed as uhexen2-abwd.

title: Per-map external texture override path (textures/<mapname>/<texname>)
description:
IMG_LoadExternalTexture (engine/h2shared/img_load.c:386) resolves world textures from a single flat namespace: textures/<texname>.{png,tga,pcx}. Two maps that both use 'wall01' must therefore agree on what it looks like, so per-map art packs cannot exist without renaming textures in the BSP.

QuakeSpasm and FTE both search a per-map directory first. Match that: for world textures, try

  textures/<mapname>/<texname>.{png,tga,pcx}   (mapname = loadmodel basename, no path/extension)

before falling back to the existing textures/<texname>.* lookup. Only the world-texture branch (img_load.c:503-541) needs this; models/, gfx/ and particles/ keep their current direct paths.

The map name is not currently threaded into IMG_LoadExternalTexture — it takes only the texture name. Either pass it as a new argument from Mod_LoadTextures (gl_model.c:539, which has loadmodel) or stash it in a file-scope string at map load. Prefer the explicit argument.

Done when: textures/<mapname>/wall01.png wins over textures/wall01.png for that map only, and a map with no per-map directory loads exactly as it does now.
close_reason: Fixed on master 74e8eccde. IMG_BuildCandidates in img_load.c emits textures/<mapname>/<texname> ahead of textures/<texname> for world textures; the map name is derived from loadmodel->name, passed explicitly from Mod_LoadTextures. models/, gfx/ and particles/ keep their direct paths. Per-map beats format, so a per-map PNG wins over a shared DDS.

title: [epic] HD texture and material support (jsHexen2/FTEQW parity)
description:
Garrett (Monolyth-42) asked on Discord 2026-08-17 whether Hexenwail can support HD textures and materials, similar to jsHexen2 or FTEQW.

Audit result: the HD *texture* half largely already ships. engine/h2shared/img_load.c loads PNG/TGA/PCX replacements via stb_image, wired into four paths:
  - world BSP textures   textures/<texname>.{png,tga,pcx}   gl_model.c:539
  - alias model skins    models/<model>_<n>.{png,...}       gl_model.c:2570, :2631
  - HUD / menu pics      gfx/<name>.{png,...}               gl_draw.c:219, :317
  - particles            particles/<name>.{png,...}         gl_rmisc.c:149
Skyboxes have a separate loader in gl_sky.c:586. Fence ({name) and liquid (*name -> #name) names are already sanitised; replacements get TEX_MIPMAP|TEX_RGBA.

The *material* half does not exist at all: no material/shader script system, no normal/gloss/specular maps, no external luma override, and — structurally — no light direction to feed a normal map, because Hexen II lighting is baked lightmaps with no deluxemaps. FTE makes bumpmapping work by running realtime lights instead.

This epic tracks the gap. Children are ordered cheapest-first; the realtime-lighting decision is the one that gates everything visually interesting.
close_reason: All five children closed on master 74e8eccde. Texture side is done: per-map override dirs, DDS/KTX block-compressed sources, and glow/luma sidecars so replacements keep their fullbright layer. Material side is deliberately not done -- decision uhexen2-0vgo.3 chose option C, and the realtime lighting that normal maps would need is filed separately as uhexen2-abwd. Documented for pack authors in USAGE.md.

title: Gamecode source row is hidden on bundle-less builds, stranding players with a loose Hexenwail progs.dat
description:
## Problem
M_Game_IsSkip() in engine/hexen2/menu.c hides the entire GAME_GAMECODE row when PR_GamecodeAvailable() returns false. This gate now over-hides as of b85802d45 (which added a pak-only state).

Specifically, PR_GamecodeAvailable() is false when:
- No bundle shipped with the build
- The install is not GAME_REGISTERED  
- -vanillaprogs was passed

On a bundle-less build, a player with a stale hand-copied Hexenwail progs.dat in their data1/ has a genuine choice to make between "Loose" (data1/) and "Pak" (from pak files), but gets no control at all — the entire row is hidden.

## Mitigation (incomplete)
The player does receive the uhexen2-bflw warning (added in b85802d45) naming the offending file, so they are not left completely in the dark. But their only remedy is to manually delete the file — they have no in-game toggle.

## Candidate Fixes
(a) Show the GAME_GAMECODE row while the "Bundled" state is inert (not clickable), offering control over the real choices  
(b) Teach the row's rotation logic to skip inert states, so it cycles only the options available on this install

Note: -vanillaprogs should probably keep hiding the row outright, since it is an explicit command-line override of the whole mechanism.

## References
- b85802d45 — commit that added pak-only state (sv_gamecode = 2)
- uhexen2-nt96 — undated ident readability fix (closed by b85802d45)
- uhexen2-bflw — mismatch warning (closed by b85802d45)
- uhexen2-8r3e — related gamecode issue

## Metadata
Field report 2026-08-16, 0.8.0-beta.r4, reported by Josh
notes:
FIXED 49fb3bd84. Took candidate (b) from the description -- rotate only through
reachable states -- rather than (a), the inert-but-visible 'Bundled'. An inert
step is what PR_GamecodeAvailable was written to prevent (uhexen2-vbnx), so
adding one back to fix a different bug would have traded one wrong row for
another.

THREE SITES, not one. The description names M_Game_IsSkip; fixing only that
would have left two live defects behind the newly-visible row:

  1. M_Game_IsSkip (engine/hexen2/menu.c) -- gate on
     PR_GamecodeAvailable() || PR_GamecodePakOnlyAvailable().
  2. M_Game_AdjustSliders GAME_GAMECODE -- the old rotation hardcoded '2
     states, 3 if pak-only', which was only ever correct because the old gate
     guaranteed state 1 was reachable. On the bundle-less installs the row now
     appears on, it would have rotated INTO state 1, which cannot load. Now
     builds the reachable set and rotates through that.
  3. M_Game_Draw -- an archived sv_gamecode=1 carried from a bundled build
     drew 'Bundled' on a build shipping no bundle. Confirmed unreachable:
     PR_BundledProgsPath gates on the same three conditions
     PR_GamecodeAvailable tests (-vanillaprogs, GAME_REGISTERED,
     PR_FindBundleDir), so with it false the install's own file loads. The row
     was naming a load that cannot happen. Folding in the rotation alone would
     not have fixed it -- the row must read correctly before it is touched.

Rotation and draw both mirror PR_GamecodeWanted's 'any nonzero non-2 means
state 1' so they agree on a hand-edited cvar.

-vanillaprogs still hides the row, as the description asked: both predicates
test it themselves.

VERIFICATION. Logic extracted into a standalone harness and run over all four
install shapes (bundle x loose-shadows-pak) x start values 0-3 x both
directions. Row hides only for (no bundle, no shadowing); no cycle reaches an
unavailable state; every press moves the label. Both MIDI tiers build clean.

NOT DONE: not exercised in the running menu. The verified part is the state
machine, not the drawing -- worth a look on a real bundle-less build, which is
the configuration this bead is about and the one nix build does not produce.
close_reason: Closed

title: Snow proximity gate ignores volume size, so map-scale snow brushes never spawn
description:
CL_UpdateEffects gates CE_SNOW on 'distance < 1024' measured from the camera to the CENTRE of the snow brush, with no regard for how large the brush is. Stock Raven code, byte-identical in Hammer of Thyrion and Shanjaq's fork, so this is inherited rather than introduced — but it interacts badly with modern map authoring.

Mods that build one map-scale snow volume in TrenchBroom instead of Raven's many small ones get almost no snow, because most of the volume's own footprint lies outside its own cutoff.

Measured on SoT (volumes up to ~2200x2400 units): at EVERY info_player_start in both snow maps, zero volumes pass the gate.
- winter from keep (-3120,664): nearest centre 1375
- winter from palace (14,1144): nearest centre 1078
- tibet from arena (3879,1919): nearest centre 1751

So 'no snow on arrival' is the correct stock behaviour on those maps, and snow only appears in patches near volume centres.

Possible fix: scale the cutoff by the volume's own horizontal half-extent, e.g. spawn when distance < 1024 + max(halfwidth, halfdepth), or test against the nearest point on the box instead of its centre. Either keeps Raven's maps behaving as before while letting large authored volumes work.

Found while triaging uhexen2-2rxl, which turned out to be a different bug (gl_particles square mode). Verified via headless h2ded savegame effect dumps — no rendering involved.
notes:
MAPPER REQUIREMENT (Mathuzzz, 2026-08-16): 'the most comfortable way is simply using one brush...or as few brushes as possible...and the particles would be producing constantly, even if the player stands in the far corner of the brush. That way, the density could also be lower.' He also asks what it would cost in performance.

That confirms nearest-point gating is the right fix, and it is affordable. Measured on SoT winter (15 volumes, counts 4-50, 0.1s interval, 7s flake life, 32768 pool):

- Remove the gate entirely: 596 flakes/0.1s = 5960/s x 7s = 41,720 live particles = 127% of the pool. OVERFLOWS. AllocParticle then returns NULL, which silently starves EVERY particle effect in the game (blood, sparks, spell impacts), not just snow. So 'always on everywhere' is not viable as-is.
- Gate on distance to the NEAREST POINT of the box instead of its centre: 2-5 volumes live depending on where you stand, worst case 17,500 particles = 53% of the pool. Fits, and gives exactly the 'stand anywhere in the brush and it snows' behaviour asked for.

So the fix is a one-line change of the distance metric, not a removal of the budget. Raven's 1024 was a particle-budget mechanism; keeping it but measuring to the box surface preserves the intent while fixing the authoring model. Mathuzzz's instinct that density could drop is the right lever if a map wants more simultaneous volumes.

Related limit worth surfacing to mappers: CE_SNOW count goes over the wire as MSG_WriteByte (sv_effect.c:249), so a per-tick count saturates and WRAPS above 255. CE_RAIN uses MSG_WriteShort and has no practical cap.
close_reason:
Fixed in 00c87edf8. CL_UpdateEffects now measures the snow gate to the nearest point on the volume's XY footprint (zero while inside it) instead of to its centre, keeping the 1024 budget and the height-agnostic behaviour. Comparison is squared, so a sqrt drops off a per-effect-per-frame path.

Verified against SoT via h2ded effect dumps — volume boxes read from the real savegame table, gate recomputed at every info_player_start:
  winter 'keep'   (-3120,664): 0 -> 3 volumes  [10.5k particles, 32% of pool]
  winter 'palace' (14,1144):   0 -> 5 volumes  [15.4k, 47%]
  tibet  'arena'  (3879,1919): 0 -> 1 volume   [3.5k, 11%]

Grid sweep for the worst standing position anywhere on each map: winter 28k (85% of the 32768 pool), tibet 16.1k (49%). No overflow; unconditional spawning would have wanted 41.7k. Headroom is fine for gameplay particles because cl_tent.c spawns those during CL_ParseServerMessage, which runs before CL_UpdateEffects in the same frame, and a hit is only 20-30 particles.

NOT visually verified — no rendered frame was taken. Behaviour confirmed arithmetically against real map data only.

title: Runtime round-trip test for the savegame artifact field
description:
uhexen2-1knr (08a65a99e) persists the selected artifact id as a trailing line in info.dat. It was verified by build and by inspection -- ordering of the writers, the single producer of savedata_t, and every other info.dat reader -- but never exercised on a live engine.

What to run, via tools/headless-drive.sh (Xvfb + xdotool, real X key events) against the retail tree at /home/josh/hexen2:

1. Start a map, acquire two or more artifacts, select a non-torch one, save. Assert the last line of <userdir>/s0/info.dat is that artifact id (0-14), not -1.
2. Quit the engine entirely, relaunch, load that save. Assert the same artifact is selected -- this is case 1 from the bug, the one the static alone could never fix.
3. Load a save written BEFORE the field existed (truncate the trailing line from a copy) while a session already has a different artifact selected. Assert the running selection is kept, not reset to the torch: fscanf hits EOF, tempi stays -1, SB_SetSelectedArtifact no-ops.
4. Backward compat: hand a new-format info.dat to a pre-08a65a99e build and assert it still loads.
5. Protocol 21 (PROTOCOL_UH2_114): assert -1 is written rather than an ex_inventory item id, which is a different id space.

Not urgent -- the failure mode is a wrong icon, not a corrupt save, and the format is additive-at-EOF in both directions.
notes: HASH CORRECTION 2026-08-19.  This bead cites uhexen2-1knr as 08a65a99e; that hash is not in master.  An interactive rebase rewrote it and the survivor is ddb1da768, same subject ('carry the selected artifact through a savegame'), same source files, plus the 0.8.0-beta.r2 version bump in quakedef.h which the rebase squashed in.  The five-step runtime plan below is unaffected -- only the hash changes.

title: SF_FindSoundFont offers .sf3 to libTiMidity, which plays Vorbis samples as raw PCM
description:
SF_FindSoundFont (engine/h2shared/soundfont.c:71-137) advertises soundfont.sf3
in four of its probe slots -- next to the executable, and <basedir>/ and
<basedir>/data1/ -- and snd_soundfont is a free-form user cvar on top of that.
Whatever it returns is handed to the synth with no format check.

On builds whose MIDI tier 1 is midi_nul.c, that synth is the vendored
libTiMidity (engine/CMakeLists.txt:595, snd_timidity.c:129 -> mid_set_soundfont).
libTiMidity cannot decode SF3:

  * its SoundFont support is Takashi Iwai's 1997 SBK/SF2 extension
    (libs/timidity/README.sf)
  * sndfont.c:295-330 load_from_file() fseeks to the sample offset and freads
    the bytes directly into sample->data, byteswapping them as sint16 under
    WORDS_BIGENDIAN -- raw 16-bit LE PCM, no decoder of any kind
  * nothing in libs/timidity mentions vorbis or ogg
  * sndfont.c:591 checks only `sampletype & 0x8000` (ROM); SF3 flags a
    Vorbis sample with bit 0x10, which that test does not catch

An SF3 file is a structurally valid RIFF/sfbk, so readsbk.c parses it without
complaint and playback proceeds. The result is not a clean failure with a
fallback -- it is Ogg Vorbis bitstream bytes played as PCM, i.e. loud noise.

WHO IS AFFECTED
Only libTiMidity-tier builds: the WASM/browser target, and any desktop build
configured without FluidSynth. FluidSynth builds are fine -- FluidSynth reads
SF3 properly via libsndfile, and where FluidSynth exists libTiMidity is not
compiled at all.

SUGGESTED FIX
Either drop the .sf3 probe names on the libTiMidity tier, or sniff the file
before accepting it (an SF3's ifil version minor is 3, and its shdr sampletype
carries 0x10). The cvar path needs the same treatment as the probe path, since
a player can name an .sf3 explicitly.

WORTH NOTING: uhexen2-kayb's closing analysis identifies this same function as
the right place to constrain what the engine will feed a parser -- the security
argument there (untrusted soundfont reaching a CVE-carrying parser) and the
correctness argument here want the same change.
notes:
FIXED c7cf3f493.

SF_IsCompressed() (engine/h2shared/soundfont.c) sniffs the RIFF/sfbk container
for either marker; SF_FindSoundFont() now takes allow_compressed, false from
snd_timidity.c and true from midi_fluid.c. A rejected candidate does not abort
the search -- it is skipped and the search continues, so an SF3 sitting in an
earlier probe slot no longer shadows a playable SF2 later in the order. The
TIMIDITY_SOUNDFONT env override is gated too, not just the cvar and probes.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION: it says 'an SF3's ifil version minor is
3'. That is wrong, and a sniff written from it would have matched no real SF3.
Measured on actual files:

    FluidR3_GM2-2.sf2          ifil = 2.2   (major 2, minor 2)
    VintageDreamsWaves-v2.sf3  ifil = 3.0   (major 3, minor 0)

The discriminator is the MAJOR field >= 3. The shdr sampletype 0x10 test the
bead also names is correct and is implemented as a second, independent marker.

VERIFICATION. Sniffer extracted verbatim into a standalone harness and run
against real files: the genuine .sf3 is caught, FluidR3 (1400+ samples) is not
a false positive. The 0x10 path was proven independently by forging the .sf3's
version stamp back to 2.1 -- still caught, so neither marker is load-bearing
alone. Termination checked against truncations at 10 lengths, a zero RIFF
size, a non-sfbk RIFF, and a file declaring 0xffffffff chunk sizes over 4 KB of
random bytes: no hang, no wild seek, 0.001s for the whole set. Chunk sizes are
clamped to the bytes the parent actually has left, so the unsigned arithmetic
cannot underflow. Both MIDI tiers build warning-free (nix build .#nixos, and
cmake -DUSE_FLUIDSYNTH=OFF for the libTiMidity arm that carries the bug).

NOT DONE: no runtime playback test. The logic is unit-tested but nothing here
has run the engine with an SF3 and listened. Cheap to do on the WASM target
when uhexen2-g3j9 lands a soundfont in the virtual FS.
close_reason: Closed

title: Selected artifact is not carried through a savegame
description:
9b4e7f450 made the inventory selection survive a level change by keeping the artifact id in a static (sb_sticky_artifact) outside the cl struct that CL_ClearState wipes. That covers 'load' within one engine run as a side effect, but the savegame itself records nothing, so two cases still reset to the torch or pick the wrong artifact:

  1. Quit the engine, relaunch, load a save -- the static is back at -1, so the re-find in SB_InvChanged misses and the clamp selects slot 0 (torch).
  2. Load an older save mid-session -- the static holds whatever the *current* playthrough had selected, not what was selected when that save was written.

Fix: persist the selected artifact id in the savegame and seed the static from it on load. It must stay save-compatible in both directions (the Discord request was explicitly 'without breaking everyone's saves'), so append it as one extra trailing line in info.dat rather than bumping SAVEGAME_VERSION: an older engine stops reading after info_mask2 and ignores it, and a pre-existing save just hits EOF where the new field would be.

Requested on Discord by Mathuzzz ('Also on reloading'), following up on uhexen2-1id8.
notes:
Verified end-to-end headless on this box against HEAD's bundled build (nix store 30skgcw9...-hexenwail-bundled-0.8.0-beta.r2), sandboxed HOME via bwrap, SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen.

Setup (demo1, crusader): impulse 43 grants all 15 artifacts; SB_InvChanged commits slot 0, so the saved player entity holds inventory=1 (torch). 10x invright moves the live selection to slot 9 (haste), then 'save s0' fires before the 4s inventory-bar timeout, so Inv_Update never commits it -- the entity data in the save still says torch. That makes the entity a control: anything that restores haste on load can only have come from info.dat.

  1. Writer: s0/info.dat is 30 lines, last line '9' (haste). s0/demo1.gip has "inventory" "1.000000".
  2. Restore, fresh process (static back at -1): load s0 -> player edict inventory 10.0 (haste id 9 + 1).
  3. Backward compat: same save with the trailing line stripped (29 lines, pre-change format) -> loads clean, no error, inventory 1.0 (torch fallback).
  4. Forward compat: engine built at 409b9dfb4^ (9a31f8bf8) loading the 30-line save -> loads clean, no version error, ignores the extra line, inventory 1.0.

Builds green at HEAD for .#nixos, .#nixos-bundled and .#h2ded.
close_reason: Implemented in 409b9dfb4, deduplicated in a7f80dd46; verified headless in both compat directions (see notes).

title: Gamecode ident: retail 1.03/1.09 progs misreport as Third-party
description:
PR_ClassifyGamecode() (engine/h2shared/pr_edict.c) identifies Raven's gamecode from a table of three whole-file CRCs read off a retail 1.11/1.12a install: 17499 (data1/PROGS.DAT), 20799 (portals/progs.dat), 33075 (data1/PROGS2.DAT).

Those are the only retail images anyone here has measured. A player on an older Raven release -- 1.03, or the 1.09 whose progdefs CRC is aliased to 1.11's in engine/hexen2/progdefs.h -- has a whole-file CRC not in the table and no HexenwailGamecode marker, so the startup line and the Game Options footer both call their retail gamecode 'Third-party'.

Not a regression and not harmful, but it is the one wrong answer the classifier can give. Note the progdefs switch already handles PROGS_V103_CRC and returns 'Raven 1.03' if the whole-file CRC ever matches, so the fix is purely to obtain the missing numbers -- run a 1.03 install and read the 'file crc' off the Gamecode: line, then add it to retail_crcs[].

Alternative if the numbers cannot be obtained: treat 'progdefs CRC is a known Raven generation AND no Hexenwail marker AND not a known mod' as weak evidence of retail. Rejected for now because mods share those progdefs CRCs (karma2 22850 and GameOfTomes 41534 both do), so it would misfile mods as Raven -- a worse error than the current one.
notes:
INVESTIGATED 2026-08-15. Not fixable here: no 1.03 or 1.09 image exists on this
box, and retail progs.dat is unfree, so the missing numbers cannot be measured.
What was done instead is to make the measurement trivial for whoever does have
one, and to put hard numbers behind the alternative this bead already rejected.

TOOL: tools/progs_crc.py (7e41d0a19)
Reads both identifying CRCs straight out of a progs.dat -- no install, no
running engine. The bead's stated fix was "run a 1.03 install and read the
'file crc' off the Gamecode: line"; that is now "send us the file, or run one
script on it". tools/ is outside filteredSrc, so it does not touch the engine
derivation hash. Verified against the known figures: it reproduces 17499 /
20799 / 33075 and the four mod CRCs from docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md exactly,
which is the check that it implements the same CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE as
common/crc.c (CRC_XOR_VALUE 0x0000, not Quake's 0xffff).

MEASURED, every progs.dat on this box:

    data1/PROGS.DAT     file 17499   progdefs 38488  (PROGS_V111_CRC)
    data1/PROGS2.DAT    file 33075   progdefs 38488  (PROGS_V111_CRC)
    portals/progs.dat   file 20799   progdefs 26905  (PROGS_V112_CRC)
    GameOfTomes         file 41534   progdefs 38488  (PROGS_V111_CRC)
    karma2              file 22850   progdefs 26905  (PROGS_V112_CRC)
    soc                 file 58269   progdefs 26905  (PROGS_V112_CRC)
    sot                 file 28154   progdefs 26905  (PROGS_V112_CRC)

THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE IS CORRECTLY REJECTED -- now with numbers.
The bead said mods share progdefs CRCs with retail. They share them EXACTLY:
GameOfTomes has retail data1's 38488, and karma2/soc/sot all have retail
portals' 26905. "Known Raven progdefs AND no Hexenwail marker AND not a known
mod" would have misfiled 4 of 4 mods in the corpus as Raven. Do not revisit
this in its general form.

A NARROWER VARIANT THAT IS NOT RULED OUT, if the numbers never turn up:
gate on PROGS_V103_CRC (14046) alone rather than on any known Raven generation.
The collision evidence above is entirely in the V111 (38488) and V112 (26905)
generations -- nothing in the corpus uses 14046, because 1.03 predates the mod
scene that standardised on 1.11+. So "progdefs == PROGS_V103_CRC && no marker
-> Raven 1.03" carries a much smaller risk than the general rule.
It is still a trade, not a win: a hypothetical 1.03-era mod currently reports
"Third-party", which is RIGHT, and would start reporting "Raven 1.03", which is
wrong. Prefer the real CRC. Take this only if 1.03 images stay unobtainable and
someone actually reports the misidentification.

BLOCKED ON: acquiring a retail 1.03 or 1.09 progs.dat. That is data
acquisition, not engineering -- ask a tester with an old CD. The moment one
exists, run tools/progs_crc.py on it and add the file crc to retail_crcs[];
the PROGS_V103_CRC arm of the switch in PR_ClassifyGamecode already returns
"Raven 1.03" and needs no change.
HASH CORRECTION 2026-08-19.  tools/progs_crc.py is cited as 7e41d0a19, which is not in master.  Survivor is 416356a56, same subject and the same two files (tools/progs_crc.py, tools/README.md).  The tool and the instructions for using it are unchanged.

title: Item spawns on a func_door (Mathuzzz) — needs map/item to reproduce
description:
Reported on Discord by Mathuzzz (2026-08-15): 'It spawns on func_door. The very same situation as my green key.'

STATUS: NOT ACTIONABLE YET -- filed so it is not lost.

WHAT IS MISSING
The message is a reply to a screenshot and never names the map or the item, so
'it' is unresolved. Mathuzzz also refers to an earlier green-key report as the
same situation, which is not in beads either. Need from the reporter:
  * map name
  * which item/key
  * whether the item ends up unreachable, floating, or riding the door

LIKELY AREA (unverified guess, do not treat as diagnosis)
Items call droptofloor() at gamecode/hc/h2/items.hc:66. An item whose map
placement sits over a func_door brush would drop onto the door rather than the
world floor, and then behave badly once the door moves. Compare the handling in
gamecode/hc/h2/misc.hc:185,217 and soul.hc:187,248, which call droptofloor()
from other spawn paths.

Note this may be map-authoring rather than an engine or gamecode defect --
resolve which before spending time on a fix.
notes:
TRACED 2026-08-15 without the repro. The bead's "likely area" guess is roughly
right about droptofloor but wrong about the consequence, and the real mechanism
gives a much sharper question to put to the reporter.

## What actually happens to an item that lands on a func_door

1. PlaceItem (gamecode/hc/h2/items.hc:48-88) sets movetype MOVETYPE_TOSS, solid
   SOLID_TRIGGER, FL_ITEM, then drops with hull temporarily HULL_POINT.
2. PF_droptofloor (engine/h2shared/pr_cmds.c:2400-2432) on success sets
   FL_ONGROUND and groundentity = trace.ent. Landing on a door therefore makes
   the item a legitimate RIDER of that door, not merely a thing resting on it.
3. PlaceItem then setorigins the item +38 (or +28 for puzzle pieces) and
   setsizes mins_z to -38, so the box bottom still touches the door surface.
   setorigin does not clear FL_ONGROUND or groundentity, so the rider link
   survives.
4. SV_PushMove (engine/hexen2/sv_phys.c:585-612) does carry it -- MOVETYPE_TOSS
   is not in the skip list, and the "standing on the pusher" test matches. But
   line 611-612 strips FL_ONGROUND from every non-MOVETYPE_WALK entity it moves.
   So the item rides for exactly ONE frame and then becomes ballistic.

So "it rides the door forever" and "it stays behind floating" are both wrong.
It rides once, then falls, and where it lands depends on the door.

## The branch that would explain an unrecoverable item

sv_phys.c:626-633 (and the identical hunk at 837-845 in SV_PushRotate). When a
pushed entity is still embedded in the pusher afterwards, the engine fails the
move -- unless the entity is SOLID_NOT or SOLID_TRIGGER, in which case it takes
the "corpse" branch:

    check->v.mins[0] = check->v.mins[1] = 0;
    VectorCopy (check->v.mins, check->v.maxs);

That collapses the bbox to zero volume, permanently. Hexen II items are
SOLID_TRIGGER, so an item caught inside a moving door does not get shoved out or
block the door -- it silently loses its touch volume and can never be picked up
again. The guard at line 628 (`mins[0] == maxs[0]`) means it happens once and is
not self-correcting.

This is id's corpse hack, written when the only SOLID_NOT/SOLID_TRIGGER things
in a door's way were gibs. Hexen II putting pickups in that solid class is what
makes it reachable.

## Is it ours?

No. All three corpse branches are present verbatim at the fork point a0304b781,
and sv_phys.c has drifted only +17/-23 lines since. The rider selection, the
FL_ONGROUND strip and the corpse branch are all untouched. Whatever Mathuzzz is
seeing, vanilla Hexen II sees it too -- which is the map-authoring-vs-engine
discriminator this bead asked for, and it points at map authoring being the
proximate cause with an engine misfeature behind it.

## The question to ask the reporter, instead of "which map"

Map and item are still wanted, but this one discriminates:

    When you walk into the item, does nothing at all happen (it cannot be
    picked up), or is it just out of reach / in the wrong place?

  * cannot be picked up at all -> the corpse branch above. Engine defect,
    fixable by exempting FL_ITEM from that branch, and worth its own bead.
  * merely misplaced or unreachable -> ordinary droptofloor onto a door,
    map-authoring, and the fix belongs in the map.

The earlier green-key report the reporter refers to is still not in beads;
whichever answer comes back, file it there too.

title: Remember the selected artifact across a level change instead of resetting to torch
description:
Requested on Discord by 'Tome of Power Abuser' (2026-08-15): the inventory selection resets to the torch on every level transition, so you re-select your artifact each map. Asked specifically whether it can be done without breaking existing saves. Spoike's suggestion in-thread: 'just save it clientside'.

WHAT IS KNOWN SO FAR (not yet root-caused)
  * The selected slot is the entity field 'self.inventory'. It is assigned in
    exactly one place, gamecode/hc/h2/invntory.hc:903 and :905.
