  * ClientReEnter() (gamecode/hc/h2/client.hc:796) resets a long list of client
    state on level entry but does NOT touch self.inventory -- so the reset is
    happening somewhere else and that place still needs finding before this can
    be estimated. Check PutClientInServer() and the engine-side client carry-
    over (spawn_parms / host_cmd.c:1040, SV_SaveSpawnparms).
  * self.inventory is a server field mirrored to the client each frame
    (engine/hexen2/sv_main.c:1615), so it is not purely a HUD-local value.

SAVE-COMPAT CONSTRAINT (the real one)
Not the saves themselves -- it is the field-set gate added in e0f7d4c0f
(uhexen2-uhub): the build now REFUSES gamecode whose entity field set has
drifted from gamecode/fieldsets. Adding a new persisted entity field to hold
the selection would trip that gate and change the progdefs the engine matches
against. Reusing the existing self.inventory, or Spoike's client-side store,
avoids the gate entirely. Prefer one of those two.

DONE = artifact selection survives a changelevel, gamecode/fieldsets unchanged,
check_progs_fields.py still passes, and old savegames still load.
close_reason: Fixed in 9b4e7f450. ROOT CAUSE (the bead's open question): the selection is not a gamecode value at all — it lives in cl.inv_selected, a slot index in the cl struct, and CL_ClearState does memset(&cl,0,sizeof(cl)) on every level change. Slot 0 is the torch. self.inventory in the gamecode is only ever written by the engine via clc_inv_select, which is why grepping invntory.hc found no persistent assignment. FIX: keep the selected artifact's ID (not slot) in a static outside cl (sb_sticky_artifact in sbar.c) so it survives the wipe; seed SB_InvChanged's existing prev_artifact re-find with it when there is no live selection. That re-find is the uhexen2-o0n2 machinery — a level change is the same problem with a wider gap, so no new mechanism. Recorded in Inv_Update, the single choke point where cl.v.inventory is computed and pushed to the server. SAVE COMPAT: client-side only, exactly Spoike's suggestion. No new entity field, gamecode/fieldsets unchanged, e0f7d4c0f field-set gate untouched, check_progs_fields.py passes (runs in the gamecode derivation checkPhase on every nix build), old saves load. VERIFIED by driving the path directly with a temporary probe command — two software-rendered map loads plus the 4s inventory-bar timer is impractical headless on llvmpipe: select haste on map1 records sticky=9; sticky survives the cl wipe; map2 rebuild selects slot 2 = artifact 9 instead of torch; with haste removed on map3 it falls back to slot 0 = torch. Probe removed before commit. NOTE: only the standard inventory path (protocols 18-20) is covered; the protocol-21 ex_inventory branch of SB_InvChanged is untouched.

title: Replacement .mdl files silently change entity physics bounds
description:
## Problem

`PF_setmodel` in engine/h2shared/pr_cmds.c (lines 325-330) applies `mod->mins`/`mod->maxs` to EVERY model type, including alias models — not just brush models. The entity's physics collision box equals whatever the model loader computed until the progs calls `setsize()`.

The client/listen-server loader in engine/h2shared/gl_model.c derives alias bounds directly from actual mesh geometry at two sites (lines 3451-3454 and 3644-3649):

```c
mod->mins[i] = aliasmins[i] - 10;
mod->maxs[i] = aliasmaxs[i] + 10;
```

(The flat ±16 Quake default sits commented out just above each, under Raven's `// FIXME: do this right`.)

**Consequence:** Dropping in a replacement `.mdl` with different extents — a higher-poly remodel, rescaled model, or fan-made weapon/item replacement — silently changes that entity's collision box. Nothing in the engine warns, and nothing in the modder-facing docs explains this is load-bearing behavior.

## Why this matters now

- **Spoike (FTE dev)** raised it on Discord 2026-08-13 in the same thread that confirmed Raven's original spec was ±10 padding. Exact framing: "beware of replacement models." Not a report that our bounds path is wrong — a hazard warning about a correct path with a subtle footgun.
- **hexen2.club** (Inky's comprehensive mod/map repository) is ramping up content. As replacement-model drop-ins become more common, this footgun grows sharper.
- **Untracked:** `bd search "replacement model"` and `bd search "setmodel bounds"` both return zero hits across the open issue space.

## Relationship to existing work

This is the flip side of issue uhexen2-3coq (CLOSED): "Dedicated server gives alias entities different implicit bounds than the listen server." That issue established that the geometry-derived box is real and load-bearing, and deliberately declined to reconcile h2ded's zero-size-point behavior with the listen server's mesh-extents box — because resizing every alias entity is exactly the change class that caused P0 uhexen2-4p8t (fattening puzzle_piece bounds silently deleted map items). Same caution applies here: the fix is warn-or-document, NOT change-the-bounds.

## Candidate solutions

Neither touches the bounds themselves:

1. **Diagnostic:** When a loaded `.mdl` is a known replacement (requires a vanilla model extent table), compare its derived extents against the original and log a console warning on mismatch. Open question: building/maintaining the vanilla extent table may not be cheap.

2. **Documentation:** Add a modder-facing note to `gamecode/README` or extend the existing "Alias model bounds" section in `docs/SrcNotes.txt` (line 52+). Cheaper, lands immediately, no ongoing maintenance.

**Recommend option 2 as immediate step, with option 1 as optional follow-up.**

## Done means

Modders opening the relevant docs (or reading console on first load with a replacement model) can understand that `.mdl` extents are load-bearing for physics.
close_reason:
RESOLVED by documentation, the option-2 path recorded on this issue.

Added a 'Replacement .mdl files change entity physics bounds' section to docs/SrcNotes.txt, immediately after the h2ded-vs-listen-server alias-bounds section uhexen2-3coq wrote. It is the content-author-facing half of that note: the listen server derives an alias entity's box from mesh geometry (aliasmins/aliasmaxs padded +/-10), PF_setmodel applies it, so a replacement .mdl changes collision and not just appearance for any entity whose progs never calls setsize(). Written for the three parties it can bite -- mod authors (call setsize), model authors (keep drop-in extents near the original's), and anyone packaging or hosting fan content (a models-only pack is not necessarily gameplay-neutral).

Deliberately NOT gamecode/README: that file is strictly a changelog of our .hc divergences from Raven's 1.29c, and this is neither a gamecode change nor a divergence.

Option 1 (extents-comparison diagnostic) NOT taken and not refiled. It needs a maintained table of vanilla per-model extents to compare a loaded .mdl against, and there is no cheap way to know what 'the original' was at load time. The maintenance burden outweighs a warning for a hazard that is documented and vanilla-inherited. Refile if replacement-model breakage is ever actually reported in the wild rather than anticipated.

The bounds themselves are untouched, per the 3coq reasoning: engine-side alias resizing is the change class that already caused a P0 (uhexen2-4p8t, fattened puzzle_piece bounds silently deleting map items).

Provenance: raised by Spoike on Discord 2026-08-13, in the conversation that also confirmed the +/-10 against Raven's original Hexen II source release.

Landed as the docs/SrcNotes.txt hunk committed alongside this close.

title: Build-time assertion that shipped progs images agree on the entity field set
description:
uhexen2-acew closed on its fallback -- the load path now reports dropped fields loudly
(cdeb34f98). This is acew's PREFERRED half, which was not done and is still worth having.

## What

packages.gamecode (flake.nix) already compiles every gamecode tree in one derivation. Extract
the entity field table from each produced progs.dat with tools/qcdis.py and fail the build if
the shipped images disagree on it.

## Why it is still wanted now that the runtime warning exists

They catch different things and neither subsumes the other:

- The runtime warning covers every source of mismatch -- a player's own progs.dat, a
  third-party fork, a save carried in from another engine -- but only at load time, only for
  the fields a particular save happens to reference, and only for a player who reads the
  console.
- A build assertion covers only what we ship, but catches a field-set divergence before it
  reaches anybody, on every field rather than the referenced ones, and costs nothing at
  runtime.

The build check is the one that would stop us from shipping the problem in the first place.

## Notes

- The images are believed to agree today: all currently selectable ones compile against the
  v1.12 progdefs layout, and our divergences from Raven are statement-level rather than
  field-level. So this should land green, and its value is as a ratchet against future drift
  -- particularly if uhexen2-2kcw vendors a third variant or uhexen2-nr9l bundles hw/siege.
- Decide what "disagree" means before writing it. Identical field sets is the strict reading;
  a superset may be tolerable in one direction (new fields a save simply never references)
  and is exactly the case that would otherwise trip a naive equality check.
- Failure message should name the differing fields, not just say the sets differ.
notes:
DONE in e0f7d4c0f. Both halves of acew's defence are now in place.

IMPLEMENTED:
- tools/qcdis.py --fields: prints the entity field table as 'name type offset' sorted by
  name. First def wins, matching the engine's ED_FindField.
- tools/check_progs_fields.py: compares images against each other and against a checked-in
  golden. On failure it names the fields that appeared, disappeared, or moved -- the bead
  asked for that specifically and a bare 'the sets differ' would be useless in a build log.
- gamecode/fieldsets/{h2,portals}.fields: the goldens.
- flake.nix packages.gamecode: doCheck + checkPhase running both gates. gamecodeSrc widened
  to admit the checker and goldens; the engine's filteredSrc hash is untouched, which is why
  those two filters are kept separate.

THE FINDING THAT MAKES THIS WORTH HAVING: our built data1/progs.dat has a field table
IDENTICAL to Raven's retail PROGS.DAT -- 497 fields, zero diff, verified directly against
/home/josh/hexen2/data1/PROGS.DAT. That equality is precisely what makes sv_gamecode 0 and 1
interchangeable today, it was previously only assumed, and it is exactly what a future
gamecode change could break silently. The golden pins it even though retail PROGS.DAT itself
cannot be in the build (unfree, only in the player's install).

Also measured, for the record:
  data1/progs.dat   497 fields   == retail PROGS.DAT, == progs2.dat
  portals/progs.dat 511 fields   17 fields retail does not have, 3 it drops, offsets shifted
  hw/hwprogs.dat    531 fields
  siege/hwprogs.dat 553 fields

DESIGN CALLS, both of which the bead asked to be decided:
1. Equality, not superset. A superset sounds tolerable -- a save never references the new
   fields -- but the engine indexes by OFFSET, and inserting a field renumbers everything
   after it, so a superset in the name domain is usually a total mismatch in the offset
   domain. Equality is both the honest check and the cheap one.
2. portals is gated against its OWN golden, not against h2. Different campaign, own gamedir,
   own 511-field layout, and saves live under fs_userdir/<gamedir> so they never cross.
   Gating it against h2 would have failed on day one for no reason. hw/siege have no
   savegames of this kind and are ungated.

VERIFIED BOTH DIRECTIONS: the build passes green with the real goldens ('progs field sets
agree (497 fields across 2 images)' / '(511 fields across 1 image)'), and moving a single
field's offset by one in h2.fields fails the build naming that field and printing the
--write-golden regeneration command.
close_reason: Closed

title: Sprites render nothing under r_oit 1 — reproduces on llvmpipe, so not an Intel driver quirk
description:
With r_oit 1 no sprite renders at all. Not dimmed, not mis-sorted -- absent. Explosion halos (sm_expld.spr) and the raven staff's white smoke clouds (CreateWhiteSmoke) are simply not drawn.

## Evidence (2026-08-15)

Headless demo1, Necromancer + raven staff held down, host_framerate 0.05, 20 frame-matched screenshots per run, 640x480 on llvmpipe. Mean luma per frame (x2550):

- r_oit 0: 552 347 276 272 275 276 436 375 312 272 274 276 277 556 350 278 272 275 275 436
- r_oit 1: 279 268 271 271 271 271 270 279 274 272 271 271 271 283 271 272 271 270 270 270

The r_oit 0 run's bright frames are the smoke clouds filling the screen. The r_oit 1 run is flat -- every sprite frame is missing. Side-by-side at matched frames 0/6/13 confirms it visually: same geometry, same viewmodel, no sprites.

Separately, an r_oit 1 pair with r_softparticles on vs off is identical to 0.5-0.7% RMSE, i.e. the soft-particle fade (uhexen2-mf9u) is a no-op under OIT because there is nothing left to fade. That is how this was found.

## This is NOT hardware-specific

uhexen2-a0hp was closed with "WBOIT pipeline didn't render visibly on Mesa Intel Iris Xe and the cause wasn't isolated. Closing out of the active list -- reopen if revisiting on different hardware." It reproduces identically on llvmpipe, a software rasteriser with a completely different backend. The Iris Xe driver-quirk hypothesis is dead; this is a logic bug in our WBOIT path.

## uhexen2-mex9's stated cause is stale

mex9 (12d4f471c) said: "Sprites still use gl_shader_alias (no OIT-aware shader yet); during an OIT pass they write to accum but leave revealage = 1.0, so the resolve discards them and projectiles/effects vanish." uhexen2-a0hp (1acf64930) then routed sprites through gl_shader_alias_oit -- gl_rmain.c:697 is now GL_ImmEnd(GL_QUADS, OIT_InPass() ? &gl_shader_alias_oit : &gl_shader_alias). So that specific cause is fixed and the symptom survived it. Whatever is wrong now is something else, and neither bead's close reason describes it.

## Where to look

- Not an FBO creation failure: the boot log prints "OIT: 640x480 FBO ready", and OIT_CreateFBO is only reached from PP_CreateFBO, so the depth attachment is genuinely shared with the scene FBO.
- OIT_EndTranslucency (gl_postprocess.c:1233) composites into GL_GetSceneFBO(), which returns pp_fbo. Check what happens when the scene did not render into pp_fbo.
- The WBOIT maths in GL_CompileOITFragShader's oit_preamble (gl_shader.c:134): out_reveal = vec4(fragColor.a, 0,0,0) with per-buffer blend (ZERO, ONE_MINUS_SRC_COLOR). An opaque sprite has a=1, driving revealage to 0, which should reveal it fully -- verify the resolve shader's sense of revealage matches that convention rather than inverting it.
- R_DrawSpriteModel keeps GL_BLEND enabled inside an OIT pass but deliberately never sets a blend func there, relying on GL_ImmEnd re-asserting glBlendFunci per draw (gl_vbo.c:502).

## Repro

  SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 glhexen2 -basedir <retail> \
    +r_oit 1 +exec <cfg>

where <cfg> sets host_framerate 0.05, _cl_playerclass 3, map demo1, then impulse 9 / impulse 4 / +attack and a burst of screenshots. Compare against the same run with +r_oit 0.

## Impact

None on players today: GL_PostProcess_Init force-resets a saved r_oit=1 to 0 at registration (gl_postprocess.c:1458), precisely because of this. It does block r_oit from ever being enabled.
notes:
FIXED in 8dcbc6284. Root cause was not in the OIT pass at all.

DIAGNOSIS: instrumented OIT_EndTranslucency with a glReadPixels of both attachments before
the composite. On exactly the frames whose sprites were missing, accum peaked at 6292 and
revealage was driven to 0 -- i.e. the sprites drew into the OIT buffers correctly, with the
right WBOIT values. So every hypothesis in this bead's 'where to look' list was wrong: the
blend funcs, the revealage convention, GL_BLEND handling in R_DrawSpriteModel, the alias_oit
shader routing. All fine. The composite was the problem.

ROOT CAUSE: oit_resolve_vert emits (-1,-1), (3,-1), (-1,3) -- counter-clockwise in NDC, so
front-facing. This engine culls FRONT faces (gl_vidsdl.c :: GL_Init(), re-asserted by
R_SetupGL every frame when gl_cull is on). The resolve's fullscreen triangle was therefore
discarded before rasterisation on every single frame, and the correctly-filled accum and
revealage buffers were composited nowhere.

PP_BlitWith3DEffects and the final blit both glDisable(GL_CULL_FACE) before their fullscreen
draws. OIT_EndTranslucency never did.

FIX: disable culling around the resolve draw and restore it after. Restored rather than left
off because unlike the other two this runs mid-frame -- R_DrawAllGlows, R_DrawViewModel and
R_Mirror all draw afterwards. Queried with glIsEnabled rather than assumed, since gl_cull 0
legitimately leaves it off.

WHY IT LOOKED HARDWARE-SPECIFIC: it never was. A front-facing triangle under front-face
culling is culled on every implementation. uhexen2-a0hp closed this as an unexplained Mesa
Intel Iris Xe quirk; reproducing it on llvmpipe is what killed that hypothesis.

SCOPE: this was not a sprite bug. It broke EVERYTHING routed through OIT -- particles,
translucent water and translucent alias models as well as sprites. Sprites were just the
visible case in the test scene.

VERIFIED on retail data1, demo1, Necromancer + raven staff held down, host_framerate 0.05,
20 frame-matched screenshots, mean luma x10:
  r_oit 0        273 268 268 271 556 350 278 ... peak 556
  r_oit 1 before 273 268 268 271 283 271 272 ... peak 283
  r_oit 1 after  273 268 268 271 561 350 278 ... peak 563
Frame-for-frame tracking restored, smoke clouds and fire sprites visibly back. Slightly
brighter on sprite frames, as expected from order-independent rather than back-to-front
compositing.

ALSO RESOLVES the stated symptom of uhexen2-a0hp and uhexen2-mex9, both of which were closed
against causes that were real but were not this one.

FOLLOW-UP filed for the r_oit force-reset at registration, which was added because of this.
close_reason: Closed

title: vid.fullbright reads 3 bytes past the end of host_colormap, and nothing validates its size
description:
Found while implementing uhexen2-lpza (colormap-accurate palette quantization), which needed
the exact layout of gfx/colormap.lmp and turned this up on the way.

`engine/h2shared/gl_vidsdl.c :: VID_Init()`:

    vid.colormap = host_colormap;
    vid.fullbright = 256 - LittleLong (*((int *)(vid.colormap + 256 * 64)));
    Con_DPrintf ("Fullbright start index: %d\n", vid.fullbright);
    if (vid.fullbright < 1 || vid.fullbright > 256)
        vid.fullbright = 224;	/* fallback: standard Quake/Hexen II value */

`256 * 64` is 16384, and it reads a 4-byte `int` there. Retail `gfx/colormap.lmp` is
**16385 bytes** — verified directly out of `/home/josh/hexen2/data1/pak0.pak`: 64 rows of
256 entries, plus ONE trailing byte. So the read takes bytes 16384..16387 and **three of
those four are past the end of the buffer.**

It has never been noticed because it fails safe by accident: the three garbage bytes make
`256 - LittleLong(...)` land outside [1,256], the guard on the next line fires, and
`vid.fullbright` gets 224 — which happens to be the right answer for retail data. The
diagnostic `Con_DPrintf` above the guard prints the garbage value, not the used one.

The correct read is the single trailing byte:

    vid.fullbright = 256 - ((byte *)vid.colormap)[256 * 64];

which is 256 - 1 = 255 for retail pak0. Note that this is NOT 224, so fixing the read
CHANGES BEHAVIOUR — check what consumes `vid.fullbright` before changing it, and whether
255 or the historical 224 is what those call sites actually want. It is plausible the
right fix is to keep 224 and delete the bogus read entirely. Decide, don't just patch the
arithmetic.

For reference, the fork-point code (`a0304b781:engine/h2shared/vid_sdl.c`) had a different
bug in the same line — `*((int *)vid.colormap + 2048)`, i.e. offset 8192, which is inside
the table rather than past it. That is stock id code. So the current line is a partial fix
of an inherited defect that moved the read from wrong-but-in-bounds to
wrong-and-out-of-bounds.

## Related, and the reason this is P3 rather than P4

Nothing in the engine validates the SIZE of `host_colormap`. `engine/hexen2/host.c ::
Host_Init()` calls `FS_LoadHunkFile("gfx/colormap.lmp", NULL)` — passing NULL for the
length out-param — and `Sys_Error`s only if the pointer is NULL. A mod shipping a
truncated or absent-trailing-byte colormap over-reads by more than three bytes, and every
consumer of the table assumes 64x256 without checking.

uhexen2-lpza's new `PP_BuildColormapLUT` inherits that same assumption rather than adding
a check, deliberately, so as not to bundle an unrelated hardening change into that commit.
Fixing it here is the right place: retain the length from FS_LoadHunkFile and validate it
is at least 256*64 before anything indexes the table.

## Acceptance

The out-of-bounds read is gone — either by reading the trailing byte correctly or by
dropping the read and keeping the constant, with the choice justified against what actually
consumes vid.fullbright. Plus a size check on host_colormap at load.
acceptance_criteria: The out-of-bounds read is gone, with the 255-vs-224 choice justified against what consumes vid.fullbright, plus a size check on host_colormap at load.
notes:
VERIFIED COMPLETE at d81eec5aa; nothing left to do. Re-checked against the tree today.

1. OOB read gone. gl_vidsdl.c :: VID_Init() assigns vid.fullbright = 224 as a
   constant. The 4-byte read at offset 256*VID_GRADES of a 16385-byte buffer is
   deleted.
2. The 224-vs-255 choice is justified in the comment, and against the consumer the
   bead asked for: gl_model.c :: Mod_LoadFullbrightTexture() scans
   'data[i] >= vid.fullbright && data[i] < 255', so deriving 255 from the trailing
   byte would ask for '>= 255 && < 255' and silently disable every fullbright mask.
   The comment says so at length precisely so nobody 'fixes' it back.
3. Con_DPrintf now prints the value actually installed.
4. Range guards reconciled. The gl_vidsdl.c (<1 || >256) guard is gone with the
   derivation; gl_model.c's surviving guard tests (<1 || >255), which is the correct
   bound.
5. Size check on host_colormap at load: host.c :: Host_Init() now Sys_Errors if
   fs_filesize < 256*VID_GRADES, read immediately after the FS_LoadHunkFile so it
   still describes that call. Covers the software lighting ramps and
   PP_BuildColormapLUT (uhexen2-lpza), neither of which bounds-checks the table.

Acceptance criteria met in full.
close_reason: Closed

title: Mods menu scans host_parms->basedir while game resolves against fs_basedir, so -basedir desyncs them
description:
The `-basedir` command-line switch sets `fs_basedir` but leaves `host_parms->basedir` pointing at the launch working directory (see `engine/h2shared/quakefs.c:1904-1916`). The two then disagree about where game data lives:

- `M_ScanMods` (`engine/hexen2/menu.c:4858`) enumerates mod directories via `Sys_ListDirectories (host_parms->basedir, ...)` and tests candidates with `FS_IsGamedir (host_parms->basedir, ...)` — so the Mods menu scans the launch CWD.
- `Host_Game_f` (`engine/h2shared/quakefs.c:1543`) and the new `ListGames` tab completer both resolve against `fs_basedir`.

Result: when the engine is started with `-basedir`, the Mods menu can list a different (or empty) set of mods than the `game` command will actually accept, and `game <TAB>` will offer directories the menu does not show.

This is the same class of bug as uhexen2-5mhd, which fixed the `Host_Game_f` side but did not touch `menu.c`. The two should be linked as related.

Suggested fix: make `M_ScanMods` use `fs_basedir` rather than `host_parms->basedir`, or reconcile the two at startup so `-basedir` updates both. Needs a check for other `host_parms->basedir` readers that should also be looking at `fs_basedir`.

Note: This was discovered during uhexen2-nzuo (console tab completion work) and intentionally left alone there to keep that change behavior-preserving.
notes:
FIXED in 498fbd51b.

M_ScanMods (hexen2/menu.c) takes FS_GetBasedir() once into a local and uses it for
all three probes (portals Sys_FileType, Sys_ListDirectories, FS_IsGamedir), so the
Mods menu now enumerates the same tree Host_Game_f and the 'game' completer resolve
against.

The audit the bead asked for turned up exactly one other stale reader:
SF_FindSoundFont step 2b (h2shared/soundfont.c), the '<basedir>/soundfont.sf2' and
'<basedir>/data1/soundfont.sf2' probes -- game-data-relative, so they move with
-basedir. Fixed in the same commit. The exedir probes above it are correct as-is:
they genuinely mean 'next to the binary' and already use exedir, which -basedir does
not and should not move.

Those were the only two. Remaining host_parms->basedir readers after this are
quakefs.c:1916 (the FS_Init assignment itself) and comments.

No behaviour change without -basedir: FS_Init sets fs_basedir = host_parms->basedir
when the switch is absent, so FS_GetBasedir() returns the same pointer.

VERIFIED: builds clean; headless run with -basedir reaches the frame loop and the
soundfont search still falls through to SOUNDFONT_PATH without faulting, i.e.
FS_GetBasedir() is populated by the time SF_FindSoundFont runs (it is called from
midi_fluid.c / snd_timidity.c at sound init, long after FS_Init).

NOT verified interactively: the Mods menu itself needs a keypress to open, so the
listing was not eyeballed under -basedir.
