title: Classic Software look: quantize through Raven's own colormap in the post-process chain
description:
The cheap answer to "can we have the 1997 software renderer back". Independent of the
restoration decision bead -- worth doing on its own merits even if that comes back NO, and
arguably the thing that makes it come back NO.

Reproduce the *look* of the 8-bit software rasterizer as a post-process preset, rather than
restoring 29K lines of span rasterizer and owning a second renderer forever.

## Why this is cheap here specifically

Both halves already exist in the tree:

- `engine/h2shared/gl_postprocess.c` -- the post-process chain, already used for the
  existing screen effects
- the render-scale control (Options > Display) -- already renders at reduced resolution and
  upscales, which is the single most recognisable part of the look
- `host_colormap` -- `host.c :: Host_Init()` already loads `gfx/colormap.lmp` and
  Sys_Errors without it, and `gl_vidsdl.c` already assigns `vid.colormap = host_colormap`.
  The engine has Raven's actual 256x64 lighting ramp in memory RIGHT NOW and does nothing
  with it.

That last point is what makes this worth doing properly rather than as a generic "retro
shader": the authentic colormap is available, so the palette quantization can be the real
one rather than a nearest-colour approximation of it.

## What the look actually consists of

Rank these by recognisability, and implement in this order -- each is independently
shippable and independently togglable:

1. **Palette quantization through the real colormap.** Upload `host_colormap` as a 256x64
   LUT plus the 256-entry palette. Fragment shader maps lit RGB -> palette index -> RGB.
   This is the single biggest contributor and it is close to exact, not an imitation.
2. **Low internal resolution.** Already have it. The preset just sets it, likely 320x240 or
   a 2x/3x integer step.
3. **Affine (perspective-incorrect) texture interpolation.** The wobble on floor and wall
   textures near the camera. Needs `noperspective` interpolation qualifiers in the world
   fragment path, gated by a cvar -- more invasive than the other three because it touches
   the main world shader rather than the post chain.
4. **Ordered dithering before quantization.** The original dithered nothing, but the
   quantizer benefits and it reads as period-correct on gradients.

Explicitly NOT in scope: emulating the span rasterizer's exact subpixel and z-buffer
behaviour, or its edge-list sort order. That is the restoration bead's problem, not this
one.

## Shape it as a preset, not a pile of cvars

The engine already has presets in the Display menu. One "Classic Software" entry that sets
the render scale and the quantize/dither/affine cvars together, with the individual cvars
still exposed for people who want to mix. That matches how the existing presets work and
keeps the menu from growing four rows nobody understands in isolation.

## Verification

Use the deterministic headless render-comparison harness (bd memory
`deterministic-headless-render-comparison-harness-2026-08-14`, proven on uhexen2-isq7 /
li13 / ebpk) to capture before/after on a fixed camera. For the palette step specifically,
a strong check is available: every output pixel must be an exact member of the 256-colour
palette. That is a machine-checkable property, not an eyeball judgement, and it is worth
asserting in the harness.

## Acceptance

A "Classic Software" preset that quantizes through Raven's own colormap at reduced internal
resolution, with each component separately togglable, and a headless capture showing every
pixel is a palette member.
acceptance_criteria: A Classic Software preset that quantizes through host_colormap at reduced internal resolution, each component separately togglable, with a headless capture proving every output pixel is a member of the 256-colour palette.
notes:
CLOSING as done. The revised scope (see the earlier scope-correction note) landed in 31a4a904c;
this note records the acceptance measurement the bead asked for, which had not been run.

IMPLEMENTED (31a4a904c): r_softemu 3 builds pp_colormap_lut, a 32x32x32 GL_R8 3D texture
filled through host_colormap's authored ramps rather than by RGB nearest-colour search
against d_8to24table. PP_BuildColormapLUT (h2shared/gl_postprocess.c) does the build and
falls back to the nearest-colour LUT with a console line if the colormap is unavailable.
Modes 1 and 2 are untouched, as the bead required. Wired into the Display menu
(hexen2/menu.c) alongside the existing presets.

ACCEPTANCE MEASUREMENT, run 2026-08-15 -- the machine-checkable property the bead specified
('every output pixel must be an exact member of the 256-colour palette'):

Headless demo1, retail data1, setpos 480 -352 40 0 90 0, r_scale 1 and r_dither 0 so nothing
downstream of the quantizer can reintroduce off-palette values, screenshot region above the
status bar, checked against gfx/palette.lmp extracted from pak0.pak:

  r_softemu 0:  19769 unique colours,   56 palette members (0.3%),   3.70% of pixels exact
  r_softemu 3:    135 unique colours,  135 palette members (100.0%), 100.00% of pixels exact

Exact, not approximately. The whole frame collapses to 135 of Raven's 256 colours.

NOTE for anyone re-running this: use r_scale 1. A reduced render scale upscales with
filtering AFTER quantization, which blends palette entries into off-palette values and will
make this check fail for a reason that is not a quantizer bug. The 'Crunchy' and 'Retro'
presets both set r_scale < 1, so they will not satisfy the property even though the
quantizer is working.

STILL NOT DONE, and explicitly out of scope for this bead's first pass: affine
(perspective-incorrect) texture interpolation, item 3 of the original ranked list. Filed
separately -- it touches the world fragment path rather than the post chain.
close_reason: Closed

title: Audit the vendored tree's bytecode against retail and our own portals build before it ships
description:
Gated on the vendored-variant decision bead, and on the vendoring bead.

Before a vendored tree ships to players, disassemble what it actually compiles to and state
what it changes. Same standard uhexen2-8zia held our own trees to, and the same standard
uhexen2-nr9l is holding hw/siege bundling to -- a third-party tree does not get a lower bar
than our own code.

## Method

`tools/qcdis.py`, with the v6 unsigned-operand fix (landed `e6dd815f1`; invocation in
`tools/README.md`). Two tiers, as established by uhexen2-8zia:

- tier 1: function symbol table -- names, numparms, locals
- tier 2: per-function opcode stream over [first_statement, next_function_start)

## Baselines

Unlike uhexen2-nr9l, this one is not blocked on obtaining reference bytecode. Both baselines
are already on the box:

- retail `portals/progs.dat` from the install -- what a Classic player runs
- our own built `portals/progs.dat` -- what an Updated player runs

Diff the vendored build against BOTH. The second is the interesting one: it says exactly
what a player gains and loses by moving from our tree to theirs, which is the question the
menu value is asking them to answer.

## Classify every divergence

Reuse uhexen2-8zia's four buckets:

  (a) an upstream uHexen2 fix -- document which
  (b) a deliberate fork change -- document whose, and why
  (c) an unreverted accident -- like uhexen2-qj8s
  (d) source differing from shipped bytecode -- harmless unless it moves the field set

Track the same counters as 8zia's results table: function count, shared, byte-identical,
opcode-differing.

## Two specific things to look for

1. **Field-set changes.** Directly feeds the cross-variant savegame bead -- if the vendored
   tree adds or removes entity fields, that hazard stops being latent and becomes live for
   any player who crosses variants mid-campaign. This is the single most important output of
   this audit.

2. **The CLASS_HENCHMAN tail.** uhexen2-h77u closed Raven's 10% dead zone with a bare
   `else`; upstream keeps `else if (chance < .90)` and merely stops counting the unassigned
   window. Confirm in the bytecode which one the vendored build has, because it is a
   deliberate balance divergence between the two values the player is choosing between, and
   it should be stated in whatever the release notes say about the variant.

## Done when

A results table exists in the style of uhexen2-8zia's, every divergence falls in a labelled
bucket, the field-set question is answered yes or no, and the outcome is recorded in
`gamecode/README` under the vendored-tree section.
acceptance_criteria: A results table in the style of uhexen2-8zia's; every divergence in a labelled bucket; the field-set question answered yes or no; outcome recorded in gamecode/README.

title: Resolve the variant coverage hole: fall back to Updated for gamedirs a variant does not ship
description:
Gated on the vendored-variant decision bead, and on the enum bead. This is the hard call in
the whole feature; it is filed separately so the reasoning gets recorded rather than being
made silently inside an implementation commit.

## The problem

jsHexen2-progs contains only `portals/` (per `ebd68cc11`; the vendoring bead re-confirms
this against current upstream). Our bundle covers `data1` AND `portals`. So a third
`sv_gamecode` value is meaningful in the mission pack and meaningless in the base game --
which is what most players run.

`PR_BundledProgsPath` resolves per map spawn and already knows the gamedir. The menu does
not, and deliberately so.

## The constraint that rules out the obvious fix

`PR_GamecodeAvailable()`'s header comment already settled the adjacent question:

    Answers only the cheap, stable half of PR_BundledProgsPath's conditions [...] The
    per-gamedir conditions are deliberately not repeated here: they depend on the searchpath
    at map spawn, and a menu item that appeared and vanished as the player moved between
    data1 and portals would be worse than one that is occasionally present but inert.

So "grey out or hide the jsHexen2 value while in data1" is already-rejected design. Do not
re-open it without engaging that argument.

## Recommended: fall back to Updated for any gamedir a variant does not cover

`PR_BundledProgsPath`, having resolved gamedir and variant, checks whether the variant ships
an image for that gamedir. If not, it falls back to value 1's image. The menu row stays
static, which is what the constraint above demands.

The honesty cost is real and is paid elsewhere: the startup provenance line (uhexen2-zixe)
already prints the actual path and whole-file crc of what loaded, so a player or a bug report
can always see which image really won. That line becomes load-bearing under this design --
do not let it regress.

Mitigate the label too: print `jsHexen2 (portals)` rather than `jsHexen2`, so the row states
its own scope without needing to know the current gamedir.

## Rejected

- **Hide or grey the row per-gamedir** -- contradicts `PR_GamecodeAvailable`'s recorded
  decision above.
- **Fall back to Classic instead of Updated** -- worse. A player who has selected a curated
  bugfix tree has expressed a preference for fixes over retail behaviour; dropping them to
  Raven's unpatched data1 inverts that.
- **Fill the variant's data1 from our own tree and ship the mix under one label** -- that is
  not vendoring, it is forking their fork, and it mislabels a mixed image as theirs.
- **Refuse to offer the variant until upstream has a data1 tree** -- legitimate, and is
  effectively what the gating decision bead recommends anyway. If the decision comes back NO
  this bead dies with it.

## Done when

A variant that covers only some gamedirs behaves predictably in the ones it does not cover,
the fallback is documented in `PR_BundledProgsPath`'s header comment alongside the existing
conditions, and the menu label states the variant's scope.
acceptance_criteria: A partially-covering variant behaves predictably in the gamedirs it does not cover; the fallback is documented in PR_BundledProgsPath's header alongside the existing conditions; the menu label states the variant's scope.

title: Generalise sv_gamecode from boolean to a variant enum (cvar, latch, bundle path, menu)
description:
Gated on the vendored-variant decision bead. Do not start until that is decided YES.

`sv_gamecode` is a boolean today. A third value needs it to become a small enum, touching
four places. Read `ebd68cc11` first -- it establishes why the cvar is latched and why
`-vanillaprogs` outranks it, and none of that changes here.

## 1. The cvar and the latch -- `engine/h2shared/pr_edict.c`

- `sv_gamecode` (`pr_edict.c :: sv_gamecode`) keeps default `"1"`, still CVAR_ARCHIVE.
- `PR_GamecodeIsUpdated()` returns qboolean and is the wrong shape. Replace with
  `PR_GamecodeVariant()` returning the latched enum; `pr_gamecode_latched` already stores an
  int with -1 meaning "never latched", so that half needs no change.
- Clamp unknown values. An archived config from a build that had three values, replayed on a
  build that has two, must not select a variant that is not there. Out-of-range falls back
  to 1 (Updated).
- `PR_GamecodeAvailable()` stays a qboolean -- the menu row's question is still "is there
  anything at all to choose between". It must NOT start answering per-variant; see the
  coverage-hole bead for why.

## 2. Bundle path resolution -- `pr_edict.c :: PR_BundledProgsPath()`

Currently composes `<bundle>/<gamedir>/<progname>`. Needs a variant component.

Its long header comment documents two ANDed conditions plus a user-directory stand-down, and
ends with "Do not reduce the AND." Preserve all of that -- the variant component is an
addition to the path, not a change to whether substitution is allowed. The
`user directory > bundle > install directory` ordering also stays exactly as it is.

## 3. Bundle layout -- `flake.nix` `packages.gamecode`, and `PR_FindBundleDir`

Today `packages.gamecode` installs to `$out/share/hexenwail/data1/{progs.dat,progs2.dat}`
and `$out/share/hexenwail/portals/progs.dat`, and `packages.nixos-bundled` / the h2ded
equivalent copy those paths by name.

Needs a variant level. Prefer keeping value 1 at the current flat paths and putting variants
in a sibling namespace, so the existing layout and every packager instruction stay valid:

    share/hexenwail/data1/progs.dat            <- value 1, unchanged
    share/hexenwail/portals/progs.dat          <- value 1, unchanged
    share/hexenwail/variants/<name>/portals/progs.dat   <- value 2

`PR_FindBundleDir` itself needs no change -- it locates the bundle root and the three lookup
layers (exedir/gamecode, ../share/hexenwail, compile-time `BUNDLED_GAMECODE_DIR`) are
unaffected. But layer 3 exists for distro packagers, so a layout addition is a packaging
note worth putting in `docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md`.

## 4. Menu -- `engine/hexen2/menu.c`

- `M_Game_Draw`'s `GAME_GAMECODE` row currently prints `Cvar_VariableValue(...) ? "Updated"
  : "Classic"`. Needs a name table indexed by the enum.
- The keybind handler currently toggles `? 0 : 1`. Needs to cycle 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0, and to
  cycle only over variants this build actually shipped.
- `M_Game_IsSkip`'s `PR_GamecodeAvailable()` check is unchanged.
- Label the variant for what it covers, not just who wrote it -- e.g. `jsHexen2 (portals)`
  rather than `jsHexen2`. See the coverage-hole bead.

## Also

The startup provenance line (uhexen2-zixe) already names the actual file loaded and its
whole-file crc. Confirm it still does under a variant -- it is the only place the player can
see which image really won, and the coverage-hole fallback makes that more important, not
less.

## Done when

Three values select three images, an archived out-of-range value degrades to Updated, the
menu cycles only over shipped variants, and `-vanillaprogs` still beats all of them.
acceptance_criteria: Three values select three images; an archived out-of-range value degrades to Updated; the menu cycles only over shipped variants; -vanillaprogs still outranks all of them.

title: Vendor jsHexen2-progs under gamecode/hc/vendor/ with a vendored-tree provenance policy
description:
Gated on the vendored-variant decision bead. Do not start until that is decided YES.

Vendor KoMiKoZa/jsHexen2-progs into the tree so it can back a third `sv_gamecode` value.

## Placement

`gamecode/hc/vendor/jshexen2/`, NOT `gamecode/hc/jshexen2/`.

The `gamecode/hc/` namespace currently means "trees we own and edit" -- h2, hw, portals,
siege. A vendored tree is governed by the opposite rule and the directory layout should say
so rather than relying on anyone remembering.

`flake.nix`'s `gamecodeSrc` filter already admits everything under `gamecode/hc/`
(`rel == "gamecode/hc" || hasPrefix "gamecode/hc/" rel`), so a subdirectory is picked up for
free and does not need a filter change. It DOES need explicit `hcc -src` and `install` lines
in `packages.gamecode` -- the four current trees are listed one per line, not globbed.

## Provenance record

`gamecode/hc/vendor/jshexen2/PROVENANCE` (or a section in `gamecode/README` pointing at it),
recording:

- upstream URL and the exact commit sha vendored, with its date
- upstream's licence, and confirmation it permits redistribution in our release zip.
  jsHexen2-progs is a fork of Raven's HexenC source; check what terms it carries and
  whether they are compatible with how we already ship `gamecode/`
- what upstream contains -- confirm the "portals/ only" claim from `ebd68cc11` against the
  repo as it stands now, since that shapes the whole coverage-hole bead
- every local delta from upstream, ideally none

## The policy inversion, stated explicitly

`gamecode/README` opens with "the policy is that our .hc wins and every divergence gets
recorded here", written for trees we author. That rule is wrong for a vendored tree and the
file must say where it stops applying:

- **our trees**: our .hc wins; divergences FROM RAVEN get recorded
- **vendored trees**: upstream wins; divergences FROM UPSTREAM get recorded, and each one
  needs a justification, because every local edit is re-sync cost

Note the already-recorded case that makes this concrete: uhexen2-9gdx took upstream's
`RandomMonsterGoodies` diagnosis but deliberately did NOT take upstream's handling of the
CLASS_HENCHMAN tail, because uhexen2-h77u closed that dead zone outright where upstream
merely stops miscounting it. In OUR portals tree that divergence is correct and recorded. In
a VENDORED tree it would be a local patch needing justification -- or, better, not applied
at all, since the whole point of the third value is to offer upstream's choices unmodified.

## Done when

The tree is in place, compiles under `hcc` in the flake build, its provenance and licence
are recorded, and `gamecode/README` states the two-policy split. No engine changes here --
those are the enum bead.
acceptance_criteria: Tree in place and compiling under hcc in the flake build; upstream sha, date and licence recorded; gamecode/README states the our-trees vs vendored-trees policy split. No engine changes.

title: PR_LatchGamecode's savegame-CRC rationale is not supported by the code
description:
Documentation-correctness bug, found while designing the vendored-gamecode variant.

`PR_LatchGamecode`'s header comment (`engine/h2shared/pr_edict.c :: PR_LatchGamecode()`) says:

    Called when a NEW GAME starts, and only then.  changelevel and restart must not
    call it: a campaign has to finish on the gamecode it began with, and a
    savegame's progdefs CRC is checked against whatever is loaded, so swapping
    mid-run would leave the player unable to load their own saves.

`ebd68cc11`'s commit message makes the same claim more strongly, and cites the crc figures
24008 / 17499 in support.

**The second half is not supported by the code.** Nothing checks a progdefs CRC on savegame
load:

- `Host_Loadgame_f` (`engine/hexen2/host_cmd.c :: Host_Loadgame_f()`) validates
  `SAVEGAME_VERSION` and nothing else.
- `progs->crc` is consulted in exactly three places, all of them the CLASS_DEMON
  availability gate: `host_cmd.c:1355`, `engine/hexen2/server/host_cmd.c:1159`, and
  `engine/hexen2/sv_user.c:172,182`.
- `pr_crc` (the whole-file CRC, `pr_edict.c:2847`) is saved and restored only by
  `PR_SaveVMState` / `PR_RestoreVMState`, which exist for CSQC VM switching, not savegames.
- The 24008 / 17499 figures in the commit message are that whole-file `pr_crc`, printed by
  the startup provenance line (uhexen2-zixe). They prove the two images differ. They are not
  a value any load path compares.

So a mid-campaign swap would not lock the player out of their saves. It would do something
arguably worse and definitely quieter -- see the separately-filed bead on cross-variant
savegame field loss.

**The latch itself is correct and must stay.** Only its stated justification is wrong. The
real reasons a campaign has to finish on the gamecode it began with:

1. Semantic mismatch mid-run. Drop tables, item behaviour and progression differ between
   images; changing them between levels of one campaign is incoherent regardless of whether
   anything refuses to load.
2. The silent field-loss hazard, which is a genuine data-integrity risk and is the thing the
   comment was reaching for.

## What to do

Rewrite the comment in `PR_LatchGamecode` to give the two reasons above, and drop the CRC
claim. Same for the `sv_gamecode` cvar comment block above it if it repeats the claim, and
check `docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md` for the same assertion.

Keep the `file.c :: Symbol()` citation convention -- `docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md` records that
bare line numbers went stale four times in one day (uhexen2-2z1z).

No behaviour change. Comment and docs only.
acceptance_criteria: The comment gives the two real reasons (semantic mismatch, silent field loss) and drops the CRC claim; docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md checked for the same assertion. No behaviour change.
notes:
FIXED in 86902bfed. Comment only, no behaviour change.

PR_LatchGamecode's header comment now gives the two real reasons (semantic mismatch
between the images; silent savegame field loss via ED_ParseEdict/ED_FindField, cross
-referenced to uhexen2-acew) and explicitly records that there is NO savegame CRC
check, so the next reader does not restore the claim. Names where progs->crc and
pr_crc actually are consulted, and what the 24008 / 17499 figures in ebd68cc11 really
are.

The sv_gamecode cvar comment block above it does not repeat the claim -- checked, it
argues from PR_LoadProgs running per map spawn, which is correct. Left alone.

docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md checked as the bead asked: it does NOT repeat the claim.
Risk item 8 ('Savegames crossing a progs change') already describes the
skip-and-continue behaviour correctly, and the CRC discussion in F7 / risk item 10 is
about PR_LoadProgs's globals-layout switch at map load, which is real. No doc edit
needed.

file.c :: Symbol() citation convention followed (uhexen2-2z1z).
close_reason: Closed

title: Cross-variant savegames can silently lose entity state -- no field-set check between shipped progs images
description:
Found while designing the vendored-gamecode variant (see the gating decision bead). This one
is independent of that decision and is filed on its own because it is a property of shipping
more than one progs image at all, which we already do.

## The mechanism

Hexen II savegames do NOT carry a progs fingerprint. `Host_Loadgame_f`
(`engine/hexen2/host_cmd.c :: Host_Loadgame_f()`) validates only `SAVEGAME_VERSION`. Entity
state is stored as field-name/value text pairs and restored through
`ED_ParseEdict` -> `ED_FindField` (`engine/h2shared/pr_edict.c :: ED_FindField()`).

When a field named in the save does not exist in the currently loaded progs, the parser
prints `Can't find field %s` (`pr_edict.c`, in the ED_ParseEdict key loop) and skips it. The
load SUCCEEDS. The entity comes back missing that field's value.

So a save written under one gamecode image and loaded under another does not fail cleanly --
it loads with silently dropped state, behind a `Con_Printf` the player is not reading.

## Why it is latent today, and when it stops being latent

Today all three shipped/selectable images almost certainly share a field set:

- Raven's retail data1/PROGS.DAT and our build both compile against the same v1.12 progdefs
  layout; `progs->crc` is 26905 (`PROGS_V112_CRC`, `engine/hexen2/progdefs.h`) for both.
- Our own divergences are statement-level, not field-level: uhexen2-h77u is a bare `else`,
  uhexen2-qj8s a reverted glyph, uhexen2-9gdx a function parameter and a local
  initialisation. None adds or removes an entity field.

So the hazard has no live trigger right now. It acquires one the moment any shipped image
changes the field set, which is exactly what a curated third-party fork plausibly does, and
is also in scope for uhexen2-nr9l if hw/siege bundling ever lands.

Note that `progs->crc` would NOT catch it anyway: it is the progdefs *structure* CRC, and it
is only consulted by the CLASS_DEMON gate (`host_cmd.c:1355`, `sv_user.c:172,182`), never on
savegame load.

## What to do

Preferred: a build-time assertion. The bundle build already compiles every tree in one
derivation (`flake.nix`, `packages.gamecode`); extract the field table from each produced
`progs.dat` with `tools/qcdis.py` and fail the build if the shipped images disagree. That
turns a silent runtime data-loss into a build error and costs nothing at runtime.

Fallback if images legitimately need to differ: make the load path loud -- promote the
`Can't find field` line out of the per-key noise into a single end-of-load warning naming
the count, so a player who has crossed images at least sees it.

Do NOT solve this by stamping a CRC into the savegame and refusing mismatches. That breaks
loading saves made by any other engine or any mod, which is a much larger blast radius than
the problem.
acceptance_criteria: Either the build fails when shipped progs images disagree on the field set, or the load path reports dropped fields loudly enough that a player who crossed images sees it.
notes:
FIXED in cdeb34f98, via the bead's stated FALLBACK (loud load-path report) rather than its
preferred build-time assertion. Reasoning below -- the two are not substitutes and the
build-time check is still worth doing on top.

IMPLEMENTED: ED_ParseEdict (h2shared/pr_edict.c) counts every key it discards for want of a
field, exposed as ED_ResetDroppedFields()/ED_DroppedFields() (h2shared/progs.h). The savegame
loader (hexen2/host_cmd.c) resets before the edict parse loop and reports once after fclose:

  WARNING: 7 saved fields could not be restored.
  This save was written by different gamecode; some entity state is lost.

Only the savegame path consumes the counter. The identical skip during .bsp parsing is a
mapper's typo, where one line per key is already the right volume, and it stays as-is.

Still a WARNING, not a refusal -- exactly as the bead insisted. Stamping a CRC into the save
and rejecting mismatches would break saves from any other engine and from every mod.

WHY THE FALLBACK AND NOT THE BUILD-TIME ASSERTION: an assertion over the images in
packages.gamecode can only speak for what we ship. It says nothing about a player's own
progs.dat, a third-party fork, or a save carried in from another engine -- all of which reach
this same silent-loss path. The runtime report covers every one of those. It catches the
problem at load rather than at build, which is strictly later, so the build check is still
worth adding; it is now belt to this bead's braces rather than the only line of defence.

VERIFIED headless on retail data1, demo1:
  - clean save round-trip: zero warnings, no false positive
  - same save with 7 unknown keys injected after classname lines: exactly 7 counted, one
    summary line after the per-key noise
Also confirmed the plain-text form: this engine has no \x02 highlight convention in
Con_Printf (nothing else in the tree uses it), so a leading \x02 would have printed a stray
control character rather than highlighting.

STILL LATENT, as the bead said: all three currently selectable images share the v1.12
progdefs layout and our divergences from Raven are statement-level, not field-level. This is
in place for when that stops being true -- see uhexen2-2kcw and uhexen2-nr9l.
close_reason: Closed

title: Decide whether to vendor a third gamecode variant (jsHexen2) as sv_gamecode 2
description:
`ebd68cc11` (uhexen2-vbnx) shipped the Classic/Updated selector and closed with a note that
there is "room for a third value if a vendored variant is added later". This bead is that
decision, so the note stops living only in a commit message.

## What a third value would mean

`sv_gamecode` stops being a boolean and becomes a small enum:

    0 = Classic  -- the progs.dat that shipped with the player's install (Raven 1.12a)
    1 = Updated  -- built from gamecode/hc/{h2,portals} (this tree)
    2 = <vendor> -- a third-party curated tree vendored under gamecode/hc/vendor/

The candidate is KoMiKoZa/jsHexen2-progs, a curated bugfix fork of the Portal of Praevus
HexenC source. We already took its diagnosis of the `RandomMonsterGoodies` self-vs-item bug
(uhexen2-9gdx, `12dede328`), so its findings have proven load-bearing.

## The recommendation is: DO NOT, not yet

The cheaper path is the one already taken for uhexen2-9gdx -- lift upstream's *findings*
into our tree, author our own fix, record the reasoning and any deliberate divergence in
`gamecode/README` per that file's policy. That gets players the fixes with zero new engine
surface, zero new bundle layout, zero variant-labelling problem, and it is the path that has
already produced a result.

Three things argue against the vendored variant specifically:

1. **It cannot answer the question for data1.** jsHexen2-progs contains only `portals/`
   (recorded in `ebd68cc11`; re-confirm current upstream scope before acting on this).
   Most players run the base game. A menu value that silently means "same as Updated" for
   data1 and "something else" for portals is a footgun in a three-item list.

2. **It inverts `gamecode/README`'s policy for its own subtree.** That file's rule is "our
   .hc wins and every divergence from Raven gets recorded here". A vendored tree's rule has
   to be the opposite -- upstream wins, local delta is a patch that must be justified and
   ideally is empty so the tree can be re-synced. Two policies in one directory is a
   standing source of confusion unless the split is made explicit (uhexen2-VENDOR).

3. **Nobody has asked for it.** There is no field report requesting "run jsHexen2's set as a
   set". The demand so far has been for individual bugs to be fixed, which cherry-picking
   already serves.

## What would change the answer

- Upstream grows a `data1/` tree, removing objection 1 outright.
- A tester or the mission-pack community asks to run the curated set as a set, rather than
  asking for specific bugs.
- Our own cherry-picking backlog against upstream grows past the point where tracking
  individual fixes costs more than tracking a whole tree.

## Scope of the gated work

If this is decided YES, the implementation beads are already filed and blocked on it:
vendoring + provenance policy, the engine/menu/bundle enum, the coverage-hole fallback, and
a pre-ship bytecode audit. Read them before re-deriving any of this.

Two findings surfaced while designing this are filed SEPARATELY and are NOT gated -- they
are real regardless of which way this goes.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded yes/no with reasoning. If no, the four gated implementation beads are closed with that reason and gamecode/README notes that cherry-picking upstream findings is the standing policy. If yes, they are unblocked.

title: Three OIT shader programs are built on the ES tier where OIT can never run
close_reason: Fixed in the commit above. The three OIT programs are no longer built on the ES tier, where OIT_InPass() can never be true. Verified: rendering unchanged (RMSE 0.063% vs desktop, same as before) and the _oit: OK lines are gone from the ES log.

title: gl_rmain.c build warnings: a dead blend helper on both tiers, two instanced-path helpers unused on ES
description:
Four -Wunused warnings out of engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c. None is a behaviour bug — R_PolyBlend works, and the ES-only pair are simply the compiled-out instanced path's helpers — but they are noise that makes a real new warning easy to miss, which is exactly the failure mode that let uhexen2-6yh1 and uhexen2-gool live.

## Both tiers
- GL_DrawBlendPoly (gl_rmain.c:4040): 'defined but not used'. Dead duplicate. R_PolyBlend no longer calls it; it inlines the same four GL_ImmVertex3f quad, and it has to, because the helper takes no colour and depended on caller-set state. Its documented other caller, GL_DoGamma, is already sitting under '#if 0' right above it. Removing the helper leaves R_PolyBlend untouched.
- unused variable 'j' in R_CollectAndBatchAliasInstances (gl_rmain.c:2688).

## ES tier only
- R_DispatchBrushInstancedPass (gl_rmain.c:2165)
- world_surf_key_cmp (gl_rmain.c:1893)
Both are called only from inside R_DrawBrushInstanced, whose body is '#ifndef USE_GLES', so on that tier they compile to unreachable code and warn. They want the same guard as their only caller.

Confirmed by forcing a full recompile of the file on both a desktop and a -DUSE_GLES=ON build; the desktop pair reproduce without any ES involvement, so this is not new with the ES work.
close_reason: Fixed in 003e58313. GL_DrawBlendPoly (dead duplicate of the quad R_PolyBlend inlines) removed, unused 'j' dropped, and the two instanced-path helpers given the same !USE_GLES guard as their only caller. gl_rmain.c compiles warning-free on both tiers; no rendering change (ES-to-ES RMSE 0.001%).

title: GPU particle SSBO path is allocated but never drawn — and allocates an invalid buffer target on the ES tier
description:
Two findings, one block of code.

## Reachable now: invalid on the ES tier
R_GPU_Particles_Init (engine/hexen2/r_part.c) runs unconditionally from R_InitParticles and does:

    glGenBuffers(1, &gpu_particle_ssbo);
    glBindBuffer(GL_SHADER_STORAGE_BUFFER, gpu_particle_ssbo);
    glBufferData(GL_SHADER_STORAGE_BUFFER, 32768 * 32, NULL, GL_DYNAMIC_DRAW);

GL_SHADER_STORAGE_BUFFER is not a valid buffer target in WebGL2 / GLES 3.0 (SSBOs are ES 3.10), so on that tier this is two GL errors and a 1 MB buffer nothing can reach — the consuming program gl_shader_particle_gpu is already skipped there (GL_InitParticleGPUProgram is behind !USE_GLES). It also carries gpu_particle_buf[32768] = 1 MB of BSS, which on WASM is 1 MB of linear memory in the module. Fixed by building the block only on the desktop tier, with no-op stubs so r_part.h and gl_vidsdl.c's unconditional R_GPU_Particles_Shutdown call are untouched.

## The larger question, left open deliberately
The whole path is dead on EVERY tier, not just ES. grep across engine/ finds:
- gpu_particle_ssbo / gpu_particle_vao / gpu_particle_buf: written by Init, freed by Shutdown, never read or bound anywhere else
- gl_shader_particle_gpu: compiled and linked by GL_InitParticleGPUProgram, listed in GL_Shaders_Shutdown, never glUseProgram'd
- GL_ParticleGPU_SetUniforms: defined in gl_shader.c, called from nowhere

So desktop startup also reserves 1 MB of BSS, a 1 MB SSBO, a VAO and a compiled program for a renderer that does not exist yet. That is either unfinished scaffolding for a real GPU particle path or leftovers from an abandoned one, and which it is decides whether the right move is to finish it or delete it. Not guessing — leaving that to whoever knows the intent.

Surfaced by uhexen2-0py6 (-DUSE_GLES=ON desktop build).
close_reason: Closed

title: Skeletal shader is built on the ES tier despite needing an SSBO, which GLSL ES 3.00 does not have
description:
GL_Shaders_Init unconditionally calls GL_InitProgram(&gl_shader_skeletal, ...). sskeletal_vert (engine/h2shared/gl_shader.c) reads its bone matrices from

  layout(std430, binding=4) restrict readonly buffer BoneBuffer { mat3x4 bones[]; };

Shader storage blocks are GLSL ES 3.10; ES 3.00 has none, and WebGL2 has none at any version. So on the ES tier this is a guaranteed compile failure on every startup — 'Failed to load shader: skeletal' plus a full source dump to the console — and then the driver is asked to link a program from a shader it just rejected.

Harmless in the sense that nothing draws with gl_shader_skeletal yet: the PV_IQM dispatch that would invoke it is still open as uhexen2-7ok0.3, and grep finds no other reference outside gl_shader.c's own init/shutdown lists. So the fix is to not build it on the tier that cannot run it.

Whoever lands uhexen2-7ok0.3 owns the follow-on decision: give the ES tier a UBO or texture-buffer skinning path, or leave skeletal models unsupported there and skip the draw.

Surfaced by uhexen2-0py6 (-DUSE_GLES=ON desktop build).
close_reason: Closed

title: gl_farclip is registered and read by nobody — the Ironwail-named far-plane knob silently does nothing
description:
engine/h2shared/gl_sky.c:119-120 registers

    /* uhexen2 doesn't have gl_farclip, use a default value */
    cvar_t gl_farclip = {"gl_farclip", "2048", CVAR_NONE};

and no code anywhere reads it. The comment is honest about why it exists -- it was added so ported Ironwail sky code had something to compile against -- but the result is a live cvar in the console that accepts a value and ignores it.

That is the same failure shape as uhexen2-isq7: the switch answers, it just answers with no change. Worse here, because gl_farclip is the name Ironwail AND QuakeSpasm use for exactly this setting, so a tester following upstream documentation types 'gl_farclip 16384', sees it accepted, and concludes the far plane is not their problem.

WHAT ACTUALLY CONTROLS DISTANCE TODAY, and it is two different things with confusingly similar names:
  - The GL projection far plane is HARDCODED to 16384 at gl_rmain.c :: R_SetupGL(). Not tunable at all.
  - r_farclip (gl_rmain.c:127, default 4096, CVAR_ARCHIVE) is a CPU-side BSP-subtree draw-distance cull, gl_rsurf.c:2800 -- and it is not really a user setting either: gl_rmisc.c:521-524 overwrites it on every level load, 16384 for protocol >= 21 and 8192 otherwise.

FIX, per the project's Ironwail-parity default: make gl_farclip the real projection far plane and default it to 16384 so current behaviour is unchanged. CVAR_ARCHIVE, clamped at the low end so a stray small value cannot clip the player's view into uselessness. Reversed-Z is already in use when GL_ARB_clip_control is available (gl_matrix.c :: GL_Frustum), so raising it costs no depth precision.

Leave the viewmodel-FOV frustum at gl_rmain.c:3945 alone: that projection exists for the weapon model at the camera and has no business following a world draw-distance knob.

ACCEPTANCE: 'gl_farclip 4096' visibly clips distant geometry on a large map and 'gl_farclip 16384' restores it; default behaviour byte-identical to before.
close_reason: Fixed in a4bd81bc9. R_SetupGL now takes its far plane from gl_farclip instead of the hardcoded 16384, and the cvar is re-defaulted to 16384 and made CVAR_ARCHIVE, so default behaviour is byte-identical and the name finally does what Ironwail and QuakeSpasm users expect. Clamped to [4096, 262144] rather than trusted -- the low bound stops a stray small value from clipping the view into uselessness with no obvious way back, the high bound is well inside what the reversed-Z projection handles. r_farclip left alone and its comment clarified: it is a CPU-side BSP-subtree cull distance that gl_rmisc.c overwrites per level from the protocol version, not a frustum control. The viewmodel-FOV frustum in R_DrawViewModel keeps its own 16384 on purpose. Verified headless on a paused SoT Arena at three long-sightline vantages: gl_farclip 4096 removes the far half of the map (31%% and 49%% of pixels change at two of the three, visually confirmed as distant geometry going black), 16384 restores it, and a default-vs-default control pair is inside the harness's 0.04 mean-luminance noise. Found by a sweep for other cvars in the same state as uhexen2-isq7; the rest of that sweep's hits are either QuakeC-facing (read by gamecode via the cvar() builtin -- noexit, samelevel, sv_walkpitch, and the scratch/saved/temp set) or inert vestigial registrations with no user-facing surface, so no further action was taken on them.

title: MonsterDropStuff: CLASS_HENCHMAN drop table has a 10% dead zone — passes the drop gate, then drops nothing
description:
MonsterDropStuff (gamecode/hc/h2/items.hc :: MonsterDropStuff) rolls a 15% gate, then rolls `chance = random()` a second time to pick WHAT to drop. The CLASS_GRUNT and CLASS_LEADER chains both end in a bare `else`, so every value of chance selects something. The CLASS_HENCHMAN chain does not:

    else if (chance < .72) self.cnt_tome  = 1;
    else if (chance < .80) self.cnt_haste = 1;
    else if (chance < .90) self.cnt_blast = 1;
                                              <-- no else

chance in [0.90, 1.0) falls out of the chain with no field set. DropBackpack is still called, finds total == 0 and no bluemana/greenmana/spawn_health, and takes its "Nothing to put in the backpack" path: remove(item); return. The henchman drops nothing at all, silently — no dprint, nothing under developer 1.

Net effect: 15% * 10% = 1.5% of henchman kills are supposed to drop something and drop nothing.

CONFIRMED IN RETAIL BYTECODE, not just our source. tools/qcdis.py on retail data1/PROGS.DAT shows `IFNOT (chance < 0.9) -> 10078` where 10078 is the function-tail label, i.e. the same missing else. So this is Raven's, present since 1997, and not something the fork introduced. The same gap is in our rebuilt gamecode because it is a faithful build of the same source.

WHO THIS AFFECTS: monster_mezzoman is CLASS_HENCHMAN (mezzoman.hc :: monster_mezzoman) — the 'leopard' in field reports. Also every other CLASS_HENCHMAN monster.

RELATION TO uhexen2-9gdx: not the same bug, and worth keeping apart. 9gdx is the 'Bad backpack!' dprint, which is reached from DropBackpack's single-item branch. This gap returns EARLIER than that print, so it produces no message at all. But the observable symptom a player reports is the same sentence — 'leopards drop nothing' — so a field report of that shape may be this and not 9gdx. Read that one before assuming a report belongs to either.

WHAT TO DECIDE (this is the real question, the code change is three characters): whether to fix it at all. Changing `chance < .90` to a bare `else` on the blast branch redistributes 10% of henchman drops into cnt_blast, which is a balance change to Raven's tuning. The honest alternatives are (a) leave it and document it as intended-by-omission, (b) give the tail its own artifact, (c) rescale the whole chain so the 15 branches divide [0,1) evenly. Pick deliberately; do not silently widen the last branch because it is the smallest diff.

ACCEPTANCE: either the chain covers [0,1) with a recorded rationale for where the 10% went, or this is closed as accepted-vanilla with the measurement retained so the next person does not re-derive it.
close_reason: Fixed in 9a813080f. Decision: bare 'else' on the cnt_blast branch, applied to all four gamecode trees (h2, hw, portals, siege). The rationale the bead asked for -- quantified across the three chains in the same function: GRUNT is 4 branches of .25 with a terminal else and no unassigned tail; LEADER is 18 branches of .05 with a terminal else whose band is .15, i.e. Raven let the last item soak up a remainder 3x its own step rather than rescaling; HENCHMAN is 11 branches of .08, the ONLY one with an unassigned tail and the ONLY one lacking a terminal else, and its final bound is a round .90 where the .08 cadence would have put .88. That reads as an edit that stopped one keyword early, so a bare else restores the convention the siblings already follow. cnt_blast now covers [.80,1.0) at 2.5x its neighbours, the same shape as the leader's helmet at 3x. Rejected alternatives, recorded in gamecode/README: rescaling all 11 bands to 1/11 changes every outcome's odds and is a strictly larger divergence; giving the tail its own artifact invents content, since the eight artifacts absent from this table are absent on purpose per the function's own 'instant items or lesser artifacts'; and leaving it conflicts with uhexen2-9r3n and uhexen2-hwky, the same defect class (an earned drop lost with no message) in the same function. Side effect: portals' it_total+=1 had been counting the dead-zone case as a drop and is now honest. Verified in the built bytecode with tools/qcdis.py -- the henchman chain's last test is IFNOT (g1 < 0.8) and the fallthrough sets cnt_blast unconditionally; the 0.9 compare is gone. Bundle crcs move to data1 24008 / portals 17171 (were 10626 / 44043); docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md's verification table now carries a note that our-build crcs are dated by construction while the retail ones are stable. Does NOT resolve uhexen2-9gdx, which is still blocked on a console line.

title: Draw_Crosshair leaves CANVAS_CROSSHAIR active; next HUD overlay added after it silently draws off-screen
description:
Draw_Crosshair (engine/h2shared/gl_draw.c) switches to CANVAS_CROSSHAIR so scr_crosshairscale can enlarge the crosshair independently, and never switches back. It is the first call in the have_world block of SCR_UpdateScreen (engine/h2shared/gl_screen.c), so everything after it inherits that canvas unless it sets its own.

CANVAS_CROSSHAIR is a small canvas whose coordinate space is nothing like CANVAS_DEFAULT's 0..vid.width by 0..vid.height, so anything drawn at CANVAS_DEFAULT coordinates after Draw_Crosshair lands off-screen and vanishes with no error, no GL warning and nothing in the log.

FOUND: while adding SCR_DrawPointFileLabel for uhexen2-m183. The label computed a correct on-screen position (verified by instrumented print: canvas 320.0, 192.4 on a 640x480 view), Draw_String was reached with those coordinates, and nothing appeared. A fixed-position probe at (40,40) also drew nothing, which is what ruled out the projection and pointed at the canvas. Cost a debugging round. Fixed for that one call site in c293ae22a by having SCR_DrawPointFileLabel set CANVAS_DEFAULT itself.

The trap is still live for the next overlay someone adds there. The existing callers happen to survive it: SCR_DrawRam/Net/Turtle/Pause draw pics whose positions come from scr_vrect, SCR_CheckDrawCenterString and Sbar_Draw set their own canvas, and the debug readouts below are explicitly moved to CANVAS_INFO.

OPTIONS:
1. Have Draw_Crosshair restore CANVAS_DEFAULT before returning. Cheapest, and makes the block's implicit contract true. Check first whether any current caller depends on the canvas persisting.
2. Set CANVAS_DEFAULT explicitly at the top of the have_world block, after the crosshair.
3. Leave it and document the contract at the block. Weakest -- the failure mode is silent.

Note GL_SetCanvas is a no-op when the canvas is already current, so restoring is nearly free.

ACCEPTANCE: an overlay added to the have_world block that draws at CANVAS_DEFAULT coordinates without setting a canvas renders where it says it does, or the contract is loud enough that it cannot be got wrong silently.
close_reason: Resolved in 3994f87b9 — the reported mechanism does not exist. Draw_Crosshair's last statement has been GL_SetCanvas(CANVAS_DEFAULT) since d63f508aa (uhexen2-3u3g, 2026-05-05), with no return path between the CANVAS_CROSSHAIR switch and it, so the canvas is not leaked into the have_world block. Verified by rendering, not just reading: a throwaway probe drawing at CANVAS_DEFAULT (40,40) and (vid.width-120, vid.height-40) was placed in the have_world block where SCR_DrawPointFileLabel sits, without naming a canvas, and run headless (offscreen SDL + llvmpipe, demo1, crosshair 1, scr_crosshairscale 3). Both strings rendered exactly where they asked with the crosshair drawn. That IS ffdy's acceptance condition, already met. What was actually wrong was two comments asserting the leak — one of them the stated rationale for a GL_SetCanvas call — and both now say what is true. The GL_SetCanvas in SCR_DrawPointFileLabel stays (no-op when the canvas matches; keeps the function independent of call position) and Draw_Crosshair's restore is now documented as load-bearing. NOT explained: what actually made the Leak label invisible during the uhexen2-m183 work. The canvas was not it. If it recurs, do not re-run this theory.

title: Documentation describes uhexen2-xsmc design as unimplemented proposal
description:
docs/GAMECODE.md and docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md contain passages that describe the bundled-gamecode feature (uhexen2-xsmc) as a proposal-in-progress or not-yet-shipped, but the feature shipped and is live on master (three of four implementation pieces closed: uhexen2-hgi3, uhexen2-r32l, uhexen2-uwtq).

The 17f8c258c rewrite touched specific passages but left broader documentation drift intact. Both documents need review to identify all references to xsmc's lookup, bundle-loading ordering, or player-visible behaviour that presume the feature is not yet live, and update them to describe the current (shipped) state.

Related: uhexen2-2z1z tracks citation line-number drift in the same documents (a separate, more localized issue). If converting bare line numbers to file.c :: Function() style (per 2z1z suggestion), this review should be combined with that work to avoid multiple passes over the same docs.
close_reason:
Fixed in e64fd176d, combined with uhexen2-2z1z as this bead suggested (same paragraphs, one pass).

Reviewed both documents. Most of the drift this bead anticipated had already been handled by 17f8c258c's status banner ('Status: implemented ... read every we-recommend-X as X-is-what-shipped') and by GAMECODE.md's rewrite, which already describes the shipped state throughout. What was genuinely still stale:

1. F5 in BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md read 'It needs promoting to a shared Sys_GetExeDir() with per-platform backings. That is a prerequisite' and quoted soundfont.c's static exe_dir() as if it were current code. uhexen2-hgi3 did the promotion: engine/h2shared/sys_exedir.c :: Sys_GetExeDir() exists, is declared in sys.h, is compiled into both the client and h2ded, and soundfont.c calls it instead of carrying its own copy. Rewritten in past tense with the shipped location named.

2. The 'Recommendation -- Candidate B' section argued for a design without ever saying where it lives. Retitled '(this is what shipped)' and given a table mapping each design element to its symbol: PR_FindBundleDir() for discovery, PR_BundledProgsPath() for the gating predicate, PR_LoadProgs() via FS_LoadHunkFileFromOSPath() for the substitution, Sys_GetExeDir() for exedir resolution, -vanillaprogs for the opt-out, and the Gamecode: print for provenance. Verified each symbol exists.

Deliberately NOT changed: the counterfactual 'would' language throughout the Findings and Candidate A/C sections. That is reasoning about designs that were rejected, not stale tense -- rewriting it to past tense would destroy the design record this document exists to be.

title: Site: build-time static search index
description:
Add site-wide search, built at compile time and served as static files.

Once the entity reference, tutorial set and map database exist, browsing is not enough — the common query is "which entity/article covers rotating platforms" or "which maps need Portal of Praevus".

- Build-time index (Pagefind, lunr, or equivalent). No search server, no third-party search widget, no query data leaving the visitor's browser.
- Index page title, headings, body text, and the structured fields on map and entity pages.
- Results grouped by section (Modding / Reference / Maps / News / Archive).
- **JS-off fallback**: the search page must still offer the alphabetical entity index, the tag lists and the full news archive, so the site remains navigable without it.
- Keep the index small enough that it is not a multi-megabyte download on mobile; if it grows past that, split per section.

Definition of done: search returns correct results for a set of ~15 canned queries covering every section, and the JS-off fallback links are in place.

title: Long bindlist.lst labels overdraw the Key Setup key column
description: In the Key Setup menu, mod-supplied labels longer than roughly 15 characters overdraw the key-name column — labels are drawn at x=16 and the key names start at x=140. The engine's own longest label is 14 chars, so this only affects mod-supplied rows from bindlist.lst (uhexen2-7aok, commit d4b01fd39). Storage cap was deliberately left at 32 chars rather than truncating to 15, because Ironwail does not truncate and silently chopping a modder's 16-char label was judged worse than an obvious visual overlap they would notice immediately. Fix options: truncate on draw with an ellipsis, widen/reflow the label column, or scroll long labels. Cosmetic, mod-facing only.
close_reason: Fixed in 4c4620f78: M_Keys_FitLabel() truncates draw-side to 14 cols with '...'; storage cap stays 32. Verified with a standalone test over the project's strlcpy/strlcat.

title: Port remaining Ironwail pointfile leak helpers (auto-load, warning, screen label)
description: uhexen2-nwx1 ported the arrow rendering from Ironwail 26902e0e2 but deliberately left the companion pieces in that same commit out of scope: the `pointfile leak` argument with auto-load on visdata-less maps, the console leak warning, and the "Leak" screen label drawn at the path origin. These make the feature discoverable to mappers rather than requiring them to know the console command. Depends on the arrow rendering already landed in 3993cff2c.
close_reason:
Landed in c293ae22a. All three companion pieces from Ironwail 26902e0e2 that uhexen2-nwx1 left out of scope are now in.

1. `pointfile leak` argument with auto-load. R_NewMap (gl_rmisc.c) issues Cbuf_AddText("pointfile leak") when cl.worldmodel->visdata is NULL. The argument form differs from a hand-typed `pointfile` in exactly two ways: a missing .pts file is silent (a leaked map whose author has not re-run qbsp would otherwise nag on every load), and a successful load sets r_pointfile_isleak, which gates the label. A hand-typed `pointfile` deliberately gets arrows and no label -- it may be someone inspecting a stale .pts on a map that now seals, and the engine has no business calling that a leak.

2. Console leak warning. 'Warning: <map> has no visibility data -- the map leaked, or vis was never run.' Con_Printf with the 'Warning: ' prefix rather than Con_Warning, which this engine does not have; the prefix is the house style (cl_parse.c:490, snd_alsa.c:171, host_async.c:52).

3. 'Leak' screen label at the path origin. Needed a world-to-screen projection the engine did not have. R_ShowPointFile projects r_pointfile[0] through GL_GetMVP while the 3D matrices are still live and hands CANVAS_DEFAULT coordinates to SCR_DrawPointFileLabel via the new R_GetPointFileLabelPos. r_refdef.vrect is already in vid.width/vid.height space and CANVAS_DEFAULT is ortho over exactly that, so no extra scaling. Points at or behind the eye, or off-view, are dropped rather than edge-clamped, which would point at the wrong place.

Two things worth recording for whoever touches this next:

- SCR_DrawPointFileLabel sets CANVAS_DEFAULT itself instead of inheriting. Draw_Crosshair switches to CANVAS_CROSSHAIR and does not switch back, so anything drawn after it in the have_world block that assumes CANVAS_DEFAULT lands off-screen. This cost a debugging round and is a live trap for the next HUD overlay added there.

- Cbuf_AddText from R_NewMap appends after everything already buffered, so in a +exec test script the queued 'pointfile leak' runs after every remaining wait and screenshot in that script. Test scripts that want to capture the result must re-issue 'pointfile leak' by hand rather than relying on the auto-load having run.

Verified against a synthesized leaked map: meso.bsp with the visibility lump length zeroed and every dleaf2_t visofs set to -1 (the shape qbsp actually leaves behind -- zeroing the lump alone is not enough, the leaf offsets would still index a NULL visdata), plus a hand-written .pts placed in front of the player start.
- auto-load fires, warning printed, '30 points read (2 significant)' (the collinear collapse reduces the straight test path to one segment, as designed)
- screenshot confirms the red arrow and the 'Leak' label centred at the path origin and lifted clear of the arrowhead
- same map with the .pts removed: warning only, no 'couldn't open' from the auto-load, while a hand-typed 'pointfile' still prints it
- SoT cathedral (vis'd, unmodified): no warning, no pointfile activity, no errors
- nix build clean, no new warnings

title: linux-x86_64-nixos built but ships in no release zip
description: The Package step in .github/workflows/release.yml zips only linux-x86_64/; the linux-x86_64-nixos/ directory exists in .#release output but never reaches a published artifact. Pre-existing and not caused by bundled-gamecode work. Either the nixos tree is meant to be published and the workflow is missing a step, or it is build-only and the derivation is doing unnecessary work. Decide which. Note it now also carries ~2.9 MB of gamecode payload that goes nowhere.
close_reason:
DECIDED: neither published nor build-only -- the tree should not exist. Removed in fef940e01.

The decision turns on a fact worth recording: .#nixos leaves the binary's RPATH pointing at absolute /nix/store paths (sdl3, libglvnd, libogg, libvorbis, alsa-lib, fluidsynth, libxmp, opusfile AND glibc). Verified with patchelf --print-rpath on the built output. A copy of that binary in a zip is startable only on a machine that already has those exact store paths -- which no download can promise, and which another NixOS machine on a different nixpkgs pin will not have either. Adding the missing zip step would therefore have shipped a binary that fails to launch for essentially everyone; the workflow was right and the derivation was wrong.

NixOS users are served by the flake (nix run github:bobberb/hexenwail), which builds against their nixpkgs and gets resolvable rpaths. BUILD_INFO.txt now says so where the platform list used to advertise the tree.

Changes: dropped the linux-x86_64-nixos assembly from the .#release derivation; collapsed the two 'for d in linux-x86_64 linux-x86_64-nixos' loops (get_demo.sh, and the ~2.9 MB gamecode payload from uhexen2-r32l) to the one remaining Linux dir; updated docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md's packaging section and verification row K2. .github/workflows/release.yml needed no change -- it never referenced the tree.

Verified by building .#release: linux-x86_64-nixos/ absent, linux-x86_64/ still carries bin/, lib/, get_demo.sh and share/hexenwail/{data1,portals}, and BUILD_INFO.txt no longer lists a platform that is not in the zip.

FILED uhexen2-9die for what this exposed: removing the tree makes the flake the only path for NixOS users, and .#nixos installs bin/glhexen2 plus an EMPTY share/hexenwail/ -- so nix run users get no bundled gamecode and silently run Raven's 1997 progs. Cannot be fixed by copying into .#nixos's installPhase without violating r32l's constraint against referencing ${gamecode} from the engine derivation.

title: fs_gamedir_nopath is not reset by the invalid-mission-pack rollback
description:
quakefs.c:1706-1709 — when the mission pack fails validation, the rollback restores fs_gamedir and fs_userdir to data1 but leaves fs_gamedir_nopath as "portals". The engine is then in a state where it reports itself as being in portals while actually running data1.

Two known consequences: it makes Host_Game_f's 'already running' check wrong in that state (quakefs.c:1399), and any future logic keyed on fs_gamedir_nopath inherits the staleness. The uhexen2-xsmc design specifically neutralises it by ANDing fs_gamedir_nopath with a path_id check rather than trusting the name alone — but that is a workaround in one consumer, not a fix.

Found by inspection during the uhexen2-xsmc design pass, not by a user report. Pre-existing and unrelated to any change made today. Reproducing it needs a deliberately invalid/incomplete Portal of Praevus install (a truncated or wrong-CRC pak3.pak); note uhexen2-ofgb concerns the same rollback path and would likely be reproduced by the same test fixture, so the two are worth doing together.
close_reason:
Fixed in 5ee1fe56e, using the same fixture as uhexen2-ofgb exactly as this bead suggested.

REPRODUCED. Scratch install with data1 symlinked from retail and portals/pak3.pak replaced by 4 KB of urandom. Note this needs the GL CLIENT, not h2ded: Host_Game_f is inside #if !defined(SERVERONLY), so the dedicated server has no 'game' command to print with. Also note a minimal scratch tree needs a hexen.rc containing 'stuffcmds' or the +commands never execute at all.

  glhexen2 -basedir <scratch> -portals +game
    before: 'Current game directory: portals'
    after:  'Current game directory: data1'

while the search path in both cases contains only data1 -- the rollback had already removed both portals entries.

SECOND CONSEQUENCE, the one the bead named, also confirmed and fixed. On the same broken install:

  glhexen2 -basedir <scratch> -portals +game portals
    before: 'Already running: portals'  -- the engine refuses a gamedir switch that is not redundant, so a player whose mission pack failed validation cannot switch into it even after fixing the install mid-session
    after:  no such message, the switch proceeds

FIX: the rollback now resets all three of fs_gamedir_nopath, fs_gamedir and fs_userdir, matching Host_Game_f's own reset-to-data1 block (quakefs.c, the 'reset gamedir tracking to data1' arm) line for line, including the qerr_strlcpy form. The rollback had the last two and was missing the first.

NO REGRESSION: a valid mission pack still reports 'Current game directory: portals'. nix build .# succeeds.

On the xsmc workaround this bead mentions: PR_BundledProgsPath ANDs fs_gamedir_nopath with a path_id check rather than trusting the name. That is still correct and is left alone -- it defends against more than this one staleness. What changes is that a future consumer no longer needs to invent its own defence.

title: Print loaded progs.dat and source at startup
description:
With bundling (uhexen2-8qp3), "which gamecode is this player running?" becomes a question on every bug report, and the answer is currently invisible — the only report is a Con_DPrintf in pr_edict.c :: PR_LoadProgs() requiring developer 1. A tester with a stale or half-installed progs looks identical to one on retail.

This is a live failure mode, not hypothetical: docs/GAMECODE.md warns that installing progs.dat without progs2.dat leaves the game on new gamecode for most maps and Raven's 1997 gamecode for the rest — "a mismatch that will not announce itself."

APPROVED AS STANDALONE CHANGE: deliberately separate from uhexen2-8qp3, so that the bundling work keeps its proven "gamecode changes leave the engine input hash untouched" property.

SCOPE: one Con_Printf line at startup naming the loaded progs, its source path if the filesystem layer can supply it, and its CRC. Observability only, with no change to load behavior.
close_reason:
PROVENANCE TURNED OUT TO BE GENUINELY REACHABLE, so no fallback to name-and-CRC was needed. FS_LoadHunkFile's second parameter is only a path_id — a per-gamedir bitmask, not a path — and it cannot distinguish a pak from a loose file within the same gamedir, which is exactly the retail-versus-installed distinction that matters here. The real information lives in FS_OpenFile_Internal(), which already holds the winning searchpath_t (pack->filename or the resolved ospath). It was recorded there — one point of truth, no duplicated search logic — deliberately rather than adding a second resolver that could drift from the search order currently being redesigned under uhexen2-xsmc.

IMPLEMENTATION: new static fs_lastfile_source[MAX_OSPATH] (quakefs.c:584), set on a pak hit (:882) and on a loose-file hit (:908), cleared on lookup failure (:927), exposed via new FS_LastFileSource() (:932, declared with a contract comment at quakefs.h:104). pr_edict.c:2074,2089 capture it immediately after FS_LoadHunkFile; the new deduplicated Con_Printf is at :2190.

CRC CHOICE — worth recording, it corrects a natural assumption. The number the pre-existing Con_DPrintf printed as "crc" is progs->crc, the progdefs interface CRC, which only ever takes three values (14046 / 38488 / 26905) because PR_LoadProgs Host_Errors on anything else — so it is fully implied by the progvstr already on the line and discriminates nothing. The useful discriminator is pr_crc, the whole-file CRC, which is also what the server already advertises as "SERVER (N CRC)". Verified against the install: retail data1 = 17499 and retail portals = 20799, matching the figures from the earlier uhexen2-zmb3 precedence work. The old developer line was relabelled "progdefs crc" so the two numbers do not read as contradicting each other.

RUNTIME CASES (headless, offscreen SDL + llvmpipe, against a scratch copy):
- Gamecode: progs.dat from <base>/data1/PROGS.DAT (H2/v1.11, file crc 17499)
- Gamecode: progs.dat from <base>/portals/progs.dat (H2MP/v1.12, file crc 20799)
- Gamecode: progs.dat from <base>/sot/progs.dat (H2MP/v1.12, file crc 28154)

Two details worth keeping: -game sot also pulls portals/ into the search path, and the line shows sot's progs winning — resolving an ambiguity that otherwise needs developer 1. And the data1 case renders PROGS.DAT in uppercase, which is the case-insensitive loose-file fallback reporting the real on-disk name — itself a useful Linux-install diagnostic.

progs2.dat IS COVERED, just not at engine init. It is chosen per-map via maplist.txt, so it cannot be known at startup. Because repeats are suppressed, a session logs one line plus one more at each genuine change. A four-map run (demo1 demo2 meso9 romeric6) produced exactly two lines — progs.dat crc 17499, then progs2.dat crc 33075 at the transition. That is the docs/GAMECODE.md half-install case announcing itself, which was the whole point of the bead.

NO LOAD-BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: no searchpath, ordering or selection logic touched — important because uhexen2-xsmc is redesigning exactly that. -nostdout needs no special handling; it is enforced in Sys_Printf below Con_Printf. h2ded prints the identical line.

VALIDATION: nix build .#default and .#h2ded both PASS, zero diagnostics in the changed files (the three fread -Wunused-result warnings in quakefs.c are pre-existing and outside the diff hunks). The engine's nix input hash changes, as expected for engine source.

TWO DELIBERATE CALLS, both trivially reversible if disliked: (1) the dedup honours "one line at startup" and turns the progs.dat → progs2.dat transition into the signal, at the cost that in a very long session the line may scroll out of a condump; (2) relabelling the existing Con_DPrintf is slightly beyond "add one line", but without it developer 1 shows two different numbers both called "crc".

API NOTE for future callers: FS_LastFileSource() has last-call-wins semantics like fs_filesize. Documented in the header; PR_LoadProgs copies it immediately, and any future caller must do the same.

Testing used a copied tree with paks symlinked plus bwrap to redirect the ~/.hexen2 userdir. /home/josh/hexen2 was verified untouched afterwards — md5s of all four progs.dat files unchanged and find -newermt showing zero writes. This is the protocol established after the uhexen2-8qp3 incident where cp through symlinks damaged the retail install.

Landed on master: f619026e1 (feat(engine): report loaded gamecode and its source path at startup)

title: Audit hw/siege gamecode against reference HexenWorld bytecode, then decide on bundling
description:
uhexen2-8zia audited gamecode/hc/h2 and gamecode/hc/portals against retail progs.dat using a disassembler (qcdis.py, tools/qcdis.py, landed e6dd815f1 with v6 unsigned-operand fix). That audit established the precedence chain and verified our changes are real (not compiler noise).

**gamecode/hc/hw and gamecode/hc/siege could not be audited** — no retail HexenWorld hwprogs.dat exists on the dev box to compare against. No baseline = no way to classify divergences as upstream-fix / deliberate-fork-change / unreverted-accident / Raven-source-differs-from-shipped-bytecode.

That gap is why uhexen2-8qp3 ships data1 + portals only. HexenWorld players keep running whatever they have today.

**What this needs:**

1. **Obtain reference bytecode.** 
   - uHexen2 distributes gamedata tarballs (gamedata-all-*.tgz) which historically carry compiled progs
   - Upstream also ships binary packages (look for hwprogs.dat or siege/progs.dat)
   - Failing that, a HexenWorld install from any source would do
   - Record where it came from and its provenance (Raven's own release, a third-party archive, etc.)

2. **Re-run the uhexen2-8zia audit method** against hw and siege trees.
   - Use tools/qcdis.py with the v6 unsigned-operand fix (see tools/README.md for invocation)
   - Method: tier 1 function symbol table (names, numparms, locals), tier 2 per-function opcode stream over [first_statement, next_function_start)
   - Classify each divergence as:
     (a) upstream uHexen2 fix (document which one)
     (b) deliberate fork change (document the bd issue and commit)
     (c) unreverted accident (like uhexen2-qj8s)
     (d) Raven's source differing from Raven's own shipped bytecode (harmless unless it breaks CRC/savegame)
   - Track: function count, shared count, byte-identical count, opcode-differing count (see uhexen2-8zia's results table as template)

3. **Then decide** whether to extend uhexen2-8qp3's bundle to hw/siege.
   - If audit finds only (a) upstream fixes and (b) documented deliberate changes: likely OK to bundle
   - If audit finds (c) unreverted accidents (like TimeBomb in h2): decision required per issue
   - If (d) dominates: probably safe but CRC/savegame implications need checking
   - Record the decision in uhexen2-8qp3's scope notes

**Known facts already in scope (audit should confirm or correct):**

- gamecode/hc/hw/invntory.hc is Raven's **untouched** HexenWorld source since 2004 import (7282897f9), including a TimeBombThink that orbits the owner at radius 90 with a 10-second fuse from proj_ofs — different from both retail h2 and the fork's h2 version (TimeBombBoom). Whether that matches shipped HexenWorld bytecode is exactly the open question.

- a14b5eecd expanded the DropBackpack "Bad backpack!" dprint into a five-call dump in **all four** trees including hw and siege — see uhexen2-o4tn (undecided fork gamecode present in these trees). Audit will reveal whether that matches any shipped build.

- packages.gamecode already builds both trees and they compile clean (hw/hwprogs.dat 953380 B, siege/hwprogs.dat 796276 B), so nothing is blocked on the build — only on having something to check them against.

**Known TimeBomb status in hw and siege (from re-verification 2026-08-13):**

The re-verification established that TimeBombExplode and TimeBombThink are present in the hw and siege trees (just as in h2 and portals), and TimeBombBoom is absent from them. This is structurally similar to the h2 situation but the context differs: gamecode/hc/hw/invntory.hc has carried untouched Raven HexenWorld source since the 2004 import, so a TimeBombThink in hw is potentially correct (Raven's original design for HexenWorld). The audit will determine whether shipped HexenWorld bytecode carries TimeBombThink/TimeBombExplode or TimeBombBoom, and whether TimeBombThink's orbit-owner radius-90 logic matches what players actually experience.

**Related work:**
- uhexen2-8zia: the method and results for h2/portals (reference for this scope)
- uhexen2-8qp3: the bundling task this audit unblocks
- uhexen2-o4tn: undecided fork gamecode (DropBackpack debug spam in all four trees)
- uhexen2-onfa: HexenWorld client port (adjacent HexenWorld work)

title: gamecode/README has never been updated in the fork era
description:
gamecode/README documents Raven's changes up to 2022-06-12 (version 1.29c). It has not been updated since this fork began, despite five commits that modify .hc source files during the fork era.

Fork-era changes not documented:
1. fcf9638ba — dead code removal (fablade.hc frame_BLADE, ravenai.hc dead functions)
2. fd1ac9ee6 — unused constants (IT_SHOTGUN, UPDATE_*, attck_cnt)
3. ab24f9519 — create_swarm dead code
4. 1ebcc230c — CheckJump parameter reduction
5. 7ff652502 — eidolon_enemy function added

Additionally, documented fork changes in the commit messages (e9731510a, fe1f2bdc1, bb570666a) were never added.

This violates the project's stated policy: "our .hc wins, and divergences get documented." The documentation half has never been executed. When uhexen2-8zia audited all divergences, the audit had to read diffs manually because README was not kept in sync.

For the next person auditing gamecode provenance, or for players asking why our progs differs from retail, README should be the reference. Add entries documenting all five fork-era .hc commits so the divergence record is written.

Related: uhexen2-8zia (audit that exposed this gap).
close_reason:
Done in b7558eab1. gamecode/README now carries a 'Hexenwail fork (diverges from 1.29c)' section above a 'uHexen2 / Raven history' section, with an entry per fork-era gamecode commit describing which trees (h2/hw/portals/siege) each touched and what changed, read from the diffs rather than the commit messages.

CORRECTION to this bead's premise: the five commits it listed as fork-era are all upstream uHexen2 work, not ours -- fcf9638ba is 2013-08-05, fd1ac9ee6 2022-04-30, ab24f9519 2011-07-03, 1ebcc230c 2012-01-15, 7ff652502 2011-06-17. fcf9638ba in fact already updated gamecode/README itself. The fork begins at a14b5eecd (2026-03-21), and 'git log --since=2023 -- gamecode/hc' gives the true set of six: a14b5eecd, e9731510a, d39212a12 (all 2026-03), fe1f2bdc1, bb570666a, ce8c9d1c4 (2026-08).

Reading the diffs rather than the messages mattered: e9731510a's message lists five portals fixes but the diff also carries the TimeBomb change, and d39212a12's message is entirely about centerprint plaques while its diff also rewrote the glyph to orbit on a 5s fuse. That undocumented change is exactly how the glyph divergence survived until uhexen2-qj8s caught it. Both are now recorded, cross-referenced to the ce8c9d1c4 revert.

Bracketed bead ids (uhexen2-qj8s, -9r3n, -hwky) are included in the entries so the full investigation is one 'bd show' away.

title: h2ded cannot run SoT — unimplemented builtin 'pimpmodel' aborts server start
description:
The dedicated server cannot load Storm Over Thyrion at all. It fails with 'unimplemented builtin' on 'pimpmodel' (from misc_modelpimper.hc), then 'Host_Error: Program error'. This is pre-existing and unrelated to uhexen2-nnwb.1; it was found while trying to use h2ded for headless mod-content testing.

IMPACT: h2ded is unusable for mod-content headless testing, which matters because the dedicated server is otherwise the cheapest way to run map/monster/physics investigations without a renderer. Every SoT investigation so far has had to use the full client with SDL offscreen + llvmpipe instead.

CONTEXT: Both this issue and uhexen2-3coq (closed today) document instances where h2ded deliberately diverges from the client — 3coq noted that h2ded compiles out Mod_ForName for alias models under SERVERONLY. The pimpmodel builtin is a different gap, but both are instances of the dedicated build diverging from the client in ways that only surface when someone tries to actually use it. Worth checking whether other builtins are similarly missing from the SERVERONLY build rather than fixing just this one.
notes: Close note correction: '(status/say работают)' should read '(status/say work)' — stray non-English word in the close reason, no bearing on the fix.
close_reason: Fixed in a7a9c1573: PF_pimpmodel now compiles under SERVERONLY as a return-value-only stub (render state skipped, Mod_FindName avoided); slot 111 no longer PF_Fixme. Audited the rest of the table — 111 was the only client/dedicated divergence. Verified h2ded -game sot +map demo1 reaches a live server (status/say работают).

title: portals gamedir added twice to search path when -game <mod> is used
description:
While confirming progs.dat precedence for uhexen2-zmb3, the portals gamedir was found to be added to the search path TWICE for -game <mod> invocations.

MECHANISM (quakefs.c):
- Line 1677 adds portals because check_portals was set by the mere presence of -game
- Lines 1741-1745 add it AGAIN, because that guard only checks that the mod is not literally named "portals"

IMPACT (minor but real):
- Extra file descriptor
- Duplicate pak3.pak hash table in memory
- Phantom path entry
- Wasted path_id bit (finite resource used for gamedir-scoped lookups)

The path_id waste is the part most likely to matter later, since those bits are a finite resource.

CONTEXT:
Found by inspection during zmb3 precedence trace, not a user report. Unrelated to the (correct) behaviour whereby a mod with no progs of its own falls through to the Mission Pack's progs rather than data1's.
close_reason:
FIXED in commit fc9724cb9 ("fix(fs): stop adding portals to the search path twice").

MECHANISM: Introduced a new local `qboolean portals_in_path = false;` in FS_Init (quakefs.c:1510). Set to true via an `else` on the step-2 portals add (lines 1711-1714), so it only triggers when the mission-pack rollback did NOT run. The second add at lines 1741-1750 is now guarded by `check_portals && !portals_in_path && q_strcasecmp(...)`.

WHY THE SECOND ADD WAS REDUNDANT: FS_Gamedir (quakefs.c:505) only frees searchpaths down to fs_base_searchpaths, which is set *after* the step-2 portals add (line 1725). So the second add was unconditionally redundant — except in the edge case of an invalid mission-pack install, where step 2 rolls back, and the flag remains false so the second add still fires (now an intentional fallback).

VALIDATION: 
- Build: 0 errors, 0 new warnings (three pre-existing warn_unused_result on fread() at quakefs.c:297, 330, 1063 are untouched and outside FS_Init).
- Runtime against /home/josh/hexen2 headless:
  - `-game sot` before: portals/pak3.pak (245 files) added twice with the 3-line block duplicated. After: once. Diff is exactly that block + one Added packfile line.
  - Plain launch (no `-game`, data1 only): byte-identical, portals absent.
  - `-game portals`: byte-identical, portals once (pre-existing q_strcasecmp guard).
  - Mod content sanity: `sot` identical both sides — progs CRC 45360, 341 models precached, maps/keep_demo.bsp, same lightmap/VBO counts, demo plays complete.
- Mission-pack fallthrough (critical constraint): tested with synthetic mod dir (no progs.dat), basedir symlinked to real data1/portals so user install untouched. Progs CRC 20799 (portals') both before and after. Control `-noportals` gives CRC 17499 (data1's), proving fallthrough really reaches Mission Pack and depends on portals being present.

INCIDENTAL FINDING: -noportals launch gives data1's progs CRC 17499, versus 20799 for Mission Pack. Relevant to uhexen2-zmb3's progs precedence documentation in docs/GAMECODE.md.
