title: sv_debugmovestep: dump nearby SOLID_BSP movers at CheckBottom failure
description:
sv_debugmovestep currently prints failure reasons, monster classname/origin, and touched entity classname — but NOT the surrounding movers. This is the missing piece that distinguishes real nnwb repros from false positives.

WHY: The nnwb investigation established the mover geometry dump is essential. During the Arena e1 yakman check, the movestep log showed 295 failures oscillating in place beside a func_train_mp — all symptoms of the reported bug. But a temporary probe printing mover absmin/absmax revealed the "platform" was actually a 258-unit-tall elevator car (shaft-filling brush), and it was stationary. Refusing to step onto its side is correct behaviour, not a bug. Without the mover dump, the next person burns the same time on the same false positive. The note states plainly that printing each mover's real absmin/absmax "is the only reliable way to tell a platform from a car (the BSP submodel lump is not straightforward to read for this)".

WHAT: Extend SV_CheckBottom's trace.fraction==1.0 failure logging to enumerate every SOLID_BSP mover within ~256 units of the failing landing spot. For each mover, print classname, origin, and real absmin/absmax bounds.

HOW: Stay print-only, gated behind the sv_debugmovestep cvar (default 0, silent). No behaviour change when off — same pattern as the existing eight instrumented paths and as r_dlightinfo. Making it permanent and cvar-gated prevents the temp-probe-and-delete cycle that caused working-tree confusion.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- sv_debugmovestep N on a map with movers prints, for each CheckBottom failure, the nearby SOLID_BSP movers with classname/origin/absmin/absmax
- Default-off produces no output and no behaviour change
- Engine builds clean
- Concrete next use: Arena has 27 func_train_mp; plat1 at 2144 -1496 64 has 7 monsters within 512u including a monster_archer at 96u and is named like a platform — a candidate for the thin-in-z, horizontally-travelling mover that a REAL nnwb repro needs
close_reason:
IMPLEMENTATION: new DEBUGMOVESTEP_MOVER_RADIUS (256) and SV_DebugMoveStep_DumpMovers() at sv_move.c:60, walking sv.edicts from index 1 (skipping worldspawn), keeping non-free SOLID_BSP entities whose abs box is within 256u of the failing foot on all three axes, printing classname/origin/absmin/absmax. Called at sv_move.c:225 (after the midpoint-trace failure log) and sv_move.c:288 (after the corner failure log).

PLACEMENT RATIONALE: the dump went on SV_CheckBottom's two return false sites rather than the SV_movestep 'CheckBottom failed at landing pos' site. Those two are the only ways CheckBottom can fail, so this covers every caller — including SV_NewChaseDir — with no double-printing, since the movestep-level log is always preceded by one of them.

OUTPUT FORMAT MATCHES THE HISTORIC PROBE character-for-character on the org= and abs= fields.

VALIDATION: nix-builder PASS (0 errors, 0 warnings in the changed file); .#h2ded (SERVERONLY) also PASS, so the new code is safe in the dedicated half. Runtime-exercised on Arena (SoT) headless, 250 frames, no player input. Three A/B runs on an identical script prove the budget is genuinely shared and truncates mid-event rather than overrunning: sv_debugmovestep 0 → 0 lines; 200 → 40 lines (20 reason + 20 mover); 5 → exactly 5, where the fifth is a reason line whose mover dump was correctly suppressed.

LANDED ON MASTER: commit f18bd4957 - 'feat(sv): dump nearby SOLID_BSP movers on CheckBottom failure'

title: gitignore: .beads/ shadowed bd's own ignore file and broke auto-export staging
description:
Root .gitignore ignored the .beads/ DIRECTORY. git add refuses any path under an ignored directory even when the file itself is tracked and matches no ignore rule, so bd's post-command auto-export ended every single bd invocation with 'Warning: auto-export: git add failed: exit status 1' and .beads/issues.jsonl had to be staged by hand with 'git add -u'.

Fixed by ignoring the contents instead: '.beads/*' plus '!.beads/issues.jsonl'. Directory stays visible so the negation is reachable; everything else (dolt db, server pid/log/port, ephemeral sqlite, backup/) stays ignored. Nothing new becomes tracked.

Note for later: bd ships its own .beads/.gitignore designed to run with the directory visible, and it deliberately contains no negations. Git never descended far enough to read it. Removing the root rule entirely would let bd's file govern and would newly track config.yaml, metadata.json, README.md and the .gitignore itself — all checked, no secrets — but that adds files nobody asked for, so it was left alone.
close_reason: Fixed: root .gitignore now uses '.beads/*' + '!.beads/issues.jsonl'. Verified — 'bd create' ran with no 'auto-export: git add failed' warning and staged .beads/issues.jsonl on its own; all 17 other entries under .beads/ still report ignored; no new untracked files.

title: Dedicated server gives alias entities different implicit bounds than the listen server
description:
PF_setmodel (engine/h2shared/pr_cmds.c:327-330) applies mod->mins/mod->maxs to EVERY model type, alias included, not just brush models. So whatever the model loader computed becomes the entity physics box until the progs calls setsize.

The two builds compute it differently:
- Client / listen server uses gl_model.c, which sets alias bounds to geometry +/-10 (gl_model.c:3323 and :3515, with Quake"s +/-16 commented out above under a "FIXME: do this right"). Spoike checked the original Hexen II source release on Discord 2026-08-13 and confirms +/-10 is what Raven specified, so this path is correct.
- Dedicated server swaps in sv_model.c, described in engine/CMakeLists.txt:677 as a "BSP-only replacement for gl_model.c". It has no alias path at all, so alias entities get no geometry-derived box there.

Effect: progs that rely on setmodel"s implicit sizing rather than calling setsize afterwards will size entities differently under h2ded than under a listen server. Well-written progs always setsize after setmodel with an mdl, so this is latent rather than active -- but it is exactly the buggy-vs-non-buggy-mod split Spoike described, and mods are where we keep getting bitten.

Also stale, worth cleaning while in here: engine/h2shared/model.c carries the same alias-bounds code WITHOUT the +/-10 (model.c:2215-2219 and :2483-2487), a third and different answer. It is not referenced anywhere in engine/CMakeLists.txt, so it is dead code -- confirm and remove, or bring it in line.

NOT urgent and NOT to be "fixed" reflexively: changing engine-side entity sizing is what caused uhexen2-4p8t. Establish first whether any shipped map or mod actually depends on the implicit alias box before touching it.
acceptance_criteria: Documented answer to whether h2ded and the listen server agree on alias entity bounds, with evidence. If they must be reconciled, the change is justified against real mod behaviour rather than symmetry. model.c is either removed as dead or made consistent.
close_reason:
ANSWER: no, they do not agree. Listen server gives an alias entity the mesh extents padded by ±10 per axis. h2ded gives it '0 0 0' / '0 0 0' — a zero-size point.

THE CHAIN:
1. engine/CMakeLists.txt:677 — h2ded compiles sv_model.c in place of gl_model.c; :699 compiles it SERVERONLY.
2. engine/h2shared/pr_cmds.c:2222 — sv.models[i] = Mod_ForName(s, true); inside PF_precache_model is wrapped in #ifndef SERVERONLY. Same at :2278 for PF_precache_puzzle_model.
3. engine/hexen2/sv_main.c:2419 → Host_ClearMemory() → engine/hexen2/server/host.c:517 memset(&sv, 0, sizeof(sv)), so sv.models[] starts NULL.
4. engine/hexen2/sv_main.c:2513 and :2529 fill only the worldmodel (index 1) and the inline BSP submodels *1..*N, unguarded — so brush models are identical on both builds.
5. Therefore on h2ded sv.models[i] stays NULL for every progs-precached .mdl, and PF_setmodel (pr_cmds.c:325-330) takes the SetMinMaxSize(e, vec3_origin, vec3_origin, true) branch.

KEY FINDING: sv_model.c does not merely lack an alias path. Mod_LoadModel (sv_model.c:190-224) calls Mod_LoadBrushModel unconditionally, with none of the RAPOLYHEADER/IDPOLYHEADER/IDSPRITEHEADER dispatch that gl_model.c:363-378 has. A .mdl reaching it would Host_Error out (sv_model.c:1113). It never fires only because step 2 removes the call. The two guards are load-bearing on each other.

NOT RECONCILED, deliberately. Reconciling means growing every alias entity's box from a point to mesh-extents on h2ded — the exact class of change that caused uhexen2-4p8t. It would also force h2ded to load and retain every .mdl, which is the cost SERVERONLY exists to avoid.

DEAD CODE REMOVED: engine/h2shared/model.c (2877 lines) was genuinely dead — no GLOB anywhere in the build system. It had been touched by 5 recent commits maintaining a file nothing compiled. Its orphaned header engine/h2shared/model.h was removed too in 5706ece1f.

DOCS: new section "Alias model bounds: h2ded vs. the listen server" in docs/SrcNotes.txt, plus a WHY comment at the hazard point in engine/h2shared/pr_cmds.c:325.

VALIDATION: nix build (client) PASS; nix build .#h2ded PASS — the latter is the one that matters, proving model.c was unreferenced.

Landed as a85ca76eb ("docs(server): record the h2ded vs listen-server alias bounds split") + 5706ece1f ("chore(engine): remove orphaned model.h alongside model.c").

title: Root-cause the 'Bad backpack!' fallthrough — field reports on archers and leopards
description:
uhexen2-hwky was closed on its second acceptance branch (make the fallthrough non-destructive) with the root cause explicitly unresolved. Field reports have continued, so tracking the remaining half here.

REPORTS (Tome of Power Abuser, Discord 2026-08-12/13, on 0.7.9-beta.r11):
- Knight archers on blackmarsh
- Leopards, "too"

Note these are DIFFERENT drop tables, which argues against one simple cause:
- monster_archer is CLASS_GRUNT (gamecode/hc/h2/archer.hc:730). MonsterDropStuff gives a grunt only greenmana, bluemana, both, or spawn_health (items.hc:1258-1275).
- "Leopard" is the mezzoman: monster_mezzoman is CLASS_HENCHMAN and monster_werepanther is CLASS_LEADER (mezzoman.hc:1515-1523). Leaders roll the full table -- all 14 artifacts plus the four armor pieces.

ANALYSIS SO FAR (no repro): every field MonsterDropStuff can set for CLASS_GRUNT, CLASS_HENCHMAN or CLASS_LEADER is covered by the dispatch chain in DropBackpack, so the fallthrough cannot be derived from the drop tables alone. The accumulated set and dispatched set are identical (19 fields, established in uhexen2-hwky). That still points at a value-level mismatch or a field mutated between accumulation and dispatch, or at the message coming from a different entity than the reporter assumes.

BLOCKED ON TWO THINGS:
1. The exact console line. The dprint prints classname and origin (items.hc:1692-1695), which identifies the failing entity directly. Requested from the reporter, not yet supplied.
2. uhexen2-zmb3. BadBackpackDump() -- which prints "total" and every nonzero inventory field, and exists specifically to answer this -- only runs from rebuilt gamecode. Testers on retail progs.dat cannot produce it, so no amount of "developer 1" from the field will help until we ship a progs.dat.

Do not re-derive the triage in uhexen2-hwky; read it first.
acceptance_criteria: A repro, or a console line naming the failing entity, that explains how DropBackpack reaches its final else. Either the dispatch chain is corrected so no fallthrough occurs, or the fallthrough is shown to be unreachable for shipped gamecode and this is closed with the analysis retained.
notes:
2026-08-14 ANALYSIS PASS (still blocked on the console line; do not re-derive this):

1. RETAIL BYTECODE NOW CHECKED. The earlier triage in uhexen2-hwky established the accumulated set == dispatched set from OUR .hc source. That left open whether the testers' retail progs.dat differs, which matters because the reports (2026-08-12/13, 0.7.9-beta.r11) predate uhexen2-zmb3 and so ran the tester's own install's gamecode, not ours. Disassembled retail data1/PROGS.DAT with tools/qcdis.py: DropBackpack is structurally identical to our source — same 19 accumulated fields, same 23-way dispatch chain in the same order, same four-disjunct single-item gate. The only difference is retail's fallthrough is 'dprint; remove(item); self = old_self; return' with one bare message and no entity info, which is why the reporters cannot supply a classname. So the divergence theory is dead: whatever reaches the final else reaches it in Raven's bytecode too.

2. NO MONSTER-SIDE WRITER OF THE DROP FIELDS. Grepped every gamecode/hc/h2/*.hc for 'self.<field> =' across all 19 accumulated fields plus spawn_health. Only artifact.hc and invntory.hc write cnt_* and both are player-side artifact use. Nothing outside items.hc writes armor_amulet/bracer/breastplate/helmet or spawn_health. So for a monster death the only fields in play are the ones MonsterDropStuff just set, and retail DropBackpack zeroes all 22 on self at the end. Pre-existing monster state is not the mechanism.

3. A NEAR MISS THAT IS NOT THIS BUG — see uhexen2-h77u. CLASS_HENCHMAN's drop chain ends at 'chance < .90' with no else, so 10% of the time it sets nothing and DropBackpack returns via its 'Nothing to put in the backpack' path. That is a genuine bug (filed separately, confirmed in retail bytecode) and it makes a mezzoman — the 'leopard' — drop nothing. It produces NO message, so it is not the Bad backpack! report, but a player reporting 'leopards drop nothing' could be describing either. Check h77u before assuming a new report belongs here.

STILL BLOCKED, unchanged: need the console line naming the failing entity, from a tester running our progs.dat (now shippable since uhexen2-zmb3).
close_reason: Root cause found and fixed in 12dede328 (portals tree). RandomMonsterGoodies rolled the loot onto self, the corpse, but DropBackpack finishes copying self -> item before calling it and never copies again, so the drop went out empty while 'total' claimed an artifact -- straight into the 'Bad backpack!' fallthrough. Also initialises it_total, which HexenC leaves holding the previous caller's value. Diagnosis credited to KoMiKoZa/jsHexen2-progs 22b5c8a; recorded in gamecode/README. The h2/hw/siege trees do not have the defect -- there the roll runs before the copy.

title: Sky set before cl.worldmodel exists is never recorded for per-map recall
description:
Found while validating uhexen2-7gl5 on 2026-08-12.

Sky_RememberForMap (engine/h2shared/gl_sky.c) opens with:

    if (!cl.worldmodel || !cl.worldmodel->name[0])
        return;

which is correct in isolation — there is no map name to key the memory on — but it means a Sky_LoadSkyBox that succeeds before the client has the world model silently records nothing, and the sky is then NOT recalled on a later revisit to that map. The skybox itself loads and displays; only the per-map memory is skipped, so the failure is invisible until hub travel.

Observed directly: a test script that issued 'sky testsky_' four frames after 'map demo1' ran the command before the client received serverinfo (console log shows the skybox faces loading at line 93, 'Blackmarsh' serverinfo at 116, CL_SignonReply at 127). On returning to demo1 the sky was gone. The same script with the command issued after signon recalls correctly, 2 for 2.

Whether a real mod can hit this is unconfirmed. A stuffcmd from a QC spawn function lands in the signon buffer, which the client parses after CL_ParseServerInfo has set cl.worldmodel, so the common case looks safe. Reachable-looking cases worth checking: a 'sky' line in a mod autoexec.cfg or config.cfg (runs at init, before any map — arguably correct to ignore), and anything that sets sky from a connect-time path.

Matters because it is the one way the uhexen2-7gl5 fix can still appear not to work in the field. If JakubM reports the skybox still disappearing on hub travel after the fix ships, check this first: have him set the sky, revisit, and report what 'sky' with no argument prints.

Possible hardening if a real case turns up: defer the record — stash the pending name and flush it into the map memory at the end of Sky_NewMap once cl.worldmodel is known.
close_reason:
Not reachable from the path that matters. Closing on code-path evidence rather than a change.

The concern was that Sky_RememberForMap bails when cl.worldmodel is absent, so a sky set at that moment is silently not recorded for per-map recall. That is true as a code property, but the mod mechanism uhexen2-7gl5 is about cannot hit it:

  - cl.worldmodel is assigned at cl_parse.c:622 INSIDE CL_ParseServerInfo ('cl_entities[0].model = cl.worldmodel = cl.model_precache[1];'), immediately before R_NewMap.
  - svc_serverinfo is the first message of the signon, so everything else in the stream is parsed after that assignment.
  - svc_stufftext does not even execute inline — cl_parse.c:1517 is 'Cbuf_AddText (MSG_ReadString ())', so a mod's stuffcmd("sky foo\n") runs at the next Cbuf_Execute in the host frame, later still.

So a stuffcmd-set sky always lands with cl.worldmodel valid and is recorded. Same for the svc_skybox path added in 08f5818d5, which is parsed later in the same signon message.

The between-maps window is also fine, and fine by design: Host_ClearMemory memsets cl at the start of SV_SpawnServer, so cl.worldmodel is NULL rather than stale, and a sky command arriving then has no map to be keyed against. Skipping the record is the correct behaviour, not a bug — Sky_NewMap will set the sky from the new map's worldspawn moments later regardless.

What actually produced the observation: a test cfg issuing 'sky testsky_' four frames after 'map demo1', i.e. from the console while the client had not yet parsed serverinfo. Console commands can interleave with connection setup in a way stuffcmds cannot, so that is a harness artifact — the same class as uhexen2-y3i5. The console log ordering in that run (skybox faces at line 93, 'Blackmarsh' serverinfo at 116, CL_SignonReply at 127) is what the original report was based on.

If a field report ever does show a mod-set sky failing to recall, this is ruled out and the next thing to check is whether the mod re-sets the sky per entry at all.

title: Listening test on snd_resample 1, then decide the default flip
description:
uhexen2-og0w landed a band-limited (Blackman-windowed sinc, 16-tap polyphase) load-time resampler behind cvar snd_resample, defaulting to 0 (legacy nearest-sample). Everything measurable says it is better; what is left is taste, and taste is exactly what sank the previous attempt.

Measured against a 128-tap double-precision reference over all 285 8-bit mono sounds in the demo pak0, 11025 -> 44100:
  point sampling (current default)  10.66 dB SNR
  Catmull-Rom (reverted in d5d3bc614) 22.29 dB SNR
  16-tap windowed sinc (new)        30.28 dB SNR
Total image energy for a 3 kHz tone drops 77 dB below the legacy path. Baseband is flat to within 0.05 dB out to 4 kHz where the legacy path is already -1.85 dB. Clip rate 0.085 percent of samples, and clamping those costs 0.16 dB of the 30.28 -- so no headroom scaling is needed.

The risk the numbers cannot settle: removing the images makes 8-bit sfx smoother, and a listener can hear smoother as muffled. Hexen II sfx have a characteristic grit that is partly this aliasing. The r5 revert came from a listening test on the box, not from a measurement.

To close: A/B it on a machine with real audio. 'snd_resample 1' flushes the sfx cache on change, so it can be toggled live mid-game -- no restart, no rebuild. Compare loud/noisy content specifically (weapon impacts, explosions, the raven and tomb ambiences) since that is where both the aliasing and the clipping live. If it holds up, flip the default to 1 and note the memory cost: the 16-bit store doubles resident sfx memory (measured 12.4 MB -> 24.1 MB for the demo's 215 sounds, against a 482 MB cache, so headroom is not a concern).

If it does NOT hold up, the cvar stays default-0 and this closes as 'measured better, sounds worse' -- which is a real answer worth recording rather than reverting again.
notes: 2026-08-13 TRIAGE: marked blocked. Requires human ears on real audio hardware; offscreen SDL cannot judge 'sounds worse'.

title: SoT docks/winter: monsters and props embedded in world brushes at spawn
description:
Map-side, for relay to Mathuzzz — not an engine defect, but now measurable.

The developer-gated droptofloor diagnostic added in c86f09b14 prints why each failed placement failed. Loading SoT maps headless surfaces a consistent set of entities the compiler placed inside solid:

docks (6 failures, all allsolid against worldspawn):
  obj_barrel        -999.2  116.8  539.6
  obj_barrel        -376.8 -1371.2 606.8
  monster_spider_yellow_small  1379.2 -420.0 -160.0
  monster_guard     1301.9 -416.4 -163.8
  monster_guard     1301.9 -506.0 -163.8
  monster_guard     1301.9 -461.2 -163.8

winter (13 failures) includes a row of six monster_guard at x=-608, y=-1544..-880, z=-3363, all allsolid, plus four barrels. Two more are a different mode — monster_archer at -848 1328 -151 and 1028 -1460 509 report 'no floor within 256' while start-solid against a func_train_mp and a door_rotating respectively.

allsolid against worldspawn means the entity origin is inside map geometry: the mapper's placement, and the progs' 'walkmonster in wall at' line is the vanilla symptom of the same thing. A monster that fails this is not removed (unlike items) but starts stuck, which plausibly matches reports of monsters that never move.

The two archers standing on a func_train_mp are the more interesting pair — that is the same combination as uhexen2-nnwb (monsters and moving trains) and may be a shared root cause rather than a placement error, since a train's rest position at spawn need not be where the mapper drew it.

Repro: any Hexenwail build, -game sot, 'developer 1', map docks or winter, read the console at load.
notes:
Released 2026-08-13 without work: claimed, then dropped on discovering a concurrent session active in the same tree. Independent observation that may help whoever picks it up: the same walkmonster-in-wall class also fires on SoT Arena — 3 monster_archer at -3712 2744 64, -2648 2704 64 and -3416 2224 64 report 'CheckBottom: midpoint trace had no ground within 2*STEPSIZE down' followed by 'walkmonster in wall at' on a plain headless map load. So the embedded-entity problem is not confined to docks/winter.
2026-08-13 TRIAGE: marked blocked. Map-side issue; engineering work done. Awaiting relay to Mathuzzz/the mapper.

title: Raise MAX_SOUNDS above 512 — the last precache ceiling a large hub can hit
description:
uhexen2-dv19 measured SoT hub-1 precache usage after Hexenwail raised MAX_MODELS 512 -> 2048 (a14b5eecd). Models are no longer a constraint (worst case courtyard 1184/2047). Sounds are: MAX_SOUNDS is still MAX_SOUNDS_H2MP = 512 (engine/hexen2/quakedef.h:90-93), the same value upstream uHexen2 uses, and SoT 'keep' reaches 408/511 with cathedral at 407 and courtyard at 403. That is 20 percent headroom on the tightest map, against 42 percent for models.

Nobody is hitting it today, so this is not urgent. It matters because mod authors design around the ceiling rather than discovering it: Mathuzzz deliberately withheld SoT's main weapon from hub 1 for exactly this class of reason.

What to check before changing anything:
- Whether the sound index is actually wire-limited. quakedef.h:89-93 says 256 for protocol 18 (byte) and 512 for protocol 19 (MAX_SOUNDS_H2MP), and fe7f194dc's message describes the SND_OVERFLOW2 mechanism UQE used to exceed it without bumping the protocol, warning that doing so breaks older clients. Any raise must go through protocol 21 (our own extension) and keep 18/19 clamped.
- svc_sound / svc_spawnstaticsound field widths in protocol.h and the matching MSG_Write/Read pairs.
- server.h sound_precache[MAX_SOUNDS] and whatever else is statically sized against it (same audit shape as uhexen2-vfvh's lightmap arrays).
- Demo compatibility: recorded demos carry the protocol they were made with.

Discovered while measuring uhexen2-dv19.
close_reason: Closed

title: Worldspawn skybox key should use _sky prefix for engine-only fields
description:
## Suggestion (from Spoike, FTEQW / FTE developer)

Engine-specific (non-standard) worldspawn fields should be prefixed with underscore to avoid colliding with the HexenC field namespace.

The skybox override key currently accepts `sky` but should support `_sky` instead:

**Problem with `sky` (unprefixed):**
- Collides with HexenC field namespace
- Mappers must either add the field to their HexenC progs or accept warnings that the field does not actually exist
- Non-standard convention

**Solution: use `_sky` (engine-only prefix):**
- Established convention for engine-only keys (other engines follow this pattern)
- Avoids touching HexenC fields entirely
- Clear signal to mappers that this is engine-specific, not mod-facing

## Action

Audit how Hexenwail parses worldspawn skybox key today. Support `_sky` as the primary key, keeping `sky` as a backwards-compatible alias for existing maps that use it.

Rationale: Aligns with Spoike's FTE convention for engine-only keys.
close_reason:
Done in 2113f9fa1.

Audit result first, since it changes what the work was: _sky already worked. Sky_NewMap (gl_sky.c:812) and Fog_ParseWorldspawn (gl_fog.c:217) both strip a leading underscore off every worldspawn key before comparing, so _sky/_skyname/_qlsky/_skyfog/_fog have always been accepted, and ED_ParseEdict has always discarded underscore-prefixed keys before the progs field lookup (pr_edict.c:1651) so they never reach HexenC.

What did NOT work was the silence, which is the actual thing Spoike's convention buys. The unprefixed spellings that shipped maps use still hit ED_FindField, miss, and print "'sky' is not a field" — exactly the warning a mapper is told to either accept or paper over with a dummy progs field. SoT docks prints two of them ('fog' and 'sky') on every load.

Fix: ED_IsEngineWorldspawnKey lists the keys the engine reads out of the entity lump itself (sky, skyname, qlsky, skyfog, fog, wad, mapversion) and ED_ParseEdict skips the warning for them. Scoped tightly — only on worldspawn (ent == sv.edicts) and only after ED_FindField has already failed, so a mod that declares one of these as a real progs field behaves exactly as before.

Verified at runtime, not just by reading. Wrote an external maps/docks.ent for SoT docks with sky -> _sky and fog -> _fog: 'Loaded external entity file', all six grimmnight_ skybox faces loaded, 'Fog: worldspawn density=0.037 rgb=(0.08, 0.07, 0.18)', zero warnings. Removed the override and loaded stock docks (unprefixed keys from the BSP): warning count went 2 -> 0.

README gained a 'Skybox and fog for mappers' section documenting _sky/_skyfog/_fog as the form to prefer and the unprefixed spellings as accepted legacy.

title: OIT fragment shaders read fragColor uninitialized; three GL_DEBUG_SEVERITY_HIGH warnings at every startup
description:
All three OIT program variants (world_oit, alias_oit, particle_oit) emit a HIGH-severity GL debug message when their fragment shader is compiled:

  GL [HIGH]: 0:10(20): warning: `fragColor' used uninitialized

Reproduced on Mesa 26.1.5 / llvmpipe by running the engine with MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DISABLE=true (a warm shader cache hides it — the message is only emitted on a real compile, which is why it has gone unnoticed).

CAUSE
GL_CompileOITFragShader (engine/h2shared/gl_shader.c:157) wraps a normal fragment shader using Ironwail's main -> main_body rename trick. Its injected preamble declares

  vec4 fragColor;

as an uninitialized global, forward-declares main_body(), and writes a new main() that calls main_body() and then reads fragColor to build the two MRT outputs. At the point the compiler analyses main(), main_body() is only a prototype, so it cannot see that the body assigns fragColor — it correctly reports a read of an uninitialized variable.

IMPACT
Benign today: every one of the three wrapped shaders (sworld_frag, salias_frag, spart_frag) assigns fragColor on every path that is not a discard, so the value main() reads is always the one main_body just wrote. Two reasons to fix anyway:

1. It is reported at GL_DEBUG_SEVERITY_HIGH, so it prints three times on every cold start and trains the eye to ignore the exact channel that would carry a real GL error.
2. It is a live trap. GLSL says the value of an uninitialized global is undefined; the wrapper is only correct because of a property of the shaders it wraps, and nothing enforces that property. Anyone adding an early 'return;' to a wrapped fragment shader gets undefined colour in OIT mode only — translucent surfaces, on some drivers, some of the time. salias_frag already contains an early return (the u_alias_r6_mode probe path); it happens to assign fragColor first.

FIX
Initialize it in the preamble: 'vec4 fragColor = vec4(0.0);'. One line, silences the diagnostic, and turns the failure mode for a future early-return from undefined garbage into transparent black.

Found while runtime-verifying uhexen2-ekdm — the engine turns out to run headlessly here under SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen with llvmpipe, which is what made the GL debug output reachable on this machine at all.
close_reason:
Fixed in b415f65c2. Preamble now declares 'vec4 fragColor = vec4(0.0);' instead of leaving the global undefined, with a comment explaining that the wrapper's correctness otherwise rests on an unenforced property of the shaders it wraps.

Verified by re-running the engine headlessly with MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DISABLE=true so the shaders actually recompile: the three GL [HIGH] lines are gone, world_oit/alias_oit/particle_oit all still report OK, and a map loads and renders. Also ran with r_oit 1 to confirm the OIT FBO path still comes up ('OIT: 640x480 FBO ready') with no GL errors.

title: Runtime-verify the config.cfg mid-session flush survives an unclean exit
description:
Follow-up to uhexen2-ghv0, fixed in commit d5db241f8. The fix is compile-verified on nix build, .#win64 and .#h2ded, but the acceptance criterion is a runtime test and this dev machine has no GL (SDL dummy driver fails at video init: 'OpenGL support is either not configured in SDL or not available in current SDL video driver (dummy)'), so the engine cannot reach a frame loop here.

WHAT TO CHECK on a box with a display:
1. Start the engine, change an archived setting in the menu (e.g. Misc/HUD glow intensity or scr_sbarscale), wait >2 seconds (CONFIG_FLUSH_DELAY in engine/hexen2/host.c), then kill -9 the process. Restart: the setting must have survived. Before d5db241f8 it would not have.
2. Rebind a key, wait >2s, kill -9, restart: the bind must have survived (Key_SetBinding marks the config dirty too).
3. Confirm no stutter while dragging a menu slider continuously. Each set marks the config dirty and the flush is a whole-file rewrite, debounced to once per 2s; if that is still visible, raise CONFIG_FLUSH_DELAY.
4. Confirm <userdir>/config.cfg.tmp is not left behind after a normal quit. Host_WriteConfiguration writes the temp then Sys_renames it into place; a leftover .tmp means the rename leg failed (it would also have printed "Couldn't write config.cfg.").
5. Windows specifically: Sys_rename is MoveFileW, which refuses an existing target, so the Windows path unlinks config.cfg first. Verify settings still persist there and no window leaves the file missing.
notes:
AMENDMENT: check 5 in the description is stale. It described a Windows-only 'unlink config.cfg first' step, which existed only between commits d5db241f8 and da1137211. da1137211 changed Sys_rename to MoveFileExW with MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING (both hexen2/sys_win.c and hexen2/server/sys_win.c), so the rename now replaces the target in one step on Windows as it does on POSIX, and there is no window where config.cfg is missing on either platform. Verify persistence on Windows as before, but there is no unlink leg to watch.

Build verification is now complete for the code as committed: nix build (Linux), nix build .#h2ded, nix build .#h2ded-win64 and the .#win64 client target all clean at da1137211. The .#win64 build had to be run against the committed revision rather than the working tree, because another session was mid-refactor on flake.nix at the time (it failed evaluation with "undefined variable 'mkWin64'") — nothing to do with this change.
close_reason:
Runtime-verified. The blocker in the description — 'this dev machine has no GL, SDL dummy driver fails at video init' — turned out to be the wrong video driver, not the wrong machine. SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen with LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 gives a real GL 4.6 context on llvmpipe (Mesa 26.1.5) and the engine reaches the frame loop, loads maps and runs. Every Linux-side check below was executed against the demo data1, engine build da1137211+ (0.7.9-beta.r11).

CHECK 1 + 2 — settings and binds survive an unclean exit: PASS
Started with '+scr_conalpha 0.42 +bind F9 screenshot', ran 12s, SIGKILL (exit 137, no shutdown path runs). config.cfg was on disk afterwards containing both:
  bind "F9" "screenshot"
  scr_conalpha "0.42"
Restarting and querying the cvar read back 0.42, so the file is not just present but loadable.

The debounce boundary was measured rather than assumed. Same run killed at 2/3/4/5/6 seconds:
  t=2s  -> no config.cfg at all
  t=3s+ -> config.cfg written, with the setting
That is exactly where CONFIG_FLUSH_DELAY=2.0 predicts once startup is accounted for, and it is also the control this test needed: the file cannot be a startup artifact, because at t=2s there is none. Only the periodic flush in _Host_Frame can have produced it, which is the code under test.

CHECK 4 — no config.cfg.tmp left behind: PASS
Absent after clean quit and absent after every SIGKILL run. (A SIGKILL mid-write could in principle strand one; none of the runs did, and a stranded .tmp is harmless — the real config is only ever replaced atomically.)

CHECK 3 — flush cost: not a stutter source, by measurement.
Timed the actual write pattern (write 5305-byte file, rename into place) 500x on this filesystem: median 22us, p95 27us, max 46us. Debounced to at most once per 2s, that is ~0.1% of one frame at 60fps, once every 120 frames. CONFIG_FLUSH_DELAY does not need raising. Note the subjective 'drag a slider and look for hitching' test is meaningless on llvmpipe, where software rasterization dominates frame time by three orders of magnitude — the isolated measurement is the stronger evidence here anyway.

CHECK 5 — Windows: still not covered, needs a Windows box. Unchanged from the amendment already in the notes: da1137211 made Sys_rename MoveFileExW with MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING, so there is no unlink leg and no window where config.cfg is missing; the remaining question is only whether persistence works there, and nothing platform-specific is left to reason about.

Test hygiene: userdir is derived from getpwuid(), not $HOME, so these runs wrote to the real ~/.hexen2/data1/. No config.cfg existed there before; the one created plus the data1 directory were removed afterwards, leaving the machine as found.

title: Demo fetch: verify get_demo.cmd on real Windows and the Flatpak download dialog
description:
uhexen2-49ep shipped the demo fetch helper on every platform, but two paths could only be reasoned about on this machine, not run. Both are user-facing first-run paths, so a silent failure means a new user bounces.

1. scripts/get_demo.cmd on real Windows. Verified: the PowerShell it wraps parses under pwsh 7.6.2, its three guard paths fire, and the full download/verify/extract path works with tar substituted for tar.exe. NOT verified: that tar.exe (the bsdtar in Windows 10 1803+) accepts '-xzf <archive> -C <dir> --strip-components=1 <member>' with a forward-slash member path against a gzipped tar; that -ExecutionPolicy Bypass actually defeats the Mark of the Web on a .ps1 extracted from a downloaded zip; that the CMDCMDLINE '/c' test pauses on double-click and stays quiet from an interactive prompt; and that Invoke-WebRequest with a curl User-Agent gets the file rather than the interstitial on Windows PowerShell 5.1, which is a different HTTP stack from pwsh 7.
   Ask Mathuzzz or Caco: unpack a release zip on a machine with no game data, double-click get_demo.cmd, confirm data1 appears and the game starts.

2. The Flatpak download dialog. flatpak/hexenwail.sh now offers the demo through zenity when no pak0.pak is present. Shellchecks clean and the no-helper, no-zenity, headless-zenity and data-present paths were exercised outside the sandbox. NOT verified inside a real flatpak: that the org.freedesktop.Platform 25.08 runtime provides a curl or wget BINARY (the script needs one; the runtime certainly has libcurl, which is not the same thing), that zenity is on PATH in the sandbox, and that the --progress --pulsate pipe behaves. If neither downloader exists the script fails with a clear message and the user still sees the old 'place your pak files here' path, so the failure mode is benign - but the feature would silently not work.
   If curl turns out to be absent, options are to add curl as a flatpak module or to fetch with something the runtime does guarantee.

Neither blocks anything that works today; both are 'the new path may not work on the platform it was written for'.
acceptance_criteria: get_demo.cmd confirmed working on a real Windows install from an unpacked release zip; the Flatpak offer confirmed to download and launch inside a real flatpak build, or the missing dependency identified and added.
notes: 2026-08-13 TRIAGE: marked blocked. Requires real Windows + a real Flatpak sandbox environment.

title: midi_win.c cleanups — vestigial hw_vol_capable, hStream type confusion, unsynchronised volume_cache
description:
Three small pre-existing defects in engine/h2shared/midi_win.c:

1. hw_vol_capable is initialised false at line 77 and never assigned anywhere. The MIDICAPS_VOLUME detection block in MIDI_Init only Con_Printf's. This is vestigial since upstream commit 892bc9588 deliberately disabled hardware MIDI volume on Vista+. Harmless but misleading — the `if (hw_vol_capable)` branch in MIDI_SetVolume (line 114) is dead code. Either remove the variable and dead branch, or wire it up honestly.

2. Line 219 passes (void **)&hStream to MIDI_SetVolume. hStream is the live HMIDISTRM, not a void* slot. CHECK_MIDI_ALIVE does `*handle = NULL`, so if it ever tripped there it would zero the actual stream handle. Currently unreachable because midi_playing is true, but it is a type-confusion landmine. Every other caller correctly passes &midi_handle.handle.

3. volume_cache[] is written by the callback thread (line 569) and read by the main thread (line 599) with no synchronisation.

These don't block functionality but should be cleaned up for correctness and maintainability.
close_reason: Fixed in c9ecbc982: MIDI_Stop teardown deferred to MIDI_Update on the main thread via a polled flag; per-channel volume rescale deferred via Host_TryInvokeOnMainThread with channel+volume packed into the param (volume_cache is now main-thread-only); Con_Printf in the callback replaced with Host_PrintAsync; hw_vol_capable dead branch removed; MIDI_Play no longer passes (void**)&hStream as a handle slot. Also fixed two latent bugs uncovered en route (refill error paths freeing track data then continuing, and end-of-data hanging when all buffers were already returned) and moved AsyncQueue_Destroy after the subsystem shutdowns so the MIDI callback thread cannot outlive the queue. nix build .#win64 and nix build clean.

title: Track libsndfile parser CVEs; re-audit on nixpkgs bump
description:
# libsndfile CVE Tracking (uhexen2-c58o follow-up)

## Finding
libsndfile 1.2.2 in runtime closure, 5 active CVEs:
- CVE-2025-52194 (CVSS 7.5)
- CVE-2026-37555 (7.5)
- CVE-2024-50613 (6.5)
- CVE-2024-50612 (5.5)
- CVE-2025-56226 (5.3)

Reported 2026-08-11 by vulnix 1.12.4 audit against ./result.

## Why It Is Reachable (Critical)
`glhexen2` links libfluidsynth.so.3 → libsndfile.so.1. FluidSynth uses libsndfile to decode audio sample data (SF3 soundfonts with Vorbis compression).

This project deliberately ships a soundfont on every distribution and exposes `snd_soundfont` cvar. `find_soundfont()` in engine/hexen2/midi_fluid.c searches in order:
1. snd_soundfont cvar value
2. <exe dir>/soundfont.sf2|sf3
3. <basedir>/soundfont.sf2|sf3
4. <basedir>/data1/
5. compile-time SOUNDFONT_PATH
6. system paths

An attacker-controlled .sf2/.sf3 (user pointing cvar at a file, or mod's config.cfg shipping a crafted file in mod directory) is parsed by libsndfile at load time. This is a genuine untrusted-input path into a library with 5 parser CVEs.

## What Is *Not* The Problem (to prevent re-investigation)
- zlib-1.3.2 CVE-2026-27820: NOT reachable. Engine has no libz in DT_NEEDED, no PAK/zip support. zlib in closure only as transitive dep of SDL3/fluidsynth, never loaded by engine.
- orc, libssh2, libmicrohttpd, cjson, nghttp2, avahi, cups, openal-soft, gstreamer, libcamera, etc.: Closure-only noise from SDL3 backends and GTK/zenity. None in binary's DT_NEEDED.
- gcc-15.3.0 CVE-2023-4039: AArch64 -fstack-protector; target is x86_64.
- cups CVE-2022-26691: cupsd local privesc; daemon not run by game.
- glibc-2.42-67 (8 CVEs, top CVE-2026-5450 CVSS 9.8): Base libc present in all Nix closures, no project-specific action available. Known-accepted item.

## Why This Is Tracking-Only, Not a Fix
flake.lock pins nixpkgs to rev 2fcb964de67f (2026-08-10), ONE DAY OLD at audit time. These CVEs are unpatched in current nixpkgs, not from a stale pin. `nix flake update` will NOT clear them immediately. No code change to make right now. Actionable work: watch for libsndfile bump landing in nixpkgs, re-run audit, then act (either upgrade or assess each CVE as not affecting soundfont path).
acceptance_criteria:
- libsndfile in runtime closure >= version where CVE-2025-52194, CVE-2026-37555, CVE-2024-50613, CVE-2024-50612, CVE-2025-56226 are resolved, OR each CVE individually assessed as not affecting the soundfont-parsing code path.
- `nix run nixpkgs#vulnix -- ./result` re-run confirms libsndfile no longer reports active advisories.
notes:
RE-AUDIT 2026-08-15. Nothing moved, and the bead's waiting strategy is unsound.

STATUS: still libsndfile 1.2.2 in the closure
(/nix/store/g1wsridnxsfm52i7klwibh80x7ripzis-libsndfile-1.2.2), flake.lock still
pinned to nixpkgs 2fcb964de67f. All 5 CVEs stand.

THE PREMISE IS WRONG -- DO NOT KEEP WAITING FOR A NIXPKGS BUMP.
The bead says "watch for libsndfile bump landing in nixpkgs". There is nothing
to watch for:
  * libsndfile 1.2.2 was released 2023-08-13 and is STILL the latest upstream
    release as of 2026-08-15 -- three years, no new release.
  * nixpkgs master (pkgs/by-name/li/libsndfile/package.nix) is also on 1.2.2,
    so the pin is not stale; there is no newer version anywhere to bump to.
  * upstream master IS actively developed (most recent commit 2026-07-21,
    "ircam: use psf_lrintf when reading samplerate"), so fixes plausibly exist
    in master but unreleased.
So the trigger this bead is waiting on may never fire. Anything time-based
here is an indefinite hold, not a scheduled one.

BETTER LEVER FOUND: drop the dependency instead of tracking it.
readelf -d on the built glhexen2 confirms libsndfile is NOT in the engine's
DT_NEEDED. The full NEEDED list is SDL3, m, mvec, dl, asound, vorbisfile,
vorbis, ogg, xmp, opusfile, fluidsynth, GLX, OpenGL, c. libsndfile arrives
ONLY transitively through libfluidsynth.so.3.

FluidSynth needs libsndfile for exactly two things: SF3 (Vorbis-compressed)
soundfonts, and the file renderer that writes .wav. Hexenwail uses neither:
  * flake.nix:661 bundles TimGM6mb.sf2 (uncompressed SF2, Debian tarball)
  * flake.nix:226 sets -DSOUNDFONT_PATH to FluidR3_GM2-2.sf2 (also SF2)
  * playback goes through the realtime audio driver, not the file renderer
So building fluidsynth with -Denable-libsndfile=0 would remove all 5 CVEs from
the runtime closure outright. nixpkgs fluidsynth 2.5.6 already carries
cmakeFlags (-Denable-framework=off, -Denable-libinstpatch=0), so this is a
one-line overlay, not a fork.

NOT DOING IT UNILATERALLY -- there is a real tradeoff, filed separately:
  * overriding fluidsynth means building it from source, so every build loses
    the binary-cache hit for it
  * find_soundfont() probes .sf2|.sf3 and snd_soundfont is user-settable, so
    dropping SF3 removes a capability players can currently use
That decision is the actionable successor to this bead.
CORRECTION 2026-08-15. The reachability analysis in this bead contains a wrong
inference, and the successor it spawned (uhexen2-kayb) has been closed as a
result. Re-scope this bead or close it.

## The wrong claim

"readelf -d on the built glhexen2 confirms libsndfile is NOT in the engine's
DT_NEEDED [...] libsndfile arrives ONLY transitively through libfluidsynth.so.3."

The readelf observation is correct. The word ONLY is not. DT_NEEDED shows the
engine's own direct links; it says nothing about the rest of the closure, and
SDL3 reaches libsndfile without going near fluidsynth. Measured with
`nix why-depends --all ./result <libsndfile>` on the current build -- seven
paths:

    hexenwail -> fluidsynth -> libsndfile
    hexenwail -> fluidsynth -> libpulseaudio -> libsndfile
    hexenwail -> sdl3 -> pipewire -> libsndfile
    hexenwail -> sdl3 -> pipewire -> lilv -> libsndfile
    hexenwail -> sdl3 -> pipewire -> spandsp -> libsndfile
    hexenwail -> sdl3 -> pipewire -> roc-toolkit -> libsndfile
    hexenwail -> sdl3 -> pipewire -> roc-toolkit -> sox -> libsndfile

## What that costs this bead

The acceptance criterion -- "`nix run nixpkgs#vulnix -- ./result` re-run confirms
libsndfile no longer reports active advisories" -- cannot be met by anything
this project controls. libsndfile leaves the closure only when SDL3 stops
pulling pipewire, which is nixpkgs' call, not ours. Combined with the finding
already recorded here (1.2.2 is three years old and is also what nixpkgs master
carries, so there is nothing to bump to), BOTH of this bead's exits are shut.

## What is still true and still worth acting on

The reachability argument stands on its own and is the useful half. A crafted
.sf2/.sf3 pointed at by snd_soundfont is parsed by libsndfile via FluidSynth,
and that path is ours to close regardless of what sits in the closure. The lever
is in our own code -- SF_FindSoundFont (engine/h2shared/soundfont.c:71-137)
probes soundfont.sf3 in four places and hands whatever it finds to the synth
unvalidated. Narrowing what the engine will accept costs nothing and needs no
overlay.

RECOMMENDED RE-SCOPE: drop the closure/vulnix criterion, keep the reachability
criterion, and let the soundfont-input hardening bead carry it. If that is not
wanted, close this as won't-fix -- an indefinite hold on a trigger that cannot
fire is not tracking.

title: GPU worldcull rebuilds src index buffer with different fan rules than R_BuildWorldVBO
description:
engine/h2shared/gl_worldcull.c:693-720 rebuilds a CPU copy of the world index buffer to upload as cull_src_ibo, with the comment "same as R_BuildWorldVBO". It is not the same.

- gl_worldcull.c fans over surf->polys->numverts, skipping surfaces where !p || p->numverts < 3
- R_BuildWorldVBO (engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c:3078-3152), which is what assigns surf->vbo_firstvert / surf->vbo_firstindex / surf->vbo_numtris and sets world_num_indices, fans over lnumverts = surf->numedges

These diverge because BuildSurfaceDisplayList strips co-linear points at engine/hexen2/gl_rsurf.c:3594, reducing poly->numverts below fa->numedges. Consequences when they diverge:
1. cull_src_ibo contents no longer line up with the surf->vbo_firstindex offsets the cull_mark compute shader reads with (src_indices[s.firstindex + i]) — wrong geometry.
2. idx_data is malloc'd at world_num_indices*4 but only partially filled, so the uninitialised tail is uploaded to the GPU.
Also minor: the malloc at gl_worldcull.c:693 is not NULL-checked.

Currently LATENT, not live: the co-linear stripping is gated on !gl_keeptjunctions.integer and gl_keeptjunctions defaults to "1" (engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:301), so the two paths agree by default. Fires only if a user sets gl_keeptjunctions 0.

Fix direction: do not re-derive the indices. Either have R_BuildWorldVBO retain its index array for worldcull to reuse, or make the worldcull rebuild fan over surf->numedges with identical skip conditions. Add the NULL check.

Acceptance: cull_src_ibo is byte-identical to world_ibo contents for any value of gl_keeptjunctions.
close_reason: Fixed in 238a7a632. Stopped re-deriving the indices: R_BuildWorldVBO now retains its index array as world_index_data (freed in R_FreeWorldVBO and on rebuild), and gl_worldcull.c uploads that verbatim as cull_src_ibo. Byte-identical to world_ibo by construction for any value of gl_keeptjunctions, which is the stated acceptance. The unchecked malloc is gone with the rebuild loop; the new path bails through R_FreeWorldCull() if there is no index data. nix build .#default, .#win64 and .#h2ded all clean, no new warnings.

title: 'Bad backpack!' — dropped single item is destroyed instead of spawned
description:
Reported by Tome of Power Abuser (Discord, on 0.7.9-beta.r4), noted as present 'for years and years'. No repro steps yet.

Source is gamecode, not engine — DropBackpack() in items.hc, present in all four gamecode trees:
- gamecode/hc/h2/items.hc:1651
- gamecode/hc/portals/items.hc:1675
- gamecode/hc/hw/items.hc:2476
- gamecode/hc/siege/items.hc:2502

Mechanism: DropBackpack sums every artifact count and full-armor piece into 'total' (h2/items.hc:1378-1476). When exactly one thing would be dropped (total==1 with no mana/health, or total==0 with exactly one of bluemana/greenmana/spawn_health — h2/items.hc:1545-1549), it skips the bag and spawns that single item directly via an if/else-if chain. If no branch matches, it hits the 'Bad backpack!' dprint and then remove(item) — so the loot is silently destroyed, not just logged. That is a real gameplay effect (the tester's 'bad backpack'), not a cosmetic debug message.

Triage already done — the obvious hypothesis is RULED OUT: the set of fields accumulated into 'total' and the set of fields tested in the dispatch chain are identical (19 fields each: cnt_torch, cnt_h_boost, cnt_sh_boost, cnt_mana_boost, cnt_teleport, cnt_tome, cnt_summon, cnt_invisibility, cnt_glyph, cnt_haste, cnt_blast, cnt_polymorph, cnt_flight, cnt_cubeofforce, cnt_invincibility, armor_amulet, armor_bracer, armor_breastplate, armor_helmet). So this is not a missing else-if branch.

That leaves a value-level mismatch: 'total' is a sum of counts, not a count of distinct item types, so total can equal 1 while every individual item.* field is falsy — e.g. if any count is negative or fractional, or if a count is mutated between accumulation and dispatch. Needs a runtime repro to confirm which.
design:
Two separable pieces of work. (1) Defensive fix, cheap and safe: in the fallthrough branch, drop the bag normally (setmodel models/bag.mdl + BackpackTouch) instead of remove(item), so a mis-classified drop loses nothing. (2) Root cause: needs a repro. Suggested instrumentation — extend the dprint to also print 'total' and each nonzero item.cnt_*/armor_* value, then reproduce with developer 1.

IMPORTANT SCOPE CAVEAT: this lives in progs.dat, not the engine. Retail players run Raven's precompiled progs.dat, so an items.hc change only reaches users running rebuilt gamecode. Confirm whether this project ships its own compiled progs.dat before committing to a gameplay-visible fix; if it does not, this may be unfixable from our side and should be closed as wontfix with the analysis retained.
acceptance_criteria: Either: a repro is found and the dispatch chain correctly spawns the single item with no dprint; or the fallthrough is made non-destructive (bag dropped rather than removed) and the scope caveat above is resolved one way or the other.
close_reason: Closed via the acceptance's second branch (non-destructive fallthrough + scope caveat resolved), in fe1f2bdc1. The fallthrough now drops a normal backpack (setmodel bag.mdl + BackpackTouch, matching the multi-item branch, including hw's scale calc) instead of remove(item), so a misclassified drop loses nothing. Added BadBackpackDump() printing 'total' and every nonzero inventory field, so the next 'developer 1' report identifies which field is lying. Applied to h2, portals, hw. siege needs no change: its entire single-item dispatch chain including 'Bad backpack!' sits inside a block comment (items.hc:2394-2515) and never executes -- siege always drops a bag. Re-verified the issue's triage mechanically rather than by eye: accumulated set and dispatched set are identical (19 fields each; bluemana/greenmana/spawn_health are the expected 3 extra, handled by the outer gate), so the root cause remains a value-level mismatch needing a repro. SCOPE CAVEAT RESOLVED: this project ships no compiled progs.dat -- gamecode/ is excluded from the nix build (flake.nix:46) and gamecode/COMPILE documents a manual hcc invocation -- so the fix reaches only players running rebuilt gamecode, not retail Raven progs.dat. Landed anyway: this is the upstream-shared gamecode source and the change is strictly safer than what it replaced. Verified all four trees compile clean with hcc from .#utils (h2 progs.dat+progs2.dat, portals, hw, siege).

title: Allow Demoness selection for the old campaign when Portals is installed
description:
Reported by Tome of Power Abuser (Discord, on 0.7.9-beta.r4): the Demoness/Succubus class cannot be picked from the New Game class menu when starting the original Hexen II campaign, even with Portal of Praevus installed. The tester's existing workaround is to start the Portals campaign and then 'map demo1' — which works, and is what prompted the request.

The menu gate is compile-time, not a missing feature:
- engine/h2shared/h2config.h:68 defines DISALLOW_DEMONESS_IN_OLD_GAME 1
- engine/hexen2/menu.c:904-910 (M_Class_Draw) and :930-936 (M_Class_Key) clamp the visible class count to MAX_PLAYER_CLASS - PORTALS_EXTRA_CLASSES (5-1=4, quakedef.h:202-203) unless m_enter_portals is set
- m_enter_portals is set only in M_SinglePlayer_Key case 0 (menu.c:1088-1093), i.e. the Portals campaign entry

Why the gate exists: class 5 only exists in the Portals gamecode. The workaround works because picking the Portals campaign loads the portals gamedir, so 'map demo1' runs old-campaign maps under Portals progs.dat. Flipping the define to 0 alone would let a player pick Demoness while the plain h2 progs.dat is loaded, which has no class 5 — likely broken player model, sbar, and class logic. sbar.c:466-468/626-628 and gl_rmisc.c:465 carry the same clamp.
design: Do NOT just flip DISALLOW_DEMONESS_IN_OLD_GAME to 0 — that decouples class availability from which progs.dat is loaded. The feature really means 'run the original campaign under Portals gamecode', which m_enter_portals already expresses. Two candidate shapes: (a) a new Single Player menu entry (old campaign + Portals gamecode) that sets m_enter_portals and then starts demo1 rather than the Portals start map; or (b) a cvar-gated relaxation of the clamp that only takes effect when the portals gamedir is actually active. Prefer (a) — it keeps the class list and the loaded gamecode consistent by construction. If the clamp is relaxed anywhere, sbar.c:466-468, sbar.c:626-628 and gl_rmisc.c:465 must be audited to match.
acceptance_criteria: With Portals installed, the player can start the original campaign as the Demoness through the menu with no console commands; the Portals gamecode is loaded for that run; player model, status bar armor values and class name all render correctly; and starting the original campaign WITHOUT Portals installed still shows only the 4 base classes.
notes:
CORRECTION to the DESIGN section above: the premise that 'picking the Portals campaign loads the portals gamedir' is wrong. OLD MISSION and NEW MISSION do not select different gamedirs. quakefs.c 'step 2' (lines ~1599-1650) calls FS_AddGameDirectory("portals", true) at filesystem init whenever the portals pak validates (GAME_PORTALS, set from pakdata entry 3 at quakefs.c:268). By the time any menu is drawn, portals/ is already in the searchpath and its progs.dat is the loaded gamecode. m_enter_portals only picks the start map in M_Difficulty_Key: set => CL_SetupIntermission(12) then keep1; clear => 'map demo1'. That is also the real reason the tester's 'start Portals, then map demo1' workaround works -- the gamedir never changed, so no consistency was ever being enforced.

Therefore option (a) (a new Single Player menu entry) is unnecessary. Implemented the minimal fix instead: flipped DISALLOW_DEMONESS_IN_OLD_GAME to 0 in engine/h2shared/h2config.h, which drops the 'else if (!m_enter_portals)' clamp at menu.c:908 and :934. The knob is retained so vanilla behavior can be restored by flipping it back.

No audit changes were needed at sbar.c:466-468, sbar.c:626-628 or gl_rmisc.c:465 -- all three clamp on !(gameflags & GAME_PORTALS), which stays true and correct; none of them consult m_enter_portals.

Known caveat (pre-existing, NOT introduced here): a custom mod riding on portals data can ship a progs.dat with no class 5. Host_Class_f's CRC check (host_cmd.c:1284) is guarded by sv.active, so it does not fire on the menu path where playerclass is set before the map loads. That caveat applies identically to the NEW MISSION / START W/ INTRO entry, which has always offered the demoness.

Builds clean via 'nix build .#default'. Left open pending runtime confirmation of the acceptance criteria (player model, status bar armor values, class name) on the test machine.
close_reason:
All acceptance criteria verified via headless testing (Xvfb + xdotool; no test machine required).

AC1 (menu-driven Demoness selection, no console): PASS. Drove the actual menu path: main menu → Single Player → Old Mission → Class screen → Down×4 to Demoness (with cport5 portrait) → difficulty screen showed Demoness-specific names (LARVA/SPAWN/FIEND/SHE BITCH from DiffNames[4]) → started demo1. M_Class_Draw/M_Class_Key executed in full.

AC2 (Portals gamecode loaded): PASS. Programs log shows 1147K. portals/progs.dat is 1174956 B (1147K); data1/PROGS.DAT is 952888 B (930K). Protocol 19 (Raven/MP/1.12). Unambiguous.

AC3 (player model, status bar armor, class name): PASS. Single item_armor_helmet spawned in two runs: Demoness showed class name DEMONESS, portrait cport5, AC 12 (HelmetAC[4]=8 + 20/5). Paladin showed PALADIN, cport1, AC 8 (HelmetAC[0]=4 + 20/5). Had sbar.c:626 clamp fired, AC would read 6. It did not. Chase cam confirmed Demoness model. Skin recolor forced with 'color 3 6' / 'color 11 4' (svc_updatecolors → CL_NewTranslation) — model recolored and kept Demoness texels, not Paladin.

AC4 (without Portals, only 4 classes): PASS. Retail data1 no portals/; same with -portals flag (hits rollback, logs "Missing or invalid mission pack"); .#demodata. All show four classes, Down×6 wraps — fifth entry never appears.

**Process note**: This bead was blocked for weeks on "needs test machine" when the machine it needed was the dev box: full H2 + Portal of Praevus at /home/josh/hexen2, menu paths testable headlessly. Worth remembering before parking future work on external validation.

**Correction note (fixed in 1d767a4a7)**: Earlier claim that portals/ is added "whenever GAME_PORTALS is set" was backwards. GAME_PORTALS is SET BY validation of pak3.pak in step 2, which only runs with -portals/-missionpack/-h2mp/-game/-mod flags. Bare glhexen2 never sees Portals. Conclusion survives (OLD MISSION only drawn when GAME_PORTALS set) but the stated reason was inverted.

title: Runtime closure ships known CVEs; nixpkgs pin is 92 days old
description:
The first `vulnix --closure` run against the .#default build (2026-08-11, while implementing uhexen2-kt1p) reported 179 CVE references across roughly 25 packages in the runtime closure. Most are irrelevant to a single-player game engine — avahi, cups and similar arrive as transitive SDL dependencies and are never reached. What deserves triage is the file-parsing path, because those libraries do touch attacker-supplied map, model, texture and music files: zlib 1.3.2 (CVE-2026-27820, CVSS 9.8, plus CVE-2023-6992), libsndfile 1.2.2, libxml2 2.15.1, giflib 5.2.2 and openexr 3.3.8 all appeared in the report.

A large part of this is simply staleness: the flake's nixpkgs input is pinned 92 days back, and flake-utils (635 days) and its systems input (1220 days) are older still. Many of these CVEs are likely already fixed upstream.

ACTION: run `nix flake update`, rebuild, re-run `vulnix --closure ./result`, and diff the findings. Then triage what survives — specifically whether the surviving parsing-path CVEs are reachable from engine code paths that read untrusted files. Anything genuinely reachable becomes its own issue; the rest goes in a vulnix whitelist with a written reason so the weekly scan stays signal.

Note the flake update itself needs a full rebuild + smoke test before it can be trusted, since nixpkgs unstable moves fast.

Acceptance criteria: flake inputs refreshed, before/after vulnix diff recorded, surviving parsing-path CVEs triaged as reachable or whitelisted-with-reason, and desktop + Windows builds still pass CI.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-11: ran `nix flake update`. nixpkgs da5ad661ba4e (2026-05-10) → 2fcb964de67f (2026-08-10); flake-utils and systems unchanged (635 and 1220 days old respectively, stable inputs not staleness). Rebuild .#default succeeds. Binary 1,521,800 bytes (down 4,096 from 1,525,896); GCC 15.2.0 → 15.3.0. Smoke test passes (SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen).

vulnix --closure before/after: 179 CVE refs / 24 packages → 30 refs / 11 packages.

FULLY RESOLVED (13 packages): curl, giflib, glib, gstreamer, libde265, libgcrypt, libusb, libxml2, ngtcp2, openexr, openssl, sqlite, unbound. Covers 3 of 5 parsing-path libraries identified in description (libxml2, giflib, openexr).

STILL PRESENT (11 packages): avahi, cjson, cups, gcc, glibc, libmicrohttpd, libsndfile, libssh2, nghttp2, orc, zlib.

PARSING-PATH SURVIVORS (untrusted game file input):
  - zlib 1.3.2: CVE-2026-27820 (CVSS 9.8), CVE-2023-6992. Via PAK/PK3 decompression, PNG loading. No newer zlib in nixpkgs.
  - libsndfile 1.2.2: CVE-2025-52194 (7.5), CVE-2026-37555 (7.5), CVE-2024-50613 (6.5), CVE-2024-50612 (5.5), CVE-2025-56226 (5.3). Audio parsing.

NEXT: (1) Decide whether to land uncommitted flake.lock bump; if yes, rebuild .#win64 and .#h2ded alongside .#default. (2) Triage zlib and libsndfile: are CVEs reachable from engine file-read paths, or whitelist with written reason for weekly scan signal-to-noise.

Before/after scan output: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-josh-tmp-claudedir-uhexen2/3a43a70a-5771-48ec-9174-c6a84fb3d20e/scratchpad/vulnix-local.txt and vulnix-after.txt. Original flake.lock backup at .../scratchpad/flake.lock.bak.

---

REACHABILITY TRIAGE (2026-08-11): Determined whether surviving parsing-path CVEs are reachable from engine code paths that read untrusted files.

zlib 1.3.2 (CVE-2026-27820 CVSS 9.8, CVE-2023-6992) — NOT REACHABLE at runtime.
  No libz in engine's DT_NEEDED list (libSDL3, libm, libmvec, libdl, libasound, libvorbisfile, libvorbis, libogg, libxmp, libopusfile, libfluidsynth, libGLX, libOpenGL, libc). ldd on fully resolved tree finds no libz.so. zlib in closure (vulnix scans stores, not runtimes) but never loaded by engine; no untrusted game file reaches it. SDL3 dlopens display/audio backends at runtime which ldd cannot see and one could hypothetically pull zlib, but that path handles display/audio server protocols, not game files. libsndfile 1.2.2 (CVE-2025-52194 7.5, CVE-2026-37555 7.5, CVE-2024-50613 6.5, CVE-2024-50612 5.5, CVE-2025-56226 5.3) — REACHABLE via hostile mod content.

But genuinely reachable, so should NOT be whitelisted as unreachable. RECOMMENDATION: leave un-whitelisted and let it age with nixpkgs bump, or pin a patched libsndfile if available.
