title: Pharaoh's scepter not spawning in Thysis map
description: Pharaoh's scepter item doesn't spawn despite completing all required steps in Thysis. May be map/script design issue but needs investigation. Workaround: noclip to grab jar. Reported by ReaperAA.
notes:
2026-08-14 SPAWNFLAGS 32768 RESOLVED (do not re-litigate this number):

spawnflags 32768 is SPAWNFLAG_NOT_DEATHMATCH — engine/hexen2/server.h:253 (0x00008000), consumed by ED_LoadFromFile in engine/h2shared/pr_edict.c before the entity's spawn function ever runs. It is not a puzzle_piece flag and puzzle_piece() never sees a meaning in it: the QUAKED comment's flags are SPAWN(1) FLOATING(2) AUTO_GET(4), and 32768 sets none of them, so the piece takes the normal immediate-spawn else branch. Consequence: the scepter spawns in single player AND in co-op; only a deathmatch game removes it (the coop branch checks SPAWNFLAG_NOT_COOP = 0x10000, which egypt5 does not set). Both earlier passes on this bead left that number unexplained.

EGYPT5 PUZZLE ENTITY INVENTORY, read straight out of the BSP entity lump in data1/pak1.pak (bsp v29, 620 entities):
  puzzle_piece        scept  sf 32768  -2104 304 112     'Dark Pharaoh's Scepter'   no targetname
  puzzle_piece        e5     sf 32768  -924 2016 -402    'Duamutef Canopic Jar'     no targetname
  puzzle_static_piece scept  sf 32768  -1264 2664 -576   targetname t44             <- the slot the scepter goes into
  puzzle_piece        e4     sf 3      -1944 -1536 -480  'Hapy Canopic Jar'         targetname t55
  puzzle_piece        speye  sf 3      -696 -840 -272    'Serpents Eye Gem'         targetname t58
  puzzle_static_piece speye  sf 0      -1944 -1096 -496  targetname t48
  puzzle_static_piece rcjem  sf 0      -696 -728 -296    targetname t56
So the scepter and the Duamutef jar are both unconditional at map load; only e4 and speye are trigger-gated (sf 3 = SPAWN|FLOATING).

PRECEDENCE THEORY CHECKED AND KILLED. PlaceItem's guard is written 'if(!self.spawnflags&FLOATING)' (items.hc), which in C precedence would read (!spawnflags) & 1 and would send every entity with ANY nonzero spawnflags — including 32768 — down the no-droptofloor, no-resize path, leaving it zero-sized. That would have resurrected the original diagnosis by a different route. It does not happen: disassembling PlaceItem in BOTH retail data1/PROGS.DAT and our own build shows 'NOT_F (self.spawnflags & 1)', i.e. the compiler binds it as !(spawnflags & FLOATING). The scepter therefore takes the droptofloor branch and gets its setsize(-8 -8 -28, 8 8 8), confirming uhexen2-4p8t's in-engine observation. Leave the source line alone; it is ugly but correct as compiled.

STILL UNEXPLAINED, unchanged: what ReaperAA actually hit. Note the original report's workaround was 'noclip to grab jar' — the JAR, not the scepter. The Duamutef jar at -924 2016 -402 is the one they could not reach normally. That points at map geometry or hub progression around the jar, not at the scepter spawning. Next person: start from the jar.
close_reason:
ANSWERED, both halves, from live engine state plus BSP geometry. The report's premise is wrong on the scepter, and the jar has a concrete geometric cause.

1. THE SCEPTER SPAWNS. EVERY TIME. This is not a spawn failure and no more time should be spent looking for one.

Loaded egypt5 headless and dumped the server edicts. EDICT 106 exists: classname puzzle_piece, netname "Dark Pharaoh's Scepter", puzzle_id scept, model models/puzzle/scept.mdl, solid 1, touch puzzle_touch(), mins/maxs (-8 -8 -28)/(8 8 8). Of the map's 620 entities, 37 are inhibited on that load and it is not one of them. Everything the two earlier passes on this bead established -- spawnflags 32768 is NOT_DEATHMATCH, PlaceItem's guard compiles as !(spawnflags & FLOATING), so droptofloor and setsize both run -- holds, and the entity is right there in the edict list to prove it.

2. WHY THE PLAYER DOES NOT SEE IT: IT IS ON TOP OF A ROTATING PEDESTAL, 230 UNITS UP.

droptofloor did not drop it to the room floor. It landed on EDICT 56 and records groundentity = entity 56. Entity 56 is the func_door_rotating with targetname t22: classname door_rotating, model *24, origin (-2152 300 50), size 56x96x56, world extent (-2153 255 47)..(-2095 353 105). The scepter's final origin is (-2104 304 132), absmin z 104 -- resting exactly on that box's top face at z 105. The room's own floor is at player-origin z -96 (hull 1 vertical scan at that column gives one open run, -96..182), so the scepter sits roughly 230 units above where a player stands. A player walks in, sees it on a pedestal, and cannot touch it.

The pedestal's movedir is (-1 0 0): it rotates about the X axis, i.e. it TIPS, which is what delivers the scepter. It fires on t22, and the only thing that targets t22 is a func_button at (-1693 951 -119)..(-1679 971 -89) -- a 14x20x30 wall button roughly 650 units north, in a different room from the scepter (y 960 vs y 304), wait -1 so it is one-shot.

So "completed all required steps and the scepter did not spawn" is almost certainly "the pedestal never tipped": the button was not found, or was pressed and the rotation was blocked. That is a different search than the one this bead has been running.

3. THE JAR: A 32-UNIT LIP AT THE TOP OF A 16-UNIT STAIR FLIGHT.

This is the half the last pass pointed at ("start from the jar") and it resolves cleanly. Walking the world clipnode hull 1 east along y=2016 gives floor heights -504, -488, -472, -456 (three risers of exactly 16), and then the ledge the jar sits on at -424 -- a riser of 32. STEPSIZE is 18 (engine/hexen2/sv_phys.c:1564, and again in sv_move.c:25), so the last step cannot be walked up; it has to be jumped. And the ledge is a niche: the legal player-origin band there is -424..-401, about 23 units of headroom, against 111 units on the step below. So the player must jump a 32-unit lip and thread a 23-unit gap to land on it. PlayerJump adds 270*scale to velocity_z against sv_gravity 800, an apex near 45 units at scale 1, so it is possible -- but it is an awkward, easily-missed jump, which is exactly the shape of "noclip to grab jar".

The jar itself is fine: EDICT 107, dropped from its spawn z of -402 to -420, sitting on that ledge, solid and touchable.

METHOD, reusable: extract maps/egypt5.bsp from data1/pak1.pak; dmodel_t is EIGHTY bytes in Hexen II, not Quake's 64, because MAX_MAP_HULLS is 8 (common/bspfile.h:25) -- reading it as 64 gives plausible-looking garbage for low model indices and nonsense for high ones, which is a trap. World collision answers come from walking clipnodes with headnode[1] out of model 0. Live entity state comes from the 'edicts' command (pr_edict.c:3021) under a headless offscreen run.

REOPEN IF: a reporter confirms the t22 pedestal DID tip and the scepter still was not obtainable. Nothing found here explains that case.

description: Ship a Hexenwail-<tag>-x86_64.AppImage release asset alongside the existing linux zip, windows zip, and flatpak bundle. AppImage covers users on distros without flatpak setup and gives a single-file no-install download. Planned 2026-08-18; full design in the design field.
design:
GOAL: release.yml publishes Hexenwail-<tag>-x86_64.AppImage (+ .zsync) next to the linux/windows zips and the .flatpak bundle.

APPROACH DECISION — build the AppImage from a plain CMake build on ubuntu-22.04, NOT from the nix output:
- Option A (chosen): dedicated `appimage` job on ubuntu-22.04 (oldest supported glibc baseline for AppImage portability), plain CMake build of engine/, then linuxdeploy + appimagetool. The linuxdeploy exclude-list leaves libGL/Mesa/X11 to the host — mandatory for a GL 4.3 game, since the host's GPU driver stack must be used.
- Option B (rejected): `nix bundle` (e.g. ralismark/nix-appimage) over packages.nixos. One-liner and reuses the cachix cache, but it bundles the whole nixpkgs closure including glibc and SDL, and inherits the nixGL problem: nix-built libGL cannot load host DRI drivers on non-NixOS. Wrong tool for a GPU-bound app.

APPDIR CONTENTS (mirrors the flatpak manifest, flatpak/io.github.hexenwail.hexenwail.yml, which is the reference for the dependency set):
- usr/bin/glhexen2 — CMake Release build, USE_CODEC_VORBIS/OPUS/XMP=ON. Do NOT set SOUNDFONT_PATH (that define is for nix/flatpak absolute paths).
- usr/bin/soundfont.sf2 — TimGM6mb (GPL-2, ~6 MB, same Debian tarball the flatpak uses, sha256 af8f3a00e416dfb262bcaa904a1c84df04a51b72bbc1313aed012bc754bdf99b). NO engine change needed: engine/h2shared/soundfont.c already probes "<exedir>/soundfont.sf2" (step 2a, lines ~305-320) before the compile-time path.
- AppRun / launcher adapted from flatpak/hexenwail.sh: game-data discovery, offer scripts/get_demo.sh when no pak files present. Data lives in ~/.hexen2 as usual (AppImage is unsandboxed, no --persist needed).
- .desktop + icon at AppDir root (appimagetool requires both): reuse flatpak/io.github.hexenwail.hexenwail.desktop (adjust Exec) and engine/resource/hexen2.png.
- Optional: metainfo under usr/share/metainfo (AppImageHub reads it; same file the flatpak installs).

DEPENDENCIES ON THE RUNNER (ubuntu-22.04 apt lacks several):
- Built from source, same pins/config as the flatpak modules: SDL3 (not in 22.04), fluidsynth v2.4.6 (all audio backends -Denable-*=off — since uhexen2-tdss the engine renders MIDI itself via fluid_synth_write_s16 and never creates a fluidsynth audio driver; also -DCMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR=lib per uhexen2-rp1z), opusfile 0.12, libxmp 4.6.3.
- From apt: libvorbis, libogg, libopus, build tools.
- linuxdeploy walks ldd and pulls these into usr/lib automatically.

LINK GUARD: port the flatpak post-install SONAME assert — grep glhexen2 for libvorbisfile.so.3, libopusfile.so.0, libxmp.so.4, libfluidsynth.so.3 and fail the job if any is missing. engine/CMakeLists.txt silently disables missing codecs (that is what uhexen2-rp1z caught), so a green build proves nothing without this.

CI WIRING (release.yml):
- New `appimage` job, needs: lint (same gating as the flatpak job), uploads artifact `appimage-bundle`.
- publish job already downloads all artifacts; add the .AppImage (+ .zsync) to SHA256SUMS and the `gh release create` asset list.
- ci.yml: add the same job (or AppDir-only without appimagetool) so PRs catch bit-rot before a release run.
- Smoke test in-job: ./Hexenwail-*.AppImage --appimage-extract, then check the binary runs far enough to print version (no GPU on runners — extract+ldd check at minimum).

UPDATES (cheap, optional): embed zsync update info "gh-releases-zsync|<owner>|hexenwail|latest|Hexenwail-*x86_64.AppImage.zsync" and upload the .zsync appimagetool emits, enabling AppImageUpdate delta updates.

OPEN QUESTION: whether to embed gamecode/ (progs.dat) inside the AppDir. v1 matches the flatpak scope (engine only, player supplies game data + gamecode via the linux zip or existing install); embedding gamecode would need the HexenC toolchain in the job and a search-path decision, so it is deferred to a follow-up if wanted.

LOCAL TESTING NOTE: dev box is NixOS — run the produced AppImage via `nix run nixpkgs#appimage-run` (FUSE-free) rather than executing it directly.

title: Audit tail: remaining latent divergences and perf-trade gates
description:
Umbrella issue listing items deliberately deferred from the 2026-08-18 rendering audit, with file:line each:

(a) r_entdist only culls on the legacy phase-2 loop (gl_rmain.c:3517-3526), dead for instanced models.

(b) MAX_ALIAS_BATCHES=256 overflow silently drops entities (gl_rmain.c:2864-2865, instances already marked collected so the legacy loop skips them too).

(c) R_PushDlights uses the previous frame's frustum (called from view.c:1127 before R_RenderView) and a hard radius+1024 distance cap — visible behavior change vs vanilla, deserves cvar gates.

(d) r_skyspeed_back/front dead on the r_skyalpha>=1 single-pass sky path (hardcoded u_time/16, /8 in the sky shader).

(e) Alias mesh build overflow: StripLength/FanLength write stripverts[stripcount+2] unbounded into 128-entry arrays and BuildTris writes commands[8192] unbounded (gl_mesh.c:121-122, :203-204, :286-320), and GL_DrawAliasFrame's count>128 clamp (gl_rmain.c:913) would desync the command walk rather than protect it.

(f) Unhandled SCALE_TYPE+SCALE_ORIGIN both-bits combo: legacy path reuses stale tmatrix, instanced path zero-scales the model (gl_rmain.c:1322 vs :2628-2668).

(g) MD5 weight binning assumes file weight order matches vertex order (md5mesh.c:314-376) — legal non-monotonic MD5s get vertices' weights swapped.

(h) R_LightPoint (gl_rlight.c:517, declared glquake.h:537) now has zero callers engine-wide after the GL_LUMINANCE removal in 7d6e6a5c1 — dead non-static function, remove or fold into the umbrella cleanup.

title: Rain should use its own texture, not the shared particle sprite
description:
Mathuzzz: rain particles are visually near-identical to snow because both draw from the same 2x2 particle atlas, so a downpour reads as drifting flakes rather than falling water.

Suggestion: give pt_rain a dedicated raindrop sprite — an elongated streak oriented along the fall direction would read correctly and is cheap, since R_DrawParticles already builds per-particle billboards from vup/vright and could bias the rain ones toward the velocity vector.

Note the atlas already has four slots addressed by ptex_coord[], currently indexed only by snow flake size, so there is an obvious place to add a rain entry. Any change here must keep the atlas layout consistent with the square-mode fix in uhexen2-2rxl, which now bypasses the atlas entirely via gl_solid_white_texture.

Raised in the same Discord thread as the missing-rain report.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED in three commits, all building (client + h2ded):

1. a63a40618 — collision. pt_rain had no leaf test at all; it now does the same Mod_PointInLeaf check snow has always done and the drop dies where it lands. Behind r_raincollide (default 1) because it changes how existing maps look; 0 restores stock exactly. Point test not a sweep, so a brush thinner than 4-16 units can still be tunnelled at 60fps — snow has the identical limitation and Raven left a commented-out stepped sweep beside it.

2. 3ece827a8 — mapper-settable fall speed, NO protocol change needed. The Z of CE_RAIN's direction vector is already written by the server, parsed by the client and round-tripped through savegames, and was then discarded — only X and Y were ever read. That free field now carries the fall speed. Zero keeps the stock rand()%956-floored-at-256 spread, so all known content (SoT's weather_rain sets '125 100 0' or '0 0 0') is bit-for-bit unchanged. Jittered +/-25% so drops do not fall in lockstep, floored at 64 u/s so a typo cannot hang drops long enough to drain the pool (lifetime = brush height / speed). svc_raineffect has no Z and passes 0.

3. 8afd6cf49 — appearance. Could not add a raindrop to the atlas: it is 2x2 and all four slots are taken by the snow sizes. Instead the billboard is stretched 3x along the drop's own velocity and thinned to 0.5x across, so the same sprite and the same single triangle draw as a directional streak. Degenerate case (looking straight up/down the rain) falls back to the stock view-aligned axes rather than collapsing.

NOT VISUALLY VERIFIED — no rendered frame was taken. Compile-verified only, on both the GL client and h2ded.

Suggested A/B for a tester: 'map demo1' in SoT, then r_raincollide 0/1 to see drops stop at geometry, and compare the streak against a snow map (winter/tibet) to confirm rain no longer reads as flakes.

title: Drop the BadBackpackDump fallback from PR_ClassifyGamecode once pre-marker builds are gone
description:
PR_ClassifyGamecode() has a second probe: if the HexenwailGamecode marker is absent it looks for BadBackpackDump, which is ours (uhexen2-hwky) and absent from both retail files, and reports a bare 'hexenwail' with no date.

That exists only for our builds shipped BEFORE the marker landed (anything at or before 0.8.0-beta.r2, including hand-installed copies from earlier release zips -- crc 24008 and older). It is an incidental marker: it survives only as long as nobody reworks that diagnostic away, which is exactly the fragility ident.hc was added to replace.

Remove it once no pre-marker gamecode is plausibly still in the field. After removal those builds fall to 'Third-party', which is wrong but harmless, and the player's fix is to update their gamecode -- which is what we would tell them anyway.

Blocked on time passing, not on work. Revisit after a couple of releases have shipped with the marker.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-08-15: deferred. The precondition is measurably NOT met yet, and
the bead did not previously say what "a couple of releases" is counted from.
Pinning it now so the next reader does not have to re-derive it.

MEASURED:
  * the marker landed in 9ad50c27f ("say whose gamecode is loaded, not just
    which file"), dated 2026-08-15
  * git merge-base --is-ancestor 9ad50c27f 0.8.0-beta.r2  ->  NOT an ancestor

So 0.8.0-beta.r2, the newest tag, does NOT carry the marker. The count of
shipped releases containing it is currently ZERO, not one or two. The first
will be 0.8.0-beta.r3, which is unreleased. Every build in the field today is
a pre-marker build, which is exactly the population the BadBackpackDump probe
exists to serve -- removing it now would misreport every single current
install as "Third-party".

REVISIT WHEN: at least two tagged releases containing 9ad50c27f have shipped
and had time to propagate, i.e. 0.8.0-beta.r4 or later is out. Check with:

    git merge-base --is-ancestor 9ad50c27f <newest-tag>

and confirm at least two such tags exist. Removal is then a ~4-line deletion
of the ED_FindFunctioni("BadBackpackDump") arm in PR_ClassifyGamecode
(engine/h2shared/pr_edict.c), plus the comment above it.

Still blocked on time passing, not on work. Deferring rather than leaving it
in `bd ready`, where it has been showing up as actionable when it is not.
HASH CORRECTION 2026-08-19.  Cited as 9ad50c27f, which is not in master.  Survivor is 04aa22e01, same subject ('say whose gamecode is loaded, not just which file') and the same 20 paths across docs/, engine/ and gamecode/.

title: Interactively test the console TAB keypress path (needs a human or SDL key injection)
description:
Split out of uhexen2-npdb, which closed on the completers themselves (all seven commands are
wired and every lister is verified against real game data). This is the one item nobody has
been able to do headlessly.

## What is untested

The keypress-to-CompleteCommand path. Every lister has been exercised directly through the
real searchpaths, and CompleteCommand's parsing has been read, but nobody has actually
pressed TAB in a running console and watched it complete.

## Why it cannot be automated on this box

- The client never reads stdin: Host_GetConsoleCommands (hexen2/host.c) returns immediately
  unless isDedicated, so console text cannot be piped in.
- SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen, which is what makes the rest of the headless harness work,
  generates no input events at all.
- No console command invokes CompleteCommand, so there is nothing to drive it with from a
  cfg either.

So this needs either a human at a keyboard or SDL key-event injection built into the engine
for testing.

## What to check when someone does sit down with it

Press TAB after each, mid-line as well as at the end (CompleteCommand completes only up to
the cursor, bash style, and splices the tail back -- that path is easy to get wrong):

  map <TAB>, changelevel <TAB>, game <TAB>, record <TAB>, record foo <TAB> (arg 2 -> maps),
  playdemo <TAB>, timedemo <TAB>, exec <TAB>, save <TAB>, load <TAB>, sky <TAB>

Specifically worth checking:
1. A unique prefix completes fully and appends a space.
2. An ambiguous prefix completes to the common stem and lists the candidates.
3. No match leaves the line untouched rather than eating characters.
4. Mid-line TAB preserves the text after the cursor.
5. sky <TAB> in a gamedir with no gfx/env (stock data1 has none -- use -game sot or karma2
   for the populated case) does nothing rather than misbehaving.
6. The completion still frees its name list -- every row's cleanup is FS_FreeNameList, and
   the list is shared and single-owner, so a leaked one would break the NEXT completion.
close_reason:
DONE 2026-08-15. All eight checks pass. The bead's premise was wrong: it said
this needs "a human or SDL key injection built into the engine", but
tools/headless-drive.sh already drives the engine under Xvfb with xdotool,
which delivers REAL X key events through SDL into Key_Event. Both facts the
bead cited are true (offscreen SDL emits no input, the client never reads
stdin) -- they just are not the only options. Nothing had to be built.

Added a console_tab scenario (d207c7e9c). Run:

  nix shell nixpkgs#xorg.xvfb nixpkgs#xdotool --command \
    ./tools/headless-drive.sh console_tab /tmp/out ~/hexen2 -condebug +"map demo1"

RESULTS, against stock data1 (42 maps; eidolon is the only eido*, romeric1..7
the only rom*, nothing matches zzz):

 1. unique arg          "map eido"          -> "map eidolon " (trailing space)  PASS
 2. ambiguous arg       "map rom"           -> "map romeric" + "7 possible
                                               completions:" columnized list    PASS
 3. no match            "map zzz"           -> line untouched, nothing eaten    PASS
 4. mid-line splice     "map eido|XY"       -> "map eidolon XY", tail restored  PASS
 5. command word        "sv_altnoc"         -> "sv_altnoclip "                  PASS
 6. arg slot 2          "record foo eido"   -> "record foo eidolon " (completed
                                               against MAPS, not demos)         PASS
 7. sky, no gfx/env     "sky "              -> nothing, line untouched          PASS
 8. repeat after 7      "map eido"          -> identical to case 1, so the
                                               shared single-owner name list is
                                               not leaking across completions   PASS

TWO HARNESS BUGS FIXED to get here, both worth knowing about:

1. bwrap binds a throwaway dir over $HOME, and a source checkout lives under
   $HOME too, so the sandbox was hiding ./result -- the binary it then tried to
   exec. Presented as a bare "No such file or directory" from env, which reads
   like a missing build. Fixed with an ro-bind after the HOME bind (same
   treatment basedir already had) plus readlink -f.

2. SILENT FAILURE MODE, recorded because it will catch the next person: the
   console cannot be opened from the main menu. Escape closes the menu, but
   with nothing connected and no demo loop the engine reopens it immediately,
   and a menu eats grave. The run then takes all eight screenshots of an
   untouched main menu and exits 0. Hence the mandatory +map demo1.

Not covered: everything here is the standard console. No claim is made about
the protocol-21 or HexenWorld clients.

title: Classic Software look: affine (perspective-incorrect) texture interpolation
description:
Item 3 of uhexen2-lpza's ranked list, the one part deliberately left out of that bead's first
pass. lpza closed with palette quantization through Raven's colormap verified exact (100% of
scene pixels are palette members under r_softemu 3); this is the remaining piece of the
1997 look.

## What it is

The 1997 span rasterizer interpolated texture coordinates linearly in screen space rather
than correcting for perspective, which is why floors and walls visibly wobble and swim as
the camera moves near them. It is the second most recognisable part of the software look
after the palette, and unlike the palette it cannot be done in the post chain.

## Why it is more invasive than the rest of lpza

Everything else in that bead lives in gl_postprocess.c and operates on the finished frame.
This one has to change how the world is rasterised: the texture coordinate varyings in the
world fragment path need the GLSL "noperspective" interpolation qualifier, gated by a cvar.
That means touching the main world shader (h2shared/gl_shader.c) and any other path that
should match -- alias models were also affine in 1997, so leaving them perspective-correct
would look inconsistent.

"noperspective" is core in GLSL 1.30+ but is NOT available in GLSL ES -- it does not exist
in ES 3.0/3.10. So the WASM/WebGL2 tier cannot have this at all, and the shader generator
has to branch rather than just splice a qualifier in. Decide whether the cvar simply reports
unavailable there or whether a fragment-side approximation is worth it (it probably is not).

## Suggested scope

- A cvar, default off, alongside r_softemu rather than folded into it -- the two are
  independent and someone may want palette quantization without the wobble.
- World surfaces first; decide on alias models with a screenshot rather than in the abstract.
- Fold into the Crunchy/Retro presets only after it is seen working.

## Verification

Same harness as lpza. This one is NOT machine-checkable the way palette membership was --
the wobble is a motion artifact, so a single still frame will not show it. Capture a short
fixed-path camera move (the burst-of-screenshots pattern) with it on and off and compare
frames near a large floor, where the effect is strongest.

title: Tab completion: wire remaining completers (exec, save, load, sky) and test interactive keypress
description:
Follow-up to uhexen2-nzuo (console argument tab completion landed in afcc75e68).

## What Is Not Yet Done

The tab completion infrastructure is now in place with listers verified against real game data in a live engine. However:

1. **Interactive TAB keypress never tested** — completion logic is harness-verified, but the keypress-to-CompleteCommand wiring is pre-existing code that was not exercised end to end in a real console session. Needs manual interactive testing or test-harness SDL key event injection.

2. **Three completers remain unwired** — now that the (command, argument_index) table pattern is established, these are simple one-line additions to `engine/hexen2/keys.c`:
   - `exec` arg1 → ListCfgs (.cfg files, similar to ListDemos pattern)
   - `save` arg1 → ListSaves (existing game saves)
   - `load` arg1 → ListSaves (existing game saves)
   - `sky` arg1 → ListSkies (hardcoded skybox asset names or enumeration, if applicable)

## Definition of Done

- Add exec/save/load/sky rows to arg_completion_types table
- Wire corresponding list functions in quakefs.c if they don't exist
- Manual or automated interactive test: press TAB mid-line after each command, verify completes correctly
- Build clean on nix targets

## Notes

This is a small follow-up; the design and primary infrastructure are complete.
notes:
COMPLETERS DONE in 3262fe089. The interactive-keypress half is split out -- see below.

WIRED, all four the bead asked for, as rows in keys.c :: arg_completion_types:
  exec arg1 -> ListCfgs, save arg1 -> ListSaves, load arg1 -> ListSaves, sky arg1 -> ListSkies

ListCfgs (h2shared/quakefs.c): ListDemos with a different extension.

ListSkies: scans gfx/env for *_rt.{png,tga,pcx} and trims the suffix -- exactly what
Sky_LoadSkyBox looks for (it builds gfx/env/<name>_<suf>.<ext> and tries those three in that
order). Only the rt face is required; demanding all six would hide a half-installed skybox
the loader itself accepts face by face. A trailing underscore turned out NOT to be a second
naming convention -- Sky_LoadSkyBox's '_' branch only declines to double the separator, so
'moon' and 'moon_' resolve to the same files and 'moon' is the form to offer.

Three extensions needed three scans, so FS_ScanFiles gained a reset flag (FS_ScanFilesEx);
the old name is now a wrapper that always resets, so ListMaps/ListDemos are unchanged.

ListSaves: directories under fs_userdir holding an info.dat, NOT the menu's fixed s0..sN /
ms0..msN slots -- the console commands take an arbitrary name. info.dat is what
Host_Loadgame_f opens first, so that test is the loader's own; a directory without one would
complete and then fail. Offered for 'save' too, so overwriting is as easy to type as loading.

VERIFIED against the retail install, -game sot, via a temporary harness calling each lister
through the real searchpaths (harness removed before commit):
  cfgs   9 names; Config.cfg + config.cfg dedupe to one 'config'; prefix 'co' -> 1
  skies  10 names: sky dunes dunes_night duske grimmnight heather night_01 ofelas volcano
         Tibet. Underscores inside names preserved, on-disk casing preserved; 'du' -> 3
  saves  exactly the two fixture dirs with info.dat, a third without one correctly absent;
         prefix 'zz' -> 0
maplist still lists the same 40 maps after the FS_ScanFilesEx split.

NOT DONE, and not doable from here: item 1, the interactive TAB keypress test. The client
does not read stdin (Host_GetConsoleCommands returns early unless isDedicated) and the
offscreen SDL driver generates no input, so there is no way to press TAB without a human at a
keyboard. That item is also about pre-existing keypress-to-CompleteCommand wiring rather than
anything this change touched. Filed separately.
close_reason: Closed

title: Dead software-renderer scaffolding: h2shared/draw.c and screen.c are unbuilt and unbuildable
description:
Found while surveying what the SDL3/GL4.3 modernization left behind. Gated on the software
renderer restoration decision, because that decision determines whether this is a seed or
litter.

`a14b5eecd` deleted the software rasterizer but did not finish the job. Two files remain in
`engine/h2shared/` that nothing builds:

    engine/h2shared/draw.c     1897 lines
    engine/h2shared/screen.c   1471 lines

Neither appears anywhere in `engine/CMakeLists.txt` or `engine/cmake/` -- the build compiles
`gl_draw.c` and `gl_screen.c` instead. Confirmed by grep for both `COMMONDIR`- and
`h2shared`-relative spellings.

They are not merely unbuilt, they are UNBUILDABLE: `draw.c` makes 23 references to
`d_pzbuffer` / `vid.buffer` / `surfcache` and `screen.c` one, and the definitions for those
went out with `d_vars.c` and `d_surf.c`. So the files cannot be validated by any build, and
nothing will ever tell us they have bit-rotted further.

Alongside them, 65 `GLQUAKE` conditionals survive across ~20 files (was 135 across 40 at the
`a0304b781` fork point). Some are live and load-bearing for the GL build -- `draw.h`'s
`#else` arms define `Draw_MenuBackdrop()` and `Draw_FlushCharBatch()` as no-ops, for
instance. But the substantial `#ifndef GLQUAKE` arms in `view.c`, `sbar.c`, `menu.c` and
`r_part.c` are dead code that has not been compiled since 2021 and cannot be compiled now.

## The decision this needs

Both readings are defensible, which is why this is filed rather than just fixed:

- **Seed.** If the restoration bead comes back YES, these files and those conditional arms
  are exactly the scaffolding it would rebuild against, and deleting them means recovering
  them from `a0304b781` anyway.
- **Litter.** If it comes back NO, this is 3,368 lines of uncompilable code plus dead
  branches in four hot files, all of it looking maintained to anyone reading the tree.
  Nothing in the tree currently says it is dead. `git checkout a0304b781 -- <path>` recovers
  any of it at any time, so deleting loses nothing.

Either way the current state -- present, unmarked, unbuildable -- is the one option that is
wrong, because it silently misleads.

## If the answer is delete

Remove `h2shared/draw.c` and `h2shared/screen.c`, and strip the `#ifndef GLQUAKE` arms in
`view.c`, `sbar.c`, `menu.c`, `r_part.c`. Keep the `draw.h` `#else` no-op defines -- those
are live. Record in the commit that `a0304b781` is the recovery point, so the archaeology
is not lost.

## If the answer is keep

Put a header comment in both files and at the top of each surviving `#ifndef GLQUAKE` block
saying it is retained deliberately as restoration scaffolding, that it does not compile
today, and naming the bead. Undocumented dead code is the failure mode here, not the dead
code itself.

## Acceptance

Either the files and dead conditional arms are gone with the recovery point recorded, or
they are annotated as deliberate scaffolding. Not left as-is.
acceptance_criteria: Either the two files and the dead #ifndef GLQUAKE arms are removed with a0304b781 recorded as the recovery point, or they carry a header saying they are deliberate scaffolding that does not compile. Not left as-is.
notes:
VERIFIED AND RE-MEASURED 2026-08-15. Every factual claim about the two files
holds. The claim about the surviving conditionals does not, and the delete arm
is a lot smaller and safer than this bead makes it sound.

## Confirmed exactly as written

    engine/h2shared/draw.c     1897 lines
    engine/h2shared/screen.c   1471 lines   (3368 total)

Neither appears in engine/CMakeLists.txt or engine/cmake/ under any spelling.
draw.c carries 22 lines referencing d_pzbuffer / vid.buffer / surfcache and
screen.c one; grep for d_pzbuffer across the whole of engine/ outside these two
files returns NOTHING, so the definitions really are gone and the files really
are unbuildable.

## Corrected: the conditionals

The bead says "65 GLQUAKE conditionals survive across ~20 files" and that
"the substantial #ifndef GLQUAKE arms in view.c, sbar.c, menu.c and r_part.c
are dead code". Current counts:

    73 occurrences across 23 files
    (72 across 22, excluding one in engine/build/CMakeFiles, a build artifact)

But an occurrence is not a dead arm. Measuring the actual non-GL arms:

    engine/hexen2/view.c     #else at 649 -> #endif at 737     ~87 lines
    engine/hexen2/r_part.c   #else at 1631 -> #endif at 1724   ~92 lines
    engine/hexen2/view.c     1057-1061                            1 line
    engine/hexen2/r_part.c   1410-1423                           ~4 lines
    engine/hexen2/sbar.c     292-295                              2 lines
    engine/hexen2/menu.c     all 11 occurrences are #ifdef GLQUAKE arms that
                             are LIVE in the GL build; only 5220-5235 has an
                             #else, and it is small

So the dead software code in the "four hot files" is roughly 185 lines
concentrated in TWO files (view.c and r_part.c). sbar.c's share is two lines and
menu.c has essentially none. "Dead branches in four hot files" overstates it by
about an order of magnitude, and menu.c and sbar.c should come off the delete
list -- touching them buys nothing and risks a live GL path.

Revised delete arm: 3368 lines (two whole files) + ~185 lines in two files.
The draw.h #else no-op defines stay live, as the bead already says.

## On the gate

This is blocked on uhexen2-q8g5, which is still open -- but q8g5 has already
recorded its recommendation ("don't restore it -- emulate the look"), and its
emulation alternative uhexen2-lpza (quantize through Raven's colormap in the
post-process chain) is CLOSED, i.e. the substitute has already shipped. So the
seed reading is close to dead on the merits; what is missing is only the
formal yes/no q8g5 asks for.

Worth noting the annotate arm is safe under BOTH outcomes and is the reversible
one. If q8g5 keeps sitting, taking the annotate arm now would satisfy this
bead's acceptance ("not left as-is") without prejudging the decision, and the
delete arm stays available afterwards at zero extra cost. Recommend either
settling q8g5 or unblocking this to annotate-only.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER EDITS: engine/hexen2/sbar.c had uncommitted work in the tree
when this was measured (uhexen2-1knr). Line numbers above are from that working
tree; re-check them against HEAD before editing.
close_reason: Resolved by the software-renderer restoration; the gating decision uhexen2-q8g5 came back YES. draw.c and screen.c are no longer dead scaffolding — both are built as part of SOFT_RENDERER_SOURCES (engine/CMakeLists.txt:430-431) and compile under -DWEB_RENDERER=software, so the surfcache / d_pzbuffer / vid.buffer definitions they reference are present again via the restored d_vars.c and d_surf.c. Both files also picked up real WEBSOFT-guarded work since this was filed (draw.c:301 calls Draw_SoftWebInit; screen.c:103/:494 own scr_centerprintbg and scr_menubgstyle for the software build). The seed-vs-litter question this issue was filed to force is answered: seed. Verified 2026-08-20.

title: Decide whether to restore the 1997 software renderer, or emulate its look
description:
Hexenwail deleted the 1997 edge/span software rasterizer during the SDL3/GL4.3
modernization. This bead records what was removed, what survived, what actually blocks a
restoration, and recommends the cheaper alternative.

## What was deleted, and where it still lives

Fork point is `a0304b781` ("Shanjaq fork (2018-2021)"). The renderer was removed by its
child `a14b5eecd` ("Hexenwail: SDL3/GL4.3 modernization (2025-2026)"). Everything is
recoverable with `git checkout a0304b781 -- <path>`.

~29,200 lines across 45 files:

- `engine/h2shared/d_*.c` (15 files) -- the span/edge rasterizer proper: d_edge, d_fill,
  d_init, d_modech, d_part, d_polyse, d_scan, d_sky, d_sprite, d_surf, d_vars, d_zpoint,
  plus d_iface.h / d_local.h
- `engine/h2shared/r_{aclip,bsp,draw,edge,efrag,light,sky,sprite,surf,vars}.c` + r_local.h,
  r_shared.h
- `engine/h2shared/model.c` + `model.h` -- a PARALLEL model loader to gl_model.c, with its
  own `msurface_t` carrying `cachespots[MIPLEVELS]`
- `engine/h2shared/draw.c`, `screen.c` -- the 8-bit 2D layer
- `engine/h2shared/vid_{sdl,win,dos,vga,svgalib,ext,cgx}.c` -- seven video backends
- `engine/hexen2/r_{alias,main,misc}.c` and the same three under
  `engine/hexenworld/client/`
- ~20 assembly files: d_draw.asm, d_draw16.asm, d_copy.asm, d_parta/d_partb.asm,
  d_polysa[2-5].asm, plus 68k Amiga variants (d_scan68k.s, amiga_r_68k.s, c2p1x1_*.s)

Note the build at the fork point was a first-class dual target: `engine/hexen2/Makefile`
defines `SW_BINARY:=hexen2` and `GL_BINARY:=glhexen2`, selected by `GL_DEFS = -DGLQUAKE`.
This was a maintained configuration as recently as the Shanjaq fork, not an abandoned one.

Do NOT use upstream uHexen2 master as the restoration base. `459c5a07b` ("software
renderer: remove all polygon based drawing code", Ozkan Sezer, 2024-06-11) stripped 508
lines of polygon drawing from d_edge/r_bsp/r_draw/r_edge/r_main. That commit is NOT an
ancestor of our fork point, so `a0304b781` carries the more complete renderer. Verified with
`git merge-base --is-ancestor`.

## What survived, which is more than expected

1. `viddef_t` (`engine/h2shared/vid.h`) is essentially unchanged -- `buffer`, `colormap`,
   `colormap16`, `rowbytes`, `conbuffer`, `conrowbytes`, `direct`, `maxwarpwidth/height` all
   still declared. Vestigial under GL, but the interface did not rot away.
2. The colormap still loads. `host.c :: Host_Init()` reads `gfx/colormap.lmp` into
   `host_colormap` and Sys_Errors without it; `gl_vidsdl.c` still assigns
   `vid.colormap = host_colormap`. The software lighting model's input is present.
3. The 8-bit texels are still in memory. `texture_t` (`gl_model.h`) still carries
   `offsets[MIPLEVELS]`, and `gl_model.c :: Mod_LoadTextures()` still copies the miptex data
   inline after the struct. The surface cache would still find what it needs.
4. 65 `GLQUAKE` conditionals survive across ~20 files (down from 135 across 40). Crucially
   `view.c`, `sbar.c`, `menu.c`, `r_part.c` and `draw.h` still carry REAL `#else` /
   `#ifndef GLQUAKE` software branches -- the non-GL arms in the shared consumers were
   preserved through the modernization, not deleted.
5. `engine/hexen2/render.h`, the software renderer's public interface, still exists.

## What actually blocks it

1. **No software model loader.** `model.c`/`model.h` are gone and `gl_model.c` is now the
   only one. `msurface_t` losing `cachespots[MIPLEVELS]` is trivial to undo (four pointers),
   but gl_model.c has since grown VBO offsets, sky-stencil indices, PimpModel snapshot state
   (uhexen2-oq0a), `content_class` (uhexen2-8nvj) and `translucent_turb` (uhexen2-ft2q).
   Either restore the parallel loader and maintain two forever, or teach one loader to serve
   both.

2. **The shared consumers diverged hard.** Diffstat `a0304b781..HEAD` on the files both
   renderers use: menu.c +6092, console.c +583, sbar.c +480, cl_parse.c +479, cl_main.c
   +444, r_part.c +337. menu.c in particular was rebuilt around a GL-only canvas system
   (`GL_SetCanvas`, `scr_sbarscale` / `scr_menuscale` / `scr_crosshairscale`, declared
   inside `#if defined(GLQUAKE)` in draw.h). Those surviving `#ifndef GLQUAKE` arms are five
   years stale and have never been compiled against any of it. This is the bulk of the work
   and it is NOT recoverable by checkout -- it has to be written.

3. **Alias models.** The PimpModel refactor and the GPU skeletal path reshaped `aliashdr_t`
   / `qmodel_t`. Software `r_alias.c` expects the 1997 layout.

4. **Every feature added since is GL-only.** Shader fog, skybox, OIT, the post-process
   chain, render scale, bicubic lightmaps, GPU particles, the ES tier. A software build is
   not just a renderer -- it is a permanent feature-regression branch of the options menu
   too.

5. **The assembly is x86-32 and DOS/Amiga-era.** Dead weight on x86-64; the C fallbacks
   exist but deliver 1997 C performance without the hand-tuned inner loops that made the
   original fast.

## Recommendation: don't restore it -- emulate the look

If the goal is the 1997 *look* -- 8-bit palette quantization, the colormap's lighting ramp,
affine/warped texture interpolation, low resolution -- that is a post-process and shader
problem, and Hexenwail already owns both halves: `gl_postprocess.c` and the render-scale
control. `host_colormap` is already loaded and can be uploaded as a LUT. Filed separately.

That gets most of the aesthetic for a small fraction of the cost and zero maintenance fork.

If the goal is genuinely the 1997 *code path* -- exact span-rasterizer output, historical
fidelity, running with no GPU at all -- then this is weeks of full-time work to first pixel
and a permanent tax on every future change, and it should be decided as such rather than
drifted into.

## Acceptance

A recorded decision. If NO, say so here and decide the fate of the dead scaffolding still in
the tree (filed separately). If YES, this needs decomposing into its own epic first --
do not start by checking files out.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded yes/no with reasoning. If no, the dead-scaffolding bead is unblocked to delete. If yes, this is decomposed into an epic before any files are checked out.
close_reason:
DECISION: YES, restored — but by a route this bead did not consider, which is why the recommendation (don't restore, emulate) was not what happened. Both paths were in fact taken.

The restoration landed via uhexen2-vcif (mining alextnewman/hexenwail), which had already done the port. That sidestepped the two blockers this bead judged fatal:

- Blocker 1 (no software model loader): dodged, not solved. model.c/model.h were restored verbatim as a parallel loader rather than teaching gl_model.c to serve both. quakeinc.h:83 records why — the surface cache, sprite pixel data and skin descriptors the software path needs were dropped from the GL model layer years ago.
- Blocker 2 (shared consumers diverged): dodged via a new WEBSOFT guard (distinct from WEBQUAKE, which marks the browser platform) rather than by reviving the five-year-stale #ifndef GLQUAKE arms. Only six WEBSOFT sites exist: quakeinc.h:83, r_part.c:23, menu.c:2848, draw.c:301, screen.c:103 and :494.
- Blocker 4 (every feature since is GL-only) was accepted rather than solved: r_soft_web.c registers the GPU-only cvars purely so shared configs link and round-trip, and menu.c:2848 hides the rows they drive.
- Blocker 5 (x86-32 assembly) is moot — the target is WASM, so the C fallbacks are the only path anyway.

Scope is narrower than this bead assumed: software is an opt-in web config (-DWEB_RENDERER=software), not a restored desktop target. webgl2 remains the default at engine/CMakeLists.txt:66 and scripts/wasm-build.sh:22. So there is no permanent maintenance fork of the desktop build.

The emulate-the-look alternative this bead recommended also shipped independently, as uhexen2-lpza (closed).

Unblocks uhexen2-t8j8: the scaffolding is a seed, not litter. Verified 2026-08-20.

title: GL_LoadTexture retires a gltexture_t slot on every flag mismatch and never reclaims it
description:
GL_LoadTexture (engine/h2shared/gl_draw.c:2559) handles a re-upload of an existing texture name whose crc, mipmap flag, alpha/holey/fence flags or dimensions changed by retiring the old entry rather than reusing it: it deletes the GL texture, removes the hash entry, sets glt->identifier[0] = 0 to mark the slot stale, and falls through to allocate a fresh entry at gltextures[numgltextures++]. That is deliberate and correct as far as it goes -- the comment (uhexen2-0fsq) explains that reusing the slot would reissue an invalid handle to code that cached the old texnum.

What is missing is reclamation. Nothing scans for stale slots to reuse, so numgltextures only ever grows, and MAX_GLTEXTURES (glquake.h:29) is 8192 with a Sys_Error('cache full, max is %i textures') behind it. The lookups that matter already skip stale entries correctly (gl_draw.c:450, 503, 542), so this is purely slot exhaustion, not a correctness bug.

Bounded in practice today, which is why this is P4: a full texture flush on map change resets the array, and the re-upload paths are rare. But the count is now one higher than it was -- 1cb4cdd4c added Mod_ReuploadAliasSkins, which fires once per model per map that a misc_modelpimp grants EF_HOLEY to, and each such call retires one slot per skin. Confirmed at runtime on SoT cathedral: 'Texture cache mismatch: 1533, models/book_0, creating new entry'.

The cheap fix is a first-free-stale-slot scan before allocating at numgltextures, which is safe precisely because the stale entry's texnum was already glDeleteTextures'd and its hash entry removed. Measure first: instrument how many stale slots a long session actually accumulates before deciding it is worth any code at all.

ACCEPTANCE: either stale slots are reclaimed, or a measurement shows the worst realistic session stays far enough under 8192 that the growth is documented and closed as accepted.
close_reason: Fixed in cda9466a6. GL_ClaimStaleTexture reclaims retired slots (marked with texnum == GL_UNUSED_TEXTURE), so numgltextures no longer grows on every flag/crc mismatch. Only slots at or above gl_texlevel are offered, because D_ClearOpenGLTextures purges by index range and a map texture below the static watermark would survive map changes. D_ClearOpenGLTextures now skips retired slots instead of re-deleting their names — measured on Mesa the driver recycles a freed name into the very next glGenTextures, so the dangling texnum on a stale slot is likely to belong to a live texture by flush time. Verified with a throwaway console command loading one identifier three times with different content: before 736 -> 737 -> 738 -> 739, after 736 -> 737 -> 737 -> 737, lookup still resolving to the newest upload. Note for the record: the returned GL name is recycled identically with and without the fix (943 in both control runs), so uhexen2-0fsq's handle-reissue concern never depended on which array slot was used.

title: Pin the real progs2.dat map count
description:
gamecode/README.txt previously asserted "Ten late-game maps use progs2.dat", drawn from ten entries in data1/pak0.pak's maplist.txt. However, docs/GAMECODE.md records that five of those names (rick3–rick7) ship in no retail pak — they are listed in the maplist but the map files do not exist in any shipped archive.

The text was softened to "Some" in 17f8c258c rather than asserting a number that may be wrong. This is safer but less useful to a player.

Someone should establish the actual count of maps a player can reach that use progs2.dat by examining the retail pak files. Known-present maps using progs2.dat are: eidolon, romeric6, meso9, rider1a, rider2c. Once verified, restore a concrete accurate count to gamecode/README.txt.

Related context: the same observation (rick3–rick7 non-existent) exposed that docs/GAMECODE.md was using rick3 as a verification test for progs2.dat, which was corrected to eidolon.
close_reason: Answered and pinned in ac268bde5: the count is FIVE. Verified against the retail install at /home/josh/hexen2 (data1/pak0.pak, data1/pak1.pak, portals/pak3.pak), not from the maplist alone. maplist.txt (pak0.pak, 193 bytes) names ten maps, all mapping to progs2.dat. rick3-rick7 are in no retail pak. The other five -- rider1a, rider2c, meso9, romeric6, eidolon -- are all in pak1.pak AND all reachable in normal play: scanning the entity lump of all 42 .bsp files in pak0+pak1 for 'map' keys shows village2->rider1a, egypt1->rider2c, meso8->meso9, romeric5->romeric6, castle5->eidolon, while rick3-rick7 are named by no map entity anywhere. So 'exists' and 'reachable' give the same answer, five. Changes: (1) flake.nix README.txt generator now says 'Five maps use progs2.dat and the rest use progs.dat: rider1a, rider2c, meso9, romeric6 and eidolon' instead of hedging with 'Some'; (2) docs/GAMECODE.md gained the reachability table; (3) added scripts/progs2_maps.py, which re-derives the list and count from any install so this does not have to be redone by hand. flake still evaluates (nix eval .#release.drvPath).

title: progs entityfields is not range-checked
description: Server-side progs entityfields range checking. CSQC half fixed in c1b139f83 via PR_CheckProgsExtents() validation in engine/hexen2/cl_csqc.c (see uhexen2-la6r for reference implementation and guard pattern). PR_LoadProgs still has unguarded entityfields in pr_edict.c — apply same overflow-safe validation before pr_edict_size computation.
close_reason:
IMPLEMENTATION (bc9fbb288): guard added in PR_LoadProgs() (engine/h2shared/pr_edict.c), placed after the header byteswap and version switch so progs->entityfields is in host order, and before the crc switch so a bad value is named rather than shadowed by 'Unexpected crc'. Same predicate CL_LoadCSProgs() already used: reject entityfields < 0 or > (INT_MAX - sizeof(edict_t)) / 4.

RUNTIME EVIDENCE (h2ded, real data1): forged entityfields = -1 -> 'Host_Error: progs.dat has bad entityfields (-1)'; forged entityfields = 2^30 -> 'Host_Error: progs.dat has bad entityfields (1073741824)'. Unmodified control still loads and 'map demo1' still starts (real images carry entityfields = 390-392).

Host_Error rather than a silent decline is correct here: unlike csprogs.dat this is the game's own progs, and the bundled-progs path already falls back to the player's copy before reaching this point.

title: FS_ReadIntoBuffer ignores fread's return value
description: quakefs.c:1093 does not check fread, so a genuine short read (stat reports N, read yields M<N) goes undetected. Not memory-unsafe: the buffer is len+1 and Hunk_AllocName zeroes, so the tail reads as zeros. Fixing it would change semantics for every loader in the engine, which is why 9f52d0a6a left it. Worth doing deliberately or documenting as accepted. Link to uhexen2-sgw7.
close_reason:
IMPLEMENTATION (bc9fbb288): FS_ReadIntoBuffer() (engine/h2shared/quakefs.c) now captures fread's return, zero-fills the unread tail, and warns via Sys_Printf.

DECIDED DELIBERATELY, per the bead's 'worth doing deliberately or documenting as accepted' — done, not documented, because the bead's own premise was incomplete. It said 'not memory-unsafe: the buffer is len+1 and Hunk_AllocName zeroes'. That holds only for LOADFILE_HUNK/TEMPHUNK. LOADFILE_MALLOC (malloc), LOADFILE_CACHE (Cache_Alloc) and LOADFILE_STACK (the caller's loadbuf) do NOT zero, so on those paths a short read left the tail as whatever the allocator was holding and the caller parsed it as file content. That is a real uninitialized-memory read, not merely an undetected truncation.

SEMANTICS UNCHANGED, which is what kept 9f52d0a6a from touching this: the function still returns the buffer, callers still size their parsing from fs_filesize, no new error path. Behaviour on the hunk paths is bit-identical to before (they were already zeroed); the other three now match them.

RUNTIME EVIDENCE (h2ded): crafted pak2.pak whose directory advertises 'shorttest.cfg' as 50000 bytes at offset 12 while the file physically holds 93 bytes there. Result: 'WARNING: FS_ReadIntoBuffer: short read on shorttest.cfg (93 of 50000 bytes)', then 'execing shorttest.cfg' and the real content ran — loader contract intact, tail zeroed so parsing stopped cleanly instead of running on. NO spurious warnings during normal startup: pak0 (696 files), pak1 (523 files), progs.dat and csprogs.dat all load silently in both h2ded and the GL client.

title: sv_globals walk trusts the progdefs CRC for numglobals
description: The for (; def->field; def++) set_address(def, &G_FLOAT(def->offset)) walk in PR_LoadProgs relies on the progdefs CRC to guarantee numglobals is at least as large as the fixed block. Not reachable by truncation — a truncated file keeps its original header, and a forged-large numglobals is now rejected by PR_CheckProgsExtents — but a deliberately forged small numglobals could place those pointers a few hundred bytes past the lump. Threat model is a malicious file, not a corrupt one. Link to uhexen2-sgw7.
close_reason:
IMPLEMENTATION (bc9fbb288): PR_LoadProgs() now measures the reach of the globals table the progdefs CRC selected and checks progs->numglobals against it, immediately before the 'for (; def->field; def++) set_address(...)' walk. The measurement takes its own cursor because def is the walk's cursor. Reach is max(offset + width) over the table, width 3 for ev_vector and 1 otherwise — derived from the table rather than hard-coded, so it tracks any future globalvars_t change automatically.

Threat model confirmed as the bead framed it: a forged-LARGE numglobals is already refused by PR_CheckProgsExtents(); this closes the forged-SMALL case, which keeps a valid-looking progdefs CRC for a layout the image no longer has.

RUNTIME EVIDENCE (h2ded, real data1): forged numglobals = 10 -> 'Host_Error: progs.dat declares 10 globals, H2/v1.11 structures need 105'. Note the CRC switch still matched, exactly as predicted — progs->crc is the progdefs interface CRC, not a checksum over the file, so editing numglobals does not disturb it. That is what made this reachable. Unmodified control still loads and starts demo1; real images carry numglobals 46448-64658 against a requirement of 105, so the margin for legitimate files is ~450x.

title: Console copy pads every non-terminal line with trailing whitespace
description:
Copying a multi-line console selection to the clipboard pads each non-terminal line out to the full console width with spaces, so pasting a console log produces ragged trailing whitespace on every line. engine/hexen2/console.c:1040 and :1050 set line_end = con_linewidth - 1 for the first and middle lines of every multi-line selection, so the padding is baseline behavior — it is not caused by clicking past end-of-line, and it affects every multi-line copy.

Purely cosmetic. Found 2026-08-13 while investigating uhexen2-z8je (which closed as not-applicable).

## CRITICAL WARNING

Anyone who fixes this MUST read this section first. The obvious fix is to trim trailing spaces in Con_CopySelectionToClipboard. **Trimming is EXACTLY what creates the crash hazard that Ironwail had to patch in c03a5bdc1:** once the line end is a trimmed length, it can fall BELOW line_start, and any length arithmetic (end - start) then underflows. 

Hexenwail is currently immune only because it never trims and uses a bounded `col <= line_end` loop. **If a trim is added, an explicit `line_start > line_end` guard MUST be added with it,** and the loop must not be converted to pointer+length form. Fixing this cosmetic wart carelessly would introduce a crash bug that does not currently exist.
close_reason:
IMPLEMENTATION (bc9fbb288): Con_CopySelectionToClipboard() (engine/hexen2/console.c) walks line_end down past trailing blanks (' ' and '\0' — unwritten grid cells read as 0) before the copy loop.

THE BEAD'S CRITICAL WARNING WAS FOLLOWED, and its analysis was correct. The trim is exactly what makes line_end < line_start reachable, so: the guard is the trim loop's own 'line_end >= line_start' condition, and the copy loop KEEPS its bounded 'col <= line_end' form. It was not converted to pointer+length, which is the shape that underflows and the shape Ironwail had to patch in c03a5bdc1. A comment at the site says this so the next person does not 'clean it up' into the crash.

RUNTIME EVIDENCE (GL client, headless, con_linewidth 78) via temporary instrumentation that drove the real Con_CopySelectionToClipboard() and read back SDL_GetClipboardText(), with the trim toggleable to capture both sides:
- PRE (trim off), 4-line selection: 315 chars, every line padded to 78 cols — reproduces the bead exactly.
- POST (trim on), same selection: 18 chars, 'AAA\nBBBBBB\nDDDD\nCC'.
- POST with blank middle lines (the underflow case): 8 chars, blanks copy as empty lines, no crash.
The instrumentation was removed before commit; the committed diff is the trim loop and its comment only (23 lines, verified by git diff).

title: docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md CMakeLists citations are stale by one line
description:
The sys_exedir.c insertion at engine/CMakeLists.txt:361 (35e0e4488) shifted every citation below it by one line:
- :511 → :512
- :563 → :564
- :578 → :579
- :743 → :744
- SOUNDFONT_PATH :513-514 → :514-515

The commit message for 35e0e4488 already uses corrected numbers; only the design doc is stale.

This is the FOURTH instance of citation drift in this document in a single day. The earlier ones (f619026e1 shifting quakefs.c and pr_edict.c) were fixed in 943475c03. Worth considering: convert remaining bare line numbers to the file.c :: Function() style that docs/SrcNotes.txt and docs/GAMECODE.md already use to avoid future drifts.

Reference: docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md (sections on F5 and gamecode sources)
notes: Doc-harmonization pass (2026-08-13) found the drift is broader than 'stale by one line': 59343680d (uhexen2-unvi, landed after this bead was filed) inserted ~52 lines into engine/CMakeLists.txt for the libTiMidity MIDI fallback, on top of the one-line shift from sys_exedir.c. Concretely: SOUNDFONT_SOURCES assignments moved from :511/:563 to :523/:575, ALL_SOURCES from :578 to :590, and the SOUNDFONT_PATH add_definitions from :513-514 to :525-527 -- a 12-14 line shift, not 1. Fixed the F5 and 'Bundle location' citations in docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md by converting them to symbolic references instead of re-pinning numbers (per the doc-harmonizer brief's guidance). Also found and fixed a third stale citation this bead didn't list: F7's pr_edict.c:2117-2158 (the PR_LoadProgs crc switch) is now at :2427-2467, pushed down by the ~130 lines 59343680d added ahead of it for the bundle-substitution path. Did not attempt a full sweep of the remaining ~35 file:LINE citations in that document (quakefs.c, flake.nix, pr_edict.c) -- confirmed several of those have also drifted (e.g. FS_AddGameDirectory moved from :400 to :382, FS_OpenFile_Internal's case-fallback block from ~:897 to :909) but a complete pass is a larger job than this session's scope; recommend treating the file.c :: Function() conversion mentioned in this bead's description as the actual fix rather than another numeric re-pin, since renumbering alone will be stale again within a day at the current edit rate.
close_reason:
Fixed in e64fd176d, by conversion rather than re-pinning -- which is what this bead's own description and the doc-harmonizer note both recommended. All 39 bare file:LINE citations in docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md are now file.c :: Symbol(), matching docs/SrcNotes.txt and docs/GAMECODE.md. Each anchor was resolved against the CURRENT tree rather than by adjusting the old number, since the drift was well past the one line this bead was filed for (the note already recorded 12-14 lines from 59343680d, and several quakefs.c citations had moved further still).

Mapping used: quakefs.c :: FS_OpenFile_Internal, FS_AddGameDirectory, Host_Game_f, FS_Init, check_known_paks and file-scope fs_gamedir_nopath; pr_edict.c :: PR_GetProgFilename, PR_LoadProgs, ED_ParseEdict; sv_main.c :: SV_SpawnServer; sys_unix.c/sys_win.c :: Sys_GetBasedir; soundfont.c :: SF_FindSoundFont; the three help_strings[] tables named by file; quakedef.h :: SAVEGAME_VERSION; sys.h :: DO_USERDIRS; and the flake.nix / release.yml regions named by block (packages.gamecode's buildPhase and installPhase, gamecodeSrc, the release derivation's Linux portable tree, the Package step) since those have no functions to cite.

Also picked up the two bare citations in docs/GAMECODE.md that this bead did not list (sv_main.c:2432 and :2502). Both pointed into SV_SpawnServer to make a point about call ORDER, so citing the function twice would have lost the meaning -- rewritten to state the ordering directly.

Verified afterwards: zero bare file:LINE citations remain in docs/*.md, and every symbol cited resolves in the current tree.

The convention is now recorded in the document header with the reason (four drifts in one day), so the next editor does not re-pin numbers out of habit and start the cycle over.

title: Sys_GetExeDir has no macOS arm
description:
docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md F5 lists _NSGetExecutablePath as the macOS backing for executable directory resolution, but the Sys_GetExeDir() implementation (35e0e4488) returns NULL on macOS.

This is NOT a regression — the prior exe_dir() also returned nothing on macOS, so behaviour is unchanged. Deliberately deferred by implementer who has no ability to build or test on macOS.

Add _NSGetExecutablePath arm when macOS becomes buildable. The entire macOS cluster (uhexen2-aoqd and children) is blocked on the absence of Mac hardware anyway, so this is naturally sequenced behind it.

Reference: docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md F5, engine/h2shared/sys_exedir.c::Sys_GetExeDir
close_reason:
Implemented in 8034d64bc. docs/BUNDLED_GAMECODE.md F5 had listed _NSGetExecutablePath as the macOS backing all along while the implementation had only GetModuleFileName and /proc/self/exe, so macOS fell through to 'return NULL' and everything layered on Sys_GetExeDir -- bundled gamecode, the soundfont search -- silently had one fewer place to look. F5 now describes what the code does.

Implementation notes worth keeping: _NSGetExecutablePath returns whatever argv[0] resolution produced, so the path may be relative, may contain . or .., and may run through a symlink -- which is how both Homebrew and MacPorts install a binary. It is passed through realpath() before the directory is taken, per Apple's own documentation and because the truncation needs a canonical path to cut. exedir is MAX_OSPATH, which is PATH_MAX on this platform, which is realpath's contract. A path too long for the buffer returns NULL rather than retrying larger: nothing else in the engine could hold it either.

The .app caveat is recorded in the file header and in F5 rather than coded around. Inside a bundle the executable lives in Foo.app/Contents/MacOS/, so that is what this returns and that is where a gamecode payload has to go -- under Contents/, not beside the .app. For a plain CLI build (Homebrew, MacPorts, nix, ./configure) the behaviour is already correct. Special-casing bundles inside this function would be the wrong layer; it belongs to whoever builds the bundle.

ON THE DEFERRAL. This bead deferred the work until macOS is buildable, and that is still true -- there is no Mac here and this is NOT a substitute for uhexen2-aoqd. It was implemented anyway because the arm is inside #elif defined(__APPLE__), so it cannot affect the platforms that do build, and leaving a documented-but-absent backing in place is worse than a well-tested-but-unrun one. What was actually verified:

- The real sys_exedir.c compiles clean with -D__APPLE__ against a stub mach-o/dyld.h (project dev shell, GLQUAKE defined). Preprocessed output confirms the new arm is the branch selected -- 12 hits for _NSGetExecutablePath/realpath, zero for /proc/self/exe.
- The arm's logic lifted verbatim into a harness with a stub _NSGetExecutablePath and run on Linux: 7/7 cases pass -- absolute path; a path with . and .. canonicalised; a symlinked binary resolving to its real directory (the Homebrew/MacPorts shape); a relative path resolved against cwd; buffer-too-small returning NULL rather than a truncated path; a nonexistent path returning NULL; a bare name with no slash returning NULL.
- nix build clean on both .#default and .#win64, no new warnings. Linux and Windows code paths byte-identical.
- Headless run confirms exe-dir resolution still drives the bundled gamecode: 'Gamecode: progs.dat from <store>/bin/../share/hexenwail/data1/progs.dat'.

NOT covered, and the reason uhexen2-aoqd stays open: actual execution on macOS hardware, and the .app bundle shape. If the first real Mac build turns up a problem here it is a fresh bug, not a reopening -- the contract this implements is documented above.

title: DropBackpack debug spam is undecided fork gamecode
close_reason:
DECIDED: option 1, KEEP, documented. Landed in 3cba7ec26.

The bead's stated risk -- 'once bundling lands, this diagnostic will ship to every player running our progs.dat' -- is true but inert, and that is what settles it. Traced the gate: dprint is builtin #25, PF_dprint (engine/h2shared/pr_cmds.c), which calls Con_DPrintf, which is a macro for CON_Printf(_PRINT_DEVEL, ...) (engine/h2shared/printsys.h), and _PRINT_DEVEL is dropped unless the developer cvar is nonzero -- engine/hexen2/console.c:383 for the client, engine/hexen2/server/host.c:282 for h2ded. A shipped player never sees it.

Against that near-zero cost, the output is load-bearing for an open bug. fe1f2bdc1's BadBackpackDump() prints WHAT was in the bag; a14b5eecd's classname+origin prints WHO dropped it. uhexen2-9gdx has field reports naming archers and leopards specifically, and only the second half can confirm or refute that. Trimming would remove the instrument for the bug that 9gdx exists to root-cause.

Documented in gamecode/README under the a14b5eecd entry, tagged [uhexen2-o4tn], stating that it is deliberate instrumentation, the gate that makes it free, and its relationship to 9gdx -- which is what option 1 asked for.

INCIDENTAL FINDING, checked and clean: siege carries the same classname/origin lines but did NOT get fe1f2bdc1's BadBackpackDump or the loot-preserving fallthrough, which looked like drift. It is not: siege's entire single-item dispatch sits inside the 'Always throw BP in Siege' /* ... */ block (gamecode/hc/siege/items.hc), so those lines never execute. Also verified siege's live 'if (!total) remove(item)' is NOT the uhexen2-9r3n bug -- siege's guard tests cnt_grenades, cnt_arrows, bluemana, greenmana and spawn_health and then forces total=TRUE, so the later check is unreachable. No siege bead needed.

title: CalcAC's non-Portals class clamp is dead code with inconsistent index base
description:
CalcAC (engine/hexen2/sbar.c:627) clamps a 0-based playerClass index with the condition:
  playerClass > MAX_PLAYER_CLASS - PORTALS_EXTRA_CLASSES
which evaluates to playerClass > 4. This can never be true for a valid 0-based class (0-4), making the non-Portals guard dead code.

By contrast, DrawLowerBar (sbar.c:468) uses a 1-based class index and correctly catches class 5 with its clamp.

Secondary issue: CalcAC's fallback assignment 'playerClass = 1' carries the comment "Default to paladin", but on a 0-based index, 1 is the Crusader, not the Paladin (which is 0). Either the comment or the value is wrong.

The two sites (CalcAC and DrawLowerBar) disagree about index base. Both clamp on !(gameflags & GAME_PORTALS), so they should use the same convention. No audit changes were needed at sbar.c:626-628 or gl_rmisc.c:465 (both consult GAME_PORTALS flag), but CalcAC's dead code clamp should be removed or fixed to match.

Unreachable in normal play (GAME_PORTALS is set when Portals pak is valid, bypassing the guard entirely; menu prevents out-of-range class), but worth fixing for code hygiene.

Discovered while verifying uhexen2-uh5c acceptance criteria.
close_reason:
Fixed in a80513eba. Fixed the clamp rather than removing it, because it turned out to be reachable rather than pure hygiene.

CONFIRMED the bead's analysis. CalcAC (engine/hexen2/sbar.c) sets playerClass = cl_playerclass.integer - 1, so 0-based, and indexes AmuletAC/BracerAC/BreastplateAC/HelmetAC with it. Its first clamp already caps the value at MAX_PLAYER_CLASS-1 = 4, so the second clamp's 'playerClass > MAX_PLAYER_CLASS - PORTALS_EXTRA_CLASSES' (> 4) can never fire. DrawLowerBar keeps the value 1-based (it does ClassNames[playerClass-1] and ABILITIES_STR_INDEX + (playerClass-1)*2) and the identical '> 4' correctly catches the Demoness at 5.

REACHABLE, contrary to 'unreachable in normal play': the menu hides the Demoness without Portals (gl_rmisc.c:440 caps the menu at MAX_PLAYER_CLASS - PORTALS_EXTRA_CLASSES), but the console is not the menu -- host_cmd.c:1249/1258 clamps cl_playerclass only to 1..MAX_PLAYER_CLASS, so 5 is accepted. On a data1-only install that gives CalcAC playerClass=4 and it reads the Demoness column (amulet 6, bracer 2, breastplate 4, helmet 8) while DrawLowerBar, one function away and correctly clamped, prints 'Paladin'. The AC number and the class name on the same bar disagree.

FIX: CalcAC's Portals clamp is now >= (correct for 0-based); DrawLowerBar's stays > (correct for 1-based). A comment at each site states its base and points at the other, since the two-bases-one-cvar arrangement is the actual trap.

SECONDARY ISSUE, also fixed: both CalcAC clamps assigned playerClass = 1 under 'Default to paladin', but 0-based index 1 is the Crusader -- the comment was right and the value wrong. Now CLASS_PALADIN - 1 in CalcAC and CLASS_PALADIN in DrawLowerBar, which makes the index base visible at the assignment.

Verified: nix build .# succeeds, and the client runs demo1 headless (SDL offscreen + llvmpipe) through signon to disconnect with the status bar drawing, no crash.

title: Invalid mission-pack install leaves a phantom portals search path entry with no rollback
description:
After fc9724cb9 (uhexen2-6h8x), the `check_portals && !portals_in_path` branch at quakefs.c:1741-1750 is reachable only when the mission pack fails validation and step 2 rolls its own searchpaths back out. In exactly that case, FS_AddGameDirectory("portals", ...) re-adds a directory that step 2 had deliberately rolled back — leaving a phantom `portals` path entry with no corresponding rollback.

This is pre-existing behaviour, not introduced by fc9724cb9; the dedup fix deliberately left it byte-identical rather than widening scope, per the constraint that the fix must not change which directories end up in the search path. But now that the redundant-add case is gone, this is the only thing that branch does, which makes the defect much easier to see and much easier to reason about fixing.

CONSEQUENCE: on a broken/incomplete Portal of Praevus install, the engine may present portals content in the search path that validation had already rejected — the opposite of what the rollback intends.

WHAT NEEDS DOING: Construct an invalid mission-pack install (e.g. truncated or wrong-CRC pak3.pak) and decide whether the correct behaviour is to skip the add entirely or to add-and-roll-back symmetrically. Both are defensible; the former is simpler.
close_reason:
Fixed in 074a763d2. DECISION: skip the add entirely -- the simpler of the two options the bead offered.

REPRODUCED FIRST, not just reasoned about. Built a scratch install with data1 symlinked from a retail copy and portals/pak3.pak replaced by 4 KB of urandom, then ran h2ded -basedir <scratch> -game testmod +path. Pre-fix log shows the full cycle: 'pak3.pak is not a packfile, ignored' / 'Missing or invalid mission pack installation' / 'Removed path .../portals' (x2, userdir and basedir) / then 'pak3.pak is not a packfile, ignored' A SECOND TIME as the -game step re-added it -- and the final search path listed both portals entries under the mod. Exactly the phantom the bead predicted, plus a duplicated warning.

BIGGER THAN THE BEAD SAID. The bead frames this as a broken-mission-pack edge case, but the same branch fires whenever portals/ is simply absent, which is the ordinary state of a player who never bought Portal of Praevus. Verified: on an install with no portals directory at all, -game testmod listed TWO portals search paths that do not exist on disk. Every mod launch on a plain Hexen II install was carrying them, and every failed file lookup statted them. Post-fix: none.

WHY SKIP RATHER THAN SYMMETRIC ROLLBACK: the condition 'check_portals && !portals_in_path' has exactly one meaning now that fc9724cb9 removed the redundant-add case. check_portals gates step 2, so if it is set step 2 ran; if it ran and portals is not on the path, validation rejected it. Re-adding undoes a rollback whose stated purpose is that the portals directory is reserved for the mission pack. A mod that wanted mission pack assets does without them -- which is already what an H2MP build does after the same rollback, so this makes the two build flavours agree.

portals_in_path existed only to drive the removed branch and is gone rather than left set-but-unread.

REGRESSION CHECK, the one that mattered: a VALID mission pack with -game testmod produces byte-identical search path output before and after, with portals still below the mod and pak3.pak's 245 files present. Verified across all three installs (invalid / absent / valid) with h2ded +path. nix build .# and .#h2ded both succeed.

NOTE for uhexen2-1bmj, which this blocks: the fs_gamedir_nopath staleness after the rollback is untouched by this change -- the rollback still restores fs_gamedir and fs_userdir to data1 while leaving fs_gamedir_nopath reading 'portals'. That is still open and now the only remaining defect in this path.

title: Soft particles: fade sprite alpha near intersecting geometry
description:
Sprites (explosion halos, smoke, splashes) that intersect world geometry show a hard, aliased cut line along the intersection, because the sprite draw uses depth test on / depth writes off (gl_rmain.c:3552-3591, depth-mask gated per model type) and any fragment behind the surface plane is depth-failed outright.

The polygon offset from uhexen2-rsy9 (gl_rmain.c:690-699) is a correctness fix for a different case — it keeps a billboard whose origin sits near-coplanar with a wall from rendering half-eaten — and cannot address deep intersections, e.g. a SPR_ORIENTED sprite lying near-parallel to a floor. Increasing the offset to cover that would float sprites in front of geometry they should be behind. Soft particles instead fade alpha as a function of the distance between the fragment's depth and the already-resolved scene depth behind it, so the sprite dissolves into the surface rather than being cut.

## What this needs in the GL 4.3 pipeline:

1. A readable copy of scene depth at sprite-draw time. Sprites draw during the translucent-entity pass, so the depth buffer is still bound as the current FBO's depth attachment and cannot be sampled simultaneously — needs either a depth resolve/blit before the translucent pass, or reuse of the Hi-Z depth resolve already built for occlusion culling (gl_worldcull.c:892, standalone since uhexen2-9912). Reusing that is the cheap path if its resolve point and resolution are compatible; verify both before committing to it.

2. A dedicated sprite fragment shader, or a variant of gl_shader_alias, that samples that depth texture at gl_FragCoord.xy, linearizes both depths (watch the reversed-Z convention — gl_clipcontrol_able), and multiplies output alpha by clamp(delta / u_soft_distance, 0, 1). Sprites currently borrow gl_shader_alias / gl_shader_alias_oit (gl_rmain.c:690-699), so this means a new program plus its uniform plumbing.

3. Interaction with the OIT path (gl_shader_alias_oit) needs deciding — the fade must be applied before the OIT weighting, not after.

4. Cvar-gated (r_softparticles, default off until validated) with a menu entry, per project convention.

## Cost
One extra depth-texture sample per sprite fragment, plus a depth resolve if the Hi-Z one cannot be reused. Sprite fill is low in Hexen II so the fragment cost is negligible; the resolve is the real expense and is the reason to check Hi-Z reuse first.

## Parity
Confirm whether Ironwail implements soft particles before designing — project convention is to default to its approach.

This issue supersedes uhexen2-jkya (which described a soft-sprite shader that never existed in the repo). Related issues: uhexen2-rsy9 (polygon offset sprite fix) and uhexen2-m0he (depth writes off for translucent sprites).
close_reason:
Implemented in 44f3b0e0c, default tuned in 32cd69e21.

r_softparticles fades a sprite's alpha by the distance between its fragment and the opaque scene depth behind it, so a billboard intersecting a wall dissolves into it instead of being sliced. r_softparticles_scale is the fade distance in world units (default 8). Off by default; "Soft Sprites" in the Rendering submenu.

## How it was built

GL_SoftDepth_Capture (gl_postprocess.c) blits the depth buffer into a private texture at the last point it holds opaque geometry only -- after R_DrawWaterSurfaces(WATER_PHASE_OPAQUE) in R_RenderView, and again after R_RenderScene in R_Mirror, which has its own view and depth range. A snapshot rather than the live attachment for two reasons: sampling the bound framebuffer's own depth is a rendering feedback loop and undefined under GL 4.3, and an opaque-only snapshot is the more correct input anyway (a sprite should dissolve into the wall, not into whichever translucent entity sorted earlier).

The design note in this issue proposed reusing the Hi-Z depth resolve from gl_worldcull.c. That does not work: the Hi-Z resolve runs at the END of the 3D pass to seed a latency-1 pyramid for the next frame's culling, whereas soft particles need depth resolved BEFORE the translucent pass. It needs its own blit. One full-res depth blit per frame, gated on the cvar.

The fade lives in a uniform on gl_shader_alias rather than in a dedicated program, because that program is shared by sprites, warp polys, unlit brush polys and alias models and only sprites want it -- same reasoning as u_alias_caustics (uhexen2-0gn3). The OIT variant needs no separate work: GL_CompileOITFragShader derives it from the same source, and the fade multiplies color.a before the preamble's weighting, which is the required ordering.

R_SoftParticleParams inverts the live projection matrix into z = zb/(za - d) and folds glDepthRange into the coefficients, so one expression covers reversed-Z, forward-Z and the mirror pass's split ranges without the shader knowing which is in play.

Soft sprites keep GL_BLEND on even when nominally opaque: the fade lands in fragColor.a and with blending off would never modulate anything. Harmless, since .spr texels are fully opaque or fully cut out, so the fade is the only source of an intermediate alpha. The fade is applied AFTER the alpha test so the cutout decision stays with the texture's own alpha.

## Ironwail parity

Checked first, per project convention. Ironwail has no soft particles -- Quake/r_sprite.c draws billboards GLS_BLEND_OPAQUE with no depth fade.
