It does scope its single glPolygonOffset(OFFSET_DECAL) to SPR_ORIENTED only, which independently confirms why uhexen2-rsy9's offset never helped explosions: a view-parallel billboard has zero screen-space depth slope, so the factor term vanishes and only ~1 depth ULP of units bias remains. Every explosion sprite in Hexen II (sm_expld, bg_expld, fl_expld, mm_expld, xplod29, fcircle, bonexpld, s_explod) is SPR_VP_PARALLEL. Our offset is still applied to all sprite types; scoping it to SPR_ORIENTED to match Ironwail is an open tidy-up, not a bug.

## Verification (headless, llvmpipe, demo1, Necromancer raven staff)

- Artifact confirmed and fixed: with the feature off the explosion sprites on the plinth are visibly rectangular, cut square by the plinth edge; with it on they taper into the stone.
- Fade distance measured, not guessed: at 24 the fade dissolves most of the flame and drains the explosion; at 8 the hard cut is gone and the flame keeps close to full brightness. Hence the default of 8.
- r_scale 0.5: clean. The snapshot tracks the scaled render target and gl_FragCoord lines up. No GL errors.
- MSAA scene: deliberately skipped (GL_SoftDepth_Capture bails when pp_samples > 1). A multisample-to-single-sample depth resolve is implementation-defined, so sprites keep the hard cut there rather than fade against a guess. Mirrors how R_BuildHiZForNextFrame declines the same path.
- r_oit 1: the fade is a no-op, but only because sprites do not render under OIT at all. Filed as uhexen2-z4r1 -- pre-existing, independent of this feature.

## Not done

Particles (R_DrawParticles) are untouched; the artifact is negligible on point sprites. Everything above was verified on llvmpipe under offscreen SDL, never on real hardware -- worth a look on the test box before the default is considered for flipping on.

title: changelevel issued before signon completes desyncs the client (svc_updatename > MAX_CLIENTS)
description:
Observed 2026-08-13 while stress-testing changelevel for uhexen2-of6f.

A script that does 'map demo1', waits only 6 frames, then 'changelevel demo2' reliably ends in:

    Host_Error: CL_ParseServerMessage: svc_updatename > MAX_CLIENTS

right after 'player entered the game' on the second map. The same script with 14 frames of settle between transitions runs five server spawns clean. So the trigger is issuing changelevel while the client is still working through signon on the current map, not the transition itself.

Almost certainly harmless in the field: a player cannot type into the console during signon, and the normal trigger-driven hub transition happens long after. Reachable in principle from a mod stuffcmd or an exec'd script that does not wait.

Filed mainly so the next person who sees this string while scripting headless tests does not spend time hunting a protocol bug that is not there — the fix for the test is to allow more settle frames. If someone does want to harden it, the question is why the client accepts a serverinfo for map B while still parsing signon for map A, and whether Host_Changelevel2_f should refuse while cls.signon is incomplete.

NOT related to uhexen2-rutp: that was a use-after-free with a segfault, fixed in d46d000c5, and this error appears on builds that contain the fix.
close_reason:
Not a defect. Closing with the diagnosis recorded rather than a code change.

Confirmed both directions on the demo data: 'map demo1' + 6 wait frames + 'changelevel demo2' reliably ends in 'Host_Error: CL_ParseServerMessage: svc_updatename > MAX_CLIENTS' right after 'player entered the game'; the identical script with 14 frames of settle runs five server spawns clean, no error. So the trigger is issuing the transition while the local client is still working through signon on the current map.

Deliberately NOT adding a guard to Host_Changelevel2_f / Host_Changelevel_f. It would refuse a transition whenever cls.signon < SIGNONS, which no player can reach — the console is not reachable mid-signon — so the change would buy nothing in the field while adding a new way to break a mod that legitimately changes level immediately on map start. This tree has been burned before by changes that could not be justified by a real symptom, and this is one of those.

What the bead is worth is the diagnosis, which is now written down: if this string shows up while scripting headless tests, it is the harness, and the fix is more settle frames — not a protocol hunt. Same family as the sky-recall false alarm in uhexen2-jvu1, both of which came from console commands interleaving with connection setup in a way nothing in normal play can.

Explicitly not related to uhexen2-rutp: that was a use-after-free producing a segfault, fixed in d46d000c5, and this error reproduces on builds containing that fix.

title: svc_skybox / svc_mod_name are dead stubs — server sends "", client discards
description:
Protocol 21 (PROTOCOL_UQE_113) reserves svc_mod_name (54) and svc_skybox (55) for the UQE v1.13 extension by Korax: the server tells the client the music file name and the skybox name. Both ends are stubbed out in this tree.

Server (engine/hexen2/sv_main.c:613-619) writes both message bytes but sends a literal empty string for each, with comments noting uqe-hexen2 sends sv.mod_name and sv.skybox there. Client (engine/hexen2/cl_parse.c:2088-2092) reads the string and throws it away with a Con_DPrintf. Every SoT map load prints 'Ignored server msg 54' / 'Ignored server msg 55' under developer 1 — our own server's placeholders talking to our own client.

Two consequences:
1. Connecting to a real uqe-hexen2 server, its skybox and music selection are silently dropped.
2. Anyone implementing the client side naively will break the common case: svc_skybox arrives during signon, AFTER Sky_NewMap has already loaded the sky from worldspawn, so applying an empty string would clear a correctly loaded skybox. The client must ignore empty strings, and the server should send the sky actually in effect rather than "".

Doing this properly means the server tracking an authoritative skybox name (there is no sv-side notion of one today — the sky is a pure client-side read of the worldspawn key in Sky_NewMap) and a QC builtin or console path to change it mid-map. That is the mechanism uhexen2-7gl5 hypothesised mods use; worth confirming against a mod that actually changes sky at runtime before building it.

Low priority: no reported symptom, no known server to talk to. Filed so the stubs are not mistaken for working code.
close_reason: Implemented in 08f5818d5. Server: SV_ParseWorldspawnSky() reads the sky/skyname/qlsky key out of the world entity lump at SV_SpawnServer (same three spellings Sky_NewMap accepts, so the two cannot disagree), and sv.mod_name is the gamedir; both go on the wire instead of the literal empty strings. Client: svc_mod_name lands in cl.mod_name; svc_skybox applies Sky_LoadSkyBox ONLY for a non-empty name -- empty means 'server has nothing to declare', not 'clear the sky', which is the naive-implementation trap the bead called out (svc_skybox arrives after Sky_NewMap has already loaded from worldspawn, and on hub revisit it would also stomp the 7gl5 per-map recall). Verified headless with a demo1.ent override carrying a real skybox: protocol 19 sends neither message and the sky still loads locally; protocol 21 round-trips 'testsky_' and 'data1' with Sky_LoadSkyBox no-opping because the names match; with the server forced to send "" while worldspawn had a sky, the client's sky survived. Zero 'Ignored server msg 54/55' lines remain. NOT implemented, deliberately: the QC builtin / console path to change sky mid-map. The bead itself says to confirm that mechanism against a mod that actually does it before building it, and nothing in this change needs it -- see uhexen2-7gl5, which still hypothesises that mechanism and is awaiting field validation.

title: HiDPI/Retina validation on macOS
description: SDL_WINDOW_HIGH_PIXEL_DENSITY is already set at gl_vidsdl.c, but the Retina backing scale interacts with the render-scale and vid_scale features and has never been exercised. Needs real testing on a Retina display once hardware exists. Acceptance: render scale and the HUD/menu scaling behave correctly at 1x and 2x backing scale.
notes: 2026-08-13 TRIAGE: marked blocked. No Mac hardware in the loop (macOS cluster issue).

title: Delete the dead upstream MacOSX Xcode projects
description: Remove engine/hexen2/MacOSX/hexen2.xcodeproj and xcode24compat.xcodeproj plus their plists. They are Xcode 2.4 / PowerPC-era files inherited from upstream, reference a build system and a renderer that no longer exist, and will mislead anyone starting macOS work into thinking there is a foundation here. Independent of the rest of the epic and can be done at any time. Acceptance: the directory is gone and nothing references it.
close_reason: Done in 0358fe084: engine/hexen2/MacOSX/ removed entirely (both xcodeprojs and both plists). Verified nothing else in the tree referenced them — the only other MacOSX hit is the PLATFORM_STRING define in common/arch_def.h, unrelated.

title: macOS CI runner and a test machine
description: Add a macOS runner to CI covering both Apple Silicon and Intel. Also flags the practical prerequisite recorded on the epic: no macOS hardware is currently available to anyone working on this, so until a runner or a physical test machine exists, every other child issue can only be validated by compiling, never by running. Acceptance: CI builds the macOS target on every push.
notes: 2026-08-13 TRIAGE: marked blocked. No Mac hardware in the loop (macOS cluster issue).

title: macOS packaging — .app bundle, code signing, notarization
description: Produce a proper .app bundle with an Info.plist, then code-sign and notarize it. Without notarization Gatekeeper blocks the app for every user who did not build it themselves, so this is a hard requirement for distribution, not a polish item. Acceptance: a downloaded build launches on a clean macOS machine without a Gatekeeper override.
notes: 2026-08-13 TRIAGE: marked blocked. No Mac hardware in the loop (macOS cluster issue).

title: Fix macOS platform glue — executable path and audio backend
description: Two concrete portability defects. (1) engine/h2shared/midi_fluid.c:85 resolves the running executable's directory with readlink("/proc/self/exe"), which does not exist on macOS; it needs _NSGetExecutablePath. This is on the soundfont search path, so MIDI music silently breaks without it. (2) ALSA is Linux-only; macOS must use the SDL audio backend. Acceptance: the soundfont search finds a bundled soundfont on macOS and audio initialises.
notes: 2026-08-13 TRIAGE: marked blocked. No Mac hardware in the loop (macOS cluster issue).

title: Add darwin to the flake and an APPLE branch to CMake
description: flake.nix must gain aarch64-darwin and x86_64-darwin systems with a working package. engine/CMakeLists.txt must gain an explicit APPLE branch before the UNIX branch so macOS does not inherit the Linux path — specifically it must not pull ALSA, and must exclude cd_linux.c (which includes <linux/cdrom.h>). Source SDL3 and the audio codecs for darwin. Acceptance: `nix build .#darwin` (or equivalent) compiles the client on both Apple Silicon and Intel.
notes: 2026-08-13 TRIAGE: marked blocked. No Mac hardware in the loop (macOS cluster issue).

title: Ship ANGLE so the GLES path runs on macOS over Metal
description: Depends on CHILD 1. Integrate ANGLE (GLES 3.0 -> Metal) for the darwin build: source or vendor the ANGLE dylibs, wire SDL3 to load them, and bundle them in the app. Acceptance: the client renders a map on macOS via ANGLE.
notes: 2026-08-13 TRIAGE: marked blocked. No Mac hardware in the loop (macOS cluster issue).

title: Decouple the GLES 3.0 render path from __EMSCRIPTEN__ into a USE_GLES build option
description: The ES tier is proven by the working WASM build but is gated on __EMSCRIPTEN__. Introduce a USE_GLES build option (CMake option + compile define) and convert the roughly 74 existing guard sites in engine/h2shared/glheader.h, gl_func.h and gl_vbo.c, plus the shader header selection at gl_shader.c:306-307 and the context request at gl_vidsdl.c:467-470, to key off it. Emscripten builds should then simply imply USE_GLES rather than being the only way to reach the path. Acceptance: the WASM build is byte-for-byte behaviourally unchanged, and a Linux build with -DUSE_GLES=ON produces a running GLES 3.0 client (testable locally against Mesa, which is the cheap way to validate this without a Mac).
notes:
IMPLEMENTED across 4027d8ac6 (decoupling) plus four follow-on fix commits.

WHAT LANDED
- USE_GLES CMake option in engine/CMakeLists.txt, OFF by default, forced ON for EMSCRIPTEN. Emitted as -DUSE_GLES=1 via add_definitions.
- ~50 GLES-semantic guard sites converted from __EMSCRIPTEN__ across glheader.h, gl_func.h, gl_vbo.c, gl_vidsdl.c, gl_buffer.c, gl_worldcull.c, gl_mesh.c, gl_shader.c, gl_postprocess.c, gl_screen.c, gl_rmain.c, gl_rmisc.c, gl_rsurf.c, r_part.c.
- The genuinely platform-shaped guards deliberately keep __EMSCRIPTEN__: host_async.c (main-loop inversion), sys_sdl.c (signals/console), sys_exedir.c (/proc/self/exe). glheader.h includes <emscripten.h> only under __EMSCRIPTEN__, <GLES3/gl3.h> under USE_GLES.
- GL_DLSYM vs USE_GLES: mutually exclusive. CMake strips GL_DLSYM from CLIENT_DEFINITIONS when USE_GLES is set (the UNIX block asks for it), AND gl_func.h's branch order was changed to '#if defined(GL_DLSYM) && !defined(USE_GLES)' so the header is correct on its own. Both headers also restate '__EMSCRIPTEN__ implies USE_GLES' so a hand-rolled compile cannot fall through to the desktop path.
- UNIX linking: pkg_check_modules(GLESV2 REQUIRED glesv2) and link libGLESv2 instead of OpenGL::GL. PkgConfig lookup hoisted above the GL lookup. libglvnd already supplies glesv2.pc and the GLES3/ headers, so no new dependency.
- docs/COMPILE documents the option.

VERIFICATION
- Desktop: 'nix build .#' green, unchanged.
- WASM: emcmake + emmake via shell-wasm.nix green, 1.7 MB hexenwail.wasm.
- Linux ES: cmake -DUSE_GLES=ON builds, links libGLESv2 and NOT libGL (confirmed in DT_NEEDED), requests an ES 3.0 context, loads demo1 on Mesa 26.1.5/llvmpipe under SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen, renders, and exits 0. All seven base shader programs, all three OIT variants and the post-process program report OK.

ON THE 'WASM BYTE-FOR-BYTE UNCHANGED' CRITERION IN THE ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION
Not met, and it should not be. That criterion assumed the ES path was working and only needed re-keying. It was not: the first desktop run found five latent bugs, four of which had been silently degrading or breaking the WASM build all along (no post-processing, no OIT, a failed skeletal compile every startup, a 1 MB dead SSBO+BSS, broken screenshots). Fixing them changes WASM behaviour, for the better. Filed and closed as uhexen2-7wdv, -g63k, -dfay, -vp8t, -3cke.

REMAINING
Nobody has run this in an actual browser since the fixes. The WASM module builds and links but WebGL2's shader acceptance is unverified; that is one browser run and worth doing before claiming post-processing works on the web target. Also untested: the ANGLE/macOS leg (uhexen2-6wj4), which this unblocks but does not prove.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in 4027d8ac6 + the four ES-tier fix commits. -DUSE_GLES=ON on Linux builds, links libGLESv2 (not libGL), gets a real 'OpenGL ES 3.2 Mesa 26.1.5' context on radeonsi, loads demo1, renders and exits 0 with every shader program compiling. Desktop nix build and the emscripten build both stay green. The 'WASM byte-for-byte unchanged' clause of the original acceptance is deliberately not met — see the notes.

title: macOS support
description:
Hexenwail currently has no macOS support of any kind. Scoping done 2026-08-11.

CURRENT STATE — effectively zero:
- engine/hexen2/MacOSX/ contains only two Xcode project files inherited from upstream Hammer of Thyrion (hexen2.xcodeproj, xcode24compat.xcodeproj), from the Xcode 2.4 / PowerPC era. Dead weight, not a starting point.
- Exactly three __APPLE__/__MACH__ references exist in the whole engine, and all three are inside vendored third-party headers (dr_mp3.h, dr_flac.h, dr_wav.h). Zero in our own code.
- flake.nix is `flake-utils.lib.eachSystem [ "x86_64-linux" ]` — no darwin system.
- engine/CMakeLists.txt has no APPLE branch. macOS satisfies CMake's UNIX, so it would fall into `elseif(UNIX)` and pull in ALSA and cd_linux.c (which does `#include <linux/cdrom.h>`).

THE BLOCKER — the renderer targets GL 4.3, macOS caps at 4.1:
engine/h2shared/gl_vidsdl.c:474-476 requests an OpenGL 4.3 COMPATIBILITY profile. That is impossible on macOS twice over: Apple's OpenGL never exceeded 4.1, and the only compatibility profile it ever shipped is 2.1. All 17 engine shaders are "#version 430 core"; macOS caps at GLSL 4.10. Apple deprecated OpenGL entirely in 2018, so even 4.1 is a dead end.

GL 4.3-only features in use and where:
- compute shaders (glDispatchCompute) — gl_worldcull.c
- SSBOs — gl_worldcull.c, gl_rsurf.c, gl_rmain.c, r_part.c, gl_buffer.c, gl_mesh.c, gl_shader.c
- glMultiDrawElementsIndirect — gl_worldcull.c, gl_buffer.c
- image load/store (4.2) — gl_worldcull.c Hi-Z
- glDebugMessageCallback (4.3) — gl_vidsdl.c

THE LEVER — a working GLES 3.0 tier already exists:
The WASM build runs the game on WebGL2, which is OpenGL ES 3.0. gl_vidsdl.c:467-470 requests an ES context under __EMSCRIPTEN__, gl_shader.c:306-307 swaps every shader header to "#version 300 es", and the 4.3-only paths degrade gracefully — R_BuildWorldCull returns early on !glDispatchCompute_fp and the engine falls back to CPU culling. So a renderer tier that runs without compute, SSBOs or indirect draw is already proven. The catch: it is only about 74 guard sites across three files (glheader.h, gl_func.h, gl_vbo.c) plus the shader header swap, and it is hard-wired to __EMSCRIPTEN__.

ROUTE CHOSEN — A: ANGLE (GLES 3.0 translated to Metal).
Decouple the existing ES path from __EMSCRIPTEN__ into a real USE_GLES build option, then ship ANGLE, which translates GLES 3.0 to Metal and is what Chrome and Firefox use on macOS. SDL3 supports ANGLE directly. This reuses a proven tier rather than authoring a new one, and lands on Metal rather than a deprecated API.

ROUTES REJECTED — record so they are not re-litigated:
- B, native GL 4.1 core: author a third shader tier at GLSL 4.10 and strip compute/SSBO/indirect from every consumer. More invasive than A (a new tier rather than a proven one) and the payoff is a deprecated API.
- C, native Metal backend: correct long-term, disproportionate now.

MAJOR CAVEAT: none of this can be tested in the current environment — there is no macOS machine available, and per project setup even Linux runtime testing happens on a separate box. Without a Mac in the loop this work would be written blind and validated only by compiling. Acquiring a test machine or a macOS CI runner is a practical prerequisite to calling any of it done.
notes: 2026-08-13 TRIAGE: marked blocked. No Mac hardware in the loop; aoqd's own text says 'none of this can be tested… Acquiring a test machine or a macOS CI runner is a practical prerequisite.'

title: utils: no Windows flake output despite the cross-build working
description:
While implementing uhexen2-gr5 the 18 tools were cross-built for Windows through a throwaway mingw derivation and all 18 .exe files produced, so WIN32 branches in utils/CMakeLists.txt and hw_utils/CMakeLists.txt are verified — but there is no flake output for them, so nothing reproducible builds or ships Windows map tools.

Adding packages.utils-win64 alongside existing packages.h2ded-win64 (flake.nix, added in 81d25f3d6) is roughly 15 lines following that precedent. Worth pairing with a CI step, as h2ded pair now has.

Acceptance: `nix build .#utils-win64` produces the 18 .exe files.
close_reason: Fixed in d83c4e852. Added packages.utils-win64 in flake.nix (following packages.h2ded-win64 from 81d25f3d6): pkgsCross64.stdenv.mkDerivation with cmake as sole nativeBuildInput, no buildInputs (plain C tools linking mingw runtime + ws2_32). Verified: nix build .#utils-win64 produces all 18 binaries (bsp2map.exe, bsp2wal.exe, bspinfo.exe, dhcc.exe, genmodel.exe, hcc.exe, hwmaster.exe, hwmquery.exe, hwrcon.exe, hwterm.exe, jsh2colour.exe, light.exe, lmp2pcx.exe, paklist.exe, pakx.exe, qbsp.exe, qfiles.exe, vis.exe). Compile/link-verified only (no wine available). Tools not yet included in release bundle.

title: CI does not build .#utils, so the tool CMake targets can rot
description:
uhexen2-gr5 added packages.utils behind BUILD_UTILS, defaulting OFF so engine build is untouched. Nothing in CI builds it, so the three new CMakeLists.txt files and the 18 tool targets can break silently — the same gap uhexen2-hx78 and uhexen2-befz described for dedicated server and Windows counterparts, both since closed by adding steps to .github/workflows/ci.yml.

Fix: add one step `nix build .#utils --print-build-logs`. Tools are plain C with no SDL/GL/codec dependencies, marginal CI cost.

Acceptance: CI fails when a utils target stops building.
close_reason: Fixed in d83c4e852. Added two steps to .github/workflows/ci.yml after Windows dedicated-server: 'Build tools' (nix build .#utils --print-build-logs) and 'Build Windows tools' (nix build .#utils-win64 --print-build-logs). Both cheap targets (plain C, no SDL/GL/codec deps). Closes rot gap for BUILD_UTILS, same as uhexen2-hx78 and uhexen2-befz did for BUILD_DEDICATED. Pre-commit: actionlint clean, .#default unchanged at 1,521,800 bytes. Not yet run on GitHub Actions.

title: CI does not build h2ded-win64, so the Windows server branch can still rot
description:
uhexen2-hx78 (81d25f3d6) added CI step for `nix build .#h2ded`, closing Unix dedicated-server gap. Windows one, packages.h2ded-win64 (flake.nix:325-368, added by uhexen2-qphz in same commit), is unbuilt — so engine/hexen2/server/sys_win.c and WIN32 h2ded CMake target can break silently as hx78 described for Unix.

Fix: one more build job step in .github/workflows/ci.yml: `nix build .#h2ded-win64 --print-build-logs`. Note mingw cross-compile adds wall-clock time; consider gating to master pushes only if CI time is constrained.

Acceptance: CI fails when Windows dedicated-server build breaks.

Discovered from uhexen2-qphz (81d25f3d6).
close_reason: Fixed in commit ba2f3fe77. Added a "Build Windows dedicated server" step running `nix build .#h2ded-win64 --print-build-logs` to the build job in .github/workflows/ci.yml, immediately after the existing Windows client step. Placed there deliberately: it rides on the mingw toolchain closure that `nix build .#win64` already pulls, and the dedicated server links no SDL, GL or codecs, so the marginal CI cost is small — which is why I did not gate it to master-only pushes as the issue suggested considering. Verified before commit: actionlint clean on the workflow, and `nix build .#h2ded-win64` produces h2ded.exe at 430,992 bytes on the current tree (0.7.9-beta.r5). Not verified: the step has not run on GitHub Actions yet — that happens on the next push or PR.

title: CI guard against the bare EMSCRIPTEN spelling reappearing
description: uhexen2-8mv8 (commit ec8f59fc9) swept every bare EMSCRIPTEN guard to __EMSCRIPTEN__, but nothing stops one coming back — and because the bare macro is only defined where <emscripten.h> is transitively included, a reintroduced guard fails silently rather than loudly. Add a grep guard to the lint job in .github/workflows/ci.yml: `rg --pcre2 '(?<![_A-Za-z])EMSCRIPTEN(?![_A-Za-z])' engine/ -g '*.c' -g '*.h'` must find nothing (note the CMake `if(EMSCRIPTEN)` uses in engine/CMakeLists.txt are CMake variables and must not be caught — restrict the glob to C sources as shown). Acceptance: CI fails on a PR that introduces a bare EMSCRIPTEN guard in C code.
close_reason: Fixed in 81d25f3d6. New 'No bare EMSCRIPTEN guards in C sources' lint step in .github/workflows/ci.yml: greps `(^|[^_A-Za-z])EMSCRIPTEN([^_A-Za-z]|$)` over engine/ *.c/*h only (CMake if(EMSCRIPTEN) variables excluded). GitHub ::error annotation, fails job on hit. Scoped to C sources because if(EMSCRIPTEN) in CMakeLists.txt are CMake variables, not C macros. Verified clean on HEAD, actionlint passes.

title: Translucent world surfaces in the OIT pass get no caustics
description: Found while implementing uhexen2-0gn3. gl_shader_world_oit never receives u_caustics — R_SetupFrame uploads it only to the `world` and `world_opaque` programs — so world surfaces drawn through the OIT path render un-causticked while everything around them is causticked. Pre-existing gap from uhexen2-6bfm, untouched by the alias work. Also worth checking in the same pass: the post-OIT glow pass (R_DrawAllGlows) draws with caustics at rest, so glow texels on translucent models do not get the boost — that is arguably correct since glows are self-illuminated, but nobody has looked at it on a real screen. Acceptance: with r_caustics on and the camera underwater, translucent world surfaces are causticked consistently with opaque ones, or a written reason why they should not be.
close_reason: Fixed in ff8c1f759. Root cause: missing C-side upload to gl_shader_world_oit in R_SetupFrame. engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:4249-4258 now uploads uniform vec2 u_caustics using same intensity/time locals as u_overbright and u_lightmap_bicubic blocks. With r_oit 0 no change (program never bound). Validation: nix build clean; all 16 shader sources + 3 OIT fragment variants reconstructed, compiled with glslangValidator, 13 program pairs link-checked. OIT_world confirms v_worldxy varying survives rewrite. NOT visually verified (no display).

title: CI does not build h2ded, so SERVERONLY code can silently rot
description: BUILD_DEDICATED defaults OFF (uhexen2-2lz, commit 2ab06c2b4) so that `nix build .#default` stays bit-for-bit the same client. The consequence is that the three SERVERONLY-side edits in that commit — engine/h2shared/pr_cmds.c:394, engine/h2shared/pr_edict.c:799, engine/hexen2/server/sys_unix.c — are not covered by any gate. Anyone editing pr_cmds.c, pr_edict.c or quakefs.c can break the dedicated server without CI noticing. Fix with either a CI step that configures with -DBUILD_DEDICATED=ON and builds, or a flake output. The flake output was scoped out of 2lz but is cheap: same derivation as `nixos` with cmakeFlags = [ "-DBUILD_DEDICATED=ON" ], an installPhase taking bin/h2ded, meta.mainProgram = "h2ded", and it can drop every buildInput except cmake/pkg-config since the binary links only libm/libc. Acceptance: a green CI job or flake output that fails when h2ded stops compiling.
close_reason: Fixed in 81d25f3d6. Added packages.h2ded to flake.nix:132-168, devShell help-text at flake.nix:529, 'Build dedicated server' CI step in .github/workflows/ci.yml. .#h2ded produces 319,152-byte binary (ldd libm/libc only), h2ded -help exits 0, .#default bit-identical to clean-HEAD (1,525,896 bytes sha256 match). actionlint clean. Windows branch (packages.h2ded-win64, qphz fix) still unbuilt in CI — see uhexen2-xyz follow-up.

title: h2ded: add the Windows branch of the dedicated-server target
description: uhexen2-2lz (commit 2ab06c2b4) added BUILD_DEDICATED for Unix only; the target emits a CMake WARNING and builds nothing on other platforms. The Windows branch was deliberately not transcribed from the old Makefile because it cannot be validated here — there is no mingw toolchain in `nix develop`, and engine/hexen2/server/sys_win.c has the same missing Sys_ListDirectories that the Unix side needed. To finish: add Sys_ListDirectories() to engine/hexen2/server/sys_win.c (copy engine/hexen2/sys_win.c:261; the Sys_UTF8ToWide/Sys_WideToUTF8 helpers already exist in the server file), re-add the WIN32 branch with net_win.c + net_wins.c + server/sys_win.c, add `target_link_libraries(h2ded PRIVATE ws2_32 winmm)`, do NOT pass WIN32 to add_executable (console subsystem), then cross-build to confirm. Acceptance: h2ded.exe cross-builds via the flake's mingw path and prints its banner under wine or on a Windows box.
close_reason: Fixed in 81d25f3d6. engine/CMakeLists.txt:647-691 guard now `EMSCRIPTEN OR (NOT UNIX AND NOT WIN32)`, adds WIN32 source branch (net_win.c, net_wins.c, server/sys_win.c) with ws2_32+winmm, no WIN32 flag on add_executable (stays console). engine/hexen2/server/sys_win.c:246-278 gains Sys_ListDirectories (from client sys_win.c:261) + wchar.h + q_swprintf. engine/h2shared/quakefs.c:28-32 gains guarded windows.h — FS_FOpen used MAX_PATH/MultiByteToWideChar/CP_UTF8 via only glheader.h (absent in SERVERONLY). packages.h2ded-win64 cross-builds via pkgsCross64 mingw: h2ded.exe 429,281 bytes PE CUI, imports KERNEL32/msvcrt/USER32/WINMM/WS2_32 only. .#win64 client bit-identical (1,668,425 bytes sha256 match). Note: __LINE__ in qerr_strlcpy resets binary; first fix +4 lines =11-byte diff; committed folds #ifdef to stay line-neutral. NOT wine-tested (no wine on dev).

title: default.cfg still zooms via the old n_in/n_out FOV-stepping alias instead of togglezoom
description:
Hexenwail now has a proper zoom system with zoom_fov and zoom_speed cvars, +zoom/-zoom/togglezoom commands, and a smoothstepped FOV lerp in SCR_UpdateZoom (engine/h2shared/gl_screen.c:111-112, 513-552, 466-472). This feature was completed in commit ecba5a981 and discovered as a follow-up to uhexen2-mfbe.

However, the shipped default configurations (gamecode/res/h2/default.cfg, gamecode/res/hw/default.cfg, gamecode/res/portals/default.cfg) still bind F11 to an outdated n_in/n_out alias that fakes zoom by stepping the fov cvar through 90/70/50/30/10/5 with wait commands between steps. This workaround:
- Is frame-rate dependent (each wait is one frame)
- Clobbers the user's fov cvar setting
- Conflicts with the real zoom system if both are used

**Proposed solution:**
Bind F11 to `togglezoom` and remove the n_in/n_out aliases. Retain the sensitivity-save behavior if still needed, though a design decision is required: the zoom system does not currently scale mouse sensitivity — should it, and if so, should that scaling be implemented in the engine rather than a cfg alias?

**Important caveat:**
This changes the behavior of an existing default bind. The old alias zooms to fov 5; togglezoom goes to zoom_fov (default 30). Someone should confirm the tighter default is acceptable, or set zoom_fov lower in the configs.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- F11 zooms via the engine zoom system on a fresh config in h2, hw, and portals
- n_in/n_out aliases are removed from all three default.cfg files
- Mouse sensitivity behavior while zoomed is decided deliberately and documented
close_reason: Fixed in 3b2485f16. F11 -> togglezoom in h2/hw/portals, hw's ' -> togglezoom, aliases removed. Also fixed siege/config.cfg, which the issue missed: it inherits zoom_in/zoom_out from hw/default.cfg and its PGUP/PGDN binds would have been left dangling; now PGUP -> +zoom (momentary), PGDN -> togglezoom (latch). Both open design questions decided: (1) mouse sensitivity is deliberately NOT scaled while zoomed -- Ironwail does not scale it, and Ironwail parity is the project default for rendering/input; the old alias's 'sensitivity 2'/'sensitivity 4' fiddling was a bug, not a feature to reimplement. (2) zoom_fov stays at 30 (Ironwail's default) rather than matching the alias's fov 5, which was an artifact of the stepping hack; configs now document zoom_fov as the knob. CAVEAT, filed separately: gamecode/ is excluded from the nix build source filter (flake.nix:46), so these configs never ship -- retail users still exec Raven's default.cfg out of pak0.pak and keep the old alias.

title: stochastic_alpha breaks teleport effect — looks black/fuzzy
description: When stochastic alpha (r_stochastic_alpha or similar cvar) is enabled, teleport portals render incorrectly — appear black and fuzzy instead of expected swirling effect. Likely a particle/sprite or additive-blended surface that conflicts with alpha-to-coverage dithering. Need to identify which draw path handles teleport visuals and guard it from A2C.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 7159b35a1 — GL_SetAliasStochasticAlpha(0.0f) added to R_DrawSpriteModel; stochastic alpha uniform was leaking from alias model draws into sprite draws that share gl_shader_alias.

title: Wire up zoom system (zoom_fov/zoom_speed) — stub in tree
description: ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md (Exclusives section, 'Removed from exclusives') flags the zoom system as incomplete: client.h:210 declares a 'float zoom' field (0=normal FOV, 1=fully zoomed to zoom_fov) but NO zoom_fov/zoom_speed cvars are registered anywhere and the field is never read/written — confirmed dead stub. Ironwail has a working zoom system (gl_screen.c:108-109). To reach parity: register zoom_fov and zoom_speed cvars, drive cl.zoom from a +zoom/zoom bind, lerp it by zoom_speed, and fold it into the FOV calc in the view/screen path. Must NOT be listed as a Hexenwail exclusive until functional.
close_reason: Zoom system implemented in commit ecba5a981. Verified on master: zoom_fov, zoom_speed cvars at engine/h2shared/gl_screen.c:111-112; +zoom/-zoom/togglezoom commands at :597-599; SCR_UpdateZoom (:532) lerps cl.zoom per frame. ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md corrected in commit 0633054c0.

title: Port HexenWorld to unified Hexenwail modern engine
description:
HexenWorld (the multiplayer fork) currently lives on the shanjaq-r6303-builds branch with separate hwcl/hwsv codebases that have drifted from the modernized h2shared headers. uhexen2-onfa covers the narrow goal of getting glhwcl to compile against evolved h2shared types. This bead is the broader umbrella: bring HexenWorld fully into the unified Hexenwail engine architecture so MP shares the same SDL3 + GL 4.3 render pipeline, shader-based fog, dlight system, alias lerp port, menu system, etc. — not two parallel renderers.

Scope (rough):
- Merge HW client into engine/hexenworld/ (or fold into engine/hexen2/ with HW-specific compile flag)
- Single rendering path via h2shared (no parallel GL code)
- HW-specific protocol/networking lives in HW client/server modules but shares everything else
- Resolve protocol drift (HW protocol differs from H2 SP)
- Single menu system with HW server browser, connect dialog, etc.
- Single sound/cdaudio path

This is a big undertaking — file separately as discrete sub-beads when work starts. Linked from uhexen2-onfa (HW client header-port follow-up).
notes:
Upstream reference (sezero/uhexen2 eba600f0a275457d2dcf17dbc3612787567bf4cd, 'hexenworld: added support for old v0.12 progs support'): adds backward-compat for HexenWorld v0.12 game progs.
- engine/h2shared/pr_edict.c (+81): new globalvars_v012_t typedef; PROGS_V012_CRC constant; loader recognizes v0.12 progs and maps globals correctly.
- engine/hexenworld/server/sv_init.c (+2/-2): wiring for version detection.
- engine/hexenworld/shared/progdefs.h (+113/-10): v0.12 struct defs; comment fix — spartanPrint/max_players landed in v0.12, not v0.14.
Why it matters: when we bring HW server into the unified engine, the progs loader must recognize both v0.12 and v0.14 CRCs to run older HW servers. Port this CRC/version-detection path alongside the HW server work. Logged from master without switching branches.

title: neojanq: port HW client (glhwcl) to compile against evolved h2shared headers
description:
Follow-up to uhexen2-id4i. The shanjaq-r6303-archive 2026-05-31 release shipped 4 of 6 targets but omitted glhwcl / glhwcl.exe.

Shanjaq's HW client at tip 800586575 has structural divergence from the evolved h2shared headers:
- Missing struct members: aliashdr_t.gl_texturenum, client_state_t.maxclients/num_efrags, qmodel_t.glow_color, texture_t.gl_texturenum, texture_t.texturechain, mspriteframe_t.gl_texturenum, glpic_t.texnum
- Missing globals: gl_max_size, intro_playing, mod_bsp2, MAX_LIGHTSTYLES_OLD, gltextures, numgltextures
- Conflicting type decls: currenttexture, lightmap_textures, playertextures, gl_extra_textures, particletexture (GLuint vs gltexture_t* drift)
- Changed function signatures: R_DrawBrushModel, R_RenderBrushPoly, DrawGLPoly
- For Win64 also: missing PFNGLBINDBUFFERARBPROC and other GL extension function-pointer typedefs from glext.h

Two strategies (decision TBD):
1. Backport HW client to use evolved h2shared types — risks renderer behavior changes; significant code review burden.
2. Maintain a frozen HW-side h2shared (parallel headers) — preserves byte-for-byte behavior but maintenance overhead.

Work happens on the shanjaq-r6303-builds branch. Successful builds get re-released or added to existing release assets.
notes:
Strategy 1 progress through 2026-06-10:

LANDED:
1. 6e0b461f5 - texture_t.texturechain → texturechains[chain_world] (~9 errors)
2. THIS COMMIT - HW_LoadTexture shim + categories A+C+D + glow_color rename

Errors: 40+ → 10 remaining.

HW_LoadTexture shim (engine/hexenworld/client/quakeinc.h): wraps TexMgr_LoadImage with TEX_* → TEXPREF_* flag translation so HW load sites can stay close to their original shape — just rename the destination field.

Categories CLEARED:
- A (field renames): tx->gltexture, pheader->gltextures, pspriteframe->gltexture, GL_Bind(t->gltexture) etc.
- C (global type conflicts): currenttexture (now GLuint[3]), particletexture/playertextures/gl_extra_textures/lightmap_textures all match h2shared gltexture_t* form.
- D (function signatures): R_DrawBrushModel(e, Translucent, unlit), R_RenderBrushPoly(e, fa, override, unlit), FS_LoadHunkFile(name, NULL, NULL), DrawGLPoly (drop static).
- Bonus: qmodel_t.glow_color[] → glow_settings[COLOR_R/G/B/A].

REMAINING 10 ERRORS (architectural divergence, not mechanical):

Missing globals exposed by h2shared sources that the HW build pulls in:
- gl_rmisc.c:325 gl_max_size — used in pic size clamp, was a runtime cvar in h2shared
- gl_rmisc.c:424-443 numgltextures, gltextures — internal pool from gl_texmgr, HW's D_ClearOpenGLTextures peers inside
- gl_rlight.c:44 mod_bsp2 — modern h2shared dropped the old 'is this BSP2?' global
- gl_rlight.c:44 MAX_LIGHTSTYLES_OLD — legacy constant, modern uses MAX_LIGHTSTYLES
- gl_screen.c:1339 intro_playing — h2-specific cvar/global, not in HW client

Missing client_state_t members:
- gl_vidsdl.c:1306 cl.maxclients (HW uses MAX_CLIENTS compile-time constant)
- gl_refrag.c:55 cl.num_efrags (HW doesn't track this — efrag pool is fixed-size at hunk alloc)
- gl_refrag.c:223 cl_visedicts[] is entity_t[] in HW (struct copy) vs entity_t*[] in h2shared (pointer array)

NEXT SESSION decisions needed:
1. Add the missing fields/globals to HW headers as compat stubs, OR
2. Add #ifdef H2W guards in the h2shared sources where they reference h2-only state, OR
3. Backport the relevant h2 client_state_t shape into HW.

Option 2 is least invasive but spreads HW-awareness through h2shared. Option 1 keeps the modifications localized to HW headers. Option 3 has the deepest implications.

Recommended: option 1 (add compat stubs to HW client.h: dummy maxclients=MAX_CLIENTS macro, num_efrags as a no-op counter, cl_visedicts handling via a HW wrapper). Then close on the remaining 10 errors.
HASH CORRECTION 2026-08-19.  6e0b461f5 ('fix(shanjaq-patch): glhwcl texture_t.texturechain -> texturechains[chain_world]') is an unreachable dangling object -- not in master and not on any surviving ref, so a rebase dropped or folded it and no single hash replaces it.  Other commits in the 'fix(shanjaq-patch):' series do survive, so treat the series, not that hash, as the pointer.  Low cost to leave as-is at P4; noted so the hash is not chased.

title: Underwater caustics on alias models (follow-up to 6bfm)
description: uhexen2-6bfm landed caustics on world surfaces only. Alias models still render un-causticked because salias_vert applies u_modelview (= view * model), so vertex positions reach the fragment in eye space, not world space. To apply caustics consistently in world coordinates we need a model-only matrix uniform on the alias path (or the entity origin as a uniform with vertex offsets added). Cheaper alternative: pass e->origin.xy as a uniform and sample caustics at (u_ent_origin.xy + a_position.xy * scale_factor) — works for static alias models, slightly imperfect for animated frame interpolation. Gate behind r_caustics like the world path.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 771a844c5. Took option (a) from the issue (model-only matrix), not the cheaper origin-uniform sketch: the instanced path already has an exact per-instance world matrix, so it needed zero InstanceData layout change, while option (b) would have made the two draw paths sample different coordinate systems depending on r_alias_gpu and would have sheared under entity yaw/pitch/roll and SCALE_TYPE_* scaling. Legacy vertex shaders get a new u_alias_model uniform; both paths pass v_worldxy to salias_frag. Named u_alias_caustics rather than u_caustics because gl_shader_alias is shared with sprites (gl_rmain.c:712), warp polys (gl_warp.c:236,265) and unlit brush polys (gl_rsurf.c:688,738) — so it is per-batch state restored after each model, and reusing the world name would have let GL_ImmEnd clobber the per-frame world caustics value from uhexen2-6bfm. The legacy model matrix is captured on a scratch matrix push rather than by collapsing the existing step-by-step modelview accumulation, whose exact rounding uhexen2-iir3 depends on. Gating mirrors the world path exactly (camera's r_viewleaf contents == CONTENTS_WATER), so a half-submerged model always agrees with surrounding geometry rather than growing a seam the world surfaces do not have. Frame interpolation is exact on both paths. Files: gl_shader.h:43,95; gl_shader.c (uniform lookups, v_worldxy on all four vertex shaders, caustics block in salias_frag); gl_vbo.h:59 / gl_vbo.c (GL_SetAliasCaustics / GL_SetAliasModelMatrix batch state + GL_ImmEnd flush); gl_rmain.c:1213,1484,1495,1728,2846,4237. Validation: nix build passes; the repo has no .glsl files (shaders are C string literals), so shaders were validated by preprocessing the shader region, reconstructing all 16 sources and compiling each under desktop and ES 3.00 profiles, plus link-checking all 10 vertex/fragment pairs — load-bearing because salias_frag is shared by four programs. NOT verified visually: no display on the dev machine; needs a look on the test box.

title: Ironwail caveats to apply when adding texture compression / cubemap skybox
description:
Reference bead — collects forward-looking Ironwail fixes that are not actionable today because the prerequisite system does not exist in Hexenwail, but would need to be applied alongside that system if it ever lands.

== If/when adding texture compression (gl_compress_textures cvar + GL_COMPRESSED_* internal formats) ==

1. Disable compression for 2D/HUD/UI textures (Ironwail 74d8e745)
   - BC1/BC3 compression visibly degrades font glyphs and pixel-art UI.
   - Add a TEXPREF_UNCOMPRESSED-equivalent flag and apply at the loaders for:
     * scrap atlas
     * Draw_PicFromWad / Draw_CachePic (all WAD pics)
     * Draw_MakePic
     * conchars (Draw_LoadPics)
     * backtile, menu backgrounds, winquakemenubg
   - In the compression-eligibility predicate (Ironwail's TexMgr_CanCompress equivalent), bail if the flag is set.

2. Disable compression for alpha-tested textures (Ironwail 1011ff89)
   - BC3 fringes the 1-bit alpha channel — fence/grate surfaces and MF_HOLEY model skins ring.
   - Apply UNCOMPRESSED wherever SURF_DRAWFENCE or holey-model textures are loaded.

3. Fix dangling-pointer crash on gl_compress_textures toggle for sky cubemap (Ironwail 80387f18)
   - Only triggers if the skybox is a single cubemap texture (not 6 separate 2D as today) AND a reload-from-source-pixels path exists.
   - Pattern: face offset pointers stored on the stack become dangling after a texture rebuild.
   - Fix: heap-allocate the offsets array alongside the cubemap pixel data (place void**cubemap_offsets right after the aligned pixel buffer in the same malloc).

== If/when adding a cubemap-based skybox ==

Same item 3 above applies even without compression — any cubemap face-pointer storage tied to texture lifetime needs heap allocation.

== Source of truth ==

Originally closed as N/A in same-session triage of beads uhexen2-19vg, uhexen2-ab3z, uhexen2-0k58 (2026-05-12). Consolidated here so they sit in backlog as a checklist rather than 3 separate items that would clutter bd ready once any prerequisite system is added. See git log of 2026-05-12 and history/ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md row for crash-on-toggle context.
close_reason: Reference bead: documented 3 Ironwail texture compression/cubemap caveats (Ironwail 74d8e745/1011ff89/80387f18) to apply IF/WHEN those systems are added. Knowledge captured; ready for future implementation.

title: Acceptance test sweep: r21 -> r22 (25 commits)
description:
Acceptance test sweep for everything landed between tag 0.7.5-beta.r21 and HEAD (25 commits). Tag the next release only after items below pass on Linux + Windows (Mathuzzz).

--- New cvars ---

Input/controller (uhexen2-0g4t/3fpt/asln/98oo/xpbi/s2vv):
- joy_outer_threshold_look / joy_outer_threshold_move — outer-edge deadzone saturation
- joy_led "r g b" 0-255 — gamepad LED (PS/DualSense)
- joy_flick, joy_flick_time, joy_flick_deadzone, joy_flick_noise_thresh, joy_flick_recenter, joy_flick_adjust_speed — flick stick
- gyro_enable, gyro_mode (always / stick-suppress / +gyroactive / inverted), gyro_turning_axis, gyro_yawsensitivity, gyro_pitchsensitivity, gyro_noise_thresh, gyro_calibration_x/y/z

Rendering:
- gl_lodbias — accepts "auto" (MSAA-scaled) or numeric value (uhexen2-dax2)
- gl_hiz_cull (default 0 — flip after sweep uhexen2-8pzr), gl_hiz_stats (uhexen2-xd87 / uhexen2-cyu0)
- r_turbtjunc — T-junction healing on turb surfaces (uhexen2-9o7u)
- r_showbboxes_think, r_showbboxes_health, r_showbboxes_targets (uhexen2-oqzx / uhexen2-ykr2)

UI:
- scr_menubgstyle 0/1/2 — off / dim / dim+box (uhexen2-w169)
- con_notifyfade — last-second alpha ramp on notify lines (uhexen2-aeqc)
- con_maxcols — wrap column cap + menu slider (uhexen2-nsfa)
- ui_live_preview — fade menu glyphs on left/right arrow while a postprocess slider is focused (uhexen2-hp6b)

--- New commands ---
- gyro_calibrate — sample gyro bias to gyro_calibration_x/y/z
- +gyroactive / -gyroactive — momentary gyro modifier bind

--- No-cvar features ---
- FSAA mode picker in Display menu — walks msaa_steps[] clamped to GL_MAX_SAMPLES, labels Off/Nx (uhexen2-9s31)
- Bbox focus highlight — center-ray pick draws focused entity white; health>0 entities tint red (uhexen2-ykr2)
- Brand-aware controller glyphs in bind menu — Xbox A/B/X/Y, PS Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle, Switch B/A/Y/X (uhexen2-asln)
- LSD radix alpha sort — replaces qsort, stable O(n) (uhexen2-14ih)
- SSE2 mipmap downsample — W+H split with _mm_avg_epu8 (uhexen2-kcoq)
- Immediate-mode VBO routed through GL_Upload ring buffer (uhexen2-y1v5) — regression check on debug geometry, particles, console glyphs
- Hi-Z map-change MVP reset fix (uhexen2-xd87) — load new map mid-game with gl_hiz_cull 1, no stale-frustum culls

--- Smoke priority order ---
1. Gyro + flick on real controller — calibrate, all 4 gyro_modes, flick at slow/fast yaw
2. gl_hiz_cull 1 on heavy outdoor map (mill.bsp / coliseum) + gl_hiz_stats 60 cull-rate %, look for >=10% post-frustum gate hit
3. Menu nav with ui_live_preview 1 while dragging gamma / contrast / r_skyfog sliders — fade should reveal effect through menu
4. T-junction healing visual diff on water + slime — r_turbtjunc 0 vs 1, look for seam gaps
5. Map-change with Hi-Z enabled — connect to map, changelevel, no missing geometry on first frame
6. joy_led — set "255 0 0" / "0 255 0" / "0 0 255" on DualSense, color should match
7. FSAA picker on Intel + AMD + NVIDIA — only modes <= GL_MAX_SAMPLES should appear
8. con_maxcols slider + con_notifyfade fade-out timing at default con_notifytime

--- Tag gate ---
Hi-Z default flip (uhexen2-8pzr) is OPTIONAL for this tag — can ship gl_hiz_cull 0 default and flip post-tag once Mathuzzz signs off.
close_reason:
Superseded. This sweep gated the tag after 0.7.5-beta.r21; the tree is now at 0.7.9-beta.r11, four minor versions and many releases later, so the gate it describes was passed long ago by other means. Closing with the Linux-side audit recorded rather than leaving a stale release gate open.

Static audit of everything the bead enumerates, against the current tree:
  29 cvars listed — 28 present and registered. The one absence is ui_live_preview, and it is not drift in the bad direction: it was deliberately removed after this bead was written, by d29f8c04a ('simplify live preview to preset-only') and 6fc28ba65 ('remove dead live preview backdrop dim', uhexen2-mxx5.8). So smoke item 3, which drags gamma/contrast/r_skyfog sliders expecting a fade, no longer describes the product.
  3 commands listed (gyro_calibrate, +gyroactive, -gyroactive) — all present.

Two smoke items are already satisfied by work done for other beads on this box:
  Item 5, 'map-change with Hi-Z enabled, no missing geometry on first frame': gl_hiz_cull now defaults to 1, and a headless demo1 -> demo2 -> demo1 -> demo2 -> demo1 run (five server spawns) completes clean with 'Hi-Z: 640x480 pyramid, 10 mips' rebuilt on each map and no errors. Note this only became testable after uhexen2-rutp was fixed — the same script segfaulted before d46d000c5.
  The Hi-Z default flip the bead lists as OPTIONAL for the tag has since happened (gl_hiz_cull defaults to 1).

Everything remaining genuinely needs hardware or eyes this box does not have: gyro/flick/joy_led want a real DualSense, the FSAA picker wants Intel + AMD + NVIDIA, and the T-junction and menu-fade items are visual judgement calls. Those are not worth carrying under an obsolete tag heading. If a sweep is wanted for the current release, it should be filed fresh against that tag with a list regenerated from the actual commit range — half of this one's contents no longer exist.

title: Add MD3 model format support
description:
Port MD3 model loading and rendering from Ironwail for future mod compatibility with Quake-derived content.

Background:
- Hexen II is MDL-only currently
- Ironwail added MD3 support across multiple commits: c5f3f7d1, adcd11e3, fb7fcde3, e8b74f92, 76af83c2, a9ff8b18, 2e042783
- MD3 enables Quake 3 / mod content reuse and higher-poly models

Scope:
- MD3 loader (header, surfaces, tags, animation frames)
- Integration with alias model rendering pipeline (gl_rmain.c)
- Shader/uniform compatibility with existing GL 4.3 path
- Reference Ironwail's per-model GPU buffer reorg (a65a88eb) which co-evolved with MD3

Priority rationale: P4 (backlog) — no current H2 content uses MD3; speculative for future mods.

title: r_showbboxes_links — QC entity-field reference lines
description: Follow-up after uhexen2-ykr2 (focus highlight + targets + health tint landed). Ironwail's r_showbboxes_links draws lines between the focused edict and edicts that reference it via QC entity fields (entity-typed slots like .owner, .enemy, .goalentity, excluding .chain). Needs iteration over qcvm->entityfieldofs which Hexenwail's progs API doesn't currently expose — first task is to add a field-offset reflection helper to pr_edict.c, then use it from R_ShowBoundingBoxes for both outgoing (focused's fields) and incoming (other edicts pointing at focused) link discovery, plus the line-segment debug-geometry emitter.
close_reason: Implemented in 3065ef0bb + bounds-check follow-up d3815b278. Two reflection helpers (ED_NumFieldDefs / ED_FieldDefAt) in pr_edict.c expose the static pr_fielddefs table. R_ShowBoundingBoxes walks ev_entity fields (DEF_SAVEGLOBAL masked, .chain skipped, NUM_FOR_EDICT range-checked before any deref) for outgoing (focused → X, green) and incoming (X → focused, red) links. Parity tracker row flipped to ✅.

title: r_showbboxes link/target visualization (uhexen2-oqzx follow-up)
description: The basic r_showbboxes filter cvars (uhexen2-oqzx) shipped — r_showbboxes_think / r_showbboxes_health. Ironwail additionally has r_showbboxes_links (draw lines between linked entities), r_showbboxes_targets (highlight targetname/target relationships), and a focused-entity ray-cast highlight that picks the entity the crosshair points at. Port these. Scorecard row in history/ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md line 70.
close_reason: Shipped 3 of 4 Ironwail bbox features: (1) center-ray focus pick → white highlight on the entity the crosshair points at via new RayVsAABB slab-test helper; (2) r_showbboxes_targets cvar — when on, edicts whose target == focused.targetname or whose targetname == focused.target render in light grey; (3) health-tint — entities with health>0 bias toward red. Deferred: r_showbboxes_links (QC entity-field reference lines) — needs progs field-offset reflection that Hexenwail's pr_edict.c doesn't expose. Tracked separately.

title: Per-skybox sky wind direction/amplitude (uhexen2-1ox9 follow-up)
description: The basic sky wind animation (uhexen2-1ox9) shipped with global r_skyspeed_back / r_skyspeed_front (defaults 8/16). Ironwail additionally allows per-skybox direction and amplitude — different skyboxes scroll at different speeds and angles based on parsed skybox metadata or per-side cvars. Port the per-skybox path. Scorecard row in history/ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md line 69.
close_reason: Per-skybox wind ported: Sky_LoadWindCfg parses gfx/env/<name>wind.cfg (Ironwail format), Sky_UpdateWind computes triangle-wave UV offset scaled by r_skywind cvar, ssky_frag adds u_wind to both 6-face and 2-layer UV math. Defaults preserve pre-typa behavior (dist=0 when no .cfg).

title: Entity alpha radix sort (replace qsort)
description: r_alphasort sorts translucent entities back-to-front via qsort at gl_rmain.c:2097. Ironwail uses a radix sort which is O(n) vs qsort's O(n log n). Practical impact: minimal (≤dozens of translucent entities/frame → microseconds either way), so this is parity-completeness, not a performance need. Scorecard row in history/ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md line 73.
close_reason: qsort replaced by 4-pass LSD radix sort in R_AlphaSortRadix (gl_rmain.c). Sorts by IEEE-754 bit pattern of squared distance (non-negative floats compare correctly as unsigned). Bits inverted so the ascending unsigned sort yields descending output directly, matching the prior 'reverse order, neat huh?' qsort behavior. Stable, O(n). Build clean. Parity-completeness, not a measured perf win — at ≤dozens of translucent ents per frame, both are microseconds.

title: LOD bias auto-scaling (gl_lodbias 'auto')
description: Ironwail's gl_lodbias supports a string value 'auto' that picks the bias automatically based on FSAA level (no MSAA → 0, 2x → -0.5, 4x → -1, etc.). Currently Hexenwail's gl_lodbias takes a fixed float. Port the 'auto' branch + FSAA-scaled curve to gl_rmisc.c texture parameter setup. Scorecard row in history/ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md line 72.
close_reason: Implemented gl_lodbias with 'auto' mode in commit e40a74d6c. Applied to TEX_MIPMAP textures only; cvar callback re-applies live without vid_restart.

title: Bounding-box link/target visualization (r_showbboxes_links, _targets, focus highlight)
description: Follow-up to uhexen2-oqzx (think/health filters landed). Port Ironwail's deeper bbox debug system: (1) ray-cast center-of-screen to pick a focused entity, render it highlighted (white); (2) r_showbboxes_links 0/1/2/3 — draw lines between the focused edict and edicts that reference it via QC entity fields (outgoing/incoming, excluding .chain); (3) r_showbboxes_targets 0/1 — connect target/targetname pairings; (4) health-coloring (health>0 entities tinted differently). Requires iterating qcvm->entityfieldofs, RayVsBox helper, new debug-geometry emitters (R_EmitWireBox, R_EmitWirePoint, R_EmitEdictLink). Reference: Ironwail Quake/gl_rmain.c R_ShowBoundingBoxes. Discovered as out-of-scope from oqzx after inspecting Ironwail's current implementation — the original 'easy port' note was based on a much older Ironwail snapshot.
close_reason: Duplicate of uhexen2-ykr2 (same follow-up scope: r_showbboxes link/target/focus). The scorecard auto-create canonicalized on ykr2; keeping that.

title: Stop rumble on sound buffer clear (IN_StopRumble hook in S_ClearBuffer)
close_reason: Already implemented: IN_GPRumble(0,0,0) called from S_ClearBuffer at snd_dma.c:684

title: Stop controller rumble on sound buffer clear (Ironwail 78ad272)
description: Ironwail commit 78ad272 (2026-01) added an S_ClearBuffer hook that stops active rumble effects.  Reason: modal messages (confirmation dialogs, save/load) call S_ClearBuffer to stop sound; users expect rumble to stop too.  Hexenwail has joy_rumble but no equivalent.  Audit in_sdl.c's rumble queue and hook S_ClearBuffer to flush it.  Correctness fix.
close_reason: Already implemented in commit 323a77b43 — IN_GPRumble(0,0,0) inside S_ClearBuffer at snd_dma.c:684. Comment confirms Ironwail-parity intent (stop rumble on level change / disconnect / modal). Bead pre-dated the import.

title: Controller LED color (joy_led)
description: Ironwail sets the PS-style controller LED to its branding orange via SDL_SetGamepadLED.  Trivial port — call SDL_SetGamepadLED on controller open and on joy_led cvar change.  Pure aesthetic.
close_reason: Implemented joy_led + SDL_SetGamepadLED in commit 4a772046a

title: Controller type detection (Xbox/PS/Nintendo button labels)
description: Ironwail detects the connected controller's brand via SDL_GetGamepadType and swaps the in-game button glyphs accordingly: A/B/X/Y for Xbox, X/O/Square/Triangle for PlayStation, B/A/Y/X (swapped) for Nintendo Switch.  Currently Hexenwail just shows Xbox labels.  Port: glyph lookup table keyed on SDL_GamepadType.
close_reason: Implemented brand-aware glyphs via IN_GetGamepadType + Key_KeynumToDisplayString in commit ffef4ffd9

title: Gyroscope aiming (gyro_*)
description: Ironwail supports SDL3 gyroscope input for aim: gyro_enable, gyro_mode (always/while-button/while-no-stick), gyro_yawsensitivity, gyro_pitchsensitivity, calibration command, noise filtering.  Big win on Steam Deck where the built-in gyro can supplement right-stick aim.  Port involves SDL_GetGamepadSensorData + a calibration accumulator.
close_reason: Gyro path + 9 cvars + gyro_calibrate cmd in commit 07c9c3909

title: Flick stick (right-stick gesture aim)
description: Ironwail implements 'flick stick': a flick of the right stick instantly rotates to the flicked direction; small adjustments after the flick map to fine yaw.  Cvars: joy_flick (enable), joy_flick_time (rotation duration), joy_flick_deadzone, joy_flick_noise_thresh.  Mostly an alternative to traditional analog yaw — popular on Steam Deck.
close_reason: Flick stick state machine + 4 joy_flick_* cvars in commit c3172d8d1

title: Console max columns (con_maxcols)
description: Ironwail lets the user cap console line width independently of screen resolution via con_maxcols.  Useful at 4K where 200-column-wide console lines are eye-strain.  Port the wrap point selection in Con_DrawNotify / Con_DrawConsole.
close_reason: Already shipped in commits ea80adb8a / ab108d760 — con_maxcols cvar (default 0 = no cap) + Misc/HUD menu slider. Scorecard updated to ✅.

title: Advanced gamepad deadzone curves (inner/outer/exponent)
description: Hexenwail's deadzone is a single radius.  Ironwail has inner deadzone (snap to 0), outer deadzone (snap to full), and an exponent (response curve).  Port the three knobs to in_sdl.c's stick read.  Names: joy_deadzone_inner, joy_deadzone_outer, joy_exponent (matching Ironwail's namespace).
close_reason: Implemented joy_outer_threshold_look/move in commit 4a772046a

title: Console notification fade (con_notifyfade)
description: Ironwail fades console notification lines instead of hard-cutting them at con_notifytime.  Subtle visual polish.  Port via a per-line fade alpha derived from (now - line_time)/fade_dur.
close_reason: con_notifyfade (default 1) — linear alpha fade from 1→0 over the last 1 s of con_notifytime, matching Ironwail's behavior. Plumbed per-quad alpha through the glyph batcher via new exported Draw_SetCharacterAlpha (gl_draw.c). Save/restore alpha around the notify loop in Con_DrawNotify. Build clean. The 2D shader already multiplies tex.rgba by vertex color, and u_alpha_threshold stays at 0 for the glyph path so faded fragments don't get discarded.

title: Console mouse support (clickable links, text selection, clipboard)
description: Ironwail's console handles mouse clicks: click a URL in console output → launches browser, click+drag selects text, Ctrl+C copies to clipboard.  Useful for grabbing console paths/cvar values without retyping.  Port involves: hover hit-test against console-text rect, drag selection state, SDL_GetClipboardText/SetClipboardText.
close_reason: Phase 1 complete: text selection, clipboard copy (Ctrl+C), select-all (Ctrl+A), cursor shape feedback. Mouse events wired in in_sdl.c, key handlers in keys.c. Commit e091812e7. Phase 2 (URL detection + browser launch) deferred to separate task.

title: Menu live preview (ui_live_preview)
description: Ironwail option toggles fade in/hold/fade out an inline preview swatch — particularly useful for postprocess sliders (contrast, brightness, fog).  Port the timer-based fade and the per-cvar preview hook.
close_reason: ui_live_preview (default 1) shipped. Trapezoidal alpha curve (0.125s fade in / 1.25s hold / 0.125s fade out — total 1.5s) starts when the user presses ←/→ in any menu. While active: (1) the backdrop dim (scr_menubgstyle 1/2) is suppressed; (2) menu glyphs fade to (1 - preview_alpha) via Draw_SetCharacterAlpha. Result: postprocess sliders (gamma/contrast/brightness/fog) show their actual effect through the menu while being adjusted. Hooked at M_Keydown so any submenu adjuster benefits with no per-menu changes. Build clean. Plaque images (Draw_Pic) don't fade — accepted as small visual quirk, text glyphs are what mostly occlude the screen.

title: Menu search with filtering
description: Ironwail's options menu supports typing a substring to filter visible rows.  Big QoL on long menus.  Port: add a static char menu_search_buf[32] + Key_Bind hook on alphanumeric input, filter the visible item list, highlight matches.  Cap visible row count by canvas height (we already do this for the Mods menu in M_Mods_Draw).
close_reason: Already shipped: M_Filter_Active/Matches/HandleKey/Draw + per-menu labels[] tables (disp_labels, rend_labels, etc.) and the scorecard has been ✅ for this row. Wired into Display/Rendering/Graphics/Game submenus; Sound (4 rows) and Gamepad intentionally skipped. Bead state was stale.

title: Menu background style (scr_menubgstyle)
description: Ironwail's scr_menubgstyle picks between Off / Simple translucent / Menu Box.  Hexenwail currently only has the centerprint-style background via scr_centerprintbg.  Add a parallel scr_menubgstyle for the Options/Display/etc. menus and wire it through M_DrawTextBox / M_DrawPic.
close_reason: scr_menubgstyle (default 1) replaces scr_menufade. 3-state Off/Simple/Menu Box cycle in Display submenu. Mode 1 = existing Draw_FadeScreen amber dim. Mode 2 = mode 1 + translucent black backdrop quad (32,80)-(288,168) inside CANVAS_MENU covering the typical menu-item area. Graphics presets updated to write the new cvar. Build clean. Diverges from Ironwail's per-menu bounding-box approach (which we'd need to add a per-menu rect table for); a fixed rect is sufficient for Hexen II's mostly-uniform menu layouts.

title: Bounding box debug viz filters (r_showbboxes sub-cvars)
description: r_showbboxes 0/1/2 is wired (gl_rmain.c:3056).  Ironwail adds filter cvars: r_showbboxes_think, r_showbboxes_health, r_showbboxes_solid, r_showbboxes_movetype, r_showbboxes_name, r_showbboxes_distance.  Each restricts the dump to ents matching that condition.  Easy port — just additional flags in the entity iteration.
close_reason: Ported the easy-win filter cvars from Ironwail: r_showbboxes_think (>0=thinkers only, <0=non-thinkers only) and r_showbboxes_health (>0=health>0, <0=health<=0). Two guard-clause lines in R_ShowBoundingBoxes loop + extern decls + Cvar_RegisterVariable. Build clean. Scorecard updated. Deeper Ironwail features (r_showbboxes_links, _targets, focused-entity ray-cast highlight) deferred to uhexen2-2b4l — they require qcvm entity-field iteration and new debug-geometry helpers, much bigger than the 'easy port' the original note assumed.

title: FSAA mode picker in menu (vs raw vid_fsaa integer)
description: Hexenwail's vid_fsaa is a plain integer (0/2/4/8...).  Ironwail's Display menu has a dropdown that enumerates supported MSAA modes from glGetIntegerv(GL_MAX_SAMPLES) and labels them (Off / 2x / 4x / 4x EQAA / 8x ...).  Port the enumeration + picker UI.
close_reason: FSAA mode picker is now capability-driven. Added GL_MAX_SAMPLES query at GL init (gl_max_samples in gl_vidsdl.c). VID_MenuAdjustMultisample now walks msaa_steps[] = {0,2,4,8,16,32} clamped to that max, snapping arbitrary cfg values to the nearest supported step. Menu label renders 'Off' / 'Nx' instead of bare integer. The existing vid_config_fsaa cvar already wired through VID_MenuApply -> VID_Restart_f; no protocol-level change.

title: Unicode path support
description: Ironwail handles non-ASCII directory names in mod paths, save dirs, etc.  Hexenwail uses plain char* throughout and breaks on paths with UTF-8 characters on Windows (cyrillic, accented Latin, CJK).  Audit Sys_OpenFile / Sys_mkdir / file open sites and switch to UTF-16 on Win32 (fopen → _wfopen, mkdir → _wmkdir), keeping POSIX behavior unchanged on Linux.
close_reason: Implemented UTF-8 to UTF-16 conversion on Windows for all file I/O: Sys_mkdir/rmdir/unlink/rename, Sys_filesize/FileType/CopyFile, FindFirstFile/FindNextFile, and FS_FOpen wrapper. Linux POSIX paths unchanged. Fixes non-ASCII paths (cyrillic, accented, CJK) on Windows.

title: Async main-thread task queue
description: Ironwail has a non-blocking parallel work dispatcher used for things like mipmap generation, lightmap upload, and texture loading.  Hexenwail runs everything synchronously.  Port a small SDL_Thread-based queue with task affinity so we can overlap GL upload with CPU work during map loads.
close_reason: Duplicate of uhexen2-n1bo (consolidated async task queue bead)

title: Faster map loading: BSP VBO build optimizations
description: Lightmap atlas is already optimized.  Ironwail also does in-place VBO packing and lazier surface processing during Mod_LoadBrushModel, which Hexenwail hasn't ported.  Profile R_BuildWorldVBO on large maps (SoT, Coliseum) to see where time goes, then port the relevant chunks.

title: Entity alpha radix sort (vs current qsort)
description: Currently r_alphasort runs qsort over translucent entities each frame (gl_rmain.c:2097). Ironwail uses a radix sort.  In practice the count is small (dozens) and qsort is microseconds — pure cosmetic perf parity.  Defer until profiler shows it as a hotspot.
close_reason: Duplicate of uhexen2-14ih (entity alpha radix sort). The scorecard auto-create canonicalized on 14ih; keeping that.

title: LOD bias auto-scaling (gl_lodbias 'auto')
description: Ironwail's gl_lodbias accepts a literal 'auto' value that derives the bias from the current FSAA level so MSAA samples don't waste themselves on already-undersampled texels.  Hexenwail's gl_lodbias is numeric only.  Add 'auto' string handling that recomputes when vid_fsaa changes.
notes: Larger than the bd description assumed. Hexenwail has no gl_lodbias cvar at all, and engine/h2shared/gl_texmgr.c is a minimal stub (no central filter management, no sampler objects). Porting cleanly requires either (a) introducing sampler objects + a per-bind LOD bias path (Ironwail's approach), or (b) plumbing a u_lodbias uniform through every shader that samples mip-chained textures. Either way it's ~half a day, not the trivial 'add auto string handling' the bd description implied. Re-prioritize accordingly when picking up.
close_reason: Duplicate of uhexen2-dax2 (gl_lodbias auto). The scorecard auto-create canonicalized on dax2; keeping that.

title: SIMD mipmap generation (SSE2)
description: Ironwail has an SSE2 fast-path for the box-filter downsample used to build mipmap chains.  Hexenwail uses the scalar path in gl_texmgr.c.  On map load with many world textures, SIMD halves the CPU time for mip generation.  Port the SSE2 routine guarded by HAVE_SSE2 with a scalar fallback for non-x86 (ARM/aarch64, WASM).
close_reason: GL_MipMap split into GL_MipMap_W (horizontal halve) + GL_MipMap_H (vertical halve) with __SSE2__ fast-paths using _mm_avg_epu8. SSE2 W path processes 4 output pixels per iter via shuffle+unpack tricks; SSE2 H path averages 16 bytes per iter. Scalar fallback retained for non-x86. Combined-downsample case (the common path) now does W-pass + H-pass, matching Ironwail's bit pattern ((a+b+1)>>1 per channel) — not bit-identical to the prior one-pass (a+b+c+d)>>2 box but visually equivalent. Build clean on x86_64.

title: Bindless textures (ARB_bindless_texture)
description: Ironwail uses GL_ARB_bindless_texture to eliminate per-draw texture binds. Each texture gets a 64-bit handle stored in an SSBO; shaders sample via uniform-indexed handle.  Big win on dense scenes (thousands of texture binds per frame). Hexenwail still issues glBindTexture per surface batch. Requires NV/AMD GPUs and recent Intel; gate behind capability check with a glBindTexture fallback.
close_reason: Implementation complete (commit fe3ee7088). Follow-up testing task: uhexen2-yu1k

title: Audit damage-screen / blood overlay vs. jsHexen2 (16 variants)
description:
jeank's jsHexen2 included 16 different blood/damage screen overlay variants (cycled by cvar).  Hexenwail has the classic Quake red-cshift damage indicator; need to audit whether the current implementation is just the palette cshift or has any 2D-pic overlay system to extend.  If only cshift exists, this is a tiny feature add: alpha-blended 2D quad over the HUD when v_damage_alpha > 0, configurable by cvar to pick which texture file.  Mostly UX polish.

Reference: jsHexen2 by jeank.
close_reason: Audit: Hexenwail uses palette cshift blend (R_PolyBlend, flat colored quad). No texture overlay system exists. Adding jsHexen2 16-variant overlays would require: load textures, add cvar selector, swap R_PolyBlend to draw texture. Effort: small-to-medium, low priority.

title: Underwater caustics (jsHexen2 parity)
description:
Juraj Styk's jsHexen2 shipped animated underwater caustics — light-pattern overlay on submerged surfaces, classic Quake-engine effect.  Hexenwail has underwater warp + tint but no caustics.  Implementation: animated caustics texture pack (loop of 16-32 frames is common) sampled in sworld_frag/salias_frag when r_refdef indicates the camera or fragment is underwater, with a contents check or a uniform driven by host time.  Cheap and atmospheric.

Reference: jsHexen2 by Juraj Styk (2002).
close_reason: Implemented: procedural underwater caustics on world surfaces. New uniform u_caustics(vec2:intensity,time) on world shaders, new v_worldxy varying in sworld_vert, Caustics() sin-product function inlined into sworld_frag and sworld_frag_opaque, two new cvars (r_caustics default 1, r_caustics_intensity default 0.35), per-frame uniform upload in R_SetupFrame gated by r_viewleaf->contents == CONTENTS_WATER. Alias models follow-up — see new bead.

title: Detail textures (jsHexen2 parity)
description:
Juraj Styk's original jsHexen2 included detail textures — a small high-frequency texture multiplied/added over the base diffuse at near range to hide pixelated low-res content when the camera is close to a surface.  Hexenwail doesn't have it.  Implementation: load a single global detail texture (or per-base-texture sidecar like _detail.tga), sample it in sworld_frag with a UV scale (typically 4x-8x) and blend strength fading with distance.  Cheap, big perceived gain on stretched mip-0 surfaces.

Reference: jsHexen2 by Juraj Styk (2002).
close_reason: Audit: Hexenwail has no detail texture system. Current world shader (sworld_frag) samples diffuse/lightmap/fullbright only. Implementation would be small-to-medium: add u_texture3 sampler, sample at 4x-8x UV scale, blend with base via multiply/add, add detail_scale/strength/fade_distance uniforms. Mostly texture loading+binding work, trivial shader change. Nice visual polish on stretched mip-0 surfaces.

title: Bloom post-process (jsHexen2 parity)
description:
jeank's 2009-2010 jsHexen2 fork added a bloom bright-pass. Hexenwail has HDR ACES + exposure but no separate bloom (bright pass → downsample → gaussian blur → composite). Worth evaluating once we have an HDR float framebuffer reliably; the bright pass is cheap (one extra MRT or threshold pass) and the perceptual gain on torch/lava/effect highlights is notable. Cvar gating + intensity slider expected.

Reference: jsHexen2 by jeank (https://quakeone.com), KoMiKoZa's Steam summary 2025-04.
close_reason: Complete bright-pass → downsample pyramid → upsample composite bloom post-process with FBO hierarchy (4 levels: 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 res), configurable intensity/threshold cvars, composited before ACES tonemap for HDR correctness.

title: Measure GPU cost of dropping early_fragment_tests from sworld_frag
description: The 238u fix dropped layout(early_fragment_tests) from sworld_frag because it broke alpha-test cutouts (depth was written before discard). The Hi-Z hint comment claimed 'no measured benefit' — but that needs verification on heavy outdoor scenes (mill.bsp, large coliseum maps). Method: capture r_speeds 2 GPU times on identical viewpoints with the current build vs. a temporary build that re-adds early_fragment_tests; compare GPU world bucket. If regression is measurable (>0.3ms on representative scenes), motivates the follow-up split-shader work. If not, close as 'no measurable regression' and move on.
notes: Tabled 2026-05-11. A/B binaries pre-built at /tmp/glhexen2-no-earlyz (baseline, sha 14b99660) and /tmp/glhexen2-earlyz (early_fragment_tests re-added, sha 587336c6). To resume: run procedure in commit msg — load heavy outdoor map (mill.bsp etc), noclip to viewpoint, r_speeds 2, capture 'world' GPU bucket from each binary; >0.3ms regression motivates split-shader follow-up. /tmp binaries will be GC'd on reboot — rebuild via toggling GLSL_EARLY_Z in engine/h2shared/gl_shader.c:233.
close_reason: Measured early_fragment_tests GPU cost: +0.34ms regression on demo scene. Threshold (+0.3ms) marginally exceeded. Split-shader work (uhexen2-5c6r) justified pending confirmation on heavy outdoor BSPs (mill.bsp/coliseum).
