title: Fix WASM build: guard remaining _fp value-tests
description:
WASM build broken on master.  After OIT and GPU profiling landed on
desktop, two function-like macros (glBlendFunci_fp, glGenQueries_fp) are
tested as values in C, which doesn't compile under Emscripten where
those *_fp tokens are #defined to ((void)0).

Partial fix exists on branch wasm-demo (commit e542a799):
- gl_postprocess.c: introduce HW_OIT_HAS_BLEND_FUNCI helper (0 on
  Emscripten, runtime-tested on desktop).  Replace 4 value-test sites.
- gl_rmain.c R_ProfileInit: #ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__ early-return.

The gl_worldcull.c part already shipped on master via the file-level
#ifndef __EMSCRIPTEN__ guard — no work needed there.

Reproducer:
  nix develop -f shell-wasm.nix --command bash -c 'cd engine && \
    mkdir -p build-wasm && cd build-wasm && \
    emcmake cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DUSE_CODEC_VORBIS=OFF \
      -DUSE_ALSA=OFF .. && emmake make -j$(nproc)'

Definition of done: clean WASM build, ~1.4 MB hexenwail.wasm produced.
close_reason:
Fixed in commit e13ab194c. WASM build now links (1,648,647 bytes), desktop build passes (1,525,512 bytes).

Changes: HW_OIT_HAS_BLEND_FUNCI helper (engine/h2shared/gl_postprocess.c:50-57) replaces four glBlendFunci_fp value-tests. R_ProfileInit guard on !glGenQueries_fp test (engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:4934). Comprehensive audit found no additional value-tests to guard beyond those five sites.

Two further WASM breaks fixed: (1) GL_QUADS/GL_POLYGON shim now centralized in engine/h2shared/glheader.h:67-77 (was duplicated in 8 files). (2) R_FreeWorldCull Emscripten stub added (engine/h2shared/gl_worldcull.c:1303-1309).

Not verified on browser yet.

title: Demo distributable: bundle engine + Hexen II demo data1 (Linux/Windows/Web)
description:
Build a redistributable demo package that bundles the modernized Hexenwail
engine with the Nov 1997 Hexen II demo data — same idea Hammer of Thyrion
has used for ~25 years.  Currently every release zip says "Requires game
data files (data1/pak0.pak, data1/pak1.pak)"; this gives us a "just run it"
download for new users and a one-click web build for hosting.

Tarball already in repo: assets/demo/hexen2demo_nov1997-linux-i586.tgz
(13 MB, sha256 2df15cde0128b7a036e71995e068ca853f13be8e2b591caac140025d66643fc0).
Source: uHexen2 v1.5.8 release — "3-level v1.11 Hexen II Demo from Nov.
1997 running on the Hammer of Thyrion engine".

== Deliverables ==

1. assets/demo/  — tarball + extracted license docs (HEXEN2_DEMO_LICENSE.txt
   from SUBLICENSE.doc, plus DEMO.TXT and ABOUT) + README explaining
   provenance and sha256.

2. flake.nix outputs:
   - demodata     — pure derivation, untar -> data1/ directory
   - demo-linux   — release/linux-x86_64 ∪ data1 → zip
   - demo-windows — release/windows-x86_64 ∪ data1 → zip
   - demo-wasm    — wasm build with -DGAME_DATA_DIR=…/data1, output is
                    index.html + .js + .wasm + .data preload bundle

3. CI: extend .github/workflows/release.yml so push of a v* tag also
   produces hexenwail-<ver>-demo-linux-x86_64.zip,
   hexenwail-<ver>-demo-windows-x86_64.zip, and
   hexenwail-<ver>-demo-web.zip, attached to the GitHub release.

4. Release notes: prepend a "Demo (no data needed)" section above the
   existing "Full version (BYO paks)" section.

5. License: each demo bundle ships with
     licenses/HEXEN2_DEMO_LICENSE.txt   (Raven/Activision sublicense)
     licenses/HEXENWAIL_LICENSE.txt     (engine GPL2+)
     DEMO_README.md                     (provenance + license summary)

== Prereq blocker ==

The WASM build is currently broken on master after some _fp value-tests
landed for OIT, GPU profiling, and compute world cull.  Partial fix on
branch wasm-demo (commit e542a799).  The gl_worldcull.c piece is already
fixed on master via #ifndef __EMSCRIPTEN__ at the top of the file, but
gl_postprocess.c (HW_OIT_HAS_BLEND_FUNCI helper) and gl_rmain.c
(R_ProfileInit guard) are not.

== Open questions ==

- Repo size: 13 MB tarball checked in.  Acceptable, or move to git-lfs?
- Web demo hosting: zip only, or also auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on
  release? (Two extra CI lines, gives a permanent URL.)
- Bundle naming: hexenwail-<ver>-demo-<plat>.zip vs.
  hexenwail-demo-<plat>.zip.  Former matches current scheme.

== Non-goals ==

- Replacing or competing with the existing "BYO paks" release.  Both go
  in the same GitHub release.
- Mac, Android, or Flatpak demo bundles for now — those can come later.
- Modifying demo data (paks travel verbatim).
notes:
2026-08-11: the data half of this epic is settled, and not the way it was written.

uhexen2-3vmk found that we have no right to redistribute Raven's demo data (only licence shipped is Activision's retail EULA, which forbids distributing copies; no shareware grant exists). So deliverables 2-5 as originally specified — demo-linux / demo-windows / demo-wasm zips containing data1, release.yml attaching them, Pages auto-deploy, release notes advertising a 'no data needed' download — cannot ship as written. menr.3-.8 are blocked on 3vmk.

uhexen2-49ep (closed, commit 9cec08fd5) delivers the user-facing goal by the other route: scripts/get_demo.sh, scripts/get_demo.ps1 and 'nix run .#get-demo' let the user fetch the demo themselves from uHexen2's SourceForge with hash verification, and the no-data error now points at them. A new user gets from zero to playing in one command without Hexenwail hosting or relicensing anything.

What remains of this epic if 3vmk stays NO:
  - menr.3-.6 (flake demodata + demo-{linux,windows,wasm} outputs): drop, or rewrite as engine-only artifacts that call get_demo on first run. The WASM case is the awkward one — a browser build cannot shell out to a script, so demo-wasm either needs the user to upload their own data (uhexen2-4zzm already covers that) or does not happen.
  - menr.7-.8 (release artifacts + Pages): same, engine-only.
  - Release notes: replace the planned 'Demo (no data needed)' section with a pointer to the fetch command.
Reopening the bundling path needs a real grant from Activision, which is the open half of 3vmk.
close_reason:
Epic resolved: deliverable 1 shipped, deliverables 2-5 will not.

Deliverable 1 (assets/demo/ — provenance, sha256, extracted licence docs) landed under menr.1/menr.2 and stands.

Deliverables 2-5 are all forms of redistributing Raven's demo data, and uhexen2-3vmk established we have no right to do that: the only licence shipped with the tarball is Activision's retail EULA, which forbids distributing copies, and no shareware or demo grant exists to be found. menr.3-.8 closed as won't-ship.

The epic's actual goal — a new user gets from zero to playing without owning the game — is met by the other route, and already is: uhexen2-49ep (9cec08fd5) ships get_demo.sh / get_demo.cmd / 'nix run .#get-demo', which fetch the demo from uHexen2's SourceForge with sha256 verification, and the engine's no-data error names them. The user still runs one command; we just do not host the bytes.

The open questions in the description (git-lfs, Pages hosting, bundle naming) are moot along with the bundles.

Reopen only if a written redistribution grant appears — the sub-issue designs are still sound, they lack permission rather than work. Full reasoning in assets/demo/README.md.

title: Investigate: how does Ironwail actually do step-mover lerp (re-attempt)
description:
Reverted three rounds of step-mover lerp work (commits 6afc64e67, 532693939, 500879b8a) in the 0.7.1 → 0.7.2 cut because the result didn't hold up under SoT mod testing — Mathuzzz repeatedly reported 'lerping needs smoothing' even after multiple iterations.

What we tried (don't repeat blindly):
1. Phase 1 (6afc64e67): added R_AliasResolveLerp helper, LERP_RESETANIM2 two-stage reset, r_lerpmove cvar, set LERP_MOVESTEP from U_NOLERP. Phase 1 alone left step-movers using msg_origins lerp via cl_main.c.
2. Phase 2 (532693939): capped CL_LerpPoint extrapolation at frac=1 for LERP_MOVESTEP. Didn't help enough.
3. Phase 3 (500879b8a): Ironwail-style render-time fixed-window lerp at 0.1s — separate branch in CL_RelinkEntities using previousorigin/currentorigin/movelerpstart. Didn't help enough.

Hypothesis I had at the time: MOVETYPE_STEP entities think every 0.1s on a 20Hz tick (Hexen II's sys_ticrate = 0.05), so per-tick msg_origins lerp pauses every other tick → visible 'move-pause-move-pause' stutter.

What to investigate before the next attempt:
- Read Ironwail's R_SetupEntityTransform (Quake/r_alias.c line ~169) AND the surrounding scaffolding — particularly how it interacts with cl_main's CL_RelinkEntities. Ironwail uses a 0.1s window assuming Quake's 10Hz physics (sys_ticrate 0.1). At Hexen II's 20Hz our window timing assumption may be wrong.
- Trace the actual server tick rate that SoT mods run at. Some mods change sys_ticrate.
- Compare against how DarkPlaces / FTE handle MOVETYPE_STEP at 20Hz — they have decades of polish here.
- Reproduce the visible bug locally first (set up SoT, find a moving monster Mathuzzz mentioned, capture before/after frames).
- Decide: do we want fixed-window render-time lerp (Ironwail's approach) OR stick with msg_origins-based per-tick lerp + adaptive extrapolation?
- The entity_t fields previousorigin/currentorigin/previousangles/currentangles/movelerpstart still exist in render.h from earlier — we don't need to add them.

Reference Ironwail commits:
- /home/josh/tmp/claudedir/ironwail/Quake/r_alias.c R_SetupEntityTransform
- /home/josh/tmp/claudedir/ironwail/Quake/cl_parse.c LERP_MOVESTEP set on U_STEP bit
- /home/josh/tmp/claudedir/ironwail/Quake/cl_main.c interaction (look for r_lerpmove gating)

Reverted-from commits to consult (in our git history): 6afc64e67, 532693939, 500879b8a.

Don't re-attempt without reproducing the bug locally first.
close_reason: Root cause was a wire-up gap, not a window-timing issue. The LERP_MOVESTEP flag was defined in render.h but never set anywhere — the prior r5 frac-cap (76d1b7e5a) and r9 render-time lerp (1b6bd15fb) both gated on LERP_MOVESTEP and so were dead code at runtime, which is why Mathuzzz couldn't perceive any improvement. Fix: restored the U_NOLERP→LERP_MOVESTEP wire-up in cl_parse.c that was lost in the 0.7.1→0.7.2 cleanup of commit 6afc64e67, plus reinstated the Ironwail-style 0.1s render-time lerp branch in CL_RelinkEntities and the r_lerpmove cvar. Bumps r4→r5. The bead hypothesis (0.1s window vs 20Hz tick mismatch) cannot be evaluated until the gate flag is actually being set; if step-mover stutter persists with this enabled, then the window-timing hypothesis becomes testable.

title: Higher-quality sample resampler in ResampleSfx (snd_mem.c)
description:
Our snd_mem.c:30 ResampleSfx uses linear/nearest-neighbor interpolation (samplefrac approach) when resampling sound assets at load time to shm->speed. For 11025→44100 sounds (most of pak0/pak1), this introduces aliasing and a muddy high-frequency response.

Improvements to consider:
- Cubic / B-spline interpolator (cheap, ~2x cost over linear)
- Windowed-sinc resampler (high quality, more code)
- Cache the resampled output once per sound (already done — sfxcache_t->speed == shm->speed)

This is the load-time analog to Ironwail's paint-time snd_filterquality, but for our different pipeline. Not urgent: the audible improvement is subtle and most users won't notice. Filed as discovered-from from uhexen2-l67u (closed N/A) — that issue's premise didn't fit our architecture.
notes:
EVIDENCE CORRECTION 2026-08-12, same day: the close reason's 'mid-session toggle' claim was reported from a run that did not actually test one. '+exec <absolute path>' silently fails -- exec only searches the game filesystem -- so that cfg never ran; the width flip mid-run came from snd_resample having been archived into ~/.hexen2/data1/config.cfg by an earlier run and exec'd at init. The claim itself is correct, but it has now been verified properly, with the cfg in the gamedir and exec'd by relative name:

  soundlist before the toggle : 218 sounds resident, 209 at (8b), 9 at (16b) -- the 9 are the
                                natively-16-bit WAVs -- Total resident 12,488,344 bytes
  'snd_resample 1' mid-game   : cache flushed, 12.49 MB -> the handful that reload
  soundlist after             : every reloaded sound now (16b), including ambience/birds.wav
                                (12,864 -> 25,728 bytes) and misc/tomb.wav (290,024 -> 580,048),
                                Total resident 1,236,968

So S_ResampleChanged's Cache_Free sweep works and the cvar can be A/B'd live in one session, which is what uhexen2-edqp needs. The other verification in the close reason (alloc == used across 223 loads, per-cvar widths) used '+snd_resample <v>' on the command line, which does execute, and stands unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented in 7acd1a7a4 as a Blackman-windowed sinc polyphase resampler (16 taps, 128 phases) behind cvar snd_resample, default 0. Scored against a 128-tap double-precision reference over every 8-bit mono sound in pak0: point 10.66 dB SNR, the reverted Catmull-Rom 22.29 dB, the new filter 30.28 dB; image energy for a 3 kHz tone is 77 dB below the legacy path. All three defects the reopen listed are handled: 16-bit store via SND_ResampledWidth() which S_LoadSound also uses for the allocation (verified alloc == used over 223 loads); rounding instead of the truncating >>8; and no headroom scaling needed because a windowed sinc only clips genuine inter-sample peaks (0.085 percent of samples, costing 0.16 dB, measured by re-running with the clamp off) rather than the old kernel's 25 percent overshoot. Default left at 0 deliberately: the numbers all favour it but de-aliasing 8-bit sfx is a taste change, and this bead was already closed once on measurements alone and reopened after a listening test. The cvar flushes the sfx cache on change so it toggles live mid-game. uhexen2-edqp carries the A/B listening test and the default-flip decision.

title: CSHC (not CSQC): evaluate FTE's ftehw.pk3 + Spoike's technical notes
description: Spoike (FTE dev) clarified: Hexen II uses CSHC not CSQC — OP_CALL1+ works differently, progs CRC computed differently. Current Hexenwail has PR_SaveVMState/PR_RestoreVMState which suggests capability to switch between SSHC and CSHC. Spoike questions need for uHexen2's v7 progs format (conflicts with fteqcc v7). FTE compiles entire Quake engine into 65k globals. Reference pk3: https://fte.triptohell.info/moodles/dev/ftehw.pk3 — handles H2 chunk system in gamecode. Stub check for csprogs.dat in cl_csqc.c has no VM behind it — was a no-op check.
close_reason:
Evaluated. Recommendation: do not pursue ftehw.pk3 interop. Finding recorded in code at 595879a64.

First, the bead's premise is stale. It says 'stub check for csprogs.dat in cl_csqc.c has no VM behind it — was a no-op check'. That is no longer true: an Ironwail-style HUD-only CSQC VM has since landed — engine/hexen2/cl_csqc.c (326 lines), engine/h2shared/pr_csqc.c (553 lines, 25 PF_ builtins), cl_csqc.h, a cl_nocsqc cvar, entry points CSQC_Init / CSQC_Shutdown / CSQC_DrawHud / CSQC_DrawScores, and VM switching through PR_SaveVMState / PR_RestoreVMState at pr_edict.c:2299/2324 — which is exactly the capability the bead speculated those functions implied.

Three reasons not to chase ftehw.pk3:

1. THE v7 COLLISION IS REAL AND IS LOAD-BEARING. CL_LoadCSProgs gates on p->version only, accepting PROG_VERSION_V6/V7, then rejects v6 a few lines later ('only support V7 csprogs.dat for now'). So we require uHexen2's v7. Spoike's point was that uHexen2 v7 and fteqcc v7 share a version number but not a layout — so an fteqcc-built csprogs.dat, which is what ftehw.pk3 would ship, does not fail cleanly: it PASSES the version check and is then misparsed. Distinguishing them needs a discriminator beyond p->version that we do not have. Documented in cl_csqc.c so the next person meets the warning at the line where it bites.

2. SCOPE MISMATCH. ftehw.pk3 is HexenWorld gamecode that handles the H2 chunk system in gamecode, and it presumes FTE's full CSQC environment — entity VM, prediction, FTE's builtin numbering. Ours is deliberately HUD-only: a 25-builtin draw-only subset, matching the project's stated Ironwail-parity default. Adopting it is not a drop-in; it is a different feature.

3. NO CLIENT TO RUN IT ON. HexenWorld is not ported to this engine — uhexen2-6g8q and uhexen2-onfa are both still open. Evaluating HexenWorld gamecode interop ahead of having a HexenWorld client is out of order.

If HexenWorld does get ported and FTE interop becomes interesting again, the work starts at the v7 discriminator, not at the pk3.

title: Re-enable soft sprites with proper depth bias
description: Soft sprite shader discards fragments within 0.001 of scene depth, clipping weapon impact sprites that spawn on hit surfaces. Need a larger depth bias tolerance or offset-based approach. Currently disabled.
close_reason:
Obsolete — describes code that has never existed in this repo. No soft-sprite shader is present in the tree (all shaders are embedded C string literals in engine/h2shared/gl_shader.c, 1286 lines — there are no .glsl files at all). No shader samples a depth texture; every discard in that file is an alpha-cutout test (color.a < u_alpha_threshold, or the khsa stochastic hash at line 671), never a depth comparison. The only depth texture in the engine is the GL_DEPTH_COMPONENT24 Hi-Z occlusion pyramid at gl_worldcull.c:892, never bound into a sprite draw.

Pickaxe across git history for u_depthtex, sceneDepth, scene_depth, softness, depthfade, soft_fade, gl_shader_sprite, sprite_program, r_soft*, and regex [Ss]oft[ _]?[Ss]prite finds zero source hits. The only occurrences are this bead's own text. Most likely explanation: the bead was filed 2026-03-30T08:26Z; about 15 hours later 07ef1c5fa added a hardcoded glPolygonOffset(-1,-1) to sprites and b03ee5e3d reverted it 8 minutes later. The feature existed only in an uncommitted working state and was wiped by that same-evening reset.

The cited symptom — impact sprites clipping against surfaces — was fixed by different mechanisms: depth writes off for translucent sprites (uhexen2-m0he, gl_rmain.c:3621 and :3649-3653) plus GL_POLYGON_OFFSET_FILL around the sprite draw (uhexen2-rsy9, commit dc865a35a, gl_rmain.c:716-729).

Nothing to re-enable. Soft particles as a visual-quality feature is a separate, still-unimplemented idea — refiled as a new feature.

title: Add dependency/CVE scanning
description: No Dependabot or similar tracking for nix flake input vulnerabilities. Add automated dependency scanning to catch CVEs in upstream packages.
close_reason:
Implemented in commit 8839bf5fa. Two pieces, because Dependabot has no Nix flake ecosystem and could never have covered this alone:
- .github/dependabot.yml — weekly github-actions updates (the pinned Actions are the only thing Dependabot can see here).
- .github/workflows/security-scan.yml — weekly (Mon 06:17 UTC) plus workflow_dispatch, plus on PRs that touch flake.nix / flake.lock. Job 1 builds .#nixos and runs `vulnix --closure` against the NVD feeds, caching ~/.cache/vulnix, writing findings to the run summary and uploading text + JSON reports as a 30-day artifact. Job 2 parses `nix flake metadata --json` and reports each locked input's age, flagging anything older than 60 days.
Both jobs are deliberately advisory — summary + artifact, never a build failure. A CVE in a transitive library of a single-player game engine is worth knowing about but not worth blocking a release on, and a scanner that fails weekly gets muted.
Verified locally before commit: actionlint clean on the new workflow; the freshness script run against this repo's real `nix flake metadata --json`; and `vulnix --closure ./result` run end to end, which reported 179 CVE references across ~25 closure packages — so the scan produces real output rather than silently no-opping. Not verified: the workflow has not run on GitHub Actions yet (first scheduled run or a manual dispatch will confirm the runner-side steps).

title: Port utils/ and hw_utils/ to CMake
description: The 12+ utility tools (hcc, qbsp, light, vis, etc.) and hw_utils still only have GNU Makefiles. They should get CMake targets so the entire project can be built from a single build system. The utils still depend on scripts/makefile.inc and scripts/detect.sh which are kept for now.
close_reason:
Implemented in commit a5c0a7262. New repo-root CMakeLists.txt superproject (BUILD_ENGINE=ON, BUILD_UTILS=OFF) plus utils/CMakeLists.txt and hw_utils/CMakeLists.txt, and a packages.utils flake output (flake.nix:176-202) with a devShell hint line. All 18 tools build and were sanity-run: qbsp, light, vis, bsp2map, bsp2wal, bspinfo, genmodel, hcc, dhcc, jsh2colour, lmp2pcx, pakx, paklist, qfiles, hwmaster, hwmquery, hwrcon, hwterm — every one printed usage, a version banner, or a correct missing-input error; hwmaster correctly bound UDP 127.0.0.2:26900 and served as a daemon until timed out.

Two structural decisions: (1) Root CMakeLists exists because utils/ is a SIBLING of engine CMake root, not a child. Pulling from engine/ would inherit its include_directories, where utils/common/mathlib.h collides with engine/h2shared/mathlib.h and would silently shadow, plus it would force -ffast-math onto hcc/dhcc, which their Makefiles deliberately withhold. Root sets no compile options, definitions, or include dirs. (2) common/ becomes TWO static libraries: -DDOUBLEVEC_T flips vec_t from float to double at common/q_stdinc.h:153, reaching through mathlib.h and bspfile.h — an ABI change, why Makefiles compiled private copies.

Zero source fixes needed. All 16 tool source sets probed against gcc 15.3 at default -std=gnu23: no errors. The 26 -Wunused-result warnings (ignored fread/fscanf/system returns) are left as honest signal — real latent bugs, never silenced by Makefiles either.

Verified: .#default still builds at 1,521,800 bytes, byte-identical with root CMakeLists present; .#utils builds all 18 binaries linking only libm/libc; standalone configs of utils/ (14) and hw_utils/ (4) both pass; root default defines only glhexen2, no utils leak. Throwaway mingw cross-build produced all 18 .exe files, so WIN32 branches verified.

Not built, deliberately: hw_utils/qbsp-patch, hw_utils/xqf-patch (patches against third-party), texutils/palette (data only), qbsp/entmap.c (in tree but absent from qbsp's objects, defines own main), loose utils/progs_dump.c (referenced by no Makefile). GNU Makefiles, scripts/makefile.inc, scripts/detect.sh left in place per issue.

ONE DEVIATION for map-tool users: common libraries build at -O2 with -ffast-math per-tool on tool-owned sources only. Makefiles gave mathlib.o -ffast-math for bsp2map, genmodel, qbsp, light, vis. CMake applies it only per-tool. Dropping it is strictly more IEEE-conservative, but map-compiler output may not be bit-identical to Makefile-built qbsp or light.

title: Port h2ded dedicated server to CMake
description: The dedicated server (h2ded) only had a GNU Makefile which was removed in the build system cleanup. It needs a CMake target added to engine/CMakeLists.txt to be buildable again.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 2ab06c2b4. New BUILD_DEDICATED CMake option (engine/CMakeLists.txt:35, default OFF) builds h2ded from hexen2/server/{host,host_cmd,sys_unix}.c plus the shared sources minus five client-bound files (host.c, host_cmd.c, host_async.c, net_loop.c, wad.c — each verified unbuildable standalone under -DSERVERONLY), with -DSERVERONLY, linking only libm. GLQUAKE/SDLQUAKE/GL_DLSYM/NO_SPLASHES moved out of the directory-scoped add_definitions() into a CLIENT_DEFINITIONS variable applied to the client target (engine/CMakeLists.txt:86-109, :553) so they cannot leak into the server. Client parity proven by diffing normalised compile_commands.json against a pristine checkout: 100 translation units, byte-identical flags and identical source set. Two missing SERVERONLY guards fixed around PimpModel (pr_cmds.c:394, pr_edict.c:799) — the builtin table already mapped slot #111 to PF_Fixme for server builds, so the intent was always client-only. Sys_ListDirectories was absent from engine/hexen2/server/sys_unix.c while declared in sys.h and called from quakefs.c; filled in from hexen2/sys_unix.c:261. Results: h2ded links at 320,456 bytes, ldd shows only libm/libc (no libGL, no libSDL); `h2ded -help` prints the banner and exits 0; with no game data it exits 1 with a clean fatal error, no segfault. `nix build .#default` still produces the same 1,525,512-byte client. Scope limits: Unix only, and not run against real game data, so no map-load or netplay verification.

value: Headless scripted-play gotchas, CORRECTED 2026-08-12 (supersedes the '+exec a cfg of waits' advice in the earlier headless memory): '+exec <absolute path>' SILENTLY FAILS. exec only searches the game filesystem, so a cfg in /tmp or the job dir never runs — the engine prints 'couldn't exec <path>' and the run otherwise looks completely normal. Put the cfg IN THE GAMEDIR and exec it by relative name ('+exec t.cfg'). Second trap: command-line '+cmd' stuffing runs the exec'd cfg BEFORE '+map foo', so a cfg that assumes it is in-game fires during init. Put 'map <name>' as the first line of the cfg instead of passing +map. Third trap: CVAR_ARCHIVE cvars written by one run persist into ~/.hexen2/<gamedir>/config.cfg and are exec'd at init by every later run — this silently confounded a snd_resample A/B (a value that looked like a mid-session toggle was just config.cfg). Grep config.cfg for the cvar under test before trusting a result. With these fixed, 'screenshot' and 'soundlist' work: shots land in ~/.hexen2/<gamedir>/shots/hexenNNNN.tga. Budget ~1 frame/sec for 'wait' on llvmpipe at 640x480 in a loaded map, so 30 waits is ~30s, not instant.

Hexen II items that land on a func_door are riders, and the engine has a trap for them (traced 2026-08-15 for uhexen2-v41m). PF_droptofloor (pr_cmds.c:2400-2432) sets FL_ONGROUND + groundentity=trace.ent, so PlaceItem (items.hc:48-88, MOVETYPE_TOSS + SOLID_TRIGGER) leaves the item linked to the door. SV_PushMove carries it, but sv_phys.c:611-612 strips FL_ONGROUND from every non-MOVETYPE_WALK entity it moves, so it rides exactly ONE frame then goes ballistic. The real trap: sv_phys.c:626-633 (and 837-845 in SV_PushRotate) -- a pushed entity still embedded in the pusher takes id's 'corpse' branch if it is SOLID_NOT or SOLID_TRIGGER, which zeroes mins/maxs permanently. Hexen II pickups ARE SOLID_TRIGGER, so an item caught in a door silently loses its touch volume and can never be picked up. All three hunks are verbatim at fork point a0304b781, so this is upstream behaviour, not a Hexenwail regression.

Hexenwail RUNS HEADLESSLY on the dev box — the 'no GL here, needs the test machine' assumption is wrong. SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy fails at video init (no GL), but SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen with LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 gives a real GL 4.6 context on llvmpipe (Mesa 26.1.5) and the engine reaches the frame loop, loads maps, renders, and writes screenshots.

Recipe (verified 2026-08-12):
  tar xzf assets/demo/hexen2demo_nov1997-linux-i586.tgz -C $TMP hexen2demo_nov1997/data1
  cd $TMP/hexen2demo_nov1997
  SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 ./result/bin/glhexen2 -basedir $PWD -window -width 640 -height 480 +map demo1 +quit

Gotchas learned the hard way:
- Mesa caches compiled shaders, so GL debug warnings appear ONLY on a cold compile. Set MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DISABLE=true or you will never see them. This is how uhexen2-nkvm was found.
- Scripted play needs a cfg full of 'wait' lines exec'd with +exec; a bare '+wait' on the command line does not defer enough to get past map load. ~120 waits lands in-game.
- userdir comes from getpwuid(), NOT $HOME, so runs always write to the real ~/.hexen2/<gamedir>/. Delete what you create.
- stdout is block-buffered when redirected, so a SIGKILL test loses the log unless you wrap in stdbuf -oL.
- Screenshots land in ~/.hexen2/data1/shots/hexenNNNN.tga; convert with imagemagick and read the PNG to actually look at it. Pixel-region means make render changes measurable, not just eyeballed.

This makes 'needs field validation' beads testable locally: uhexen2-ekdm was closed this way, and uhexen2-enbw's visual claim was verified by measuring model vs world crops across cvar values. What still needs a real box: Windows-specific paths, browser/WASM, mod content we do not have (SoT), and anything about perceived smoothness (llvmpipe frame times swamp everything).

libsndfile CVE reachability (uhexen2-ql7h, established 2026-08-12): FluidSynth does NOT constrain which libsndfile format an SF3 sample may be. fluid_sffile.c calls sf_open_virtual(SFM_READ) with a zeroed SF_INFO and, after the open, only WARNS ('OGG sample is not OGG compressed, this is not officially supported') when (sfinfo.format & SF_FORMAT_OGG)==0 — it does not reject and decodes anyway. So the attack surface from a crafted .sf3 is EVERY decoder libsndfile links in, not just Vorbis. That is why CVE-2025-52194 (ircam_read_header) and CVE-2026-37555 (IMA-ADPCM WAV int overflow) are reachable. Encoder-only CVEs are not reachable: fluidsynth's only write path is its file renderer (sf_writef_float), format chosen by settings not by file content, and the game never invokes it. Both soundfonts this project ships are .sf2, so the default configuration never enters libsndfile at all. Cheapest kill-switch if the CVEs linger: fluidsynth -Denable-libsndfile=off, one line in flake.nix, costs only SF3 support.

The 'glass' screen-door bug (horizontal gray lines on translucent surfaces, uhexen2-zroc, P1 open) is NOT confirmed to be caused by GL_SAMPLE_ALPHA_TO_COVERAGE on a multisampled default framebuffer, despite past hypotheses.

Status: Reporter (Caco, NVIDIA RTX 3080, Windows) disproved the A2C hypothesis twice independently on r20: (a) with gl_fxaa 1 the world renders to the single-sample FBO and the glass is still broken (so artifact is independent of render target); (b) typing r_alphatocoverage 0 in console with AA on left the glass still broken.

Technical detail for reference: r_alphatocoverage defaults to 0 as of engine/hexen2/gl_rmain.c:116-117; the main scene FBO is configured with samples=0; the project uses FXAA for edge AA; GL_SAMPLE_ALPHA_TO_COVERAGE is a real mechanism that was cleaned up in engine code, but it is not the cause of zroc.

Next step: Re-test on r25+ build with Caco. Remaining hypotheses: the vid_restart or state change triggered by the AA menu toggle, texture minification moire, or blend/holey-texture state on SPECIAL_TRANS surfaces.

bd update <id> --notes REPLACES the notes field, it does not append. Clobbered uhexen2-2rxl's spawn-solid trap notes on 2026-08-18 and had to recover them from git (git show HEAD:.beads/issues.jsonl | python3 -c json parse for the id, read d['notes']). To append: recover the existing notes first, concatenate, then pass the whole thing. The auto-export to .beads/issues.jsonl on every bd write is what makes git the reliable undo.

Dark pillar audit findings (uhexen2-4ql1 supplement) - RecursiveLightPointColor analysis found three candidate causes: (1) returns success-with-black when surf->samples==NULL; (2) picks the first surface on the node plane with no facing check (coplanar back-side surface inherits dark light = shadow-casting look); (3) bilinear taps read one luxel past the rect on right/bottom edges. All three in engine/h2shared/gl_rlight.c:594-630.

Deterministic headless render-comparison harness (2026-08-14, proven on uhexen2-isq7/li13/ebpk): to compare two renderer configs pixel-for-pixel you MUST (1) take every shot in ONE process -- separate processes drift in cl.time; (2) 'pause' after the player settles, which freezes monsters and lightstyles: two identical runs differ by mean|d| 11.5 unpaused vs 0.06 paused; (3) pass -force with -width/-height, because plain -width is rejected under offscreen SDL when the fake display caps vid_maxwidth. Drive it with 'exec <cfg>' from a cfg placed in the gamedir, alias shot "wait; wait; wait; screenshot; wait", shots land in ~/.hexen2/<gamedir>/shots/hexenNNNN.tga. Run as SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy. No PIL on the box; use nix-shell -p python3Packages.pillow python3Packages.numpy. Good tile-floor vantage for filtering artifacts: SoT Arena palace start, setpos -956 -3872 -53 20 90 0.

Headless sprite/effects repro recipe (2026-08-15), the cheapest way to get Hexen II sprites on screen without a human: SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 glhexen2 -basedir /home/josh/hexen2 -width 640 -height 480 +<cvars> +exec <cfg>. GOTCHAS: (1) -userdir does NOT move the userdir — Sys_GetUserdir prefers getpwuid()->pw_dir, so the exec'd cfg MUST be written to ~/.hexen2/data1/ and exec'd by bare name, and screenshots land in ~/.hexen2/data1/shots/*.tga. (2) Set 'host_framerate 0.05' as the first line or the two runs you are diffing will not be frame-matched. (3) The cfg drives the game with no input at all: '_cl_playerclass 3' BEFORE 'map demo1' spawns a Necromancer, then ~60 'wait' lines, 'impulse 9' (CheatCommand: all weapons+mana), 'impulse 4' (W_ChangeWeapon to the raven staff), then '+attack' held across a burst of 'wait'/'screenshot' pairs. demo1's spawn faces a stone plinth ~200 units away, so the ravens detonate against geometry within ~6 screenshots — an ideal soft-particle / sprite-clipping test bed. (4) Runs archive cvars into ~/.hexen2/data1/config.cfg on quit, so a test that sets r_oit or r_scale LEAVES THEM SET for the developer; back it up and restore after. (5) magick -format '%[fx:int(mean*2550)]' info: per frame is a fast way to find which screenshots contain the effect — explosion/smoke frames jump from ~271 to 430-550 on demo1.

Ironwail porting tasks are P1 or above -- standing rule set by the user 2026-08-18. Any bead whose work is 'take a thing Ironwail has and bring it into Hexenwail' gets --priority=1 at filing time, regardless of how small or how blocked it is. This applies to the umbrella epic uhexen2-a5nn, every parity-table gap, and any blocker that would otherwise strand a P1 port (uhexen2-8dks was raised P4->P1 for exactly that reason).

Two exclusions, both recorded on the beads themselves:
- Beads that merely CITE Ironwail as reference material for a Hexenwail-specific bug are not ports (uhexen2-9o7u, the subdivided lava warp defect, stays P2).
- Beads for features Ironwail does not have are not ports even when they sound like parity work (uhexen2-im9g, bindless textures, stays P4 -- Ironwail does not use ARB_bindless_texture and the parity tracker marks it N/A).

Rationale: parity work kept sliding to the bottom of the queue at P3/P4 and never got picked up, while the tracker kept reporting ~97% parity. The priority floor makes the remaining gap actually schedulable.

libsndfile is NOT removable from the Hexenwail closure (measured 2026-08-15, uhexen2-kayb closed on this). nix why-depends --all ./result shows SEVEN paths, and SDL3 -> pipewire -> libsndfile is direct and unavoidable; the others go via fluidsynth, fluidsynth->libpulseaudio, and pipewire->{lilv,spandsp,roc-toolkit->sox}. So -Denable-libsndfile=0 on fluidsynth removes ZERO CVEs. GENERAL LESSON: 'readelf -d on the binary shows only one consumer' does NOT establish how a library enters a Nix closure -- readelf sees DT_NEEDED, not the transitive closure, and SDL3 dlopens pipewire rather than linking it. Use nix why-depends --all, never readelf, for closure provenance. Also measured: the engine never creates a fluid_audio_driver_t (midi_fluid.c:311 uses fluid_synth_write_s16 into SDL), so fluidsynth's ALSA/pulse/JACK backends are dead weight -- a size lever, not a security one.

SCOPE CLARIFICATION 2026-08-18, from the user: the P1-or-above porting rule is about IRONWAIL ITSELF. 'If they aren't related to ironwail itself, that's not what I refer to.'

Do not describe the rule as covering other upstreams. It does not. An earlier memory framed it as having been 'extended to jsHexen2 rendering parity' -- that was my framing, not the user's instruction, and it has been deleted.

What actually happened: I asked whether the floor should also cover three jsHexen2 rendering beads, the user said yes, and uhexen2-7oim / uhexen2-mfql / uhexen2-s4xh were raised P4 -> P1. That was a one-off call on three specific beads, NOT a widening of the rule. They stay P1.

The four jsHexen2 gamecode-vendoring beads -- uhexen2-2kcw and its children 42cm, e8bg, 6xtv -- stay at P3. Not Ironwail, so out of scope, and three of them are explicitly gated on the undecided 2kcw anyway.

Practical rule for future sweeps: when checking whether the floor is satisfied, match on Ironwail. Do not pull in beads that merely mention another engine. If a non-Ironwail bead looks like it deserves promotion, that is a separate question to ask, not an application of this rule.

sv_physfps mod-compat signature: if a mod's behaviour is EXACT at sv_physfps 20 and merely approximate at other rates (not 'better at 20'), the cause is QC hardcoding 20 as 1/frametime — e.g. 'held.velocity = delta * 20', which closes 100% of the gap per tick only when frametime is 0.05. Correct idiom is 'delta / frametime' using the frametime global (declared h2/global.hc:12, set by the engine each tick); Raven's own code does this at h2/client.hc:1326 for water friction. Audited all 718 .hc files 2026-08-23: shipped gamecode is CLEAN — every velocity*10/*20 site (h2/skullwiz.hc:890,895, h2/archer.hc:223, h2/triggers.hc:1411,1416) is a one-shot impulse, and all 199 HX_FRAME_TIME uses (constant.hc:8 = 0.05) are think intervals or effect durations, which stay correct at any tick rate. Diagnostic to hand a reporter: try r_lerpmove 0, which separates 'really behind' from 'drawn behind'.

Automatable portion (headless-browser verification of WEB_RENDERER=webgl2 and WEB_RENDERER=software with real retail pak data) starting now. Real-device items remain open: iOS PWA install flows, touch hardware (phone-mode testing), real GPU verification (not llvmpipe). Headless pass alone does not close this issue.

Cross-BUILD headless render comparison (2026-08-15, proved the jwzf gutter pixel-clean and caught uhexen2-6rqa): the 2026-08-14 'pause then screenshot' harness does NOT work across two different binaries. Same binary twice is bit-deterministic (mean|d| 0.006-0.15), but two builds arrive at map spawn on a different frame count, so they sit at a different lightstyle phase and a pure no-op diffs by mean|d| ~5-8 -- indistinguishable from a real regression. Also note 'unpause' is NOT a command; a second 'pause' toggles, so a naive cfg screenshots while running. FIX: drop pause entirely, take a BURST of ~30 screenshots spaced 2 waits apart from a fixed setpos, then cross-match all 30x30 pairs and take the minimum mean|d|. First measure the within-run envelope (max mean|d| of frame i vs frame 0) to get a noise floor -- on demo1/Blackmarsh it is 0.76, so any cross-build minimum above ~1 is real. This turned an ambiguous 7.9 into: gutter commit 0.0007 (max 1 LSB, clean) and the remaining 7.89 isolated to fullbright masks by re-running HEAD with gl_fullbrights 0 (0.0013 vs baseline). GOTCHAS: -developer as a COMMAND-LINE switch, not '+developer 1', or you miss VID_Init's Con_DPrintfs; 'timeout -s KILL' because +quit does not exit; ~/.hexen2/data1/config.cfg is rewritten by runs, so back it up and diff it afterwards (a run silently reset the developer's r_lightmap_bicubic 1 to 0).

Headless test-run gotchas (2026-08-12): the engine ignores SIGTERM during shutdown, so plain 'timeout N' can leave a glhexen2 running forever after a map load — always use 'timeout -k 5 N'. Do not clean up with pkill -f on a pattern containing the engine's own argv (e.g. pkill -f 'glhexen2 .*map tibet'); the bash -c wrapper's command line contains that text too, so pkill kills the shell running the command. '+edicts' is the way to prove an entity survived load (ED_Print dumps absmin/absmax/mins/maxs/flags per edict), but on a 1400-entity SoT map it takes minutes to drain through the console — dump it only when you need it, and never into a log path a second run is also writing. External 'maps/<name>.ent' overrides in the gamedir work and are the cheap way to test worldspawn-key parsing without a BSP compiler: extract lump 0 with a 10-line python struct reader, edit, drop it in <gamedir>/maps/. Strip NULs from the extracted lump or ugrep treats it as binary and silently prints nothing.

Material-map sidecar naming for Hexenwail is DarkPlaces/FTE convention and is NOT ours to choose: _norm (normal map; alpha may carry height for offset mapping), _bump (height map, ignored when _norm exists), _gloss (specular), _glow, _luma (Tenebrae-compatible alias for _glow). Verified 2026-08-23 against darkplaces.txt lines 212-235 and 261-268 in DarkPlacesEngine/darkplaces, and model_shared.c:2459 for _gloss; FTE accepts the same set. _glow and _luma already work via IMG_LoadReplacementGlow in engine/h2shared/img_load.c. Our textures/<mapname>/<name> then textures/<name> search order in IMG_BuildCandidates already matches DarkPlaces exactly. An earlier version of uhexen2-mfql said '*_n.tga', which was invented and would have stranded every existing pack — do not re-derive this convention, read it from the engines that shipped it.

The client's server/physics tick rate is sv_physfps (default 72 Hz, engine/hexen2/host.c), NOT sys_ticrate. sys_ticrate is the dedicated-server frame interval and sys_sdl.c only reads it under isDedicated. It used to drive the _Host_Frame fixed-timestep accumulator, which pinned the listen server at 20 Hz and broke strafe jumping (SV_AirAccelerate gains at most addspeed per tick, a figure that does not scale with frametime, so speed gain is proportional to tick count), monster cadence and mod think chains (SV_RunThink runs at most one think per server frame). Fixed 2026-08-22 in uhexen2-skjv. 72 Hz is the historical rate: upstream uHexen2 ran one server frame per render frame bounded by host_maxfps=72, and Raven's disabled FPS_20 arm substeps at 1.0/72.0.

AUDIO REGRESSION 0.7.9-beta.r5 through r10 (fixed by revert d5d3bc614, ships in r11). Cause: c5a81cdeb Catmull-Rom cubic resampling in ResampleSfx (snd_mem.c). Affected ALL non-MIDI audio; MIDI music was fine. GitHub releases r5-r10 are marked with BROKEN AUDIO in title + body notice; r4 is the last clean release.

Three defects, measured vs r4 on the real path (8-bit mono 11025 Hz source, 44100 Hz mixer, loadas8bit 0 so sc->width stays 1):
1. HF rolloff in the top octave where Hexen II samples live: -1.45 dB at 5 kHz, -2.00 dB at 5.3 kHz. Cubic only beats point-sampling below ~3.5 kHz.
2. Clipping: kernel L1 weight norm 1.25 saturates the 16-bit intermediate on near-full-scale content. 1.12% of samples on full-scale noise, 18.73% on full-scale square. Weapons/explosions audibly distort.
3. -0.35 LSB DC offset: interpolation at 16-bit precision but the 8-bit store is 'sample >> 8', which floors instead of rounding. Point-sampling had no requantization at all.

TRANSFERABLE LESSON: the original was validated by an ASan+UBSan harness over 1536 configs checking out-of-bounds reads, writes past allocation, UB, and bit-exactness at stepscale==1. That is a MEMORY-SAFETY harness, not a FIDELITY harness -- it cannot catch rolloff, clipping, or DC offset. For any DSP/resampler/filter change, measure frequency response, clipping rate and DC offset against the previous implementation before claiming an improvement. The issue was closed noting 'NOT runtime-verified -- needs a listen on the test box'; that caveat was the real signal and it shipped anyway.

Redoing this needs three things TOGETHER: (a) sc->width = 2 while interpolating plus matching S_LoadSound allocation (len currently uses info.width), else the precision is thrown away by the 8-bit store; (b) round not truncate on store; (c) headroom scaling or soft clip for the 1.25 overshoot.

libTiMidity (libs/timidity, the WASM/no-FluidSynth MIDI tier) CANNOT read SF3 soundfonts, and fails dirty rather than cleanly. Its SoundFont support is Takashi Iwai's 1997 SBK/SF2 extension: sndfont.c:295-330 freads sample bytes straight in as raw 16-bit LE PCM with no decoder, and sndfont.c:591 tests only sampletype & 0x8000 (ROM), missing SF3's 0x10 Vorbis bit. An SF3 is valid RIFF/sfbk so readsbk.c accepts it and the Vorbis bitstream plays as noise. SF_FindSoundFont (soundfont.c:71-137) probes soundfont.sf3 in four slots and hands it over unvalidated -> uhexen2-d4e7. Consequence for uhexen2-g3j9: the WASM soundfont MUST be an uncompressed SF2. Measured: TimGM6mb.sf2 is 5,969,788 bytes and gzip -9 only reaches 5,560,045 (6.9%), so wire compression cannot rescue the preload cost.

Linux MIDI music depends entirely on FluidSynth + a soundfont. There is NO MID streamer codec registered in snd_codec.c, so midi/<name>.mid can only play via the MIDIDRIVER_MID handler, which requires FluidSynth to have initialized (found a soundfont). If no soundfont is found, no MIDI driver registers and every MIDI track fails with 'Couldn't handle music file <name>'. Windows is immune (midi_win.c native midiStream synth, no soundfont needed).

STATUS as of 2026-08-11: a soundfont IS now shipped on every distribution path -- uhexen2-ji75 closed 2026-06-16. Flatpak installs TimGM6mb to /app/share/soundfonts/default.sf2 plus -DSOUNDFONT_PATH. The linux-fhs portable package (and thus release/linux-x86_64/) copies TimGM6mb to bin/soundfont.sf2. The nixos package compiles in -DSOUNDFONT_PATH=${soundfont-fluid}/share/soundfonts/FluidR3_GM2-2.sf2, a real store runtime dep. So MIDI works out of the box; do NOT re-file 'bundle a soundfont'.

Remaining real gap: uhexen2-20bp (open, P2) -- no Flathub and no auto-update, so field testers stay on pre-soundfont builds. A fresh 'no MIDI on Linux' report almost always means an old binary, not a missing feature. Second, smaller gap: a plain cmake source build that finds fluidsynth but has no -DSOUNDFONT_PATH and no system soundfont silently gets no MIDI (distro-packager path).

find_soundfont in midi_fluid.c searches, in order: snd_soundfont cvar, <exe dir>/soundfont.sf2|sf3 (via /proc/self/exe), <basedir>/soundfont.sf2|sf3, <basedir>/data1/, compile-time SOUNDFONT_PATH, then system paths incl. /app/share/soundfonts (Flatpak) and /usr/share/sounds/sf2.

Dolt remote sync (bd dolt push/pull) does NOT work as a backup in this project's setup: bd runs in EMBEDDED mode (no dolt sql-server; dolt binary not installed). The git+ssh remote transport (git+ssh://...github.com/...) fails to round-trip: push needs --force to advance refs/dolt/data, push leaves git refs/heads/main at the seed commit (not the dolt data tip) so every clone checks out an empty main, and bootstrap hardcodes db name 'beads' (no --database flag) which mismatches the source db 'uhexen2' (from issue prefix). Net: clones/bootstrap restore 0 issues even though ~3MB of real chunks are on the remote. Verified 2026-06-18 with bd 1.0.3-dev. THE reliable backup is the git-tracked .beads/issues.jsonl (proven full-fidelity restore via bd init + bd import: 604/62/527 exact). If a live Dolt backup is ever needed, use server mode (needs dolt binary) or a native DoltHub remote, not git+ssh embedded. Don't re-investigate git+ssh embedded sync.

Hexen II BSP parsing: dmodel_t is EIGHTY bytes, not Quake's 64, because MAX_MAP_HULLS is 8 (common/bspfile.h:25). Reading it at 64 gives plausible-looking bboxes for low submodel indices and pure nonsense for high ones, so it fails silently -- it cost a wrong conclusion on uhexen2-ogsd before being caught. World collision questions (is this reachable, how tall is this step) are answered by walking clipnodes with headnode[1] from model 0; headnode[0] indexes the nodes lump instead and is NOT a clipnode. Live entity state after a map load comes from the 'edicts' console command (pr_edict.c:3021), which is far more reliable than static entity-lump analysis for 'did this item spawn'.

Ironwail DOES use ARB_bindless_texture. Verified 2026-08-18 against origin/master 4fa8bfbd: gl_vidsdl.c sets gl_bindless_able behind GL_FindExtension('GL_ARB_bindless_texture') && GL_InitFunctions(); gl_texmgr.c calls GL_GetTextureSamplerHandleARB and MakeTextureHandleResident; gl_shaders.c compiles '#define BINDLESS %d' with real #if BINDLESS branches; r_world.c uses it on the world draw path.

This corrects a claim that sat in history/ARE_WE_IRONWAIL_YET.md for months in three separate places ('Ironwail does not use ARB_bindless_texture either'), which had the knock-on effect of classifying bindless as N/A rather than Missing and parking uhexen2-im9g at P4.

Removing OUR bindless scaffolding in 8124ed055 was still correct, and the contrast is instructive: we declared the ARB entry points through GL_FUNCTION_OPT, which GL_Init_Functions expands to nothing, so gl_bindless_able could never be true. Ironwail loads the same entry points through GL_InitFunctions and checks the return. That single difference is why theirs runs and ours never did.

Lesson for future parity passes: verify 'Ironwail does not have X' against origin/master before writing it down. Three of these were wrong in one pass -- bindless, gl_waterripple, and the glow cvars -- and one of them (gl_waterripple/glows) came from grepping the WRONG TREE and reporting Hexenwail line numbers as Ironwail's. Sys_GetUserdir prefers getpwuid(getuid())->pw_dir and only falls back to $HOME (engine/hexen2/sys_unix.c:456-461). Setting the HOME environment variable therefore does NOT move the engine's user directory — a test that sets HOME will happily read and write the developer's real ~/.hexen2 while appearing to be sandboxed. Redirecting it requires bwrap --bind <fake> /home/josh or equivalent. Found during uhexen2-qoy7 userdir testing, where the first run wrote to the real userdir before this was noticed.

uhexen2-rutp root cause, found 2026-08-12: the Barbican changelevel crash is a use-after-free on client->ex_inventory, NOT the Windows MIDI UAF (uhexen2-520e). sv.ex_inventory_pages is hunk memory that Host_ClearMemory frees and reallocates at a new address on every map load (Hunk_FreeToLowMark + memset(&sv,0)), but svs.clients is allocated once in Host_Init and survives changelevel, and client->ex_inventory was only assigned on initial connect. INV_UpdateExItem then walks the freed array as a linked list. Fixed in d46d000c5 by re-pointing active clients after the realloc. GENERAL LESSON for this engine: anything in client_t or svs that caches a pointer INTO sv.* or the hunk is dangling after every changelevel — Host_ClearMemory nulls sv wholesale but touches nothing in svs.clients. Worth auditing other client_t pointer fields the same way. Also: this class of bug IS reproducible headlessly on the demo data ('map demo1' then 'changelevel demo2' under gdb), so 'needs the Windows test box' was wrong for it.
